declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.isProper_projectiveBundleToBase
declarations.doc:
**The projection `π : 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` of the projective bundle of a finite locally free sheaf of
modules is proper.**

This is the properness clause of Stacks 0800 for the graded algebra `Sym(ℰ)`: its degree-zero
part is the structure sheaf and it is generated in degree one by `ℰ`, which is spanned by
finitely many sections on a cover of `X` by affine opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_projectiveBundleToBase
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E] :
    IsProper (projectiveBundleToBase X E)
declarations.comment: proper, for the projective bundle of a finite locally free module

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.isProper_projectiveBundleToBase_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**The projection `π : 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` of the projective bundle of a quasi-coherent module of
finite type is proper.**

This is the properness clause of Stacks 0800 for the graded algebra `Sym(ℰ)`, under the
finiteness hypothesis of Tag 01W8 rather than finite local freeness. Both chartwise conditions
of `Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.isProper_relativeProjToBase` now hold at *every* affine open of
the base: the degree-zero one is unconditional, and the finite-type one follows from generation
in degree one together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_finset_span_of_isFiniteType`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_projectiveBundleToBase_of_isFiniteType [E.IsQuasicoherent] [E.IsFiniteType] :
    IsProper (projectiveBundleToBase X E)
declarations.comment: proper, for the projective bundle of a quasi-coherent module of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.relativeProj_finiteType_iff_and_isLocallyProjective_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0800.** Let `𝒜` be a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra over a scheme `S` and
`p : Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ S` its relative homogeneous spectrum. The conditions

1. `𝒜_0` is a finite type `𝒪_S`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒜_0`-algebra,
2. `𝒜_0` is a finite type `𝒪_S`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒪_S`-algebra

are equivalent, and under them `p` is locally projective and in particular proper.

Each condition is written out as the source defines it: finite type of `𝒜_0` is
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`, and a quasi-coherent algebra is of finite type over `𝒜_0`, resp.
over `𝒪_S`, when over every affine open `U` of `S` its algebra of sections `𝒜(U)` is a finite type
`𝒜_0(U)`-algebra, resp. a finite type `𝒪_S(U)`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeProj_finiteType_iff_and_isLocallyProjective_isProper :
    ((SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧
        ∀ U : s.base.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
          Algebra.FiniteType (s.sectionRingGrading U 0) (s.sectionRing U)) ↔
      (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧
        ∀ U : s.base.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
          (show Γ(s.base, U) →+* s.sectionRing U from s.sectionRingBaseMap U).FiniteType)) ∧
    ((SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧
        ∀ U : s.base.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
          Algebra.FiniteType (s.sectionRingGrading U 0) (s.sectionRing U)) →
      IsLocallyProjective (relativeProjToBase s) ∧ IsProper (relativeProjToBase s))

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.projQuotientIso
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism `Z ≅ Proj (𝒮 / I(Z))`.** It is the lift of `i` through the closed immersion
`Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.ambientHom`, which is invertible because the two closed
subschemes have the same ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def projQuotientIso [CompactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮)]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    Z ≅ projQuotient 𝒮 i
declarations.comment: the absolute case, over an affine base

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.projQuotientIso_hom_comp_ambientHom
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism is canonical**: it is compatible with the two morphisms to `Proj 𝒮`, so it
is an equality of closed subschemes of `Proj 𝒮` and not merely an abstract isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem projQuotientIso_hom_comp_ambientHom [CompactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮)]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    (projQuotientIso 𝒮 i).hom ≫ ambientHom 𝒮 i = i
declarations.comment: the identification is over the ambient Proj; the absolute case, over an affine base

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjGradedIdeal.exists_iso_projQuotient_twistKer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0801.** Let `S` be a scheme, `𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra,
`p : X = Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ S` the relative homogeneous spectrum and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed subscheme.
Let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒜` be the kernel of the canonical map `𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{d ≥ 0} p_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d))`. If `p` is
quasi-compact then `Z = Proj_S(𝒜/ℐ)`.

The ideal is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjGradedIdeal.twistKerGradedIdeal`, the
degreewise kernel of the homogeneous-section map of Tag 01NR followed by the unit of the
pullback–pushforward adjunction at `i`; the quotient is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjGradedIdeal.quotAlgebra` and the closed immersion
`Proj_S(𝒜/ℐ) ⟶ Proj_S(𝒜)` is `projQuotientHom`. The equality `Z = Proj_S(𝒜/ℐ)` of the source is
read, as everywhere in this repository, as an isomorphism over the ambient relative Proj.

The proof is `ker_eq_ker_projQuotientHom_twistKer` fed to `exists_iso_projQuotient_of_ker_eq`,
which produces the isomorphism from the equality of ideal sheaves by
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.lift` and `isIso_lift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_projQuotient_twistKer [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact (relativeProj 𝒜).toBase] :
    ∃ e : Z ≅ (relativeProj (quotAlgebra 𝒜 (twistKerGradedIdeal 𝒜 D i))).scheme,
      e.hom ≫ projQuotientHom 𝒜 (twistKerGradedIdeal 𝒜 D i) = i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjTwists.exists_finiteType_degreeQuotientPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0802.** A closed subscheme of finite presentation of a quasi-compact
relative `Proj` over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base is the relative `Proj` of the quotient
of `𝒜` by the graded ideal generated by a quasi-coherent finite type submodule `ℱ` of a single
homogeneous piece `𝒜_d` with `d > 0`.

The relative case of Tag 0801 — the graded-quotient presentation that
`…RelativeProjGradedIdeal.exists_finiteType_degreeQuotientPresentation` consumes — is
`…RelativeProjTwists.gradedQuotientPresentation`, so the statement carries no hypothesis beyond
the tag's own.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteType_degreeQuotientPresentation (A : SheafGradedAlgebra S)
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ (relativeProj A).scheme)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact (relativeProj A).toBase]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation i) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ ℱ : (A.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule,
      ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧
          Nonempty (DegreeQuotientPresentation A i ℱ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjGradedIdeal.exists_finiteType_presentation_supp
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, `𝒜` a
quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra, `p : X = Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ S` the relative homogeneous spectrum,
`i : Z ⟶ X` a closed subscheme and `U ⊆ S` an open of the base. Assume

1. `p` is quasi-compact,
2. `i` is of finite presentation,
3. `U ∩ p(i(Z)) = ∅`,
4. `U` is quasi-compact, and
5. every graded piece `𝒜_n` is a finite type `𝒪_S`-module.

Then there are `d > 0` and a quasi-coherent finite type `𝒪_S`-submodule `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d` such that

(a) `Z = Proj_S(𝒜/ℱ𝒜)`, read as a `DegreeQuotientPresentation` — an identification of `Z` with
the relative Proj of the quotient of `𝒜` by the graded ideal generated by `ℱ`, over `Proj_S(𝒜)`;
and

(b) the support of `𝒜_d/ℱ` does not meet `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_presentation_supp (U : S.Opens)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact (relativeProj A).toBase]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation i)
    (hU : (U : Set S) ∩ Set.range (i ≫ (relativeProj A).toBase).base = ∅)
    (hUc : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (hA : ∀ n : ℕ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} (A.piece (n : ℤ))) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ ℱ : (A.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule,
      ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧
          (U : Set S) ∩ (⟨(cokernel ℱ.ι).val, (cokernel ℱ.ι).isSheaf⟩ :
              RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} S.toRingedSpace).supp = ∅ ∧
            Nonempty (DegreeQuotientPresentation A i ℱ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjTwists.exists_finiteType_presentation_supp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0803.** Let `i : Z ⟶ Proj_S(𝒜)` be a closed subscheme of finite
presentation of a quasi-compact relative `Proj` over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base, let
`U` be a quasi-compact open of the base missing the image of `Z`, and let every `𝒜_n` be of
finite type. Then `Z` is the relative `Proj` of the quotient of `𝒜` by the graded ideal generated
by a quasi-coherent finite type submodule `ℱ` of a single homogeneous piece `𝒜_d` with `d > 0`,
and `ℱ` may be chosen so that the support of `𝒜_d/ℱ` is disjoint from `U`.

The relative case of Tag 0801 — the vanishing-ideal presentation that
`…RelativeProjGradedIdeal.exists_finiteType_presentation_supp_of_vanishingIdeal` consumes — is
`…RelativeProjTwists.vanishingIdealPresentation`, so the statement carries no hypothesis beyond
the tag's own.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteType_presentation_supp (A : SheafGradedAlgebra S) {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ (relativeProj A).scheme) (U : S.Opens)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact (relativeProj A).toBase]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation i)
    (hU : (U : Set S) ∩ Set.range (i ≫ (relativeProj A).toBase).base = ∅)
    (hUc : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (hA : ∀ n : ℕ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} (A.piece (n : ℤ))) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ ℱ : (A.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule,
      ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧
          (U : Set S) ∩ (⟨(cokernel ℱ.ι).val, (cokernel ℱ.ι).isSheaf⟩ :
              RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} S.toRingedSpace).supp = ∅ ∧
            Nonempty (DegreeQuotientPresentation A i ℱ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.reesAwayEquivAffineBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0804.** For `a ∈ I` the standard affine chart of `Proj` of the Rees
algebra at the degree-one element `a⁽¹⁾` is the affine blowup algebra `R[I/a]`: the degree-zero
part of the localization of `R[It]` at `a⁽¹⁾` is `R[I/a]`.

This is the chart computation behind the second assertion of tag 0804; the covering statement
itself is `Stacks.Blowup.iSup_opensRange_blowUpAffineChart`.
declarations.statement:
def reesAwayEquivAffineBlowup (ha : a ∈ I) :
    Away (reesGrading I) (reesDegOne I ha) ≃+* affineBlowup I a
declarations.comment: the chart D₊(a⁽¹⁾) is Spec of the affine blowup algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.iSup_opensRange_blowUpAffineChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0804, second assertion.** Let `b : X' ⟶ S` be the blowup of a scheme
`S` in a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ`, and let `U` be an affine open of `S`. Then `b⁻¹(U)`
is covered by the spectra of the affine blowup algebras `Γ(S, U)[ℐ(U)/a]` for `a ∈ ℐ(U)`: the
morphisms `Stacks.Blowup.blowUpAffineChart` are open immersions whose images have supremum
`b⁻¹(U)`.

Together with the first assertion, `Stacks.Blowup.isPullback_blowUpChart`, this completes tag
0804.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_opensRange_blowUpAffineChart (U : S.affineOpens) :
    ⨆ r : ℐ.ideal U, (blowUpAffineChart ℐ U r.2).opensRange
      = blowUpToBase ℐ ⁻¹ᵁ (U : S.Opens)
declarations.comment: b⁻¹(U) is covered by the spectra of the affine blowup algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineBlowupStandardOpenIso
declarations.doc:
The standard affine chart of the Rees projective spectrum is canonically the
spectrum of the affine blowup algebra.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def affineBlowupStandardOpenIso {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.affineOpens) (a : I.ideal U) :
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradedRing U.1
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradingGradedRing U.1
    Spec (.of <| affineBlowupAlgebra (I.ideal U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))
      (Localization.Away (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1)))) ≅
      (Proj.basicOpen ((reesSituation I).sectionRingGrading U.1)
        (reesDegreeOne I U a).1).toScheme
declarations.comment: affine blowup algebra chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineBlowupStandardOpenIso_over
declarations.doc:
The affine blowup chart is an isomorphism over the affine base: its structure
map is induced by the canonical inclusion of the ring into its blowup algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineBlowupStandardOpenIso_over {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.affineOpens) (a : I.ideal U) :
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradedRing U.1
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradingGradedRing U.1
    (affineBlowupStandardOpenIso I U a).hom ≫
        (Proj.basicOpen ((reesSituation I).sectionRingGrading U.1)
          (reesDegreeOne I U a).1).ι ≫
        Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.projInclusionToOpen (reesSituation I) U.1 U.2 =
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap (X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))
          (affineBlowupAlgebra (I.ideal U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))
            (Localization.Away (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1)))))) ≫
        U.2.isoSpec.inv
declarations.comment: affine blowup chart over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineBlowupStandardOpenIso_fraction
declarations.doc:
On the standard chart at `a`, a degree-one section `b` divided by `a`
corresponds to the generating fraction `b/a` in the affine blowup algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineBlowupStandardOpenIso_fraction {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.affineOpens) (a b : I.ideal U) :
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradedRing U.1
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradingGradedRing U.1
    (((Spec.preimage
      ((affineBlowupStandardOpenIso I U a).hom ≫
        (Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec
          ((reesSituation I).sectionRingGrading U.1)
          (reesDegreeOne I U a).1 (reesDegreeOne I U a).2 (by omega)).hom)).hom
      (HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk
        ((reesSituation I).sectionRingGrading U.1)
        (reesDegreeOne I U a).2 1 (reesDegreeOne I U b).1
        (by simp)) :
      affineBlowupAlgebra (I.ideal U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))
        (Localization.Away (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1)))) :
      Localization.Away (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))) =
      IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.Away (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1)))
        (b : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1))
        ⟨(a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U.1)), Submonoid.mem_powers _⟩
declarations.comment: canonical affine blowup fractions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.blownUpAffine_chart_cover
declarations.doc:
Degree-one Rees elements give an affine open cover of the inverse image of
an affine open under the blowup morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem blownUpAffine_chart_cover {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (U : X.affineOpens) :
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradedRing U.1
    letI := (reesSituation I).sectionRingGradingGradedRing U.1
    (⋃ a : I.ideal U,
      Set.range ((Proj.basicOpen ((reesSituation I).sectionRingGrading U.1)
        (reesDegreeOne I U a).1).ι ≫
        Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.relativeProjChart (reesSituation I) U)) =
      (blowUpToBase I ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).1
declarations.comment: affine chart covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isPullback_blowUpChart
declarations.doc:
The blowup restricted to an affine open `U` of the base is `Proj` of the Rees algebra of
`ℐ(U)`: the chart over `U` is the preimage of `U` under the blowup morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_blowUpChart (U : S.affineOpens) :
    IsPullback (Stacks.RelativeProj.chartToOpen (fun W : S.affineOpens ↦ reesGrading (ℐ.ideal W))
      U (reesBase ℐ U)) (blowUpChart ℐ U) U.1.ι (blowUpToBase ℐ)
declarations.comment: the canonical identification of b⁻¹(U) with Proj of the Rees algebra

registrations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.relativeProjChart_isPullback
registrations.comment: canonical local projective-spectrum identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPullback_blowUpToBase_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0805.** Blowing up commutes with flat base change: for a flat
`g : X₁ ⟶ X₂` and a quasi-coherent ideal `I` on `X₂`, the blowup of `X₁` in the inverse image
of `I` sits in a cartesian square over the blowup of `X₂` in `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_blowUpToBase_comap {X₁ X₂ : Scheme.{u}} (g : X₁ ⟶ X₂) [Flat g]
    (I : X₂.IdealSheafData) :
    ∃ h : blowUp (I.comap g) ⟶ blowUp I,
      IsPullback (blowUpToBase (I.comap g)) h g (blowUpToBase I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isTerminal_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0806. The universal property of blowing up.** The blowup of a scheme
`X` in a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf `ℐ` is a final object of the category `C` of schemes over
`X` on which the inverse image of the centre is an effective Cartier divisor.

Unconditional. The five geometric inputs of
`Stacks.Blowup.exists_nonempty_isTerminal`, which is the uniqueness half of the tag reduced to
them, are now all theorems:

* separatedness of the blowup morphism is tag 01O2,
  `Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.isSeparated_relativeProjToBase`;
* membership of the blowup in `C` is tag 02OS part (2),
  `Stacks.Blowup.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalIdeal`;
* the blowup is an isomorphism over the complement of the centre by tag 02OS part (1),
  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_blowUpToBase_restrict_compl_support`;
* scheme-theoretic density of the complement of an effective Cartier divisor is tag 07ZU,
  `Stacks.Divisors.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`, transported
  along the open immersions of the gluing cover by
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Opens.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_preimage_of_isOpenImmersion`;
* the existence of the classifying morphism, which the source deduces from the universal
  property of relative `Proj` (Constructions, Section 01NS), is
  `Stacks.Blowup.exists_hom_blowUp_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`.

This supersedes `Stacks.Blowup.exists_nonempty_isTerminal_blowUp`, which is the same statement
with the last two of those as hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTerminal_blowUp {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    ∃ h : IsCartierOver I (Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)),
      Nonempty (IsTerminal
        (⟨Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I), h⟩ : CartierOver I))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_lift_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of blowing up, Stacks tag 0806, as a unique factorization.**  A
morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` along which the inverse image of the centre is an effective Cartier divisor
factors through the blowup in exactly one way.  This is the terminality statement
`Stacks.Blowup.isTerminal_blowUp` read as a `∃!`.
declarations.comment: the terminality of the blowup read as a unique factorization: a morphism along which the inverse image of the centre is an effective Cartier divisor factors through the blowup in exactly one way

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isIso_blowUpToBase_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0807].** Blowing up a scheme in an effective Cartier divisor does not change
it: the blowup morphism is an isomorphism.

The identity of `X` lies in the category `C` of [Stacks, Tag 0806] precisely because `I` is an
effective Cartier divisor, and the blowup is a final object of `C`
(`Stacks.Blowup.isTerminal_blowUp`), so the classifying morphism of the identity is a two-sided
inverse of the blowup morphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0808.** The blowup of a reduced scheme in a quasi-coherent ideal is
reduced.
declarations.statement: theorem isReduced_blowUp [IsReduced X] : IsReduced (blowUp I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullbackDefined_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0809.** Every effective Cartier divisor on a scheme has a defined
pullback along the blowup of the scheme in any quasi-coherent ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_blowUpToBase (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined (blowUpToBase I) D
declarations.comment: effective Cartier divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0809.** Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along the
blowup of a scheme in any quasi-coherent ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_blowUpToBase :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections (blowUpToBase I).toLRSHom
declarations.comment: meromorphic functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpMulIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080A.** Blowing up `X` in `I` and then in the inverse image of `J` is
canonically, over `X`, the blowup of `X` in `I * J`.
declarations.comment: canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpMulIso_unique
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism of Stacks tag 080A is the unique isomorphism of these two blowups over
`X`: both are terminal in the same category.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowUpMulIso_unique
    (e : Over.mk (blowUpToBase (J.comap (blowUpToBase I)) ≫ blowUpToBase I) ≅
      Over.mk (blowUpToBase (I * J))) : e = blowUpMulIso I J
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_mul_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
The product of a finitely presented centre with a centre of finite type is again a finitely
presented centre: by [Stacks, Tag 01TV] both statements say that the ideal is finitely generated
over every affine open, and the ideal of `I * J` there is the product of the two ideals.

This is the finite-presentation clause of [Stacks, Tag 080B].
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_mul_subschemeι (I J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : FinitePresentation I.subschemeι) (hJ : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (J.ideal U).FG) :
    FinitePresentation (I * J).subschemeι
declarations.comment: the centre Y is of finite presentation. Y is the explicit product I * J of the first centre with the second-centre ideal that Stacks Lemma 31.32.5, Tag 0803, supplies, and a product of a finitely presented centre with a centre of finite type is finitely presented

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_centre_supportSet_eq_and_nonempty_blowUpCompositionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080B.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `I`
be a finitely presented centre on `X` with blowup `b : X' ⟶ X`, and let `Z'` be a finitely
presented centre on `X'`. Then there is a finitely presented centre `Y` on `X` whose support is
`Supp I ∪ b(Supp Z')` and for which the two-step blowup `Bl_{Z'}(X') ⟶ X' ⟶ X` is the blowup of
`X` in `Y`, over `X`.

The centre is the product `I · J` of `I` with the second-centre ideal that
`Stacks.Blowup.exists_secondCentre` produces from `Z'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_centre_supportSet_eq_and_nonempty_blowUpCompositionIso
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : FinitePresentation I.subschemeι) (Z' : (blowUp I).IdealSheafData)
    (hfp : FinitePresentation Z'.subschemeι) :
    ∃ Y : X.IdealSheafData, FinitePresentation Y.subschemeι ∧
      Y.supportSet = I.supportSet ∪ (blowUpToBase I).base '' Z'.supportSet ∧
        Nonempty (Over.mk (blowUpToBase Z' ≫ blowUpToBase I) ≅ Over.mk (blowUpToBase Y))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_centre_supportSet_eq
declarations.doc:
**The support of the centre of [Stacks, Tag 080B].** There is a finitely presented centre
`Y` on `X` with `Supp Y = Supp I ∪ b(Supp Z')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_centre_supportSet_eq [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : FinitePresentation I.subschemeι)
    (Z' : (blowUp I).IdealSheafData) (hfp : FinitePresentation Z'.subschemeι) :
    ∃ Y : X.IdealSheafData, FinitePresentation Y.subschemeι ∧
      Y.supportSet = I.supportSet ∪ (blowUpToBase I).base '' Z'.supportSet
declarations.comment: part (1), the support of the centre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_centre_nonempty_blowUpCompositionIso
declarations.doc:
**The composite of two blowups is a blowup, [Stacks, Tag 080B].** There is a finitely
presented centre `Y` on `X` for which blowing `X` up in `Y` is the two-step blowup
`Bl_{Z'}(X') ⟶ X' ⟶ X`, over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_centre_nonempty_blowUpCompositionIso [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : FinitePresentation I.subschemeι)
    (Z' : (blowUp I).IdealSheafData) (hfp : FinitePresentation Z'.subschemeι) :
    ∃ Y : X.IdealSheafData, FinitePresentation Y.subschemeι ∧
      Nonempty (Over.mk (blowUpToBase Z' ≫ blowUpToBase I) ≅ Over.mk (blowUpToBase Y))
declarations.comment: part (2), the composite of the two blowups is the blowup in the centre

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.strictTransformSheaf
declarations.doc:
The strict transform of an `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` along the blowup of the base in `ℐ`: the
quotient of the pullback of `ℱ` to `X ×_S S'` by the submodule of sections supported on the
inverse image of the exceptional divisor.
declarations.statement: abbrev strictTransformSheaf (ℱ : X.Modules) : (blowUpPullback f ℐ).Modules
declarations.comment: strict transform of a module

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.strictTransformIdeal
declarations.doc:
The quasi-coherent ideal of sections of `𝒪_{X ×_S S'}` supported on the inverse image of
the exceptional divisor, assembled from its modules of sections over the affine opens of
`X ×_S S'`.
declarations.statement: def strictTransformIdeal : (blowUpPullback f ℐ).IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: ideal of the strict transform of a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.strictTransform
declarations.doc:
The strict transform of `X` along the blowup of the base in `ℐ`: the closed subscheme of
`X ×_S S'` cut out by the ideal of sections supported on the inverse image of the exceptional
divisor.
declarations.statement: abbrev strictTransform : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: strict transform of a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.ideal_strictTransformIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080D, part (2).** On an affine open, the defining ideal of the strict
transform of `X` consists of exactly the sections of `𝒪_{X ×_S S'}` supported on `pr_{S'}⁻¹ E`.
This is `Stacks.Blowup.ideal_strictTransformIdeal_of_quasiCompact` with its retrocompactness
hypothesis discharged, so it is the equality that tag 080D's definition asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem ideal_strictTransformIdeal (U : (blowUpPullback f ℐ).affineOpens) :
    (strictTransformIdeal f ℐ).ideal U =
      (SheafOfModules.supportedSectionsSubmodule (exceptionalPullbackSet f ℐ)
        (SheafOfModules.unit (blowUpPullback f ℐ).ringCatSheaf)).toSubmodule.obj
          (Opposite.op U.1)
declarations.comment: the defining ideal of the strict transform of a scheme, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isQuasicoherent_strictTransformSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080D, part (1).** The strict transform of a quasi-coherent module is
quasi-coherent on `X ×_S S'`, with no hypothesis. Recorded as an instance because the strict
transform of a strict transform is formed by instance search on the quasi-coherence of the
first.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasicoherent_strictTransformSheaf (ℱ : X.Modules) [ℱ.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (strictTransformSheaf f ℐ ℱ).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the strict transform of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080D (1).** The strict transform of a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F`: the
quotient of `pr_X^* F` by the submodule of sections supported on `pr_{S'}^{-1}(Supp E)`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev sheaf (F : X.Modules) : (baseChange f b).Modules
declarations.comment: strict transform of a module

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.ideal
declarations.doc:
The quasi-coherent ideal of sections of `𝒪_{X ×_S S'}` supported on
`pr_{S'}^{-1}(Supp E)`, assembled from its values on affine opens.
declarations.statement: public def ideal : (baseChange f b).IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: ideal of the strict transform of a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080D (2).** The strict transform of `X`: the closed subscheme of
`X ×_S S'` cut out by the ideal of sections supported on `pr_{S'}^{-1}(Supp E)`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev scheme : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: strict transform of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformBlowUpIso
declarations.doc:
The strict transform of `X` under the blowup of `S` in `ℐ` is the blowup of `X` in the
inverse image of `ℐ`, canonically as `X`-schemes.
declarations.comment: scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformSheafBlowUpIso
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F`, the strict
transform of `F` under the blowup of `S` in `ℐ` is canonically the direct image, along the closed
immersion `X' ⟶ X ×_S S'` of part (1), of the strict transform of `F` relative to the blowup of
`X` in the inverse image `ℐ·𝒪_X`. The sheaf `F` is not assumed quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
def strictTransformSheafBlowUpIso (F : X.Modules) :
    sheaf f (blowUpToBase ℐ) (exceptionalIdeal ℐ) F ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (strictTransformBlowUpι f ℐ)).obj
        (sheaf (𝟙 X) (blowUpToBase (ℐ.comap f)) (exceptionalIdeal (ℐ.comap f)) F)
declarations.comment: sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformIdeal_eq_bot_of_flat_at_exceptional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080F (1).** If `X` is flat over `S` at every point lying over the
centre of the blowup, then the strict transform of `X` is the whole base change `X ×_S S'`: the
ideal cutting it out is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransformIdeal_eq_bot_of_flat_at_exceptional
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : S.IdealSheafData)
    (hflat : ∀ x : X, f x ∈ I.support → IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    Stacks.StrictTransform.ideal f (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I) = ⊥
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_strictTransformSheaf_quotient_of_flat_at_exceptional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080F (2).** If a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` is flat over `S` at
every point lying over the centre of the blowup, then the canonical quotient map from `pr_X^* F`
onto the strict transform of `F` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_strictTransformSheaf_quotient_of_flat_at_exceptional
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : S.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hflat : ∀ x : X, f x ∈ I.support → IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    IsIso (Stacks.StrictTransform.π f (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I) F)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformSheafPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080G.** Let `b : S' ⟶ S` be the blowup of `S` in a closed subscheme
cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf `I`, let `g : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of schemes
over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `g' : X ×_S S' ⟶ Y ×_S S'` be the
base change of `g`. Then `g'_*` of the strict transform of `F` relative to `b` is the strict
transform of `g_* F`.
declarations.statement:
def strictTransformSheafPushforwardIso {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ S) (I : S.IdealSheafData)
    (F : X.Modules) [IsAffineHom g] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    let g' : Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange (g ≫ f) (blowUpToBase I) ⟶
        Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange f (blowUpToBase I) :=
      pullback.lift
        (pullback.fst (g ≫ f) (blowUpToBase I) ≫ g)
        (pullback.snd (g ≫ f) (blowUpToBase I))
        (by rw [Category.assoc]; exact pullback.condition)
    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward g').obj
        (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf (g ≫ f) (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I) F) ≅
      Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward g).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpProductIso_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080H**, part (1). Let `D` be an effective Cartier divisor on `S` and
let `I` be any quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. The blowup of `S` in `I * D` is the blowup of `S` in
`I`, as `S`-schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowUpProductIso_exists {S : Scheme.{u}} (I D : S.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) :
    Nonempty (Over.mk (blowUpToBase I) ≅ Over.mk (blowUpToBase (I * D)))
declarations.comment: part (1): isomorphism of blowups

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.exists_baseChange_iso_sheaf_iso_mul
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 080H] part (2).** Let `D` be an effective Cartier divisor on `S` and let `F`
be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules with no nonzero local sections supported in `f^{-1}D`. Given an
isomorphism `e` of the blowup of `S` in `I` with the blowup of `S` in `I * D` over `S` — part (1)
of the tag — the induced isomorphism of the two base changes, specified by both its projections,
carries the strict transform of `F` for the centre `I * D` to the strict transform for the centre
`I`.

Part (1) of the tag, which supplies `e`, is not in the repository; see the implementation notes
of this file. Everything else here is unconditional, [Stacks, Tag 02OS] part (1) being the
instance `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_blowUpToBase_restrict_compl_support`.

The hypothesis `_hD` that `D` is an effective Cartier divisor is the tag's, and is retained so
that the statement is the tag's; it is used only through `e`, which part (1) deduces from it, so
the conclusion in fact holds for any `D` admitting such an `e`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_baseChange_iso_sheaf_iso_mul (f : X ⟶ S) (I D : S.IdealSheafData)
    (_hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (F : X.Modules)
    (hF : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U)),
      s ∈ (supportedSectionsSubmodule (f.base ⁻¹' D.supportSet) F).toSubmodule.obj (op U) →
        s = 0)
    (e : Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) ≅
      Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase (I * D))) :
    ∃ g : baseChange f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) ≅
        baseChange f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase (I * D)),
      (g.hom ≫ pullback.fst f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase (I * D)) =
        pullback.fst f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)) ∧
      (g.hom ≫ pullback.snd f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase (I * D)) =
        pullback.snd f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) ≫ e.hom.left) ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g.hom).obj
        (sheaf f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase (I * D))
          (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal (I * D)) F) ≅
        sheaf f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I) F)
declarations.comment: part (2): strict transforms of modules

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.strictTransformSheaf_comp_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 080I] part (1).** For `b` the blowup of `S` in `I`, `c` the blowup of the
blowup in `J`, and `d` the blowup of `S` in a third centre `K` whose support is
`Supp I ∪ b(Supp J)`, the iterated strict transform of `F` agrees with the strict transform in
the composite centre, compatibly with both projections and with the quotient maps.

This is `Stacks.StrictTransform.exists_baseChange_iso_sheaf_iso_comp_blowUp` with its one
hypothesis `hQJ` discharged by
`Stacks.StrictTransform.supportedSections_sheaf_blowUp_union_eq_zero`, applied on the first base
change over the first blowup with centre `J` and divisor `AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I`,
whose own hypothesis is the defining property
`Stacks.StrictTransform.supportedSections_sheaf_eq_zero` of the first strict transform.
Unconditional.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransformSheaf_comp_blowUp (f : X ⟶ S) (I K : S.IdealSheafData)
    (J : (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp I).IdealSheafData)
    (hK : K.supportSet = I.supportSet ∪
      (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I).base '' J.supportSet)
    (e : Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) ≅
      Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K))
    (F : X.Modules) :
    let b := AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I
    let f₁ : baseChange f b ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp I := pullback.snd f b
    let c := AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J
    let d := AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K
    let pK := pullback.fst f d
    let pI := pullback.fst f b
    let pJ := pullback.fst f₁ c
    let FK := (Scheme.Modules.pullback pK).obj F
    let FI := (Scheme.Modules.pullback pI).obj F
    let QK := sheaf f d (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal K) F
    let QI := sheaf f b (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I) F
    let QJ := sheaf f₁ c (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal J) QI
    ∃ (g : baseChange f₁ c ≅ baseChange f d) (hg : g.hom ≫ pK = pJ ≫ pI),
      (g.hom ≫ pullback.snd f d = pullback.snd f₁ c ≫ e.hom.left) ∧
      ∃ s : (Scheme.Modules.pullback g.hom).obj QK ≅ QJ,
        let t : (Scheme.Modules.pullback g.hom).obj FK ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback pJ).obj FI :=
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g.hom pK).app F) ≪≫
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hg).app F) ≪≫
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp pJ pI).symm.app F)
        let qK : FK ⟶ QK := π f d (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal K) F
        let qI : FI ⟶ QI := π f b (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I) F
        let qJ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback pJ).obj QI ⟶ QJ :=
          π f₁ c (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal J) QI
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g.hom).map qK ≫ s.hom =
          t.hom ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullback pJ).map qI ≫ qJ
declarations.comment: part (1): strict transform of a module

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.strictTransform_comp_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 080I] part (2).** For `b` the blowup of `S` in `I`, `c` the blowup of the
blowup in `J`, and `d` the blowup of `S` in a third centre `K` whose support is
`Supp I ∪ b(Supp J)`, the strict transform along `c` of the strict transform of `X` along `b`
agrees with the strict transform of `X` along `d`, compatibly with both projections.

Unconditional: the support identity is
`Stacks.StrictTransform.iso_preimage_exceptionalPreimage_blowUp` and the open immersion away from
the second exceptional divisor is
`Stacks.StrictTransform.isOpenImmersion_exceptionalComplement_ι_comp_fst`, both of which are
theorems now that [Stacks, Tag 02OS] part (1) is the instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_blowUpToBase_restrict_compl_support`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransform_comp_blowUp (f : X ⟶ S) (I K : S.IdealSheafData)
    (J : (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp I).IdealSheafData)
    (hK : K.supportSet = I.supportSet ∪
      (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I).base '' J.supportSet)
    (e : Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) ≅
      Over.mk (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K)) :
    let X₁ := scheme f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I) (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I)
    let f₁ : X₁ ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp I :=
      (ideal f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I)).subschemeι ≫
        pullback.snd f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)
    ∃ g : scheme f₁ (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J) (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal J) ≅
        scheme f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K) (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal K),
      (g.hom ≫ (ideal f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal K)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.fst f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K) =
        (ideal f₁ (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal J)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.fst f₁ (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J) ≫
          (ideal f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal I)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.fst f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase I)) ∧
      (g.hom ≫ (ideal f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal K)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.snd f (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase K) =
        (ideal f₁ (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal J)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.snd f₁ (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase J) ≫ e.hom.left)
declarations.comment: part (2): strict transform of a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` is a **`U`-admissible blowup** if there is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals `I` on `X` whose closed subscheme is of finite presentation over `X` and supported away
from `U`, together with an isomorphism of `X'` with the blowup of `X` in `I` carrying the blowup
morphism to `f`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleBlowup (U : X.Opens) (f : X' ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080L.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and
`U ⊆ X` an open subscheme. If `b : X' ⟶ X` is a `U`-admissible blowup and `b' : X'' ⟶ X'` is a
`b⁻¹(U)`-admissible blowup, then the composite `b' ≫ b : X'' ⟶ X` is a `U`-admissible blowup.

The single centre is the product of the first centre with the second-centre ideal of
`Stacks.Blowup.exists_secondCentre`, and the two halves of [Stacks, Tag 080B] do the rest. The
support clause that `…comp_of_secondCentreIdeal` asks for comes from
`AlgebraicGeometry.supportSet_mul_eq_union_image` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_mul`: the support of the product centre is the
support of the first centre together with the image of the support of the second, and it
contains the support of `J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAdmissibleBlowup.comp [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U : X.Opens) (b : X' ⟶ X) (b' : X'' ⟶ X')
    (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup U b) (hb' : IsAdmissibleBlowup (b ⁻¹ᵁ U) b') :
    IsAdmissibleBlowup U (b' ≫ b)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_admissibleBlowup_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080M.** A blowup admissible over the intersection of two quasi-compact
opens extends to a blowup of the ambient scheme admissible over the first open, with its
restriction to the second open given by a cartesian square.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_isPullback
    {X V' : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U V : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X)) (b : V' ⟶ V.toScheme)
    (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ U) b) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup U f ∧ ∃ g : V' ⟶ X', IsPullback b g V.ι f

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_admissibleBlowup_dominating
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080N.** Let `U` be an open subscheme of a scheme `X` and let
`b_i : Y_i ⟶ X`, `i ∈ ι`, be a finite family of `U`-admissible blowups. There is a `U`-admissible
blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` which factors through every `b_i`, with each factor map `X' ⟶ Y_i` itself a
`b_i⁻¹(U)`-admissible blowup.

Take `X'` to be the blowup of `X` in the product `I = ∏ I_i` of the centres. The product is again
of finite type and supported away from `U`, so `b` is `U`-admissible. Writing `I = I_i · J_i`,
blowing up a product is blowing up the factors in succession (Stacks tag 080A), so `X'` is the
blowup of `Y_i` in the inverse image of `J_i`; flat base change along the isomorphism
`Y_i ≅ Bl_{I_i}(X)` (Stacks tag 0805) identifies that inverse image taken on `Y_i` with the one
taken on `Bl_{I_i}(X)`. The inverse image of `J_i` on `Y_i` is again of finite type and supported
away from `b_i⁻¹(U)`, so the factor map is `b_i⁻¹(U)`-admissible.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_dominating {X : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.Opens)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ X)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsAdmissibleBlowup U (f i)) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ X),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup U b ∧
        ∃ g : ∀ i, X' ⟶ Y i,
          (∀ i, g i ≫ f i = b) ∧
            (∀ i, IsAdmissibleBlowup (f i ⁻¹ᵁ U) (g i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_admissibleBlowup_disjoint_open_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080P.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`U, V` be disjoint quasi-compact open subschemes of `X`. Then there is a `U ∪ V`-admissible
blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` such that `X'` is the disjoint union of two open subschemes `X' = X'₁ ⨿ X'₂`
with `b⁻¹(U) ⊆ X'₁` and `b⁻¹(V) ⊆ X'₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_disjoint_open_cover
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U V : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X)) (hUV : Disjoint U V) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ X) (U₁ U₂ : X'.Opens),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup (U ⊔ V) b ∧
        Disjoint U₁ U₂ ∧ U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤ ∧
          b ⁻¹ᵁ U ≤ U₁ ∧ b ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ U₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_admissibleBlowup_pairwise_disjoint_open_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080P for a finite family.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme and let `U_i`, `i ∈ ι`, be a finite family of pairwise disjoint
quasi-compact open subschemes of `X`. Then there is a `⋃ U_i`-admissible blowup `b : X' ⟶ X`
such that `X'` is the disjoint union of open subschemes `X'_i`, `i ∈ ι`, with
`b⁻¹(U_i) ⊆ X'_i`.

This is the form in which the source iterates Tag 080P: the decomposition of `U` into the
finitely many loci where a locally constant invariant takes a fixed value is separated by a
single blowup. The proof is that of the two-piece case verbatim. Choose quasi-coherent sheaves
of ideals `ℐ_i` of finite type with `X ∖ U_i = V(ℐ_i)` and blow up `∑ ℐ_i`; the piece `X'_i` is
the union of the affine charts of Stacks tag 0804 attached to the sections of `ℐ_i`. Two such
pieces are disjoint because `ℐ_iℐ_j` is contained in the nilradical for `i ≠ j`, and they cover
because over an affine open every section of `(∑ ℐ_i)(W)` is a sum of sections of the
`ℐ_i(W)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_pairwise_disjoint_open_cover
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : ∀ i, IsCompact (U i : Set X))
    (hUd : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (U i) (U j)) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ X) (V : ι → X'.Opens),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup (⨆ i, U i) b ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (V i) (V j)) ∧ ⨆ i, V i = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i, b ⁻¹ᵁ U i ≤ V i
declarations.comment: stated for a finite family of pairwise disjoint quasi-compact opens; the source's two-piece statement is the case of a two-element index type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_iso_free_over_of_flat_over_at_of_flat_fiber_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080Q.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of finite presentation and let
`F` be a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module. If `F` is flat over `S` at `x` and the stalk at `x` of
the restriction of `F` to the fibre of `f` through `x` is a flat module over the local ring of
that fibre, then `F` is free of finite rank on an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_free_over_of_flat_over_at_of_flat_fiber_stalk {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (x : X)
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt (Scheme.Hom.toLRSHom f).toShHom F x)
    (hfiber :
      letI := Stacks.Flatness.stalkModule
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F) (f.asFiber x)
      Module.Flat (ToType ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x)))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F).val.presheaf (f.asFiber x)))) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ n : ℕ,
      Nonempty (F.over U ≅ SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))

declarations.name: Matrix.fromRows_mul_adjugate
declarations.doc: **Stacks 080R.**
declarations.statement:
theorem fromRows_mul_adjugate (A₁ : Matrix m m R) (A₂ : Matrix p m R) :
    fromRows A₁ A₂ * adjugate A₁ =
      fromRows (A₁.det • (1 : Matrix m m R))
        (Matrix.of fun (i : p) (j : m) => (A₁.updateRow j (A₂ i)).det)

declarations.name: Matrix.fromRows_mul_adjugate_apply_inr
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 080R**, identifying the bottom block's entries as `m × m` minors of the stacked
matrix — with no sign, taking the rows in the order `1, …, ĵ, …, m` with `i` at slot `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fromRows_mul_adjugate_apply_inr (A₁ : Matrix m m R)
    (A₂ : Matrix p m R) (i : p) (j : m) :
    (fromRows A₁ A₂ * adjugate A₁) (Sum.inr i) j =
      ((fromRows A₁ A₂).submatrix (Function.update Sum.inl j (Sum.inr i)) id).det

declarations.name: ab_top_block
declarations.doc:
**Top block.** With `B = adj(A₁)` and `f = det(A₁)`, the top `m × m` block of
`A * B` is `f • 1`: for all row/column indices `i, j` in the top block,
`(A * B)_{i j} = f · δ_{i j}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab_top_block (hmn : m₀ + 1 ≤ n) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin (m₀ + 1)) R)
    (i j : Fin (m₀ + 1)) :
    (A * (topBlock hmn A).adjugate) (Fin.castLE hmn i) j
      = (topBlock hmn A).det • (1 : Matrix (Fin (m₀ + 1)) (Fin (m₀ + 1)) R) i j
declarations.comment: top block

declarations.name: ab_bottom_block
declarations.doc:
**Bottom block.** With `B = adj(A₁)`, for a row index `i` lying in the bottom
block (i.e. `m ≤ i`, here `m₀ + 1 ≤ i`) and any column index `j`,
`(A * B)_{i j} = (-1)^{m - j} · det(M_{i j})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab_bottom_block (hmn : m₀ + 1 ≤ n) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin (m₀ + 1)) R)
    (i : Fin n) (j : Fin (m₀ + 1)) :
    (A * (topBlock hmn A).adjugate) i j
      = (-1) ^ (m₀ - (j : ℕ)) * (minorMat hmn A i j).det
declarations.comment: bottom block

declarations.name: generalizingMap_suppMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 080T (topological formulation).** If `N` is a finite `S`-module that is
flat over `R`, then generalizations lift along `π : Supp(N) → Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizingMap_suppMap [Module.Finite S N] [Module.Flat R N] :
    GeneralizingMap (suppMap (R := R) (S := S) (N := N))

declarations.name: AffineBlowup.fImage_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc: If `a ∈ I` and `V(f) = V(I)`, then the image of `f` in `R' = R[I/a]` is a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem fImage_mem_nonZeroDivisors (ha : a ∈ I) (f : R)
    (hf : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ({f} : Set R) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R)) :
    fImage I a f ∈ nonZeroDivisors (Rprime I a)
declarations.comment: f nonzerodivisor in R'

declarations.name: AffineBlowup.blowup_localization_f_iso_a
declarations.doc:
Assume `a ∈ I` and `V(f) = V(I)`. Let `R'f` be a localization of `R' = R[I/a]` away from
the image of `f`, and `R'a` a localization of `R'` away from the image of `a`. Then `R'f` is also
a localization of `R'` away from the image of `a`, and `R'f ≃ₐ[R] R'a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowup_localization_f_iso_a (ha : a ∈ I) (f : R)
    (hf : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ({f} : Set R) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))
    (R'f R'a : Type*) [CommRing R'f] [CommRing R'a]
    [Algebra (Rprime I a) R'f] [Algebra (Rprime I a) R'a]
    [Algebra R R'f] [Algebra R R'a]
    [IsScalarTower R (Rprime I a) R'f] [IsScalarTower R (Rprime I a) R'a]
    [IsLocalization.Away (fImage I a f) R'f]
    [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R (Rprime I a) a) R'a] :
    IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R (Rprime I a) a) R'f ∧
      Nonempty (R'f ≃ₐ[R] R'a)
declarations.comment: R'_f = R'_a

declarations.name: AffineBlowup.ringLocalization_a_iso_blowup_localization_a
declarations.doc:
Let `R'a` be a localization of `R' = R[I/a]` away from the image of `a`, and `Ra'` a
localization of `R` away from `a`. Then the canonical map `R_a → R'_a` induced by `R → R'` is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringLocalization_a_iso_blowup_localization_a
    (R'a Ra' : Type*) [CommRing R'a] [CommRing Ra']
    [Algebra (Rprime I a) R'a] [Algebra R Ra'] [Algebra R R'a]
    [IsScalarTower R (Rprime I a) R'a]
    [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R (Rprime I a) a) R'a]
    [IsLocalization.Away a Ra'] :
    Function.Bijective
      (IsLocalization.Away.map Ra' R'a (algebraMap R (Rprime I a)) a)
declarations.comment: R'_a = R_a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_epi_isIso_restrict
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a quasi-coherent module of finite type on a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme
`X` whose restriction to a quasi-compact open `U` is of finite presentation.  Then there is a
morphism `φ : G ⟶ F` with `G` of finite presentation, `φ` surjective, and `φ|_U` an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_epi_isIso_restrict [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact U.1)
    [(F.restrict U.ι).IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (_ : G.IsFinitePresentation) (φ : G ⟶ F),
      Epi φ ∧ IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformSheaf_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080W.** A short exact sequence of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules which
remains short exact after every base change of the base scheme `S` has short exact strict
transforms along the blowup of `S` in any quasi-coherent ideal, with the three maps determined
by the quotient maps onto the strict transforms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransformSheaf_shortExact {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (I : S.IdealSheafData) (C : ShortComplex X.Modules)
    [C.X₁.IsQuasicoherent] [C.X₂.IsQuasicoherent] [C.X₃.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hC : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
      (C.map (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g))).ShortExact) :
    let b := blowUpToBase I
    let E := exceptionalIdeal I
    let p := pullback.fst f b
    let F₁ := (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj C.X₁
    let F₂ := (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj C.X₂
    let F₃ := (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj C.X₃
    let q₁ : F₁ ⟶ Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₁ := Stacks.StrictTransform.π f b E C.X₁
    let q₂ : F₂ ⟶ Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₂ := Stacks.StrictTransform.π f b E C.X₂
    let q₃ : F₃ ⟶ Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₃ := Stacks.StrictTransform.π f b E C.X₃
    ∃ (f' : Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₁ ⟶ Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₂)
      (g' : Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₂ ⟶ Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f b E C.X₃)
      (w : f' ≫ g' = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk f' g' w).ShortExact ∧
        (q₁ ≫ f' = (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).map C.f ≫ q₂) ∧
        (q₂ ≫ g' = (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).map C.g ≫ q₃)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_forall_restrict_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080Y**, the locality on `S` of Remark 38.30.1, for a finite family of
quasi-compact opens. Let `S` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `U ⊆ S` a quasi-compact open,
and let `W j ⊆ S` be finitely many quasi-compact opens carrying `W j ∩ U`-admissible blowups
`c j : V j ⟶ W j`. There is one `U`-admissible blowup `p : S' ⟶ S` whose restriction to each
`W j` factors through `c j`.

Each `c j` extends to a `U`-admissible blowup `q j : T j ⟶ S` with `IsPullback (c j) _ (W j).ι
(q j)` by [Stacks, Tag 080M], and [Stacks, Tag 080N] produces a `U`-admissible `p : S' ⟶ S`
factoring through every `q j` by a `q j ⁻¹ᵁ U`-admissible blowup `k j`. The restriction
`p ∣_ W j` and the composite `(p ⁻¹ᵁ W j).ι ≫ k j` agree over `S`, so the cartesian square of
[Stacks, Tag 080M] lifts them to the required map `r` to `V j`; and `r` is the base change of
`k j` along the flat `g j`, hence admissible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_forall_restrict_factors
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (W : ι → S.Opens) (hW : ∀ j, IsCompact ((W j : S.Opens) : Set S))
    (V : ι → Scheme.{u}) (c : ∀ j, V j ⟶ (W j).toScheme)
    (hc : ∀ j, Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup ((W j).ι ⁻¹ᵁ U) (c j)) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (p : S' ⟶ S), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U p ∧
      ∀ j, ∃ r : (p ⁻¹ᵁ W j).toScheme ⟶ V j, r ≫ c j = p ∣_ (W j) ∧
        Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup (c j ⁻¹ᵁ ((W j).ι ⁻¹ᵁ U)) r
declarations.comment: locality on S: finitely many admissible blowups of quasi-compact opens of S are all refined by the restrictions of a single U-admissible blowup of S, each refinement itself an admissible blowup of the local solution

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_finite_cover_restrict_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080Y**, the locality on `S` of Remark 38.30.1 in the paragraph's own
formulation. Let `S` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `U ⊆ S` a quasi-compact open.
Suppose that every point `s` of `S` has a quasi-compact open neighbourhood `W s` carrying a
`W s ∩ U`-admissible blowup `c s : V s ⟶ W s`. Then there is a finite set of points whose
neighbourhoods already cover `S`, and one `U`-admissible blowup `p : S' ⟶ S` whose restriction
to each of those neighbourhoods factors through the blowup given there.

The finite set comes from quasi-compactness of `S`, the blowup from
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_forall_restrict_factors` applied to the finite
subfamily.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_finite_cover_restrict_factors
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (W : S → S.Opens) (hWmem : ∀ s : S, s ∈ W s)
    (hW : ∀ s : S, IsCompact ((W s : S.Opens) : Set S))
    (V : S → Scheme.{u}) (c : ∀ s : S, V s ⟶ (W s).toScheme)
    (hc : ∀ s : S, Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup ((W s).ι ⁻¹ᵁ U) (c s)) :
    ∃ (F : Finset S) (S' : Scheme.{u}) (p : S' ⟶ S),
      (∀ x : S, ∃ s ∈ F, x ∈ W s) ∧ Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U p ∧
        ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ r : (p ⁻¹ᵁ W s).toScheme ⟶ V s, r ≫ c s = p ∣_ (W s) ∧
          Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup (c s ⁻¹ᵁ ((W s).ι ⁻¹ᵁ U)) r
declarations.comment: locality on S: a solution on a quasi-compact open neighbourhood of every point of S is refined, over a finite subcover, by the restrictions of a single U-admissible blowup of S, each refinement itself an admissible blowup of the local solution

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierBoundaryDivisorReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080Y**, the reduction to a divisor of Remark 38.30.1 in full. On a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme `S` a quasi-compact open `U` becomes, after a single
`U`-admissible blowup, the complement of an effective Cartier divisor `D` supported on the
boundary; and then `U` is scheme theoretically dense.

The centre is the one of `AlgebraicGeometry.cartierBoundaryReduction`, and `D` is the
exceptional divisor of its blowup: an effective Cartier divisor by [Stacks, Tag 02OS] part (2)
(`Stacks.Blowup.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalIdeal`), whose support is the boundary by
that theorem. The density is then [Stacks, Tag 07ZU]
(`Stacks.Divisors.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`): the
complement of an effective Cartier divisor is scheme theoretically dense.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cartierBoundaryDivisorReduction [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S)) : CartierBoundaryDivisorReduction S U
declarations.comment: the reduction to a divisor: after one U-admissible blowup the boundary is an effective Cartier divisor whose complement is the inverse image of U, and that inverse image is scheme theoretically dense

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierBoundaryReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 080Y.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme `S`, a
quasi-compact open `U` becomes the complement of an effective Cartier divisor after a single
`U`-admissible blowup: a finite type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf `I` cutting out `S ∖ U` is
finitely presented as a closed subscheme, is disjoint from `U`, and the exceptional divisor of
the blowup of `S` in `I` is exactly the complement of the inverse image of `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cartierBoundaryReduction [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens)
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S)) : CartierBoundaryReduction S U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StrictTransformProblem.isSolvable_of_local
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 080Y], the local-global reduction.** Suppose the property `P` is local on the
base: for every strict-transform problem with that property, if the base is covered by finitely
many quasi-compact opens over each of which the restricted triple has `P`, then the triple itself
has `P`. Then the strict-transform problem is local on the base too: if every point of `S` has a
quasi-compact open neighbourhood over which the problem is solvable, the problem is solvable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSolvable_of_local (D : StrictTransformProblem.{u})
    (hP : ∀ E : StrictTransformProblem.{u}, @E.P = @D.P →
      ∀ {ι : Type} [Finite ι] (W : ι → E.S.Opens) (hW : ∀ i, IsCompact (W i : Set E.S)),
        (⋃ i, (W i : Set E.S)) = Set.univ →
        (∀ i, (E.restrict (W i) (hW i)).P (E.restrict (W i) (hW i)).f
          (E.restrict (W i) (hW i)).F) →
        E.P E.f E.F)
    (hlocal : ∀ s : D.S, ∃ (W : D.S.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set D.S)),
      s ∈ (W : Set D.S) ∧ (D.restrict W hW).IsSolvable) :
    D.IsSolvable
declarations.comment: the local-global reduction, the remark's third paragraph; the locality of P on the base is the hypothesis the remark states it under

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StrictTransformProblem.isSolvable_of_isSolvableIn
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 080Y], the successive reduction.** To solve the strict-transform problem it
suffices to find a *sequence* of `U`-admissible blowups `S = S₀ ← S₁ ← … ← Sₙ` whose iterated
strict transform has the property `P`: such a sequence is replaced by a single `U`-admissible
blowup with the same effect.

The sequence is contracted one stage at a time: the amalgamation of [Stacks, Tag 080B], fed by
the second-centre factorization of [Stacks, Tag 0803], replaces the last two centres by a single
admissible centre on the previous base, and [Stacks, Tag 080I] identifies the iterated strict
transform with the strict transform in it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSolvable_of_isSolvableIn (n : ℕ) (D : StrictTransformProblem.{u})
    (h : D.IsSolvableIn n) : D.IsSolvable
declarations.comment: the successive reduction, the paragraph beginning `The general strategy will be to use that a composition of U-admissible blowups is a U-admissible blowup': it suffices to find a sequence of U-admissible blowups S = S_0 <- S_1 <- ... <- S_n such that, setting F_0 = F and X_0 = X and F_i/X_i the strict transform of F_{i-1}/X_{i-1}, the triple F_n/X_n/S_n has P. The sequence is IsSolvableIn n and the single blowup it is replaced by is IsSolvable

declarations.name: exists_fin_generating_family_quotient_ker_lsmul_of_fittingIdeal_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
If the `k`th Fitting ideal of a finite module over a local ring is generated
by `f`, then the quotient by the submodule of elements annihilated by `f` is generated by `k`
elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_generating_family_quotient_ker_lsmul_of_fittingIdeal_eq_span_singleton
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) (f : R)
    (h : fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) = Ideal.span {f}) :
    ∃ g : Fin k → M ⧸ LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul R M f),
      Submodule.span R (Set.range g) = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_idealSheafData_forall_blowUp_exists_free_of_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0810.** Let `S` be an affine scheme, `s : Γ(S, ⊤)`, `r ≥ 0` an integer,
`f : X ⟶ S` an affine morphism and `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Assume

1. `f` is of finite presentation and flat with geometrically integral fibres;
2. `F` is of finite type;
3. `F` restricted to `f⁻¹(D(s))` is of finite presentation;
4. for every point `x` of `X` which is generic in its fibre and whose image lies in `D(s)`, the
   stalk `F_x` is free of rank `r` over `𝒪_{X,x}`.

Then there is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ` on `S` whose ideal of global sections is
finitely generated and whose support is `V(s)`, such that over every point `z` of the blowup
`Bl_ℐ(S)` there is a point of `X ×_S Bl_ℐ(S)` above `z` with an open neighbourhood on which the
strict transform of `F` is free of rank `r`.

This is the geometric reading of the ring-level
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fg_ideal_forall_blowup_chart_exists_away_basis`: hypotheses (1)–(4) are
converted into its hypotheses on `Γ(S, ⊤) → Γ(X, ⊤)` and `Γ(F, ⊤)`, and its conclusion — the
`a`-power-torsion quotient of the base change becomes free of rank `r` after inverting one
element per prime of each affine blowup chart — is carried onto the sheaf-level strict transform
by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_free_open_of_chart_at`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_idealSheafData_forall_blowUp_exists_free_of_rank
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom f] [Flat f]
    [GeometricallyIntegral f] (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (s : Γ(S, ⊤)) (r : ℕ)
    (hFU : (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ S.basicOpen s).ι).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hrank : ∀ x : X, f.base x ∈ S.basicOpen s → f.base ⁻¹' {f.base x} ⊆ closure {x} →
      letI := Stacks.ModuleStalkSpecialization.stalkModule F x
      Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin r) (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x))) :
    ∃ ℐ : S.IdealSheafData,
      (ℐ.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top S⟩).FG ∧
      (ℐ.support : Set S) = (↑(S.basicOpen s))ᶜ ∧
      ∀ z : Stacks.Blowup.blowUp ℐ,
        ∃ (W : (Limits.pullback f (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase ℐ)).Opens)
          (x : ↥(Limits.pullback f (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase ℐ))),
          x ∈ W ∧ (pullback.snd f (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase ℐ)).base x = z ∧
          Nonempty ((Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase ℐ)
            (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdeal ℐ) F).restrict W.ι ≅
              SheafOfModules.free.{u} (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))
declarations.comment: the scheme-level form

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictTransform.exists_fg_ideal_forall_chartFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0810, read on the strict transform.** Let `S` be an affine scheme, `X`
an affine scheme over it with `Γ(S, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` flat and of finite presentation with
geometrically integral fibres, let `F` be a quasi-coherent module on `X` presented as `M^~` with
`M` finite over `Γ(X, ⊤)`, let `t : Γ(S, ⊤)` and `r : ℕ`, and assume `M` is finitely presented
after inverting `t` and free of rank `r` at every extended prime `qΓ(X, ⊤)` with `t ∉ q`. Then
there is a finitely generated ideal `I ⊆ Γ(S, ⊤)` with `V(t) = V(I)` such that for every `a ∈ I`
and every prime `q'` of the affine blowup algebra `Γ(S, ⊤)[I/a]`, the chart
`Spec (Γ(X, ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(S,⊤)} Γ(S, ⊤)[I/a])` of a base change satisfies
`Stacks.StrictTransform.ChartFreeOfRank` for the image of `a` and the extension of `q'`: on every
such chart on which the inverse image of the centre is the zero locus of the image of `a`, the
strict transform of `F` of [Stacks, Tag 080D] is free of rank `r` on a basic open `D(g)` with `g`
outside `q'·(Γ(X, ⊤) ⊗ Γ(S, ⊤)[I/a])`.

This is the scheme-level form of the ring-level
`exists_fg_ideal_forall_blowup_chart_exists_away_basis`: the ideal, the chart algebras and the
element `g` are the ring-level ones, and the module the ring-level statement produces a basis for
is identified with the strict transform by `Stacks.StrictTransform.affineChartSheafIso`, through
`Stacks.StrictTransform.nonempty_restrict_basicOpen_free_of_basis`. It is the form the proof of
[Stacks, Tag 0811] consumes, which is about the strict transform and not about the chart-level
torsion quotient: freeness of the strict transform near the generic point of a fibre of
`X ×_S Bl_I(S) ⟶ Bl_I(S)` is the flatness conjunct of
`AlgebraicGeometry.GenericFibreFlatteningBlowup`.

The charts are universally quantified inside `Stacks.StrictTransform.ChartFreeOfRank`: nothing is
claimed here about their existence, which is the content of [Stacks, Tag 0804] for the blowup of
`S` in `I` together with the base change of that covering along `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_ideal_forall_chartFreeOfRank [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (M : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤))
    (e : F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom).obj (tilde M))
    [Algebra Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (halg : (algebraMap Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) : Γ(S, ⊤) →+* Γ(X, ⊤)) = f.appTop.hom)
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)] [Module.Flat Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)]
    [Module.Finite Γ(X, ⊤) M] (t : Γ(S, ⊤)) (r : ℕ)
    (hfibre : ∀ (q : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤)) (hq : q.IsPrime),
      letI := hq
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral q.ResidueField (q.Fiber Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (hfp : Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (algebraMap Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) t))
      (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) t)) M))
    (hrank : ∀ (q : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤)) (hq : q.IsPrime), t ∉ q →
      letI := hq
      let 𝔮 := Ideal.map (algebraMap Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)) q
      ∀ h𝔮 : 𝔮.IsPrime,
        letI := h𝔮
        Nonempty (LocalizedModule 𝔮.primeCompl M ≃ₗ[Localization 𝔮.primeCompl]
          (Fin r → Localization 𝔮.primeCompl))) :
    ∃ I : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤), I.FG ∧
      (∀ q : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤), q.IsPrime → (t ∈ q ↔ I ≤ q)) ∧
      ∀ (a : Γ(S, ⊤)) (ha : a ∈ I),
        letI : Fact (a ∈ I) := ⟨ha⟩
        ∀ q' : Ideal (Blowup I a), q'.IsPrime →
          ChartFreeOfRank f F (CommRingCat.of (Γ(X, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, ⊤)] Blowup I a))
            (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) (Γ(X, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, ⊤)] Blowup I a)))
            (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) (Γ(X, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, ⊤)] Blowup I a) (f.appTop.hom a)) r
            (Ideal.map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight q')
declarations.comment: the conclusion read on the strict transform of [Stacks, Tag 080D]: on every affine chart of a base change on which the inverse image of the centre is the zero locus of the image of the chart's denominator, the strict transform of the module is free of rank r on a basic open through every extended prime of the chart base. The hypotheses are the source's own, read on the global sections of the two affine schemes; the existence of such charts is not claimed

declarations.name: exists_fg_ideal_forall_blowup_chart_exists_away_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0810.** Let `R → S` be flat and of finite presentation with
geometrically integral fibres, let `f : R`, and let `M` be a finite `S`-module which is finitely
presented after inverting `f` and free of rank `r` at every extended prime `pS` with `f ∉ p`.
Then there is a finitely generated ideal `I ⊆ R` with `V(f) = V(I)` such that for every `a ∈ I`,
writing `R' = R[I/a]` and `S' = S ⊗[R] R'`, the quotient `M'` of `S' ⊗[S] M` by its `a`-power
torsion is free of rank `r` after inverting some `g : S'` outside `p'S'`, for every prime `p'` of
`R'`.

This is `exists_fg_ideal_forall_blowup_chart_exists_away_basis_of_projective` with its hypothesis
`Module.Projective R S` supplied by Stacks 05FT,
`Algebra.projective_of_geometricallyIntegral_fibres`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_ideal_forall_blowup_chart_exists_away_basis
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] (f : R) (r : ℕ)
    (hfibre : ∀ (p : Ideal R) (hp : p.IsPrime),
      letI := hp
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral p.ResidueField (p.Fiber S))
    (hfp : Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S f))
      (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R S f)) M))
    (hrank : ∀ (p : Ideal R) (hp : p.IsPrime), f ∉ p →
      letI := hp
      let q := Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) p
      ∀ hq : q.IsPrime,
        letI := hq
        Nonempty
          (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl M ≃ₗ[Localization q.primeCompl]
            (Fin r → Localization q.primeCompl))) :
    ∃ I : Ideal R, I.FG ∧
      (∀ (p : Ideal R), p.IsPrime → (f ∈ p ↔ I ≤ p)) ∧
      ∀ (a : R) (ha : a ∈ I),
        letI : Fact (a ∈ I) := ⟨ha⟩
        let R' := Blowup I a
        let S' := S ⊗[R] R'
        let N := S' ⊗[S] M
        let M' := N ⧸ Submodule.torsion' S' N
          (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap S S' (algebraMap R S a)))
        ∀ (p' : Ideal R') (_hp' : p'.IsPrime), ∃ g : S',
          g ∉ Ideal.map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight p' ∧
          Nonempty
            (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) M' ≃ₗ[Localization.Away g]
              (Fin r → Localization.Away g))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_opens_finitelyLocallyFree_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0811.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `U ⊆ S` be a
quasi-compact open. Assume

1. `f` is affine, of finite presentation, flat, with geometrically integral fibres;
2. `F` is of finite type;
3. `F` restricted to `X_U` is of finite presentation;
4. `F` is flat over `S` at every generic point of a fibre over a point of `U`.

Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup of `S` — given by a centre `I` of finite presentation whose
support avoids `U` — and an open subscheme `V` of `X ×_S Bl_I(S)` such that

* **(a)** the strict transform of `F` along the blowup is free of finite rank on an open
  neighbourhood, inside `V`, of every point of `V`, that is, finitely locally free on `V`, and
* **(b)** `V` surjects onto `Bl_I(S)`.

The rank at the generic point of a fibre over `U` is made constant by iterating
[Stacks, Tag 080P]; the complement of `U` is made an effective Cartier divisor and then, locally
on the base, principal on an affine open, by the observations of [Stacks, Tag 080Y]; and that case
is [Stacks, Tag 0810].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_opens_finitelyLocallyFree_surjective
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffineHom f] [Flat f] [GeometricallyIntegral f]
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (U : S.Opens)
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (hFU : (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : ∀ x : X, f.base x ∈ U → f.base ⁻¹' {f.base x} ⊆ closure {x} →
      IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (U : Set S) (I.support : Set S) ∧
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase I) ∧
      ∃ V : (Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange f (blowUpToBase I)).Opens,
        (∀ z : Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange f (blowUpToBase I), z ∈ V →
          ∃ (W : (Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange f (blowUpToBase I)).Opens) (n : ℕ),
            z ∈ W ∧ W ≤ V ∧
            Nonempty ((Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (blowUpToBase I)
              (exceptionalIdeal I) F).restrict W.ι ≅
                SheafOfModules.free.{u} (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))) ∧
        Function.Surjective (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f (blowUpToBase I)).base
declarations.comment: the full statement under hypotheses (1)-(4) of the source: a U-admissible blowup and an open of the base change on which the strict transform is finitely locally free and which surjects onto the blowup

declarations.name: fittingIdealZero_quotient_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0812.** The zeroth Fitting ideal of a quotient of a finite
projective algebra by a finitely generated ideal is finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdealZero_quotient_fg
    (A : Type u) (C : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [Module.Finite A C] [Module.Projective A C] (J : Ideal C) (hJ : J.FG) :
    (fittingIdeal (R := A) (M := C ⧸ J) 0).FG
declarations.comment: finite generation of the Fitting ideal

declarations.name: map_fittingIdealZero_quotient_eq_mul_of_etale_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0812.** Let `C` be a finite locally free `A`-algebra and let `J` be
an ideal of `C`. If `C` becomes étale over `A` after inverting `h`, then the extension of
the zeroth Fitting ideal of `C ⧸ J` is the product of the extension of `J` with another
ideal. This other ideal can be chosen finitely generated whenever `J` is finitely
generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_fittingIdealZero_quotient_eq_mul_of_etale_away
    (A : Type u) (C : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [Module.Finite A C] [Module.Projective A C] (h : C)
    (het : Algebra.Etale A (Localization.Away h)) (J : Ideal C) :
    ∃ J' : Ideal (Localization.Away h),
      (fittingIdeal (R := A) (M := C ⧸ J) 0).map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away h)) =
          J.map (algebraMap C (Localization.Away h)) * J' ∧
        (J.FG → J'.FG)
declarations.comment: factorization after localization

declarations.name: exists_ideal_map_eq_mul_after_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0813.** Let `A → B` be étale, let `a ∈ A`, and let `J` be a
finitely generated ideal of `B` with `V(J) ⊆ V(aB)`. At every prime `q` of `B`,
after localizing at some `g ∉ q`, the extension of a finitely generated ideal
`I` of `A`, with `V(I) ⊆ V(a)`, is the product of the extension of `J` and a
finitely generated ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_map_eq_mul_after_localization
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Algebra.Etale A B] (a : A) (J : Ideal B) (hJ : J.FG)
    (hV : algebraMap A B a ∈ J.radical) (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, I.FG ∧ a ∈ I.radical ∧
      ∃ g : B, g ∉ q ∧
        ∃ J' : Ideal (Localization.Away g), J'.FG ∧
          Ideal.map ((algebraMap B (Localization.Away g)).comp (algebraMap A B)) I =
            Ideal.map (algebraMap B (Localization.Away g)) J * J'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFlatOver_strictTransformSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0814.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `U ⊆ S` be
a quasi-compact open. Assume given finitely many commutative squares `jᵢ ≫ f = fᵢ ≫ eᵢ` with

1. `eᵢ : Sᵢ ⟶ S` quasi-compact and étale,
