2. `jᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ X` étale and jointly surjective,
3. a centre `Iᵢ` on `Sᵢ` which is finitely presented as a closed subscheme and supported away
   from `eᵢ⁻¹(U)` — so the blowup of `Sᵢ` in `Iᵢ` is an `eᵢ⁻¹(U)`-admissible blowup — such that
   the strict transform of `jᵢ^* F` along it is flat over it.

Then there is a centre `I` on `S`, finitely presented and supported away from `U`, exhibiting the
blowup of `S` in `I` as a `U`-admissible blowup, such that the strict transform of `F` along that
blowup is flat over it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFlatOver_strictTransformSheaf {S X : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S)) {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (Sᵢ Xᵢ : ι → Scheme.{u}) (e : ∀ i, Sᵢ i ⟶ S) (j : ∀ i, Xᵢ i ⟶ X)
    (fᵢ : ∀ i, Xᵢ i ⟶ Sᵢ i) (Iᵢ : ∀ i, (Sᵢ i).IdealSheafData)
    (he : ∀ i, Etale (e i) ∧ QuasiCompact (e i)) (hj : ∀ i, Etale (j i))
    (hcoverX : ∀ x : X, ∃ i : ι, ∃ y : Xᵢ i, (j i).base y = x)
    (hcomm : ∀ i, j i ≫ f = fᵢ i ≫ e i)
    (hadm : ∀ i, FinitePresentation (Iᵢ i).subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (e i ⁻¹ᵁ U : Set (Sᵢ i)) ((Iᵢ i).support : Set (Sᵢ i)))
    (hflat : ∀ i, IsFlatOver
      (pullback.snd (fᵢ i) (blowUpToBase (Iᵢ i))).toLRSHom.toShHom
      (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf (fᵢ i) (blowUpToBase (Iᵢ i)) (exceptionalIdeal (Iᵢ i))
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (j i)).obj F))) :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (U : Set S) (I.support : Set S) ∧
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase I) ∧
      IsFlatOver (pullback.snd f (blowUpToBase I)).toLRSHom.toShHom
        (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I) F)
declarations.comment: the surjectivity half of condition (1) is not assumed; it is unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFlatOver_strictTransformSheaf_of_affineCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0815.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation with `X` quasi-compact, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open such that the restriction of
`F` to `f⁻¹(U)` is of finite presentation and flat over `U`. Then there is a centre `I` on `S`,
finitely presented and supported away from `U`, exhibiting the blowup of `S` in `I` as a
`U`-admissible blowup, such that the strict transform of `F` along that blowup is an
`𝒪_{X ×_S S'}`-module of finite presentation and flat over the blowup.

The centre is the one of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flatteningCentre_supportSet_eq_compl`, whose
support is `S ∖ U`; so the inverse image of `U` in the blowup is the complement of the exceptional
divisor, hence retrocompact and scheme-theoretically dense, and [Stacks, Tag 081N] gives finite
presentation of the flat strict transform from its finite presentation over that open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFlatOver_strictTransformSheaf_of_affineCharts
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [CompactSpace X] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (hFfp : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj F).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hFflat : IsFlatOver (f ∣_ U).toLRSHom.toShHom
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj F)) :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (U : Set S) (I.support : Set S) ∧
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase I) ∧
      (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (blowUpToBase I)
        (exceptionalIdeal I) F).IsFinitePresentation ∧
      IsFlatOver (pullback.snd f (blowUpToBase I)).toLRSHom.toShHom
        (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf f (blowUpToBase I) (exceptionalIdeal I) F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_and_quasiSeparatedSpace_of_isAffine
declarations.doc: An affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_and_quasiSeparatedSpace_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    CompactSpace X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X
declarations.comment: (1), quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_and_isSeparated_of_isAffine
declarations.doc: An affine scheme is quasi-compact and separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_and_isSeparated_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    CompactSpace X ∧ X.IsSeparated
declarations.comment: (1), quasi-compact and separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_iff_scheme_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
A morphism to a separated scheme is separated if and only if its source is a separated
scheme. The direction from the source to the morphism holds with no hypothesis on the target; it
is the converse that uses `Y.IsSeparated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_scheme_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y) [Y.IsSeparated] :
    IsSeparated f ↔ X.IsSeparated
declarations.comment: (2), separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_and_quasiSeparated_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism to a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if
and only if its source is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCompact_and_quasiSeparated_iff (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] :
    (QuasiCompact f ∧ QuasiSeparated f) ↔ (CompactSpace X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
declarations.comment: (2), quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_and_isSeparated_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism to a quasi-compact separated scheme is quasi-compact and separated if and only if
its source is a quasi-compact separated scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCompact_and_isSeparated_iff (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace Y] [Y.IsSeparated] :
    (QuasiCompact f ∧ IsSeparated f) ↔ (CompactSpace X ∧ X.IsSeparated)
declarations.comment: (2), quasi-compact and separated

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteSubalgebras.isFiltered_finiteSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0817], the directedness assertion.**  The finite quasi-coherent subalgebras of
an integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras form a filtered category.

No hypothesis on `X` is used: not quasi-compactness, not quasi-separatedness, not Noetherian and
not affineness.  This is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteTypeSubalgebraFiltered.isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra`,
which is unconditional, transported along `equivFiniteTypeSubalgebra`.

This is one of the two declarations covering part (1) of the tag; the other is
`nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_finiteSubalgebra (A : AlgebraSheaf X) (hAqc : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A)
    (hAint : A.IsIntegral) : IsFiltered (FiniteSubalgebra A)
declarations.comment:
part (1), the directedness assertion: the finite quasi-coherent subalgebras of an
integral quasi-coherent algebra sheaf form a filtered category; no hypothesis on X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteSubalgebras.nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0817, the colimit assertion of part (1).**  On a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme an integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras is the
colimit of the canonical diagram of all its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras, with the
inclusions of the subobjects as the structure morphisms.

For an integral algebra sheaf a finite type quasi-coherent subalgebra is finite
([Stacks, Tag 02JJ] on affine sections), so this is the tag 05JT form of the same statement,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteTypeSubalgebraFiltered`'s
`nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone`, transported along
`equivFiniteTypeSubalgebra`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (A : AlgebraSheaf X) (hAqc : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A) (hAint : A.IsIntegral) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteSubalgebraCocone A))
declarations.comment:
part (1), the colimit assertion: an integral quasi-coherent algebra sheaf is the
colimit of its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras, for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.exists_small_index_finite_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0817, part (2).**  On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme an
integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras is a directed colimit, over a nonempty
directed preorder in the universe of the scheme, of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebras that are both
finite and of finite presentation.

Part (1) of the tag writes `A` as the colimit of its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras,
[Stacks, Tag 086N] writes each of those as a colimit of finite finitely presented ones, and the
two colimits are spliced by
`Stacks.FinitelyPresentableComposition.exists_directed_index_algebraSheaf`; its presentability
hypothesis holds along these cocones by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817Presentable.presentableAlong_of_isFinitePresentation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_index_finite_finitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : AlgebraSheaf X) (hAqc : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A)
    (hAint : AlgebraSheaf.IsIntegral A) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (F : I ⥤ AlgebraSheaf X) (t : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A)
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A t)),
      ∀ i, AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent (F.obj i) ∧ AlgebraSheaf.IsFinite (F.obj i) ∧
        AlgebraSheaf.IsFinitePresentation (F.obj i)
declarations.comment:
part (2): A is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent
algebras, for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated and A quasi-coherent and integral

The diagonal of a quasi-separated morphism locally of finite type is of finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EventualLimit.eventually_isClosedImmersion_comp_π_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081B (1).**  Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be the limit of a directed inverse system of
quasi-compact schemes over `S` whose transition morphisms are affine.  If `f : Y ⟶ X` is a closed
immersion and `Y` is locally of finite type over `S`, then the composite `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` is a closed
immersion for all sufficiently large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isClosedImmersion_comp_π_app
    (hcomm : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    [∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsAffineHom (D.map (homOfLE h).op)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ s)] [IsClosedImmersion f] :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsClosedImmersion (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EventualLimit.eventually_isImmersion_comp_π_app_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081B (2).** Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be the limit of a directed inverse system of schemes
over `S` whose transition morphisms are affine and whose stages are quasi-separated. If
`f : Y ⟶ X` is an immersion, `Y` is locally of finite type over `S`, and `Y` is quasi-compact,
then the composite `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` is an immersion for all sufficiently large `i`.

These are exactly the source's hypotheses, and the index type `I` is in a universe unrelated to
that of the schemes.  `AlgebraicGeometry.EventualLimit.eventually_isImmersion_comp_π_app` drops
the quasi-separatedness of the stages but ties `I` to the universe of the schemes, which is where
Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_preimage_eq` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isImmersion_comp_π_app_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
    (hcomm : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    [∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsAffineHom (D.map (homOfLE h).op)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ s)] [IsImmersion f] [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsImmersion (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EventualLimit.eventually_isIso_comp_π_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081B (3)**, in the form in which the limit is presented through an isomorphism
`f : Y ≅ lim Xᵢ`: the composites `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` are isomorphisms for all sufficiently large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isIso_comp_π_app (hp : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map p)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ c.pt) [IsIso f]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    [∀ i : I, LocallyOfFiniteType (t.app (op i))]
    [∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsClosedImmersion (D.map (homOfLE h).op)]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ p)] :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsIso (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: eventually_isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismLimitSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081D.** A directed inverse system `(S_i)` of schemes with affine transition
morphisms, a chosen limit cone `S = lim S_i`, a chosen index `0`, and a morphism `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` of
schemes over `S₀`, where `S₀`, `X₀` and `Y₀` are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: structure MorphismLimitSituation (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
declarations.comment: the base changes f_i (i ≥ 0) and f are stageHom and limitHom; toMorphismDescentSituation restricts to the cofinal stages i ≥ 0, which are qcqs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_baseChange_of_isIso_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
If the base change of a finitely presented morphism to the inverse limit is an isomorphism,
then its base change to some stage is already an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isIso_baseChange_of_isIso_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (S : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (S.map g)]
    (c : Cone S) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (S.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (S.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    [IsIso ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀), IsIso ((Over.pullback (S.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isProper_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081F.** Assumptions and notation as in Situation 081D: `D` is a cofiltered inverse
system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit cone `c`, and `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` is a
morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over the quasi-compact quasi-separated stage
`D.obj i₀`. If `f₀` is locally of finite type and its base change to the limit is proper, then
its base change to some later stage is proper.

Chow's lemma over the quasi-compact quasi-separated `Y₀` needs `f₀` to be separated, which is
not assumed; following the Stacks proof, Stacks 01ZQ supplies separatedness at some stage `i₁`
and the situation is re-indexed there before
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isProper_baseChange_of_isLimit_of_isOneAffineOpenStep` is applied.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_baseChange_of_isLimit
    (hc : IsLimit c) (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    [IsProper ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀), IsProper ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081G.** Assumptions and notation as in Situation 081D, and let `F₀` be a
quasi-coherent `O_{X₀}`-module, with `F` and `F_i` its pullbacks to the base changes `X` and
`X_i` of `X₀`. Assume `f₀` is locally of finite type, `F₀` is of finite type, and the
scheme-theoretic support of `F` is proper over `Y`. Then the scheme-theoretic support of `F_i`
is proper over `Y_i` for some `i`.

The base change of `X₀` to a stage is the fibre product of `X₀.hom` with the transition
morphism, so the pullback of `F₀` to it is its pullback along
`CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst`. The proof applies Stacks 081F to the restriction of `f₀`
to the scheme-theoretic support of `F₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_baseChange_of_isLimit
    (hc : IsLimit c) (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (F₀ : X₀.left.Modules)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left] [F₀.IsQuasicoherent] [F₀.IsFiniteType]
    (hlim : IsProper ((Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst X₀.hom (c.π.app i₀))).obj F₀)).subschemeι ≫
        ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left)) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀), IsProper ((Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst X₀.hom (D.map hi))).obj F₀)).subschemeι ≫
        ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_pullback_snd_eq_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081I.** The defining ideal sheaf of the scheme-theoretic image of a
quasi-compact morphism after flat base change is the inverse image of its defining ideal
sheaf.

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosure.SmoothPullback.bijective_toIntegralClosure_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081K**, over a pair of affine opens. Let `g : Y ⟶ S` be a smooth
morphism, let `𝒜 = f_*𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras and let `𝒜'` be the
integral closure of `𝒪_S` in `𝒜`. Over an affine open `V ⊆ Y` lying over an affine open
`U ⊆ S`, the canonical map from `𝒜'(U) ⊗_{Γ(S, U)} Γ(Y, V)` to the integral closure of `Γ(Y, V)`
in `(g^*𝒜)(V) = Γ(X ×_S Y, q⁻¹V)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_toIntegralClosure_sections [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Smooth g]
    {U : S.Opens} {V : Y.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hVU : V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    letI := (f.app U).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := (g.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := ((pullback.snd f g).app V).hom.toAlgebra
    Function.Bijective
      ((sectionsBaseChangeEquiv f g hU hV hVU).mapIntegralClosure.toAlgHom.comp
        (TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure Γ(S, U) Γ(Y, V) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)))
declarations.comment:
affine-open comparison map. The equality of subsheaves is asserted over a pair of
affine opens `V ⊆ Y`, `U ⊆ S` with `V ⊆ g⁻¹U`, as bijectivity of the canonical map out of the base
change of the sections of the integral closure, the quasi-coherent algebra being presented as
`f_*𝒪_X` for `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The identification of the sections of the
pullback is `sectionsBaseChangeEquiv`, pinned by `sectionsBaseChangeEquiv_tmul_one` and
`sectionsBaseChangeEquiv_one_tmul`. The same assertion in terms of the integral-closure
subalgebra itself is `range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback`. The sheaf-level equality is
not asserted here. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosure.SmoothPullback.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081K**, over a pair of affine opens and in terms of the integral-closure
subalgebra itself. For `g` smooth and `𝒜 = f_*𝒪_X` with `f` affine, the sections over `V` of the
integral closure of `𝒪_Y` in `g^*𝒜` are the image of `Γ(Y, V) ⊗_{Γ(S, U)} 𝒜'(U)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback [IsAffineHom f] [Smooth g]
    {U : S.Opens} {V : Y.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hVU : V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    haveI := IsSeparated.of_isAffineHom f
    haveI : IsAffineHom (pullback.snd f g) := MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f g) ‹IsAffineHom f›
    letI := (f.app U).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := (g.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := ((pullback.snd f g).app V).hom.toAlgebra
    Set.range ((integralClosureAlgebraι
        (pushforwardAlgebra (pullback.snd f g))).right.hom.app (op V)) =
      Set.range ((sectionsBaseChangeEquiv f g hU hV hVU).toAlgHom.comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id Γ(Y, V) Γ(Y, V))
          (integralClosure Γ(S, U) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)).val))
declarations.comment:
affine sections of the integral-closure subalgebra. Both sides are read over a
pair of affine opens `V ⊆ Y`, `U ⊆ S` with `V ⊆ g⁻¹U`: the left is the sections of the
integral-closure subalgebra of Stacks 035F in the pullback, the right the image of the base
change of `𝒜'(U)`, which is the sections of that subalgebra over `U` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_of_isAffineOpen`.
The pullback is presented as `f_*𝒪_{X ×_S Y}`, not as `algebraPullback g`; the two agree by
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.isIso_baseChangeAlgebraHom`, whose sections over an open are not
computed in this repository, so the sheaf-level equality is not asserted here. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_algebraPullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081K.** Let `g : Y ⟶ S` be a smooth morphism of schemes, let `𝒜` be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_S`-algebras and let `𝒜' = integralClosureAlgebra 𝒜` be
the integral closure of `𝒪_S` in `𝒜`. Then the integral closure of `𝒪_Y` in `g^*𝒜` is `g^*𝒜'`:
the two subsheaves `integralClosureAlgebra (g^*𝒜)` and `g^*𝒜'` of `g^*𝒜` have the same sections
over every open `W` of `Y`. No hypothesis is placed on `𝒜` beyond quasi-coherence, and none on
`g` beyond smoothness.
declarations.comment:
the whole statement, in the development's own terms: the integral closure
`integralClosureAlgebra` of the structure sheaf, the pullback `algebraPullback` of algebra
sheaves, an arbitrary quasi-coherent `𝒜`, an arbitrary open of `Y`, and no hypothesis beyond
`g` smooth. The two subsheaves of `g^*𝒜` are compared by the ranges of their sections, which is
how the development writes an inclusion of algebra sheaves. The mathematics is
`range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_eq`, where Stacks 03GG and 03GV are consumed; what
is added here is the transport `image_range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app` of the integral closure
along an isomorphism of algebra sheaves, together with `normalizationAlgebraIso` and
`Stacks.AlgebraPullbackQcoh.baseChangeAlgebraHom_naturality`.

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `g : Y ⟶ S` be a smooth morphism, let `𝒜 = f_* 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of
`𝒪_S`-algebras with `f : X ⟶ S` affine, and let `𝒜' ⊆ 𝒜` be the integral closure of `𝒪_S` in
`𝒜`. Then `g^*𝒜'` is the integral closure of `𝒪_Y` in `g^*𝒜`: inside `g^*𝒜 = (X ×_S Y)_* 𝒪`,
the two subsheaves have the same sections over every open `W` of `Y`. Here `𝒜'` is presented as
`(f.fromNormalization)_* 𝒪`, by
`range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_eq_range_normalizationAlgebraι_app`, and its pullback as the
direct image of the structure sheaf of `f.normalization ×_S Y`, which is `g^*𝒜'` by
`isIso_baseChangeAlgebraHom_fromNormalization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_eq [IsAffineHom f] (W : Y.Opens) :
    Set.range ((integralClosureAlgebraι
        (pushforwardAlgebra (pullback.snd f g))).right.hom.app (op W)) =
      Set.range ((baseChangeNormalizationAlgebraι f g).right.hom.app (op W))
declarations.comment:
the equality of subsheaves, over an arbitrary open of `Y`. The quasi-coherent
algebra is presented as `f_* 𝒪_X` for `f` affine rather than as an abstract quasi-coherent
algebra, and the pullback as a direct image from a fibre product rather than through
`algebraPullback`; the latter two agree by `isIso_baseChangeAlgebraHom_fromNormalization`, and
the integral-closure subalgebra `𝒜'` is identified with the relative normalization by
`range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_eq_range_normalizationAlgebraι_app`. The affine-open
comparison map, which is where Stacks 03GG is consumed, is
`Stacks.IntegralClosure.SmoothPullback.bijective_toIntegralClosure_sections`. Transport of the
integral-closure subalgebra along an isomorphism of algebra sheaves, which removes the
presentation of `𝒜` as `f_* 𝒪_X`, is
`Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.image_range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app`, and the resulting
presentation-free form of this clause is
`Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_algebraPullback_eq`. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_relativeSpec_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `g : Y ⟶ S` be smooth and let `𝒜` be any quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras, with
`𝒜' ⊆ 𝒜` the integral closure of `𝒪_S` in `𝒜`. Writing `X = Spec_S(𝒜)` for the relative
spectrum, so that `𝒜 ≅ (relativeSpecToBase 𝒜)_* 𝒪_X` by
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.pushforwardAlgebraIso` and `g^*𝒜 ≅ (X ×_S Y)_* 𝒪` by
`isIso_baseChangeAlgebraHom_self` at `X`, the integral closure of `𝒪_Y` in `g^*𝒜` is `g^*𝒜'`:
the two subsheaves have the same sections over every open `W` of `Y`. No hypothesis is placed on
`𝒜` beyond quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_relativeSpec_eq (W : Y.Opens) :
    haveI : IsSeparated (relativeSpecToBase A) := IsSeparated.of_isAffineHom _
    Set.range ((integralClosureAlgebraι (pushforwardAlgebra
        (pullback.snd (relativeSpecToBase A) g))).right.hom.app (op W)) =
      Set.range ((baseChangeNormalizationAlgebraι (relativeSpecToBase A) g).right.hom.app
        (op W))
declarations.comment:
the equality of subsheaves for an arbitrary quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-algebra `𝒜`,
over an arbitrary open of `Y`. `𝒜` enters through its relative spectrum, so that `𝒜` itself is
`(relativeSpecToBase 𝒜)_* 𝒪` up to the isomorphism
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.pushforwardAlgebraIso`. Invariance of the integral-closure
subalgebra under an isomorphism of algebra sheaves, which lets the statement be read off
`integralClosureAlgebra 𝒜` directly, is
`Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.image_range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app`, and the resulting
statement — the equality of the subsheaves `integralClosureAlgebra (g^*𝒜)` and
`g^*(integralClosureAlgebra 𝒜)` of `g^*𝒜` — is
`Stacks.IntegralClosure.SheafLevel.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_algebraPullback_eq`. See
the module docstring and `range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_pullback_eq`.

    RelativeDimensionLE f e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_flat_finitePresentation_strictTransform_of_affineCase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081R.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be of finite type and quasi-separated and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open such
that `X_U ⟶ U` is flat and locally of finite presentation. Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup
of `S` along which the strict transform of `X` is flat and of finite presentation.

Both hypotheses of the source are present: (1) `f` of finite type and quasi-separated, and (2)
`X_U ⟶ U` flat and locally of finite presentation. Hypothesis (2) is what
`exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_flat_finitePresentation_strictTransform_of_affineCharts`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_flat_strictTransform` omit the flatness half of,
on the ground that it enters only through the affine case they take as an input. It does enter
only through it, but the hypothesis-free `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentre` that
those forms take is false in general, so no proof of the affine case can supply it. With
hypothesis (2) present the chain closes:
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentre.of_affineCase`
produces the chart predicate precisely from hypothesis (2), by the source's own route through the
immersion into affine space of [Stacks, Tag 04II], and the affine case it calls on is
`AffineChartFlatteningCentreUnderSourceHypotheses.of_compactSpace`, itself proved from
[Stacks, Tag 0811].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_flat_finitePresentation_strictTransform_of_affineCase
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S)) (hflat : Flat (f ∣_ U))
    (hfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ∣_ U)) :
    ∃ ℐ : S.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation ℐ.subschemeι ∧
        Disjoint (U : Set S) (ℐ.support : Set S) ∧
          Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase ℐ) ∧
            Flat (strictTransformToBlowUp f ℐ) ∧
              FinitePresentation (strictTransformToBlowUp f ℐ)
declarations.comment: the conclusion in full -- the strict transform flat AND of finite presentation -- under exactly the source's hypotheses (1) and (2). The affine case of the flatness assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0815] is proved inside, from hypothesis (2), by `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentre.of_affineCase` (through the immersion into affine space of [Stacks, Tag 04II] and `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentreUnderSourceHypotheses.of_compactSpace`, proved from [Stacks, Tag 0811]); the finite-presentation clause comes from the flatness clause by [Stacks, Tag 081N]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransform
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated morphism of finite type with `S` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open such that `f` is an isomorphism over
`U`. Then there is a centre `M` on `S`, finitely presented and supported away from `U`, such
that the blowup of `S` in `M` is `U`-admissible and the strict transform of `X` along it is an
open subscheme of that blowup.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransform {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    [IsIso (f ∣_ U)] :
    ∃ M : S.IdealSheafData, FinitePresentation M.subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (U : Set S) (M.support : Set S) ∧
        Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase M) ∧
          IsOpenImmersion (strictTransformToBlowUp f M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformOpenImmersion_of_isIso_morphismRestrict
declarations.doc:
A separated morphism of finite type which is an isomorphism over a quasi-compact open `U` of
a quasi-compact quasi-separated base satisfies `AlgebraicGeometry.StrictTransformOpenImmersion`:
along the blowup in some finitely presented centre avoiding `U`, its strict transform is an
open subscheme of the blowup.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictTransformOpenImmersion_of_isIso_morphismRestrict {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    [IsIso (f ∣_ U)] : StrictTransformOpenImmersion f U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_dominating_of_affineCase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 081T.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism with `S` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open such that `f` is an isomorphism over
`U`. Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup `b : S' ⟶ S` which dominates `X`: a morphism
`g : S' ⟶ X` with `g ≫ f = b`.

The hypotheses are exactly the source's. Both results the source cites are supplied by proved
declarations: [Stacks, Tag 080Y] by `AlgebraicGeometry.cartierBoundaryReduction` and
[Stacks, Tag 081S] by `AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformOpenImmersion_of_isIso_morphismRestrict`,
each of which stands on its own hypotheses alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_dominating_of_affineCase (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    [IsIso (f ∣_ U)] :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (b : S' ⟶ S),
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U b ∧ ∃ g : S' ⟶ X, g ≫ f = b
declarations.comment: complete, under exactly the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenImmersion_isClosedImmersion_comp_eq_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081U.** An immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` which is quasi-compact factors as
an open immersion followed by a closed immersion.

The intermediate algebraic space is the scheme-theoretic image of the morphism: it is a closed
subspace of the target by Stacks 082X, and the morphism onto it is an open immersion by the
quasi-compact case of Stacks 088G.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isClosedImmersion_comp_eq_of_isQuasiCompact
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : Z ⟶ X) (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f)
    (hq : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    ∃ (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (j : Z ⟶ W) (i : W ⟶ X),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS j ∧
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ∧ j ≫ i = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChangeAlgebraHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The base-change comparison of `𝒪_Y`-algebras is natural in the algebraic space affine over
`X`.**  For a morphism `φ : Z₁ ⟶ Z₂` of algebraic spaces affine over `X`, the square

```
g^* (f₂_* 𝒪_{Z₂}) ⟶ (f₂')_* 𝒪_{Y ×_X Z₂}
       ↓                       ↓
g^* (f₁_* 𝒪_{Z₁}) ⟶ (f₁')_* 𝒪_{Y ×_X Z₁}
```

of `𝒪_Y`-algebras commutes, the vertical maps being the pullback of the direct-image map of `φ`
and the direct-image map of its base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineOverBaseChangeAlgebraHom_naturality (g : Y ⟶ X) {Z₁ Z₂ : AffineOver B S hS X}
    (φ : Z₁ ⟶ Z₂) :
    (algebraPullback B S hS g).map (pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS φ.hom) ≫
        affineOverBaseChangeAlgebraHom B S hS g Z₁ =
      affineOverBaseChangeAlgebraHom B S hS g Z₂ ≫
        pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS (affineOverBaseChangeMap B S hS g φ).hom
declarations.comment: naturality in Z of the base-change comparison g^*(f_* 𝒪_Z) ⟶ f'_* 𝒪_{Y ×_X Z}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChangeMap_comp_projection
declarations.doc:
**The projections of the geometric base change are natural in the affine algebraic space
being base-changed.**

This has exactly the type of the `affineBaseChange_projection_naturality` field of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseChangeCompatibility`, and is proved with no anti-equivalence and
no base-change compatibility: it is the defining property of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChangeMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineOverBaseChangeMap_comp_projection (g : Y ⟶ X) {Z Z' : AffineOver B S hS X}
    (φ : Z ⟶ Z') :
    (affineOverBaseChangeMap B S hS g φ).hom.left ≫
        affineOverBaseChangeProjection B S hS g Z' =
      affineOverBaseChangeProjection B S hS g Z ≫ φ.hom.left
declarations.comment: naturality of the projections of the geometric base change Y ×_X Z ⟶ Z in Z; the anti-equivalence of the tag and its compatibility with base change are not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChangeFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Base change of the algebraic spaces affine over `X`, as a functor
`AffineOver X ⥤ AffineOver Y`.**

On objects it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChange` and on morphisms
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineOverBaseChangeMap`.  This has exactly the type of the
`affineBaseChange` field of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseChangeCompatibility`, of which
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.BoundedDirectImageAlgebraFactorization` constructs only
the action on objects.
declarations.statement:
def affineOverBaseChangeFunctor (g : Y ⟶ X) :
    AffineOver B S hS X ⥤ AffineOver B S hS Y
declarations.comment: base change of the algebraic spaces affine over X as a functor; the anti-equivalence of the tag and its compatibility with base change are not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The direct-image functor `f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y` of Stacks 081V is faithful.**

This is the faithfulness half of the anti-equivalence clause of the tag, and no more: the functor
is not shown full by this statement — that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor` below — nor essentially surjective,
and nothing is proved about the tag's compatibility with base change.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_pushforwardRingMap_eq` is the content;
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor_iff` is what strips the two full
subcategories and the opposite category off it.

Restricting the target to the bounded quasi-coherent algebras changes nothing, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (quasicoherentPushforwardAlgebraFunctor B S hS X).Faithful
declarations.comment: faithfulness of the direct image functor f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y from the algebraic spaces affine over X; the corrected anti-equivalence and the base-change compatibility as a whole are affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_bounded

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The direct-image functor `f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y` of Stacks 081V is full.**

This is the fullness half of the anti-equivalence clause of the tag, and no more: nothing is
proved here about the functor's essential surjectivity, which would need the relative spectrum of
a quasi-coherent algebra, nor about the tag's compatibility with base change.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_pushforwardAlgebraMap_eq` is the content;
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor_iff` is what strips the two full
subcategories and the opposite category off it.

Faithfulness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor`, so the two
together make the functor fully faithful, and clause (a) of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor_iff_bijective` — that
`f ↦ f_*` be bijective — is delivered.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (quasicoherentPushforwardAlgebraFunctor B S hS X).Full
declarations.comment: fullness of the direct image functor f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y from the algebraic spaces affine over X; the corrected anti-equivalence and the base-change compatibility as a whole are affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_bounded

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.algebraPullback_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The pullback of a quasi-coherent algebra sheaf along a morphism of algebraic spaces is
quasi-coherent.**

This is the `algebraPullback_isQuasicoherent` field of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseChangeCompatibility`, at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.algebraPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraPullback_isQuasicoherent (g : Y ⟶ X)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) :
    ((algebraPullback B S hS g).obj A).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the algebraPullback_isQuasicoherent clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor `f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y` from the algebraic spaces affine over `X` to the
quasi-coherent sheaves of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras *whose sections at every étale chart of `X`
are fewer than the cutoff of the ambient big fppf site*.
declarations.statement:
def boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (AffineOver B S hS X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ BoundedQuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS X
declarations.comment: the direct image functor f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y from the algebraic spaces affine over X, in the corrected form with the target restricted to the quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebras whose sections at every étale chart of X number fewer than the big fppf site's cutoff — the bound the direct image of an affine morphism satisfies by construction, and which the tag's unrestricted target fails (not_essSurj_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor_of_cutoff_le_mk_sections). This registration is the functor itself; its faithfulness, fullness and essential surjectivity are faithful_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor, full_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor and essSurj_boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor (via boundedRelativeSpec, Stacks 081W), and the base-change compatibility is the subject of the other 081V registrations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_bounded
declarations.doc:
For every algebraic space `X`, the direct image
`f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y` is an anti-equivalence from the algebraic spaces affine over `X` onto the
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebras with fewer than the big fppf site's cutoff many sections over every
étale chart; and for every morphism `g : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces the direct image commutes with
base change along `g`, naturally in the affine space.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_bounded :
    (∀ X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS, (boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor B S hS X).IsEquivalence) ∧
      ∀ {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y ⟶ X),
        Nonempty (quasicoherentPushforwardAlgebraFunctor B S hS X ⋙
            quasicoherentAlgebraPullback B S hS g ≅
          (affineOverBaseChangeFunctor B S hS g).op ⋙
            quasicoherentPushforwardAlgebraFunctor B S hS Y)
declarations.comment: corrected form: f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y is an anti-equivalence from the algebraic spaces affine over X onto the quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebras with fewer than the big fppf site's cutoff many sections over every étale chart (the unrestricted target is refuted by not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart, and the bounded algebras are exactly the essential image by essImage_boundedPushforwardAlgebraFunctor_iff), and it commutes with arbitrary base change g : Y ⟶ X, naturally in the affine space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraMap
declarations.doc:
**The contravariant action of `f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y` on morphisms, as a morphism of
`𝒪_X`-algebras.**  A morphism `f : Y ⟶ Z` of algebraic spaces over `X` induces
`f_* : Z.hom_* 𝒪_Z ⟶ Y.hom_* 𝒪_Y`, and that map of sheaves of commutative rings carries the
structure-algebra map of the first to the structure-algebra map of the second.

This is one piece of Stacks 081V: the functor of the anti-equivalence on morphisms.  It is
functorial, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraMap_id` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraMap_comp`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraFunctor` is the functor they assemble; the
anti-equivalence itself is not constructed, see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
def pushforwardAlgebraMap (f : Y ⟶ Z) :
    pushforwardAlgebra B S hS Z ⟶ pushforwardAlgebra B S hS Y
declarations.comment: the direct image f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y on morphisms, as a map of 𝒪_X-algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The direct-image functor of Stacks 081V.**  The contravariant functor from the algebraic
spaces over `X` to the sheaves of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras which sends `f : Y ⟶ X` to
`f_* 𝒪_Y` and a morphism over `X` to the map it induces on direct images.

This is the functor of Stacks 081V on the whole over-category rather than on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineOver X`, and with values in all algebra sheaves rather than in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentAlgebra X`: quasi-coherence of `f_* 𝒪_Y` for a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated `f` is Stacks 03M9, which is stated nowhere in this development,
so restricting the codomain is not available.  It is *not* shown to be an anti-equivalence; see
the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardAlgebraFunctor :
    (Over X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the direct image functor f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineQuasicoherentPushforwardAlgebraFunctor
registrations.comment: the direct image functor f ↦ f_* 𝒪_Y on the algebraic spaces affine over X, with values in the quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 081W.** The relative spectrum `\underline{Spec}_X(𝒜)` of an arbitrary quasi-coherent
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras `𝒜` on an algebraic space `X`: the algebraic space affine over `X`
corresponding to `𝒜` under the anti-equivalence of Stacks 081V.

**Where it lives.** It is an algebraic space of the big fppf site
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpectrumSite 𝒜`, a big fppf site containing the site `B` of `X`,
and it is affine over `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpectrumBase 𝒜`, which is `X` read in that
site (Stacks 03FP, `AlgebraicGeometry.changeBigSite`). It cannot in general live in `B` itself:
an algebra with at least `B.cutoff` sections over an étale chart is the direct image of no
algebraic space of `B` affine over `X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_essSurj_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor_of_cutoff_le_mk_sections`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_quasicoherentAlgebra_cutoff_le_mk_sections`), so the site is
enlarged, as Stacks 03FO allows, past the cardinality of the sections of `𝒜`.

**What it is.** It is the object of Stacks 081V over the enlarged site corresponding to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpectrumAlgebra 𝒜`, which is `𝒜` read on the small étale site of
`X` enlarged (its sections over the charts of `X` are those of `𝒜`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpectrumRestrictIso`): its direct image is that algebra
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraRelativeSpectrumIso`) and it is unique up to unique
isomorphism with that property (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_relativeSpectrum`).
When `𝒜` is bounded it is the relative spectrum `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeSpec`
built inside the site of `X`, read in the enlarged site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_iso_changeBigSite_boundedRelativeSpec`).

No hypothesis is placed on `𝒜` beyond quasi-coherence. This is the only declaration registered
as Stacks 081W; the bounded construction `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeSpec` and the
value `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeSpec` of a given anti-equivalence are not.
declarations.comment: the relative spectrum Spec_X(A) of an arbitrary quasi-coherent O_X-algebra A on an algebraic space X, with no further hypothesis: the algebraic space affine over X corresponding to A under 081V. It lives on an enlargement relativeSpectrumSite A of the big fppf site of X (Stacks 03FO; necessary, since an algebra with at least B.cutoff sections over a chart is the direct image of no space affine over X in the same site: not_essSurj_affinePushforwardAlgebraFunctor_of_cutoff_le_mk_sections), over X read there by 03FP; its direct image is A read there (pushforwardAlgebraRelativeSpectrumIso, relativeSpectrumRestrictIso) and it is unique up to unique isomorphism with that property (existsUnique_iso_relativeSpectrum)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.directImageSpec_factorization
declarations.doc:
**The canonical factorization through the relative spectrum of `f_* 𝒪_Y`.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X`
be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces.  Then `f_* 𝒪_Y` is a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebra, and `f` factors as `Y ⟶ \underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y) ⟶ X` through
the canonical morphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toDirectImageSpec`, which is the unique morphism
over `X` whose direct-image map is the identification `\underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)_* 𝒪 ≅ f_* 𝒪_Y`.

The relative spectrum is that of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeSpec`, and the size
condition it needs is proved for `f_* 𝒪_Y` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionsBelowCutoff_pushforwardAlgebra`, so nothing beyond the
hypotheses of Stacks 081X is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem directImageSpec_factorization :
    (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      (toDirectImageSpec B S hS f hfqc hfqs).left ≫ (directImageSpec B S hS f hfqc hfqs).obj.hom =
        f ∧
      ∀ g : Over.mk f ⟶ (directImageSpec B S hS f hfqc hfqs).obj,
        g = toDirectImageSpec B S hS f hfqc hfqs ↔
          pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS g = (directImageSpecIso B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of f_* 𝒪_Y, the factorization Y → Spec_X(f_* 𝒪_Y) → X, and its canonicity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: A closed immersion of algebraic spaces is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_of_isClosedImmersion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsFinite B S hS f
declarations.comment: finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: A closed immersion of algebraic spaces is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_of_isClosedImmersion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS f
declarations.comment: integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
If a composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is integral and its second leg is
separated, then its first leg is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_of_comp_of_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : IsIntegralHom B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
If a composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is finite and its second leg is
separated, then its first leg is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_of_comp_of_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : IsFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsFinite B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (1): finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.range_integralClosureInclusion_app_eq_integralClosure'
declarations.doc:
The sections of the integral closure of the structure sheaf in a quasi-coherent algebra
sheaf over an affine étale chart are the integral closure of the ring of functions on the chart
in the sections of the algebra over it.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_integralClosureInclusion_app_eq_integralClosure'
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) (U : SmallEtale B S hS F)
    (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) :
    letI : Algebra ((structureSheaf B S hS F hF).obj.obj (op U))
        (A.right.obj.obj (op U)) := (A.algebraMap (op U)).toAlgebra
    Set.range (((integralClosureInclusion A).right.hom.app (op U)).hom) =
      (integralClosure ((structureSheaf B S hS F hF).obj.obj (op U))
        (A.right.obj.obj (op U)) : Set _)
declarations.comment: the sections of the integral closure over an affine chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_integralClosureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Quasi-coherence of the integral closure.**  The integral closure of the structure sheaf in a
quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_F`-algebras is again a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_F`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_integralClosureSheaf (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) : (integralClosureSheaf A).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of the integral closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The integral closure of the structure sheaf in an algebra sheaf.**  Its sections over a
chart are the locally integral sections of `A`, and the structure-algebra map is the one of
`A`, whose values are integral.

This is the subalgebra of Stacks 0820 as data, which is what Stacks 0821 names; the two
assertions the source makes about it are discussed in the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
def integralClosureSheaf (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, m} B S hS F hF) :
    AlgebraSheaf.{u, m} B S hS F hF
declarations.comment: the integral closure of the structure sheaf in an algebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureInclusion
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the integral closure into the algebra, as a morphism of algebra sheaves.
On each chart it is the inclusion of the subring of locally integral sections.  It is what makes
the integral closure a *subalgebra* of `A`, as Stacks 0821 names it.
declarations.statement:
def integralClosureInclusion (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, m} B S hS F hF) :
    integralClosureSheaf A ⟶ A
declarations.comment: the inclusion exhibiting the integral closure as a subalgebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**The normalization of `X` in `Y`.**  For a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces whose
direct image `f_* 𝒪_Y` is quasi-coherent, it is the relative spectrum
`ν : X' = \underline{Spec}_X(𝒪') ⟶ X` of the integral closure `𝒪'` of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y`,
regarded as an algebraic space affine over `X`.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationIn (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent) :
    AffineOver B S hS X
declarations.comment: the normalization of X in Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism `f' : Y ⟶ X'` to the normalization of `X` in `Y`**, as a morphism
over `X`.  It is the factorization `Y ⟶ \underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 081X followed by
the morphism of relative spectra induced by the inclusion `𝒪' ⊂ f_* 𝒪_Y`.
declarations.statement:
def toNormalizationIn (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hqc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hid : pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (idAffineOver B S hS Y).obj ≅ unitAlgebra B S hS Y) :
    Over.mk f ⟶ (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj
declarations.comment: the canonical factorization of f through the normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInQcqsHom
declarations.doc:
**The normalization morphism `ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y`** (Definition 0822), for a
quasi-compact quasi-separated `f : Y ⟶ X`.  It is affine
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_normalizationInQcqsHom`) with `ν_* 𝒪_{X'}` the integral
closure `𝒪'` of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInQcqsPushforwardIso`),
which is what `X' = \underline{Spec}_X(𝒪')` means.
declarations.statement: def normalizationInQcqsHom : normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs ⟶ X
declarations.comment: the normalization ν : X' = Spec_X(𝒪') ⟶ X of X in Y, for f qcqs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_normalizationInQcqsHom
declarations.doc: **`ν : X' ⟶ X` is affine.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_normalizationInQcqsHom :
    IsAffineHom B S hS (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: ν : X' ⟶ X is affine, X' being a relative spectrum over X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInQcqsPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**`ν_* 𝒪_{X'} ≅ 𝒪'`**: the direct image of the structure sheaf of the normalization is the
integral closure of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y`, as sheaves of `𝒪_X`-algebras.  With affineness of `ν`
this identifies `X'` with `\underline{Spec}_X(𝒪')`.
declarations.comment: ν_* 𝒪_{X'} = 𝒪', i.e. X' = Spec_X(𝒪')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toNormalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism `f' : Y ⟶ X'`** of Definition 0822: on a `T`-point `y` of `Y` it is
the unique morphism `T ⟶ X'` over `X` inducing `ν_* 𝒪_{X'} ≅ 𝒪' ⊂ f_* 𝒪_Y ⟶ (f ∘ y)_* 𝒪_T`.
declarations.statement: def toNormalizationInQcqs : Y ⟶ normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism f' : Y ⟶ X'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toNormalizationInQcqs_comp
declarations.doc: **The factorization of Definition 0822: `ν ∘ f' = f`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem toNormalizationInQcqs_comp :
    toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs ≫ normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs = f
declarations.comment: the natural factorization Y ⟶ X' ⟶ X of f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_normalizationInQcqsHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, property (1): the normalization `ν : X' ⟶ X` is integral.**  It is the
relative spectrum of the integral closure `𝒪'`, an integral `𝒪_X`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_normalizationInQcqsHom :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: property (1): ν is integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_normalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, properties (1) and (2) for the normalization of Stacks 0822.**  Let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, and
`f = ν ∘ f'` its factorization through the normalization `ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y`.  Then `ν` is
integral, and for every factorization `f = π ∘ g` with `π : Z ⟶ X` an integral morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` there is a unique `h : X' ⟶ Z` with `h ∘ f' = g` and `π ∘ h = ν`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_normalizationInQcqs :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f.hom (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
      (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: properties (1) and (2) hold for the normalization f = ν ∘ f' of Stacks 0822

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_iff_exists_iso_normalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823: the normalization is characterized by properties (1) and (2).**  Let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated.  A factorization `f = ν'' ∘ f''` of `f` through
an algebraic space `X''` has properties (1) and (2) — `ν''` integral, and every factorization of
`f` through an integral morphism receiving a unique compatible morphism from `X''` — if and only
if it is isomorphic to the factorization `f = ν ∘ f'` through the normalization of `X` in `Y`;
the isomorphism is then unique, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_normalizationInQcqs_of_isRelativeNormalization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_iff_exists_iso_normalizationInQcqs
    {X'' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX'' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X'')
    (ν'' : X'' ⟶ X.1) (f'' : Y.1 ⟶ X'') :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f.hom ν'' f'' ↔
      ∃ e : (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs).1 ≅ X'',
        (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ≫ e.hom = f'' ∧
          e.hom ≫ ν'' = (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: the factorization through the normalization is characterized by (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_comparison_normalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, the final clause.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
let `f = π ∘ g` with `π : Z ⟶ X` an integral morphism of algebraic spaces, and let `h : X' ⟶ Z`
be the morphism of property (2), so `h ∘ f' = g` and `π ∘ h = ν`.  Then `h : X' ⟶ Z` is the
normalization of `Z` in `Y`: the factorization `g = h ∘ f'` has properties (1) and (2) for `g`,
and it is uniquely isomorphic to the factorization of `g` through the normalization of `Z` in
`Y` of Stacks 0822, `g` being quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_comparison_normalizationInQcqs {Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (π : Z ⟶ X) (hπ : IsIntegralHom B S hS π.hom) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hg : g ≫ π = f)
    (h : normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs ⟶ Z)
    (hh : toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs ≫ h = g)
    (hhπ : h ≫ π = normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS g.hom h.hom (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
      ∃ (hgqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS g.hom) (hgqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g.hom),
        ∃! e : (normalizationInQcqs B S hS g hgqc hgqs).1 ≅
            (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs).1,
          (toNormalizationInQcqs g hgqc hgqs).hom ≫ e.hom =
              (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
            e.hom ≫ h.hom = (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS g hgqc hgqs).hom
declarations.comment: moreover, in (2) the morphism h : X' ⟶ Z is the normalization of Z in Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, the characterization.**  Two factorizations of `f` through an integral
morphism of algebraic spaces which both have the universal property are joined by a unique
isomorphism compatible with the two factorizations and the two integral morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso {ν' : X'' ⟶ X} {f'' : Y ⟶ X''}
    (h : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (h' : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν' f'')
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX'' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X'') :
    ∃! e : X' ≅ X'', f' ≫ e.hom = f'' ∧ e.hom ≫ ν' = ν
declarations.comment: properties (1) and (2) characterize the factorization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, the final clause.**  Let `f = π ∘ g` be a factorization of `f` through an
integral morphism `π : Z ⟶ X`, and let `k : X' ⟶ Z` be the comparison morphism supplied by the
universal property.  Then `k` exhibits `X'` as the normalization of `Z` in `Y`.
declarations.comment: moreover, the comparison morphism is the normalization of Z in Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0823, properties (1) and (2) for the canonical factorization.**  The factorization
`f = ν ∘ f'` of `f` through the normalization `ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y` has `ν` integral, and
every factorization of `f` through an integral morphism `π : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces
receives a unique morphism `h : X' ⟶ Z` with `f' ∘ h = g` and `π ∘ h = ν`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_toNormalizationIn
    (P : RelativeSpecUniversalProperty B S hS E C)
    (D : IntegralAlgebraDictionary B S hS E) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hqc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hid : pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (idAffineOver B S hS Y).obj ≅ unitAlgebra B S hS Y)
    (hloc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegralLocalOnAffineCharts) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f.hom
      (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj.hom.hom
      (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: the canonical factorization has properties (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0824.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source
is a disjoint union of finitely many algebraic spaces `Y i`, and let `X' i` be the
normalization of `X` in `Y i`. Then a disjoint union of the `X' i` is the normalization of `X`
in `Y`.

The normalization morphism is integral because its base change along a morphism from an affine
object of the site is the induced morphism out of the coproduct of the base changes of the
summands, which is a finite coproduct of integral morphisms of schemes; the universal property
is checked summand by summand, each factorization of `f` through an integral morphism
restricting to one of `f i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_coproduct {I : Type v} [Finite I]
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (F : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (F i))
    (Y : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, (⟨F i, (hF i).isSheaf⟩ :
      Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y ι)) (f : Y.obj ⟶ X)
    (N : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hN : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (N i))
    (νs : ∀ i, N i ⟶ X) (fs : ∀ i, F i ⟶ N i)
    (hnorm : ∀ i, IsRelativeNormalization B S hS ((ι i).hom ≫ f) (νs i) (fs i))
    (P : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (κ : ∀ i, (⟨N i, (hN i).isSheaf⟩ :
      Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ P)
    (hP : IsColimit (Cofan.mk P κ))
    (ν : P.obj ⟶ X) (hν : ∀ i, (κ i).hom ≫ ν = νs i)
    (f' : Y.obj ⟶ P.obj) (hf' : ∀ i, (ι i).hom ≫ f' = fs i ≫ (κ i).hom) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInIsoOfIsIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0825.**  The integral closure of `X` in `Y` is `Y`: for an integral morphism
`f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces whose direct image `f_* 𝒪_Y` is integral over `𝒪_X`, the
normalization `X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y` is canonically isomorphic to `Y` over `X`.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationInIsoOfIsIntegralHom (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hint : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegral) :
    (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj ≅ Over.mk f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInIsoOfIsIntegralHom'
declarations.doc:
For an integral morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces, the normalization `X' ⟶ X` of `X`
in `Y` is canonically isomorphic to `Y` over `X`.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationInIsoOfIsIntegralHom' (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent) :
    (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj ≅ Over.mk f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_toNormalizationInQcqs_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0825.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be an integral morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.  Then
the integral closure of `X` in `Y` is equal to `Y`: the canonical morphism `f' : Y ⟶ X'` of
Stacks 0822 from `Y` to the normalization `ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y` is an isomorphism.

An integral morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the normalization is defined at no
further hypothesis.  By Stacks 0415 `f` is affine and universally closed; universal closedness
makes `f_* 𝒪_Y` integral over `𝒪_X` (Stacks 0A0Q), so the integral closure `𝒪' = ν_* 𝒪_{X'}` is
all of `f_* 𝒪_Y`, and since `Y` and `X'` are both affine over `X`, direct image reflects that
isomorphism of algebras to `f'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_toNormalizationInQcqs_of_isIntegralHom (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f.hom) :
    IsIso (toNormalizationInQcqs f
      (isQuasiCompact_of_isIntegralHom f.hom Y.property X.property hf)
      (isQuasiSeparated_of_isIntegralHom f.hom Y.property X.property hf))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_id_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0825, in the form of the characterization of Tag 0823.** An integral morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` is the normalization of `Y` in `X`: the factorization
of `f` as the identity of `X` followed by `f` itself has the two characterizing properties.

Integrality of the second factor is the hypothesis, and a factorization `f = g ≫ π` through an
integral morphism `π : Z ⟶ Y` already has `g` as a morphism out of `X`, which is therefore the
unique morphism compatible with the two factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_id_of_isIntegralHom (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f f (𝟙 X)
declarations.comment: in the form of the characterization of Tag 0823: an integral morphism is the normalization of its target in its source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isQuasiCompactSpace_preimage_eq_of_isSiteSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0827.** Notation and assumptions as in Situation 084R: let `X = limit D` be the
limit of a cofiltered inverse system `D` of algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition
morphisms, the index category being small enough for the site so that `X` is an algebraic space
by Stacks 07SF. Then for every quasi-compact open subspace `U ⊆ X` there is a stage `i` and a
quasi-compact open subspace of `D i` whose inverse image in `X` is `U`.

Neither quasi-separatedness nor quasi-compactness of the stages, which Situation 084R also
assumes, is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isQuasiCompactSpace_preimage_eq_of_isSiteSmall (hb : IsSiteSmall B S
    hS D)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f))
    (U : Subfunctor (limit D)) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.toFunctor) :
    ∃ (i : I) (V : Subfunctor (D.obj i)), IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor ∧ V.preimage (limit.π D i) = U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isQuasiCompactSpace_preimage_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0827.** Notation and assumptions as in Situation 084R: let `X = limit D` be the
limit of a cofiltered inverse system `D` of algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition
morphisms, the index category being small enough for the site so that `X` is an algebraic space
by Stacks 07SF. Then for every quasi-compact open subspace `U ⊆ X` there is a stage `i` and a
quasi-compact open subspace of `D i` whose inverse image in `X` is `U`.

Neither quasi-separatedness nor quasi-compactness of the stages, which Situation 084R also
assumes, is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isQuasiCompactSpace_preimage_eq (hSize : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hHomSize : ∀ i j : I, #(i ⟶ j) < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f))
    (U : Subfunctor (limit D)) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.toFunctor) :
    ∃ (i : I) (V : Subfunctor (D.obj i)), IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor ∧ V.preimage (limit.π D i) = U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isClosedImmersion_comp_limitπ'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0828, part (1).** Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over an
algebraic space `Bspace`, with affine transition morphisms and quasi-compact stages, and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a closed immersion with `Y` locally of finite type over `Bspace`.  Then `Y ⟶ Xᵢ`
is a closed immersion for all sufficiently large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isClosedImmersion_comp_limitπ'
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (contains : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (Bspace : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicBase : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Bspace)
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicStage : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Bspace)
    (c : Cone D) (isLimit : IsLimit c) (s : c.pt ⟶ Bspace)
    (commutes : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraic : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ c.pt)
    (quasiCompactStage : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (affine : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), Space.IsAffineHom B S contains (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (finiteType : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S contains (f ≫ s))
    (closed : Space.IsClosedImmersion B S contains f) :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, Space.IsClosedImmersion B S contains (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (1): closed immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isImmersion_comp_limitπ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0828, part (2).** Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over an
algebraic space `Bspace`, with affine transition morphisms and quasi-separated stages, and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be an immersion whose source is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over
`Bspace`.  Then `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` is an immersion for all sufficiently large `i`.

The image of `Y` in one stage `Xᵢ₀` lies in a quasi-compact open subspace `V`, and the system of
preimages of `V` in the stages above `i₀` has quasi-compact stages and limit the preimage of `V`
in `X`, through which `f` factors by an immersion.  An affine étale atlas of `V` reduces the
statement to schemes, where it is Stacks 081B, part (2)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.EventualLimit.eventually_isImmersion_comp_π_app`), and the immersion is
carried back to the stages by effective descent of immersions along surjective étale
morphisms; quasi-separatedness of `Xᵢ₀` makes the base change of `Y` to the atlas quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isImmersion_comp_limitπ
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (contains : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (Bspace : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicBase : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Bspace)
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicStage : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Bspace)
    (c : Cone D) (isLimit : IsLimit c) (s : c.pt ⟶ Bspace)
    (commutes : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraic : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Y)
    (quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S contains Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ c.pt)
    (affine : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsAffineHom B S contains (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (quasiSeparated : ∀ i,
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S contains B.contains_terminal (D.obj (op i)))
    (finiteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S contains (f ≫ s))
    (immersion : IsImmersion B S contains f) :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsImmersion B S contains (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (2): immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isIso_comp_limitπ
declarations.doc:
**An isomorphism onto a directed limit is eventually an isomorphism onto the stages.**  Let
`X = lim Xᵢ` be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `Bspace` and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be an isomorphism.  If the stages `Xᵢ` are quasi-compact and locally of finite type
over `Bspace`, the transition morphisms are closed immersions, and `Y` is locally of finite
presentation over `Bspace`, then `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` is an isomorphism for all sufficiently large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isIso_comp_limitπ
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (contains : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (Bspace : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicBase : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Bspace)
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicStage : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Bspace)
    (c : Cone D) (isLimit : IsLimit c) (s : c.pt ⟶ Bspace)
    (commutes : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (algebraic : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ c.pt) (iso : IsIso f)
    (quasiCompactStage : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (finiteType : ∀ i, IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S contains (t.app (op i)))
    (closed : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsClosedImmersion B S contains (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (finitePresentation : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S contains (f ≫ s)) :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsIso (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (3): isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_mono_comp_limitπ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0828, part (4).** Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over an
algebraic space `Bspace`, with affine transition morphisms and quasi-separated stages, and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a monomorphism whose source is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over
`Bspace`.  Then `Y ⟶ Xᵢ` is a monomorphism for all sufficiently large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_mono_comp_limitπ
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (contains : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (Bspace : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicBase : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Bspace)
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (algebraicStage : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains (D.obj (op i)))
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Bspace)
    (c : Cone D) (isLimit : IsLimit c) (s : c.pt ⟶ Bspace)
    (commutes : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map s)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S contains)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (algebraic : IsAlgebraicSpace B S contains Y)
    (quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S contains Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ c.pt) [Mono f]
    (affine : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsAffineHom B S contains (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (quasiSeparated : ∀ i,
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S contains B.contains_terminal (D.obj (op i)))
    (finiteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S contains (f ≫ s)) :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, Mono (f ≫ c.π.app (op i))
declarations.comment: part (4): monomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered
declarations.doc:
The finite type quasi-coherent submodules of a quasi-coherent module form a directed
system.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject B S hS X hX F)
declarations.comment: the directedness clause, for an arbitrary quasi-coherent module on an arbitrary algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject
declarations.doc:
**The directedness assertion of Stacks 0829.**  The quasi-coherent submodules of finite type
of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-module form a directed system: the image in the module of the direct
sum of two of them is a quasi-coherent submodule of finite type containing both.

Stacks 0829 states this for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space; those two
hypotheses enter only its colimit assertion, through Stacks 07V9, so the statement here is for
an arbitrary algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject B S hS F hF G)
declarations.comment: directedness, for an arbitrary algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0829, the colimit assertion.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then `F` is the
