colimit of the canonical diagram of its finite type quasi-coherent submodules.

The diagram is directed by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject`,
which together with this declaration covers the whole of Stacks 0829.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone_of_qcqs
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone B S hS X hX F))
declarations.comment: the colimit clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_and_nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0829.** On a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space `X`, a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` is the directed colimit of its quasi-coherent submodules of finite type: the
category `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FiniteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject` of those submodules is
filtered and their canonical cocone with point `F` is a colimit cocone.

Directedness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered`, which
uses Descent 03DX(2) and the cokernel clause of Stacks 03M1, that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderCokernels_quasicoherentSheaves`. For the colimit, the
supremum of the submodules is `⊤`: its inclusion is surjective on sections over affine charts,
every section there lying in one of them by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiniteType_submodule_mem_of_qcqs`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_and_nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone_of_qcqs
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject B S hS X.1 X.2 F) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone B S hS X.1 X.2 F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_algebra_of_idealQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 082A, over the system datum.**  Let `S` be a scheme, `X` an algebraic
space over `S` and `𝒜` an `𝒪_X`-algebra.  Let `D` be a filtered system of `𝒪_X`-algebras with a
cocone `ψ` over `𝒜`, and for each `i` let `ℐ_i` be a sheaf of ideals of `D_i` killed by `ψ_i`
and carried into `ℐ_j` by every transition map.  If every quotient `D_i/ℐ_i` is quasi-coherent
of finite presentation and the constructed cocone of those quotients over `𝒜` is colimiting,
then `𝒜` is the colimit of a system of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebras of finite presentation
indexed by a directed poset.

The members of the system and the morphisms between them are *constructed*: they are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientSystem` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientSystemCocone`, built from the quotient of an algebra sheaf
by a sheaf of ideals and its universal property.  See the module documentation for what each of
the three hypotheses is and why it is a separate missing ingredient rather than the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_algebra_of_idealQuotients [IsFiltered P]
    (hstage : ∀ p : P, ((D.obj p).idealQuotient (I p)).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ((D.obj p).idealQuotient (I p)).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hcol : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A (idealQuotientSystemCocone A D ψ I hkill hmap))) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder J) (_ : Nonempty J) (_ : IsDirected J (· ≤ ·))
      (E : J ⥤ AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (φ : E ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj A)
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ)),
      ∀ j, (E.obj j).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (E.obj j).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: PARTIAL, but the construction and not the reindexing: the members A_{i,j} = B_i/I_{i,j} of the source's system and the morphisms between them are constructed here, as quotients of an algebra sheaf on an algebraic space by a sheaf of ideals and factorizations through them, which is the object whose absence was the recorded obstruction. Three inputs are carried, each separately identified. (1) The system datum D, psi -- in the source B_i = Sym(F_i) with the maps induced by Stacks 07V9 -- because at the algebraic space level this tree has the symmetric algebra of a module but neither its functoriality in the module nor the ungraded universal property giving Sym(F_i) to A, both of which exist only for schemes (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.symmetricAlgebraSheafMap, Stacks.SymAlgSheaf.algebraLift), nor quasi-coherence of Sym. (2) Quasi-coherence and finite presentation of each stage, which are conditions on the sections of a sheafification over the affine etale charts; this is where the source's finite generation of I_{i,j} is used, so the ideals here are arbitrary. (3) The colimit property of the constructed cocone, colimits in AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf being constructed nowhere in this tree. The source's quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are absent because they are used only to produce the system datum, which is hypothesis (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_algebra_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and `𝒜` a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebra.  Then `𝒜` is the colimit, in the category of all `𝒪_X`-algebras, of a
system of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebras of finite presentation indexed by a nonempty directed
partially ordered set.  The colimit is taken in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf`, which is
stronger than in the full subcategory of the quasi-coherent algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_algebra_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder J) (_ : Nonempty J) (_ : IsDirected J (· ≤ ·))
      (E : J ⥤ AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (ψ : E ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj A)
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A ψ)),
      ∀ j, (E.obj j).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (E.obj j).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent algebra on a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space is the colimit, among all algebra sheaves, of a system of quasi-coherent algebras of finite presentation indexed by a nonempty directed poset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_and_isColimit_finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082B.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over `S` and `𝒜` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebra.  Then `𝒜` is the directed colimit of its
finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-subalgebras: they form a filtered category, and the cocone of
their inclusions into `𝒜` is a colimit cocone.

Directedness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra`.  The cocone is a
colimit because its legs are injective on sections and, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteTypeSubalgebra_section`, jointly surjective on the
sections over affine étale charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_and_isColimit_finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1) (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeSubalgebra B S hS X.1 X.2 A) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone B S hS X.1 X.2 A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**The finite type quasi-coherent subalgebras of a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-algebras on
an algebraic space form a filtered category**, with no hypothesis beyond quasi-coherence of the
algebra.

Nonemptiness is the image of the canonical morphism from the structure sheaf, and upper bounds
are the subalgebras generated by two subalgebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeSubalgebra B S hS Y.1 Y.2 A)
declarations.comment:
the directedness assertion; the colimit assertion is blocked on Stacks 07SU
through 0829 and 07V9 by the source's own route

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_isColimit_finiteSubalgebra_and_exists_directed_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082C.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over a
scheme `S` and let `A` be an integral quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebra.  Then

1. the finite quasi-coherent subalgebras of `A` form a directed (filtered) category and `A` is
   the colimit of the cocone of their inclusions, and
2. `A` is the colimit of a directed system, over a nonempty directed preorder, of
   quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-algebras that are finite and of finite presentation.

The hypotheses are the source's.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_isColimit_finiteSubalgebra_and_exists_directed_finite
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) (hint : A.IsIntegral) :
    (IsFiltered (FiniteSubalgebra B S hS X hX A) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteSubalgebraCocone B S hS X hX A))) ∧
      ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
        (D : I ⥤ AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A)
        (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A t)),
        ∀ i, (D.obj i).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (D.obj i).IsFinite ∧ (D.obj i).IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
The finite quasi-coherent subalgebras of an integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative
`𝒪_Y`-algebras on an algebraic space `Y` form a filtered category.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_finiteSubalgebra (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hqcoh : A.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hint : A.IsIntegral) :
    IsFiltered (FiniteSubalgebra B S hS Y.1 Y.2 A)
declarations.comment: part (1), the directedness assertion, and with no hypothesis beyond quasi-coherence and integrality of the algebra: neither quasi-compactness nor quasi-separatedness of the space is used. The colimit assertion of part (1) is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone and part (2) is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation; those two name their own restrictions, this one has none

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone
declarations.doc:
An integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_Y`-algebras `A` on a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space `Y` is the colimit of the cocone of the inclusions of its finite
quasi-coherent subalgebras, provided (`hgen`) every section of `A` over an affine étale chart of
`Y` lies in the image of one finite quasi-coherent subalgebra of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hqcoh : A.IsQuasicoherent) (hint : A.IsIntegral)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj)
    (hgen : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj →
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1,
        IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
        ∀ x : A.right.obj.obj (op U),
          ∃ C : FiniteSubalgebra B S hS Y.1 Y.2 A,
            x ∈ Set.range ((C.obj.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)).hom)) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (finiteSubalgebraCocone B S hS Y.1 Y.2 A))
declarations.comment: part (1), the colimit assertion, over the carried input hgen: for every affine etale chart U of the space and every section x of the algebra over U there is a finite quasi-coherent subalgebra of the algebra, on the whole space, having x among its sections over U. hgen is the algebraic-space analogue of what the scheme-level development derives from Stacks 01PF, namely Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SubalgebraGeneratedByModule.exists_finiteTypeSubalgebra_section, and it is asked only AT THE SPACE AND THE ALGEBRA OF THE STATEMENT. It replaces the colimit assertion of Stacks 082B, which is blocked by the source's own route on Stacks 07SU through Stacks 0829 and Stacks 07V9, and is strictly weaker than it: hgen mentions no cocone, no colimit and no index, and quantifies only over sections over single affine etale charts. Everything else is proved: directedness of the index is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteSubalgebra, which has no restriction at all, sectionwise injectivity of the legs is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.injective_subobject_arrow_app, and the passage from sections over the affine etale charts to the colimit property is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.nonempty_isColimit_of_affineChartSections_of_injective. The identification of the finite with the finite type quasi-coherent subalgebras over an integral algebra, which is Algebra Lemma 10.36.5 on the affine etale charts, is proved as AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentAndIsFinite_eq_isQuasicoherentAndIsFiniteType'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
An integral quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_Y`-algebras on a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space `Y` is the colimit of a system, indexed by a nonempty directed
preorder, of quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebras each of which is finite and of finite presentation,
provided `hgen` (as in `nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone`), `hstage` (every finite
quasi-coherent algebra on `Y` is a filtered colimit of finitely presented quotients of an algebra
sheaf, one of them integral) and `hpres` (every finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent
algebra is finitely presentable along every filtered colimit cocone of quasi-coherent algebras).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (A : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (hint : A.obj.IsIntegral)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj)
    (hgen : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj →
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1,
        IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
        ∀ x : A.obj.right.obj.obj (op U),
          ∃ C : FiniteSubalgebra B S hS Y.1 Y.2 A.obj,
            x ∈ Set.range ((C.obj.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)).hom))
    (hstage : ∀ C : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y,
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj →
      C.obj.IsFinite →
        ∃ (ℬ : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (f : ℬ ⟶ C.obj) (J : Type u)
          (inst : SmallCategory J),
          let _ := inst
          ∃ (_ : IsFiltered J) (ι : J → ℬ.IdealSheaf)
            (hι : ∀ j j' : J, (j ⟶ j') → ι j ≤ ι j')
            (hkill : ∀ (j : J) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)ᵒᵖ) (a : ℬ.right.obj.obj U),
              a ∈ (ι j).obj U → (f.right.hom.app U).hom a = 0)
            (hqcoh : ∀ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsQuasicoherent),
            (∀ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
            (∃ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsIntegral) ∧
            Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk C
              (idealQuotientQcohCocone ℬ ι hι C f hkill hqcoh))))
    (hpres : ∀ T : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y, T.obj.IsFinite → T.obj.IsFinitePresentation →
      ∀ (J : Type (u + 1)) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
        (Φ : J ⥤ QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (c : Cocone Φ), IsColimit c →
        Stacks.FinitelyPresentableComposition.PresentableAlong T c) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ)) ∧
      ∀ i, (D.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (D.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: part (2), over three carried inputs. (a) hgen, the same input as in AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_finiteSubalgebraCocone: every section of the algebra over an affine etale chart lies in the image of one finite quasi-coherent subalgebra on the whole space. Part (1) is PROVED from it here and is not assumed. (b) hstage, the carried input of Stacks 086Z itself — see the module documentation of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Limits.FiniteAlgebraSurjectiveSystem for what it says — asked at every finite quasi-coherent algebra on the space rather than at one; Stacks 086Z is not restated, the theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective is called, so the finiteness, the finite presentation and the directedness of every inner system are that theorem's and not assumed here. (c) hpres, presentability of a finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent algebra ALONG THE TWO SYSTEMS' OWN COCONES, which is the analogue for algebraic spaces of the input the source takes from Cohomology of Spaces Lemma 69.5.3 and is weaker both than that lemma and than CategoryTheory.IsFinitelyPresentable of the stages: nothing is asked about any filtered colimit other than the two being spliced. On schemes the corresponding statement is a theorem, Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817Presentable.presentableAlong_of_isFinitePresentation, proved by carrying Stacks 01ZC across the relative spectrum of Stacks 01SA; for algebraic spaces the relative spectrum of Stacks 081W and the limit-preserving criterion AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_stage_map_of_relativelyLimitPreserving of Stacks 04AK are proved but the passage from a colimit of algebra sheaves to a limit of algebraic spaces affine over the base is not, so hpres is not proved. What is proved on top of the three: part (1) from hgen, including its directedness which has no restriction, the lifting of each inner index from Type u to the morphism universe of the quasi-coherent algebras along CategoryTheory.AsSmall, the splice itself, and that every stage of the resulting directed system is finite and of finite presentation. No declaration in this file assumes any assertion of Stacks 082C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_algebraPullback_integralClosureSheaf_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082E.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let
`A` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras. The integral closure of `𝒪_Y` in
`f^*A` is `f^*A'`, where `A' ⊆ A` is the integral closure of `𝒪_X` in `A`: there is an
isomorphism `f^*A' ≅ (f^*A)'` of algebra sheaves on `Y` whose composite with the inclusion of
`(f^*A)'` into `f^*A` is the pullback of the inclusion of `A'` into `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_algebraPullback_integralClosureSheaf_unconditional (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f.hom)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hA : A.IsQuasicoherent) :
    ∃ e : (algebraPullback B S hS f).obj (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf A) ≅
        AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf ((algebraPullback B S hS f).obj A),
      e.hom ≫ AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureInclusion ((algebraPullback B S hS f).obj A) =
        (algebraPullback B S hS f).map (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureInclusion A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.existsUnique_iso_baseChange_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082F.**  Let `Y₂ = X₂ ×_{X₁} Y₁` be a fibre square of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `f : Y₁ ⟶ X₁` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `φ : X₂ ⟶ X₁` smooth, and let
`Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ' ⟶ Xᵢ` be the normalization of `Xᵢ` in `Yᵢ` (Stacks 0823).  Then `X₂' ≅ X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁'`,
by a unique isomorphism compatible with the two factorizations of `f₂` and with the two
morphisms to `X₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_baseChange_of_isSmooth
    (hnorm₁ : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν₁ f₁')
    (hnorm₂ : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f₂ ν₂ f₂')
    (hX₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁) (hX₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₂)
    (hY₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₁) (hX₁' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁')
    (hX₂' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₂')
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hφ : IsSmooth B S hS φ)
    (sq : IsPullback g f₂ f φ) (sqP : IsPullback p q φ ν₁) :
    ∃! e : X₂' ≅ P, f₂' ≫ e.hom = hnorm₁.baseChangeFactorization sq sqP ∧ e.hom ≫ p = ν₂
declarations.comment: X₂' ≅ X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁' for f qcqs and φ smooth, for normalizations given by the universal property of Tag 0823

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_normalizationInQcqs_baseChange_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082F, for the normalizations of Stacks 0822.**  Let `Y₂ = X₂ ×_{X₁} Y₁` be a fibre
square of algebraic spaces over `S` with `f : Y₁ ⟶ X₁` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and
`φ : X₂ ⟶ X₁` smooth, and let `P = X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁'` for `X₁'` the normalization of `X₁` in `Y₁`,
with `f₂P : Y₂ ⟶ P` the base change of `Y₁ ⟶ X₁'`.  Then `f₂ : Y₂ ⟶ X₂` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and the normalization `X₂'` of `X₂` in `Y₂` is isomorphic to `P` by a unique
isomorphism compatible with the two factorizations of `f₂` and the two morphisms to `X₂`.
declarations.comment: X₂' ≅ X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁' for f qcqs and φ smooth, for the normalizations of Tag 0822

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.existsUnique_baseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082F, the morphism `h`.**  The base change `X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁' ⟶ X₂` is an integral
morphism through which `f₂` factors, so the universal property of the normalization `X₂'` of
`X₂` in `Y₂` supplies a unique morphism `h : X₂' ⟶ X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁'` compatible with the two
factorizations of `f₂` and with the two morphisms to `X₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_baseChangeComparison
    (hnorm₁ : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν₁ f₁')
    (hnorm₂ : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f₂ ν₂ f₂')
    (hX₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁) (hX₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₂)
    (hX₁' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁')
    (sq : IsPullback g f₂ f φ) (sqP : IsPullback p q φ ν₁) :
    ∃! h : X₂' ⟶ P, f₂' ≫ h = hnorm₁.baseChangeFactorization sq sqP ∧ h ≫ p = ν₂
declarations.comment: the morphism h of the proof: the base change X₂ ×_{X₁} X₁' ⟶ X₂ is integral and f₂ factors through it, so the universal property of Tag 0823 supplies a unique h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etale_decomposition_isFinite_of_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 082H.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `y` be a point of `|Y|` and let `x₁, …, x_n` be points of `|X|` mapping to `y`. Assume that
`f` is locally of finite type, that `f` is separated, that `f` is quasi-finite at each `xᵢ`, and
that `f` is quasi-compact or `Y` is decent. Then there are an object `U` of the big fppf category
over `S`, an **étale** morphism `g : h_U ⟶ Y` and a point `u` of `|h_U|` over `y`, together with a
decomposition of `U ×_Y X` into two open-and-closed subspaces `W` and `V` — their join sheafifies
to everything and their meet is the sheafification of nothing — such that

* `V ⟶ U` is **finite**;
* every point of the fibre of `|V| ⟶ |U|` over `u` maps to one of the `xᵢ`;
* no point of the fibre of `|W| ⟶ |U|` over `u` maps to any `xᵢ`.

This is the composite of the three paragraphs of the source proof with its finiteness clause; see
the module documentation for which file carries which. The hypotheses are those of the tag and
nothing else, apart from the ambient `HasSheafify` assumption on the site discussed there.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_decomposition_isFinite_of_isQuasiFiniteAt
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : points B S hS Y) {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → points B S hS X)
    (hx : ∀ i, pointsMap B S hS X f (x i) = y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hqf : ∀ i, IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f (x i))
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f ∨ IsDecentSpace B S hS Y) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Y)
      (u : points B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) (W V : Subfunctor (pullback g f)),
      IsEtale B S hS g ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) g u = y ∧
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧ IsClosedSubspace B S hS W ∧
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧ IsClosedSubspace B S hS V ∧
      (W ⊔ V).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) = ⊤ ∧
      W ⊓ V = (⊥ : Subfunctor (pullback g f)).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      IsFinite B S hS (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst g f) ∧
      (∀ v : points B S hS V.toFunctor,
        pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst g f) v = u →
          ∃ i, pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd g f) v = x i) ∧
      (∀ t : points B S hS W.toFunctor,
        pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor (W.ι ≫ pullback.fst g f) t = u →
          ∀ i, pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor (W.ι ≫ pullback.snd g f) t ≠ x i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.isIso_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082I, the isomorphism conclusion for an integral morphism.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an
integral morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the
normalization of `Y` in `X`. Then `f'` is an isomorphism, so the open subspace `U' ⊆ Y'` of the
tag may be taken to be all of `Y'`.

The identity of `X` factors `f` through the integral morphism `f`, so the universal property
yields `k : Y' ⟶ X` with `f' ≫ k = 𝟙` and `k ≫ f = ν`; uniqueness in the universal property
for the factorization `f = f' ≫ ν` identifies `k ≫ f'` with `𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isIntegralHom (h : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y')
    (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f) : IsIso f'
declarations.comment: the isomorphism conclusion when f is integral: the canonical morphism to the normalization is an isomorphism, so the open subspace may be taken to be the whole normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082I for a finite morphism.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the normalization of `Y` in `X`. Then
there is an open subspace `U' ⊆ Y'` such that `(f')⁻¹(U') ⟶ U'` is an isomorphism and the point
set of `(f')⁻¹(U')` is the set of points of `X` at which `f` is quasi-finite; one may take
`U' = Y'`.

A finite morphism is integral by Tag 0414, so `f'` is an isomorphism and hence so is its base
change `(f')⁻¹(Y') ⟶ Y'`; and a finite morphism is locally quasi-finite by Tag 0A4X, hence
quasi-finite at every point of its source, which is the whole of `(f')⁻¹(Y')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_of_isFinite
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (h : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (hf : IsFinite B S hS f) :
    ∃ U' : Subfunctor Y', IsOpenSubspace B S hS U' ∧ IsIso (U'.fromPreimage f') ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (U'.preimage f').toFunctor (U'.preimage f').ι) ↔
          IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: both numbered conclusions in the case of a finite morphism, with the open subspace the whole normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_and_range_pointsMap_preimage_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082I.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is of
finite type and separated, and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the normalization of `Y` in
`X`, in the sense of the characterization of Tag 0823. Then there is an open subspace
`U' ⊆ Y'` such that `(f')⁻¹(U') ⟶ U'` is an isomorphism and the point set of `(f')⁻¹(U')` is
the set of points of `X` at which `f` is quasi-finite.

The open subspace is the image of the quasi-finite locus. It is covered by the étale
morphisms of `IsRelativeNormalization.exists_isEtale_isPullback_of_isQuasiFiniteAt`, one for
each point of quasi-finiteness, which makes it open and identifies its inverse image;
and `(f')⁻¹(U') ⟶ U'` is an isomorphism after base change to each of them, hence an
isomorphism by Tag 041Y.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_and_range_pointsMap_preimage_eq
    {X Y Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y} {ν : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X ⟶ Y'}
    (h : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ∃ U' : Subfunctor Y', IsOpenSubspace B S hS U' ∧ IsIso (U'.fromPreimage f') ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (U'.preimage f').toFunctor (U'.preimage f').ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: both numbered conclusions, for every factorization of f with the universal property of Tag 0823 (the normalization of Y in X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_toNormalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082I, at the normalization of Definition 0822.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is of finite type and separated, and let `X ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y` be the
normalization of `Y` in `X` constructed in Definition 0822 (it exists since `f` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Then there is an open subspace `U' ⊆ Y'` such that
`(f')⁻¹(U') ⟶ U'` is an isomorphism and the point set of `(f')⁻¹(U')` is the set of points of
`X` at which `f` is quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_toNormalizationInQcqs
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    ∃ U' : Subfunctor (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hft.2
        (isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated B S hS hsep)).obj,
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS U' ∧
      IsIso (U'.fromPreimage (toNormalizationInQcqs f hft.2
        (isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated B S hS hsep)).hom) ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (U'.preimage (toNormalizationInQcqs f hft.2
          (isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated B S hS hsep)).hom).toFunctor
          (U'.preimage (toNormalizationInQcqs f hft.2
            (isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated B S hS hsep)).hom).ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X.obj | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f.hom x}
declarations.comment: both numbered conclusions, at the normalization of Y in X constructed in Definition 0822

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.isIntegralHom_fromNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABS and 082J, integrality of the normalization morphism.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-finite separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`,
`f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the normalization of `Y` in `X`. Then `ν` is integral.

Over a surjective étale scheme chart `w : W ⟶ Y` the chart description of the normalization
identifies the base change of `ν` with the morphism `fromNormalization` of the induced morphism
of schemes `W ×_Y X ⟶ W`, which is integral; condition (3) of Tag 03ZQ promotes that to
integrality of `ν`. The chart description is applicable because `f` is representable by
Tag 0418, quasi-compact, and separated, hence quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_fromNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS N.fromNorm
declarations.comment: the normalization morphism is integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.isOpenImmersion_toNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABS and 082J, the open immersion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite separated
morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the normalization of `Y`
in `X`. Then `f'` is an open immersion.

By Tag 0ABR the image `U'` in `Y'` of the quasi-finite locus of `f` is an open subspace whose
inverse image under `f'` is that locus and over which `f'` restricts to an isomorphism. Local
quasi-finiteness makes the locus the whole of `X`, so both the inclusion of the inverse image
and the restriction of `f'` are isomorphisms, and `f'` is their composite with the inclusion of
`U'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_toNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS N.toNorm
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism to the normalization is an open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.isQuasiCompact_toNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABS and 082J, quasi-compactness of the open immersion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-finite
separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `ν : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X ⟶ Y'` be the
normalization of `Y` in `X`. Then `f'` is quasi-compact.

This is Tag 03KS applied to the factorization `f = f' ≫ ν`: the composite is quasi-compact
because `f` is quasi-finite, and `ν` is quasi-separated because an integral morphism is
separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_toNorm_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS N.toNorm
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism to the normalization is quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABS and 082J, quasi-affineness.** A quasi-finite separated morphism of algebraic
spaces
over `S` is quasi-affine.

Such a morphism is representable by Tag 0418, so each of its represented base changes is a
morphism of schemes which is separated, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite and
quasi-compact, hence quasi-affine by Tag 02LR — the statement for schemes, proved there by
exactly the factorization through the relative normalization that the source uses here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiFinite_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f
declarations.comment: a quasi-finite separated morphism is quasi-affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_comp_eq_of_isQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082K, Zariski's main theorem, the finite factorization.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then `f = π ∘ j` with `j : X ⟶ T` a quasi-compact open
immersion into an algebraic space `T` and `π : T ⟶ Y` finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_comp_eq_of_isQuasiFinite
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (j : X ⟶ T) (π : T ⟶ Y),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS j ∧ IsQuasiCompact B S hS j ∧
        IsFinite B S hS π ∧ j ≫ π = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082M, the standing data.**  A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`
together with a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`: the data whose quotients, flat over the test
scheme, the functor of quotients of `F/X/Y` classifies.
declarations.statement: structure QuotientSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.mk_kernel_quotientProjection
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the projection `F_T ⟶ F_T / K` is `K` again.  Together with surjectivity of
the projection this says that the submodules of `F_T` list the quotients of `F_T` once each,
which is the source's identification of two quotients with the same kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_kernel_quotientProjection (T : SchemesOver D.Y)
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) :
    Subobject.mk (kernel.ι (D.quotientProjection T K)) = K
declarations.comment: the identification of two quotients of F_T that have the same kernel: the submodules of F_T list the quotients of F_T once each

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082M.**  The set `Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` of quotients of `F_T` which are quasi-coherent and
flat over the test scheme `T`, the two conditions of the source.

A quotient of `F_T` is recorded by its kernel, a submodule `K` of `F_T`, the quotient itself
being `F_T / K`; this is exactly the source's identification of two quotients of `F_T` that
have the same kernel.
declarations.statement: def quotients (T : SchemesOver D.Y) : Set (Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T))
declarations.comment: the set of quotients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.finitePresentationQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082M.**  The subset `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}(T)` of `Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` consisting of those
quotients `F_T ⟶ Q` for which `Q` is of finite presentation as an `𝒪_{X_T}`-module.
declarations.statement:
def finitePresentationQuotients (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    Set (Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T))
declarations.comment: the finite-presentation subfunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientPullback
declarations.doc:
The pullback of a quotient of `F_T` along a morphism `h : T' ⟶ T` of test schemes,
`Q ↦ (X_{T'} ⟶ X_T)^*Q`, recorded by its kernel.
declarations.statement:
def quotientPullback {T' T : SchemesOver D.Y} (h : T' ⟶ T)
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T')
declarations.comment: the pullback Q' = (X_{T'} ⟶ X_T)^*Q of a quotient of F_T along a morphism T' ⟶ T of test schemes over Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientPullback_mem_quotients'
declarations.doc:
The pullback of a quotient of `F_T` which is quasi-coherent and flat over `T` is
quasi-coherent and flat over `T'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientPullback_mem_quotients' {T' T : SchemesOver D.Y} (h : T' ⟶ T)
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) (hK : K ∈ D.quotients T) :
    D.quotientPullback h K ∈ D.quotients T'
declarations.comment: the pullback clause: if F_T ⟶ Q is an element of Q_{F/X/Y}(T) and T' ⟶ T is a morphism of schemes over Y, then Q' = (X_{T'} ⟶ X_T)^*Q is a quasi-coherent 𝒪_{X_{T'}}-module flat over T', so it is an element of Q_{F/X/Y}(T')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientPullback_mem_finitePresentationQuotients
declarations.doc: The pullback of a finitely presented quotient is a finitely presented quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientPullback_mem_finitePresentationQuotients {T' T : SchemesOver D.Y} (h : T' ⟶ T)
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) (hK : K ∈ D.finitePresentationQuotients T) :
    D.quotientPullback h K ∈ D.finitePresentationQuotients T'
declarations.comment: Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y} is a subfunctor of Q_{F/X/Y}: finite presentation of a quotient is preserved by the pullback along a morphism of test schemes, so the finitely presented quotients are stable under the transition maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
The value of the functor of quotients at a test scheme `T` over `Y` is the set
`Q_{F/X/Y}(T)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientsFunctor_obj (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    D.quotientsFunctor.obj (Opposite.op T) = D.quotients T
declarations.comment: the functor Q_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets obtained from the pullback clause, through its value at a test scheme T over Y, which is the set Q_{F/X/Y}(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
The action of the functor of quotients on a morphism of test schemes is
pullback of quotients.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientsFunctor_map {T' T : SchemesOver D.Y} (h : T' ⟶ T)
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) (hK : K ∈ D.quotients T) :
    (D.quotientsFunctor.map (Opposite.op h)
      ⟨K, hK⟩ : D.quotients T').1 = D.quotientPullback h K
declarations.comment: the functor Q_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets obtained from the pullback clause, through its transition maps, which are the pullback Q ↦ (X_{T'} ⟶ X_T)^*Q of quotients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctorToQuotientsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The finite-presentation subfunctor is a subfunctor of the functor of
quotients: at every test scheme its value is a subset of the value of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsFunctor`, and the two actions agree.
declarations.statement:
def finitePresentationQuotientsFunctorToQuotientsFunctor :
    D.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor ⟶ D.quotientsFunctor
declarations.comment: Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets is a subfunctor of Q_{F/X/Y}: the inclusion of the finitely presented quotients into all of them is a morphism of functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.sourceRestricted
declarations.doc:
**Situation 082M on a member of a covering of the source.**  For a morphism
`a : W ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces, the standing data consisting of `W`, the composite
`a ≫ f : W ⟶ Y` and the pullback `a^*F` of the module.

Its functor of quotients is the source's `Q_{F i/X i/Y}` when `a` is a member of a covering of
`X`, and the source's `Q_{F ijk/X ijk/Y}` when `a` is the composite `X ijk ⟶ X i ×_X X j ⟶ X`:
in both cases the module is *the* pullback of `F` to the member, which is what the source
writes.

Quasi-coherence of `a^*F` is Stacks 03GA, which holds along an arbitrary morphism of algebraic
spaces by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ModulePullbackQuasicoherentFromChartDiagrams.lean`, so no
local-presentation hypothesis on `a` is asked for.

It is made reducible below so that the identifications `(D.sourceRestricted a).Y = D.Y` and
`(D.sourceRestricted a).f = a ≫ D.f`, on which the types of the restriction maps below depend,
are available to the unifier.
declarations.statement:
def sourceRestricted {W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : W ⟶ D.X) :
    QuotientSituation B S hS
declarations.comment: the standing data on a member of a covering of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor of quotients of `F/X/Y`,
`Q_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`: its value at a test scheme `T` over `Y` is the set
`Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` of quotients of `F_T` that are quasi-coherent and flat over `T`, and its action
on a morphism of test schemes is pullback of quotients.
declarations.statement: def quotientsFunctor : (SchemesOver D.Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the functor of quotients Q_{F/X/Y} of F/X/Y, with its two functor laws and the stability of the quotients of the source under pullback along a morphism of test schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082P for `Q_{F/X/Y}`.**  The functor of quotients `Q_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`
of Stacks 082N satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) D.quotientsFunctor
declarations.comment: the functor of quotients Q_{F/X/Y}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082P for `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}`.**  The finite-presentation subfunctor of the functor of
quotients satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) D.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor
declarations.comment: the finite-presentation subfunctor Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.isSheafFor_quotientsFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
In Situation 082M the functor of quotients satisfies the
sheaf property for the fpqc topology: for every fpqc covering `{U i ⟶ T}` of schemes over `Y`,
every compatible family of quotients of the `F_{U i}`, quasi-coherent and flat over `U i`, has a
unique amalgamation, a quotient of `F_T` quasi-coherent and flat over `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_quotientsFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).map (g i).left).hom) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor D.quotientsFunctor (Presieve.ofArrows U g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.isSheafFor_finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
In Situation 082M the finite-presentation subfunctor of the functor of quotients satisfies
the sheaf property for the fpqc topology: for every fpqc covering `{U i ⟶ T}` of schemes over `Y`,
every compatible family of finitely presented quotients of the `F_{U i}`, flat over `U i`, has a
unique amalgamation, a finitely presented quotient of `F_T` flat over `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).map (g i).left).hom) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor D.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor (Presieve.ofArrows U g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_limitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082Q, corrected.**  In Situation 082M assume that (a) `f : X ⟶ Y` is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and also locally of finite presentation, and (b) `F` is of finite
presentation.  Then `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}` is limit preserving: for a directed limit `T = lim T_i` of
affine schemes over `Y`, `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}(T) = colim Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}(T_i)`.

The tag as written, without local finite presentation of `f`, is false:
`not_forall_finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_limitPreserving`
(in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Quot.QuotientFunctorLimitPreservingSpaceCounterexample`)
proves the negation, with `X = Spec ℚ[t][y_a]/((t - a) y_a)` over `Spec ℚ[t]` and
`T = Spec ℚ(t)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_limitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (D : QuotientSituation B S hS) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hF : D.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u + 1, u, u} D.testScheme D.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor
declarations.comment: corrected per the 082Q erratum: f also locally of finite presentation; as written the statement is false, see not_forall_finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor_limitPreserving

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SliceFinite.isFiniteType_kernel_of_epi
declarations.doc:
On a site with no products and no pullbacks assumed, the kernel of a surjection from a sheaf
of modules of finite type onto a sheaf of modules of finite presentation is of finite type. This
also gives Stacks Project, Tag 01BP part (2).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCardinalGenerated_of_pullback_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Being locally generated by `r` sections descends along an fpqc covering for quasi-coherent
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCardinalGenerated_of_pullback_fpqc {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherent) (r : ℕ) {I : Type v} (X' : I → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, X' i ⟶ X)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows X' f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X)
    (hgen : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.IsCardinalGenerated.{u}
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f i)).obj M) (Cardinal.lift.{u, 0} r)) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCardinalGenerated.{u} M (Cardinal.lift.{u, 0} r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_injective_ideal_sum_with_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082V.** For `f : X ⟶ S` flat, locally of finite presentation and locally
quasi-finite and `g` a nonzero global function on `X`, there are opens `V ⊆ f ⁻¹ U` on which `g`
stays nonzero and a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf `F ⊆ 𝒪_U` such that a finite direct sum of `r > 0`
copies of `F` injects into `f_* 𝒪_V` with `g|_V` in the image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_injective_ideal_sum_with_section
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U)
      (F : (SheafOfModules.unit U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf).Submodule),
      F.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ∃ (r : ℕ) (_hr : 0 < r)
        (φ : (∐ fun _ : Fin r => F.toSheafOfModules) ⟶
          (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (f.resLE U V hVU)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit _)),
        Mono φ ∧
          ∃ t : Γ((∐ fun _ : Fin r => F.toSheafOfModules), ⊤),
            Scheme.Modules.Hom.app φ ⊤ t =
              (show Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (f.resLE U V hVU)).obj
                (SheafOfModules.unit _), ⊤) from (V.ι.appTop).hom g) ∧
          (V.ι.appTop).hom g ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082X.** The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`:
the intersection of all closed subspaces of the target containing the image of the
morphism.
declarations.statement: def schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor (f : X ⟶ Y) : Subfunctor Y
declarations.comment: underlying subfunctor construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_le_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082X.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` factors through its
scheme-theoretic image.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_le_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Subfunctor.range f ≤ schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f
declarations.comment: the morphism factors through the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082X.** The scheme-theoretic image is contained in every closed subspace of the
target through which the morphism factors.
declarations.comment: minimality of the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor
declarations.doc: **Stacks 082X.** The scheme-theoretic image is a closed subspace of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f)
declarations.comment: the image is a closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082X.** The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`:
the intersection of all closed subspaces of the target containing the image of the
morphism.
declarations.statement: def schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor (f : X ⟶ Y) : Subfunctor Y
declarations.comment: the scheme-theoretic image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isEtale_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082Z, part (3).** The scheme-theoretic image of a *quasi-compact* morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` commutes with étale base change of the target: for
`g : V ⟶ Y` étale, the scheme-theoretic image of `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is the inverse image along `g` of
the scheme-theoretic image of `f`.

Both sides are closed subspaces of `V`, hence are determined by their defining ideal sheaves,
and on an étale scheme chart `W` of `V` both of those ideals are the kernel ideal of `f` on the
chart `g ∘ W` of `Y` — by Stacks 082Z for the base change of `f` and for `f` itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isEtale_of_isQuasiCompact
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : V ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS (pullback.snd f.hom g.hom) =
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f.hom).preimage g.hom
declarations.comment: part (3): compatibility with étale localization of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticImage_eq_kernelIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082Z.** For a quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` the
scheme-theoretic image of `f` is the closed subspace of `Y` cut out by the kernel of the
structure map `f♯ : 𝒪_Y ⟶ f_*𝒪_X`: its defining ideal sheaf of Stacks 03MB is that kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticImage_eq_kernelIdealSheaf (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) :
    definingIdealSheaf B S hS Y (schemeTheoreticImage B S hS f.hom Y.2) =
      kernelIdealSheaf B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): the image is the closed subspace cut out by that ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_schemeTheoreticImage_eq_closure_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082Z, part (4).** The set of points of the scheme-theoretic image of a quasi-compact
morphism of algebraic spaces is the closure of the image of its point map.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_ι_schemeTheoreticImage_eq_closure_of_isQuasiCompact (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f).toFunctor
        (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f).ι) =
      closure (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X f))
declarations.comment: part (4): the image is dense in the scheme-theoretic image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.denseRange_pointsMap_toSchemeTheoreticImage_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 082Z, part (4)**, read inside the scheme-theoretic image: a quasi-compact morphism of
algebraic spaces has dense image on the points of its scheme-theoretic image.
declarations.statement:
theorem denseRange_pointsMap_toSchemeTheoreticImage_of_isQuasiCompact (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS X (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS f))
declarations.comment: part (4): density of the image on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_kernelIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The kernel of the structure map of a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces is a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_kernelIdealSheaf (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) :
    (kernelIdealSheaf B S hS f).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (1): the ideal sheaf of the image is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_reducedClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0830, part (1).** The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism out of a reduced
algebraic space is the reduced closed subspace supported on the closure of the image of its
point map.

The identification itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_of_isReduced_of_range_pointsMap_eq`,
which needs no descent; what it has to be fed is that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reducedClosedSubspace` is a closed subspace, the existence half of
Stacks 03IQ. That comes from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_reducedClosedSubspace`
together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isClosedImmersion`, effective
descent for closed immersions along the surjective étale morphisms of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_reducedClosedSubspace (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced W)) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f =
      reducedClosedSubspace B S hS Y hY
        (closure (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X f))) isClosed_closure
declarations.comment: part (1): the image is the reduced induced structure on the closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0830, part (2).** The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism out of a reduced
algebraic space commutes with étale base change of the target: for an étale morphism
`g : V ⟶ Y`, the scheme-theoretic image of `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is the inverse image along `g` of the
scheme-theoretic image of `f`.

By part (1) both sides are reduced closed subspaces, so it is enough to identify their point
sets and appeal to the uniqueness half of Stacks 03IQ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_reducedClosedSubspace`. The inverse image along `g` of the reduced
closed subspace on the closure of the image of `f` is a closed subspace by Stacks 083Q, is
étale-locally reduced because its projection to that subspace is a base change of `g`, hence
étale, and has point set the preimage along `|g|` of that closure. That preimage is the closure
of the image of `X ×_Y V ⟶ V`, because `|g|` is open by Stacks 03IR and the image of
`X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is the preimage along `|g|` of the image of `f` by Stacks 03H4.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isEtale
    {V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : V ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
    (hXred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced W))
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS (pullback.snd f g) =
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f).preimage g
declarations.comment: part (2): compatibility with étale base change of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0832.** The inverse image of a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme under a
morphism of schemes which is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite is
scheme-theoretically dense.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_preimage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    {W : S.Opens} (hW : Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense W) :
    Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (f ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_exists_surjective_etale_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0833.** Let `U` be an open subspace of an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S`
contained in a big fppf site `B`. Then `U` is scheme-theoretically dense in `X` -- the
scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X V` in `V` is all of `V` for every étale morphism `V ⟶ X` of
algebraic spaces over `S` -- if and only if there are a scheme `V` and a surjective étale
morphism `φ : V ⟶ X` for which that holds over the open subschemes of `V` alone: the
scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X W` in `W` is all of `W` for every open subscheme `W` of `V`.
The second condition says exactly that the open subscheme `U ×_X V` of `V` is
scheme-theoretically dense in the sense of Stacks 01RB.

The first condition trivially implies the second, since the composite of an open immersion with
an étale morphism is étale. For the converse let `C` be an étale scheme chart of `X`; by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_forall_chart` it suffices to make the
scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X C` in `C` everything, and the two conditions are compared
over `T = V ×_X C`. The projection `T ⟶ V` is a base change of the étale chart `C`, hence étale
and so flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, so Stacks 0832 carries
scheme-theoretic density of `U ×_X V` in `V` to scheme-theoretic density of `U ×_X T` in `T`;
chartwise this is read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_preimage_eq_top_iff`, which identifies
closures of inverse images with scheme-theoretic dominance of the representing morphisms of
schemes. The projection `T ⟶ C` is a base change of `φ`, hence surjective étale, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subfunctor_eq_top_of_isSurjective_isEtale_preimage` descends the
closure over `T` to the closure over `C`.

Scheme-theoretic density of `U ×_X V` in `V`, rather than merely the equality of the
scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X V` with `V`, is what the second condition has to say, and
the source's literal reading of it is false. Take for `X` a scheme and for `φ` the identity,
which is a surjective étale morphism from a scheme: the literal reading of condition (2) is
then exactly that the scheme-theoretic closure of `U` in `X` is `X`, whereas condition (1),
applied to the open immersions `W ⟶ X` -- which are étale -- is exactly that `U` is a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme of `X` in the sense of Stacks 01RB. Stacks 01RC
exhibits an affine scheme `X = Spec(k[x, z₁, z₂, …]/(xⁿzₙ))` and an open `U = X ∖ V(z₁, z₂, …)`
with the former but not the latter: the closure is `X` because `A ⟶ ∏ₙ A_{zₙ}` is injective,
while `U` is not even topologically dense in `X`, hence not scheme-theoretically dense. The
literal reading would moreover make the quasi-compactness hypothesis of Stacks 0835
superfluous, and contradict the remark that follows Stacks 0834. By Stacks 01RD the two
readings agree exactly when the inclusion is quasi-compact, and it is the density form that
Stacks 0832 transports.

The part of the source's argument for (2) implies (1) that does hold for the bare equality is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticClosure_eq_top_of_isSurjective_isEtale`: a surjective
étale chart over which the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image is everything already
forces the scheme-theoretic closure of `U` in `X` to be everything.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_exists_surjective_etale_chart
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS U ↔
      ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B S hS φ ∧ IsEtale B S hS φ ∧
          ∀ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ψ : W ⟶ V),
            AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ψ) →
              schemeTheoreticClosure B S hS (U.preimage (yoneda.map ψ ≫ φ)) = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0834, part (1).** The *scheme-theoretic closure* of a subspace `U` of an algebraic
space `X` over `S` is the scheme-theoretic image of Stacks 082X of its inclusion.
declarations.statement: abbrev schemeTheoreticClosure (U : Subfunctor X) : Subfunctor X
declarations.comment: part (1): the scheme-theoretic closure of an open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0834, part (2).** An open subspace `U` of an algebraic space `X` over `S` is
*scheme-theoretically dense in `X`* when, for every étale morphism `φ : V ⟶ X` of algebraic
spaces over `S`, the scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X V` in `V` is all of `V`.

This is the first of the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0833, and is in general strictly
stronger than the scheme-theoretic closure of `U` itself being all of `X`.
declarations.statement: def IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (U : Subfunctor X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): scheme-theoretic density of an open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_schemeTheoreticClosure_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B`, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`
and let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace. If the inclusion `U ⟶ X` is quasi-compact, then `U` is
scheme-theoretically dense in `X` if and only if the scheme-theoretic closure of `U` in `X` is
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_schemeTheoreticClosure_eq_top
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS U.ι) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS U ↔ schemeTheoreticClosure B S hS U = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_mono_fSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0836.** Let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion of algebraic spaces over a scheme
`S` contained in a big fppf site `B`. Then `U` is scheme-theoretically dense in `X` if and only
if the canonical homomorphism `𝒪_X ⟶ j_* 𝒪_U` of sheaves of commutative rings on the small
étale site of `X` is injective, that is, a monomorphism.

Both sides are tested on the étale scheme charts of `X`. On the one hand the structure map of
the morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 03G8 is a monomorphism exactly when, over every étale
scheme chart `V` of `X`, pullback of regular functions along the open immersion of schemes
representing `U ×_X V` is injective; the sections of the direct image over `V` are a limit over
the étale charts of `U` above `U ×_X V`, which for a representable morphism is attained at the
single chart `U ×_X V`. On the other hand the scheme-theoretic closure of `U ×_X V` is all of
`V` exactly when that open immersion of schemes is scheme-theoretically dominant, and -- since
the charts of `X` include every open subscheme of every chart -- dominance over all charts is
the same as injectivity on global sections over all charts. Finally density may be tested on
the charts alone, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_forall_chart`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_mono_fSharp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS U ↔
      Mono (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk U.ι :
          (⟨U.toFunctor, hU.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
          (⟨X, hX⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))).fSharp

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_inf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0837.** If `U` and `V` are scheme-theoretically dense open subspaces of an
algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site `B`, then so is `U ∩ V`.

Let `φ : W ⟶ X` be an étale morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`. The scheme-theoretic
closure of `(U ∩ V) ×_X W` in `W` is a closed subspace containing the inverse image of
`U ∩ V`, hence is all of `W` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_top_of_preimage_inf_le`: the density of `U` along the étale
morphism `V ×_X W ⟶ X` and the density of `V` along `φ` are used in turn.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_inf (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (U V : Subfunctor X)
    (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hUdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS U)
    (hVdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS V) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (U ⊓ V) ∧ IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS (U ⊓ V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyPrincipal
declarations.doc:
A closed subspace `Z` of an algebraic space `X` is *locally principal* when its defining ideal
sheaf `𝓘_Z ⊆ 𝒪_X` is locally generated by one section on the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsLocallyPrincipal (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) : Prop
declarations.comment: locally_principal_closed_subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
A closed subspace `D` of an algebraic space `X` is an *effective Cartier divisor* when its
defining ideal sheaf `𝓘_D ⊆ 𝒪_X` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module on the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) : Prop
declarations.comment: effective_cartier_divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (2) ⟹ (4).** If the inverse image of `D` is an effective Cartier divisor on
one surjective étale scheme chart, then every point of `|D|` has an affine étale neighbourhood
on which `D` is cut out by a nonzerodivisor.

The point of `|D|` lifts to a field-valued point of `D ×_X U` on the surjective chart, whose
image in `U` lies in the support of the chart ideal sheaf.  By the affine-local form of
Stacks 01WS that ideal sheaf is generated by a nonzerodivisor on an affine open `V` of `U`
around that image; `V` is again an étale chart of `X`, the inverse image of `D` on it is the
base change of `D ×_X U`, and its ideal sheaf is therefore the principal ideal sheaf of the
restricted generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover B S hS X D) :
    HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_of_hasAffinePrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (4) ⟹ (3).** If every point of `|D|` has an affine étale neighbourhood on
which `D` is cut out by a nonzerodivisor, then the inverse image of `D` is an effective Cartier
divisor on every étale scheme chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_of_hasAffinePrincipal (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D) :
    HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (4) implies part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_iff_hasAffinePrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (3) ⟺ (4).** The inverse image of a closed subspace is an effective Cartier
divisor on every étale scheme chart if and only if every point of `|D|` has an affine étale
neighbourhood on which the subspace is cut out by a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_iff_hasAffinePrincipal (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D ↔
      HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D
declarations.comment: parts (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover_iff_etalePullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (2) ⟺ (3).** The inverse image of a closed subspace is an effective Cartier
divisor on one surjective étale scheme chart if and only if it is so on every étale scheme
chart.

The nontrivial direction passes through condition (4): a surjective chart gives affine charts
cut out by nonzerodivisors at every point of `|D|`, and those descend to an arbitrary chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover_iff_etalePullbacks (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    HasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover B S hS X D ↔
      HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_of_isEffectiveCartier
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (1) ⟹ (3).** If a closed subspace is an effective Cartier divisor, then its
inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor on every étale scheme chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks_of_isEffectiveCartier (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (1) implies part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover_of_isEffectiveCartier
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (1) ⟹ (2).** If a closed subspace is an effective Cartier divisor, then its
inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor on some surjective étale scheme chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover_of_isEffectiveCartier (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    HasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (1) implies part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods_of_isEffectiveCartier
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (1) ⟹ (4).** If a closed subspace is an effective Cartier divisor, then
every point of `|D|` has an affine étale neighbourhood on which the subspace is cut out by a
nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods_of_isEffectiveCartier (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (1) implies part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_definingIdealSheaf_of_etalePullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, condition (3) implies rank one.** If the inverse image of a closed subspace
`D` is an effective Cartier divisor on every étale scheme chart, then the defining ideal sheaf
of `D` is finite locally free of rank one on the small étale site of `X`.

Over an arbitrary chart the affine opens on which the chart ideal sheaf is generated by a
nonzerodivisor are again charts and they cover it; over such a chart the defining ideal is
generated by the pullback of that nonzerodivisor at *every* chart above it, so multiplication by
it is an isomorphism from the structure sheaf onto `𝓘_D`, which is a one-legged colimit cofan of
the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_definingIdealSheaf_of_etalePullbacks
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D) :
    RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X D).toSheafOfModules 1
declarations.comment: part (3) implies the rank clause of part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (3) ⟹ (1).** If the inverse image of a closed subspace is an effective
Cartier divisor on every étale scheme chart, then the subspace is an effective Cartier divisor.

The defining ideal sheaf is then finite locally free of rank one on the small étale site, and
the small étale site is essentially small at the universe of the sections of its structure
sheaf, so Stacks 0B8M applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (3) implies part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (2) ⟹ (1).** If the inverse image of a closed subspace is an effective
Cartier divisor on one surjective étale scheme chart, then the subspace is an effective Cartier
divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover B S hS X D) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C, (4) ⟹ (1).** If every point of `|D|` has an affine étale neighbourhood of
`X` on which `D` is cut out by a nonzerodivisor, then `D` is an effective Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h : HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (4) implies part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083C.** For a closed subspace `D` of an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S` the
following are equivalent: `D` is an effective Cartier divisor on `X`; the inverse image of `D`
is an effective Cartier divisor on some surjective étale scheme chart of `X`; it is so on every
étale scheme chart of `X`; and every point of `|D|` has an affine étale neighbourhood of `X` on
which `D` is cut out by a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_tfae (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D,
        HasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover B S hS X D,
        HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D,
        HasAffinePrincipalEtaleNeighborhoods B S hS X D]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of parts (1), (2), (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyPrincipal_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks
declarations.doc:
**A closed subspace whose inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor on every étale
scheme chart is locally principal.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD : HasEffectiveCartierEtalePullbacks B S hS X D) :
    IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (3) implies the local principality of part (1) of 083B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_ι_openComplement
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a locally principal
closed subspace. Then the inclusion of the open complement `X \ Z` into `X` is an affine
