morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_ι_openComplement (hZ : IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS X Z) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS (openComplement B S hS Z.1).ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoFunctorSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083F, Equation 77.7.1.1.**  The functor `F_iso` of a map `u : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules: it sends a scheme `T` over `Y` to a one-element set if the base
change `u_T` along `X ×_Y T ⟶ X` is an isomorphism, and to the empty set otherwise.

The base change is taken for the inverse image of modules of Stacks 03LU for the small étale
ringed sites, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback`.
declarations.statement: abbrev isoFunctorSmallEtale : (D.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the functor F_iso of Equation 77.7.1.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.surjFunctorSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083F, the variant `F_surj`.**  The functor sending a scheme `T` over `Y` to a
one-element set if the base change `u_T` is surjective, and to the empty set otherwise.

Surjectivity is restriction-stable because the inverse image of modules is a left adjoint and so
preserves epimorphisms; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isSurjectiveAt_of_hom`.
declarations.statement: abbrev surjFunctorSmallEtale : (D.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the variant F_surj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.zeroFunctorSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083F, the variant `F_zero`.**  The functor sending a scheme `T` over `Y` to a
one-element set if the base change `u_T` is zero, and to the empty set otherwise.
declarations.statement: abbrev zeroFunctorSmallEtale : (D.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the variant F_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.IsInjAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083F, the variant `F_inj`.**  The condition the source asks of a scheme `T` over
`Y` for its variant `F_inj`: that the base change `u_T` of `u` along `X ×_Y T ⟶ X` is injective,
which for a map of sheaves of modules is being a monomorphism.

This is a condition on test schemes and *not* a subterminal presheaf on them: it is not stable
under restriction along a morphism of test schemes, because the inverse image of modules is only
right exact.  The file's notes give the counterexample.  The restriction-stable condition this
development uses in its place is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.IsUniversallyInjectiveAt`.
declarations.statement: def IsInjAt (T : D.SchemesOver) : Prop
declarations.comment: the variant F_inj: the condition that u_T is injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083F.** The standing data of Stacks 083F: a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `S` and a map `u : F ⟶ G` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement: structure ModuleMapSituation
declarations.comment: standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.zeroSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**`F_zero` as a subfunctor of the base.**  Its sections over an object `U` of the big fppf
category over `S` are the sections `x` of `Y` over `U` such that the base change of `u` along
`X ×_Y U ⟶ X`, the base change at the test scheme `x` names, is zero.
declarations.statement: def zeroSubfunctor (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Subfunctor D.Y.1
declarations.comment: the variant F_zero, read as a subfunctor of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isSheaf_flatInjFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083H**, injectivity clause.  The functor `F_inj` of test schemes over `Y` on which
the base change of `u` is injective, a functor on the test schemes over `Y` with flat morphisms,
satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology there.

The topology is generated by the fpqc covering families, so the sheaf property is tested on the
pullback, along a flat morphism `Z ⟶ X`, of the sieve generated by an fpqc covering family
`{T_i ⟶ X}`.  The fibre products `T_i ×_X Z` form an fpqc covering of `Z` whose projections to
`Z` and to `T_i` are both flat, so each projection to `Z` lies in that pullback sieve.  The
functor is subterminal, so it suffices that injectivity of `u` at every `T_i ×_X Z` gives
injectivity at `Z`, and this is descent of injectivity along the flat jointly surjective family
of base-change spaces `X ×_Y (T_i ×_X Z) ⟶ X ×_Y Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_flatInjFunctor :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (flatFpqcTopology D.Y) D.flatInjFunctor
declarations.comment: F_inj, the functor of injectivity of u_T on the test schemes over the base with flat morphisms (the category Stacks 05MJ puts it on, injectivity not being stable under arbitrary base change), is a sheaf for the fpqc topology there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isSheaf_surjFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083H**, surjectivity clause.  The locus of test schemes over `Y` on which the base
change of `u` is surjective is a sheaf for the fpqc topology.

The locus is subterminal, so the sheaf condition is the implication from surjectivity at every
member of a covering sieve to surjectivity at its target.  A covering sieve contains a flat
family which is jointly surjective after base change, and surjectivity descends along such a
family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_surjFunctor :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) (D.surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: F_surj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isSheaf_zeroFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083H**, vanishing clause.  The locus of test schemes over `Y` on which the base
change of `u` vanishes is a sheaf for the fpqc topology.

The locus is subterminal, so the sheaf condition is the implication from vanishing at every
member of a covering sieve to vanishing at its target, and vanishing descends along the flat
jointly surjective family of base-change spaces the sieve contains.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_zeroFunctor :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) (D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: F_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isSheaf_isoFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083H**, isomorphism clause.  The locus of test schemes over `Y` on which the base
change of `u` is an isomorphism is a sheaf for the fpqc topology.

The locus is subterminal, so the sheaf condition is the implication from being an isomorphism at
every member of a covering sieve to being one at its target, and being an isomorphism descends
along the flat jointly surjective family of base-change spaces the sieve contains.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_isoFunctor :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) (D.isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: F_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.surjFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (1).**  In Situation 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of
algebraic spaces and let `u' : ℱ' ⟶ 𝒢'` be the pullback of `u` to `X'`.  If `𝒢` is of finite
type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the support of `𝒢`, then `F_surj = F'_surj` and
`F_zero = F'_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.G)
    (hGsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.G) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.inverseImageSituation g).surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) ∧
      D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.inverseImageSituation g).zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (1): F_surj = F'_surj and F_zero = F'_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.injFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (2).**  In Situation 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of
algebraic spaces and let `u' : ℱ' ⟶ 𝒢'` be the pullback of `u` to `X'`.  If `ℱ` is of finite
type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the support of `ℱ`, then `F_inj = F'_inj` and
`F_zero = F'_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hFsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.F) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.injFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.inverseImageSituation g).injFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) ∧
      D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.inverseImageSituation g).zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (2): F_inj = F'_inj and F_zero = F'_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (3).**  In Situation 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of
algebraic spaces and let `u' : ℱ' ⟶ 𝒢'` be the pullback of `u` to `X'`.  If `ℱ` and `𝒢` are of
finite type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the supports of `ℱ` and `𝒢`, then
`F_iso = F'_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.G)
    (hFsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.F) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom))
    (hGsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.G) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
      (D.inverseImageSituation g).isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (3): F_iso = F'_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.surjFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (1).**  In the situation of Stacks 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat
morphism of algebraic spaces and let `u'` be the inverse image of `u` on `X'`.  If `𝒢` is of
finite type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the support of `𝒢`, then the surjectivity
loci of `u` and `u'` agree and so do their vanishing loci.

Both equalities come from the corresponding conditions at a single test scheme: the comparison
`X' ×_Y T ⟶ X ×_Y T` of the two base changes is flat and its image contains the support of the
base change of `𝒢`, so surjectivity and vanishing descend along it, and the loci, being
subterminal, are determined by the conditions.

The form with the quasi-coherence of `g^*ℱ` and `g^*𝒢` discharged by Stacks 03GA is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.surjFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.G)
    (hGsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.G) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.pullbackSituation g hF hG).surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) ∧
      D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.pullbackSituation g hF hG).zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (1) over `pullbackSituation`; see `inverseImageSituation`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.injFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (2).**  In the situation of Stacks 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat
morphism of algebraic spaces and let `u'` be the inverse image of `u` on `X'`.  If `ℱ` is of
finite type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the support of `ℱ`, then the universal
injectivity loci of `u` and `u'` agree and so do their vanishing loci.

Universal injectivity at a test scheme is injectivity of the base change over every further test
scheme, and the two situations have the same test schemes, so the equality of the two universal
injectivity loci follows from injectivity agreeing at every single test scheme, which is the
descent of injectivity along the comparison of the two base changes.

The form with the quasi-coherence of `g^*ℱ` and `g^*𝒢` discharged by Stacks 03GA is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.injFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injFunctor_and_zeroFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hFsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.F) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.injFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.pullbackSituation g hF hG).injFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) ∧
      D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
        (D.pullbackSituation g hF hG).zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (2) over `pullbackSituation`; see `inverseImageSituation`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083I part (3).**  In the situation of Stacks 083F let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat
morphism of algebraic spaces and let `u'` be the inverse image of `u` on `X'`.  If `ℱ` and `𝒢`
are of finite type and the image of `|X'| ⟶ |X|` contains the supports of both, then the
isomorphism loci of `u` and `u'` agree.

The comparison `X' ×_Y T ⟶ X ×_Y T` of the two base changes is flat and its image contains the
supports of the base changes of `ℱ` and of `𝒢`, so being an isomorphism descends along it at
every test scheme, and the loci, being subterminal, are determined by the conditions.

The form with the quasi-coherence of `g^*ℱ` and `g^*𝒢` discharged by Stacks 03GA is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoFunctor_inverseImageSituation_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoFunctor_pullbackSituation_eq (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.G)
    (hFsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.F) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom))
    (hGsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS D.X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.G) ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom)) :
    D.isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
      (D.pullbackSituation g hF hG).isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (3) over `pullbackSituation`; see `inverseImageSituation`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_isoFunctor_of_surj_of_inj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083J, clause (3), reduced.**  The isomorphism locus `F_iso` is limit preserving
once the surjectivity locus `F_surj` and the universal injectivity locus `F_inj` are.

The source deduces clause (3) from clauses (1) and (2) through the kernel of `u_{T_0}`; this is
the balanced-category route, available because the categories of `𝒪`-modules at hand are
abelian, hence balanced.  It needs no finiteness hypothesis at all.  What is carried is limit
preservation of `F_surj` — clause (1) — and of `F_inj`.

**`hinj` is not supplied by Stacks 083J.**  The tag's three clauses are about `F_surj`, `F_zero`
and `F_iso`; limit preservation of `F_inj` is asserted by none of them, so this is a reduction of
clause (3) to a statement the source does not prove.  Worse for its usefulness, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.injFunctor_eq_isoFunctor_of_epi` the two functors
`F_inj` and `F_iso` coincide as soon as `u` is an epimorphism, so on the situations the source's
own proof of clause (3) reduces to — those where clause (1) has produced a stage with `u`
surjective — `hinj` is verbatim this theorem's conclusion and `hsurj` holds for free.  Neither
carry follows from the conclusion in general, so the statement is not circular; but clause (3) is
a theorem with nothing carried,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_isoFunctor` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ModuleMapLociLimitPreservingUnconditional.lean`, by the
source's own route — `limitPreserving_isoFunctor_iff_kernelSituation` at the stage clause (1)
provides, with Stacks 082T for finite type of the kernel there.  Prefer that.  This statement is
kept because it asks for no finiteness at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_isoFunctor_of_surj_of_inj
    (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS) (P : ModulePullbackSystem.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hsurj : LimitPreserving.{u, u, w, w'} D.testScheme (D.surjFunctor P))
    (hinj : LimitPreserving.{u, u, w, w'} D.testScheme (D.injFunctor P)) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, w, w'} D.testScheme (D.isoFunctor P)
declarations.comment: clause (3), reduced to clause (1) and limit preservation of F_inj; both carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_surjFunctor_iff_cokernelSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083J, clause (1), reduced to clause (2).**  The surjectivity locus `F_surj` of `u`
is limit preserving exactly when the vanishing locus `F_zero` of the cokernel situation is.

The hypotheses of the two clauses match on the nose: the source module of the cokernel situation
is `𝒢` (`cokernelSituation_F`), so clause (1)'s hypothesis that `𝒢` be of finite type with
quasi-compact scheme-theoretic support over `B` *is* clause (2)'s hypothesis on the source
module of the cokernel situation, and the two situations have the same test category and the
same underlying-scheme functor (`cokernelSituation_testScheme`).  What is carried is clause (2)
itself — and clause (2) is now a theorem, so clause (1) is available outright as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_surjFunctor` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ModuleMapLociLimitPreservingUnconditional.lean`.  This
equivalence is the whole of that proof; it is stated here because it needs nothing of
clause (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_surjFunctor_iff_cokernelSituation :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, w, w'} D.testScheme (D.surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)) ↔
      LimitPreserving.{u, u, w, w'} D.testScheme
        ((D.cokernelSituation).zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: clause (1), reduced to clause (2) for the cokernel situation; (2) is carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_zeroFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083J, clause (2), at the source's hypotheses.**  In the situation of Stacks 083F,
if `ℱ` is of finite type and the scheme-theoretic support of `ℱ` (Stacks 07U1) is quasi-compact
over `B`, then the vanishing locus `F_zero` is limit preserving.

The support hypothesis is the source's sentence verbatim: the composite of the inclusion of the
scheme-theoretic support `Z ⟶ X` with `f : X ⟶ B` is a quasi-compact morphism.  It implies the
compactness at the affine stages that the proof spends, by
`hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport`, and then this is
`limitPreserving_zeroFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_zeroFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hFqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS D.X D.F).ι ≫ D.f.hom)) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} D.testScheme
      (D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: clause (2): F_zero is limit preserving, at the source's hypotheses verbatim -- F of finite type and its scheme-theoretic support (07U1) quasi-compact over B, i.e. Z -> X -> B quasi-compact. Nothing is carried: the support hypothesis gives compactness of the support at the affine stages (hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport: 03HF on the pasted square Z x_X X_T = Z x_B T, 07U0(4), 03H4), and the rest is limitPreserving_zeroFunctor. The index universe is the universe of the schemes, and must be: the clause is FALSE one universe up, by SmallnessNecessary/Basic.lean

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_surjFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083J, clause (1), at the source's hypotheses.**  In the situation of Stacks 083F,
if `𝒢` is of finite type and the scheme-theoretic support of `𝒢` (Stacks 07U1) is
quasi-compact over `B`, then the surjectivity locus `F_surj` is limit preserving.

The cokernel situation has source module `𝒢`, source space `X` and structure morphism `f`, so
`hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport` applied to it turns
the source's hypothesis on `𝒢` into the one `limitPreserving_surjFunctor` asks for.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_surjFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.G)
    (hGqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS D.X D.G).ι ≫ D.f.hom)) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} D.testScheme
      (D.surjFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: clause (1): F_surj is limit preserving, at the source's hypotheses verbatim -- G of finite type and its scheme-theoretic support (07U1) quasi-compact over B, i.e. Z -> X -> B quasi-compact. Nothing is carried: the support hypothesis on G is turned into compactness at the affine stages for the cokernel situation (whose source module is G) by hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport, and the rest is limitPreserving_surjFunctor. Index universe as in clause (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.limitPreserving_isoFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083J, clause (3), at the source's hypotheses.**  In the situation of Stacks 083F,
if `ℱ` is of finite type, `𝒢` is of finite presentation, and the scheme-theoretic supports of
`ℱ` and `𝒢` (Stacks 07U1) are quasi-compact over `B`, then the isomorphism locus `F_iso` is
limit preserving.

Both support hypotheses are the source's sentence verbatim, and
`hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport`, applied to the
situation and to its cokernel situation, turns them into the ones `limitPreserving_isoFunctor`
asks for; a module of finite presentation is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_isoFunctor_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hGfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.G)
    (hFqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS D.X D.F).ι ≫ D.f.hom))
    (hGqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS D.X D.G).ι ≫ D.f.hom)) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} D.testScheme
      (D.isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS))
declarations.comment: clause (3): F_iso is limit preserving, at the source's hypotheses verbatim -- F of finite type, G of finite presentation, and the scheme-theoretic supports (07U1) of F and G quasi-compact over B. Nothing is carried: the two support hypotheses are turned into compactness at the affine stages by hasQuasiCompactSupportOverTarget_of_isQuasiCompact_schemeTheoreticSupport (for the situation and for its cokernel situation), and the rest is limitPreserving_isoFunctor, the source's own deduction of (3) from (1) and (2) through ker(u_{T_0}) and Stacks 082T. Index universe as in clause (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapFlatTargetSituation.exists_closedSubscheme_isZeroAt_of_isZeroAt_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**The main clause of Stacks 083K.**

In Situation 0CWA — `S = \Spec(R)` affine, `X` an algebraic space over `S`, `u : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map
of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with `𝒢` flat over `S` — let `T ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact
morphism of schemes such that the base change `u_T` is zero.  Then there is a closed subscheme
`Z ⊆ S` such that (a) `T ⟶ S` factors through `Z` and (b) the base change `u_Z` is zero.

The subscheme is `Z = \Spec(\Gamma(S, ⊤)/I)` for `I = \ker(\Gamma(S, ⊤) ⟶ \Gamma(T, ⊤))`, the
smallest closed subscheme of `S` through which `T ⟶ S` factors; the factorisation is therefore
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_hom_specQuotientOver` at an equality of ideals.  That `I` kills
the image of `u` over every affine chart is
`val_app_mem_ker_smul_top_of_isZeroAt_of_quasiCompact`,
and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapFlatTargetSituation.isZeroAt_specQuotient_of_forall_mem_smul_top`
turns that into `u_Z = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubscheme_isZeroAt_of_isZeroAt_of_quasiCompact (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (B.inclusion.map T.hom))
    (hzero : (D.toModuleMapSituation B S hS).IsZeroAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
      (D.baseTest B S hS T)) :
    ∃ Z : BigFppfOver B S hS,
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion (B.inclusion.map Z.hom) ∧ Nonempty (T ⟶ Z) ∧
        (D.toModuleMapSituation B S hS).IsZeroAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
          (D.baseTest B S hS Z)
declarations.comment: main clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapFlatTargetSituation.exists_closedSubscheme_isZeroAt_locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isZeroAt_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**The finite-presentation clause of Stacks 083K, in the shape the source states it.**

In Situation 0CWA, assume in addition that `ℱ` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module whose scheme
theoretic support is quasi-compact, and let `T ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes such
that the base change `u_T` is zero.  Then there is a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ S`, locally of finite
presentation over `S` — and affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so of finite
presentation — through which `T ⟶ S` factors and at which `u_Z = 0`.

This is
`exists_fg_ideal_isZeroAt_specQuotient_of_quasiCompact`
with `Z = \Spec(\Gamma(S, ⊤)/J)`, whose closed immersion into `S` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_specQuotientToBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubscheme_isZeroAt_locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isZeroAt_of_quasiCompact
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (hcpt : CompactSpace (points B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS D.X D.F).toFunctor))
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hqc : QuasiCompact (B.inclusion.map T.hom))
    (hzero : (D.toModuleMapSituation B S hS).IsZeroAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
      (D.baseTest B S hS T)) :
    ∃ Z : BigFppfOver B S hS,
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion (B.inclusion.map Z.hom) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map Z.hom) ∧ Nonempty (T ⟶ Z) ∧
        (D.toModuleMapSituation B S hS).IsZeroAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)
          (D.baseTest B S hS Z)
declarations.comment: finite presentation clause

declarations.name: Module.exists_ideal_rTensor_eq_zero_iff_map_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 083L.** If the target of a linear map is projective, the base
changes on which the map vanishes are cut out by an ideal of the base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_rTensor_eq_zero_iff_map_eq_bot
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (f : M →ₗ[A] N) (hN : Module.Projective A N) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, ∀ (B : Type x) [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B),
      letI := φ.toAlgebra
      f.rTensor B = 0 ↔ Ideal.map φ I = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.zeroLocusRepresentation_of_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083M.**  In Situation 083F, assume that
1. `f` is locally of finite presentation,
2. `𝒢` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation flat over `B`,
3. the support of `𝒢` is proper over `B`.

Then the functor `F_zero` is an algebraic space and `F_zero ⟶ B` is a closed immersion; if `ℱ`
is of finite type, then `F_zero ⟶ B` is of finite presentation.

The conclusion `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.ZeroLocusRepresentation` is the
existence of a subfunctor `Z` of `B` which is a closed subspace (an algebraic space whose
inclusion is a closed immersion), whose inclusion is of finite presentation when `ℱ` is of finite
type, and which represents `F_zero`.  The hypotheses are exactly the source's.

The proof is the source's: pass to the closed subspace cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal of
`𝒢` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.nonempty_fittingReduction`) and apply Stacks
0CWC there, whose dévissage is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.devissageInput`.  The
case of the first paragraph of the proof, `f` of finite presentation, is the special case of a
morphism of finite presentation, which is in particular locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroLocusRepresentation_of_hasProperSupport (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hGfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.G)
    (hGflat : IsFlatOver B S hS D.X.property D.f.hom D.G)
    (hproper : HasProperSupport B S hS D.X.property D.Y.property D.f.hom
      (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hf)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.G)) :
    D.ZeroLocusRepresentation
declarations.comment: every case: f locally of finite presentation (which includes the case of the first paragraph of the proof, f of finite presentation), G of finite presentation and flat over B, the support of G proper over B; F_zero is represented by a closed subspace of B, of finite presentation over B when F is of finite type -- at the source's hypotheses alone

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoLocusRepresentation_of_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083N.**  In Situation 083F, assume that
1. `f` is locally of finite presentation,
2. `ℱ` is locally of finite presentation and flat over `B`,
3. the support of `ℱ` is proper over `B`, and
4. `u` is surjective.

Then the functor `F_iso` is an algebraic space and `F_iso ⟶ B` is a closed immersion; if `𝒢` is
of finite presentation, then `F_iso ⟶ B` is of finite presentation.

The conclusion `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.IsoLocusRepresentation` is the
existence of a subfunctor `Z` of `B` which is a closed subspace (an algebraic space whose
inclusion is a closed immersion), whose inclusion is of finite presentation when `𝒢` is of finite
presentation, and which represents `F_iso`.  Being of finite presentation is a local condition
for modules on a site, so `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite` is the source's "locally
of finite presentation".  The hypotheses are exactly the source's.

The proof is the source's: Stacks 083M applied to the kernel inclusion `Ker(u) ⟶ ℱ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.zeroLocusRepresentation_of_hasProperSupport` on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.kernelSituation`), transported to `F_iso` by
Stacks 0CVM and Stacks 082T
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoLocusRepresentation_of_kernelSituation`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocusRepresentation_of_hasProperSupport (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (hFflat : IsFlatOver B S hS D.X.property D.f.hom D.F)
    (hproper : HasProperSupport B S hS D.X.property D.Y.property D.f.hom
      (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hf)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj D.F))
    (hu : Epi D.u) :
    D.IsoLocusRepresentation
declarations.comment: the full statement at the source's hypotheses alone: f locally of finite presentation, F locally of finite presentation and flat over B with support proper over B, u surjective; F_iso is represented by a closed subspace of B, of finite presentation over B when G is of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 083P.** For an open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme,
scheme-theoretic density is equivalent to topological density together with containment of every
embedded point, and also to containment of every associated point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U,
      Dense (U : Set X) ∧ (∀ x : X, IsEmbeddedPoint X x → x ∈ U),
      Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints X ⊆ (U : Set X)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_gysinBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0ER3.** The square of Remark 0ER3 is cartesian: `D'` is the fibre product
`D ×_X X'`, by Stacks 083Q.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_gysinBaseChange :
    IsPullback (gysinBaseChangeHom D p hp p' hp' f E)
      (gysinBaseChangeSubspace D p hp p' hp' f E).1.ι E.1.ι f
declarations.comment: the square of Remark 0ER3 is cartesian

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.isPullback_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083Q.** The inverse image of a subfunctor along a morphism of presheaves is
canonically the fibre product of that subfunctor with the source of the morphism.
declarations.comment: fibre-product characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083Q.** The inverse image of a closed subspace of an algebraic space along a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed subspace of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubspace_preimage
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (Z : Subfunctor X)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS (Z.preimage f)
declarations.comment: closedness of inverse image

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.preimage
registrations.comment: inverse-image construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083R.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` the following are
equivalent: `f` is proper; the base change of `f` along every morphism to `Y` from a presheaf
represented by an object of the site is proper; the same for the objects with affine underlying
scheme; the base change of `f` along some surjective étale morphism to `Y` from a represented
presheaf is proper; and there is a Zariski covering of `Y` along each member of which the base
change of `f` is proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProper B S hS f,
        ∀ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj W ⟶ Y),
          IsProper B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj W ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
            IsProper B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            IsProper B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor Y) (_ : IsZariskiCover B S hS I U),
          ∀ i, IsProper B S hS (pullback.fst (U i).ι f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_ι_openComplement_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
Let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor on an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S`. Then
the inclusion of the open complement `X ∖ D` into `X` is an affine morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_ι_openComplement_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS (openComplement B S hS D.1).ι
declarations.comment: the complement is affine over the ambient algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_openComplement_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
Let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor on an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S`. Then
the open complement `X ∖ D` is scheme-theoretically dense in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_openComplement_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS (openComplement B S hS D.1)
declarations.comment: the complement is scheme theoretically dense in the ambient algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimensionAtPoint_lt_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
Let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor on an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S`, and
let `x` be a point of `|D|` at which the dimension of `X` is finite.  Then the dimension of `D`
at `x` is strictly smaller than the dimension of `X` at the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionAtPoint_lt_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D)
    (x : points B S hS D.1.toFunctor)
    (hfin : dimensionAtPoint B S hS X.1 X.2
      (pointsMap B S hS D.1.toFunctor D.1.ι x) < ⊤) :
    dimensionAtPoint B S hS D.1.toFunctor D.2.1 x <
      dimensionAtPoint B S hS X.1 X.2 (pointsMap B S hS D.1.toFunctor D.1.ι x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
The *sum* `D₁ + D₂` of two closed subspaces of an algebraic space `X`: the
closed subspace cut out by the product `𝓘_{D₁} 𝓘_{D₂}` of their defining ideals, formed on a
surjective étale scheme chart of `X` and descended.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sumClosedSubspaces (D₁ D₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1
declarations.comment: the sum of two effective Cartier divisors, for arbitrary closed subspaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
The sum is cut out by the product of the ideal sheaves of the summands: over an étale chart of
`X` lying over the chart on which it is formed, the defining ideal of `D₁ + D₂` is the ideal of
regular functions killed by the closed subscheme that the product of the chart ideal sheaves of
`D₁` and `D₂` cuts out there.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealAt_sumClosedSubspaces (D₁ D₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    (m : A ⟶ (⟨CostructuredArrow.mk (atlasHom B S hS X), atlasHom_etale B S hS X⟩ :
      SmallEtale B S hS X.1)) :
    definingIdealAt B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂) (op A) =
      RingHom.ker ((chartKer B S hS X D₁ A.1.hom *
        chartKer B S hS X D₂ A.1.hom).subschemeι.appTop).hom
declarations.comment: the sum of two effective Cartier divisors, for arbitrary closed subspaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_sumClosedSubspaces_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
On an affine étale chart the defining ideal of the sum is the product of
the defining ideals of the summands.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealAt_sumClosedSubspaces_of_isAffine (D₁ D₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj A.1.left)]
    (m : A ⟶ (⟨CostructuredArrow.mk (atlasHom B S hS X), atlasHom_etale B S hS X⟩ :
      SmallEtale B S hS X.1)) :
    definingIdealAt B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂) (op A) =
      definingIdealAt B S hS X D₁ (op A) * definingIdealAt B S hS X D₂ (op A)
declarations.comment: the sum of two effective Cartier divisors, for arbitrary closed subspaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083V.** The sum of two effective Cartier divisors on an algebraic space is again an
effective Cartier divisor: its defining ideal sheaf is the tensor product of the defining ideal
sheaves of the summands, and a tensor product of invertible sheaves is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_sumClosedSubspaces
    (hD₁ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D₁)
    (hD₂ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D₂) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_left_of_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083W.** If the sum `Z + Y` of two closed subspaces of an algebraic space is an
effective Cartier divisor, then so is the first summand `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_left_of_sumClosedSubspaces
    (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X Z Y)) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X Z
declarations.comment: effectivity of the first closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_right_of_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083W.** If the sum `Z + Y` of two closed subspaces of an algebraic space is an
effective Cartier divisor, then so is the second summand `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_right_of_sumClosedSubspaces
    (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X Z Y)) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X Y
declarations.comment: effectivity of the second closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_sumClosedSubspaces_of_definingIdealAt_eq_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083W.** A closed subspace `D` of an algebraic space whose defining ideal is, on
every affine étale chart lying over the chart carrying the sum, the product of the defining
ideals of `Z` and `Y` is the sum `Z + Y` of Stacks 083U: that chartwise formula is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_sumClosedSubspaces_of_isAffine` asserts of the sum, and
it determines a closed subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_sumClosedSubspaces_of_definingIdealAt_eq_mul
    (hD : ∀ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj A)) →
      (A ⟶ sumAtlasChart B S hS X) →
        definingIdealAt B S hS X D (op A) =
          definingIdealAt B S hS X Z (op A) * definingIdealAt B S hS X Y (op A)) :
    D = sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X Z Y
declarations.comment: identification with the sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_definingIdealAt_eq_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083W.** Let `Z, Y` be two closed subspaces of an algebraic space `X` with defining
ideal sheaves `ℐ` and `𝒥`.  If `ℐ𝒥` defines an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X`, then `Z` and
`Y` are effective Cartier divisors and `D = Z + Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_definingIdealAt_eq_mul
    (hD : ∀ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj A)) →
      (A ⟶ sumAtlasChart B S hS X) →
        definingIdealAt B S hS X D (op A) =
          definingIdealAt B S hS X Z (op A) * definingIdealAt B S hS X Y (op A))
    (h : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X Z ∧ IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X Y ∧
      D = sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X Z Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyPrincipal_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083X.** The inverse image of a locally principal closed subspace along a morphism
of algebraic spaces is a locally principal closed subspace of the source.

The defining ideal of `f⁻¹(Z)` on an affine chart `T` of `Y` lying over an affine chart `U` of
`X` is the ideal generated by the image of the defining ideal of `Z` on `U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_preimage_eq_map`), because the closed subscheme
`Z ×_X T` of `T` is the base change of the closed subscheme `Z ×_X U` of `U`.  Local principality
is then inherited chart by chart: every point of a chart of `Y` has such a pair `(T, U)` above
it with the defining ideal of `Z` on `U` generated by a single section, and the pullback of that
section generates the defining ideal of `f⁻¹(Z)` on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_preimage (f : Y ⟶ X) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZ : IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS X Z) :
    IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS Y ⟨Z.1.preimage f.hom,
      isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS f.hom Z.1 X.2 Y.2 Z.2⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPullbackDefined
declarations.doc:
The *pullback of a closed subspace `D ⊆ X` along a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces is
defined* when the inverse image `f⁻¹(D) ⊆ Y` is an effective Cartier divisor; in that case
`f^*D = f⁻¹(D)` is the *pullback of the effective Cartier divisor*.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsPullbackDefined {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083Z (2).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y` along a flat
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is defined.

A surjective étale scheme chart `q : V ⟶ Y` lifts to a surjective étale scheme chart
`p : U ⟶ X` sitting over it by a morphism `α : U ⟶ V` of the site, and `α` is flat because `f`
is.  By Stacks 083C the inverse image of `D` is an effective Cartier divisor on `V`, hence by
the scheme case Stacks 02OO also on `U`; and the inverse image of `D` on `U` through `α` is the
inverse image of `f⁻¹(D)` through `p`, so Stacks 083C applies again, on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_isFlat {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS Y D)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) :
    IsPullbackDefined B S hS f D
declarations.comment: part (2): a flat morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_weaklyAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 083Z (1).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y` along a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is defined as soon as `f` carries no weakly associated point of
`X` into `|D|`.

A surjective étale scheme chart `q : V ⟶ Y` lifts to a surjective étale scheme chart
`p : U ⟶ X` over a morphism `α : U ⟶ V` of the site.  By Stacks 083C the inverse image of `D` is
an effective Cartier divisor on `V`, and the ideal sheaf of `f⁻¹(D) ×_X U` is its inverse image
along `α`; the scheme case Stacks 02OO (1) therefore applies, because a weakly associated point
of `U` lying over `|D ×_Y V|` would be a weakly associated point of `X` carried into `|D|`.
Stacks 083C then returns the conclusion on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_weaklyAssociatedPoints {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS Y D)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X,
      pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x ∉
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS D.1.toFunctor D.1.ι)) :
    IsPullbackDefined B S hS f D
declarations.comment: part (1): no weakly associated point of the source is carried into the divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalPreimage_id
declarations.doc:
**The exceptional divisor of a blowup is an effective Cartier divisor on the fibre product
in which the strict transform lives.**

Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowup of an algebraic space `X` in a closed subspace `Z`, and let
`E = b^{-1}Z ⊆ X'` be its exceptional divisor.  Then the preimage of `E` along the projection
`X ×_X X' ⟶ X'` — the subspace the strict transform of an `𝒪_X`-module divides out the sections
supported on — is an effective Cartier divisor on `X ×_X X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalPreimage_id {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1} {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS (strictTransformPullback B S hS (𝟙 X) b)
      ⟨exceptionalPreimage B S hS (𝟙 X) b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1,
        exceptionalPreimage_isClosedSubspace B S hS (𝟙 X) b
          (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).2⟩
declarations.comment: part (2), at the exceptional divisor of a blowup

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preimage_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0840.** The inverse image of a sum of closed subspaces is the sum of the inverse
images: `f^*(D₁ + D₂) = f^*D₁ + f^*D₂` for the sum of Stacks 083U.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimage_sumClosedSubspaces (f : Y ⟶ X) (D₁ D₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    (⟨(sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂).1.preimage f.hom,
        isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS f.hom (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂).1 X.2 Y.2
          (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂).2⟩ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) =
      sumClosedSubspaces B S hS Y
        ⟨D₁.1.preimage f.hom, isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS f.hom D₁.1 X.2 Y.2 D₁.2⟩
        ⟨D₂.1.preimage f.hom, isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS f.hom D₂.1 X.2 Y.2 D₂.2⟩
declarations.comment: the inverse image commutes with the sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_sumClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0840.** If the pullbacks of two closed subspaces along `f : Y ⟶ X` are defined,
then so is the pullback of their sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_sumClosedSubspaces (f : Y ⟶ X) (D₁ D₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (h₁ : IsPullbackDefined B S hS f D₁) (h₂ : IsPullbackDefined B S hS f D₂) :
    IsPullbackDefined B S hS f (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂)
declarations.comment: the pullback of the sum is defined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.associatedInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
The *invertible sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` associated to an effective Cartier divisor* `D ⊆ X`: the
inverse tensor power `𝓘_D^{⊗ -1}` of its defining ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def associatedInvertibleSheaf (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: part (1): the associated invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.associatedInvertibleSheaf_isInvertible
declarations.doc: The sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` associated to an effective Cartier divisor is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedInvertibleSheaf_isInvertible (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property
      (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)
declarations.comment: part (1): the associated invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealSheafHom
declarations.doc:
The sheaf-hom `SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(𝓘_D, 𝒪_X)`, the second description of `𝒪_X(D)`. Its sections over
an étale chart `U` are the morphisms `𝓘_D|_U ⟶ 𝒪_X|_U` of `𝒪_X|_U`-modules on the slice site over
`U`, hence live one universe above the sections of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def idealSheafHom (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: part (1): the associated invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
The two descriptions of `𝒪_X(D)` agree: a section of `𝓘_D^{⊗ -1}` over an étale chart `U`
is the same thing as a morphism `𝓘_D|_U ⟶ 𝒪_X|_U`, by a linear equivalence of sections.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    (modulePresheaf B S hS X (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)).obj (Opposite.op U)
        ≃ₗ[(structureCommRings B S hS X).obj (Opposite.op U)]
      internalHomObj (structureCommRings B S hS X)
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D))
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))) U
declarations.comment: part (1): the associated invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
The identification of the two descriptions of `𝒪_X(D)` is given by the evaluation pairing: the
morphism `𝓘_D|_U ⟶ 𝒪_X|_U` attached to a section `s` of `𝓘_D^{⊗ -1}` over `U` sends a section `t`
of `𝓘_D` over an étale chart `V` over `U` to the value of the evaluation pairing on the restriction
of `s` tensored with `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv_apply (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    (s : (modulePresheaf B S hS X
      (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)).obj (Opposite.op U))
    (V : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ) (f : V.unop ⟶ U)
    (t : (modulePresheaf B S hS X (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D)).obj V) :
    homSectionCoeff (structureCommRings B S hS X)
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D))
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))) U
        (associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv B S hS X D hD U s) V f t =
      tensorHomAt (structureCommRings B S hS X)
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD))
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D))
        (modulePresheaf B S hS X (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
        (tensorPairing (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property
          (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D) (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)
          (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))
          (associatedInvertibleSheafEvaluation B S hS X D hD)) V
        ((modulePresheaf B S hS X
          (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)).restrictₛₗ f.op s ⊗ₜ t)
declarations.comment: part (1): the associated invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalSection
declarations.doc:
The *canonical section* `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)`: the global section corresponding, under the
identification of `𝒪_X(D)` with `SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(𝓘_D, 𝒪_X)`, to the inclusion `𝓘_D ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalSection (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD).sections
declarations.comment: part (2): the canonical section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalSection_apply
declarations.doc:
The canonical section of `𝒪_X(D)` is, on every étale chart, the inclusion `𝓘_D ⟶ 𝒪_X` read
through the identification of `𝒪_X(D)` with `SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(𝓘_D, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalSection_apply (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ) :
    associatedInvertibleSheafHomEquiv B S hS X D hD U.unop
        ((canonicalSection B S hS X D hD).val U) =
      idealInclusionSection B S hS X D U
declarations.comment: part (2): the canonical section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.negativeDivisorSheaf
declarations.doc: The sheaf `𝒪_X(-D) = 𝒪_X(D)^{⊗ -1}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def negativeDivisorSheaf (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: part (3): the negative of a divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.negativeDivisorSheafIso
declarations.doc: The identification `𝒪_X(-D) ≅ 𝓘_D`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def negativeDivisorSheafIso (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    negativeDivisorSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D
declarations.comment: part (3): the negative of a divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.differenceDivisorSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `𝒪_X(D - D') = 𝒪_X(D) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(-D')` attached to a pair of effective Cartier
divisors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differenceDivisorSheaf (D D' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D)
    (hD' : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D') :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: part (4): the difference of two divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_tensorInvertibleSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0842.** For two effective Cartier divisors `D₁, D₂` on an algebraic space `X` with
sum `D = D₁ + D₂` there is a *unique* isomorphism
`𝒪_X(D₁) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(D₂) ⟶ 𝒪_X(D)` carrying `1_{D₁} ⊗ 1_{D₂}` to `1_D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_tensorInvertibleSheafIso :
    ∃! e : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
        ⟨(structureCommRings B S hS X), Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _
        ((structureCommRings B S hS X)) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        ((structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property)⟩).obj
        ((associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D₁ hD₁))).obj
        ((associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D₂ hD₂))) ≅
        associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂)
          (isEffectiveCartierDivisor_sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂ hD₁ hD₂),
      ∀ U : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ,
        (e.hom.val.app U).hom
            ((tensorCanonicalSection B S hS X D₁ D₂ hD₁ hD₂).val U) =
          (canonicalSection B S hS X (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂)
            (isEffectiveCartierDivisor_sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X D₁ D₂ hD₁ hD₂)).val U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularSection_iff_etaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0844, conditions (1) and (2).** A global regular function on an algebraic space
is a regular section of the structure sheaf if and only if its image in the étale local ring
at every geometric point is a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_etaleLocalRing (f : GlobalFunctions B S hS X hX) :
    IsRegularSection (structurePresheaf B S hS X)
        (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B S hS X hX) f ↔
      ∀ (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x),
        IsSMulRegular (etaleLocalRing B S hS X x)
          (etaleLocalRingGerm B S hS X x (op V)
            (chartValue B S hS X hX f V.chart))
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularSection_iff_affineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0844, conditions (1) and (3).** A global regular function on an algebraic space
is a regular section of the structure sheaf if and only if its restriction to every affine
étale chart is a nonzerodivisor there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_affineEtale (f : GlobalFunctions B S hS X hX) :
    IsRegularSection (structurePresheaf B S hS X)
        (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B S hS X hX) f ↔
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, IsAffine (etaleChartScheme B S hS U) →
        IsSMulRegular (Γ(etaleChartScheme B S hS U, ⊤))
          (chartValue B S hS X hX f U)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularSection_iff_exists_surjectiveChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0844, conditions (1) and (4).** A global regular function on an algebraic space
is a regular section of the structure sheaf if and only if there is a surjective étale scheme
chart on which its restriction is a regular section.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_exists_surjectiveChart (f : GlobalFunctions B S hS X hX) :
    IsRegularSection (structurePresheaf B S hS X)
        (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B S hS X hX) f ↔
      ∃ C : SmallEtale B S hS X, IsSurjective B S hS C.obj.hom ∧
        IsRegularSection (etaleChartScheme B S hS C).presheaf
          ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ (etaleChartScheme B S hS C).presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).mp
              (etaleChartScheme B S hS C).IsSheaf)
          (chartFunctionSections B S hS X hX f C)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroSchemeSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0845.** Intersect the closed subspaces whose defining ideals are contained in the
ideals generated by local evaluations of the section.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zeroSchemeSubfunctor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections) : Subfunctor X.1
declarations.comment: underlying subfunctor construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroSchemeSubfunctor_isClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0845.** The subfunctor cut out by evaluation at a section of a module sheaf is a
closed subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSchemeSubfunctor_isClosedSubspace (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS (zeroSchemeSubfunctor B S hS X L s)
declarations.comment: closedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGreatest_zeroScheme_of_exists_definingIdealAt_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (1).**  Among the closed subspaces of `X` on which the section vanishes — read
chartwise: those whose defining ideal contains the evaluation ideal of the section on every
affine étale chart — the zero scheme of the section is the greatest.

The hypothesis is the surjectivity half of Stacks 03MB for the evaluation ideal: some closed
subspace of `X` has that ideal as its defining ideal on the affine étale charts.  It is used
only to see that the zero scheme is itself a member of the ordered set; the upper-bound half
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_zeroSchemeSubfunctor` is unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGreatest_zeroScheme_of_exists_definingIdealAt_eq (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections)
    (hZ : ∃ Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1 →
      definingIdealAt B S hS X Z (op U) = sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U) :
    IsGreatest {W : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1 |
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1 →
        sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U ≤ definingIdealAt B S hS X W (op U)}
      (zeroScheme B S hS X L s)
declarations.comment: part (1): maximality, with vanishing on a closed subspace read chartwise and with the realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_eq_zeroScheme_iff_of_exists_definingIdealAt_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (2).**  A morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces factors through the zero
scheme of the section exactly when the section vanishes after pullback along `f` — read
chartwise: on every affine étale chart `U` of `X` the evaluation ideal of the section is killed
by pullback of regular functions along every point of `Y` lying over `U`.

The hypothesis is the same one as in part (1), and is used only for the direction from factoring
to vanishing; the converse
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_eq_zeroScheme_of_sectionEvaluationIdealAt_le` is
unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comp_eq_zeroScheme_iff_of_exists_definingIdealAt_eq
    (X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections)
    (hZ : ∃ Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1 →
      definingIdealAt B S hS X Z (op U) = sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (⟨(zeroScheme B S hS X L s).1.toFunctor,
        (zeroScheme B S hS X L s).2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS),
      g ≫ ObjectProperty.homMk (zeroScheme B S hS X L s).1.ι = f) ↔
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U.1.left) →
        ∀ (a : BigFppfOver B S hS) (k : a ⟶ U.1.left) (y : yoneda.obj a ⟶ Y.1),
          yoneda.map k ≫ U.1.hom = y ≫ f.hom →
            sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U ≤
              RingHom.ker (Scheme.Γ.map ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k).op).hom
declarations.comment: part (2): factorization, with vanishing of the pulled-back section read chartwise and with the realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme_of_epi_inverseTensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (3).**  The zero scheme of a section of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module is a
locally principal closed subspace of `X`.

Two hypotheses are carried, and both are used.  The first is an epimorphism `p` onto the
defining ideal sheaf of the zero scheme from the inverse tensor power `L^{⊗ -1}` of Stacks
01CU, which in the source is the image factorization of the evaluation map `L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X`
cutting out `Z(s)`; its source is pinned to `L^{⊗ -1}` rather than left arbitrary, since for an
arbitrary source the identity of the ideal sheaf would witness the hypothesis.  The second is
local generation of `L^{⊗ -1}` by one section, which for an invertible module is the descent
clause of Stacks 0B8M.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme_of_epi_inverseTensorPower (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    (hfree : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
        (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L (-1)) 1)
    (p : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
        (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L (-1) ⟶
      idealSheafOfModules B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s))
    (hp : Epi p) :
    IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s)
declarations.comment: part (3): locally principal, assuming an epimorphism onto the ideal sheaf from the inverse tensor power of the invertible module and local generation of that power by one section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_zeroScheme_eq_span_generator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (4), first half, read chartwise.**  On an affine étale chart `U` of `X` where
`L` is free of rank one, with generator `t` and coordinate functional `l₀`, the zero scheme of
the section is cut out by the single regular function `l₀(s|_U)`.

The hypothesis is the one of parts (1) and (2): some closed subspace of `X` has the evaluation
ideal of the section as its defining ideal on the affine étale charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealAt_zeroScheme_eq_span_generator (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections)
    (hZ : ∃ Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1 →
      definingIdealAt B S hS X Z (op U) = sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U)
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1)
    (t : ToType (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (l₀ : Module.Dual
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).obj.obj
        (op U))
      (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (hb : ∀ x, l₀ x • t = x) :
    definingIdealAt B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s) (op U) =
      Ideal.span {l₀ (s.eval (op U))}
declarations.comment: part (4) read chartwise: the zero scheme is cut out on an affine chart by one regular function, with the realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGreatest_zeroScheme_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (1).**  Let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s` a global section of `L`.
Among the closed subspaces of `X` on which `s` vanishes — read chartwise: those whose defining
ideal contains the evaluation ideal of `s` on every affine étale chart — the zero scheme of `s`
is the greatest.

The hypotheses are the source's own and nothing else: invertibility of `L` discharges the
realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_definingIdealAt_eq_sectionEvaluationIdealAt_of_isInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGreatest_zeroScheme_of_isInvertible (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L)
    (s : L.sections) :
    IsGreatest {W : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1 |
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1 →
        sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U ≤ definingIdealAt B S hS X W (op U)}
      (zeroScheme B S hS X L s)
declarations.comment: part (1): maximality of the zero scheme among the closed subspaces on which the section vanishes, read chartwise, with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_eq_zeroScheme_iff_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (2).**  Let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s` a global section of `L`.
A morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces factors through the zero scheme of `s` exactly when
`s` vanishes after pullback along `f` — read chartwise: on every affine étale chart `U` of `X`
the evaluation ideal of `s` is killed by pullback of regular functions along every point of `Y`
lying over `U`.

The hypotheses are the source's own and nothing else: invertibility of `L` discharges the
realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_definingIdealAt_eq_sectionEvaluationIdealAt_of_isInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comp_eq_zeroScheme_iff_of_isInvertible (X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L)
    (s : L.sections) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (⟨(zeroScheme B S hS X L s).1.toFunctor,
        (zeroScheme B S hS X L s).2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS),
      g ≫ ObjectProperty.homMk (zeroScheme B S hS X L s).1.ι = f) ↔
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U.1.left) →
        ∀ (a : BigFppfOver B S hS) (k : a ⟶ U.1.left) (y : yoneda.obj a ⟶ Y.1),
          yoneda.map k ≫ U.1.hom = y ≫ f.hom →
            sectionEvaluationIdealAt B S hS X L s U ≤
              RingHom.ker (Scheme.Γ.map ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k).op).hom
declarations.comment: part (2): a morphism factors through the zero scheme exactly when the pulled-back section vanishes, read chartwise, with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_zeroScheme_eq_span_generator_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (4), first half, read chartwise.**  Let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and
`s` a global section of `L`.  On an affine étale chart `U` of `X` where `L` is free of rank one,
with generator `t` and coordinate functional `l₀`, the zero scheme of `s` is cut out by the
single regular function `l₀(s|_U)`.

Invertibility of `L` discharges the realization of the evaluation ideal by a closed subspace,
through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_definingIdealAt_eq_sectionEvaluationIdealAt_of_isInvertible`.
The chart data `t`, `l₀`, `hb` is local freeness of rank one on `U`, which for an invertible `L`
holds on a cover of `X` by Stacks 0B8Q; it is what makes the chartwise reading of the part a
statement about one regular function, and it is what the global form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection` supplies for
itself instead of assuming.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealAt_zeroScheme_eq_span_generator_of_isInvertible (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L)
    (s : L.sections)
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toSchemes B S hS X.1).obj U).1)
    (t : ToType (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (l₀ : Module.Dual
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).obj.obj
        (op U))
      (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (hb : ∀ x, l₀ x • t = x) :
    definingIdealAt B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s) (op U) =
      Ideal.span {l₀ (s.eval (op U))}
declarations.comment: part (4) read chartwise: the zero scheme is cut out on an affine chart by one regular function, with L carried as free of rank one on that chart by a generator t and a coordinate functional l₀; the chart U and the functional l₀ occur in the conclusion, which names the function as l₀ of the section over U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0846 (4).**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `L` be an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `s` be a global section of `L`.  The zero scheme `Z(s)` of
Stacks 0845 is an effective Cartier divisor on `X` if and only if `s` is a regular section of
`L` in the sense of Stacks 0843.

The hypotheses are the source's own and nothing else: no local freeness of `L` of rank one on a
chart, and no chart data, is assumed.  Invertibility of `L` supplies that data chart by chart,
by Stacks 0B8Q, and both sides of the equivalence are local on the small étale site of `X`, so
the chartwise content of the part can be assembled into the global statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection
    (hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s) ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structurePresheaf B S hS X.1)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).property s
declarations.comment: part (4): the zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor exactly when the section is regular, with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
The zero scheme of a global section `s` of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` is a locally
principal closed subspace of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme
    (hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L) :
    IsLocallyPrincipal B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s)
declarations.comment: part (3): the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module is a locally principal closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularSection_iff_forall_injective_mul_generator
declarations.doc:
**A global section of a module free of rank one on every étale chart is regular exactly when
the generators of its evaluation ideals are nonzerodivisors.**  This is the chartwise content of
Stacks 0846 (4): the zero scheme is cut out on each chart by the single element
`l₀(s|_U)`, and regularity of `s` is injectivity of multiplication by each of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_forall_injective_mul_generator (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections)
    (t : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, ToType (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (l₀ : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      Module.Dual ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).obj.obj (op U))
        (L.val.obj (op U)))
    (hb : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (x), l₀ U x • t U = x) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structurePresheaf B S hS X.1)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).property s ↔
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        Function.Injective
          (fun r : ToType ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).obj.obj (op U)) =>
            r * l₀ U (s.eval (op U)))
declarations.comment: part (4) read chartwise: the section is regular exactly when the functions cutting out the zero scheme are nonzerodivisors, with L carried as free of rank one on every chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iso_eq_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847, part (2): the isomorphism is unique.**  Let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier
divisor on an algebraic space `X` and let `s` be a global section of an `𝒪_X`-module `L`.  Two
isomorphisms `𝒪_X(D) ≅ L` which both carry the canonical section `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)` to `s` are
equal.

Composing one with the inverse of the other gives an endomorphism of `𝒪_X(D)` fixing `1_D`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_id_of_comp_eq_of_isInvertible` makes it the identity: `𝒪_X(D)` is
invertible and `1_D` is regular by part (1) of the same tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem iso_eq_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp_eq
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)) (s : L.sections)
    (i j : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ L)
    (hi : canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D hD ≫ i.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)
    (hj : canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D hD ≫ j.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) :
    i = j
declarations.comment: part (2): uniqueness of the isomorphism — two isomorphisms from the sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor to an invertible module, both carrying the canonical section to the given section, are equal; with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalSection_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847, part (1).** The canonical section `1_D` of the invertible sheaf `𝒪_X(D)`
attached to an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` is a regular section: multiplication by it is a
monomorphism `𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_X(D)`.  Tensoring by the invertible sheaf `𝓘_D` reflects monomorphisms,
and it turns multiplication by `1_D` into the inclusion `𝓘_D ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalSection_isRegular :
    IsRegularSection (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property
      (canonicalSection B S hS X D hD)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_associatedInvertibleSheaf_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847, part (2), existence.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and
let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module with a regular global section `s`.  Then there is an
effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` and an isomorphism `𝒪_X(D) ≅ L`.

Contraction with `s` is a monomorphism `L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X` whose image is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals isomorphic to `L^{⊗ -1}`; by Stacks 03MB that sheaf of ideals is the defining ideal sheaf
`𝓘_D` of a closed subspace `D`, which is therefore an effective Cartier divisor, and
`𝒪_X(D) ≅ L` because both are inverse to `𝓘_D`.
declarations.statement:
