theorem exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_associatedInvertibleSheaf_iso
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L)
    (s : L.sections)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property s) :
    ∃ (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D),
      Nonempty (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ L)
declarations.comment: part (2), existence: a regular global section of an invertible module cuts out an effective Cartier divisor whose associated invertible sheaf it is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_unique_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iso_canonicalSectionHom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847, part (2).**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `L` be an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module with a regular global section `s`.  Then there is a *unique* effective
Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X`, namely the zero scheme `Z(s)` of Stacks 0845, carrying a *unique*
isomorphism `𝒪_X(D) ≅ L` which takes the canonical section `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)` to `s`.

Contraction with `s` is a monomorphism `L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X` whose image is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals isomorphic to `L^{⊗ -1}`; by Stacks 03MB that sheaf of ideals is the defining ideal sheaf
`𝓘_D` of a closed subspace `D`, which is therefore an effective Cartier divisor.  The
identification of `𝓘_D` with `L^{⊗ -1}` carries the inclusion `𝓘_D ⟶ 𝒪_X` to contraction with
`s`, so the pairing `L ⊗ 𝓘_D ≅ 𝒪_X` it induces curries `s` to that inclusion, exactly as the
evaluation pairing `𝒪_X(D) ⊗ 𝓘_D ≅ 𝒪_X` curries `1_D`; the isomorphism matching the two pairings
therefore carries `1_D` to `s`.  Uniqueness of the divisor is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_zeroScheme_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp`, which also identifies it as
`Z(s)`, and uniqueness of the isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iso_eq_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iso_canonicalSectionHom_comp
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L)
    (s : L.sections)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property s) :
    ∃ (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D)
      (i : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ L),
      D = zeroScheme B S hS X L s ∧
      canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D hD ≫ i.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s ∧
      (∀ (D' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD' : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D')
          (i' : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D' hD' ≅ L),
        canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D' hD' ≫ i'.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s → D' = D) ∧
      ∀ i' : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ L,
        canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D hD ≫ i'.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s → i' = i
declarations.comment: part (2): a regular global section of an invertible module cuts out a unique effective Cartier divisor, the zero scheme of the section, carrying a unique isomorphism from its associated invertible sheaf to the module which takes the canonical section to the given section; with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.effectiveCartierDivisor_regularSectionPair_mutuallyInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847, part (3).**  The constructions `D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D)` and `(L, s) ↦ Z(s)` are
mutually inverse, so they are a bijection between the effective Cartier divisors on `X` and the
pairs consisting of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and a regular global section of it, taken up to
isomorphism of pairs.

The first conjunct is that `D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D)` lands in such pairs — `𝒪_X(D)` is invertible by
Stacks 0841 and `1_D` is regular by part (1) — and that the round trip
`D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D) ↦ Z(1_D)` is the identity, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroScheme_canonicalSection_eq`.  The second is that `(L, s) ↦ Z(s)`
lands in the effective Cartier divisors and that the round trip
`(L, s) ↦ Z(s) ↦ (𝒪_X(Z(s)), 1_{Z(s)})` returns `(L, s)` itself: there is an isomorphism
`𝒪_X(Z(s)) ≅ L` carrying the canonical section to `s`, which is part (2).  The third is that
`(L, s) ↦ Z(s)` is constant on isomorphism classes of pairs,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroScheme_eq_of_iso`, which is what makes it a map out of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierDivisor_regularSectionPair_mutuallyInverse :
    (∀ (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D),
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD) ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structureCommRings B S hS X)
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property (canonicalSection B S hS X D hD) ∧
          zeroScheme B S hS X (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)
            (canonicalSection B S hS X D hD) = D) ∧
      (∀ (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)),
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
          (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L → ∀ (s : L.sections),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection (structureCommRings B S hS X)
          (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property s →
        ∃ (hZ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s))
          (i : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s) hZ ≅ L),
          canonicalSectionHom B S hS X (zeroScheme B S hS X L s) hZ ≫ i.hom =
            L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ∧
      ∀ (L L' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)) (s : L.sections)
        (s' : L'.sections) (i : L ≅ L'), SheafOfModules.sectionsMap i.hom s = s' →
        zeroScheme B S hS X L s = zeroScheme B S hS X L' s'
declarations.comment: part (3): the constructions D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D) and (L, s) ↦ Z(s) are mutually inverse, hence a bijection between the effective Cartier divisors and the pairs of an invertible module with a regular global section taken up to isomorphism; with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroScheme_canonicalSection_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847 (2): an effective Cartier divisor is the zero scheme of its canonical
section.**  This is the assertion of the source that the construction `D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D)` followed
by `(L, s) ↦ Z(s)` is the identity on effective Cartier divisors.

The evaluation ideal of `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)` of Stacks 0845 is the defining ideal of `D` on every
affine étale chart, and a closed subspace whose defining ideal is the evaluation ideal on every
affine chart is the zero scheme, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroSchemeSubfunctor_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_canonicalSection_eq :
    zeroScheme B S hS X (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD)
        (canonicalSection B S hS X D hD) = D
declarations.comment: part (2): the construction D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D) followed by (L, s) ↦ Z(s) is the identity on effective Cartier divisors, with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_zeroScheme_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0847 (2): the effective Cartier divisor is unique.**  Let `L` be an `𝒪_X`-module with
a global section `s`.  An effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` carrying an isomorphism
`𝒪_X(D) ≅ L` which sends the canonical section `1_D` to `s` is the zero scheme `Z(s)` of
Stacks 0845 — so there is at most one such divisor.

The isomorphism matches the evaluation ideals of the two pairs, so the defining ideal of `D` is
the evaluation ideal of `(L, s)` on every affine étale chart, which by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroSchemeSubfunctor_eq` makes `D` the zero scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_zeroScheme_of_canonicalSectionHom_comp
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : L.sections)
    (i : associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X D hD ≅ L)
    (hi : canonicalSectionHom B S hS X D hD ≫ i.hom = L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) :
    D = zeroScheme B S hS X L s
declarations.comment: part (2): uniqueness of the divisor — an effective Cartier divisor with an isomorphism from its associated invertible sheaf to L carrying the canonical section to s is the zero scheme of s, with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0849.** A scheme `S`, an algebraic space `X` over `S`, and a quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_X`-algebra, commutative and concentrated in nonnegative degrees: the data from which the
relative homogeneous spectrum `Proj_X(𝒜)` is built.
declarations.statement: structure RelativeProjSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The functor `F` of Stacks 084A** for Situation 0849: on a test object `T` the limit, over
the quasi-compact test objects `W ⟶ T`, of the unions `F(W)` of the classes of quadruples
`(d, f, ℒ, ψ)`, and on a quasi-compact `T` the union `F(T)` itself
(`relativeProjFunctorEquivF`).

Its restriction maps are the pullback of quadruples (`relativeProjFunctorEquivF_map_mk`), its
value on an arbitrary test object is the limit over the quasi-compact opens
(`bijective_restrictCompactOpens`), and on a quasi-compact test object two quadruples have the
same class exactly when they are equivalent in the sense of 084A
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjQcohSheaf.F.mk_eq_mk_iff_equivalent`).
declarations.statement: def relativeProjFunctor : (BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the functor F of quadruples for Situation 0849, constructed from the restriction datum f^*A of the situation: on a quasi-compact test scheme its value is the set of equivalence classes of quadruples (d, f, L, psi), on an arbitrary test scheme T the limit over the quasi-compact opens of T, with restriction maps the pullback of quadruples

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjFunctorEquivF_map_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084A, functoriality: the restriction map of `F` is the pullback of quadruples.**
For a morphism `τ : T' ⟶ T` of quasi-compact test objects and a point `x` of `F(T)` which is the
class of a quadruple `(d, f, ℒ, ψ)`, the restriction of `x` to `T'` is the class of the pullback
quadruple `(d, f ∘ τ, τ^*ℒ, τ^*ψ)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GradedAlgebraRestriction.quadrupleRestrict`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeProjFunctorEquivF_map_mk {T T' : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase}
    (τ : T' ⟶ T) (hT : CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase).obj T))
    (hT' : CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase).obj T'))
    (x : s.relativeProjFunctor.obj (op T)) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1) {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (P : (GradedAlgebraPoints.ofQuasicoherentFamily s.shrink.pointAlgebra).Quadruples T f d)
    (hx : s.relativeProjFunctorEquivF T hT x = GradedAlgebraPoints.F.mk _ f hd P) :
    s.relativeProjFunctorEquivF T' hT' (s.relativeProjFunctor.map τ.op x) =
      GradedAlgebraPoints.F.mk _ (yoneda.map τ ≫ f) hd
        (s.quadrupleRestriction.quadrupleRestrict τ f (yoneda.map τ ≫ f) rfl P)
declarations.comment: functoriality: on quasi-compact test schemes the restriction map of F along h : T' -> T sends the class of a quadruple (d, f, L, psi) to the class of its pullback (d, f o h, h^*L, h^*psi)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.bijective_restrictCompactOpens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084A: for an arbitrary test scheme `T`, `F(T) = lim_{V ⊆ T quasi-compact open}
F(V)`.**  The map sending a point `x` of `F(T)` to the family of its restrictions `x|_V`, read as
classes of quadruples over the quasi-compact opens `V` of `T`, is a bijection onto the families
of classes of quadruples over the quasi-compact opens which are compatible with the restrictions
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GradedAlgebraRestriction.FRestrict` along the inclusions.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_restrictCompactOpens (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase) :
    Function.Bijective (s.restrictCompactOpens T)
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary test scheme T, F(T) is the limit of F(V) over the quasi-compact opens V of T: restricting to the quasi-compact opens is a bijection onto the compatible systems of classes of quadruples over them

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjπ_app_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084A: the morphism `F ⟶ X` sends the quadruple `(d, f, ℒ, ψ)` to `f`.**  On a
quasi-compact test object `T`, a point of `F(T)` which is the class of a quadruple
`(d, f, ℒ, ψ)` is sent by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjπ` to the
`T`-point `f` of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeProjπ_app_mk (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)
    (hT : CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase).obj T))
    (x : s.relativeProjFunctor.obj (op T)) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1) {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (P : (GradedAlgebraPoints.ofQuasicoherentFamily s.shrink.pointAlgebra).Quadruples T f d)
    (hx : s.relativeProjFunctorEquivF T hT x = GradedAlgebraPoints.F.mk _ f hd P) :
    s.relativeProjπ.app (op T) x = yonedaEquiv f
declarations.comment: the morphism F -> X of functors sends the class of a quadruple (d, f, L, psi) to f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GradedAlgebraPoints.F
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084A.** The value `F(T)` on a test object of the functor of quadruples of the
relative homogeneous spectrum of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra: the union over `d ≥ 1`
of the sets of quadruples `(d, f : T → X, ℒ, ψ)` of degree `d`, modulo strict equivalence inside
a degree and the equivalence of Tag 01NW across degrees.

The identifications relate quadruples over one and the same `T`-point of `X`, so the set is
fibred over the `T`-points of `X`, which is the morphism a quadruple records. Two quadruples of
positive degree over one `T`-point have the same class exactly when they are equivalent in the
sense of 084A (a common multiple `m = a d = a' d'` and an isomorphism
`β : ℒ^{⊗ a} ≅ ℒ'^{⊗ a'}` matching the restrictions of `ψ` and `ψ'` to `f^*𝒜^{(m)}`):
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjQcohSheaf.F.mk_eq_mk_iff_equivalent`, the relation
`UnionRel` being cofinal equality (`unionRel_iff_cofinallyEqual`).

The functor `F : Sch^{opp} → Sets` of Stacks 084A, built from these sets for the restriction
datum of Situation 0849, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjFunctor`.
declarations.statement: def F (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the value F(T) of the functor on a test object, as the union over d ≥ 1 of the quadruples (d, f : T → X, L, psi) modulo strict equivalence inside a degree and the equivalence of Tag 01NW across degrees, the restriction of the graded algebra to the scheme points of X being a datum; the functor F itself, with its restriction maps and the limit over the quasi-compact opens, is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor
declarations.doc: **Stacks 084B, first assertion: the functor `F` of Stacks 084A is an algebraic space.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor :
    IsAlgebraicSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor
declarations.comment: first assertion: the functor F of Tag 084A is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084B, second assertion: `Z ×_X F = Proj_Z(g^*𝒜)`.** For every scheme point
`g : Z → X` an object of the site whose scheme is the relative Proj of the restriction `g^*𝒜`
(`relativeProjPoints_algebra`), with a cartesian square identifying it with `Z ×_X F`.

The restriction `g^*𝒜` is that of the re-presentation of `𝒜` with sections in the universe `u`
(`smallAlgebra`, compared with `𝒜` by `smallAlgebraEquiv`); when the sections of `𝒜` already lie
in `u` it is isomorphic to the restriction of `𝒜` itself by `shrinkPointAlgebraIso`.
declarations.statement: def relativeProjPoints : RelativeProjPoints s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjπ
declarations.comment: second assertion: for every morphism g : Z -> X from a scheme of the site, a canonical isomorphism Proj_Z(g^*A) = Z x_X F, as a cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.isPullback_projComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084B, third assertion: compatibility with further base change.** For a morphism
`h : Z' ⟶ Z` of test objects and a scheme point `g : Z → X`, the comparison morphism
`Proj_{Z'}((g ∘ h)^*𝒜) ⟶ Proj_Z(g^*𝒜)` exhibits the source as `Z' ×_Z Proj_Z(g^*𝒜)`; it is
compatible with the identifications with `Z ×_X F` and `Z' ×_X F` of the second assertion; and
it is the canonical one: the identification `Proj_{Z'}((g ∘ h)^*𝒜) ≅ Proj_{Z'}(h^*(g^*𝒜))` of
the restricted algebras followed by the base-change morphism of Tag 01O3.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_projComparison {Z Z' : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase}
    (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ s.space.1) (h : Z' ⟶ Z) :
    IsPullback (s.quadrupleRestriction.projComparison
      s.shrink.contains_relativeProj_pointAlgebra g h)
        (s.relativeProjPoints.fibreHom Z' (yoneda.map h ≫ g))
        (s.relativeProjPoints.fibreHom Z g) h ∧
      yoneda.map (s.quadrupleRestriction.projComparison
        s.shrink.contains_relativeProj_pointAlgebra g h) ≫
          s.relativeProjPoints.fibreToSpace Z g =
        s.relativeProjPoints.fibreToSpace Z' (yoneda.map h ≫ g) ∧
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase).map
          (s.quadrupleRestriction.projComparison s.shrink.contains_relativeProj_pointAlgebra g h) =
        (s.quadrupleRestriction.restrictProjIso g h).hom ≫
          Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjBaseChangeTwist.baseChangeHom
            (s.shrink.pointAlgebra Z g)
            ((BigFppfOver.toScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase).map h)
declarations.comment: third assertion: the identifications Proj_Z(g^*A) = Z x_X F are compatible with further base change Z' -> Z, through the canonical base-change morphism of Tag 01O3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.Proj
declarations.doc:
The relative homogeneous spectrum `Proj_X(𝒜)` of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra on
an algebraic space `X` over `S`: the algebraic space `F` of Stacks 084B, the functor of
quadruples, with structure morphism `π`.
declarations.statement: def Proj : AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase
declarations.comment: Proj_X(A): the algebraic space F of Tag 084B, with structure morphism pi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.π
declarations.doc: The structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` of the relative Proj.
declarations.statement: def π : s.Proj ⟶ s.space
declarations.comment: the structure morphism pi : Proj_X(A) -> X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.baseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
For a scheme point `g : Z ⟶ X`, the canonical isomorphism
`γ : Proj_Z(g^*𝒜) ≅ Proj_X(𝒜) ×_X Z` of Stacks 084B; the scheme of
`s.relativeProjPoints.fibre Z g` is `Proj_Z(g^*𝒜)` by `s.relativeProjPoints.fibreIso Z g`.
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism gamma : Proj_U(phi^*A) -> Proj_X(A) x_X U over U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.chartPresentation
declarations.doc:
For an étale presentation `(U, R)` of `X`, the relative Projs `P_U = Proj_U(𝒜_U)` and
`P_R = Proj_R(𝒜_R)` form an étale presentation of `Proj_X(𝒜)`: the chart
`P_U = Proj_X(𝒜) ×_X U ⟶ Proj_X(𝒜)` is surjective and étale and `P_U ×_{Proj_X(𝒜)} P_U = P_R`,
the two projections lying over the two maps `R ⇉ U` and exhibiting `P_R` as `P_U ×_U R` along
each.
declarations.statement: def chartPresentation : Presentation s.site s.base s.containsBase s.Proj.1 s.Proj.2
declarations.comment: the etale covering P_U -> Proj_X(A) with P_U x_P P_U = P_R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointTwistAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084D, clause (1), after base change to a scheme point of the base.**  The
quasi-coherent sheaf of `ℤ`-graded algebras `⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_{Proj_T(f^*𝒜)}(n)` on the base change
`T ×_X Proj_X(𝒜)` of the relative Proj along the `T`-point `f` of `X`, with its multiplication
and its unit.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointTwistAlgebra :
    SchemeGradedAlgebra (relativeProj (d.algebra T f)).scheme
declarations.comment: the base-change clause: for every scheme point f : T -> X of the base, the sheaf of Z-graded algebras (+)_{n in Z} O(n) -- homogeneous pieces, multiplication and unit, which are the three fields of the type -- on the base change Proj_T(f^*A) of the relative Proj, which d.fibreIso identifies with the scheme of T x_X Proj_X(A). It is Tag 01NR's graded algebra there, which is what the tag asks the base change to agree with. Quasi-coherence of the pieces is NOT part of this type; it is isQuasicoherent_pointTwist below. The sheaf on Proj_X(A) itself is NOT produced here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.isQuasicoherent_pointTwist
declarations.doc: **Stacks 084D, quasi-coherence of the twists after base change to a scheme point.**
declarations.statement: theorem isQuasicoherent_pointTwist (n : ℤ) : (d.pointTwist T f n).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the base-change clause, quasi-coherence half: every homogeneous twist O(n) on the base change Proj_T(f^*A) of the relative Proj along a scheme point f : T -> X of the base is a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointPsi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084D, clause (2), after base change to a scheme point of the base.**  The canonical
homomorphism of graded algebras `ψ : π^*𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪(n)`, read at the `T`-point `f` of `X` in
the adjoint form that Stacks 01NR produces: in each degree `n ≥ 0` a map
`(f^*𝒜)_n ⟶ (π_T)_*𝒪_{Proj_T(f^*𝒜)}(n)`.

That it is a homomorphism of graded algebras is `…pointPsi_one` and `…pointPsi_mul`, and
`…pointPsi_chart` identifies it on the projective-spectrum charts with the absolute
homogeneous-section map of Stacks 01MP, which is what makes it the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointPsi (n : ℕ) :
    (d.algebra T f).piece (n : ℤ) ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (relativeProj (d.algebra T f)).toBase).obj
        (d.pointTwist T f (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the base-change clause for psi: the degreewise maps of the canonical homomorphism psi : pi^*A -> (+)_{n >= 0} O(n) on the base change Proj_T(f^*A) of the relative Proj along a scheme point f : T -> X of the base, in the adjoint form (f^*A)_n -> (pi_T)_* O(n) that Tag 01NR produces psi in. This declaration is the family of maps and nothing more; that it preserves the unit, is multiplicative, and is Tag 01MP's homogeneous-section map on the charts are the three companion theorems pointPsi_one, pointPsi_mul and pointPsi_chart below. psi on Proj_X(A) itself is NOT produced here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointPsiHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084D, clause (2), after base change to a scheme point of the base, as a
homomorphism of graded algebras.**  The canonical homomorphism

`ψ : π_T^*(f^*𝒜) ⟶ ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_{Proj_T(f^*𝒜)}(n)`

of sheaves of `ℤ`-graded algebras on `Proj_T(f^*𝒜)`, where `π_T : Proj_T(f^*𝒜) ⟶ T` is the
structure morphism: the transpose across `π_T^* ⊣ (π_T)_*` of the homogeneous-section map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointPsi`, assembled with its multiplicativity
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjTwists.TwistData.psiTransposeHom`).  The source writes the
target as `⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪(n)`; since `π_T^*(f^*𝒜)` vanishes in negative degrees the two targets
receive the same homomorphisms, and the components in degrees `n ≥ 0` are the transposes of
`pointPsi` (`…pointPsiHom_app_natCast`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointPsiHom :
    Stacks.PullbackGradedAlgebra.pullbackGradedAlgebra
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjQcohSheaf.ringedSpaceHom
          (relativeProj (d.algebra T f)).toBase)
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjQcohSheaf.situationAlgebra (d.algebra T f))
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjQcohSheaf.isSheafStruct _) ⟶
      d.pointTwistAlgebra T f
declarations.comment: the base-change clause for psi as a homomorphism of graded algebras: on the base change Proj_T(f^*A) of the relative Proj along a scheme point f : T -> X of the base, the canonical homomorphism psi : pi_T^*(f^*A) -> (+)_n O(n) of sheaves of Z-graded algebras (multiplicative by construction), whose degree-n components for n >= 0 are the adjoint transposes of pointPsi. psi on Proj_X(A) itself is NOT produced here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointTwistTheta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01O3 at a scheme point of the base: the base-change isomorphism `θ`.**  For a further
morphism of schemes `g : Z ⟶ T`, the inverse image along the base-change morphism
`Proj_Z(g^*f^*𝒜) ⟶ Proj_T(f^*𝒜)` of the twists at the point `f` is the graded algebra of twists
of `Proj_Z(g^*f^*𝒜)`, as `ℤ`-graded algebras.

This is what makes the base-change clause of Stacks 084D a *compatible* family rather than a
statement at one point at a time, and it is the scheme-point case of the `θ` of Stacks 085C.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointTwistTheta {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : Z ⟶ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) :
    pbAlgS (baseChangeHom (d.algebra T f) g) (d.pointTwistAlgebra T f) ≅
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.twistAlgebra ((d.algebra T f).pullback g)
declarations.comment: the base-change clause is compatible with further base change: for g : Z -> T the inverse image of (+)_d O_{Proj_T(f^*A)}(d) along the base-change morphism is (+)_d O_{Proj_Z(g^*f^*A)}(d) as Z-graded algebras. This is Tag 01O3's theta, and it is the scheme-point case of the theta of Tag 085C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.basePsi_pointTwistTheta
declarations.doc:
**The base-change clause of Stacks 084D for `ψ`, at a scheme point of the base.**  For a
further morphism of schemes `g : Z ⟶ T`, the base change along `g` of the homogeneous-section
map `ψ` of the twists at the point `f` — the morphism
`g^*(f^*𝒜)_k ⟶ (π_Z)_* h^*𝒪_{Proj_T(f^*𝒜)}(k)` adjoint to
`(f^*𝒜)_k ⟶ (π_T)_*𝒪(k) ⟶ (π_T)_* h_* h^*𝒪(k)`, where `h : Proj_Z(g^*f^*𝒜) ⟶ Proj_T(f^*𝒜)` is the
base-change morphism (`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjBaseChangeTwist.basePsi`) — followed
by the isomorphism `θ` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjPoints.pointTwistTheta` is the
homogeneous-section map of Stacks 01NR for `Proj_Z(g^*f^*𝒜)`.

So the isomorphism `θ` of the graded algebras of twists is compatible with `ψ`: base change
carries the whole of Stacks 084D's datum at `f` — graded algebra and `ψ` — to Stacks 01NR's datum
on `Proj_Z(g^*f^*𝒜)`.  The proof is the gluing statement
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwistExistenceBasis.glueIso_psi` behind `θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem basePsi_pointTwistTheta {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T)
    (k : ℕ) :
    basePsi (relativeProj (d.algebra T f)).toBase
        (relativeProj ((d.algebra T f).pullback g)).toBase g
        (baseChangeHom (d.algebra T f) g) (baseChangeHom_comp_toBase (d.algebra T f) g)
        (d.pointPsi T f k) ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (relativeProj ((d.algebra T f).pullback g)).toBase).map
        ((d.pointTwistTheta T f g).hom.app (k : ℤ)) =
      (twistDataOfGradedAlgebra ((d.algebra T f).pullback g)).ψ k
declarations.comment: the base-change clause for psi, compatible with further base change: for g : Z -> T the base change along g of psi at the scheme point f, followed by Tag 01O3's theta (pointTwistTheta), is Tag 01NR's psi for Proj_Z(g^*f^*A), degree by degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.twistGradedAlgebra_psi_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084D on the relative Proj `P = Proj_X(𝒜)` of Situation 0849.**  For any presentation
`X = U/R` used to construct the twists:

1. `⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_P(n)` (`…RelativeProjSituation.twistGradedAlgebra`) is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
   `ℤ`-graded `𝒪_P`-algebras: its homogeneous pieces are the twists `𝒪_P(n)`, quasi-coherent, and
   its multiplication and unit are `…RelativeProjSituation.twistAlgebraMul` and
   `…RelativeProjSituation.twistAlgebraUnit`;
2. the canonical `ψ_n : π^*𝒜_n ⟶ 𝒪_P(n)`, `n ≥ 0` (`…RelativeProjSituation.psiTwistHom`), is a
   homomorphism of graded algebras `π^*𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(n)`: it carries the multiplication and
   the unit of `π^*𝒜` (`…RelativeProjSituation.psiSourceMul`,
   `…RelativeProjSituation.psiSourceUnit`) to those of the twists;
3. its base change to any scheme `f : T ⟶ X` over `X` agrees with Stacks 01NR: there are
   isomorphisms `e_{T,f,n} : (T ×_X P ⟶ P)^*𝒪_P(n) ≅ 𝒪(n)^a` with the twists of Stacks 01NR on
   `T ×_X P = Proj_T(f^*𝒜)`, carrying the inverse images of the multiplication, of the unit and of
   `ψ` to the multiplication, the unit and `ψ` of Stacks 01NR, and compatible with further base
   change along any `τ : T' ⟶ T` (through the comparison of twists of Tag 01O3).
declarations.statement:
theorem twistGradedAlgebra_psi_baseChange :
    -- (1) the quasi-coherent sheaf of `ℤ`-graded algebras `⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_P(n)`
    (∀ n : ℤ, (s.twistGradedAlgebra Px).piece n = (s.twistModule Px n).obj) ∧
    (∀ n : ℤ, ((s.twistGradedAlgebra Px).piece n).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
    (∀ i j : ℤ,
      haveI := SmallEtale.instHasSheafify s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}
      haveI := SmallEtale.instWEqualsLocallyBijective s.site s.base s.containsBase
        s.relativeProjFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u}
      SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.mulSheaf.{u, u + 1, u, u}
          (J := SmallEtale.topology s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor)
          (s.twistGradedAlgebra Px) i j =
        (modulesTensorObjIso s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor
            s.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor (s.twistModule Px i).obj
            (s.twistModule Px j).obj).inv ≫ s.twistAlgebraMul Px i j) ∧
    (haveI := SmallEtale.instHasSheafify s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}
     haveI := SmallEtale.instWEqualsLocallyBijective s.site s.base s.containsBase
        s.relativeProjFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u}
     SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.oneHom.{u, u + 1, u}
          (J := SmallEtale.topology s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor)
          (s.twistGradedAlgebra Px) = s.twistAlgebraUnit Px) ∧
    -- (2) `ψ : π^*𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(n)` is a homomorphism of graded algebras
    (∀ i j : ℕ, s.psiSourceMul (i : ℤ) (j : ℤ) ≫ s.psiTwistHom Px (i + j) =
      (s.psiTwistHom Px i ⊗ₘ s.psiTwistHom Px j) ≫ s.twistAlgebraMul Px (i : ℤ) (j : ℤ)) ∧
    s.psiSourceUnit ≫ s.psiTwistHom Px 0 = s.twistAlgebraUnit Px ∧
    -- (3) the base change to every scheme point is the graded algebra and `ψ` of Stacks 01NR
    ∃ e : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1) (n : ℤ),
        (modulePullback s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)).obj
          (s.twistModule Px n).obj ≅
          ((representedQuasicoherentSchemeEquivalence s.site s.base s.containsBase
            (s.relativeProjPoints.fibre T f)).functor.obj (s.twistPieceQcoh T f n)).obj,
      (∀ (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1)
        (i j : ℤ),
        (modulePullbackTensorIso s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)
            (s.twistModule Px i).obj (s.twistModule Px j).obj).inv ≫
          (modulePullback s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)).map
            (s.twistAlgebraMul Px i j) ≫ (e T f (i + j)).hom =
        ((e T f i).hom ⊗ₘ (e T f j).hom) ≫
          representedTensorChartMul s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.twistPieceMul T f i j)) ∧
      (∀ (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1),
        (modulePullbackUnitIso s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)).inv ≫
            (modulePullback s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)).map
              (s.twistAlgebraUnit Px) ≫ (e T f 0).hom =
          representedUnitChartHom s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.twistPieceUnit T f)) ∧
      (∀ (T : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1) (n : ℕ),
        (modulePullback s.site s.base s.containsBase (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f)).map
            (s.psiTwistHom Px n) ≫ (e T f (n : ℤ)).hom = s.fibrePsiHom T f n) ∧
      ∀ {T T' : BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase} (τ : T' ⟶ T)
        (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ s.space.1)
        {y : s.relativeProjPoints.fibre T' (yoneda.map τ ≫ f) ⟶ s.relativeProjPoints.fibre T f}
        (hy : s.relativeProjPoints.LiesOver y τ) (n : ℤ),
        e T' (yoneda.map τ ≫ f) n =
          eqToIso (congrArg (fun k :
              (⟨yoneda.obj (s.relativeProjPoints.fibre T' (yoneda.map τ ≫ f)),
                isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda s.site s.base s.containsBase _⟩ :
                AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase) ⟶
                  ⟨s.relativeProjFunctor, s.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor⟩ =>
              (modulePullback s.site s.base s.containsBase k).obj (s.twistModule Px n).obj)
              (s.representedSpaceMap_comp_fibreToSpaceHom τ f hy).symm) ≪≫
            attachedModuleIsoPullback
              (X := ⟨s.relativeProjFunctor, s.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor⟩)
              (s.twistModule Px n).obj (s.fibreToSpaceHom T f) y
              (e T f n) (s.twistPieceComparison τ rfl y hy n)
declarations.comment: on the constructed relative Proj P = Proj_X(A) itself: the quasi-coherent sheaf of Z-graded O_P-algebras (+)_n O_P(n) (twistGradedAlgebra: pieces, quasi-coherence, multiplication, unit), the canonical psi : pi^*A -> (+)_{n >= 0} O_P(n) as a homomorphism of graded algebras (multiplicative and unital), and for every scheme T -> X identifications of the base change with the graded algebra of Tag 01NR on Proj_T(f^*A) carrying multiplication, unit and psi to those of Tag 01NR, natural in the scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_relativeProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084E.** In the relative Proj situation of Stacks 0849, the structure morphism
`π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is separated.

There is no hypothesis on the graded algebra.  The relative Proj enters through a surjective
étale scheme chart of `X`, as Stacks 084B presents it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeProj {X P : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS P) (π : P ⟶ X)
    {t : Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.{u}} (d : RelativeProjChart B S hS π t) :
    IsSeparated B S hS π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_relativeProj_of_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084E, with the chart situation pinned to `𝒜`.** The structure morphism of the
relative Proj is separated, with no hypothesis on the graded algebra.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_relativeProj` read on the chart presentation whose
situation is the restriction `𝒜|_V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeProj_of_chart
    {P : (BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase P) (π : P ⟶ s.space.1)
    (c : RelativeProjSituationChart s π) :
    IsSeparated s.site s.base s.containsBase π
declarations.comment: for a chart presentation whose chart situation is the restriction of the graded algebra of the space, rather than an unrelated situation on the chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.isSeparated_relativeProjπ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084E.** In Situation 0849 the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` of the
relative homogeneous spectrum is separated.

There is no hypothesis on the graded algebra, exactly as in the source. Over a surjective étale
scheme chart `g : U ⟶ X` the base change of `π` is the scheme-level relative Proj of the
restriction `g^*𝒜` (Stacks 084B), whose structure morphism is separated (Stacks 01O2), and
separatedness descends along the chart (Stacks 03KM).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeProjπ :
    IsSeparated s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjπ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_relativeProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084F.** In the relative Proj situation of Stacks 0849, the structure morphism
`π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is quasi-compact if one of the following holds: `𝒜` is of finite type as a
sheaf of `𝒜₀`-algebras; `𝒜` is generated by `𝒜₁` as an `𝒜₀`-algebra and `𝒜₁` is a finite type
`𝒜₀`-module; or there is a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒜₀`-submodule `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜₊` such that
`𝒜₊/ℱ𝒜` is a locally nilpotent sheaf of ideals of `𝒜/ℱ𝒜`.

The relative Proj enters through a surjective étale scheme chart of `X`, as Stacks 084B
presents it, and the three hypotheses are those of Stacks 07ZX on the restricted algebra living
on that chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_relativeProj {X P : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS P) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (π : P ⟶ X)
    {t : Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.{u}} (d : RelativeProjChart B S hS π t)
    (h : t.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero ∨ t.IsFinitelyGeneratedInDegreeOne ∨
      t.HasNilpotentPositiveQuotient) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_relativeProj_of_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084F, with the chart situation pinned to `𝒜`.** The structure morphism of the
relative Proj is quasi-compact as soon as the restriction `𝒜|_V` satisfies one of the three
conditions of Stacks 07ZX.

The three conditions of the source are affine-local on the base, so for a quasi-coherent graded
algebra on `X` they hold exactly when they hold for the restriction to a surjective étale chart;
the version in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.RelativeProj` can only state them for a
situation unrelated to `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_relativeProj_of_chart
    {P : (BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase P) (π : P ⟶ s.space.1)
    (c : RelativeProjSituationChart s π)
    (h : c.situation.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero ∨
      c.situation.IsFinitelyGeneratedInDegreeOne ∨ c.situation.HasNilpotentPositiveQuotient) :
    IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase π
declarations.comment: with the three conditions read on the restriction of the graded algebra of the space to the chart, rather than on an unrelated situation on the chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.isQuasiCompact_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084F.** In Situation 0849 the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is
quasi-compact if, étale locally on `X`, one of the following holds: `𝒜` is of finite type as an
`𝒜₀`-algebra; `𝒜` is generated by `𝒜₁` as an `𝒜₀`-algebra and `𝒜₁` is a finite type
`𝒜₀`-module; there is a finite type `𝒜₀`-submodule `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜₊` such that `𝒜₊/ℱ𝒜` is a locally
nilpotent sheaf of ideals of `𝒜/ℱ𝒜`. Each condition holds at every étale point exactly when it
holds at one surjective étale point (`holdsAtEtalePoints_isFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero_iff` and its
siblings in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.RelativeProjPoint.EtaleLocalConditions`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_π
    (h : s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero ∨
      s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsFinitelyGeneratedInDegreeOne ∨
      s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.HasNilpotentPositiveQuotient) :
    IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteType_relativeProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084G.** In the relative Proj situation of Stacks 0849, if `𝒜` is of finite type as
a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras then the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is of finite type.

The relative Proj enters through a surjective étale scheme chart of `X`, as Stacks 084B
presents it, and the hypothesis is that of Stacks 07ZY on the restricted algebra living on that
chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_relativeProj {X P : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS P) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (π : P ⟶ X)
    {t : Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.{u}} (d : RelativeProjChart B S hS π t)
    (h : t.IsFiniteType) :
    IsFiniteType B S hS π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteType_relativeProj_of_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084G, with the chart situation pinned to `𝒜`.** The structure morphism of the
relative Proj is of finite type as soon as the restriction `𝒜|_V` is of finite type as a sheaf of
algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_relativeProj_of_chart
    {P : (BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase P) (π : P ⟶ s.space.1)
    (c : RelativeProjSituationChart s π) (h : c.situation.IsFiniteType) :
    IsFiniteType s.site s.base s.containsBase π
declarations.comment: with the finite type condition read on the restriction of the graded algebra of the space to the chart, rather than on an unrelated situation on the chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.isFiniteType_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084G.** In Situation 0849, if `𝒜` is of finite type as a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras,
the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` of the relative homogeneous spectrum is of finite
type.

The hypothesis is read étale locally, on the restriction `g^*𝒜` of Stacks 084B to every étale
scheme point `g` of `X` (taken through the `u`-small re-presentation of `𝒜`, identified with `𝒜`
by `smallAlgebraEquiv`); by `holdsAtEtalePoints_isFiniteType_iff` it suffices at one surjective
étale scheme point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_π
    (hft : s.HoldsAtEtalePoints Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFiniteType.IsFiniteType) :
    IsFiniteType s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.universallyClosed_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084H.** In Situation 0849, if `𝒪_X → 𝒜₀` is integral and `𝒜` is of finite type as
an `𝒜₀`-algebra, the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` of the relative homogeneous spectrum
is universally closed.

Both hypotheses are read étale locally, on the restriction `g^*𝒜` of Stacks 084B to every étale
scheme point `g` of `X` (taken through the `u`-small re-presentation of `𝒜`, identified with `𝒜`
by `smallAlgebraEquiv`); by `holdsAtEtalePoints_isIntegralInDegreeZero_iff` and
`holdsAtEtalePoints_isFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero_iff` it suffices at one surjective étale scheme
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_π
    (hint : s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsIntegralInDegreeZero)
    (hft : s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero) :
    UniversallyClosed s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_relativeProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084H.** In the relative Proj situation of Stacks 0849, if the structure sheaf maps
integrally into `𝒜₀` and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒜₀`-algebra, then the structure morphism
`π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is universally closed.

The relative Proj enters through a surjective étale scheme chart of `X`, as Stacks 084B
presents it, and the two hypotheses are the hypotheses of Stacks 07ZZ on the restricted algebra
living on that chart. Universal closedness is étale local on the target — the leg used is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_etale_atlas` of Stacks 03IT — so the conclusion
follows from the case of schemes, which is
`Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.universallyClosed_relativeProjToBase_of_isIntegralInDegreeZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_relativeProj {X P : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (π : P ⟶ X)
    {t : Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.{u}} (d : RelativeProjChart B S hS π t)
    (hint : t.IsIntegralInDegreeZero) (hft : t.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS π

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.properFiniteType_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084I.** For a relative `Proj` situation the two finite type conditions are
equivalent: that the degree-zero part of the graded algebra is a finite type module over the
structure sheaf and the graded algebra is of finite type over its degree-zero part, and that the
degree-zero part is a finite type module over the structure sheaf and the graded algebra is of
finite type over the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem properFiniteType_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [s.IsDegreeZeroFiniteType ∧ s.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero,
        s.IsDegreeZeroFiniteType ∧ s.IsFiniteTypeOverBase]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the two finite-type conditions, both read over every affine open of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.properFiniteType_tfae_and_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084I.** In Situation 0849 — `X` an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and `𝒜` a
quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra — the following conditions are equivalent:

1. `𝒜₀` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒜₀`-algebra,
2. `𝒜₀` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒪_X`-algebra;

and if they hold, the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is proper.

`𝒜₀` being of finite type is `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite` of the degree-zero piece; the
two algebra conditions are read on the restriction of `𝒜` to every étale chart.  The relative Proj
`π : P ⟶ X` is any morphism of algebraic spaces presented, on a surjective étale chart, as the
relative Proj of the restriction of `𝒜` (Stacks 084B), which is how the source's proof reaches
the scheme case.
declarations.statement:
theorem properFiniteType_tfae_and_isProper :
    List.TFAE
        [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧ s.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero,
          SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧ s.IsFiniteTypeOverBase] ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite (s.algebra.piece 0) ∧ s.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero →
        ∀ {P : (BigFppfOver s.site s.base s.containsBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u},
          IsAlgebraicSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase P → ∀ (π : P ⟶ s.space.1),
            RelativeProjSituationChart s π → IsProper s.site s.base s.containsBase π)
declarations.comment: both assertions for Situation 0849: the equivalence of the two finite-type conditions, with finite type of A_0 the finite type O_X-module condition on the small etale site and the two algebra conditions read on the restriction of A to every etale chart, and properness of the structure morphism of the relative Proj under them, the relative Proj entering through its Tag 084B chart presentation on the restriction of A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.tfae_finiteType_and_isProper_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084I.** In Situation 0849 — `X` an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and `𝒜` a
quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra — the following conditions are equivalent:

1. `𝒜₀` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒜₀`-algebra,
2. `𝒜₀` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `𝒜` is of finite type as an `𝒪_X`-algebra;

and if they hold, the structure morphism `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` of the relative homogeneous
spectrum of Stacks 084C is proper.

The conditions are read étale locally, on the restriction `g^*𝒜` of Stacks 084B to every étale
scheme point `g` of `X`, as for Stacks 084G and 084H: `𝒜₀` of finite type is
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` of the degree-zero piece of `g^*𝒜`, and the two algebra conditions
are the hypotheses of Stacks 084H and 084G.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_finiteType_and_isProper_π :
    List.TFAE
        [s.HoldsAtEtalePoints (fun A => SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (A.piece 0)) ∧
            s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero,
          s.HoldsAtEtalePoints (fun A => SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (A.piece 0)) ∧
            s.HoldsAtEtalePoints Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFiniteType.IsFiniteType] ∧
      (s.HoldsAtEtalePoints (fun A => SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (A.piece 0)) ∧
          s.HoldsAtEtalePoints SheafGradedAlgebra.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero →
        IsProper s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_open_notMem_weaklyAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084K.** A reduced scheme can have a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme that
omits a weakly associated point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_open_notMem_weaklyAssociatedPoint :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X),
      IsReduced X ∧ Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U ∧
        x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ∧ x ∉ (U : Set X)

The sub-`𝒪`-module sheaf of `F` whose local sections have all their germs outside `Z`
equal to zero.
declarations.statement:

    (F : X.Modules) : F.Submodule

The submodule of sections of `F` supported on `Z`: its sections over an open `U` are the

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_eq_on_of_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084N.** Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `T` with
structure morphisms `p : X ⟶ T` and `q : Y ⟶ T`, and let `f, g : X ⟶ Y` be morphisms over `T`.
Let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace with `f` and `g` agreeing on `U`. If the scheme-theoretic closure
of `U` in `X`, that is the scheme-theoretic image of `U ⟶ X`, is all of `X` and `q` is separated,
then `f = g`.

The agreement locus of `f` and `g` is a closed subspace of `X` containing `U`, so minimality of
the scheme-theoretic image of `U ⟶ X` puts that image inside the agreement locus, which is
therefore all of `X`. Openness of `U`, and indeed algebraicity of `U`, are not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_eq_on_of_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_top (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (p : X ⟶ T) (q : Y ⟶ T)
    (f g : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ q = p) (hg : g ≫ q = p) (U : Subfunctor X)
    (_hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) (hfg : U.ι ≫ f = U.ι ≫ g)
    (hclosure : schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS U.ι = ⊤) (hq : IsSeparated B S hS q) :
    f = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084P**, the local assertion. The relative diagonal of a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type is locally of finite presentation.

The diagonal is the first factor of a factorisation of the identity of the source through the
fibre square. The identity is locally of finite presentation because it is étale (Stacks
0468), and the second projection is locally of finite type by base change, so Stacks 05WT
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_pullbackDiagonal (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)
declarations.comment: the local assertion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084P**, the global assertion. The relative diagonal of a quasi-separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type is of finite presentation.

Quasi-compactness of the diagonal is quasi-separatedness of the morphism (Stacks 03HL, part
(3)). Quasi-separatedness of the diagonal follows from its separatedness by Stacks 03KK, and
the diagonal is separated because it is so after every represented base change (Stacks 03HK,
part (4)) and the two readings agree for a representable morphism (Stacks 03KY), the diagonal
being representable by Stacks 03HK, part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_pullbackDiagonal (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)
declarations.comment: the global assertion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_iff_isFiniteTypeOnSite_kernelIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084Q.** A closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` is of finite
presentation if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
`𝓘 = Ker(𝒪_X ⟶ i_*𝒪_Z)` is of finite type as an `𝒪_X`-module, that is, of finite type on the
small étale site of `X` in the sense of Stacks 03DL (5), which is how Properties of Spaces,
Section 66.30 reads the condition.

Both implications go through the affine étale charts of `X`.  On such a chart `C` the sections
of `𝓘` are the ideal cut out by the cartesian projection `Z ×_X C ⟶ C`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ker_structureSharp_app_eq_ker_appTop`, Stacks 03G8 part (2)), and
finite type of `𝓘` is finite generation of those ideals
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_kernelIdealSheaf_iff_forall_affine_fg_ker`); on the
other side, finite generation of that ideal over an affine chart is local finite presentation of
the projection, by the case of schemes (Stacks 01TV) together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isFiniteType_of_fg_ideal_top`.  Local finite
presentation on all affine charts is local finite presentation of `i`, and the two remaining
conjuncts of finite presentation hold for every closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_iff_isFiniteTypeOnSite_kernelIdealSheaf (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS i.hom ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite (kernelIdealSheaf B S hS i).toSheafOfModules
declarations.comment: finite type of the ideal sheaf on the small étale site of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LimitSituation
declarations.doc:
**Situation 084R.** A *limit situation* for a presheaf `X` on the big fppf site of `S`:
a directed index set with a chosen element, an inverse system of algebraic spaces over `S`
indexed by it whose transition morphisms are affine and whose stages are quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and an identification of `X` with the limit of that system.

This is the algebraic-space analogue of `AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation`, which is
Situation 086P for schemes, and the two have the same fields. By Stacks 07SF the limit of
such a system *is* an algebraic space over `S`, so the situation is not vacuous for a
reason it should not be: `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LimitSituation.const` builds one for every
quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
structure LimitSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSituation.exists_isIso_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0852**, and **Stacks 084S**. In the situation of Stacks 084W, if the base change
`f` of `f₀` to the limit `B` is an isomorphism and `f₀` is locally of finite presentation, then
the base change `f_i` of `f₀` to some stage `B_i` is an isomorphism.

This is Stacks 0852. Stacks 084S draws the same conclusion in the limit situation of Stacks
084R, with the source and the target in addition assumed representable over the stage;
hypothesis (a) of that tag is not needed here, since the three properties into which being an
isomorphism is decomposed all descend without it.

This is the statement under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD), which asks
nothing of the index.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base) (hf : IsIso D.mapLimit)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.initial ≤ i), IsIso (D.mapAt i hi)
declarations.comment: without hypothesis (a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isAbsolutelySeparated_system_obj_of_isSiteSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084T.** In the situation of Stacks 084R, over an arbitrary base scheme, if the
limit `X` of the inverse system is separated then some stage `X_i` is separated.

Separatedness is the absolute notion, taken over the terminal scheme, so the whole descent may
be read there: the relocalization along `S ⟶ Spec ℤ` carries the descent situation over `S` to
one over the terminal scheme, which is affine, and the absolute separatedness of a presheaf and
of its view over the terminal scheme are the same condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAbsolutelySeparated_system_obj_of_isSiteSmall {I : Type u} [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I)
    (hb : Space.IsSiteSmall B S hS D.system)
    (hX : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ D.limitCone.pt) :
    ∃ i, D.base ≤ i ∧ IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ (D.system.obj (op i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commSq_chart_specOfGlobalFunctions
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a `u`-model of the ring of global functions of an algebraic space `X` over `S`,
let `V` be an étale scheme chart of `X`, let `g₁, …, gₙ` be polynomials in `n` variables over `A`
and let `h₁, …, hₙ` be global functions on `V` with `g_λ(h) = 0`. Write
`C = A[x₁, …, xₙ]/(g₁, …, gₙ)`. Then the square whose top is the chart, whose left vertical is a
canonical morphism `p : X ⟶ Spec A`, whose right vertical is the morphism `V ⟶ Spec C` attached
to `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coordinateHom` and whose bottom is the spectrum of `A → C` commutes.

The hypothesis `hp` is the chart formula of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_specMap_of_globalHom`,
which determines `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem commSq_chart_specOfGlobalFunctions (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (e : A ≃+* globalFunctions B S hS X.1) {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
    (h : Fin n → Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V.1.left, ⊤))
    (hrel : ∀ l, MvPolynomial.eval₂
      ((globalFunctionsChartRestriction B S hS X V).comp e.toRingHom) h (g l) = 0)
    (p : X.1 ⟶ schemePoints B S hS (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)))
    (hp : yonedaEquiv (V.1.hom ≫ p) =
      specMapOfGlobalHom A ((globalFunctionsChartRestriction B S hS X V).comp e.toRingHom)) :
    V.1.hom ≫ p =
      yonedaEquiv.symm (specMapOfGlobalHom (presentationAlgebra g)
          (coordinateHom g ((globalFunctionsChartRestriction B S hS X V).comp e.toRingHom)
            h hrel)) ≫
        schemePointsMap B S hS
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (presentationStructureHom g)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084W.** The standing situation for descending a property of a
morphism of algebraic spaces along a directed limit: a directed inverse system of algebraic
spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms and algebraic limit, a distinguished stage of
the system, and a morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces over that
stage.
declarations.statement:
structure MorphismDescentSystem (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_universallyInjective_mapAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 084X.** In the situation of Stacks 084W, if the base change `f` of `f₀` to the
limit `B` is universally injective and `f₀` is locally of finite type, then the base change
`f_i` of `f₀` to some stage `B_i` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:

    (D : MorphismDescentSystem B S hS hZ I)

    (ft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), UniversallyInjective B S hS (D.mapAt i le)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSituation.exists_isAffineHom_mapAt_of_isAffineHom_mapLimit_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
Notation and assumptions as in Situation 70.6.1 (tag 084W), carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSituation`, in the chapter's setting of Section 70.2
(tag 07SD): `B = lim B_i` a directed inverse limit of algebraic spaces over `S` with affine
transition morphisms, `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` a morphism of algebraic spaces over `B₀` with `B₀`, `X₀`
and `Y₀` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and `f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_i`, `f : X ⟶ Y` its base changes
to `B_i` for `i ≥ 0` and to `B`. If `f` is affine, then `f_i` is affine for some `i ≥ 0`.

The hypothesis `hconv` is the chapter's standing convention that every ring considered has its
spectrum in the big fppf site, read for the system of bases; nothing is asked of the index. The
implementation notes of this module show that the statement fails without it; the
corresponding failure of Stacks 07SQ, on which the proof rests, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.not_forall_exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj`.

The proof is the source's:
`exists_isAffineHom_mapAt_of_descentAffineStage_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits` with Stacks
07SQ supplied by
`DescentSituation.exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineHom_mapAt_of_isAffineHom_mapLimit_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS D.mapLimit) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.initial ≤ i), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.mapAt i hi)

theorem exists_isAffineHom_mapAt (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isSeparated_pullbackMap_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0851.** In the situation of Stacks 084W, if the base change `f : X ⟶ Y` of
`f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` to the limit `B = lim B_i` is separated, then the base change `f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_i` of
`f₀` to some stage `B_i` with `i ≥ 0` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparated_pullbackMap_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits {I : Type u} [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (base : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hbase : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (base.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (base.map a))
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS base)
    (hQc : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (base.obj i)) (i₀ : I)
    {X₀ Y₀ : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (p : X₀ ⟶ base.obj (op i₀))
    (q : Y₀ ⟶ base.obj (op i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (hf₀ : f₀ ≫ q = p)
    (hX₀ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀) (hY₀ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₀)
    (hB₀qs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (base.obj (op i₀)))
    (hX₀qc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X₀) (hX₀qs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X₀)
    (hY₀qc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y₀) (hY₀qs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y₀)
    (hf : IsSeparated B S hS (pullback.map (limit.π base (op i₀)) p (limit.π base (op i₀)) q
      (𝟙 _) f₀ (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp [hf₀]))) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i₀ ≤ i), IsSeparated B S hS (pullback.map (base.map (homOfLE hi).op) p
      (base.map (homOfLE hi).op) q (𝟙 _) f₀ (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp [hf₀]))
declarations.comment: under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD) on the system of bases, every stage quasi-compact; proved in an enlarged site
