declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceSectionMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `𝒜_d ⟶ π_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d))` of Stacks 085L**, in degree `d`: the
homogeneous section map `𝒜_d ⟶ π_*(𝒪_P(d))` of Stacks 01MP followed by the direct image of the
twist `𝒪_P(d) ⟶ (i_*𝒪_Z)(d)` of the structure map of the closed subspace.

The source states the map into the direct sum over `d ≥ 0`; it is graded, and this is its
degree-`d` component.  The composite is the one the source names, for any datum of twists; at the
twists of Stacks 084D on `P = Proj_X(𝒜)`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1359Bridge.psiTwistSections`,
it is the canonical map of the source.
declarations.statement:
def closedSubspaceSectionMap (T : ClosedSubspaceTwistSections s P π) (i : Z ⟶ P) (d : ℕ) :
    s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ) ⟶ twistedStructureDirectImage T i d
declarations.comment: the canonical map 𝒜 ⟶ ⨁ π_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d)), degreewise; at the twists of Tag 084D it is the source's map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceGradedIdeal
declarations.doc:
**The graded ideal `ℐ ⊆ 𝒜` of Stacks 085L**, in degree `d`: the sectionwise kernel of the
canonical map, as a submodule of the degree-`d` piece of `𝒜`.

This is the kernel of the map the source writes down, not a choice of ideal with the right
properties; at the twists `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1359Bridge.psiTwistSections` it is the ideal
`ℐ` of the source.
declarations.statement:
def closedSubspaceGradedIdeal (T : ClosedSubspaceTwistSections s P π) (i : Z ⟶ P) (d : ℕ) :
    (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule
declarations.comment: the graded ideal ℐ ⊆ 𝒜, degreewise, as the kernel of that canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_closedSubspaceGradedIdealObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085L, the quasi-coherence of `ℐ`.**  Let `π : P = Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` be quasi-compact
and `i : Z ⟶ P` a closed immersion.  Then for any quasi-coherent twists `𝒪_P(d)` with homogeneous
section maps, in particular those of Stacks 084D
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1359Bridge.psiTwistSections`), the degree-`d` piece of the graded
ideal `ℐ`, the kernel of the canonical map `𝒜_d ⟶ π_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d))`, is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module.

The proof is the source's.  `π` is separated (Stacks 084E), hence quasi-separated; `i_*𝒪_Z` is
quasi-coherent as `i` is a closed immersion, and so is its tensor product with the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_P(d)`; the direct image along the quasi-compact quasi-separated `π` is quasi-coherent by
Stacks 03M9, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_qcqs`; and the
kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent (Stacks 03M1(3),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels_quasicoherentSheaves_smallEtale`).  The `let`
ascribes the last at this module's spelling of the structure ring sheaf, which instance
resolution does not identify with the `RingedSite.ringSheaf` spelling of that lemma on its own.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_closedSubspaceGradedIdealObj {s : RelativeProjSituation.{u, u}}
    (T : ClosedSubspaceTwistSections s s.Proj s.π)
    {Z : AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase} (i : Z ⟶ s.Proj)
    (hπ : IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom) (d : ℕ) :
    (closedSubspaceGradedIdealObj T i d).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: ℐ is a quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-module, degreewise, for π quasi-compact and i a closed immersion, for any quasi-coherent twists on Proj_X(𝒜), those of Tag 084D included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1359Bridge.exists_iso_quotientProjHom_psiKernelGradedIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085L.**  Let `π : P = Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` be the relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_X`-algebra on an algebraic space `X` (twists `𝒪_P(d)` and `ψ` built from a presentation of
`X`), and `i : Z ⟶ P` a closed subspace.  Let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒜` be the kernel of the canonical map
`𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{d ≥ 0} π_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d))`: in degree `d ≥ 0` the sections killed by the adjoint
`𝒜_d ⟶ π_*𝒪_P(d)` of `ψ_d` followed by `π_*` of `𝒪_P(d) ⟶ i_*i^*𝒪_P(d) = (i_*𝒪_Z)(d)`, and
`ℐ_n = 𝒜_n = 0` for `n < 0`.  If `π` is quasi-compact, `ℐ` is a quasi-coherent graded ideal and
there is an isomorphism `Z ≅ Proj_X(𝒜/ℐ)` over `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_quotientProjHom_psiKernelGradedIdeal
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom)
    (hπ : IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom) :
    (∀ (d : ℕ) (V : (SmallEtale s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)ᵒᵖ)
        (x : (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)).val.obj V),
        x ∈ ((psiKernelGradedIdeal s Px i hi hπ).piece (d : ℤ)).obj V ↔
          (psiKernelMap s Px i d (s.psiTwistHom Px d)).val.app V x = 0) ∧
      ∃ e : Z ≅ (psiKernelGradedIdeal s Px i hi hπ).quotientSituation.Proj,
        e.hom ≫ (psiKernelGradedIdeal s Px i hi hπ).quotientProjHom = i
declarations.comment: Z ≅ Proj_X(𝒜/ℐ) over P for π quasi-compact, ℐ the kernel of 𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{d ≥ 0} π_*((i_*𝒪_Z)(d))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteType_chartDegreeSubmodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085M on an affine étale chart.**

Let `𝒜` be the quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra of a relative Proj situation on an algebraic
space `X`, let `V` be an étale chart of `X` with affine underlying scheme, and let `𝒜|_V` be the
restriction of Stacks 01NN carried by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartSheafAlgebra`.
For a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ Proj_V(𝒜|_V)` of finite presentation with `Proj_V(𝒜|_V) ⟶ V`
quasi-compact there are a degree `d > 0` and a quasi-coherent finite type submodule
`ℱ ⊆ (𝒜_d)|_V` of the **module restriction of `𝒜_d`** with `Z = Proj_V((𝒜|_V)/ℱ(𝒜|_V))`.

This is the step of the source's proof reading "by the case of schemes, Divisors 0802, applied
over `U`".  Compactness and quasi-separatedness of the base, which Stacks 0802 asks for, are
discharged from affineness of the chart; the graded algebra is not an input but the restriction of
`𝒜`, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartSheafAlgebra_piece`, which is what makes the
submodule a submodule of `(𝒜_d)|_V`.

Neither the globalization of `ℱ` to a submodule of `𝒜_d` on `X` nor the descent of the
presentation to `X` is claimed; see *What is not proved* in the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_chartDegreeSubmodule
    (hV : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine (chartScheme V)) {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ (relativeProj (relativeProjChartSheafAlgebra s V)).scheme)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i]
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact
      (relativeProj (relativeProjChartSheafAlgebra s V)).toBase]
    (hi : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation i) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧
      ∃ ℱ : (restrictToChartScheme s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1 s.space.2
          (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)) V).Submodule,
        ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
          SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧
            Nonempty (DegreeQuotientPresentation
              (relativeProjChartSheafAlgebra s V) i ℱ)
declarations.comment: the chart half: over an affine étale chart V of X there are d > 0 and a quasi-coherent finite type submodule ℱ of the module restriction (𝒜_d)|_V cutting out a closed subscheme of finite presentation of Proj_V(𝒜|_V), with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own, exactly as the scheme case Tag 0802. The globalization of ℱ to a submodule of 𝒜_d on X — the colimit clause of Tag 0829, still resting on Tag 07V9 — and the descent of the presentation to X are NOT claimed, so the existence assertion of Tag 085M on X is not delivered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceDegreeProducts_le_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085M, the containment `Z ⊆ Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜)`, in graded-ideal form.**

Let `ψ : 𝒜 ⟶ ℬ` be a degreewise map of graded `𝒪_X`-algebras which is multiplicative in the
bidegree `(d, e)`, and suppose every local section of `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d` is killed by `ψ` — that is, `ℱ`
consists of equations for the closed subspace `ℬ` presents.  Then every local section of the
graded ideal `ℱ𝒜` in degree `d + e` is killed by `ψ` as well, so `ℱ𝒜` is contained in the graded
ideal of that closed subspace.

This is the step of the source's proof reading "`Z ⊆ Z'` since `ℱ𝒜 ⊆ ℐ`".  Its content is the
passage from the objectwise products to the ideal they generate: the kernel of `ψ` has local
membership, so a section of `𝒜_{d+e}` that is only *locally* a sum of products `a · b` with
`a` a section of `ℱ` is killed by `ψ` too.

Neither the degree `d > 0` nor the finite type submodule `ℱ` of the source's conclusion is
produced here; see *What is not proved* in the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedSubspaceDegreeProducts_le_ker
    {ℬ : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u, u, u + 1}
      (structureRingSheaf s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space)}
    (ψ : ∀ n : ℤ, s.algebra.piece n ⟶ ℬ.piece n)
    (hmul : ∀ (U : (SmallEtale s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)ᵒᵖ)
      (a : (s.algebra.piece d).val.obj U) (b : (s.algebra.piece e).val.obj U),
      (ψ (d + e)).val.app U ((s.algebra.mul d e).app U a b) =
        (ℬ.mul d e).app U ((ψ d).val.app U a) ((ψ e).val.app U b))
    {ℱ : (s.algebra.piece d).Submodule}
    (hℱ : ℱ ≤ Stacks.SheafOfModules.kerSubmodule (ψ d)) :
    closedSubspaceDegreeProducts s d e ℱ ≤
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.kerSubmodule (ψ (d + e))
declarations.comment: the containment Z ⊆ Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜) in graded-ideal form: the graded ideal ℱ𝒜 generated by ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d is killed by every degreewise, bidegree-(d,e)-multiplicative map of graded algebras killing ℱ. The existence of d > 0 and of the finite type quasi-coherent ℱ is not claimed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.exists_finiteType_iso_quotientProjHom
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space, `𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_X`-algebra whose relative Proj `π : Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` is quasi-compact, and
`i : Z ⟶ Proj_X(𝒜)` a closed immersion locally of finite presentation. Then there are `d > 0`
and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-submodule `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d` of finite type such that `Z = Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜)` as
closed subspaces of `Proj_X(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_iso_quotientProjHom (s : RelativeProjSituation.{u, u})
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated s.site s.base s.containsBase
      (BigFppfSite.contains_terminal s.site) s.space.1)
    (hπ : IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.π.hom)
    {Z : AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase} (i : Z ⟶ s.Proj)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ (F : (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule)
      (hF : F.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite), F.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType ∧
        ∃ e : Z ≅ (GradedIdeal.ofDegree s F hF).quotientSituation.Proj,
          e.hom ≫ (GradedIdeal.ofDegree s F hF).quotientProjHom = i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.exists_finiteType_degreeSubmodule_range_eq_quotientProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085N.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`,
`𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra and `π : P = Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` its relative Proj
(Stacks 084A–084B).  Let `i : Z ⟶ P` be a closed subspace and `U ⊆ |X|` open.  Assume
(1) `π` quasi-compact, (2) `i` of finite presentation, (3) `|U| ∩ |π|(|i|(|Z|)) = ∅`,
(4) `U` quasi-compact and (5) every `𝒜_n` of finite type.  Then there are `d > 0` and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-submodule of finite type `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d` with (a) `Z = Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜)` and
(b) the support of `𝒜_d/ℱ` disjoint from `U`.

Clause (a) says that `Z` and the closed subspace `Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜) ⟶ P`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.quotientProjHom` of the graded ideal `ℱ𝒜`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeProjSituation.degreeIdeal`) have the same range in `P`; clause
(b) is disjointness from `U` of the support (Stacks 04KA) of the cokernel of `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d`.
"`X` quasi-separated" is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated` (Stacks 03BS).
The source writes the closed subspace as `i : Z → X`; its hypothesis (3) and conclusion (a) place
`Z` in `P`, and it is formalized as `i : Z ⟶ P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_degreeSubmodule_range_eq_quotientProj
    (hX : IsQuasiCompactSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated s.site s.base s.containsBase s.site.contains_terminal
      s.space.1)
    {Z : AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase} (i : Z.1 ⟶ s.relativeProjFunctor)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion s.site s.base s.containsBase i)
    (hπ : IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjπ)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation s.site s.base s.containsBase i)
    {U : Set (points s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)}
    (hZU : Disjoint U (Set.range fun z ↦
      pointsMap s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor s.relativeProjπ
        (pointsMap s.site s.base s.containsBase Z.1 i z)))
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hUc : IsCompact U)
    (hA : ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (s.algebra.piece n)) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (_ : 0 < d) (ℱ : (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule)
      (hℱ : ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite),
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧
        Subfunctor.range i = Subfunctor.range (s.quotientProjHom (s.degreeIdeal ℱ)
          (s.isQuasicoherentOnSite_degreeIdeal_piece ℱ hℱ)) ∧
        Disjoint (supportOfSheaf s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureRingSheaf s.site s.base s.containsBase
            s.space)).obj (cokernel ℱ.ι))) U
declarations.comment: the relative Proj P = Proj_X(𝒜) of Stacks 084A-084B; clause (a) is the equality of the ranges of i : Z ⟶ P and of the closed immersion Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜) ⟶ P, clause (b) the disjointness from U of the support of 𝒜_d/ℱ; the closed subspace written i : Z → X in the source is i : Z ⟶ P, which condition (3) and clause (a) require

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteType_degreeSubmodule_disjoint_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085N.**  Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over `S` and `𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_X`-algebra; let `π : P = Proj_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` be the
relative Proj (`…RelativeProjSituation.relativeProjFunctor`), let `i : Z ⟶ P` be a closed subspace
and let `U` be an open of `|X|`.  Assume (1) `π` quasi-compact, (2) `i` of finite presentation,
(3) `|U| ∩ |π|(|i|(|Z|)) = ∅`, (4) `U` quasi-compact and (5) every `𝒜_n` of finite type.  Then
there are a degree `d > 0` and a quasi-coherent finite type `𝒪_X`-submodule `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d` with
(a) `Z = Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜)` and (b) the support of `𝒜_d/ℱ` disjoint from `U`.

Clause (a) is the structure `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceDegreeQuotientPresentation`,
the form in which Stacks 085M records the same assertion; clause (b) is disjointness from `U` of
the support of Stacks 04KA of the cokernel of `ℱ ⊆ 𝒜_d`.  This is
`…RelativeProjSituation.exists_finiteType_degreeSubmodule_range_eq_quotientProj`, whose clause (a)
is the equality of the ranges of `i` and of `Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜) ⟶ P`, read through
`…RelativeProjSituation.nonempty_closedSubspaceDegreeQuotientPresentation_of_range_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_degreeSubmodule_disjoint_support
    (hX : IsQuasiCompactSpace s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated s.site s.base s.containsBase s.site.contains_terminal
      s.space.1)
    {Z : AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase}
    (i : Z ⟶ (⟨s.relativeProjFunctor, s.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeProjFunctor⟩ :
      AlgebraicSpaces s.site s.base s.containsBase))
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom)
    (hπ : IsQuasiCompact s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjπ)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation s.site s.base s.containsBase i.hom)
    {U : Set (points s.site s.base s.containsBase s.space.1)}
    (hZU : Disjoint U (Set.range fun z ↦
      pointsMap s.site s.base s.containsBase s.relativeProjFunctor s.relativeProjπ
        (pointsMap s.site s.base s.containsBase Z.1 i.hom z)))
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hUc : IsCompact U)
    (hA : ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (s.algebra.piece n)) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (ℱ : (s.algebra.piece (d : ℤ)).Submodule),
      ℱ.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType ℱ.toSheafOfModules ∧

              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureRingSheaf s.site s.base s.containsBase
                s.space)).obj (cokernel ℱ.ι))) U
declarations.comment: the relative Proj P = Proj_X(𝒜) of Stacks 084A-084B; clause (a) as the data ClosedSubspaceDegreeQuotientPresentation (Z identified over P with Proj_X(𝒜/ℱ𝒜) and its closed immersion into P), clause (b) the disjointness from U of the support of 𝒜_d/ℱ; the closed subspace written i : Z → X in the source is i : Z ⟶ P, which condition (3) and clause (a) require

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_proj_reesGrading_affineChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085R, the canonical isomorphism.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic
space over `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace with quasi-coherent defining sheaf of ideals
`ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowup of `X` in `Z`.  Let `U = Spec A` be an affine
scheme of the site étale over `X` and let `I ⊆ A` be the ideal corresponding to `ℐ|_U`.  Then
`U ×_X X'` is a scheme, and it is canonically isomorphic over `U` to the homogeneous spectrum
`Proj(⨁_{d ≥ 0} Iᵈ)` of the Rees algebra of `I` in `A`.

The first isomorphism exhibits the fibre product as the algebraic space of a scheme of the
site, namely the relative `Proj` `P_U` of the Rees algebra of `ℐ|_U`, compatibly with the
projections to `U`; the second identifies that scheme over `U` with `Proj` of the Rees algebra
of `I`, where `I` is the ideal of sections of `ℐ|_U` over `A`, which is the defining ideal of
the centre on the chart by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reesChartIdeal_selfPresentation_eq_ofIdealTop`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_proj_reesGrading_affineChart
    {X X' W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj}
    {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    {a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X} (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'} (sq : IsPullback q r a b)
    (I : Ideal ↥Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V,
      (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1))
    (hI : (reesChartIdeal (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).ideal
        (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) = I) :
    ∃ e : W ≅ schemeSpace (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU),
      e.hom ≫ schemeSpaceMap (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU) = q ∧
      ∃ f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) ≅
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
            (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU),
        f.hom ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
            (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU) =
          Stacks.Blowup.toSpec I ≫
            (Stacks.RelativeProj.isAffineOpen (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))).isoSpec.inv ≫
              (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1.ι
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism clause: for an affine scheme U = Spec A of the site étale over X, the fibre product U ×_X X' is the scheme Proj of the Rees algebra of the ideal I of A corresponding to the restriction of the centre's defining sheaf of ideals, by an isomorphism over U; the blowup b is named by the universal property of Stacks 085U, and the only side conditions are the three B.Contains conditions on the relative Projs of the chart's own presentation that the construction of Stacks 085Q already takes; the tag's affine open covering clause is a separate registration

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iSup_opensRange_specAffineBlowupι_affineChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085R, the affine open covering.**  In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_proj_reesGrading_affineChart`, the scheme representing
`U ×_X X'` has an affine open covering by the spectra of the affine blowup algebras
`A[I/a]`, `a ∈ I`: the morphisms `Spec A[I/a] ⟶ U ×_X X'` obtained by composing the standard
chart `Stacks.Blowup.specAffineBlowupι` with the identification of the previous theorem -- the
same isomorphism over `U`, whose compatibility with the projections to `U` is restated here --
are open immersions whose images have supremum the whole space.

The sources of the covering morphisms are the spectra of the affine blowup algebras
`Stacks.Blowup.affineBlowup I a` by construction, so this is the tag's "Moreover" clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iSup_opensRange_specAffineBlowupι_affineChart
    {X X' W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj}
    {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    {a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X} (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).relativeProj)
    {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'} (sq : IsPullback q r a b)
    (I : Ideal ↥Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V,
      (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1))
    (hI : (reesChartIdeal (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).ideal
        (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) = I) :
    ∃ e : W ≅ schemeSpace (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU),
      e.hom ≫ schemeSpaceMap (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU) = q ∧
      ∃ f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) ≅
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
            (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU),
        (f.hom ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
            (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V) hcU) =
          Stacks.Blowup.toSpec I ≫
            (Stacks.RelativeProj.isAffineOpen (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))).isoSpec.inv ≫
              (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1.ι) ∧
        (∀ c : I, _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
            (Stacks.Blowup.specAffineBlowupι I (c : _) c.2 ≫ f.hom)) ∧
          ⨆ c : I, (Stacks.Blowup.specAffineBlowupι I (c : _) c.2 ≫ f.hom).opensRange = ⊤
declarations.comment: the affine open covering clause: the scheme U ×_X X' is covered by the images of the open immersions Spec A[I/a] ⟶ U ×_X X', a ∈ I, out of the spectra of the affine blowup algebras; same hypotheses and same side conditions as the canonical-isomorphism clause

declarations.doc:

space over `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace with quasi-coherent defining sheaf of ideals
`ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowup of `X` in `Z`.  Let `U = Spec A` be an affine

theorem exists_iso_proj_reesGrading_affineChart_unconditional
    {X X' W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj}

    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    {a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X} (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'} (sq : IsPullback q r a b)
    (I : Ideal ↥Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V,
      (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1))
    (hI : (reesChartIdeal (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).ideal
        (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) = I) :
    ∃ e : W ≅ schemeSpace (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
        (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
      e.hom ≫ schemeSpaceMap (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
          (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) = q ∧
      ∃ f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) ≅

              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
              (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
        f.hom ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
            (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
              (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) =
          Stacks.Blowup.toSpec I ≫
            (Stacks.RelativeProj.isAffineOpen (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))).isoSpec.inv ≫
              (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1.ι

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085R, the affine open covering.**  In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_proj_reesGrading_affineChart_unconditional`, the scheme

declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iSup_opensRange_specAffineBlowupι_affineChart_unconditional
    {X X' W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj}
    {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    {a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X} (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'} (sq : IsPullback q r a b)
    (I : Ideal ↥Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V,
      (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1))
    (hI : (reesChartIdeal (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).ideal
        (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) = I) :
    ∃ e : W ≅ schemeSpace (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
        (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
      e.hom ≫ schemeSpaceMap (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
          (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) = q ∧
      ∃ f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) ≅
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
            (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
              (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
        (f.hom ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
            (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
              (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) =
          Stacks.Blowup.toSpec I ≫
            (Stacks.RelativeProj.isAffineOpen (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))).isoSpec.inv ≫
              (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1.ι) ∧
        (∀ c : I, _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
            (Stacks.Blowup.specAffineBlowupι I (c : _) c.2 ≫ f.hom)) ∧
          ⨆ c : I, (Stacks.Blowup.specAffineBlowupι I (c : _) c.2 ≫ f.hom).opensRange = ⊤
declarations.comment: the affine open covering clause: the scheme U ×_X X' is covered by the images of the open immersions Spec A[I/a] ⟶ U ×_X X', a ∈ I, out of the spectra of the affine blowup algebras; same hypotheses as the canonical-isomorphism clause and, like it, no side conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_preimage_of_isPullback_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085S.** Let `g : X₁ ⟶ X₂` be a flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`Z₂ ⊆ X₂` be a closed subspace and let `b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂` be the blowup of `X₂` in `Z₂`.  Then for
any cartesian square with legs `q : W ⟶ X₁` and `r : W ⟶ X₂'` over `g` and `b₂`, the projection
`q` is the blowup of `X₁` in the inverse image of `Z₂`.

So the square expressing `W = X₁ ×_{X₂} X₂'` is the cartesian square of the source, with
`W = X₁'`.

Flatness enters only to see that the inverse image of the centre in `W` — which is the inverse
image along `r` of the exceptional divisor of `b₂` — is an effective Cartier divisor; the
universal property of `q` holds for an arbitrary `g`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_pullbackFst_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085S for the chosen fibre product.** The first projection of the fibre product
`X₁ ×_{X₂} X₂'` of a flat morphism `g : X₁ ⟶ X₂` with the blowup `b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂` of `X₂` in a
closed subspace `Z₂` is the blowup of `X₁` in the inverse image of `Z₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_pullbackFst_of_isFlat
    {X₁ X₂ X₂' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g : X₁ ⟶ X₂} (hg : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    {Z₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X₂.1} {b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂}
    (hb₂ : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z₂ b₂) :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace g Z₂) (pullback.fst g b₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPullback_blowup_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085S in the source's phrasing.** For a flat morphism `g : X₁ ⟶ X₂` of algebraic
spaces over `S`, a closed subspace `Z₂ ⊆ X₂` with inverse image `Z₁ ⊆ X₁`, the blowup
`b₁ : X₁' ⟶ X₁` of `X₁` in `Z₁` and the blowup `b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂` of `X₂` in `Z₂`, there is a
morphism `X₁' ⟶ X₂'` making the square

```
X₁' ⟶ X₂'
 ↓      ↓
X₁ ⟶  X₂
```

cartesian.

The fibre product `X₁ ×_{X₂} X₂'` is a blowup of `X₁` in `Z₁` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_pullbackFst_of_isFlat`, and any two blowups of `X₁` in
`Z₁` are isomorphic over `X₁`, so `X₁'` is itself a fibre product.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalDivisor_blowUpAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085T part (2).** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be a
closed subspace and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z` of Stacks 085Q, the
relative `Proj` of the Rees algebra `⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝓘_Zⁿ`.  Then the exceptional divisor `b⁻¹(Z)` is
an effective Cartier divisor on `X'`.

By Stacks 083C (2) ⟹ (1) it is enough to see this on one surjective étale scheme chart of `X'`,
and the construction supplies one: the relative `Proj` `P_U` of the Rees algebra on the
presenting scheme `U` of the étale presentation, whose composite with `b` is `P_U ⟶ U ⟶ X`.  The
inverse image of `b⁻¹(Z)` there is therefore the inverse image along `P_U ⟶ U` of the closed
subscheme `Z ×_X U` of `U`, whose ideal sheaf is the sheaf of ideals `𝓘_Z|_U` the Rees algebra is
formed from, and for a scheme that inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor by Stacks 02OS
(2).

The parameters `hcU`, `hcR` and `heq` are the ones the blowup of Stacks 085Q is built from: two
containment conditions on the big fppf site and the normalisation and cocycle conditions making
the two projections of the relative `Proj`s an internal equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalDivisor_blowUpAlong :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS (blowUpAlong Z P hcU hcR heq)
      (exceptionalDivisor Z P hcU hcR heq)
declarations.comment: part (2), the exceptional divisor b⁻¹(Z) of the blowup of an algebraic space along a closed subspace is an effective Cartier divisor on the blowup

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.isIso_and_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_and_twist_neg_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085T.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be
a closed subspace and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` in `Z`, in the sense of the
universal property of Stacks 085U.  Then

1. the restriction `b⁻¹(X ∖ Z) ⟶ X ∖ Z` of `b` is an isomorphism;
2. the exceptional divisor `E = b⁻¹(Z)` is an effective Cartier divisor on `X'`;
3. `𝒪_{X'}(E) = 𝒪_{X'}(-1)`: for every affine scheme `V = Spec A` étale over `X`, with `I ⊆ A` the
   ideal of `Z` on `V`, the fibre product `V ×_X X'` is identified over `V` with the scheme
   `Proj(⨁_{d ≥ 0} Iᵈ)` (by `e` and `f`, as in Stacks 085R), and under that identification the
   base change of the invertible sheaf `𝒪_{X'}(E)` of Stacks 0841 is the twist `𝒪(-1)`.

Part (3) is the characterization of the twists of the relative `Proj` in Stacks 084D (their base
change to schemes over `X` are the twists of Stacks 01NR), applied to the affine schemes étale
over `X`, which cover it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_and_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_and_twist_neg_one
    {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1} {b : X' ⟶ X}
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    IsIso ((openComplementOfClosedSubspace B S hS X Z).1.fromPreimage b.hom) ∧
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X' (preimageClosedSubspace b Z) ∧
      ∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
        (a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X), IsEtale B S hS a.hom →
        ∀ (I : Ideal ↥Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V,
            (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1)),
          (reesChartIdeal (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)).ideal
            (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) = I →
        ∀ {W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'},
          IsPullback q r a b →
        ∃ e : W ≅ schemeSpace (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
            (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
          e.hom ≫ schemeSpaceMap (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
              (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
              (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) = q ∧
          ∃ f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) ≅
              (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
                (reesProjChart (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
                  (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
                  (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)),
            f.hom ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
                (reesProjChartHom (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace a Z))
                  (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal _) (selfPresentation B S hS V)
                  (contains_relativeProj_reesChartSituation_selfPresentation Z V a)) =
              Stacks.Blowup.toSpec I ≫
                (Stacks.RelativeProj.isAffineOpen (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))).isoSpec.inv ≫
                  (Stacks.Blowup.topAffineOpen ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)).1.ι ∧
            Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.hom).obj
                (baseChangeModule B S hS (associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS X'
                  (preimageClosedSubspace b Z) hb.isPullbackDefined) _ (e.inv ≫ r).hom) ≅
              twistingSheaf (Stacks.Blowup.reesGrading I) (-1))
declarations.comment: all three parts, for any blowup b of X in a closed subspace Z in the sense of the Stacks 085U universal property: (1) b is an isomorphism over the complement of Z, (2) the exceptional divisor is an effective Cartier divisor, (3) O(E) = O(-1), read as in Stacks 084D on every affine scheme V etale over X, where V x_X X' = Proj of the Rees algebra (Stacks 085R) and the base change of O(E) is the twist O(-1); no other hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_fromPreimage_openComplement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085T, part (1).** The blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` of an algebraic space `X` in a closed
subspace `Z` is an isomorphism over the open complement of `Z`: the restriction
`b⁻¹(X ∖ Z) ⟶ X ∖ Z` of `b` is an isomorphism.

Both `X ∖ Z` and `b⁻¹(X ∖ Z)` are algebraic spaces over `X` on which the inverse image of `Z`
has no points, hence is an effective Cartier divisor, so each admits a unique morphism to `X'`
over `X` by the universal property of Stacks 085U.  The morphism out of `X ∖ Z` lands in
`b⁻¹(X ∖ Z)` and is inverse to the restriction of `b`, the two composites being identified with
the identities by the uniqueness of those lifts.
declarations.comment: part (1): the blowup is an isomorphism away from the centre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpTwistSpaceNegOneIsoAssociatedInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085T, part (3): the canonical isomorphism `𝒪_{X'}(-1) ≅ 𝒪_{X'}(E)`.**  Let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of an algebraic space `X` along a closed subspace `Z` (Stacks
085Q, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpAlong'`, with the equivalence-relation field of its descent
datum discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalenceRelation_post_reesProj`), with
exceptional divisor `E = b⁻¹(Z)`, an effective Cartier divisor by part (2).  Then the twisting
sheaf `𝒪_{X'}(-1)` is isomorphic to the invertible sheaf `𝒪_{X'}(E)` of Stacks 0841 (1).

Here `𝒪_{X'}(n)` is the `n`th tensor power (Stacks 01CU) of the invertible sheaf `𝒪_{X'}(1)`
obtained by descending, along the étale presentation `P_R ⇉ P_U` of `X'` and the equivalence of
Stacks 03M3, the twisting sheaf `𝒪_{P_U}(1)` of the blowup `P_U` of the presenting scheme `U` in
`𝓘_Z|_U`, with transition morphism `α'` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpTwistDescentDatum`).

**Why the isomorphism is canonical.**  The descent datum of `𝒪_{X'}(1)` is characterised
without reference to `E` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_blowUpTwistDescentDatum_alpha_iff`): a
morphism `β : t^*𝒪_{P_U}(1)^a ⟶ s^*𝒪_{P_U}(1)^a` is the transition `α'` if and only if
`β ≫ s^*c = t^*c ≫ α_𝒪`, where `α_𝒪` is the canonical descent datum of `𝒪_{X'}` and
`c = (blowUpChartTwistOneToUnit)^a ≫ u⁻¹`, built from the canonical map `𝒪(1) ⟶ 𝒪` of the
scheme blowup `P_U` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpChartTwistOneToUnit`: Stacks 02OS (3)
followed by the inclusion into `𝒪`, which on the standard chart at `a ∈ 𝓘(U)` is
`t ↦ (t / a⁽¹⁾) · b^♯(a)`, the map induced by the shift `A(1) ⟶ A` of the Rees algebra,
`AlgebraicGeometry.incl_app_twistOneIsoExceptionalIdealModule_hom`) and the identification
`u : φ^*𝒪_{X'} ≅ 𝒪_{P_U}^a` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackPresentationAtlasUnitIso`,
built from `𝒪` alone.  That lemma combines the uniqueness of the transition
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_blowUpTwistDescentDatum_alpha`), its computation at the atlas
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpAtlasMapComputes_idealSheaf`) and on the chart
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpChartTwistOneIsoIdealSheaf_hom_comp_ι`).  So `𝒪_{X'}(1)` is the
descent of `𝒪_{P_U}(1)` along the unique datum compatible with `𝒪(1) ⟶ 𝒪`, and the isomorphism
below is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpTwistSpaceNegOneIso`, the inverse of the descended
`𝒪_{X'}(1) ≅ 𝓘_E` of Stacks 02OS (3).

The parameters `hcU`, `hcR` and `hcRR` are the containment conditions on the big fppf site under
which the relative `Proj`s of the blowup are objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
def blowUpTwistSpaceNegOneIsoAssociatedInvertibleSheaf (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj)
    (P : Presentation B S hS X.obj X.property)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj) :
    blowUpTwistSpace Z P hcU hcR (isEquivalenceRelation_post_reesProj (centreIdeal Z)
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P hcU hcR hcRR) (-1) ≅
      associatedInvertibleSheaf B S hS (blowUpAlong Z P hcU hcR
          (isEquivalenceRelation_post_reesProj (centreIdeal Z)
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P hcU hcR hcRR))
        (exceptionalDivisor Z P hcU hcR (isEquivalenceRelation_post_reesProj (centreIdeal Z)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P hcU hcR hcRR))
        (isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalDivisor_blowUpAlong Z P hcU hcR
          (isEquivalenceRelation_post_reesProj (centreIdeal Z)
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P hcU hcR hcRR))
declarations.comment: part (3): the canonical isomorphism O_{X'}(-1) = O_{X'}(E) on the blowup of an algebraic space, O_{X'}(1) being descended along the unique transition compatible with the canonical map O(1) → O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_blowUpAlongHom'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085U.**  The blowing up `b : X' ⟶ X` of an algebraic space `X` along a closed
subspace `Z ⊆ X` is a final object of the category `𝒞` of algebraic spaces over `X` on which the
inverse image of `Z` is an effective Cartier divisor.

Membership in `𝒞` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalDivisor'` and finality is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_hom_blowUpAlong'`; the two are assembled by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_of_existsUnique_lift`.  The hypotheses are exactly the
data the construction of Tag 085Q itself takes — an étale presentation `P` of `X`, the universe
choice `HasSheafify` for the quotient presheaf, and the three `B.Contains` side conditions on
the relative `Proj`s which `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartOfSituation` already asks
for; nothing is assumed about `Z` beyond being a closed subspace, and in particular no
separatedness or density input is used.

This declaration alone carries Tag 085U.  Both halves are recovered from it by projection —
membership as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.isPullbackDefined`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalDivisor'` up to unfolding
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exceptionalDivisor'`, and finality as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.existsUnique_lift`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_blowUpAlongHom'` — so neither of those two is
registered.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_blowUpAlongHom' :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR)
declarations.comment: the blowup of an algebraic space along a closed subspace is a final object of the category of those Y over X whose inverse image of the centre is an effective Cartier divisor; both halves, membership and finality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_id_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085V.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor.  **The blowup of `X` in `Z` is the identity morphism
of `X`.**

Being the blowup of `X` in `Z` is the universal property of Tag 085U, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong` records: terminality in the category `𝒞` of algebraic
spaces over `X` on which the inverse image of `Z` is an effective Cartier divisor.  The
identity of `X` is an object of `𝒞` precisely because `Z` is an effective Cartier divisor, and
it is terminal in `𝒞` because it is already terminal in all of `Spaces/X` and `𝒞` is a full
subcategory.  Since terminal objects are unique up to unique isomorphism over `X`, this says
that the blowup of `X` in `Z` exists and is the identity of `X`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.isIso_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_id_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hZ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X Z) :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z (𝟙 X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isBlowupAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085W**, with the étale-chart representability of Stacks 085Q carried as a
hypothesis.

Let `X` be a reduced algebraic space over `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be the closed subspace cut out by a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowup of `X` in `Z`.  Then `X'` is
reduced.

The chart datum is the source's: a surjective étale morphism `a : U ⟶ X` from a scheme `U` of
the site, and the fibre product `W = U ×_X X'` as a cartesian square.  The hypothesis `hrep`
supplies what Stacks 085Q would: some blowup of `U` in the inverse image of `Z` is
representable by a scheme isomorphic to a scheme blowup of `U`.  See the module documentation
for why that hypothesis is upstream of this conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isBlowupAlong
    {X X' W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1} {b : X' ⟶ X}
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : schemeSpace V ⟶ X)
    (haE : IsEtale B S hS a.hom) (haS : IsSurjective B S hS a.hom)
    {q : W ⟶ schemeSpace V} {r : W ⟶ X'} (sq : IsPullback q r a b)
    (hrep : ∃ (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (p : Y ⟶ schemeSpace V),
      IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace a Z) p ∧
      ∃ (V' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (_ : Y.1 ≅ yoneda.obj V')
        (I : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V).IdealSheafData),
        Nonempty ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V' ≅ blowUp I)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X'.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T)
declarations.comment: given the étale-chart representability of the blowup supplied by Stacks 085Q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isBlowupAlong_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085W.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be the closed
subspace cut out by a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.  If `X` is reduced then so is the blowup
`b : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Z`.

Nothing about the blowup is assumed beyond its universal property, Stacks 085U: the étale chart
of `X'` the proof runs on is the one the construction of Stacks 085Q supplies, namely the
relative `Proj` `P_U` of the Rees algebra of the chart ideal on the presenting scheme `U` of the
presentation `P`.  That scheme is the blowup of the *scheme* `U`, by
`Stacks.Blowup.reesSituationBlowUpIso`, so it is reduced by Stacks 0808; `P_U ⟶ X'` is
surjective étale, so Stacks 06MI carries reducedness to the constructed blowup, and from there
to `b` along the isomorphism of any two blowups in the same centre.

Besides `Z`, the blowup `b` and reducedness of `X` the statement takes only the data the
construction of Stacks 085Q itself takes: the presentation `P`, the universe choice
`HasSheafify` for the quotient presheaf, and the three `B.Contains` side conditions on the
relative `Proj`s which `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartOfSituation` already asks for.
None of that appears in the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isBlowupAlong_of_presentation
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj)
    (P : Presentation B S hS X.obj X.property)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal Z)
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal Z)
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal Z)
        (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X'.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T)
declarations.comment: the blowup of a reduced algebraic space in a closed subspace is reduced, with no assumed inputs beyond the Stacks 085Q construction data — the étale presentation P of the space, the HasSheafify universe choice for the quotient presheaf, and the three B.Contains size conditions on the relative Projs of the chart, relation and double situations — none of which occurs in the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_blowUpAlongHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085X.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed
subspace and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z` of Stacks 085Q.  Then for every
effective Cartier divisor `D` on `X` the pullback `b⁻¹(D)` is defined in the sense of Stacks
083Y: the inverse image of `D` along `b` is again an effective Cartier divisor, on `X'`.

By Stacks 083C (2) ⟹ (1) it is enough to see this on one surjective étale scheme chart of `X'`,
and the construction supplies one: the relative `Proj` `P_U` of the Rees algebra of `𝓘_Z|_U` on
the presenting scheme `U` of the étale presentation, whose composite with `b` is `P_U ⟶ U ⟶ X`.
The inverse image of `b⁻¹(D)` there is therefore the inverse image along `P_U ⟶ U` of the closed
subscheme `D ×_X U` of `U`, which is an effective Cartier divisor on `U` by Stacks 083C
(1) ⟹ (3); and for a scheme the inverse image of an effective Cartier divisor along a blowup is
an effective Cartier divisor by Stacks 0809.

The parameters `P`, `hcU`, `hcR` and `heq` are the ones the blowup of Stacks 085Q is built from
and only name the blowup; the hypothesis on `D` is the source's own.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_blowUpAlongHom (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    IsPullbackDefined B S hS (blowUpAlongHom Z P hcU hcR heq) D
declarations.comment: for the blowup of Stacks 085Q: with no assumed inputs beyond the construction data P, hcU, hcR and heq naming the blowup, every effective Cartier divisor on an algebraic space has a defined pullback along it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_isBlowupAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085X, for an arbitrary blowup.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`,
let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be *a* blowup of `X` in `Z`, in the sense
of the universal property of Stacks 085U.  Then for every effective Cartier divisor `D` on `X`
the pullback `b⁻¹(D)` is defined in the sense of Stacks 083Y.

This is the source's statement: nothing distinguishes `b` beyond being a blowup of `X` in a
closed subspace, and `D` is an arbitrary effective Cartier divisor.  A blowup in a fixed centre
is unique up to isomorphism over the base,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.exists_iso`, and the blowup of Stacks 085Q is one,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_blowUpAlongHom'` (Stacks 085U); so `b` is isomorphic over
`X` to the constructed blowup, for which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_blowUpAlongHom` gives the conclusion; and that
conclusion crosses the isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_iso_over`.

The parameters `P`, `hcU`, `hcR` and `hcRR` are those of the construction of Stacks 085Q, used
only to produce the blowup `b` is compared against; none of them occurs in the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_isBlowupAlong {X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {b : X' ⟶ X}
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    IsPullbackDefined B S hS b D
declarations.comment: the source statement, for any b which is a blowup of X in a closed subspace in the sense of the Stacks 085U universal property; with no assumed inputs apart from the Stacks 085Q construction data P, hcU, hcR and hcRR, which does not occur in the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_exists_isBlowupAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085X.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be a blowup of `X` in a closed subspace.  Then for every effective Cartier divisor
`D` on `X` the pullback `b⁻¹(D)` is defined in the sense of Stacks 083Y: the inverse image of
`D` along `b` is an effective Cartier divisor on `X'`.

"A blowup of `X` in a closed subspace" is `∃ Z, IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b`: `b` is a final object
of the category of algebraic spaces over `X` on which the inverse image of the closed subspace
`Z` is an effective Cartier divisor (Stacks 085U), so `b` is isomorphic over `X` to the blowing
up of `X` along `Z` of Stacks 085Q.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_exists_isBlowupAlong {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (b : X' ⟶ X) (hb : ∃ Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    ∀ D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D →
      IsPullbackDefined B S hS b D
declarations.comment: the full statement, for every morphism b which is a blowup of X in some closed subspace (Stacks 085U universal property) and every effective Cartier divisor D on X; no construction data and no size condition on the site among the hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_comp_of_isBlowupAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085Y.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z, Y ⊆ X` be closed subspaces.  Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be a blowup of `X` in `Z` and let
`b' : X'' ⟶ X'` be a blowup of `X'` in the inverse image `b⁻¹(Y)`, both in the sense of the
universal property of Stacks 085U.  Then the composite `b' ≫ b` is the blowup of `X` in the sum
`Z + Y`, the closed subspace cut out by the product of the two defining ideals (Stacks 083U).

Read through that universal property, which is how `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong` says
"is the blowup", the conclusion asserts both that the blowup of `X` in `Z + Y` exists and that
it is `b' ≫ b`; that is the source's "`X'' ⟶ X` is canonically isomorphic to the blowing up of
`X` in `𝓘𝓙`", and the isomorphism itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_blowup_comp_of_isBlowupAlong'`.

The hypotheses on the two blowups are the source's own: each is named only by being a blowup of
its centre.  What is carried beyond them is the construction data of Stacks 085Q for the second
centre `b⁻¹(Y)` — an étale presentation `P` of `X'`, the `HasSheafify` universe choice, and the
three `B.Contains` side conditions on the relative `Proj`s which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartOfSituation` already asks for.  That data produces the
*constructed* blowup of `X'` in `b⁻¹(Y)`, which is what Stacks 085X is proved for; none of it
occurs in the conclusion, and no input of Stacks 085Y is assumed.

The proof is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_comp_of_isBlowupAlong` with its Tag 085X
hypothesis discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_isBlowupAlong`, applied
to the effective Cartier divisor `b⁻¹(Z)` on `X'` — effective Cartier because `b` is the blowup
of `Z`, so this is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.isPullbackDefined` of `hb`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_comp_of_isBlowupAlong'
    {Z Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1} {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    {b' : X'' ⟶ X'} (hb' : IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace b Y) b')
    (P : Presentation B S hS X'.obj X'.property)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y)) P).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y)) P).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace b Y)) P).relativeProj) :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS X Z Y) (b' ≫ b)
declarations.comment: with no assumed inputs beyond the Stacks 085Q construction data P, hcU, hcR and hcRR for the second centre, which does not occur in the conclusion: for b a blowup of X in Z and b' a blowup of X' in the inverse image of Y, both in the sense of the Stacks 085U universal property, the composite b' followed by b is the blowup of X in the sum Z + Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_isBlowupAlong_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 085Z.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a
closed subspace whose closed immersion is of finite presentation — equivalently, whose
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` is of finite type.  Then every blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in
`Z` (in `𝓘`) is a proper morphism.

The source's proof: properness is étale local on the target (Stacks 083R), blowing up commutes
with flat base change (Stacks 085S), and over a scheme chart the blowup is proper because `𝓘`
is of finite type there (Stacks 02NS, 01WC).  That is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_isBlowupAlong_of_hasReesProjChartInSite`, applied on the
chart of an étale presentation of `X`, on which the relative `Proj`s the argument reads lie in
the site by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasReesProjChartInSite_of_isFinitePresentation`.

The only argument beyond the source's is the instance `HasSheafify` for the big fppf topology:
the existence of sheafification of `Type u`-valued presheaves on the site, which this library's
construction of blowups of algebraic spaces (Stacks 085Q) and its chart description
(Stacks 085R) are stated with.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_isBlowupAlong_of_isFinitePresentation (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (b : X' ⟶ X) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.1.ι) (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    IsProper B S hS b.hom
declarations.comment: the blowup b : X' -> X of an algebraic space X in a closed subspace Z whose closed immersion is of finite presentation (equivalently, whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is of finite type) is a proper morphism, at the source's hypotheses: the relative Proj charts the proof reads are shown to lie in the site by hasReesProjChartInSite_of_isFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isCompositeCentre_isBlowupAlong_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0860.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S`.  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace of finite presentation and let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` in `Z`.  Let `Z' ⊆ X'` be a closed subspace of finite
presentation and let `c : X'' ⟶ X'` be the blowing up of `X'` in `Z'`.  Then there exists a
closed subspace `Y ⊆ X` of finite presentation such that `|Y| = |Z| ∪ |b|(|Z'|)` and
`c ≫ b : X'' ⟶ X` is isomorphic to the blowing up of `X` in `Y`.

The blowups are named by their universal property, Stacks 085U
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong`), so "isomorphic to the blowing up of `X` in `Y`" is
`IsBlowupAlong B S hS Y (c ≫ b)`, and `|Y| = |Z| ∪ |b|(|Z'|)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCompositeCentre`.  Quasi-separatedness of `X` is absolute
quasi-separatedness, which needs the terminal scheme in the site (`hZ`).

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isCompositeCentre_isBlowupAlong` with its second centre
supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasSecondCentre`; see the module documentation for how that
replaces the source's appeal to Stacks 085N.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompositeCentre_isBlowupAlong_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1} {b : X' ⟶ X} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (hZfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.1.ι)
    {Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1} {c : X'' ⟶ X'} (hc : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z' c)
    (hZ'fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z'.1.ι) :
    ∃ Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1, IsFinitePresentation B S hS Y.1.ι ∧
      IsCompositeCentre B S hS b Z Z' Y ∧ IsBlowupAlong B S hS Y (c ≫ b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0862, part (1).** The strict transform of an `𝒪_X`-module `F` along a morphism
`b : A' ⟶ A` relative to a subspace `E ⊆ A'`: pull `F` back to `X ×_A A'` along `pr_X` and divide
out the submodule of those sections that are supported on `|pr_{A'}^{-1}E|`.

Stated for an arbitrary morphism `b` together with an arbitrary subspace `E` of its source, this
specializes to the strict transform with respect to the blowup of `A` in a closed subspace
`Z ⊆ A` on taking `b` that blowup and `E = b^{-1}Z` its exceptional divisor.  Stacks 0862 states
the construction for a quasi-coherent `F`, which is the case it is applied in; the construction
itself uses nothing of `F`, so no quasi-coherence hypothesis is carried here.

Quasi-coherence of the strict transform is *not* asserted: it would need the preamble of the
section containing Stacks 0862 — that `E` is an effective Cartier divisor, that its preimage is
locally principal, and that the complement of the latter has an affine inclusion — none of which
is available for algebraic spaces, together with quasi-coherence of a cokernel on the small étale
site.  See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def strictTransformSheaf (E : Subfunctor A'.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS (strictTransformPullback B S hS f b).1
      (strictTransformPullback B S hS f b).2
declarations.comment: strict transform of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransform
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0862, part (2).** The strict transform of an algebraic space `f : X ⟶ A` over `A`
along a morphism `b : A' ⟶ A` relative to a subspace `E ⊆ A'`: the closed subspace of `X ×_A A'`
determined by the ideal of those sections of `𝒪_{X ×_A A'}` that are supported on
`|pr_{A'}^{-1}E|`.

Stated for an arbitrary morphism `b` together with an arbitrary subspace `E` of its source, this
specializes to the strict transform with respect to the blowup of `A` in a closed subspace
`Z ⊆ A` on taking `b` that blowup and `E = b^{-1}Z` its exceptional divisor.

The closed subspace is realized as the infimum of those closed subspaces whose defining ideal is
dominated by that ideal of supported sections, which is a closed subspace unconditionally, and
which coincides with the closed subspace cut out by the ideal whenever the latter exists, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSubfunctor_eq_of_definingIdealSheaf_eq`.

Quasi-coherence of the defining ideal is *not* asserted: it would need the preamble of the
section containing Stacks 0862 — that `E` is an effective Cartier divisor, that its preimage is
locally principal, and that the complement of the latter has an affine inclusion — none of which
is available for algebraic spaces.  See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def strictTransform (E : Subfunctor A'.1) :
    ClosedSubspaces B S hS (strictTransformPullback B S hS f b).1
declarations.comment: strict transform of a space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_baseChange_blowup_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0863, part (1).** Let `Z ⊆ 𝔅` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`,
let `b : 𝔅' ⟶ 𝔅` be the blowup of `𝔅` in `Z` and let `f : X ⟶ 𝔅` be an algebraic space over
`𝔅`.  Let

```
U ⟶ X
↓     ↓
𝒱 ⟶ 𝔅
```

be a commutative square with étale horizontal arrows, and let `v' : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝒱` be the blowup of
`𝒱` in the inverse image `Z ×_𝔅 𝒱` of `Z`.  Then:

* `𝒱' = 𝒱 ×_𝔅 𝔅'`, by a cartesian square over `v` and `b`;
* the resulting morphism `m : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝔅'` is étale;
* the induced morphism `U ×_𝒱 𝒱' ⟶ X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` is étale.

The first assertion is Stacks 085S applied to `v`, which is flat because it is étale.  The
second is the base change of an étale morphism along `b`.  For the third,
`U ×_𝒱 𝒱' = (X ×_𝔅 𝔅') ×_X U`, so the morphism is a base change of the étale morphism
`u : U ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_baseChange_blowup_of_isEtale
    {𝔅 X 𝒱 U B' V' W W' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS 𝔅.1} {b : B' ⟶ 𝔅} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    {f : X ⟶ 𝔅} {v : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝔅} (hv : IsEtale B S hS v.hom)
    {u : U ⟶ X} (hu : IsEtale B S hS u.hom) {w : U ⟶ 𝒱} (hcomm : u ≫ f = w ≫ v)
    {v' : V' ⟶ 𝒱} (hv' : IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) v')
    {pX : W ⟶ X} {pB' : W ⟶ B'} (sq : IsPullback pX pB' f b)
    {qU : W' ⟶ U} {qV' : W' ⟶ V'} (sq' : IsPullback qU qV' w v') :
    ∃ m : V' ⟶ B', IsPullback v' m v b ∧ IsEtale B S hS m.hom ∧
      ∃ can : W' ⟶ W, can ≫ pX = qU ≫ u ∧ can ≫ pB' = qV' ≫ m ∧
        IsEtale B S hS can.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the blowup localizes étale-locally, and the induced morphisms are étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtale_strictTransformSheaf_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0863, part (3).** In the situation of part (1), let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module.  Then
there are `m : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝔅'` presenting `𝒱' = 𝒱 ×_𝔅 𝔅'` and a morphism
`can : U ×_𝒱 𝒱' ⟶ X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` over `u : U ⟶ X` and over `m`, and `can` is étale and pulls the
strict transform of `F` relative to the blowup `b : 𝔅' ⟶ 𝔅` of `𝔅` in `Z` back to the strict
transform of `F|_U` relative to the blowup `v' : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝒱` of `𝒱` in `Z ×_𝔅 𝒱`.

The two commutations `can ≫ pr_X = pr_U ≫ u` and `can ≫ pr_{𝔅'} = pr_{𝒱'} ≫ m` say that `can`
is *the* canonical morphism of the tag, the universal property of `X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` determining it
from them; so pulling back along it is the restriction to `U ×_𝒱 𝒱'` that the tag speaks of.

Here the strict transform is the one of Stacks 0862,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheaf`, taken with respect to the blowup together with
its exceptional divisor `b^{-1}Z`, respectively `v'^{-1}(v^{-1}Z)`; the fibre products are the
ones of `AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct`, and `F|_U` is the pullback `u^*F` of
Stacks 03LU, which for the étale `u` is restriction of sections by Stacks 03LW.

`m`, `can` and their properties come from part (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_baseChange_blowup_of_isEtale`, applied to the two canonical
cartesian squares; the identification of the strict transforms is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheafEtaleRestrictionIso`, whose hypothesis on the
exceptional divisors is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_preimage_exceptional`.

No quasi-coherence of `F` is assumed: the source assumes it because that is the case the tag is
applied in, and neither the construction of the strict transform nor this comparison uses it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEtale_strictTransformSheaf_restriction
    {𝔅 X 𝒱 U B' V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS 𝔅.1} {b : B' ⟶ 𝔅} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    {f : X ⟶ 𝔅} {v : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝔅} (hv : IsEtale B S hS v.hom)
    {u : U ⟶ X} (hu : IsEtale B S hS u.hom) {w : U ⟶ 𝒱} (hcomm : u ≫ f = w ≫ v)
    {v' : V' ⟶ 𝒱} (hv' : IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) v')
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    ∃ (m : V' ⟶ B') (can : strictTransformPullback B S hS w v' ⟶
        strictTransformPullback B S hS f b),
      IsPullback v' m v b ∧ IsEtale B S hS can.hom ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w v' ≫ u ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS w v' ≫ m ∧
        Nonempty ((modulePullback B S hS can).obj
            (strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F) ≅
          strictTransformSheaf B S hS w v'
            (preimageClosedSubspace v' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)).1
            ((modulePullback B S hS u).obj F))
declarations.comment: part (3): the strict transform of a module restricts to the strict transform of its restriction; stated for an arbitrary module, the source's quasi-coherence being unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_of_isBlowupAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0863, part (2).** Let `Z ⊆ 𝔅` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`,
let `b : 𝔅' ⟶ 𝔅` be the blowup of `𝔅` in `Z`, let `f : X ⟶ 𝔅` be an algebraic space over `𝔅`,
let

```
U ⟶ X
↓     ↓
𝒱 ⟶ 𝔅
```

be a commutative square with étale horizontal arrows and let `v' : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝒱` be the blowup of
`𝒱` in the inverse image `Z ×_𝔅 𝒱`.  Then the strict transform `U'` of `U` with respect to `v'`
is `X' ×_X U`, where `X'` is the strict transform of `X` with respect to `b`.

Precisely: there are `m : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝔅'` presenting `𝒱' = 𝒱 ×_𝔅 𝔅'` and an étale
`can : U ×_𝒱 𝒱' ⟶ X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` over `u` and over `m`, sitting in a cartesian square that presents
`U ×_𝒱 𝒱' = (X ×_𝔅 𝔅') ×_X U`, and `U'` is the inverse image of `X'` along `can` — which under
that presentation is the base change of `X'` along `u`.

**No hypothesis beyond the source's is carried, and in particular being a blowup is not
assumed.**  The two blowups are the ones Tag 085Q constructs,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.blowUpAlongHom'` for `𝔅` in `Z` and for `𝒱` in `Z ×_𝔅 𝒱`; that each
of them *is* the blowup, in the sense of the universal property of Stacks 085U, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_blowUpAlongHom'`.  The arguments `P`, `P'` and the six
`B.Contains` side conditions are the construction data Tag 085Q itself takes — an étale
presentation of the space being blown up and the set-theoretic conditions on the three relative
`Proj`s that `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeProjChartOfSituation` asks for — and nothing is
assumed about `Z` beyond being a closed subspace.

The two halves of the argument are as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_of_isEtale`: the étale comparison
of the ideals of supported sections, and that the strict transform of `X` is honestly cut out
by that ideal, which comes from the exceptional divisor `b^{-1}Z` being an effective Cartier
divisor — one half of the universal property of Stacks 085U.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_of_isBlowupAlong
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Bl.obj} (P : Presentation B S hS Bl.obj Bl.property)
    (hcU : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcR : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    (hcRR : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal Z)
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal Z) P).relativeProj)
    {f : X ⟶ Bl} {v : Vv ⟶ Bl} (hv : IsEtale B S hS v.hom)
    {u : U ⟶ X} (hu : IsEtale B S hS u.hom) {w : U ⟶ Vv} (hcomm : u ≫ f = w ≫ v)
    (P' : Presentation B S hS Vv.obj Vv.property)
    (hcU' : B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)) P').relativeProj)
    (hcR' : B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)) P').relativeProj)
    (hcRR' : B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z))
      (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)) P').relativeProj) :
    ∃ (m : blowUpAlong' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR' ⟶
        blowUpAlong' Z P hcU hcR hcRR)
      (can : strictTransformPullback B S hS w
          (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR') ⟶
        strictTransformPullback B S hS f (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR)),
      IsPullback (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR') m v
          (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR) ∧
        IsEtale B S hS can.hom ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR) =
          strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w
            (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR') ≫ u ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR) =
          strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS w
            (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR') ≫ m ∧
        IsPullback can
          (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w
            (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR'))
          (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR)) u ∧
        strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS w
            (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR')
            (preimageClosedSubspace
              (blowUpAlongHom' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) P' hcU' hcR' hcRR')
              (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)).1 =
          (strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS f (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR)
            (preimageClosedSubspace (blowUpAlongHom' Z P hcU hcR hcRR) Z).1).preimage
            can.hom
declarations.comment: part (2), for the blowups of 085Q themselves: the strict transform of an étale chart U is the base change along u of the strict transform of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0863, part (2).** Let `Z ⊆ 𝔅` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`,
let `b : 𝔅' ⟶ 𝔅` be the blowup of `𝔅` in `Z`, let `f : X ⟶ 𝔅` be an algebraic space over `𝔅`,
let

```
U ⟶ X
↓     ↓
𝒱 ⟶ 𝔅
```

be a commutative square with étale horizontal arrows and let `v' : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝒱` be the blowup of
`𝒱` in the inverse image `Z ×_𝔅 𝒱`.  Then the strict transform `U'` of `U` with respect to `v'`
is `X' ×_X U`, where `X'` is the strict transform of `X` with respect to `b`.

Precisely: there are `m : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝔅'` presenting `𝒱' = 𝒱 ×_𝔅 𝔅'` and an étale
`can : U ×_𝒱 𝒱' ⟶ X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` over `u` and over `m`, sitting in a cartesian square that presents
`U ×_𝒱 𝒱' = (X ×_𝔅 𝔅') ×_X U`, and `U'` is the inverse image of `X'` along `can` — which under
that presentation is the base change of `X'` along `u`.

**No hypothesis beyond the source's is carried.**  The existence of a closed subspace cut out by
the ideal of sections supported on the exceptional preimage, which is all that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_of_isEtale` asks for beyond the
étale comparison of those ideals, comes from the exceptional divisor `b^{-1}Z` being an
effective Cartier divisor on `𝔅'`; and that is one half of the universal property of Stacks
085U, so `hb` supplies it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Bl.1} {b : B' ⟶ Bl} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    {f : X ⟶ Bl} {v : Vv ⟶ Bl} (hv : IsEtale B S hS v.hom)
    {u : U ⟶ X} (hu : IsEtale B S hS u.hom) {w : U ⟶ Vv} (hcomm : u ≫ f = w ≫ v)
    {v' : V' ⟶ Vv} (hv' : IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) v') :
    ∃ (m : V' ⟶ B') (can : strictTransformPullback B S hS w v' ⟶
        strictTransformPullback B S hS f b),
      IsPullback v' m v b ∧ IsEtale B S hS can.hom ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w v' ≫ u ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS w v' ≫ m ∧
        IsPullback can (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w v')
          (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b) u ∧
        strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS w v'
            (preimageClosedSubspace v' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)).1 =
          (strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS f b
            (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1).preimage can.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): the strict transform of an étale chart U is the base change along u of the strict transform of X, for an arbitrary blowup and with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_strictTransformSheaf_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0863, parts (2) and (3).** In the situation of part (1) there are `m : 𝒱' ⟶ 𝔅'`
presenting `𝒱' = 𝒱 ×_𝔅 𝔅'` and an étale `can : U ×_𝒱 𝒱' ⟶ X ×_𝔅 𝔅'` over `u` and over `m`,
sitting in a cartesian square that presents `U ×_𝒱 𝒱' = (X ×_𝔅 𝔅') ×_X U`, such that

* the strict transform `U'` of `U` with respect to `v'` is the inverse image of the strict
  transform `X'` of `X` with respect to `b` along `can`, which is part (2); and
* for every `𝒪_X`-module `F` the pullback along `can` of the strict transform of `F` with
  respect to `b` is the strict transform of `F|_U` with respect to `v'`, which is part (3).

Both for the *same* `m` and the same `can`: the two parts are read off the single comparison
morphism that part (1), `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_baseChange_blowup_of_isEtale`,
returns for the two canonical cartesian squares.  This is what a consumer of the tag needs, the
two parts separately leaving the two copies of `can` unidentified.

No hypothesis beyond the source's is carried, and no quasi-coherence of `F`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtale_strictTransformSheaf_restriction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransform_eq_preimage_strictTransformSheaf_iso
    {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Bl.1} {b : B' ⟶ Bl} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    {f : X ⟶ Bl} {v : Vv ⟶ Bl} (hv : IsEtale B S hS v.hom)
    {u : U ⟶ X} (hu : IsEtale B S hS u.hom) {w : U ⟶ Vv} (hcomm : u ≫ f = w ≫ v)
    {v' : V' ⟶ Vv} (hv' : IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace v Z) v') :
    ∃ (m : V' ⟶ B') (can : strictTransformPullback B S hS w v' ⟶
