        strictTransformPullback B S hS f b),
      IsPullback v' m v b ∧ IsEtale B S hS can.hom ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w v' ≫ u ∧
        can ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b =
          strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS w v' ≫ m ∧
        IsPullback can (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS w v')
          (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b) u ∧
        strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS w v'
            (preimageClosedSubspace v' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)).1 =
          (strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS f b
            (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1).preimage can.hom ∧
        ∀ F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
          Nonempty ((modulePullback B S hS can).obj
              (strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F) ≅
            strictTransformSheaf B S hS w v'
              (preimageClosedSubspace v' (preimageClosedSubspace v Z)).1
              ((modulePullback B S hS u).obj F))
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (3) for one and the same comparison morphism, for an arbitrary blowup and with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_strictTransform
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0864, clause (1).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` be an algebraic space over `S`,
let `Z ⊆ A` be a closed subspace, let `b : A' ⟶ A` be the blowup of `A` in `Z` and let
`f : X ⟶ A` be an algebraic space over `A`.  Then the strict transform `X'` of `X` — the closed
subspace of `X ×_A A'` of Stacks 0862, clause (2) — with its morphism
`X' ⟶ X ×_A A' ⟶ X`, **is the blowup of `X` in the inverse image `f⁻¹Z`.**

No hypothesis beyond `b` being the blowup of `A` in `Z` is carried: in particular no second
blowup is assumed to exist, and nothing is assumed of `f`.

Both halves of the universal property of Stacks 085U are checked.  Membership in the category
`𝒞` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_strictTransform_of_isBlowupAlong`.  For
finality, an object `y : Y ⟶ X` of `𝒞` gives a morphism `Y ⟶ X ×_A A'` with components `y` and
the classifying morphism of `b`, which factors through `X'` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_eq_strictTransformSpaceι`; and the factorization is unique
because `X' ⟶ X ×_A A'` is a monomorphism, `X ×_A A'` is a fibre product and the classifying
morphism of `b` is unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_strictTransform (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS (preimageClosedSubspace f Z)
      (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 ≫
        strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)
declarations.comment: part (1): the strict transform of X is the blowup of X in the inverse image of the centre, for an arbitrary blowup of the base and with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheafIso_modulePushforward_strictTransformSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0864, clause (2).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` be an algebraic space over `S`,
let `Z ⊆ A` be a closed subspace, let `b : A' ⟶ A` be the blowup of `A` in `Z`, let `f : X ⟶ A`
be an algebraic space over `A` and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module.  Then the strict transform `F'` of
`F` — the quotient of `pr_X^*F` by its sections supported on the exceptional preimage — **is the
direct image, along the closed immersion `X' ⟶ X ×_A A'` of the strict transform of `X`, of the
strict transform of `F` relative to the blowup `X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `f⁻¹Z`.**

The isomorphism carries the quotient map onto `F'` to the canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheafPushforwardComparison`, and since that quotient map
is an epimorphism there is exactly one isomorphism which does; that is the sense in which the
isomorphism of clause (2) is canonical.

That `X' ⟶ X` is the blowup of `X` in `f⁻¹Z`, which is what makes the strict transform of `F`
relative to it the one clause (2) speaks of, is clause (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_strictTransform`; the statement is otherwise
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheafIso_modulePushforward_of_isBlowupAlong` at
`i` the closed immersion of the strict transform.

No hypothesis beyond `b` being the blowup of `A` in `Z` is carried: in particular no second
blowup is assumed to exist, nothing is assumed of `f`, and `F` is an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module —
the Stacks Project states clause (2) for a quasi-coherent `F`, and the argument uses nothing of
`F`.  See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransformSheafIso_modulePushforward_strictTransformSpace
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    ∃ e : strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F ≅
        (modulePushforward B S hS
            (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1)).obj
          (strictTransformSheafOver B S hS
            (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 ≫
              strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)
            (preimageClosedSubspace
              (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 ≫
                strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)
              (preimageClosedSubspace f Z)) F),
      strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F ≫ e.hom =
        strictTransformSheafPushforwardComparison B S hS f b Z
          (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1) F
declarations.comment: part (2): the strict transform of a module is the direct image, along the closed immersion of the strict transform of X into X ×_A A', of the strict transform of that module relative to the blowup X' ⟶ X, by the isomorphism carrying the quotient map onto the first to the canonical comparison; for an arbitrary blowup of the base, an arbitrary module, and with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSubfunctor_eq_top_of_isFlatAt_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0865, part (1).** Let `Z ⊆ A` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`,
let `b : A' ⟶ A` be the blowup of `A` in `Z` and let `f : X ⟶ A` be an algebraic space over
`A`.  If `X` is flat over `A` at every point lying over `Z`, then the strict transform of `X`
with respect to `b` is the whole base change `X ×_A A'`.

The hypotheses are the source's and nothing else.  The ideal of sections of `𝒪_{X ×_A A'}`
supported on the exceptional preimage vanishes on every étale chart,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformIdealSubmodule_eq_bot_of_isFlatAt`; the strict
transform is then the whole base change by Stacks 03MB, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSubfunctor_eq_top_of_forall_definingIdealAt_eq_bot`.

The source reduces part (1) to the case of schemes by étale localization, Stacks 0863 parts (2)
and (3), which this library does not have; the route taken instead is native to algebraic
spaces and runs through the étale charts of the fibre product.  See the module documentation of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatAtPointBaseChange.lean`.

The conditional form of this statement in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformProperties.lean` keeps the name
without the suffix `_unconditional`; the suffix marks the same conclusion with that form's
assumed input discharged, and the tag is registered here.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictTransformSubfunctor_eq_top_of_isFlatAt_unconditional (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (hflat : ∀ x : points B S hS X.1,
      pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.1.ι) →
        IsFlatAt B S hS f.hom x) :
    strictTransformSubfunctor B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) = ⊤
declarations.comment: part (1), with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_strictTransformSheafQuotient_of_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0865, part (2).** In the situation of part (1), let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module which is flat over `A` at every point lying over `Z`.  Then the canonical quotient
map `pr_X^*F ⟶ F'` onto the strict transform of `F` is an isomorphism, so the strict transform
of `F` is `pr_X^*F`.

The hypotheses are the source's and nothing else: `b` is the blowup of `A` in `Z` in the sense
of the universal property of Stacks 085U, `F` is quasi-coherent, and `F` is flat over `A` at the
points above `Z` — read at geometric points, condition (2) of Stacks 05VU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`, a geometric point lying over `Z` when its
underlying point of `|X|` does.

The submodule of sections of `pr_X^*F` supported on the exceptional preimage vanishes,
`Space.supportedSections_exceptionalPreimage_ι_eq_zero_of_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`;
the strict transform is the cokernel of its inclusion, so the quotient map is the cokernel
projection of a zero morphism and hence invertible.

The source reduces part (2) to the case of schemes by étale localization, Stacks 0863 parts (2)
and (3); the route taken instead is native to algebraic spaces and runs through the étale charts
of the fibre product, exactly as for part (1).  See the module documentation of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatModuleSupportedSections.lean`.

The conditional form of this statement in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformProperties.lean` keeps the name
without the suffix `_unconditional`; the suffix marks the same conclusion with that form's
assumed input discharged, and the tag is registered here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_strictTransformSheafQuotient_of_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_unconditional
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b)
    (hflat : ∀ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1,
      pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom xbar.image ∈
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.1.ι) →
        IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar) :
    IsIso (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F)
declarations.comment: part (2), with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_modulePushforward_strictTransformSheaf_iso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0866.** Let `Z ⊆ A` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`, let
`b : A' ⟶ A` be the blowup of `A` in `Z`, let `g : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic
spaces over `A`, let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let `g' : X ×_A A' ⟶ Y ×_A A'` be the base
change of `g`.  Then `g'_*` of the strict transform of `F` relative to `b` is the strict
transform of `g_* F`, compatibly with the two quotient maps and the base-change comparison.

`F` is quasi-coherent, which is the tag's own hypothesis on it.

The hypotheses are the tag's own, and the three inputs the argument runs on are all proved.

The base-change isomorphism `α : g'_* pr_X^*F ≅ pr_Y^* g_*F` — the base-change clause of
Stacks 07U8, that is Stacks 02KG for an affine morphism of algebraic spaces — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_iso_modulePushforward_modulePullback_of_isAffineHom` at the
cartesian square of the two ambient base changes along `b`.

The identification `β` of the direct image of the sections supported on the exceptional
preimage with the sections of `pr_Y^*(g_*F)` supported there, compatibly with `α`, is
Stacks 085B transported along `α`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_modulePushforward_supportedSectionsSubmodule_of_eq_preimage`,
together with the identification of the exceptional preimage upstairs as the inverse image of the
one downstairs, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exceptionalPreimageSet_comp_eq_preimage`.

Right exactness of `g'_*` on the sequence at hand — that the direct image along the affine
morphism `g'` preserves the cokernel defining the strict transform, which is the use the
Stacks Project makes of Stacks 01SB — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesCokernel_submoduleι_modulePushforward_of_isAffineHom`, applied
to the base change `g'` of `g`, which is affine by Stacks 03WI; its two quasi-coherence inputs
are quasi-coherence of `pr_X^*F`, which is Stacks 03GA, and quasi-coherence of the submodule of
sections supported on the exceptional preimage, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_supportedSections_exceptionalPreimage` above, the
exceptional divisor of a blowup being an effective Cartier divisor and hence locally principal.

What this proof does is the argument of the Stacks Project: the strict transform is a cokernel,
right exactness of the affine direct image carries it through `g'_*`, and `α` identifies the
resulting cokernel with the cokernel defining the strict transform of `g_* F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_modulePushforward_strictTransformSheaf_iso_unconditional
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (hg : IsAffineHom B S hS g.hom) :
    ∃ (α : (modulePushforward B S hS (strictTransformPullbackMap B S hS g f b)).obj
              ((modulePullback B S hS
                (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS (g ≫ f) b)).obj F) ≅
            (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).obj
              ((modulePushforward B S hS g).obj F))
        (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (strictTransformPullbackMap B S hS g f b)).obj
              (strictTransformSheaf B S hS (g ≫ f) b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F) ≅
            strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)
              ((modulePushforward B S hS g).obj F)),
      (modulePushforward B S hS (strictTransformPullbackMap B S hS g f b)).map
            (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS (g ≫ f) b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F) ≫ e.hom =
        α.hom ≫ strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)
          ((modulePushforward B S hS g).obj F)
declarations.comment: the hypotheses are the tag's own -- a blowup of the ambient space along a closed subspace, an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over it, and a quasi-coherent module -- and the base-change isomorphism of the base-change clause of Stacks 07U8, Stacks 02KG for an affine morphism of algebraic spaces, is proved on the way

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_sumClosedSubspaces_and_strictTransformSheaf_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0867.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `𝔅` be an algebraic space over `S`, let
`Z ⊆ 𝔅` be a closed subspace, let `D ⊆ 𝔅` be an effective Cartier divisor, let `Z + D` be the
closed subspace cut out by the product of the ideal sheaves of `Z` and `D`, and let
`b : B' ⟶ 𝔅` be the blowup of `𝔅` in `Z`.

1. `b` is also the blowup of `𝔅` in `Z + D`; so every blowup of `𝔅` in `Z + D` is isomorphic
   to `b` over `𝔅`
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_blowup_sumClosedSubspaces_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`).
2. For every morphism of algebraic spaces `f : X ⟶ 𝔅` and every `𝒪_X`-module `F` whose subsheaf
   of sections supported on `|f⁻¹D|` is zero, the strict transform of `F` relative to the
   blowup of `𝔅` in `Z` agrees with the strict transform of `F` relative to the blowup of `𝔅`
   in `Z + D`, which by (1) is the same morphism `b`.

Part (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_sumClosedSubspaces_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor` and
part (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheaf_preimage_sumClosedSubspaces`.  The
source asks `F` to be quasi-coherent; the statement holds for every `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBlowupAlong_sumClosedSubspaces_and_strictTransformSheaf_eq
    {𝔅 B' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS 𝔅.obj)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS 𝔅 D)
    {b : B' ⟶ 𝔅} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) :
    IsBlowupAlong B S hS (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS 𝔅 Z D) b ∧
      ∀ (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : X ⟶ 𝔅) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
        HasNoSectionsSupportedIn B S hS X
            (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom ⁻¹' subspacePointSet B S hS 𝔅.1 D.1) F →
          strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b
              (preimageClosedSubspace b (sumClosedSubspaces B S hS 𝔅 Z D)).1 F =
            strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F
declarations.comment: both parts: (1) the blowup of the space in Z is the blowup in Z + D; (2) for a module on an algebraic space over the base with no nonzero sections supported on the inverse image of D, the strict transforms for the centres Z and Z + D agree; stated for every module, quasi-coherent or not

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheaf_comp_iso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0868, part (1).** Let `Z ⊆ A` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`,
let `b : A' ⟶ A` be the blowup of `A` in `Z`, let `Z' ⊆ A'` be a closed subspace and let
`c : A'' ⟶ A'` be the blowup of `A'` in `Z'`.  Let `Y ⊆ A` be a closed subspace with
`|Y| = |Z| ∪ |b|(|Z'|)` and such that the composition `A'' ⟶ A` is the blowup of `A` in `Y`.
Then for any algebraic space `f : X ⟶ A` over `A` and any `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the strict
transform of `F` with respect to `c` of the strict transform of `F` with respect to `b` is the
strict transform of `F` with respect to `A'' ⟶ A`, compatibly with the identification of the
two ambient base changes and with the quotient maps onto the two strict transforms.

The identification of the ambient base changes `(X ×_A A') ×_{A'} A'' ≅ X ×_A A''`, together
with its compatibility with the projections to `X` and to `A''` — the two equations of the
conclusion, the first of which the comparison of the modules is stated relative to — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iteratedStrictTransformPullbackIso`, and is proved here
unconditionally.

The comparison of the modules themselves, the last conjunct, is produced with its compatibility
with the two quotient maps onto the strict transforms: pulled back along the identification of
the ambient base changes, the quotient map `pr_X^*F ⟶ F'` for the composite blowup becomes, over
the induced identification of the two pullbacks of `F`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformInnerModulePullbackIso`), the composite of the pullback
of the first quotient map with the second.  Since the first of those is an epimorphism, there is
exactly one isomorphism which does that; that is the sense in which the comparison is canonical.

Its two halves are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iteratedStrictTransformSheaf_iso` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformComposition.lean` — which carries the
compatibility of the iterated quotient with the two projections — and the universal property of
the quotient by the supported sections,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheafIso`, applied to the pullback of the
quotient map for the composite blowup along the ambient identification.  That pullback is an
epimorphism because the pullback of modules is a left adjoint; it kills only the sections
supported on the exceptional preimage of `(c ≫ b)⁻¹Y` because over the part of
`(X ×_A A') ×_{A'} A''` lying off that set it is invertible
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_modulePullback_map_cokernelπ_supportedSectionsSubmodule`, the
points there missing the exceptional preimage downstairs), which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelSectionsSupportedIn_of_mono_modulePullback_map`; and its target
has no nonzero local section supported there because the restriction of the strict transform
along that identification is the strict transform of the restriction, Stacks 0863 part (3) in
its geometry-free form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheafEtaleRestrictionIso` — applicable because the
identification is an isomorphism, hence étale.

The hypothesis of the iterated comparison on the supported sets is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exceptionalPreimageSet_compositeCentre`, which is where `hY` and the
blowup `b` are used: a blowup is injective on the points off its centre, so the exceptional
preimage of `(c ≫ b)⁻¹Y` splits as the inverse image of the first exceptional preimage together
with the exceptional preimage of `c⁻¹Z'`.

The conditional form of this statement in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformProperties.lean` keeps the name
without the suffix `_unconditional`; the suffix marks the same conclusion with that form's
assumed input discharged, and the tag is registered here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransformSheaf_comp_iso_unconditional (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A'.1) (Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (hc : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z' c)
    (hY : IsCompositeCentre B S hS b Z Z' Y) (_hd : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Y (c ≫ b)) :
    ∃ e : strictTransformPullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c ≅
        strictTransformPullback B S hS f (c ≫ b),
      ∃ hsrc : e.hom ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f (c ≫ b) =
          strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS
              (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c ≫
            strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b,
      (e.hom ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f (c ≫ b) =
        strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS
          (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c) ∧
      ∃ cmp : (modulePullback B S hS e.hom).obj
            (strictTransformSheaf B S hS f (c ≫ b) (Y.1.preimage (c ≫ b).hom) F) ≅
          strictTransformSheaf B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c
            (Z'.1.preimage c.hom) (strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F),
        (modulePullback B S hS e.hom).map
              (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f (c ≫ b)
                (Y.1.preimage (c ≫ b).hom) F) ≫ cmp.hom =
          (strictTransformInnerModulePullbackIso B S hS f (c ≫ b)
              (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)
              (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c e.hom hsrc F).hom ≫
            (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS
                  (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c)).map
                (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F) ≫
              strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS
                (strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f b) c (Z'.1.preimage c.hom)
                (strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) F)
declarations.comment: part (1): the strict transform of a module for the blowup of the base in the composite centre is the strict transform along the second blowup of the strict transform along the first, by the isomorphism carrying the pullback of the quotient map onto the former to the composite of the two quotient maps onto the latter, over the identification of the two ambient base changes and the identification of the two pullbacks of the module it induces; for an arbitrary module and with no assumed inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSpace_comp_iso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0868, part (2).** In the situation of part (1), the strict transform of `X` with
respect to `c` of the strict transform of `X` with respect to `b` is the strict transform of `X`
with respect to `A'' ⟶ A`: the two closed subspaces are isomorphic over the ambient base change
`X ×_A A''`.

The morphism `X' ×_{A'} A'' ⟶ X ×_A A''` of ambient base changes along which the comparison is
made is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iteratedStrictTransformSpaceMap`; `X'` here is the first strict
transform, the ambient base change of the second being taken over `A'` and not over `X ×_A A'`.
Its two triangles over `X` and over `A''` are the first two conjuncts of the conclusion and hold
with no hypothesis at all.

The comparison of the two closed subspaces is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iteratedStrictTransformSpace_iso` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformSpaceComposition.lean`.  Its route is the
source's own, read on ideals: the image of the second strict transform in `(X ×_A A') ×_{A'} A''`
is a closed subspace whose defining ideal is exactly the ideal of functions supported on the
exceptional preimage of `(c ≫ b)^{-1}Y`, so it *is* the strict transform of `X` with respect to
the composite by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSubfunctor_eq_of_definingIdealSheaf_eq`,
and the identification of the two ambient base changes transports that across Stacks 0863 part
(2).  One inclusion of ideals is the geometry of the two blowups (Stacks 085T through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exceptionalPreimageSet_compositeCentre`, and Stacks 0862 off the
exceptional divisor); the other is Stacks 082Z together with the fact that the second strict
transform has no nonzero local function supported there, which is Stacks 083S for the two
exceptional divisors it is built from.

The conditional form of this statement in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/StrictTransformProperties.lean` keeps the name
without the suffix `_unconditional`; the suffix marks the same conclusion with that form's
assumed input discharged, and the tag is registered here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransformSpace_comp_iso_unconditional (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A'.1) (Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (hc : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z' c)
    (hY : IsCompositeCentre B S hS b Z Z' Y) (hd : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Y (c ≫ b)) :
    ∃ (k : strictTransformPullback B S hS
          (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)) c ⟶
        strictTransformPullback B S hS f (c ≫ b))
      (j : strictTransformSpace B S hS
          (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)) c
          (Z'.1.preimage c.hom) ≅
        strictTransformSpace B S hS f (c ≫ b) (Y.1.preimage (c ≫ b).hom)),
      (k ≫ strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f (c ≫ b) =
        strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS
            (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)) c ≫
          strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) ≫
            strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b) ∧
      (k ≫ strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS f (c ≫ b) =
        strictTransformPullbackToBlowUp B S hS
          (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)) c) ∧
      j.hom ≫ strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f (c ≫ b) (Y.1.preimage (c ≫ b).hom) =
        strictTransformSpaceι B S hS
            (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)) c
            (Z'.1.preimage c.hom) ≫ k
declarations.comment: part (2): strict transform of a space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheaf_shortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0869, as far as this library reaches it.**  In the situation of Stacks 0862, let
`0 ⟶ F₁ ⟶ F₂ ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0` be a sequence of `𝒪_X`-modules which is short exact after every base
change `Y ⟶ A`.  Then the strict transforms of the `Fᵢ` relative to `(b, E)` form a short
complex whose two maps are determined by the quotient maps onto the strict transforms; the
left-hand map is a monomorphism and the right-hand map is an epimorphism, and exactness in the
middle is equivalent to epimorphy of the morphism induced on the subsheaves of sections
supported on the exceptional preimage.

Everything asserted here is unconditional.  Exactness in the middle — the heart of the tag — is
*not* proved; the last conjunct is the exact reduction of it, and the module documentation
records what would discharge the reduced statement and why that input is absent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransformSheaf_shortComplex
    (hC : ∀ (Y P : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (t : Y ⟶ A) (pX : P ⟶ X) (pY : P ⟶ Y),
      IsPullback pX pY f t → (C.map (modulePullback B S hS pX)).ShortExact) :
    ∃ (f' : strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b E C.X₁ ⟶ strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b E C.X₂)
      (g' : strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b E C.X₂ ⟶ strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b E C.X₃)
      (w : f' ≫ g' = 0),
      Mono f' ∧ Epi g' ∧
      (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b E C.X₁ ≫ f' =
        (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).map C.f ≫
          strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b E C.X₂) ∧
      (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b E C.X₂ ≫ g' =
        (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).map C.g ≫
          strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b E C.X₃) ∧
      ((ShortComplex.mk f' g' w).Exact ↔
        Epi (supportedSectionsMap (exceptionalPreimageSet B S hS f b E)
          ((modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).map C.g)))
declarations.comment: partial: the short complex of strict transforms with its two maps pinned down by the quotient maps, monomorphic on the left and epimorphic on the right, all unconditional; exactness in the middle is NOT proved and is instead reduced, as an equivalence, to epimorphy of the induced map on the subsheaves of sections supported on the exceptional preimage — the statement that Stacks 0863 parts (2) and (3) together with the scheme-level Stacks 080W would supply and that this library cannot reach

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_strictTransformSheaf_shortComplex_of_isBlowupAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0869.**  In the situation of Stacks 0862 — a blowup `b : A' ⟶ A` of an algebraic
space `A` in a closed subspace `Z`, with exceptional divisor `E = b^{-1}Z`, and an algebraic
space `f : X ⟶ A` over `A` — let `0 ⟶ F₁ ⟶ F₂ ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0` be a sequence of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules which is short exact after every base change `Y ⟶ A`.  Then the strict transforms
of the `Fᵢ` form a short complex whose two maps are determined by the quotient maps onto the
strict transforms, the left-hand map is a monomorphism, the right-hand map is an epimorphism,
and the complex is exact in the middle: the strict transforms form a short exact sequence.

The strict transform is the one of Stacks 0862,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheaf`, and "being the blowup of `A` in `Z`" is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong`, the universal property of Stacks 085U, since Stacks
085Q constructs no blowup of an algebraic space in this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictTransformSheaf_shortComplex_of_isBlowupAlong {Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1}
    {b : A' ⟶ A}
    (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (C : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hqc₁ : C.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hqc₂ : C.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hqc₃ : C.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hC : ∀ (Y P : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (t : Y ⟶ A) (pX : P ⟶ X) (pY : P ⟶ Y),
      IsPullback pX pY f t → (C.map (modulePullback B S hS pX)).ShortExact) :
    ∃ (f' : strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₁ ⟶
          strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₂)
      (g' : strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₂ ⟶
          strictTransformSheaf B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₃)
      (w : f' ≫ g' = 0),
      Mono f' ∧ Epi g' ∧
      (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₁ ≫ f' =
        (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).map C.f ≫
          strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₂) ∧
      (strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₂ ≫ g' =
        (modulePullback B S hS (strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b)).map C.g ≫
          strictTransformSheafQuotient B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom) C.X₃) ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk f' g' w).Exact
declarations.comment: the strict transforms of a short exact sequence of quasi-coherent modules which stays short exact after every base change again form a short exact sequence, with its two maps pinned down by the quotient maps onto the strict transforms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAdmissibleBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086B.** A morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` is a
**`U`-admissible blowup**, for an open subspace `U ⊆ X`, when there is a closed subspace
`Z ⊆ X` whose closed immersion into `X` is of finite presentation and whose points are disjoint
from those of `U`, such that `f` exhibits `X'` as the blowup of `X` in `Z`.

Being the blowup of `X` in `Z` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong`, the universal
property of Tag 085U: `f` is a terminal object of the category of algebraic spaces over `X` on
which the inverse image of `Z` is an effective Cartier divisor.  Since terminal objects are
unique up to unique isomorphism and the blowup of `X` in `Z` is such a terminal object, this is
the source's "`X'` is isomorphic to the blowup of `X` in `Z`"; see the module documentation, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAdmissibleBlowup.exists_iso_blowup` for that reading as a
theorem.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleBlowup (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) (f : X' ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAdmissibleBlowup_comp_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`
and let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace.  Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be a `U`-admissible blowup and let
`c : X'' ⟶ X'` be a `U`-admissible blowup.  Then the composition `c ≫ b : X'' ⟶ X` is a
`U`-admissible blowup.

Since `b` is an isomorphism over `U`, the source regards `U` as an open subspace of `X'` as well;
as a subspace of `X'` it is the inverse image `b⁻¹(U)`, which is how the admissibility of `c`
is stated.  Quasi-separatedness of `X` is absolute quasi-separatedness, which needs the terminal
scheme in the site (`hZ`).  The source also takes `U` quasi-compact; that hypothesis is not
needed and is omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdmissibleBlowup_comp_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) {b : X' ⟶ X} {c : X'' ⟶ X'}
    (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b)
    (hc : IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS
      ⟨U.1.preimage b.hom, isOpenSubspace_preimage B S hS b.hom U.1 X.2 X'.2 U.2⟩ c) :
    IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U (c ≫ b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.exists_restrictionToOpen
declarations.doc:
**The blowup of `X` in a closed subspace `Z` restricts, over an open subspace `V ⊆ X`, to
the blowup of `V` in `Z ∩ V`.**  This is the clause "whose restriction to `V` is `V'`" of Tag
086D, and the one step of its proof that the universal property of Tag 085U supplies on its own.

The inverse image `f⁻¹(V)` is an open subspace of `X'` and exhibits a cartesian square over
`V ⊆ X` by Tag 083Q; the inclusion of an open subspace is étale, hence flat, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.of_isPullback_of_isFlat` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsBlowupAlong.exists_restrictionToOpen {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {f : X' ⟶ X}
    (V : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hf : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z f) :
    ∃ (P : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (p : P ⟶ openSubspace B S hS X V) (q : P ⟶ X'),
      IsPullback p q (openSubspaceι B S hS X V) f ∧
        IsBlowupAlong B S hS (closedSubspaceRestrict B S hS X V Z) p
declarations.comment: unconditional: the restriction over an open subspace `V` of the blowup of `X` in `Z` is the blowup of `V` in `Z ∩ V`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isPullback'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086D.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`,
let `U, V ⊆ X` be quasi-compact open subspaces and let `b : V' ⟶ V` be a `U ∩ V`-admissible
blowup.  Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup `f : X' ⟶ X` whose restriction to `V` is `V'`,
the restriction being recorded as a cartesian square.

The extension of the centre is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_closedSubspace_extension_disjoint`: the centre `W ⊆ V` of `b`,
together with the empty closed subspace on `U`, extends to a finitely presented `Z ⊆ X` whose
points avoid those of `U` and with `Z ∩ V = W`, by the induction principle of Stacks 08GP.  The
blowup of `X` in `Z` exists by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isBlowupAlong_of_isFinitePresentation`, it is `U`-admissible,
and by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong.exists_restrictionToOpen` its restriction to `V`
is the blowup of `V` in `Z ∩ V = W`, hence isomorphic over `V` to `V'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isPullback'
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (U V : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.1.toFunctor)
    (b : V' ⟶ openSubspace B S hS X V)
    (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS (openSubspaceRestrict B S hS X V U) b) :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : X' ⟶ X), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U f ∧
      ∃ e : V' ⟶ X', IsPullback b e (openSubspaceι B S hS X V) f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_factoring
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086E, clause (a).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `U ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact open subspace and let
`b i : X i ⟶ X`, `i : ι` with `ι` finite, be `U`-admissible blowups.  There is a `U`-admissible
blowup `c : X' ⟶ X` which factors as `X' ⟶ X i ⟶ X` for every `i`.

Take for `X'` the blowup of `X` in the sum `Z i₀ + Z i₁ + ⋯` of the centres of the given
blowups, Stacks 083U; the sum of finitely many finitely presented centres disjoint from `U` is
again finitely presented (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_ι_sumClosedSubspaces`)
and disjoint from `U` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subspacePointSet_sumClosedSubspaces`), so `c` is
`U`-admissible.  The inverse image of the sum along `c` is an effective Cartier divisor, hence so
is the inverse image of each summand `Z i` by Stacks 083W, and the universal property of `b i`,
Stacks 085U, then produces the factorisation through `b i`.  For the empty family the identity of
`X` is a `U`-admissible blowup, being the blowup in the empty closed subspace.

The hypotheses beyond the source's are the construction data of Stacks 085Q for the blowup of
`X`: an étale presentation `P` of `X`, the universe choice `HasSheafify` for the quotient
presheaf, and the three `B.Contains` smallness side conditions on the relative `Proj`s, asked for
every closed subspace of `X` since the centre is built inside the proof.  None of these says
anything about blowups; they are exactly what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBlowupAlong_blowUpAlongHom'` takes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_factoring
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (hZtop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (_hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (_hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZtop X.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (_hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (Xi : ι → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hb : ∀ i, IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U (b i))
    (P : Presentation B S hS X.obj X.property)
    (hc : ∀ K : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj,
      B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj ∧
        B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj ∧
          B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal K)
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj) :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (c : X' ⟶ X), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U c ∧
      ∃ g : ∀ i, X' ⟶ Xi i, ∀ i, g i ≫ b i = c
declarations.comment: clause (a): a U-admissible blowup factoring through each member of a finite family of U-admissible blowups, with no assumed inputs beyond the Stacks 085Q construction data for X -- a presentation P, the HasSheafify universe choice, and the three B.Contains side conditions on the relative Projs, asked for EVERY closed subspace of X because the centre is the sum of the given centres and is built inside the proof, so it cannot be named in advance -- none of which occurs in the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_factoring_isAdmissibleBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086E, clause (b).**  In the situation of clause (a) the dominating `U`-admissible
blowup `c : X' ⟶ X` can be chosen so that, in addition, each factor morphism `g i : X' ⟶ X i` is
itself a `b i⁻¹(U)`-admissible blowup.

Writing the centre of `c` as `Z i + J i` — every member of the family is a summand of the sum,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_eq_sumClosedSubspaces_of_mem` — the blowup `c i` of `X i` in the
inverse image of `J i` exists by Stacks 085Q and 085U, and Stacks 085Y identifies the composite
`c i ≫ b i` with the blowup of `X` in `Z i + J i`, the input it needs being Stacks 085X for `c i`
and the exceptional divisor of `b i`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullbackDefined_of_isBlowupAlong`).  Blowups in a fixed centre are
isomorphic over the base, so `X'` is isomorphic over `X` to the source of `c i ≫ b i`, and the
factor morphism transported along that isomorphism is again the blowup of `X i` in the inverse
image of `J i`.  That centre is finitely presented (a base change of `J i`) and disjoint from
`b i⁻¹(U)` (the inverse image of a disjointness), so the factor morphism is
`b i⁻¹(U)`-admissible.  For the empty family the identity of `X` is the blowup in the empty
closed subspace and there is nothing to factor.

The hypotheses beyond the source's are the construction data of Stacks 085Q, now also for each
`X i` because the second blowup of the tower is formed there: étale presentations `P` of `X` and
`Pi i` of `X i`, the universe choice `HasSheafify`, and the `B.Contains` smallness side
conditions on the relative `Proj`s.  None of them occurs in the conclusion, and none says
anything about blowups.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_factoring_isAdmissibleBlowup
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (hZtop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (_hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (_hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZtop X.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (_hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (Xi : ι → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hb : ∀ i, IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U (b i))
    (P : Presentation B S hS X.obj X.property)
    (hc : ∀ K : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.obj,
      B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj ∧
        B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj ∧
          B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal K)
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) P).relativeProj)
    (Pi : ∀ i, Presentation B S hS (Xi i).obj (Xi i).property)
    (hci : ∀ (i : ι) (K : ClosedSubspaces B S hS (Xi i).obj),
      B.Contains (reesChartSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) (Pi i)).relativeProj ∧
        B.Contains (reesRelationSituation (centreIdeal K)
          (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) (Pi i)).relativeProj ∧
          B.Contains (reesDoubleSituation (centreIdeal K)
            (isCartesianOnAffineCharts_centreIdeal K) (Pi i)).relativeProj) :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (c : X' ⟶ X), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U c ∧
      ∃ g : ∀ i, X' ⟶ Xi i, (∀ i, g i ≫ b i = c) ∧
        ∀ i, IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS
          ⟨U.1.preimage (b i).hom,
            isOpenSubspace_preimage B S hS (b i).hom U.1 X.2 (Xi i).2 U.2⟩ (g i)
declarations.comment: clause (b): the factor morphisms of the dominating blowup are themselves admissible blowups, with no assumed inputs beyond the Stacks 085Q construction data for X and for the X i -- presentations P and Pi, the HasSheafify universe choice, and the B.Contains side conditions on the relative Projs, asked for EVERY closed subspace of X and of each X i because the centres are built inside the proof and cannot be named in advance -- none of which occurs in the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_openSubspace_decomposition'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086F.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S` and let `U, V ⊆ X` be quasi-compact open subspaces with disjoint sets
of points.  Then there is a `U ∪ V`-admissible blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` such that `X'` is the
disjoint union of two open subspaces `X' = X'₁ ⊔ X'₂` with `b⁻¹(U) ⊆ X'₁` and
`b⁻¹(V) ⊆ X'₂`.

"`X'` is the disjoint union of `X'₁` and `X'₂`" is recorded as follows: the two
are open and closed subspaces with complementary sets of points, whose join sheafifies to `X'`
and whose meet is the sheafification of the bottom subfunctor.

Two finitely presented closed subspaces `Z₁, Z₂` with `|Z₁| ∩ |U| = ∅`, `|Z₂| ∩ |V| = ∅` and
`|Z₁| ∪ |Z₂| = |X|` are produced by two applications of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_closedSubspace_disjoint_superset`, the second to `V` and the
quasi-compact open complement of `Z₁`; the blowup in `Z₁ ∩ Z₂` is then the one sought, by
`exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_openSubspace_decomposition_of_closedSubspaces`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_openSubspace_decomposition'
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (U V : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.1.toFunctor)
    (hUV : Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 V.1)) :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : X' ⟶ X) (X'₁ X'₂ : OpenSubspaces B S hS X'.1),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS (openSubspaceUnion B S hS X U V) b ∧
        IsClosedSubspace B S hS X'₁.1 ∧ IsClosedSubspace B S hS X'₂.1 ∧
          Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X'.1 X'₁.1)
            (subspacePointSet B S hS X'.1 X'₂.1) ∧
            subspacePointSet B S hS X'.1 X'₁.1 ∪ subspacePointSet B S hS X'.1 X'₂.1
                = Set.univ ∧
              (X'₁.1 ⊔ X'₂.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) = ⊤ ∧
                X'₁.1 ⊓ X'₂.1
                    = (⊥ : Subfunctor X'.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
                  U.1.preimage b.hom ≤ X'₁.1 ∧ V.1.preimage b.hom ≤ X'₂.1

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_affine_scheme_punctured_without_quasiCompact_dense_open
declarations.doc:
There is an affine scheme with a closed point such that its punctured complement contains no
quasi-compact dense open subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_scheme_punctured_without_quasiCompact_dense_open :
    ∃ (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine S) (s : S),
      IsClosed ({s} : Set S) ∧
        ¬ ∃ U : Set {x : S // x ≠ s}, IsOpen U ∧ IsCompact U ∧ Dense U
declarations.comment: punctured_affine

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_affineOpen_without_disjoint_quasiCompact_dense_union
declarations.doc:
In some affine scheme, an affine open has no disjoint quasi-compact open whose union with it
is dense.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_without_disjoint_quasiCompact_dense_union :
    ∃ (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine S) (U : S.Opens),
      IsAffineOpen U ∧
        ¬ ∃ V : S.Opens, IsCompact V.1 ∧ (U ⊓ V = ⊥) ∧ Dense (U.1 ∪ V.1)
declarations.comment: disjoint_dense_union

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_qcqs_without_separated_quasiCompact_dense_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086I.** There is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with no separated
quasi-compact dense open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_qcqs_without_separated_quasiCompact_dense_open :
    ∃ X : Scheme.{u}, CompactSpace X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧
      ¬ ∃ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set X) ∧
        Scheme.IsSeparated V

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.SurjectionCoequalizer.coequalizer_of_surjection
declarations.doc:
A surjection `φ : F ⟶ G` of sheaves of sets on a site exhibits `G` as the coequalizer of
the two projections from the fiber product `F ×_G F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coequalizer_of_surjection
    {F G : Sheaf J (Type max v u)} (φ : F ⟶ G) (hφ : IsSurjectiveSheafType J φ) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (coequalizerCofork J φ))

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.comp_eq_zero_of_degreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
Let `S : 0 → A → B → C → 0` be a termwise split exact sequence of complexes in a preadditive
category `𝒜`, with a splitting `σ i` in each degree. If `b : K ⟶ B` and `b' : B ⟶ L` are
morphisms of the homotopy category `K(𝒜)` with `b ≫ (B → C) = 0` and `(A → B) ≫ b' = 0`, then
`b' ∘ b = 0` in `K(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem comp_eq_zero_of_degreewiseSplit
    {S : ShortComplex (HomologicalComplex 𝒜 c)}
    (σ : ∀ i, (S.map (HomologicalComplex.eval 𝒜 c i)).Splitting)
    {K L : HomotopyCategory 𝒜 c}
    (b : K ⟶ (quotient 𝒜 c).obj S.X₂) (b' : (quotient 𝒜 c).obj S.X₂ ⟶ L)
    (hb : b ≫ (quotient 𝒜 c).map S.g = 0) (hb' : (quotient 𝒜 c).map S.f ≫ b' = 0) :
    b ≫ b' = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_directed_colimit_finitePresentation_with_epi_maps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086M.** A finite type quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme is a directed colimit of finitely presented modules with surjective
transition maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_colimit_finitePresentation_with_epi_maps
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] [M.IsFiniteType] :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder ι) (_ : Nonempty ι) (_ : IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·))
      (F : ι ⥤ X.Modules) (_e : colimit F ≅ M),
      (∀ i, (F.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
        ∀ ⦃i j : ι⦄ (h : i ≤ j), Epi (F.map (homOfLE h))

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteAlgebraLimitPresentation.exists_isColimit_finite_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086N.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, a finite
quasi-coherent algebra is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent
algebras whose transition maps are surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isColimit_finite_finitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : AlgebraSheaf X) (hAqc : A.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hAfin : A.IsFinite) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (F : I ⥤ AlgebraSheaf X) (t : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A)
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A t)),
      (∀ i, (F.obj i).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (F.obj i).IsFinite ∧
        (F.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
        ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), AlgebraSheaf.Hom.IsSurjective (F.map (homOfLE h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallDescentSituation
declarations.doc:
**Situation 086P.** A directed inverse system `(S_i)_{i ∈ I}` of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, indexed by a directed *set* `I`,
together with its limit `S = lim S_i`, the projections `f_i : S ⟶ S_i`, and a chosen element
`0 ∈ I`.

The source's directed set is a set, which here means that the index preorder is `u`-small,
`u` being the universe of the schemes: the field `small`. For such an index the limit of
Stacks 01YX, glued from the affine-locally computed limits, is the categorical limit in
`Scheme.{u}`, and the chosen limit cone of the underlying
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation` records it with its projections. Without the bound the
categorical limit in `Scheme.{u}` of a large system need not be that scheme; see
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/SmallnessNecessary/Basic.lean`. Nonemptiness of `I` is
witnessed by the chosen element `base`.
declarations.statement:
structure SmallDescentSituation (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    extends DescentSituation.{v, u} I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086Q.** In a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, if the limit is separated then every
sufficiently late stage is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isSeparated
    {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (d : DescentSituation.{v, u} I)
    [d.limitCone.pt.IsSeparated] :
    ∃ i₀ : I, ∀ i : I, i₀ ≤ i → (d.system.obj (Opposite.op i)).IsSeparated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_antitone_opens_iff_fiber_degree_ge
declarations.doc:
A flat, locally finitely presented, separated and locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes has
a decreasing sequence of open subschemes of its target through which a field-valued point factors
exactly when the corresponding fibre has degree at least the index; a fibre which is not finite
counts as having infinite degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_antitone_opens_iff_fiber_degree_ge {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] :
    ∃ U : ℕ → S.Opens,
      U 0 = ⊤ ∧ Antitone U ∧
        ∀ (d : ℕ) (k : Type u) [Field k] (g : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
          (∃ h : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (U d).toScheme, h ≫ (U d).ι = g) ↔
            (¬ IsFinite (pullback.fst g f) ∨
              ∃ r : ℕ, d ≤ r ∧ IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (pullback.fst g f) r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_overHomOfPushforwardAlgebraIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086S.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `P` be an algebraic space affine over `X`, and let `e : P_* 𝒪_P ≅ f_* 𝒪_Y` identify its
direct-image algebra with that of `f`, so that `P` is the relative spectrum
`\underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)`.  Then `f` is quasi-affine if and only if the canonical morphism
`Y ⟶ P` over `X` of Stacks 081X attached to `e` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_overHomOfPushforwardAlgebraIso
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (P : AffineOver B S hS X)
    (e : pushforwardAlgebra B S hS P.obj ≅ pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom ↔
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS (overHomOfPushforwardAlgebraIso B S hS e).left.hom
declarations.comment: for every algebraic space P affine over X with an identification e of its direct-image algebra with f_* O_Y, i.e. every relative spectrum of f_* O_Y: a quasi-compact f is quasi-affine iff the canonical morphism Y ⟶ P over X of 081X attached to e is an open immersion; quasi-separatedness of f is not needed once P and e are given

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_toDirectImageSpec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086S, in the corrected (bounded) form.**  A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism
`f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` is quasi-affine if and only if its canonical
factorization `Y ⟶ \underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 081X is an open immersion.

The relative spectrum is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.directImageSpec`, Stacks 081W in its corrected
form: the relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent algebra whose sections over every chart number
fewer than the cutoff of the site.  The unbounded form of 081V that the source's
`\underline{Spec}_X` presupposes is refuted in this development by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart`.
The size condition on `f_* 𝒪_Y` is proved, not assumed
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionsBelowCutoff_pushforwardAlgebra`), so the hypotheses are exactly
those of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_toDirectImageSpec {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom ↔
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS (toDirectImageSpec B S hS f hfqc hfqs).left.hom
declarations.comment: corrected (bounded) form: Spec_X(f_* O_Y) is directImageSpec f, the relative spectrum of 081W in its bounded form (the unbounded 081V is refuted by not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart), whose size condition on f_* O_Y is proved; the morphism is toDirectImageSpec f, the canonical factorization of 081X; hypotheses exactly f quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isOpenImmersion_qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` whose
canonical morphism `Y ⟶ \underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)` is an open immersion is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_of_isOpenImmersion_qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hoi : IsOpenImmersion B S hS
      (qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap B S hS E C f hfqc hfqs
        fun hqc hqs => isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_qcqs B S hS f hqc hqs).left.hom) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: proves only: the factorization is an open immersion implies f is quasi-affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_affineOver
declarations.doc:
Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `P` be an
algebraic space affine over `X` by `p`, and let `g : Y ⟶ P` be a morphism over `X` whose map on
direct-image algebras `p_* 𝒪_P ⟶ f_* 𝒪_Y` is an isomorphism. Then `f` is quasi-affine if and only
if `g` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isOpenImmersion_affineOver {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (P : AffineOver B S hS X) (g : Over.mk f ⟶ P.obj)
    (hring : IsIso (pushforwardRingMap B S hS g)) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom ↔ IsOpenImmersion B S hS g.left.hom
declarations.comment: both directions, for every P affine over X by p and every g : Y ⟶ P over X whose map on direct-image algebras p_* O_P ⟶ f_* O_Y is an isomorphism: a quasi-compact f is quasi-affine iff g is an open immersion; this is the general form, and the canonical morphism of 081X is one such g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isOpenImmersion_qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap_unconditional
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` whose
canonical morphism `Y ⟶ \underline{Spec}_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 081X is an open immersion is
quasi-affine.

The hypothesis `E` is an inhabitant of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence`,
which `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart`
proves uninhabited, so the statement is vacuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_of_isOpenImmersion_qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap_unconditional
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hoi : IsOpenImmersion B S hS
      (qcqsDirectImageFactorizationMap_unconditional B S hS E C f hfqc hfqs).left.hom) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: proves only: the factorization is an open immersion implies f is quasi-affine — and presupposes AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence, which this development proves uninhabited (not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart), so the statement is vacuous; the non-vacuous form is isQuasiAffineHom_of_isOpenImmersion_boundedRelativeSpecDirectImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_antitone_isOpenSubspace_iff_fibre_degree_ge
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `f : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X` be a morphism
from a scheme which is flat, locally of finite presentation, separated and locally quasi-finite.
Then there is a descending chain of open subspaces
`X = X₀ ⊇ X₁ ⊇ X₂ ⊇ …`
such that a field-valued point of `X` factors through `Xᵈ` exactly when the fibre of `f`
above it has degree at least `d`; a fibre which is not finite counts as having infinite
degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_antitone_isOpenSubspace_iff_fibre_degree_ge
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {W : BigFppfOver B S hS} (f : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hlqf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    ∃ Y : ℕ → Subfunctor X,
      Y 0 = ⊤ ∧ Antitone Y ∧ (∀ d, IsOpenSubspace B S hS (Y d)) ∧
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X),
        (∃ g : yoneda.obj p.siteObject ⟶ (Y d).toFunctor,
            g ≫ (Y d).ι = yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) ↔
          (¬ (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.{u})
                (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf
                (pullback.fst (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) f) ∨
            ∃ r : ℕ, d ≤ r ∧
              (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} r)
                (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf
                (pullback.fst (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086U (David Rydh).** A decent algebraic space over a scheme has a dense open
subspace which is a scheme: its schematic locus of Stacks 03JH is a representable open subspace
whose set of points is dense.

The reduction to the local statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_nonempty_of_isDecentSpace` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isAlgebraicSpace`,
which is Stacks 03JH together with the reduction of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/DenseSchematicLocus.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isDecentSpace
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor X, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isHomeomorph_pointsLimitComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086V.** Let `D` be a directed inverse system of decent algebraic spaces over `S`
with affine transition morphisms, indexed by a category small enough for the site, so that
`limit D` is an algebraic space by Stacks 07SF. Then `|limit D| = lim |D i|` as topological
spaces: the canonical map `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsLimitComparison` from the points of
the limit to the inverse limit of the point spaces of the stages is a homeomorphism.

It is bijective by Stacks 0CUJ, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_point_limit`, which is
where decency is used, and it is inducing because the point topology of the limit is the
inverse-limit topology, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology_limit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomeomorph_pointsLimitComparison (hSize : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hHomSize : ∀ i j : I, #(i ⟶ j) < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f))
    (hDecent : ∀ i, IsDecentSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) :
    IsHomeomorph (pointsLimitComparison B S hS D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology_limit
declarations.doc:
The point topology of the limit of a cofiltered inverse system of algebraic spaces over `S`
with affine transition morphisms, indexed by a small enough category, is the infimum of the
topologies induced by the limit projections on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointTopology_limit (hSize : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hHomSize : ∀ i j : I, #(i ⟶ j) < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f)) :
    pointTopology B S hS (limit D) =
      ⨅ i : I, TopologicalSpace.induced (pointsMap B S hS (limit D) (limit.π D i))
        (pointTopology B S hS (D.obj i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology_limit_of_isSiteSmall
declarations.doc:
The point topology of the limit of a cofiltered inverse system of algebraic spaces over `S`
with affine transition morphisms, indexed by a site-small category, is the infimum of the
topologies induced by the limit projections on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointTopology_limit_of_isSiteSmall (hb : IsSiteSmall B S hS D)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f)) :
    pointTopology B S hS (limit D) =
      ⨅ i : I, TopologicalSpace.induced (pointsMap B S hS (limit D) (limit.π D i))
        (pointTopology B S hS (D.obj i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_points_limit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086W.** The inverse limit of a cofiltered inverse system of nonempty
quasi-compact algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms has a point, provided
the index category is small enough for the site: its object type and all of its morphism types
have cardinality below the cofinality of the site's size cutoff.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_points_limit (hSize : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hHomSize : ∀ i j : I, #(i ⟶ j) < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f))
    (hCompact : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hNonempty : ∀ i, Nonempty (points B S hS (D.obj i))) :
    Nonempty (points B S hS (limit D))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isSeparated_system_app_of_isSiteSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086X.** Let `Y` be a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `X = lim X_i`
be a directed limit, over `Y` and with affine transition morphisms, of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S`, as in the standing situation of Stacks 084R. If
`X ⟶ Y` is separated then `X_i ⟶ Y` is separated for all `i` large enough.

Fix the distinguished stage `0` of the system and choose an affine étale surjective chart
`U ⟶ X_0`, which exists because `X_0` is quasi-compact, and let `u : U ⟶ Y` be its composite
with the structure morphism. Base changing the whole situation along `u` is again a situation of
Stacks 084R — the stages stay quasi-compact because `U` is quasi-compact and `Y` is
quasi-separated — whose limit `X ×_Y U` is separated over the affine scheme `U`, hence a
separated algebraic space. So some stage `X_i ×_Y U` is separated by Stacks 084T, that is,
`X_i ×_Y U ⟶ U` is separated. Affineness of the transition morphism `X_i ⟶ X_0` turns the chart
`U ⟶ X_0` into a chart `U_i = U ×_{X_0} X_i ⟶ X_i` of that stage, again surjective and étale and
with `U_i ⟶ X_i ⟶ Y` factoring through `u`; separatedness of `X_i ⟶ Y` therefore descends from
that of `X_i ×_Y U ⟶ U`. Finally the transition morphisms are affine, hence separated, so
`X_k ⟶ Y` is separated for every `k ≥ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentSituation.exists_isSeparated_system_app_of_isSiteSmall [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I) (hb : Space.IsSiteSmall B S hS D.system)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y)
    (t : D.system ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y) (f : D.limitCone.pt ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ j, D.limitCone.π.app j ≫ t.app j = f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ∃ i, D.base ≤ i ∧ ∀ k, i ≤ k → IsSeparated B S hS (t.app (op k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isSeparated_system_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086X.** Let `Y` be a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `X = lim X_i`
be a directed limit, over `Y` and with affine transition morphisms, of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S`, as in the standing situation of Stacks 084R. If
`X ⟶ Y` is separated then `X_i ⟶ Y` is separated for all `i` large enough.

Fix the distinguished stage `0` of the system and choose an affine étale surjective chart
`U ⟶ X_0`, which exists because `X_0` is quasi-compact, and let `u : U ⟶ Y` be its composite
with the structure morphism. Base changing the whole situation along `u` is again a situation of
Stacks 084R — the stages stay quasi-compact because `U` is quasi-compact and `Y` is
quasi-separated — whose limit `X ×_Y U` is separated over the affine scheme `U`, hence a
separated algebraic space. So some stage `X_i ×_Y U` is separated by Stacks 084T, that is,
`X_i ×_Y U ⟶ U` is separated. Affineness of the transition morphism `X_i ⟶ X_0` turns the chart
`U ⟶ X_0` into a chart `U_i = U ×_{X_0} X_i ⟶ X_i` of that stage, again surjective and étale and
with `U_i ⟶ X_i ⟶ Y` factoring through `u`; separatedness of `X_i ⟶ Y` therefore descends from
that of `X_i ×_Y U ⟶ U`. Finally the transition morphisms are affine, hence separated, so

declarations.statement:
theorem DescentSituation.exists_isSeparated_system_app [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I) (hI : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y)
    (t : D.system ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y) (f : D.limitCone.pt ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ j, D.limitCone.π.app j ≫ t.app j = f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ∃ i, D.base ≤ i ∧ ∀ k, i ≤ k → IsSeparated B S hS (t.app (op k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 086Y.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over a
scheme `S` and let `M` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then `M` is the colimit of
a system of `𝒪_X`-modules of finite presentation indexed by a directed poset, all of whose
transition maps are surjective.

The source writes `ℱ = lim ℱ_i`, but its proof produces `colim 𝒢_i/𝒦_a`; the conclusion is a
colimit, as in the scheme-level counterpart Stacks 086M.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_epi
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [M.IsFiniteTypeOnSite] :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj M)
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk M φ)),
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).IsFinitePresentationOnSite) ∧
        ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j), Epi (D.map (homOfLE h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective_of_elementaryData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086Z, over elementary data about `ℬ` and the family of ideals.**  Same
conclusion as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective`: `A` is
the colimit of a system of quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebras over a nonempty directed preorder, every
member finite and of finite presentation and every transition map locally surjective.

The carried input no longer mentions the quotients `ℬ/ℐ_j` except at the single index where
integrality is asked.  It asks instead: `ℬ` quasi-coherent and of finite presentation, each `ℐ_j`
quasi-coherent as an `𝒪_Y`-module with finitely generated ideal of sections over each affine
étale chart, `f` locally surjective, and every section of `ℬ` which `f` kills locally a section
of some `ℐ_j`.  Those are the data of the first three steps of the source's proof and nothing
more.

See the section documentation above: this is a formally weaker statement than the theorem it
calls, deliberately, and it does not make Stacks 086Z unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective_of_elementaryData
    (A : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj)
    (hA : A.obj.IsFinite)
    (hdata :
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj →
      A.obj.IsFinite →
        ∃ (ℬ : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (f : ℬ ⟶ A.obj) (J : Type u)
          (inst : SmallCategory J),
          let _ := inst
          ∃ (_ : IsFiltered J) (ι : J → ℬ.IdealSheaf)
            (_ : ∀ j j' : J, (j ⟶ j') → ι j ≤ ι j'),
            (∀ (j : J) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)ᵒᵖ) (a : ℬ.right.obj.obj U),
                a ∈ (ι j).obj U → (f.right.hom.app U).hom a = 0) ∧
              ℬ.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ℬ.IsFinitePresentation ∧
              (∀ j, (AlgebraSheaf.idealModule ℬ (ι j)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
              (∀ (j : J) (W : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1),
                IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
                  (Stacks.Sites.sectionIdeal (ι j) (op W)).FG) ∧
              Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) f.right.hom ∧
              (∀ (U : (SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)ᵒᵖ) (a : ℬ.right.obj.obj U),
                  (f.right.hom.app U).hom a = 0 →
                    Stacks.Sites.memSieve (O := ℬ.right) ι a ∈
                      SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1 U.unop) ∧
              ∃ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsIntegral) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ)) ∧
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (D.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.obj) (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom.right.hom
declarations.comment: the same conclusion as AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective — the directedness of the index, the finiteness and the finite presentation of every stage, the surjectivity of every transition map and the colimit — but over an ELEMENTARY carried input in place of that theorem's hsource. THIS REGISTRATION IS FORMALLY WEAKER THAN THAT ONE AND DOES NOT REPLACE IT: the carried input here is strictly stronger, so the unrestricted reading of the tag remains the one carried there. What this registration claims is that the three non-elementary conjuncts of hsource — quasi-coherence of every quotient B/I_j, finite presentation of every quotient B/I_j, and the colimit property of the constructed cocone — are each DERIVABLE, and it derives them: quasi-coherence from quasi-coherence of B and of I_j by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_idealQuotient, finite presentation from finite presentation of B and finite generation of the ideal of sections I_j(W) over each affine etale chart by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.isFinitePresentation_idealQuotient, and the colimit from local surjectivity of f together with local membership in the family of every section f kills by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_idealQuotientQcohCocone_of_locally. Every conjunct that remains carried is a condition on sections of B, of the I_j and of A over the objects of the small etale site, or on a single affine etale chart. STILL CARRIED, and NOT dischargeable in this tree today: (i) quasi-coherence of AlgebraicGeometry.Space.symmetricAlgebraSheaf for a quasi-coherent module, which is the B of the source and is recorded as absent in StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.SymmetricAlgebraSheafMap (Stacks 01CK/01CL hold for a ringed space, as Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_symmetricAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent, but not for the small etale site of an algebraic space); (ii) finite presentation of that same Sym(F), the sections of which over a chart are only LOCALLY finite sums of homogeneous ones; (iii) integrality at one index, the fourth step of the source. Note also that Stacks 086Y, AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_epi_of_isFiniteType, is itself proved only over three carried inputs h07V9, hstage and hcoker, so Stacks 086Z is NOT unconditional in this tree by this route or any other presently available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086Z.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `𝒜` be a finite quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebra.
Then `𝒜` is the colimit of a system of quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebras indexed by a nonempty
directed preorder, every member of which is finite and of finite presentation, and every
transition map of which is surjective (locally surjective as a morphism of sheaves on the small
étale site, which for quasi-coherent algebras is surjectivity on the sections over every affine
étale chart).

The proof is the source's.  Stacks 086Y gives a quasi-coherent module `𝒢` of finite presentation
with an epimorphism `𝒢 ⟶ 𝒜`; then
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective_of_epi`
forms `Sym(𝒢)`, writes the kernel of `Sym(𝒢) ⟶ 𝒜` as the union of its finite type
quasi-coherent submodules `ℰ` (Stacks 0829), takes the quotients `Sym(𝒢)/(ℰ)`, shows they are
finite for `ℰ` large, and reindexes by a directed preorder.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective_of_isFinite
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (A : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj)
    (hA : A.obj.IsFinite) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ)) ∧
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (D.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.obj) (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom.right.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 086Z.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `A` be a finite quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebra.
Then `A` is the colimit of a system of quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-algebras indexed by a nonempty
directed preorder, every member of which is finite and of finite presentation, and every
transition map of which is surjective.

All four assertions of the source are in the conclusion: the index is a nonempty preorder which
is directed, every stage is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.IsFinite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.IsFinitePresentation`, every transition map is locally
surjective, and the cocone with vertex `A` is colimiting.  Quasi-coherence of the stages is
structural, the diagram taking values in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentAlgebra`.
