The quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `Y` and the finiteness of `A` are used by being
handed to `hsource`, which is the *data* of the third step of the source's proof — one algebra
sheaf and a filtered family of sheaves of ideals of it — together with integrality at a single
index, **for this `Y` and this `A` and no other**.  The system itself is built from that data by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientDiagram` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientQcohCocone`; see the module documentation for what `hsource`
stands for and for what is proved on top of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_isFinite_isFinitePresentation_locallySurjective
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (A : QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj)
    (hA : A.obj.IsFinite)
    (hsource :
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.obj →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.obj →
      A.obj.IsFinite →
        ∃ (ℬ : AlgebraSheaf.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (f : ℬ ⟶ A.obj) (J : Type u)
          (inst : SmallCategory J),
          let _ := inst
          ∃ (_ : IsFiltered J) (ι : J → ℬ.IdealSheaf)
            (hι : ∀ j j' : J, (j ⟶ j') → ι j ≤ ι j')
            (hkill : ∀ (j : J) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)ᵒᵖ) (a : ℬ.right.obj.obj U),
              a ∈ (ι j).obj U → (f.right.hom.app U).hom a = 0)
            (hqcoh : ∀ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsQuasicoherent),
            (∀ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
            (∃ j, (ℬ.idealQuotient (ι j)).IsIntegral) ∧
            Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A
              (idealQuotientQcohCocone ℬ ι hι A f hkill hqcoh)))) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentAlgebra B S hS Y) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ)) ∧
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (D.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.obj) (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom.right.hom
declarations.comment: the directedness of the index, the finiteness of every stage, the finite presentation of every stage and the surjectivity of every transition map, over the carried input hsource. hsource is the DATA the first three steps of the source's proof produce, not the system they build: one algebra sheaf B (in the source Sym(F) for the finitely presented module F of Stacks 086Y), a map B to the algebra, and a FILTERED family of sheaves of ideals of B killed by that map and growing along the index (in the source the finite type submodules of the kernel ideal, Stacks 0829), plus quasi-coherence and finite presentation of each quotient B/I_j, the colimit property of the constructed cocone, and integrality — not finiteness — at ONE index, which is the single-index half of the fourth step. hsource is asked only AT THE Y AND THE A OF THE STATEMENT, not for every quasi-compact quasi-separated space and every finite algebra. The MEMBERS AND THE TRANSITION MAPS OF THE SYSTEM ARE NOT CARRIED: they are AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientDiagram and AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotientQcohCocone, built from the quotient of an algebra sheaf on an algebraic space by a sheaf of ideals and its universal property (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.idealQuotient, idealQuotientMapOfLE, idealQuotientLift), and SURJECTIVITY OF EVERY TRANSITION MAP IS PROVED, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_idealQuotientQcohDiagram_map, so hsource asserts no surjectivity at all. Of the three inputs that leave Stacks 082A partial in AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_algebra_of_idealQuotients, ALL THREE ARE NOW DISCHARGEABLE FROM ELEMENTARY DATA and none may be SUBSTITUTED for: in each case that data is not among the remaining conjuncts of hsource, so replacing a conjunct by it would make hsource STRONGER and this theorem weaker. (1) B and the map are now CONSTRUCTIBLE at the algebraic space level: functoriality of the symmetric algebra is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.symmetricAlgebraSheafMap in Spaces/SymmetricAlgebraSheafMap.lean and the ungraded universal property producing a morphism of algebra sheaves Sym(F) to A out of a morphism of modules F to A is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SymAlgSheaf.algebraLift in Spaces/SymmetricAlgebraSheafUngradedLift.lean, so with Stacks 086Y one may take B = Sym(F) and the map = algebraLift; quasi-coherence of Sym(F) is still unproved at this level but hsource asks NO quasi-coherence of B, so it is not needed here. (2) The colimit property of the constructed cocone is now EQUIVALENT, at the level of all algebra sheaves, to two elementary local conditions — local surjectivity of the map and local membership of every section it kills in some member of the family — by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_idealQuotientAlgCocone_iff_locally in Spaces/Limits/AlgebraSheafIdealQuotientColimit.lean, and AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_isColimit_idealQuotientQcohCocone_of_locally supplies the quasi-coherent form that hsource asks for from those two conditions, with no affine-chart verification and no cohomology. It is NOT substituted into hsource: the quasi-coherent algebras are a full subcategory, whose inclusion reflects but need not preserve colimits, so at that level the implication runs one way only and substituting the local conditions would make this hypothesis STRONGER and the theorem weaker. (3) Quasi-coherence and finite presentation of a sheafified quotient over an affine etale chart — the identification of the sections of B/I_j over such a chart with the objectwise quotient — is NOW PROVED, in Spaces/Limits/AlgebraSheafIdealQuotientCokernel.lean. The step that was missing, the identification of the underlying module of B/I_j with the COKERNEL of the inclusion of I_j, is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleIdealQuotientCokernelIso, an epi-mono factorisation in the balanced category of O_Y-modules whose exactness input is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.kerIdeal_toIdealQuotient (the quotient morphism kills exactly the sections of the ideal, Spaces/Limits/AlgebraSheafIdealQuotientKernel.lean) and whose epimorphism input is local surjectivity of the quotient morphism. From it: quasi-coherence of B/I_j is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_idealQuotient, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_cokernel_unconditional, GIVEN quasi-coherence of B and of I_j; the sections over an affine chart W are B(W)/I_j(W), by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.bijective_idealQuotientSectionsLift and idealQuotientSectionsRingEquiv, whose surjectivity half is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_val_app_of_epi_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite, the restated form of Descent 03DW, unconditional in this tree by faithfully flat descent with no Cech cohomology; and finite presentation of B/I_j is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AlgebraSheaf.isFinitePresentation_idealQuotient, GIVEN finite presentation of B and finite generation of the ideal of sections I_j(W) over every affine chart, which is where the source's finite generation of the ideals enters and is why no finiteness is asked of them here. The conjunct is nevertheless NOT removed from hsource: hsource asks no quasi-coherence of B, no quasi-coherence of the I_j, no finiteness of them and no finite presentation of B, and none of those follow from its remaining conjuncts — finite presentation of a structure-algebra map on every affine chart says nothing about the restriction maps being base changes, so it does not imply quasi-coherence — so dropping the conjunct would require ADDING FOUR NEW ONES (quasi-coherence of B, quasi-coherence of each I_j, finite presentation of B, and finite generation of each I_j(W)), which makes hsource STRONGER and this theorem weaker. What has changed is that a caller holding those four can now produce the conjunct with no further mathematics. Stacks 086Y and Stacks 0829 are both proved here (as AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_isFinitePresentation_epi_of_isFiniteType and as AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone_of_07V9 with AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject). hsource asserts no finiteness of any stage and no directedness; finiteness of every stage, directedness, surjectivity of every transition map and survival of the colimit are proved. The source argues on one affine étale chart while this tree's finiteness predicates quantify over all of them, so the chart-uniformity of the carried integrality is carried too

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_directed_limit_isFinitePresentation_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0870.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S`.  If `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then `X` is a directed limit
`X = lim X_i` of algebraic spaces `X_i` affine over `Y` and of finite presentation over `Y`.

The system is indexed by the opposite of a nonempty directed preorder, so it is an inverse
system; `t` is the family of structure morphisms `X_i ⟶ Y`, which are affine and of finite
presentation, `p` is the family of projections `X ⟶ X_i`, each of which composes with the
structure morphism to `f`, and `X` is the limit of the underlying presheaves, that is, of the
fppf sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_limit_isFinitePresentation_of_isAffineHom
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
      (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y) (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
      (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p)),
      (∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsAffineHom B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
            ∀ i, p.app i ≫ t.app i = f
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only: a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces affine and of finite presentation over Y, with X its limit and the projections compatible with f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type and quasi-affine,
whose target is the functor of points of a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme of the site, is a
closed immersion into an algebraic space of finite presentation over that target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isQuasiAffineHom
    {Z : BigFppfOver B S hS} {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj Z)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hqa : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f)
    (hZqc : CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z))
    (hZqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)) :
    ∃ (X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f' : X' ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X' ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS f' ∧
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ∧ i ≫ f' = f
declarations.comment: for a target represented by a quasi-compact quasi-separated object of the site; a general algebraic-space target needs the unproved direction of 086S and Stacks 0870

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isQuasiAffineHom_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is locally of finite type and quasi-affine, with `Y` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated.  Then there are a morphism of finite presentation `f' : X' ⟶ Y` and a closed
immersion `i : X ⟶ X'` with `i ≫ f' = f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isQuasiAffineHom_of_qcqs
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hfqa : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f' : X' ⟶ Y) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X' ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS f' ∧
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ∧ i ≫ f' = f

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedImmersion_isFinitePresentation_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
registrations.comment:
a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, locally of finite type, with source
  and target quasi-compact and quasi-separated, is a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ X'` followed by a
  morphism of finite presentation `f' : X' ⟶ Y` with `i ≫ f' = f`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there are a separated morphism of finite presentation
`f' : X' ⟶ Y` and a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ X'` with `i ≫ f' = f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation_of_isFiniteType
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (i : X ⟶ X') (f' : X' ⟶ Y),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X' ∧ IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ∧ IsSeparated B S hS f' ∧
        IsFinitePresentation B S hS f' ∧ i ≫ f' = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinitePresentation_comp_eq_of_isQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0874.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite separated morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, with `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Then `f = π ∘ j` with `j : X ⟶ T` a quasi-compact open immersion into an algebraic space `T`
and `π : T ⟶ Y` finite and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinitePresentation_comp_eq_of_isQuasiFinite
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (j : X ⟶ T) (π : T ⟶ Y),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS j ∧ IsQuasiCompact B S hS j ∧
        IsFinite B S hS π ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS π ∧ j ≫ π = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_chartModule_of_isFlatOver_of_dense_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0876.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`
contained in a big fppf site `B` which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be an
`𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent of finite type on charts and flat over `Y`, and let `V ⊆ Y`
be an open subspace whose inclusion is quasi-compact and which is scheme-theoretically dense in
the sense of Tag 0834.  If `F` restricted to `f⁻¹V` is of finite presentation on charts, then on
every commuting square of étale scheme charts the restriction of `F` to the chart of `X` is of
finite presentation.

Hypothesis (3) of the source is exactly the two hypotheses `hVqc` and `hVdense` here.  They give
the chartwise conditions of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_chartModule_of_isFlatOver_of_dense_open_charts` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRetrocompactOnCharts_of_isQuasiCompact` (Stacks 03HD) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDenseOnCharts_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense`
(Stacks 0836), and on one commuting square of charts the statement is then Stacks 081N for the
vertical morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_chartModule_of_isFlatOver_of_dense_open
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {f : X ⟶ Y} (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F) (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS hX f F)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι)
    (hVdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS V)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOverOpenOnCharts B S hS hX f F V hV)
    (d : ChartDiagram B S hS X Y f) :
    (chartModule B S hS hX F d.U).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: hypotheses (1) and (2) and the conclusion are read on the etale scheme charts: they are the corresponding properties of the restriction of the module to the charts, as for Space.IsFlatOver of Tag 05VV. Hypothesis (4) is read on the open subscheme that V cuts out in each chart of the target, which by Space.preimage_chartOpenOfOpenSubspace is the chart-level inverse image of V. The conclusion is stated on a commuting square of charts of f rather than on an arbitrary chart of the source, since not every chart of the source is the source of such a square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_fromPreimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0877.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`
contained in a big fppf site `B` which is locally of finite type and flat, and let `V ⊆ Y` be an
open subspace whose inclusion is quasi-compact and which is scheme-theoretically dense in the
sense of Tag 0834.  If the restriction `f⁻¹V ⟶ V` of `f` is locally of finite presentation, then
`f` is locally of finite presentation.

Local finite presentation is the every-étale-chart condition of Tag 03MJ, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyOfFinitePresentation_chartDiagram_of_fromPreimage` for the
commuting square of charts given by the chart data.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_fromPreimage
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι)
    (hVdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS V)
    (hfV : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (V.fromPreimage f)) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeDimensionLE_of_dense_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0878.** A flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` locally of finite type has
relative dimension at most `d` if its restriction over a dense open subspace of the target does,
provided the morphism is locally of finite presentation or the open immersion is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimensionLE_of_dense_open (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Subfunctor Y)
    (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVdense : Dense (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι)))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι))
    (hfin : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ∨ IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι) :
    HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_of_isIso_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf
site `B` which is separated, locally of finite type and flat, and let `V ⊆ Y` be an open subspace
such that `f^{-1}V ⟶ V` is an isomorphism and the inclusion of `V` is quasi-compact and
scheme-theoretically dense. Then `f` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_of_isIso_pullback_snd (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Subfunctor Y)
    (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hiso : IsIso (pullback.snd f V.ι))
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι)
    (hVdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS V) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal_disjoint_pullbackIdealSubsheaf_eq_idealSmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087B.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`,
let `φ : W ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact separated étale morphism, let `U ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact
open subspace and let `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_W` be a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with
`V(𝓘) ∩ φ⁻¹(U) = ∅`.  Then there is a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓙 ⊆ 𝒪_X`
such that

1. `V(𝓙) ∩ U = ∅`, and
2. `φ⁻¹(𝓙) 𝒪_W = 𝓘 𝓘'` for some finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘' ⊆ 𝒪_W`.

The inverse-image ideal `φ⁻¹(𝓙) 𝒪_W` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackIdealSubsheaf`, which
is defined for representable morphisms; a separated étale morphism is representable by
Stacks 0418, and the statement names that proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal_disjoint_pullbackIdealSubsheaf_eq_idealSmul
    {X W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (φ : W ⟶ X) (hφqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS φ.hom) (hφsep : IsSeparated B S hS φ.hom)
    (hφet : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (U : Subfunctor X.1) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.toFunctor)
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS W)).Submodule)
    (hI : IsFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal B S hS W I)
    (hIU : Disjoint (idealZeroLocus B S hS W I)
      (subspacePointSet B S hS W.1 (U.preimage φ.hom))) :
    ∃ J : (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).Submodule,
      IsFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal B S hS X J ∧
        Disjoint (idealZeroLocus B S hS X J) (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U) ∧
        ∃ I' : (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS W)).Submodule,
          IsFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal B S hS W I' ∧
            pullbackIdealSubsheaf B S hS φ
                (relativelyRepresentable_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_isSeparated B S hS φ.hom W.2 X.2
                  (isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isEtale' B S hS hφet) hφsep) J =
              Stacks.Sites.idealSmul (O := structureSheaf B S hS W.1 W.2) I I'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFlatteningBlowup_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Flattening by blowing up for algebraic spaces.** Let `A` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `f : X ⟶ A` be locally of finite presentation with
`X` quasi-compact, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `U ⊆ A` be a
quasi-compact open subspace such that `F_U = F|_{X ×_A U}` is of finite presentation and flat
over `U`. Then there is a blowup `b : A' ⟶ A` in a finitely presented closed subspace `Z`
disjoint from `U` (a `U`-admissible blowup) such that the strict transform of `F` with respect
to `b` is an `𝒪_{X ×_A A'}`-module of finite presentation, flat over `A'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlatteningBlowup_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (hAqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS A.1)
    (hAqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal A.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS A.1) (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ A)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFft : F.IsFiniteTypeOnSite)
    (hFUfp : ((modulePullback B S hS (restrictOverι f U)).obj F).IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hFUflat : IsFlatOver B S hS (restrictOver f U).2 (restrictOverHom f U).hom
      ((modulePullback B S hS (restrictOverι f U)).obj F)) :
    ∃ (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1) (A' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : A' ⟶ A),
      IsFlatteningBlowup f F U Z b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isBlowupAlong_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087F, corrected.**  Let `f : X ⟶ A` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and
let `U ⊆ A` be an open subspace.  Assume that `A` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, that `U`
is quasi-compact, that `f` is of finite type **and separated**, and that `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` is an
isomorphism.  Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup `b : A' ⟶ A`, with centre `Z`, such that
`b⁻¹(U)` is scheme-theoretically dense in `A'` and the strict transform of `X` is an open
immersion into `A'`.

Without separatedness the statement is false; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBlowupAlong_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_unconditional
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {A X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ A)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (hAqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS A.1) (hAqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ A.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hiso : IsIso (pullback.snd f.hom U.1.ι)) :
    ∃ (A' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : A' ⟶ A) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1),
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.1.ι ∧
        Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS A.1 U.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS A.1 Z.1) ∧
          IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b ∧
            IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS (U.1.preimage b.hom) ∧
              IsOpenImmersion B S hS
                (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)).hom
declarations.comment: corrected: f separated; as published the statement is false (the affine line with doubled origin over 𝐀¹, with U = 𝐀¹ minus the origin)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_dominating_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087G.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` and let `U ⊆ Y` be an open subspace. Assume that `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
that `U` is quasi-compact, that `f` is proper and that `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` is an isomorphism. Then
there is a `U`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y` which dominates `X`, that is, there is a
factorization `Y' ⟶ X ⟶ Y` of the blowup morphism.

Being a `U`-admissible blowup is Stacks 086B, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAdmissibleBlowup`;
quasi-separatedness of `Y` is absolute quasi-separatedness; and `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` is the projection
`X ×_Y U ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_dominating_of_isProper {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f.hom U.1.ι)) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ Y), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b ∧
      ∃ g : Y' ⟶ X, g ≫ f = b

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.AxesReflection.exists_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated_without_quasiCompact_dense_open_subscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087I.** There exists a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space which
does not contain a quasi-compact dense open subscheme.

The space is the quotient of `Spec k[x, z₁, z₂, …]/(x zᵢ, zᵢ zⱼ)` by the reflection
`x ↦ -x` over the punctured line, for `k` of characteristic different from two.

The space is an algebraic space by Stacks 02WW, through Stacks 0265 and the effective descent
along the covering sieves at the monomorphisms locally of finite type that it consumes. The big
fppf site carrying it is produced inside the proof, and so is existentially quantified.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated_without_quasiCompact_dense_open_subscheme :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
      (F : (BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ F),
      Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ F ∧
      Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ F ∧
      ¬ ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ) (f : yoneda.obj V ⟶ F),
        CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ).obj V) ∧
        Space.IsOpenImmersion B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ f ∧
        Dense (Set.range (Space.pointsMap B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ (yoneda.obj V) f))
declarations.comment: a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space with no quasi-compact dense open subscheme: the quotient of a line glued to countably many axes by a reflection

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.dualNumber_diagram_commutes_up_to_homotopy
declarations.doc:
The prescribed endomorphism of the left column and the identity endomorphisms of the middle
and right columns make the two squares commute in the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualNumber_diagram_commutes_up_to_homotopy :
    ∃ (i : dualNumberLeftComplex k ⟶ dualNumberMiddleComplex k)
      (p : dualNumberMiddleComplex k ⟶ dualNumberRightComplex k)
      (a : dualNumberLeftComplex k ⟶ dualNumberLeftComplex k),
      (i.f 1 = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ 1 → i.f n = 0) ∧
      (p.f 0 = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ 0 → p.f n = 0) ∧
      (a.f 1 = ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.mulLeft (dualNumberRing k)
        (1 + (DualNumber.eps : dualNumberRing k)))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ 1 → a.f n = 0) ∧
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (DualNumberModuleCat k) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map a ≫
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient (DualNumberModuleCat k) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i =
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient (DualNumberModuleCat k) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i) ∧
      (i ≫ p = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_commRing_distinguished_triangle_trace_nonadditive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087L.** There exist a commutative ring `R`, a distinguished triangle of perfect
complexes in the homotopy category `K(R)` and an endomorphism `(a, b, c)` of this triangle with
`Tr(a) + Tr(c) ≠ Tr(b)`, the traces taken in `R` itself. The vertices are bounded complexes of
finite projective `R`-modules and `a`, `b`, `c` are presented by cochain maps; the trace in `R` is
the alternating trace evaluated by `Stacks.Trace.commutativeAdditiveCommutatorQuotientEval`, which
for a commutative ring identifies `R/[R,R]` with `R`. The witness is the dual numbers over `ℚ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_commRing_distinguished_triangle_trace_nonadditive :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (hR : CommRing R),
      letI : CommRing R := hR
      ∃ (P Q S : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
        (hP : CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.finiteProjectiveComplex R P)
        (hQ : CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.finiteProjectiveComplex R Q)
        (hS : CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.finiteProjectiveComplex R S),
        let q := HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
        ∃ (f : q.obj P ⟶ q.obj Q) (g : q.obj Q ⟶ q.obj S)
          (h : q.obj S ⟶ (q.obj P)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
          (a : P ⟶ P) (b : Q ⟶ Q) (c : S ⟶ S),
          (Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang _) ∧
          (∃ t : Triangle.mk f g h ⟶ Triangle.mk f g h,
            t.hom₁ = q.map a ∧ t.hom₂ = q.map b ∧ t.hom₃ = q.map c) ∧
          Stacks.Trace.commutativeAdditiveCommutatorQuotientEval R
              (CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.alternatingTrace R P hP a) +
            Stacks.Trace.commutativeAdditiveCommutatorQuotientEval R
              (CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.alternatingTrace R S hS c) ≠
            Stacks.Trace.commutativeAdditiveCommutatorQuotientEval R
              (CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.alternatingTrace R Q hQ b)
declarations.comment: Stacks' rings are commutative and its traces of perfect complexes lie in `R`: here `R` is a `CommRing` and the alternating traces are evaluated in `R`.

declarations.name: extendScalarsExtComparison_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Flat base change for Ext.**
For a flat ring map `f : R → R'`, an `R`-module `M`, an `R'`-module `N'`, and
each `i ≥ 0`, the comparison map `c^i` of `extendScalarsExtComparison` is an
isomorphism of abelian groups (here phrased as bijectivity of the underlying
group homomorphism).

The rings are arbitrary, in independent universes `uR` and `uS`; the modules live in
`ModuleCat.{max uS v}` for any `v`, and `R` is assumed `Small.{max uS v}`, which holds whenever
the module universe contains `R`. These are the constraints under which Mathlib's
scalar-extension adjunction relates module categories of one size and provides `Ext` with enough
projectives; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem extendScalarsExtComparison_bijective {R : Type uR} {R' : Type uS}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Small.{max uS v} R]
    (f : R →+* R') (hf : f.Flat) (M : ModuleCat.{max uS v} R) (N' : ModuleCat.{max uS v} R')
    (i : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (extendScalarsExtComparison f M N' i)

declarations.name: isomorphism_of_flat_surjective_087P
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 087P (Lemma 10.126.10).**
Under the stated hypotheses there is `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, with `φ_g : S_g → S'_g` an
isomorphism (i.e. bijective).
declarations.statement:
theorem isomorphism_of_flat_surjective_087P
    (hIq : I.map (algebraMap R S) ≤ q)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (φ : S → S'))
    (hiso : Function.Bijective (phiqBar I φ q Sq S'q))
    (hft : (algebraMap R S).FiniteType)
    (hfp : (algebraMap R S').FinitePresentation)
    (hflat : Module.Flat R S'q) :
    ∃ g : S, g ∉ q ∧ Function.Bijective (phig φ g)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.canonicalExtTensorComparison_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087Q.** The canonical Hom--tensor map is bijective for a finitely presented
source and flat tensor factor. The canonical Ext--tensor map is bijective below the
pseudo-coherence cutoff for a flat tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalExtTensorComparison_bijective [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)] :
    ∀ (M : Type v) (N : Type w) (L : Type x)
        [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
        [AddCommGroup L] [Module R L] [Module.Flat R L],
        (Module.FinitePresentation R M →
          Function.Bijective
            (TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) M N L)) ∧
        (∀ (d : ℕ), IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) M (-(d : ℤ)) →
          ∀ i < d, Function.Bijective
            (canonicalExtTensorComparison R (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w x} M))
              (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w x} N))
              (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w x} L)) i))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.baseChange_ext_bijective_of_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087R.** The canonical Ext base-change map is bijective in degree zero for finitely
presented modules, below the pseudo-coherence cutoff, and in every degree for finite modules
over a Noetherian ring.

The maps `η` and `t` are characterized on original elements by `m ↦ 1 ⊗ m` and
`n ⊗ s ↦ s ⊗ n`. The equation `c.comp β = a` and its uniqueness clause specify the canonical
comparison in every degree. The commuting square using `uliftExtLinearEquiv₀` transports `β`
in degree zero to `homBaseChangeComparison` on the original modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_ext_bijective_of_pseudoCoherent
    (R : Type uR) (S : Type uS) (M : Type uM) (N : Type uN)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{uM} R)] :
    let RM := ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max uR uS uM uN} M)
    let RN := ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max uR uS uM uN} N)
    let L := ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max uR uS uM uN} S)
    let SM := ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{max uR uS uM uN} (S ⊗[R] M))
    let SN := ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{max uR uS uM uN} (S ⊗[R] N))
    let E := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj SN
    ∃ (η : RM ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj SM)
        (t : ModuleCat.of R (RN ⊗[R] L) ⟶ E),
      (∀ m : M, η (ULift.up m) = ULift.up ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] m)) ∧
      (∀ (n : N) (s : S), t (ULift.up n ⊗ₜ[R] ULift.up s) =
        ULift.up (s ⊗ₜ[R] n)) ∧
      (∀ t' : ModuleCat.of R (RN ⊗[R] L) ⟶ E,
        (∀ (n : N) (s : S), t' (ULift.up n ⊗ₜ[R] ULift.up s) =
          ULift.up (s ⊗ₜ[R] n)) → t' = t) ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ,
        let c : Ext SM SN i →+ Ext RM E i :=
          ((Ext.mk₀ η).precomp E (zero_add i)).comp
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).mapExtAddHom SM SN i)
        let a : (Ext RM RN i) ⊗[R] S →+ Ext RM E i :=
          (((Ext.mk₀ t).postcomp RM (add_zero i)).comp
            (canonicalExtTensorComparison R RM RN L i).toAddMonoidHom).comp
              (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : Ext RM RN i →ₗ[R] Ext RM RN i)
                (ULift.moduleEquiv.symm.toLinearMap : S →ₗ[R] L)).toAddMonoidHom
        ∃ β : (Ext RM RN i) ⊗[R] S →+ Ext SM SN i,
          c.comp β = a ∧
          (∀ γ : (Ext RM RN i) ⊗[R] S →+ Ext SM SN i,
            c.comp γ = a → γ = β) ∧
          (∀ (e : Ext RM RN i) (s r : S),
            β (e ⊗ₜ[R] (r * s)) = r • β (e ⊗ₜ[R] s)) ∧
          (∀ h : i = 0, ∀ x : (Ext RM RN 0) ⊗[R] S,
            uliftExtLinearEquiv₀.{uS, max uS uM, max uS uN, uR} S (S ⊗[R] M) (S ⊗[R] N)
                ((h ▸ β) x) =
              homBaseChangeComparison R S M N
                (TensorProduct.congr (uliftExtLinearEquiv₀.{uR, uM, uN, uS} R M N)
                  (LinearEquiv.refl R S) x)) ∧
          (i = 0 → Module.FinitePresentation R M → Function.Bijective β) ∧
          (∀ d : ℕ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) M (-(d : ℤ)) →
            i < d → Function.Bijective β) ∧
          (IsNoetherianRing R → Module.Finite R M → Function.Bijective β)

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.isHQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiProjective_of_exists_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**A quasi-projective morphism to a scheme admitting an ample invertible module is
H-quasi-projective**: it admits a quasi-compact immersion into a projective space over the base.

Quasi-projectivity is finite type together with an invertible module ample relative to the
morphism, and H-quasi-projectivity is a quasi-compact immersion into `ℙⁿ_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiProjective_of_exists_isAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (h : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI := h; Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective f) : AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isHQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 087S, part (2). Over a base carrying an ample invertible module, a
quasi-projective morphism is H-quasi-projective.**

The relatively ample module of quasi-projectivity and the ample module on the base combine into an
absolutely ample module on `X` by [Stacks, Tag 0892] part (1), and [Stacks, Tag 01VS] turns that
into a quasi-compact immersion into `ℙⁿ_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiProjective (f : X ⟶ S) (M : S.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M] (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    (hf : IsQuasiProjective f) : IsHQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveMorphism_of_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 087S, part (1). Over a base carrying an ample invertible module, a
projective morphism is H-projective.**

`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isQuasiProjective_and_isProper` makes `f` quasi-projective and
proper, from [Stacks, Tag 07RL] and [Stacks, Tag 01WC]; part (2) makes it H-quasi-projective; and
clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0BCL] turns H-quasi-projective and proper into H-projective. Nothing is
assumed beyond the source's hypothesis that `M` is an ample invertible module on `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjectiveMorphism_of_isProjective
    (f : X ⟶ S) (M : S.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M]
    (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M) (hf : IsProjective f) : IsProjectiveMorphism f
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pushforwardCoh
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T], the induced functor.** Direct image along a closed immersion of
locally Noetherian schemes carries a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module to a coherent `𝒪_X`-module
annihilated by the ideal sheaf cutting out `Z`, hence induces a functor
`Coh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ {ℱ ∈ Coh(𝒪_X) | ℐℱ = 0}`.
declarations.comment: the induced functor

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pushforwardCohEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T].** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of locally Noetherian schemes
and let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals cutting out `Z`. Direct image along `i`
is an equivalence from the category of coherent `𝒪_Z`-modules to the category of coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules annihilated by `ℐ`.

The functor of this equivalence is `Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pushforwardCoh`, which composed with
the inclusion of the full subcategory *is* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforward i`, by
`pushforwardCoh_comp_ι`.
declarations.comment: the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pushforward_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T], coherence of the direct image.** The direct image of a coherent
module along a closed immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent.

Local Noetherianity of the source is not assumed: it follows from that of the target by
`isLocallyNoetherian_of_isClosedImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pushforward_of_isClosedImmersion
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (G : Z.Modules) [G.IsCoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj G).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: coherence of the direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_of_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T], essential surjectivity.** A coherent module on `X` annihilated,
section by section, by the kernel of the comorphism of a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` is the
direct image along `i` of a coherent module on `Z`.

The module on `Z` is `i^* M`: it is coherent because `Z` is locally Noetherian and the pullback
of a coherent module is coherent, and the unit `M ⟶ i_* i^* M` is an isomorphism by
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isIso_unit_app_of_smul_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_of_smul_eq_zero
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (M : X.Modules) [M.IsCoherent]
    (h : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, U)), (i.app U).hom a = 0 → ∀ m : Γ(M, U), a • m = 0) :
    ∃ G : Z.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj G ≅ M)
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity onto coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_iff_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T], the essential image on coherent modules.** A coherent module on `X`
is the direct image of a coherent module on `Z` exactly when the kernel of the comorphism of
the closed immersion annihilates it section by section.

This is the characterisation of the essential image of `i_*` restricted to coherent modules:
the forward implication is the general essential-image criterion
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pushforward_essImage_iff`, which needs no coherence at all, and the
reverse one is `exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_of_smul_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_iff_smul_eq_zero
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (M : X.Modules) [M.IsCoherent] :
    (∃ G : Z.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj G ≅ M)) ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, U)), (i.app U).hom a = 0 → ∀ m : Γ(M, U), a • m = 0
declarations.comment: the essential image on coherent modules

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag087TCoherentImage.coherentPushforwardEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 087T].** Direct image along a closed immersion of locally Noetherian schemes
is an equivalence from the coherent modules on the source onto the coherent modules on the
target annihilated by the defining ideal, and the equivalence is the one induced by direct
image.

The second component of the pair is `ObjectProperty.liftCompιIso`, which is `Iso.refl`: the
functor was built as the lift of `ι ⋙ i_*`, so no identification is needed.
declarations.statement:
def coherentPushforwardEquivalence :
    Σ e : CoherentModulesOn Z ≌ CoherentAnnihilatedModules i,
      e.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
          (fun M : X.Modules => M.IsCoherent ∧ AnnihilatedByKer i M) ≅
        ObjectProperty.ι (fun M : Z.Modules => M.IsCoherent) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward i

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_cohomologyToLimit_of_isProper_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**The theorem on formal functions over a complete base, [Stacks, Tag 087U].** For `A`
Noetherian and complete with respect to `J`, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper and `F` coherent, the
comparison `Hᵖ(X, F) ⟶ limₙ Hᵖ(X, F / 𝓙ⁿ F)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`.

This is `Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_cohomologyToLimit` with its three hypotheses discharged:
the finiteness of the cohomology by [Stacks, Tag 02O6], and the two uniform Artin-Rees bounds
by [Stacks, Tag 02OB] over the unconditional [Stacks, Tag 02O8].

This is the declaration [Stacks, Tag 087U] is registered on; the conditional statements of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalGeometry/CompletionProper/FormalFunctions.lean`, where the
comparison map and the reduction are built, are untagged.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_cohomologyToLimit_of_isProper_of_isAdicComplete
    (F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (p : ℕ) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    IsIso (cohomologyToLimit (baseIdealSheaf A J f) F p)
declarations.comment: for all p ≥ 0: A Noetherian and J-adically complete, f : X ⟶ Spec A proper, F coherent; 02O6 and 02OB are proved theorems used in the proof

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicSystemsEquivFGModuleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087W.** Coherent inverse systems on an affine Noetherian scheme are equivalent to
finite modules over the completion of its ring of global sections.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def coherentAdicSystemsEquivFGModuleCat
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (I : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    CoherentAdicSystems
      (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop I) ≌
        FGModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I Γ(X, ⊤))

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.globalSectionsComparison
declarations.doc: **Stacks 087W.** The canonical comparison with the inverse limit of global sections.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def globalSectionsComparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (I : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : CoherentAdicSystems (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop I)) :
    completedModuleAsBase X I F ≅ limit (globalSectionsSystem F)
declarations.comment: inverse-limit object

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.globalSectionsComparison_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks 087W.** The comparison is natural in morphisms of coherent adic systems.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSectionsComparison_naturality
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (I : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤))
    {F G : CoherentAdicSystems (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop I)}
    (f : F ⟶ G) :
    (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤)
      (AdicCompletion I Γ(X, ⊤)))).map
        ((coherentAdicSystemsEquivFGModuleCat X I).functor.map f).hom ≫
      (globalSectionsComparison X I G).hom =
    (globalSectionsComparison X I F).hom ≫
      limMap (F := globalSectionsSystem F) (G := globalSectionsSystem G)
        (Functor.whiskerRight f.hom
        (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤)))
declarations.comment: naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.globalSectionsComparison_projection_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087W.** Projection from the corresponding completed module onto any term is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSectionsComparison_projection_surjective
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (I : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : CoherentAdicSystems (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop I))
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Surjective
      (((globalSectionsComparison X I F).hom ≫
        limit.π (globalSectionsSystem F) (op n)).hom)
declarations.comment: surjective projections

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.globalSectionsComparison_projection_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087W.** The kernel of the projection is exactly the `(n+1)`-st ideal power multiple,
so the induced map from the quotient is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSectionsComparison_projection_ker
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (I : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : CoherentAdicSystems (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop I))
    (n : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.ker
      (((globalSectionsComparison X I F).hom ≫
        limit.π (globalSectionsSystem F) (op n)).hom) =
      I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, ⊤) (completedModuleAsBase X I F))
declarations.comment: canonical quotient

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.abelian_coherentAdicSystems
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of Tag 087X: the category of coherent adic systems on a Noetherian scheme is
abelian.** It is preadditive, has kernels, cokernels and finite products, and its coimage-image
comparisons are invertible.
declarations.statement:
public instance abelian_coherentAdicSystems {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Abelian (CoherentAdicSystems I)
declarations.comment: the category is abelian

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.restrictFunctor_exact
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Tag 087X: restriction to an open subscheme is exact on coherent adic systems.**
Restriction preserves finite limits, being compatible with the kernel construction, and finite
colimits, being a left adjoint computed termwise.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictFunctor_exact {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (restrictFunctor I f) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (restrictFunctor I f)
declarations.comment: restriction to an open is exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exact_iff_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Tag 087X: exactness in `Coh(X, ℐ)` may be checked on an open covering of `X`.**
A pair of morphisms `α : F ⟶ G` and `β : G ⟶ H` of coherent adic systems on a Noetherian scheme
is an exact sequence if and only if, for every member `U j` of an open covering of `X`, the
restrictions of `α` and `β` to `U j` form an exact sequence.

Both the condition that the composite vanish and the exactness of the resulting short complex are
local.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_iff_restrict {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    {F G H : CoherentAdicSystems I} (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H)
    {J : Type v} (U : J → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) :
    (∃ h : α ≫ β = 0, (ShortComplex.mk α β h).Exact) ↔
      ∀ j : J, ∃ h : (restrictFunctor I (U j).ι).map α ≫ (restrictFunctor I (U j).ι).map β = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk ((restrictFunctor I (U j).ι).map α)
          ((restrictFunctor I (U j).ι).map β) h).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness may be checked on an open covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.epi_iff_epi_app_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 087Y.** A morphism of coherent adic systems is surjective exactly when its
component at the lowest level is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem epi_iff_epi_app_zero {F G : CoherentAdicSystems I} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    Epi f ↔ Epi (f.hom.app (op 0))

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.finiteTypeAssociatedGradedData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 087Z.** For a Noetherian scheme `X` and a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals `ℐ`, the transition kernels of an object of `Coh(X, ℐ)` form a finite type, graded,
quasi-coherent module over the associated graded algebra `⨁ ℐ ⁿ / ℐ ⁿ⁺¹`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteTypeAssociatedGradedData {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : CoherentAdicSystems I) :
    Nonempty (AssociatedGradedData I F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Completion of a coherent sheaf along a quasi-coherent ideal, as a coherent adic inverse
system.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completionFunctor (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf ⥤
      Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems I
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctor_obj
declarations.doc: The `n`-th term of the completion is the quotient by `I ^ (n+1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completionFunctor_obj (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (n : ℕ) :
    ((completionFunctor X I).obj F).obj.obj (op n) = idealPowerQuotient I (n + 1) F.obj
declarations.comment: object formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionProjection_transition
declarations.doc: The projections are compatible with the transition maps of the inverse system.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completionProjection_transition (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (n : ℕ) :
    completionProjection X I F (n + 1) ≫
        ((completionFunctor X I).obj F).obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op =
      completionProjection X I F n
declarations.comment: transition maps

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctor_map_quotient
declarations.doc: Completion maps are exactly the maps induced on the successive quotients.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completionFunctor_map_quotient (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    {F G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf} (f : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ) :
    completionProjection X I F n ≫ ((completionFunctor X I).map f).hom.app (op n) =
      f.hom ≫ completionProjection X I G n
declarations.comment: morphism maps

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctor_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0881: the completion functor `Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(X, I)` of Stacks 0880 is exact.**

It is right exact because the completion of a coherent module is a quotient construction, and it
preserves monomorphisms by Artin–Rees; a right exact functor between abelian categories which
preserves monomorphisms is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completionFunctor_exact :
    exactFunctor _ _ (completionFunctor X I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionInternalHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0882.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `I` a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
on `X` and `G`, `F` coherent `𝒪_X`-modules; put `H = SheafHom(G, F)`. Then

`lim_n H⁰(X, H / Iⁿ H) = Mor_{Coh(X, I)}(G^∧, F^∧)`.

The left side is the inverse limit of the global sections of the completion of the internal hom;
the right side the morphisms of coherent adic systems between the completions of `G` and `F`. The
identification is additive.

Four steps: global sections commute with the inverse limit; the comparison
`lim H / Iⁿ H ⟶ SheafHom(G, lim F / Iⁿ F)` is an isomorphism
(`isIso_completedSheafHomComparison`); the global sections of an internal hom are the morphisms
(`internalHomSectionsTopEquiv`); and a morphism `G ⟶ lim F / Iⁿ F` is a morphism of coherent adic
systems `G^∧ ⟶ F^∧` (`completionHomLimitEquiv`).

Stacks states this for a Noetherian scheme; it holds, as here, on any locally Noetherian one.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completionInternalHomEquiv (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (G F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) :
    limit (C := ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) (Stacks.Coherent.globalSectionsSystem
      ((completionFunctor X I).obj (internalHomCoherent X G F))) ≃+
      ((completionFunctor X I).obj G ⟶ (completionFunctor X I).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.fullyFaithful_completionFunctor_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0883.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `J`, let
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper and let `𝓙 = J · 𝒪_X`. Then the completion functor
`Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(X, 𝓙)` of Stacks 0880 is fully faithful.

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_isZero_Hgroup_transitionKernel_tensorPowModule_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0884.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` a proper
morphism and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample relative to `f`. Let `𝓕` be an object of
`Coh(X, 𝓘)` for `𝓘 = I · 𝒪_X`. Then there is an integer `d₀` such that

  `H¹(X, Ker(𝓕_{n+1} ⟶ 𝓕_n) ⊗ L ^⊗ d) = 0`

for every `n ≥ 0` and every `d ≥ d₀` — one `d₀` for the whole system.

The hypotheses are exactly the source's. The proof is the degree-one case of
`Stacks.Coherent.exists_isZero_Hgroup_transitionKernel_tensorPowModule_of_pos` (Stacks 087Z and
Stacks 0897 part (2)), whose ampleness hypothesis on `V(𝓘)` follows from `f`-ampleness by
Stacks 01VK over the affine base and Stacks 0892 part (2) along the closed immersion
`V(𝓘) ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isZero_Hgroup_transitionKernel_tensorPowModule_of_isRelativelyAmple
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L)
    (𝓕 : CoherentAdicSystems (baseIdealSheaf A I f)) :
    ∃ d₀ : ℤ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ), d₀ ≤ d →
      IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ 1
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf,
              Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
                ((isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf X))⟩).obj (transitionKernel 𝓕 n)).obj
          (Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule X L d))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctor_of_isProjective_of_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Grothendieck's existence theorem for a projective morphism**, [Stacks, Tag 0885], read at
clause (1) of Tag 01W8.

Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to `I`, let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be projective —
a closed immersion over `Spec A` into a projective bundle `𝐏(ℰ)` — and set `𝓘 = I · 𝒪_X`. Then
the completion functor `Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(X, 𝓘)` of Stacks 0880 is an equivalence.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses. In particular `UniversallyClosed f` and
`LocallyOfFiniteType f` are *derived* from projectivity, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isProper`, rather than assumed; so is the local Noetherianity of
`X` that the completion functor of Stacks 0880 needs, and so is the `f`-ample invertible module
`L` the proof chooses.

Full faithfulness is Stacks 0883
(`Stacks.Algebraization.fullyFaithful_completionFunctor_of_isProper`). Essential surjectivity is
`Stacks.Algebraization.essSurj_of_forall_exists_epi` fed by the generation statement
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_epi_completionFunctor_of_vanishing`, whose own input is the uniform
`H¹`-vanishing of Stacks 0884
(`Stacks.Coherent.exists_isZero_Hgroup_transitionKernel_tensorPowModule`); and that theorem's
single hypothesis, part (2) of Stacks 0897 for the associated graded algebra of `𝓘`, is
`Stacks.Coherent.hasAssociatedGradedTwistVanishing_of_isProper`, which needs only properness and
the invertibility of `L`.

The name's `_of_vanishing` records the shape the statement had while that hypothesis was still
carried; it is kept because the statement itself did not change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_completionFunctor_of_isProjective_of_vanishing
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective f) :
    letI : IsProper f := hf.isProper
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    (completionFunctor X (baseIdealSheaf A I f)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0887: the functor `f^* : Coh(Y, 𝒥) ⟶ Coh(X, ℐ)`.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
Noetherian schemes and a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝒥` on `Y`, termwise pullback is a functor
from the coherent adic systems along `𝒥` to those along `ℐ = f^{-1}𝒥 𝒪_X`.

It is built as a lift of termwise pullback, so its action on objects and morphisms is the
canonical one; see `Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicPullback_obj_obj`.
declarations.statement:
public def coherentAdicPullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData) :
    CoherentAdicSystems J ⥤ CoherentAdicSystems (J.comap f)
declarations.comment: the functor f^*

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicPullback_obj_obj
declarations.doc: **The functor of Stacks 0887 sends the system `(G_n)` to the system `(f^*G_n)`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem coherentAdicPullback_obj_obj {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G : CoherentAdicSystems J) (n : ℕᵒᵖ) :
    ((coherentAdicPullback f J).obj G).obj.obj n =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (G.obj.obj n)
declarations.comment: the functor sends (G n) to (f^* G n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicPullback_rightExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0887: the pullback functor on coherent adic systems is right exact.**

Termwise pullback of inverse systems preserves all colimits, being a left adjoint; the inclusion
of `Coh(Y, 𝒥)` preserves finite colimits, cokernels there being levelwise; so the composite of
`f^*` with the inclusion of `Coh(X, ℐ)` preserves finite colimits, and that inclusion reflects
them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem coherentAdicPullback_rightExact {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    [IsNoetherian Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData) :
    rightExactFunctor _ _ (coherentAdicPullback f J)
declarations.comment: right exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.coherentAdicPullback_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0887: along a flat morphism the pullback functor on coherent adic systems is
exact.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem coherentAdicPullback_exact {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData) [Flat f] :
    exactFunctor _ _ (coherentAdicPullback f J)
declarations.comment: exactness when f is flat

declarations.name: Ideal.existsUnique_canonicalMap_of_smul_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0888.** In an exact sequence whose two end modules are annihilated by
an ideal `I`, elements `f, g ∈ I` determine a unique linear map `N → M`. Its value at `y` is
`g • x` for any lift `x` of `f • y`, and its composite with `M → N` is multiplication by
`f * g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_canonicalMap_of_smul_eq_bot
    (i : T →ₗ[A] M) (a : M →ₗ[A] N) (q : N →ₗ[A] Q)
    (hia : Function.Exact i a) (haq : Function.Exact a q)
    (I : Ideal A)
    (hT : I • (⊤ : Submodule A T) = ⊥)
    (hQ : I • (⊤ : Submodule A Q) = ⊥)
    {f g : A} (hf : f ∈ I) (hg : g ∈ I) :
    ∃! b : N →ₗ[A] M,
      (∀ (y : N) (x : M), a x = f • y → b y = g • x) ∧
        b.comp a = LinearMap.lsmul A M (f * g)
declarations.comment: canonical_fg_map

declarations.name: Ideal.pow_le_annihilator_ker_mapQ_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0888.** In an exact five-term sequence whose end modules are
annihilated by `K ^ t`, the power `K ^ (2 * t)` annihilates the kernel of the map induced after
reduction modulo any ideal `J`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_le_annihilator_ker_mapQ_of_exact
    (i : T →ₗ[A] M) (a : M →ₗ[A] N) (q : N →ₗ[A] Q)
    (_hi : Function.Injective i) (hia : Function.Exact i a)
    (haq : Function.Exact a q) (_hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (K : Ideal A) (t : ℕ) (_ht : 0 < t)
    (hT : K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A T)
    (hQ : K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A Q) (J : Ideal A) :
    K ^ (2 * t) ≤ Module.annihilator A
      ↑(LinearMap.ker (Submodule.mapQ (J • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
        (J • (⊤ : Submodule A N)) a
        (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top J a)))
declarations.comment: annihilation_mod_ideal

declarations.name: Ideal.pow_le_annihilator_coker_mapQ_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0888.** In an exact five-term sequence whose end modules are
annihilated by `K ^ t`, the power `K ^ (2 * t)` annihilates the cokernel of the map induced
after reduction modulo any ideal `J`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_le_annihilator_coker_mapQ_of_exact
    (i : T →ₗ[A] M) (a : M →ₗ[A] N) (q : N →ₗ[A] Q)
    (_hi : Function.Injective i) (_hia : Function.Exact i a)
    (haq : Function.Exact a q) (_hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (K : Ideal A) (t : ℕ) (_ht : 0 < t)
    (_hT : K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A T)
    (hQ : K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A Q) (J : Ideal A) :
    K ^ (2 * t) ≤ Module.annihilator A
      (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range
        (Submodule.mapQ (J • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) (J • (⊤ : Submodule A N)) a
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top J a)))
declarations.comment: annihilation_mod_ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_idealPowerQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
Let `a : M ⟶ N` be a morphism of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose kernel and cokernel are
annihilated by `𝒦 ᵗ`, and let `ℐ` be any quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Then `𝒦 ²ᵗ` annihilates both
the kernel and the cokernel of the induced map `M / ℐ ⁿ M ⟶ N / ℐ ⁿ N`.

This is the sheaf-of-modules form of `Ideal.pow_le_annihilator_ker_mapQ_of_exact` and
`Ideal.pow_le_annihilator_coker_mapQ_of_exact`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_idealPowerQuotientMap
    (I K : X.IdealSheafData) {M N : X.Modules} [M.IsQuasicoherent] [N.IsQuasicoherent]
    (a : M ⟶ N) {t : ℕ}
    (hk : idealPowerMultiple K t (kernel (C := X.Modules) a) = ⊥)
    (hc : idealPowerMultiple K t (cokernel (C := X.Modules) a) = ⊥) (n : ℕ) :
    idealPowerMultiple K (2 * t)
        (kernel (C := X.Modules) (idealPowerQuotientMap I I n n le_rfl a)) = ⊥ ∧
      idealPowerMultiple K (2 * t)
        (cokernel (C := X.Modules) (idealPowerQuotientMap I I n n le_rfl a)) = ⊥
declarations.comment: annihilation_mod_ideal, over sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_iff_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0888, conditions (1) and (2) on an affine scheme.** For a morphism `α`
of `Coh(Y, 𝓘)` on an affine Noetherian scheme `Y` the following are equivalent: one positive power
of `𝓚` annihilates every levelwise kernel `Ker(α_n)` and every levelwise cokernel `Coker(α_n)`;
and one positive power of `K = 𝓚(⊤)` annihilates the kernel and the cokernel of the map
`α_Y : M → N` of finite modules over the completion which Tag 087W attaches to `α`.

Both ideal sheaves on an affine scheme are attached to ideals of `Γ(Y, ⊤)`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.equivOfIsAffine`, so the statement may be reduced to that
presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_iff_affine {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Y]
    [IsNoetherianRing Γ(Y, ⊤)] (ℐ 𝒦 : Y.IdealSheafData)
    {F G : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems ℐ} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower 𝒦 f.hom ↔
      IsAffineKernelCokernelAnnihilated (𝒦.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top Y⟩) f
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1) and (2) on an affine scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0888.** For a morphism `α` of `Coh(X, 𝓘)` on a Noetherian scheme `X` and
a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓚`, the following are equivalent:

1. one positive power of `𝓚` annihilates every levelwise kernel `Ker(α_n)` and every levelwise
   cokernel `Coker(α_n)`;
2. for every affine open `U ⊆ X` one positive power of `𝓚(U)` annihilates `Ker(α_U)` and
   `Coker(α_U)`, where `α_U` is the map of finite modules over the completion attached to `α|_U`
   by Tag 087W;
3. the conclusion of (2) holds for the members of some finite affine open covering of `X`.

A morphism satisfying these conditions is the source's *map whose kernel and cokernel are
annihilated by a power of `𝓚`*.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_tfae {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (ℐ 𝒦 : X.IdealSheafData) {F G : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems ℐ} (α : F ⟶ G) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower 𝒦 α.hom,
        ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsAffineLocalKernelCokernelAnnihilated 𝒦 α U,
        ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : Finite J) (U : J → X.affineOpens),
          iSup (fun j => (U j).1) = ⊤ ∧
            ∀ j, IsAffineLocalKernelCokernelAnnihilated 𝒦 α (U j)]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0888 (1).** A morphism `α` of inverse systems of sheaves of modules has *kernel and
cokernel annihilated by a power of `K`* if there is one positive exponent `t` for which `K ^ t`
annihilates both `Ker(α_k)` and `Coker(α_k)`, simultaneously for every index `k`.

Kernel and cokernel are taken levelwise, in the abelian category `X.Modules`. This is the notion
the source names at the end of the remark, once its three conditions have been shown
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public def IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower (K : X.IdealSheafData) {F G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules}
    (α : F ⟶ G) : Prop
declarations.comment: the notion named by the remark

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_unique_algebraization_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0889 (1) on a Noetherian scheme.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `ℐ` a
quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, `G` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `(F_n)` a coherent `ℐ`-adic system. A
morphism `α : (F_n) ⟶ G^∧` whose levelwise kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a power of
`ℐ` admits a triple `(F, a, β)`, unique up to a unique isomorphism, with `F` a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module, `a : F ⟶ G` a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of
`ℐ`, `β : (F_n) ≅ F^∧` an isomorphism, and `α = a^∧ ∘ β`. Uniqueness: for a second such triple
`(F', a', β')` there is exactly one isomorphism `d : F ≅ F'` of triples, that is, with
`a' ∘ d = a` and `d^∧ ∘ β = β'`.

The existence is `Stacks.Algebraization.exists_unique_algebraization` with its one premise
supplied by `Stacks.Algebraization.isPowerAnnihilated_of_restrict`: on a Noetherian scheme the
affine-local annihilation of a sheaf of modules by powers of `ℐ|_U` is annihilation by a single
power of `ℐ`, because quasi-compactness extracts a finite affine covering and annihilation by a
fixed power is local on the base. The uniqueness there is read on `lim (F_n)`, and
`completionMap_comp_eq_iff_limMap` turns it into the compatibility `d^∧ ∘ β = β'`. The conditions
are exactly those of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_unique_algebraization_of_isNoetherian {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (Fsys : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (α : Fsys.obj ⟶ ((completionFunctor X I).obj G).obj)
    (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower I α) :
    ∃ (F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (a : F ⟶ G)
      (β : Fsys.obj ≅ ((completionFunctor X I).obj F).obj),
      (α = β.hom ≫ ((completionFunctor X I).map a).hom ∧
          IsPowerAnnihilated I (kernel (C := X.Modules) a.hom) ∧
            IsPowerAnnihilated I (cokernel (C := X.Modules) a.hom)) ∧
        ∀ (F' : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (a' : F' ⟶ G)
            (β' : Fsys.obj ≅ ((completionFunctor X I).obj F').obj),
          α = β'.hom ≫ ((completionFunctor X I).map a').hom →
            IsPowerAnnihilated I (kernel (C := X.Modules) a'.hom) →
              IsPowerAnnihilated I (cokernel (C := X.Modules) a'.hom) →
                ∃! d : F ≅ F',
                  d.hom ≫ a' = a ∧
                    β.hom ≫ ((completionFunctor X I).map d.hom).hom = β'.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): algebraization of a map into a completion

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_unique_algebraization_dual_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0889 (2).** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `ℐ` a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, `G` a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `(F_n)` a coherent `ℐ`-adic system. A morphism `α : G^∧ ⟶ (F_n)` whose
levelwise kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a power of `ℐ` admits a triple `(F, a, β)`,
unique up to a unique isomorphism, with `F` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module, `a : G ⟶ F` a morphism whose
kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `ℐ`, `β : F^∧ ≅ (F_n)` an isomorphism, and
`α = β ∘ a^∧`.

The existence is `Stacks.Algebraization.exists_algebraization_dual`, whose affine-local
annihilation of the kernel and the cokernel of `a` becomes annihilation by a single power of `ℐ`
by `Stacks.Algebraization.isPowerAnnihilated_of_restrict`, using that `X` is quasi-compact. The
uniqueness is `Stacks.Algebraization.unique_algebraization_dual`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_unique_algebraization_dual_of_isNoetherian {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (Fsys : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (α : ((completionFunctor X I).obj G).obj ⟶ Fsys.obj)
    (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower I α) :
    ∃ (F : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (a : G ⟶ F)
      (β : ((completionFunctor X I).obj F).obj ≅ Fsys.obj),
      (α = ((completionFunctor X I).map a).hom ≫ β.hom ∧
          IsPowerAnnihilated I (kernel (C := X.Modules) a.hom) ∧
            IsPowerAnnihilated I (cokernel (C := X.Modules) a.hom)) ∧
        ∀ (F' : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) (a' : G ⟶ F')
            (β' : ((completionFunctor X I).obj F').obj ≅ Fsys.obj),
          α = ((completionFunctor X I).map a').hom ≫ β'.hom →
            IsPowerAnnihilated I (kernel (C := X.Modules) a'.hom) →
              IsPowerAnnihilated I (cokernel (C := X.Modules) a'.hom) →
                ∃! d : F ≅ F',
                  a ≫ d.hom = a' ∧
                    ((completionFunctor X I).map d.hom).hom ≫ β'.hom = β.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): algebraization of a map out of a completion

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.isCoherentAdicSystem_liftedQuotientTower
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A: the tower of algebraizations is a coherent adic system along `𝒦`.** Let `X` be
Noetherian, let `ℐ, 𝒦` be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves satisfying hypothesis (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 088A] at every level, and let `(G_e)` be a tower of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, the
term `e` annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`, whose termwise `ℐ`-completion is identified naturally with the
tower of `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`-reductions of an object `(F_n)` of `Coh(X, ℐ)`. Then the underlying inverse
system of `(G_e)` is an object of `Coh(X, 𝒦)`.

Only the quotient clause needs proof. The transition `G_{e+1} ⟶ G_e` descends through the
projection onto `G_{e+1} / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ G_{e+1}`, and `Stacks.Coherent.completion_quotientDesc_eq`
identifies the completion of that descent with the composite of
`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerQuotientAdicCompletionIso`, the given identification and
`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerQuotientAdicCollapseIso`, hence with an isomorphism. Both modules are
annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`, so completion reflects the isomorphism by
`Stacks.Coherent.isIso_of_isIso_completion_map_of_power_annihilated`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherentAdicSystem_liftedQuotientTower [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : CoherentAdicSystems I) (h : IsCompletionEquivalenceOnPowerThickenings I K)
    (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (hG : ∀ e : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple K (e + 1) (G.obj (op e)).obj = ⊥)
    (c : G ⋙ completionFunctor X I ≅
      idealPowerQuotientAdicTower I K ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj F) :
    IsCoherentAdicSystem K (G ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _)
declarations.comment: proof step 4, adic form: the tower of algebraizations lies in Coh(X, 𝒦)

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.isCoherentAdicSystem_and_annihilated_idealPowerQuotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the opening step of the proof.** For a locally Noetherian `X`, quasi-coherent
ideal sheaves `ℐ, 𝒦`, an exponent `e` and a coherent adic system `(F_n)` along `ℐ`, the reduction
`n ↦ F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ F_n` is again a coherent adic system along `ℐ`, and every one of its terms is
annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ`.

This is the sense in which the source's `(F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ F_n)` is "a system of `Coh(X, ℐ)`" lying in
the full subcategory of objects annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ` — the subcategory which hypothesis (1) of
Tag 088A, read through the closed-immersion equivalence of Tag 087T, identifies with
`Coh(X_e, ℐ_e)`.

The first clause is `Stacks.Coherent.isCoherentAdicSystem_idealPowerQuotientSystem`, whose
substance is that the two orders of division agree. The second is
`Stacks.Algebraization.idealPowerMultiple_idealPowerQuotient_eq_bot`, applied to each term; it
needs the term to be quasi-coherent, which is the coherence clause of the given system.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherentAdicSystem_and_annihilated_idealPowerQuotientSystem
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {I : X.IdealSheafData} (K : X.IdealSheafData) (e : ℕ)
    {F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules} (hF : IsCoherentAdicSystem I F) :
    IsCoherentAdicSystem I (idealPowerQuotientSystem K e F) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple K e ((idealPowerQuotientSystem K e F).obj (op n)) = ⊥
declarations.comment: proof step 1: the 𝒦ᵉ-reduction is in Coh(X, ℐ), annihilated by 𝒦ᵉ

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_whiskerRight_idealPowerQuotientFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the second step of the proof.** Reducing a morphism of inverse systems of
quasi-coherent modules modulo the fixed power `𝒦 ᵉ` doubles the exponent in hypothesis (2): if
`𝒦 ᵗ` annihilates every levelwise kernel and cokernel of `α`, then `𝒦 ²ᵗ` annihilates every
levelwise kernel and cokernel of
`n ↦ (F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ F_n ⟶ G_n / 𝒦 ᵉ G_n)`.

This is the source's first application of the remark of Tag 0888, which this library has over
sheaves of modules as
`Stacks.Algebraization.idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_idealPowerQuotientMap`; the source
applies it a second time further on and reaches `𝒦 ⁴ᵗ`.
