Applied with `(G_n) = H ^∧` it is the statement that the comparison map of hypothesis (2) of
Tag 088A survives the reduction of the opening step with its kernel–cokernel condition intact,
which is what makes the reduced system an object to which Tag 0889 can be applied.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_whiskerRight_idealPowerQuotientFunctor
    (K : X.IdealSheafData) (e : ℕ) {F G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules}
    (hF : ∀ n : ℕ, (F.obj (op n)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hG : ∀ n : ℕ, (G.obj (op n)).IsQuasicoherent)
    {α : F ⟶ G} (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K α) :
    IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K
      (Functor.whiskerRight α (idealPowerQuotientFunctor K e))
declarations.comment: proof step 2: the 𝒦ᵉ-reduction of a map with 𝒦ᵗ-annihilated kernel and cokernel has 𝒦²ᵗ-annihilated kernel and cokernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_coherent_annihilated_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the third step of the proof.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `ℐ, 𝒦` be
quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, let `e` be an exponent and let `(F_n)` be an object of
`Coh(X, ℐ)`. If hypothesis (1) of Tag 088A holds at the level `e` — that is, the completion
functor of `X_e = V(𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹)` along `ℐ 𝒪_{X_e}` is an equivalence — then the `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`-reduction of
`(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`.

This is where hypothesis (1) enters. The reduction is carried to `X_e` by the pullback functor
of Tag 0887, where the hypothesis algebraizes it to a coherent module `M`; the algebraization on
`X` is `G = i_* M`, coherent by Tag 087T and annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹` because it is a direct image
along the inclusion of `V(𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹)`. The comparison of completions is
`Stacks.Coherent.completionPushforwardIso`, which identifies the completion of `i_* M` with the
direct image of the completion of `M`, followed by
`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerQuotientSystemPushforwardIso`, which is Tag 0EL1 identifying
`i_* i^* F_n` with `F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ F_n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_coherent_annihilated_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem
    [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (e : ℕ) (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (h : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme :=
        LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι
      (completionFunctor (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme
        (I.comap (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι)).IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
      idealPowerMultiple K (e + 1) G.obj = ⊥ ∧
      Nonempty (((completionFunctor X I).obj G).obj ≅
        idealPowerQuotientSystem K (e + 1) Fsys.obj)
declarations.comment: proof step 3: hypothesis (1) algebraizes the 𝒦ᵉ-reduction

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_coherentAdicSystem_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the fourth step of the proof: the algebraizations assemble.** Let `X` be a
Noetherian scheme, let `ℐ, 𝒦` be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves and let `(F_n)` be an object of
`Coh(X, ℐ)`. If hypothesis (1) of Tag 088A holds at every level — the completion functor of
`X_e = V(𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹)` along `ℐ 𝒪_{X_e}` is an equivalence — then the coherent modules `G_e`
algebraizing the reductions `(F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ F_n)` form an object of `Coh(X, 𝒦)`.

The modules themselves and their defining property are the third step,
`Stacks.Coherent.exists_coherent_annihilated_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem`. What is
added here is the identification `G_{e+1} / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ G_{e+1} ≅ G_e`, read off the completions by
`Stacks.Coherent.nonempty_idealPowerQuotient_iso_of_completion_iso`: completion along `ℐ`
carries the left-hand side to

`(F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺² F_n) / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ (…) ≅ F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ F_n`,

by `Stacks.Coherent.completionIdealPowerQuotientSystemIso` and
`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerQuotientSystemCollapseIso`, which is the completion of the right-hand
side; and completion along `ℐ`, although not known to be full on all of `Coh(𝒪_X)`, is fully
faithful on the modules annihilated by `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`. The assembly of the identified modules into an
object of `Coh(X, 𝒦)` is `Stacks.Coherent.exists_coherentAdicSystem_of_succQuotientIso`.

The conclusion keeps the sequence `G` alongside the assembled system, because the rest of the
source's argument speaks about the terms: the comparison with `H ^∧` is built level by level.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_coherentAdicSystem_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem
    [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (h : ∀ e : ℕ,
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme :=
        LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι
      (completionFunctor (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme
        (I.comap (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι)).IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ Gsys : CoherentAdicSystems K,
      ∃ G : ℕ → AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
        (∀ e : ℕ, Gsys.obj.obj (op e) = (G e).obj) ∧
        ∀ e : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple K (e + 1) (G e).obj = ⊥ ∧
          Nonempty (((completionFunctor X I).obj (G e)).obj ≅
            idealPowerQuotientSystem K (e + 1) Fsys.obj)
declarations.comment: proof step 4: the algebraizations G_e assemble into an object of Coh(X, 𝒦)

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_lifted_quotient_tower
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the fourth step in the form the rest of the proof needs it.** Under hypothesis
(1) of Tag 088A at every level, the algebraizations `G_e` of the reductions
`(F_n / 𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹ F_n)` form a tower of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, the term `e` annihilated by
`𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`, whose termwise `ℐ`-completion is identified with the tower of reductions **naturally
in `e`**.

`Stacks.Coherent.exists_coherentAdicSystem_completion_iso_idealPowerQuotientSystem` assembles
the same modules into an object of `Coh(X, 𝒦)`, but its identification of completions is one
isomorphism for each `e` separately. What is added here is the naturality: the transition
`G_{e+1} ⟶ G_e` is obtained by lifting the transition of the tower of reductions through the
full faithfulness of completion on the `𝒦 ᵉ⁺²`-annihilated modules
(`Stacks.Coherent.exists_unique_completion_preimage_of_power_annihilated`), so the chosen
isomorphisms commute with the transitions by construction.

This is the datum that
`Stacks.Coherent.exists_tower_map_to_completion` consumes to produce the comparison
`(G_e) ⟶ H ^∧_𝒦` along `𝒦`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_lifted_quotient_tower [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (h : ∀ e : ℕ,
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme :=
        LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι
      (completionFunctor (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme
        (I.comap (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι)).IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
      (∀ e : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple K (e + 1) (G.obj (op e)).obj = ⊥) ∧
      Nonempty (G ⋙ completionFunctor X I ≅
        idealPowerQuotientAdicTower I K ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj Fsys)
declarations.comment: proof step 4, natural form: the algebraizations G_e form a tower whose ℐ-completion is the tower of 𝒦-power reductions of (F_n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_lifted_quotient_tower_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A, the fifth step: the comparison along `𝒦` exists and satisfies the hypothesis of
Tag 0889.** Let `X` be Noetherian, let `ℐ, 𝒦` be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves satisfying
hypothesis (1) of Tag 088A at every level, and let `α : (F_n) ⟶ H ^∧_ℐ` be a comparison whose
levelwise kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a power of `𝒦` — hypothesis (2). Then the
tower `(G_e)` of algebraizations of the reductions carries a morphism `γ : (G_e) ⟶ H ^∧_𝒦` whose
kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a single positive power of `𝒦`.

This is the whole of the source's passage from the comparison along `ℐ` to the comparison along
`𝒦`: the tower is `Stacks.Coherent.exists_lifted_quotient_tower`, the comparison is
`Stacks.Coherent.exists_tower_map_to_completion` — the reduction of `α` lifted through the
fullness of completion on `𝒦`-power-annihilated towers — and the annihilation is
`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_tower_map_eq_bot`, the remark of Tag 0888
followed by the reflection of annihilation along completion.

What remains of the proof of Tag 088A after this is the final identification: Tag 0889 applied
to `γ` algebraizes it, and its uniqueness clause, threaded through the two towers, identifies
`(F_n)` with the completion of the resulting module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_lifted_quotient_tower_comparison [IsNoetherian X]
    (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (h : ∀ e : ℕ,
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme :=
        LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι
      (completionFunctor (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme
        (I.comap (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι)).IsEquivalence)
    (H : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (α : Fsys ⟶ (completionFunctor X I).obj H)
    (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K α.hom) :
    ∃ (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
      (γ : G ⟶ completionTermTower K H),
      (∀ e : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple K (e + 1) (G.obj (op e)).obj = ⊥) ∧
      Nonempty (G ⋙ completionFunctor X I ≅
        idealPowerQuotientAdicTower I K ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj Fsys) ∧
      ∃ s : ℕ, 0 < s ∧ ∀ e : ℕ,
        idealPowerMultiple K s (kernel (C := X.Modules) (γ.app (op e)).hom) = ⊥ ∧
          idealPowerMultiple K s (cokernel (C := X.Modules) (γ.app (op e)).hom) = ⊥
declarations.comment: proof step 5: the comparison (G_e) ⟶ H^∧_𝒦 along 𝒦, with its levelwise kernels and cokernels annihilated by a power of 𝒦

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.essImage_completionFunctor_of_pow_le
declarations.doc:
**Tag 088A in the case `ℐ ᵐ ≤ 𝒦`.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `ℐ, 𝒦` be
quasi-coherent ideal sheaves on `X` with `ℐ ᵐ ≤ 𝒦` for some `m ≥ 1`, let `H` be a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and let `(F_n)` be an object of `Coh(X, ℐ)` admitting a map `α : (F_n) ⟶ H ^∧`
whose levelwise kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a power of `𝒦`. Then `(F_n)` is in the
essential image of the completion functor of Tag 0880.

Hypothesis (1) of the source is not needed here, and no reduction modulo a power of `𝒦` occurs:
the containment turns hypothesis (2) into the hypothesis of Tag 0889 part (1) by
`Stacks.Coherent.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_of_pow_le`, and
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_unique_algebraization_of_isNoetherian` then algebraizes `α`,
delivering a coherent module `F` and an isomorphism `(F_n) ≅ F ^∧`. The isomorphism is of the
underlying inverse systems and is promoted to the full subcategory `Coh(X, ℐ)` by
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isoMk`.

The source's own application has `ℐ` the pullback of an ideal of the base and `𝒦` the ideal of
the complement of the dense open on which Chow's lemma is an isomorphism; no power of `ℐ` is
contained in `𝒦` there, so this case does not cover it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem essImage_completionFunctor_of_pow_le [IsNoetherian X] {I K : X.IdealSheafData}
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hIK : I ^ m ≤ K)
    (H : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (α : Fsys.obj ⟶ ((completionFunctor X I).obj H).obj)
    (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K α) :
    (completionFunctor X I).essImage Fsys
declarations.comment: the case ℐᵐ ≤ 𝒦, hypothesis (1) unused; incomparable case not claimed

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.essImage_completionFunctor_of_isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 088A].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `ℐ, 𝒦 ⊆ 𝒪_X` be quasi-coherent
ideal sheaves. Let `(F_n)` be an object of `Coh(X, ℐ)` and suppose

1. for every `e`, completion along `ℐ 𝒪_{X_e}` is an equivalence on `Coh(𝒪_{X_e})`, where
   `X_e = V(𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹)` is the closed subscheme cut out by the positive power `𝒦 ᵉ⁺¹`, and
2. there is a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `H` and a morphism `α : (F_n) ⟶ H ^∧_ℐ` whose levelwise
   kernels and cokernels are annihilated by a power of `𝒦`.

Then `(F_n)` is in the essential image of the completion functor of [Stacks, Tag 0880]: it is
the `ℐ`-completion of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.

The proof is the source's, assembled from the steps carried above and in
`FormalGeometry.CoherentAdicSystem`. Dividing `(F_n)` by the powers of `𝒦` and algebraizing the
reductions with hypothesis (1) produces the tower `(G_e)` of
`Stacks.Coherent.exists_lifted_quotient_tower`, which is an object of `Coh(X, 𝒦)` by
`Stacks.Coherent.isCoherentAdicSystem_liftedQuotientTower`; the reduction of `α`, lifted through
the fullness of completion on the annihilated towers, is the comparison
`γ : (G_e) ⟶ H ^∧_𝒦` of `Stacks.Coherent.exists_tower_map_to_completion`, and its levelwise
kernels and cokernels are annihilated by one power of `𝒦`
(`Stacks.Coherent.idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_tower_map_eq_bot`). So [Stacks, Tag 0889]
part (1) algebraizes `γ` to a coherent module `M` with `(G_e) ≅ M ^∧_𝒦`.

What remains is to recognize `(F_n)` as `M ^∧_ℐ`. Reading the identification of the completed
tower `(G_e) ^∧_ℐ` with the tower of reductions of `(F_n)` along the *other* index
(`Stacks.Coherent.liftedQuotientRowTowerIso`) turns the algebraization of `γ` into an
identification of the `𝒦`-completions of the terms of `(F_n)` and of `M ^∧_ℐ`, compatible with
`α` and with `α ^∧` by `Stacks.Coherent.liftedQuotientRowIso_map_to_completion`; the uniqueness
clause of Tag 0889 applied termwise then identifies the two systems, which is
`Stacks.Coherent.nonempty_iso_of_completion_iso_over_power_annihilated`.

`Stacks.Coherent.essImage_completionFunctor_of_pow_le` is the special case `ℐ ᵐ ≤ 𝒦`, where
hypothesis (1) is not needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem essImage_completionFunctor_of_isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower [IsNoetherian X]
    (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (Fsys : CoherentAdicSystems I)
    (h : ∀ e : ℕ,
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme :=
        LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι
      (completionFunctor (K ^ (e + 1)).subscheme
        (I.comap (K ^ (e + 1)).subschemeι)).IsEquivalence)
    (H : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (α : Fsys ⟶ (completionFunctor X I).obj H)
    (hα : IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K α.hom) :
    (completionFunctor X I).essImage Fsys

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.exists_isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_comparisonMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088B.** Let `Y` be a Noetherian scheme and let `𝒥, 𝒦 ⊆ 𝒪_Y` be quasi-coherent
sheaves of ideals. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism which is an isomorphism over
`V = Y ∖ V(𝒦)`, and set `ℐ = f^{-1}𝒥 𝒪_X`. Let `(𝒢_n)` be an object of `Coh(Y, 𝒥)`, let `𝓕` be
a coherent `𝒪_X`-module, and let `β : (f^*𝒢_n) ⟶ 𝓕^` be an isomorphism in `Coh(X, ℐ)`. Then
there exists a map

`α : (𝒢_n) ⟶ (f_*𝓕)^`

in `Coh(Y, 𝒥)` whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝒦`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_comparisonMap
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y] (J K : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hf : IsIso (f ∣_ K.support.compl))
    (G : CoherentAdicSystems J) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : IsNoetherian X :=
      { toIsLocallyNoetherian := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
        toCompactSpace := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f }
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent :=
      AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.isCoherent_pushforward f F
    ∀ _β : (coherentAdicPullback f J).obj G ≅
        (completionFunctor X (J.comap f)).obj ⟨F, inferInstance⟩,
      ∃ α : G ⟶ (completionFunctor Y J).obj
          ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F, inferInstance⟩,
        IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower K α.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctor_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088C: Grothendieck's existence theorem for a proper morphism.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be a proper morphism
of schemes and set `𝓘 = I · 𝒪_X`. Then the completion functor `Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(X, 𝓘)` of
Stacks 0880 is an equivalence.

This is `Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctor_of_devissage` with both of its
hypotheses discharged: `hFF` by the theorem on formal functions in degree zero over a complete
base, `isIso_globalSectionsToLimit_of_isProper`, and `hDev` by
`Stacks.Coherent.essImage_completionFunctor_of_devissageStep`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_completionFunctor_of_isProper
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    (completionFunctor X (baseIdealSheaf A I f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: Grothendieck's existence theorem: A Noetherian and complete with respect to I, f : X -> Spec A proper and the ideal sheaf I O_X; the completion functor of 0880 from coherent O_X-modules to coherent I O_X-adic systems is an equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completion_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088D.** The first term of the completion of a coherent sheaf whose support is
proper over the base again has support proper over the base.

That term is the quotient `F / I · F`, so its support is a closed subset of the support of `F`,
and a closed subset of a closed subset proper over the base is proper over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completion_hasProperSupport
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : CoherentModulesProperOver f) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    HasProperSupport f
      (((completionFunctor X (baseIdealSheaf A I f)).obj F.obj).obj.obj (op 0))
declarations.comment: proper support of the completion

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctorProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088D.** The completion functor of Stacks 0880, restricted to the coherent sheaves
and the coherent adic systems whose support is proper over the affine base.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completionFunctorProperOver
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    CoherentModulesProperOver f ⥤ CoherentAdicSystemsProperOver f (baseIdealSheaf A I f)
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver_holds
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 088E], Grothendieck's existence theorem.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring
complete with respect to an ideal `I` and let `f : Z ⟶ Spec A` be separated and of finite type
(`IsSeparated`, `LocallyOfFiniteType` and `QuasiCompact`). Then the functor of [Stacks, Tag 088D]

  `Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_Z) ⥤ Coh_{support proper over A}(Z, I 𝒪_Z)`

is an equivalence.

`Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver_of_adicBaseChangeUnitCondition`
at `Stacks.Algebraization.hasAdicBaseChangeUnitCondition`. Following the source, the proof reduces
to Stacks 088C on the closed subschemes of `Z` proper over `A`, after showing that every coherent
adic system with support proper over `A` is annihilated by the ideal sheaf of such a subscheme
(Chow's lemma, the projective case 0885, and Stacks 088B through
`Stacks.Algebraization.transport_of_isDirectImageComparison`).

This is the carrier of Stacks 088E: it takes no input beyond the source's hypotheses, and
supersedes the conditional forms
`Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver` and
`Stacks.Algebraization.isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver_of_adicBaseChangeUnitCondition`,
which take theirs as an argument.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver_holds
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    (completionFunctorProperOver A I f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: Grothendieck's existence theorem: A Noetherian and complete with respect to I, X separated and of finite type over A; the functor of 088D from coherent O_X-modules with support proper over A to coherent I-adic systems with support proper over A is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AdicCoherentModuleSystem
declarations.doc:
**The systems `(ℱₙ, φₙ)` of Stacks 088F.** For `f : X ⟶ Spec A` locally of finite type, a
coherent `𝒪_{Xₙ}`-module for every `n`, together with an isomorphism `φₙ : iₙ^* ℱₙ₊₁ ≅ ℱₙ`
along the transition `iₙ : Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁`, whose first term has support proper over `S₁`.

The three fields other than `obj` are clauses (1), (2) and (3) of the remark. Clause (2) asks
for an isomorphism as *data*, as in the source, not merely for the existence of one: the
transition maps of the system are part of it.
declarations.statement:
public structure AdicCoherentModuleSystem (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
declarations.comment: the systems (F n, phi n) of clauses (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_adicThickeningCompletionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The completion functor is an equivalence.** Let `A` be a Noetherian
ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, put `S = Spec A`, `Sₙ = Spec (A / Iⁿ)`, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be separated and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact) and
`Xₙ = X ×_S Sₙ`. Then the completion functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.adicThickeningCompletionFunctor`, from the coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with support
proper over `A` to the systems `(ℱₙ, φₙ)` — `ℱₙ` coherent on `Xₙ`, `φₙ : iₙ^*ℱₙ₊₁ ≅ ℱₙ`, and
`Supp(ℱ₁)` proper over `S₁` — sending `ℱ` to its restrictions `ℱ|_{Xₙ}`, is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_adicThickeningCompletionFunctor
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    (adicThickeningCompletionFunctor A I f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the completion functor from the coherent O_X-modules with support proper over A to the systems (F n, phi n) of clauses (1), (2) and (3) is an equivalence of categories, for A Noetherian and I-adically complete and X -> Spec A separated and of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_adicThickeningTransitionCompletionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be
proper and `Xₙ = X ×_S Sₙ`. Then completion `ℱ ↦ (ℱ|_{Xₙ})` is an equivalence from the category
of all coherent `𝒪_X`-modules to the category of systems `(ℱₙ, φₙ)` with `ℱₙ` a coherent
`𝒪_{Xₙ}`-module and `φₙ : iₙ^*ℱₙ₊₁ ≅ ℱₙ` an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_adicThickeningTransitionCompletionFunctor [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete I A] [IsProper f] :
    (adicThickeningTransitionCompletionFunctor A I f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the remark's last sentence: for X proper over A, with the conditions on the supports omitted, completion from all coherent O_X-modules to the systems of coherent O_{X_n}-modules F n with isomorphisms phi n is an equivalence of categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_and_dense_toSchemeTheoreticImage_of_qc_or_reduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088G.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `h : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of algebraic
spaces over `S`.  Assume either that `h` is quasi-compact or that `Z` is reduced, and let
`Z̄ ⊆ X` be the scheme-theoretic image of `h`.  Then the morphism `Z ⟶ Z̄` is an open immersion
which identifies `Z` with a scheme-theoretically dense open subspace of `Z̄`; moreover `Z` is
topologically dense in `Z̄`.

Spelled out, the five assertions are: the morphism onto the scheme-theoretic image is an open
immersion; it is an isomorphism onto its range, which is the identification of `Z` with a
subspace of `Z̄`; that range is an open subspace of `Z̄`; it is scheme-theoretically dense in
`Z̄`; and the induced map on points has dense range.

Each is proved separately in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Morphisms/ImmersionSchemeTheoreticallyDenseOpen.lean`,
the identification being the only one not stated there: it is
`CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.toRange` of the morphism onto the image, which is an isomorphism
because that morphism is an open immersion and hence a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_and_dense_toSchemeTheoreticImage_of_qc_or_reduced
    {Z X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (h : Z ⟶ X) (hh : IsImmersion B S hS h)
    (hq_or_hr : IsQuasiCompact B S hS h ∨
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced W)) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS h) ∧
      IsIso (Subfunctor.toRange (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS h)) ∧
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS (Subfunctor.range (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS h)) ∧
      IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS (Subfunctor.range (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS h)) ∧
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS Z (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Decent.closure_iUnion_range_residuePairMap_meets_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The closure of the union of the off-diagonal products of residue-field spectra
meets the diagonal in `Spec(A ⊗ℤ A)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma closure_iUnion_range_residuePairMap_meets_diagonal (_hp : Function.Injective p) :
    (closure (⋃ n, ⋃ m, ⋃ (_ : n ≠ m),
        range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (residuePairMap A k p n m))) ∩
      range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (diagonalMap A))).Nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_of_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated
declarations.doc: **Stacks 088J.** A locally separated algebraic space is decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentSpace_of_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hsep : IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    IsDecentSpace B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088L.**  Let `f : U ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `U` an
affine scheme, `f` locally of finite type and `X` locally separated.  Then `U` admits an
immersion into affine `n`-space over `X`, over `X`.

The hypothesis `hcard` bounds the ring of sections of `U` by the cofinality of the site's
cutoff; it is not part of Stacks 088L, but is the condition under which the directed limit
used in the proof is an algebraic space in this development, inherited from Stacks 07SF and
Stacks 0828.  See `exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_of_isRegular` for the form in which it
disappears, and the implementation notes of this file for why it cannot be removed outright.

Quasi-separatedness of `X`, which Stacks 088L also assumes, is not needed: this development's
Stacks 0828, part (2) does not assume it of the stages.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hls : IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (hcard : #Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, ⊤) < B.cutoff.ord.cof) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (j : yoneda.obj U ⟶ affineSpaceOver B S hS X n),
      j ≫ prod.fst = f ∧ IsImmersion B S hS j
declarations.comment: with the cutoff-cofinality side condition on the sections of `U` that the directed limit in the proof requires; quasi-separatedness of `X` is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088L** over a big fppf site whose size cutoff is a regular cardinal: an affine
scheme locally of finite type over a locally separated algebraic space admits an immersion
into affine `n`-space over that space.

Regularity of the cutoff discharges the cardinality side condition of
`exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver` for every `U`: the sections of an affine object of the
site are bounded by its size, which is below the cutoff, which is its own cofinality.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_of_isRegular (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hreg : B.cutoff.IsRegular)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hls : IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (j : yoneda.obj U ⟶ affineSpaceOver B S hS X n),
      j ≫ prod.fst = f ∧ IsImmersion B S hS j
declarations.comment: verbatim, over a big fppf site whose size cutoff is a regular cardinal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088L.**  Let `f : U ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `U` an
affine scheme, `f` locally of finite type, and `X` quasi-separated and locally separated.
Then there is an immersion `U ⟶ 𝔸ⁿ_X` over `X`.

Writing `U = Spec A` with `A` the filtered union of its finite type `ℤ`-subalgebras `Aᵢ`, the
graph `U ⟶ X ⨯ U` is an immersion because `X` is locally separated (Stacks 03KO), and
`X ⨯ U` is the directed limit of the stages `X ⨯ Spec Aᵢ`, which have affine transition
morphisms and are quasi-separated because `X` is.  Stacks 0828, part (2), which places no bound
on the index set, then makes `U ⟶ X ⨯ Spec Aᵢ` an immersion for some `i`, and `Spec Aᵢ` is a
closed subscheme of affine space over `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X)
    (hls : IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (j : yoneda.obj U ⟶ affineSpaceOver B S hS X n),
      j ≫ prod.fst = f ∧ IsImmersion B S hS j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_not_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated_not_isImmersion'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088M**: the hypothesis of Stacks 088L that `X` be locally separated cannot be
dropped.

Over a field in which two is invertible there is a finite type morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of
algebraic spaces with `Y` an affine scheme and `X` quasi-separated — so every hypothesis
of Stacks 088L except local separatedness holds — such that `X` is *not* locally separated
and `Y` admits no immersion over `X` into relative affine `n`-space over `X`, for any `n`.

The witness is the one of Stacks 088W, the chart `𝔸¹_k ⟶ 𝔸¹_k/R` of Stacks 02Z1, and the
failure of local separatedness is the corresponding half of Stacks 02Z1.

The remark also raises the question whether Stacks 088L holds without quasi-separatedness.
That is an open question, not a result, and it is not stated here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated_not_isImmersion'
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)
      (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hS).obj Y) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X ∧
      IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of k)) hS f ∧
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ X ∧
      ¬ IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ X ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ affineSpaceOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS X n),
        j ≫ prod.fst = f → ¬ IsImmersion B (Spec (.of k)) hS j
declarations.comment: the failure of 088L without local separatedness; the question the remark raises about quasi-separatedness is open and is not a theorem

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseOpen_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088N.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X`
Noetherian and `f` of finite presentation.  Then `Y` has a dense open subspace which admits,
over `X`, an immersion into relative affine `n`-space over `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_denseOpen_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {Y X : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXN : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor Y),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
      (letI : TopologicalSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS Y) :=
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology B S hS Y;
        DenseRange (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι)) ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : V.toFunctor ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineSpaceOver B S hS X n),
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsImmersion B S hS i ∧
          i ≫ prod.fst = V.ι ≫ f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_of_isOpenImmersion_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088Q.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and
let `j₁ : U ⟶ X₁`, `j₂ : U ⟶ X₂` be open immersions of algebraic spaces over `Y`, with `U`,
`X₁` and `X₂` separated and of finite type over `Y`. There is a commutative diagram
`X₁ ⟵ X₁' ⟶ X ⟵ X₂' ⟶ X₂` under `U` and over `Y`, in which `b_k : X_k' ⟶ X_k` is a
`U`-admissible blowup (`U` being the open subspace `j_k(U)` of `X_k`), `i_k : X_k' ⟶ X` is an
open immersion, and `X` is separated and of finite type over `Y`. Moreover the morphisms
`u_k : U ⟶ X_k'` of the diagram are open immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_of_isOpenImmersion_unconditional
    {Y U X₁ X₂ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y) (j₁ : U ⟶ X₁) (j₂ : U ⟶ X₂)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.1)
    (hj₁ : IsOpenImmersion B S hS j₁.hom) (hj₂ : IsOpenImmersion B S hS j₂.hom)
    (hj : j₁ ≫ f₁ = j₂ ≫ f₂)
    (hUft : IsFiniteType B S hS (j₁ ≫ f₁).hom)
    (hX₁ft : IsFiniteType B S hS f₁.hom) (hX₁sep : IsSeparated B S hS f₁.hom)
    (hX₂ft : IsFiniteType B S hS f₂.hom) (hX₂sep : IsSeparated B S hS f₂.hom) :
    ∃ (X₁' X₂' X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b₁ : X₁' ⟶ X₁) (b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂)
      (i₁ : X₁' ⟶ X) (i₂ : X₂' ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (u₁ : U ⟶ X₁') (u₂ : U ⟶ X₂'),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS ⟨Subfunctor.range j₁.hom, @isOpenSubspace_range_of_open B S hS
        _ _ j₁.hom (mono_of_isOpenImmersion B S hS _ hj₁) U.2 hj₁⟩ b₁ ∧
      IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS ⟨Subfunctor.range j₂.hom, @isOpenSubspace_range_of_open B S hS
        _ _ j₂.hom (mono_of_isOpenImmersion B S hS _ hj₂) U.2 hj₂⟩ b₂ ∧
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS i₁.hom ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS i₂.hom ∧
      IsSeparated B S hS g.hom ∧ IsFiniteType B S hS g.hom ∧
      i₁ ≫ g = b₁ ≫ f₁ ∧ i₂ ≫ g = b₂ ≫ f₂ ∧
      u₁ ≫ b₁ = j₁ ∧ u₂ ≫ b₂ = j₂ ∧ u₁ ≫ i₁ = u₂ ≫ i₂ ∧
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS u₁.hom ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS u₂.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasChowBlowupDiagram_of_isFiniteType_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `U ⊆ X` be an open
subspace. Assume that `U` is quasi-compact, that `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, that
`i : U ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` is an immersion over `Y`, and that `f` is of finite type and separated. Then there
is a commutative diagram
```
        U
     ↙  ↓  ↘  ↘
   X ← X' → Z' → Z
     ↘  ↓  ↙    ↓
        Y  ←  ℙⁿ_Y
```
in which the arrows with source `U` are open immersions, `X' ⟶ X` is a `U`-admissible blowup,
`X' ⟶ Z'` is an open immersion and `Z' ⟶ Y` is proper and representable; more precisely
`Z' ⟶ Z` is a `U`-admissible blowup and `Z ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` is a closed immersion, through which `i`
factors (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasChowBlowupDiagram`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChowBlowupDiagram_of_isFiniteType_of_isSeparated
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.toFunctor)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (n : ℕ) (i : U.toFunctor ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver B S hS Y n) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    (hiY : i ≫ prod.fst = U.ι ≫ f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    HasChowBlowupDiagram B S hS hX f U hU n i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseOpen_hasChowBlowupDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088S.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces
over `S`, with `Y` Noetherian.  Then there are a dense open subspace `U ⊆ X`, an integer `n` and
an immersion `i : U ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` over `Y` for which the diagram of Stacks 088S exists
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasChowBlowupDiagram`): a `U`-admissible blowup `X' ⟶ X`, an open
immersion `X' ⟶ Z'`, a proper representable `Z' ⟶ Y`, a `U`-admissible blowup `Z' ⟶ Z` and a
closed immersion `Z ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y`, with the arrows out of `U` open immersions and everything
commuting.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_denseOpen_hasChowBlowupDiagram (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop Y) :
    ∃ (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U),
      (letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS X) := pointTopology B S hS X;
        DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)) ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : U.toFunctor ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver B S hS Y n),
        IsImmersion B S hS i ∧ i ≫ prod.fst = U.ι ≫ f ∧
          HasChowBlowupDiagram B S hS hX f U hU n i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRelativelyAmple_of_isAdmissibleBlowup_of_projectiveSpaceImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088T.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact algebraic space, `i : Z ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` a closed
immersion, `U ⊆ Z` an open subspace and `b : Z' ⟶ Z` a `U`-admissible blowup, as in Lemmas 088R
and 088S, and let `g = b ≫ (Z ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y ⟶ Y)`. Then

1. `g` is a composition of projective morphisms: `b` is proper and representable and carries a
   `b`-ample invertible module, and `Z ⟶ Y` is proper and representable and carries an ample
   invertible module relative to it;
2. there exists a `g`-ample invertible `𝒪_{Z'}`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativelyAmple_of_isAdmissibleBlowup_of_projectiveSpaceImmersion
    {Y Z Z' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (hY : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) {n : ℕ}
    {hP : B.Contains (projectiveSpaceOver n S)} (D : ProjectiveSpaceImmersion B S hS n hP Z Y)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS Z.1) {b : Z' ⟶ Z} (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b) :
    (IsProper B S hS b.hom ∧ yoneda.relativelyRepresentable b.hom ∧
        ∃ L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z'.1 Z'.2,
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS Z'.1)
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Z'.1 Z'.2).O)).property L ∧
          IsRelativelyAmple B S hS b L) ∧
      (IsProper B S hS D.hom.hom ∧ yoneda.relativelyRepresentable D.hom.hom ∧
        ∃ M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2,
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS Z.1)
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Z.1 Z.2).O)).property M ∧
          IsRelativelyAmple B S hS D.hom M) ∧
      ∃ L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z'.1 Z'.2,
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS Z'.1)
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Z'.1 Z'.2).O)).property L ∧
        IsRelativelyAmple B S hS (b ≫ D.hom) L

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_finiteType_affine_not_immersion_into_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 088W.**  There is a finite-type morphism `Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces with `Y`
an affine scheme and `X` quasi-separated which admits no immersion of `Y`, over `X`, into
relative affine `n`-space over `X` for any `n`.

Take for `X` the quotient `𝔸¹_k/R` of Stacks 02Z1 over a field in which two is invertible,
for `Y` its chart `𝔸¹_k`, and for the morphism the chart itself: it is étale, hence locally
of finite type, and quasi-compact because its source is quasi-compact and `X` is
quasi-separated — that is
`AffineOverAlgebraicSpace.isFiniteType_quotientSpaceMap`.  The nonexistence of an immersion
is `AffineOverAlgebraicSpace.not_isImmersion_affineSpaceOver_quotientSpaceMap`.

Algebraicity and quasi-separatedness of the target come from Stacks 02Z1 in the form in
which the relation of this example is an affine morphism, so Stacks 0265 applies to it with
no effective-descent input:
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient_of_isAffineHom`
rests on the relation being affine, which is Mathlib's `IsAffineHom` instance for a morphism
between affine schemes, and the descent that Stacks 0265 then consumes is effective descent at
the affine monomorphisms locally of finite type, proved outright in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AffineHomCoveringSieveDescent.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_affine_not_immersion_into_affineSpace
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)
      (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hS).obj Y) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS (yoneda.obj Y) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X ∧
      Space.IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of k)) hS f ∧
      Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ X ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ Space.affineSpaceOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS X n),
        j ≫ prod.fst = f → ¬ Space.IsImmersion B (Spec (.of k)) hS j
declarations.comment: the counterexample

declarations.name: valuationRing_quotient_of_prime
declarations.doc: For any prime ideal `p ⊆ A`, the quotient ring `A ⧸ p` is a valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuationRing_quotient_of_prime (𝔭 : Ideal A) [𝔭.IsPrime] :
    ValuationRing (A ⧸ 𝔭)

declarations.name: valuationRing_localization
declarations.doc:
Let `M ⊆ A` be a submonoid with `M ≤ nonZeroDivisors A`, and let `S` be any
commutative ring that is a localization of `A` at `M`. Then `S` is a valuation
ring. (`S` is an integral domain by
`IsLocalization.isDomain_of_le_nonZeroDivisors`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem valuationRing_localization (M : Submonoid A) (hM : M ≤ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization M S] :
    haveI : IsDomain S := IsLocalization.isDomain_of_le_nonZeroDivisors (S := S) hM
    ValuationRing S

declarations.name: valuationRing_localization_atPrime
declarations.doc:
For any prime ideal `p ⊆ A`, the localization `A_p = Localization.AtPrime p`
is a valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuationRing_localization_atPrime (𝔭 : Ideal A) [𝔭.IsPrime] :
    ValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭)

declarations.name: residueValuationSubring_mem_or_inv_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 088Z.** `C` satisfies the valuation criterion of tag 052K: for every
`x : L`, either `x ∈ C` or `x⁻¹ ∈ C`. Via `ValuationSubring.ofSubring` this says exactly
that `C` is a valuation ring with fraction field `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem residueValuationSubring_mem_or_inv_mem (A' : ValuationSubring L)
    (A : ValuationSubring (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A')) (x : L) :
    x ∈ residueValuationSubring A' A ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ residueValuationSubring A' A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAmple_tensor_of_power_sections_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0890.** Let `L` and `M` be invertible modules on a scheme `X`. If `L`
is ample and the nonvanishing opens of the global sections of the positive tensor powers of `M`
cover `X`, then `L ⊗ M` is ample.

At a point `x`, ampleness of `L` gives `n ≥ 1` and `s ∈ Γ(X, L^{⊗ n})` with `x ∈ X_s` and `X_s`
affine, and the cover gives `m ≥ 1` and `t ∈ Γ(X, M^{⊗ m})` with `x ∈ X_t`. The section
`s^m ⊗ t^n` of `(L ⊗ M)^{⊗ nm}`, read through `tensorPowerProductIso`, has nonvanishing open
`X_s ⊓ X_t`, which contains `x` and is affine by Tag 01PV.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_tensor_of_power_sections_cover (X : Scheme.{u}) (L M : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property M]
    (hL : IsAmple X L)
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧
      ∃ t : (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property M (m : ℤ)).sections,
        x ∈ nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace)
          (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
            (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property M (m : ℤ)) t) :
    IsAmple X (tensorProductModule X L M)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isRelativelyAmple_unitModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0891.** The structure sheaf `𝒪_X` is ample relative to `f : X ⟶ S` if and only
if the preimage under `f` of every affine open of `S` is a quasi-affine scheme — that is, if and
only if `f` is quasi-affine.

The quasi-compactness clause of Tag 01VH is not an extra condition on the right-hand side: it
follows from quasi-affineness of the affine preimages by
`Stacks.RelativeAmple.quasiCompact_of_forall_isQuasiAffine_preimage`. On each preimage the
equivalence is Tag 01QE applied to `(f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι^* 𝒪_X`, which
`Stacks.RelativeAmple.pullbackUnitModuleIso` identifies with the structure sheaf of the open
subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_unitModule_iff {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsRelativelyAmple f (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X) ↔
      ∀ V : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.IsQuasiAffine

declarations.name: Stacks.AmplePullbackDatum.exists_threshold_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0892].** For `L` ample relative to `f : X ⟶ S` and `M` an ample
invertible `𝒪_S`-module there is a threshold `n` with `L ⊗ f^* M ^⊗ a` ample on `X` for every
`a ≥ n`.

`Stacks.AmplePullbackPart1.exists_threshold_isAmple` with both of its inputs discharged:
quasi-compactness of `X` by `Stacks.AmplePullbackPart1.compactSpace_of_isAmple`, and the pointwise
datum by `Stacks.AmplePullbackDatum.eventualAffineDatum`. The module is
`Stacks.AmplePullbackPart1.tensorPullbackPowModule`, that is `L ⊗ f^* (M ^⊗ a)`.

The tree's nearest previous statement of part (1),
`Stacks.AmplePullback.exists_isAmple_tensorPullbackPow_of_iso_unitModule`, assumes both
`L ≅ 𝒪_X` and `M ≅ 𝒪_S` and carries no attribute; this statement assumes neither.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_threshold_isAmple (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L)
    (hM : IsAmple S M) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : ℕ, n ≤ a →
      IsAmple X (Stacks.AmplePullbackPart1.tensorPullbackPowModule f L M a)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRatioNoAmple.isAmple_modulePullback_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc: The pullback of an ample invertible module along a quasi-affine morphism is ample.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_of_isQuasiAffineHom [IsQuasiAffineHom f] (hM : IsAmple S M) :
    IsAmple X ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleBridge.isRelativelyAmple_pullbackModule_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
If `L` is ample relative to `f : X ⟶ S` and the square with sides `p : X' ⟶ X`,
`f' : X' ⟶ S'`, `f` and `g : S' ⟶ S` is cartesian, then the pullback of `L` along `p` is ample
relative to `f'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_pullbackModule_of_isPullback {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} {p : X' ⟶ X}
    {f' : X' ⟶ S'} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} (hsq : IsPullback p f' f g) (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f' (pullbackModule p L)
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary cartesian square

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleBaseChange.isRelativelyAmple_modulePullback_unconditional
declarations.doc:
If `L` is ample relative to `f : X ⟶ S`, then its pullback to `X ×_S S'` is ample relative
to the base change `X ×_S S' ⟶ S'`, for any `g : S' ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_modulePullback_unconditional
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple (pullback.snd f g)
      (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule (pullback.fst f g) L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_of_unique_lift_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0894, universally closed part.**
Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `h : U ⟶ X` be quasi-compact morphisms of schemes and suppose that
`h(U)` is dense in `X`. If every valuative square for `f` whose generic-point map factors through
`h` has a unique lift, then `f` is universally closed.
declarations.statement:
public lemma universallyClosed_of_unique_lift_of_denseRange
    {U X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact h] (hdense : DenseRange h)
    (hvaluative : ∀ (D : AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSq f)
      (g : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = D.i₁ → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed f
declarations.comment: universally closed conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_unique_lift_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0894, separated part.**
Under the hypotheses of the refined valuative criterion, a quasi-separated morphism `f` is
separated.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isSeparated_of_unique_lift_of_denseRange
    {U X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact h] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated f]
    (hdense : DenseRange h)
    (hvaluative : ∀ (D : AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSq f)
      (g : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = D.i₁ → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f
declarations.comment: separated conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.refinedValuative_unique_iff_hasLift_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
If `f` is separated, the dotted arrows in the refined valuative criterion are automatically
unique: every valuative square for `f` whose generic-point map factors through `h` has a unique
lift as soon as it has one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem refinedValuative_unique_iff_hasLift_of_isSeparated
    {U X S : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] :
    (∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = D.i₁ → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct)) ↔
    (∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = D.i₁ → D.commSq.HasLift)
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the dotted arrows is guaranteed when f is separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_hasLift_of_denseRange_not_universallyClosed_not_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
The uniqueness of the dotted arrows in the refined valuative criterion
`universallyClosed_of_unique_lift_of_denseRange` cannot be dropped. There are quasi-compact
morphisms `f : X ⟶ S` and `h : U ⟶ X`, with `f` quasi-separated and `h(U)` dense in `X`, such
that every commutative square from `Spec K ⟶ Spec A` (with `A` a valuation ring with fraction
field `K`) whose top map factors through `h` admits a dotted arrow, while `f` is neither
universally closed nor separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hasLift_of_denseRange_not_universallyClosed_not_isSeparated :
    ∃ (U X S : Scheme.{u}) (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S),
      QuasiCompact f ∧ QuasiCompact h ∧ QuasiSeparated f ∧ DenseRange h ∧
      (∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U),
        g ≫ h = D.i₁ → D.commSq.HasLift) ∧
      ¬ UniversallyClosed f ∧ ¬ IsSeparated f
declarations.comment: the uniqueness assumption of Lemma 0894 is necessary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_of_infinitesimal_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A closed immersion can be detected after a closed, point-bijective base change
under a finite-type or finite-presentation hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_of_infinitesimal_baseChange
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    [IsClosedImmersion g] (hg : Function.Bijective g.base)
    [IsClosedImmersion (pullback.snd f g)]
    (hfinite : (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ∨ FinitePresentation g) :
    IsClosedImmersion f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GradedProperCohomology.moduleFinite_gradedCohomologySum_and_exists_isZero_pieceTwistCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0897].** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `B` a finitely generated graded
`A`-algebra, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` a proper morphism and `𝓑 = f^* B̃`. Let `F` be a quasi-coherent
graded `𝓑`-module of finite type. Then

1. for every `p` the graded `B`-module `Hᵖ(X, F) = ⨁ₙ Hᵖ(X, Fₙ)` is a finite `B`-module, and
2. if `L` is an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module there is a `d₀` with
   `Hᵖ(X, Fₙ ⊗ L^{⊗d}) = 0` for all `p > 0` and all `d ≥ d₀`, uniformly in the graded degree
   `n`.

The `B`-module structure in (1) is `HomogeneousSections.gradedCohomologyModule` for the
homogeneous-sections datum of `𝓑 = f^* B̃`: a homogeneous `b ∈ 𝒜ₖ` carries the degree-`n` summand
to the degree-`n + k` summand by `Hᵖ(X, −)` of multiplication by the global section of `𝓑ₖ` that
`b` names.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_gradedCohomologySum_and_exists_isZero_pieceTwistCohomology
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.GradedModule.{u, u, u} (pullbackGradedAlg 𝒜 f))
    (hqc : ∀ n : ℤ, (pieceModule F n).IsQuasicoherent) (hft : F.IsFiniteType) :
    (letI := (pullbackHomogeneousSections 𝒜 f).gradedCohomologyModule F
     ∀ p : ℕ, Module.Finite B (gradedCohomologySum F p)) ∧
      ∀ (L : X.Modules) (_ : IsInvertibleModule X L), IsAmple X L →
        ∃ d₀ : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ∀ n : ℤ,
          IsZero (cohomologyOf X p (pieceTwist F L n (d : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: both parts, at the hypotheses of the source: A Noetherian, B a finitely generated graded A-algebra, f : X → Spec A proper, F a quasi-coherent graded f^* B-tilde-module of finite type, and L ample invertible in part (2); (1) is finiteness of ⨁_n H^p(X, F_n) over B for the degreewise B-action, (2) is H^p(X, F_n ⊗ L^d) = 0 for p > 0, d ≥ d_0 and every degree n, which is H^p(X, F ⊗ L^d) = 0 since cohomology on X commutes with direct sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedImmersion_algebraization_of_isPullback_holds
declarations.doc:
**Algebraization of a cartesian system of closed immersions over the adic thickenings.** Let
`A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, write `S = Spec A` and
`Sₙ = Spec (A / Iⁿ)`, and let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated of finite type; put `Xₙ = X ×_S Sₙ`. Given a
system of morphisms `jₙ : Zₙ ⟶ Xₙ` with transition maps making every square over `Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁`
cartesian, with `j 0 : Z₀ ⟶ X₀` a closed immersion and `Z₀ ⟶ S₀` proper, there is a closed
immersion `g : W ⟶ X` with `W` proper over `S` recovering the system by base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_closedImmersion_algebraization_of_isPullback_holds
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (Z : ℕ → Scheme.{u}) (j : ∀ n, Z n ⟶ adicBaseChange A I f n) (t : ∀ n, Z n ⟶ Z (n + 1))
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (t n) (j n) (j (n + 1)) (adicBaseChangeSucc A I f n))
    (hclosed : IsClosedImmersion (j 0))
    (hproper : IsProper (j 0 ≫ pullback.snd f (adicThickeningι A I 0))) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (g : W ⟶ X) (k : ∀ n, Z n ⟶ W),
      IsClosedImmersion g ∧ IsProper (g ≫ f) ∧
      (∀ n, IsPullback (k n) (j n ≫ pullback.snd f (adicThickeningι A I n)) (g ≫ f)
        (adicThickeningι A I n)) ∧
      (∀ n, k n ≫ g = j n ≫ pullback.fst f (adicThickeningι A I n)) ∧
      ∀ n, t n ≫ k (n + 1) = k n
declarations.comment: at the source's hypotheses and with no further input: A Noetherian and I-adically complete, f : X -> Spec A separated of finite type (IsSeparated, LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact), a system j n : Z n -> X n with cartesian transition squares whose j 0 is a closed immersion (source hypothesis 1) and whose Z 0 -> S 0 is proper (source hypothesis 2), concluding a closed immersion g : W -> X with W proper over Spec A recovering the system by base change. The halg binder of AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedImmersion_algebraization_of_isPullback is discharged here, by AlgebraicGeometry.adicFiniteSystemAlgebraization_of_adicFiniteAlgebraAlgebraization at AlgebraicGeometry.adicFiniteAlgebraAlgebraization_holds, and its hrig binder by AlgebraicGeometry.adicMorphismRigidity

declarations.name: Stacks.GrothendieckAlgebraization.exists_isProper_isAmple_algebraization
declarations.doc:
**Grothendieck's algebraization theorem, [Stacks, Tag 089A].**

Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, let `Xₙ` be a tower of
schemes over the thickenings `Sₙ = Spec (A / Iⁿ⁺¹)` with transitions `iₙ : Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁` whose squares
over `Sₙ ⟶ Sₙ₊₁` are cartesian, and let `ℒₙ` be invertible modules on the `Xₙ` with isomorphisms
`φₙ : iₙ^* ℒₙ₊₁ ≅ ℒₙ`. If `X₀ ⟶ S₀` is proper and `ℒ₀` is ample on `X₀`, then there are a proper
morphism `fX : X ⟶ Spec A`, an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ`, morphisms `kₙ : Xₙ ⟶ X` with
`iₙ ≫ kₙ₊₁ = kₙ` exhibiting every `Xₙ` as `X ×_{Spec A} Sₙ`, and isomorphisms `ℒₙ ≅ ℒ|_{Xₙ}`
compatible with the `φₙ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isProper_isAmple_algebraization (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] {Xn : ℕ → Scheme.{u}}
    (q : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ adicThickening A I n) (i : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ Xn (n + 1))
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (i n) (q n) (q (n + 1)) (adicThickeningSucc A I n))
    (L : ∀ n, (Xn n).Modules) (hL : ∀ n, IsInvertibleModule (Xn n) (L n))
    (φ : ∀ n, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (i n)).obj (L (n + 1)) ≅ L n)
    (hproper : IsProper (q 0))
    (hample : letI := hL 0; IsAmple (Xn 0) (L 0)) :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (fX : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsProper fX ∧
      ∃ (M : X.Modules) (hM : IsInvertibleModule X M), @IsAmple X M hM ∧
        ∃ (k : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ X) (hk : ∀ n, i n ≫ k (n + 1) = k n),
          (∀ n, IsPullback (k n) (q n) fX (adicThickeningι A I n)) ∧
          ∃ e : ∀ n, L n ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (k n)).obj M,
            ∀ n, (φ n).hom ≫ (e n).hom =
              (Scheme.Modules.pullback (i n)).map (e (n + 1)).hom ≫
                (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (i n) (k (n + 1))).hom.app M ≫
                  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (hk n)).hom.app M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_valuativeSquare_toSchemeTheoreticImage
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `Z` be its scheme-theoretic image and let `z` be a point of `|Z|`. There is a valuation
ring `A` with fraction field `K`, a morphism `Spec K ⟶ X` and a morphism `Spec A ⟶ Z` making
the square over the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Z` commute, such that the closed point of
`Spec A` maps to `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuativeSquare_toSchemeTheoreticImage (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (z : points B S hS (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f).toFunctor) :
    ∃ (q : ValuativeSquare (toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS f))
      (w : points B S hS (yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base))),
      pointsToScheme B S hS (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base) w = closedPoint q.R ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base)) q.special w = z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 089C].**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type with scheme-theoretic support `Z ⊆ X`.
Then the inverse image `f⁻¹(Z)` is the scheme-theoretic support of `f^*F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_modulePullback {f : Y ⟶ X} (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J F.val) :
    schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS Y ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F) =
      (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).preimage f.hom
declarations.comment: flatness of the morphism, quasi-coherence of the module and finiteness of its type are the hypotheses of the tag and are all consumed; the affine-chart description of the pullback of modules, Descent Proposition 03DX(2) read across the morphism, is proved, not carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_preimage_of_isFlat_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B`, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` and let `V ⊆ Y` be an open subspace whose inclusion is quasi-compact.
If `V` is scheme-theoretically dense in `Y`, then `f⁻¹V` is scheme-theoretically dense in
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_preimage_of_isFlat_of_isQuasiCompact
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι)
    (hdense : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS V) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense B S hS (V.preimage f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isFlat_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism `g : V ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over `S` commutes with flat base change: for a flat `f : X ⟶ Y`, the
scheme-theoretic image of `V ×_Y X ⟶ X` is the inverse image along `f` of the scheme-theoretic
image of `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_pullback_snd_of_isFlat_of_isQuasiCompact
    {X Y V : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : V ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hg : IsQuasiCompact B S hS g.hom) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS (pullback.snd g.hom f.hom) =
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS g.hom).preimage f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_valuationRing_extension_lift_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 089F.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let
`Spec A ⟶ Y` be a morphism with `A` a valuation ring. If the closed point of `Spec A` maps to
a point of `|Y|` in the image of `|X| → |Y|`, then there is an extension of valuation rings
`A ⟶ A'` and a commutative square filling in `Spec A' ⟶ X` over `Spec A ⟶ Y`.

The point of `|X|` above the closed point is produced by a chart `U ⟶ X ×_Y Spec A` of the
fibre product (Stacks 03H4, 03H5). The chart is flat over `Spec A` because flatness is stable
under base change (Stacks 03MO) and may be read on étale charts, so the induced homomorphism
`A ⟶ 𝒪_{U, u}` is flat and local, hence faithfully flat; a prime of the stalk contracting to
the zero ideal of `A` therefore exists, and factoring the resulting map to its fraction field
through a valuation subring gives `A'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuationRing_extension_lift_of_isFlat
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V ≅ Spec (.of A))
    (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj V))
    (hp : e.hom ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p.value
      (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.carrier)) = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    (himage : ∃ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x =
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) g (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj V))) :
    ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : IsDomain A') (_ : ValuationRing A') (ι : A →+* A'),
      ValuationRing.IsExtension ι ∧
      ∃ (V' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (e' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V' ≅ Spec (.of A'))
        (j : V' ⟶ V) (lift : yoneda.obj V' ⟶ X),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j ≫ e.hom =
          e'.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι) ∧
        lift ≫ f = yoneda.map j ≫ g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_refinedValuativeCriterion
declarations.doc:
The refined valuative criterion makes `f` universally closed when the quasi-compact map `h`
has dense image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyClosed_of_refinedValuativeCriterion
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {U X Y : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hh : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS h)
    (hdense : letI : TopologicalSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS X) :=
        pointTopology B S hS X
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS U h))
    (hunique : ∀ (q : ValuativeSquare f)
      (g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = q.generic → Subsingleton q.Lift)
    (hexists : ∀ (q : ValuativeSquare f)
      (g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = q.generic →
        ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: universally closed conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_refinedValuativeCriterion
declarations.doc: With quasi-separatedness, the same refined valuative criterion makes `f` separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_of_refinedValuativeCriterion
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {U X Y : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hh : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS h)
    (hqs : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hdense : letI : TopologicalSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS X) :=
        pointTopology B S hS X
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS U h))
    (hunique : ∀ (q : ValuativeSquare f)
      (g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = q.generic → Subsingleton q.Lift)
    (hexists : ∀ (q : ValuativeSquare f)
      (g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U),
      g ≫ h = q.generic →
        ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: separated conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasChowSchemeCover_of_isSeparated_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Chow's lemma for algebraic spaces, [Stacks, Tag 089J].**

Let `A` be a ring whose spectrum lies in the chosen big fppf site, and let `X` be an algebraic
space over `Spec A` whose structure morphism is separated and of finite type. Then there is an
object `X'` of the site — a scheme over `Spec A` — and a proper surjective morphism from the
presheaf it represents to `X`, such that the structure morphism of `X'` to `Spec A` is
H-quasi-projective.

The morphism `f` quantified over is the structure morphism of `X` and nothing else: its target
is the presheaf represented by the base, which is terminal by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTerminal_yoneda_obj_base`.

The proof is Stacks 089J's. An affine surjective étale chart exists by Stacks 03H6; a separated
algebraic space over an affine base is reasonable by Stacks 03JX, so the fibre degrees of that
chart are bounded, by the degree stratification of Stacks 07S8; and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasChowSchemeCover_of_chart_fibre_le` performs the induction on that
bound.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChowSchemeCover_of_isSeparated_isFiniteType
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (hA : B.Contains (Spec A))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec A) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec A) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec A) hA f) (hft : IsFiniteType B (Spec A) hA f) :
    HasChowSchemeCover B (Spec A) hA X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chowDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Chow's lemma for algebraic spaces, [Stacks, Tag 089L].** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of finite
type. Then there are algebraic spaces `X'` and `X̄'` and a commutative diagram
`X ⟵ X' ⟶ X̄' ⟶ Y` over `Y` in which `X' ⟶ X` is proper and surjective, `X' ⟶ X̄'` is an open
immersion and `X̄' ⟶ Y` is proper and representable.

Every quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space has a finite surjective scheme cover
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsFiniteSurjectiveSchemeCover_of_isQuasiCompactSpace`), so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chowDiagram_of_forall_finiteSchemeCover` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chowDiagram (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y)
    (hfsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hfft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ (X' Xbar : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
      (_hXbar : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Xbar) (q : X' ⟶ X) (j : X' ⟶ Xbar) (g : Xbar ⟶ Y),
      IsProper B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS q ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS j ∧
        IsProper B S hS g ∧ yoneda.relativelyRepresentable g ∧ q ≫ f = j ≫ g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isProper_isSurjective_isImmersion_projectiveSpace
declarations.doc:
**Chow's lemma over a quasi-compact separated base, [Stacks, Tag 089M].** Let `S` be a
scheme and `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, separated and of finite type,
with `Y` separated and quasi-compact. Then there are an algebraic space `X'`, a proper surjective
morphism `q : X' ⟶ X` and an immersion `i : X' ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` with `q ≫ f = i ≫ (ℙⁿ_Y ⟶ Y)`.

Relative projective space `ℙⁿ_Y` is the fibre product `Y ×_S ℙⁿ_S` over the presheaf represented
by `S`, which is terminal, with `ℙⁿ_S` the object `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.projectiveSpaceSiteObj`
of the site; `ℙⁿ_Y ⟶ Y` is the first projection. "Separated" for `Y` is the absolute notion of
[Stacks, Tag 03BS].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_isSurjective_isImmersion_projectiveSpace
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hfft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYsep : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Y) (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (hP : B.Contains (projectiveSpaceOver n S))
      (X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (q : X' ⟶ X)
      (i : X' ⟶ pullback ((isTerminal_yoneda_obj_base B S hS).from Y)
        ((isTerminal_yoneda_obj_base B S hS).from
          (yoneda.obj (projectiveSpaceSiteObj B S hS n hP)))),
      IsProper B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS q ∧ IsImmersion B S hS i ∧
        q ≫ f = i ≫ pullback.fst _ _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.abelian_coherentAdicSystems
declarations.doc:
**The category `Coh(F, 𝓘)` of coherent adic systems on a Noetherian algebraic space is
abelian.**

It is preadditive, has finite products, kernels and cokernels, and every monomorphism is a kernel
and every epimorphism a cokernel.
declarations.statement: def abelian_coherentAdicSystems : Abelian (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘)
declarations.comment: the category is abelian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentAdicInverseImage_exact
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Stacks 089P: the inverse image along a flat morphism of Noetherian algebraic
spaces is exact.**  For a flat morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of Noetherian algebraic spaces and a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_X`, the functor
`f^* : Coh(X, 𝓘) ⥤ Coh(X', f⁻¹𝓘 · 𝒪_{X'})` preserves finite limits and finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentAdicInverseImage_exact (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) :
    exactFunctor (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘)
      (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X'.1 X'.2 (pullbackIdealImage B S hS f 𝓘))
      (coherentAdicInverseImage B S hS f 𝓘 hN'.2.2)
declarations.comment: part (3): the inverse image along a flat morphism of Noetherian algebraic spaces is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_iff_forall_exact_coherentAdicChartRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks 089P: exactness in `Coh(X, 𝓘)` can be checked étale locally.**  For a
Noetherian algebraic space `X`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_X` and an étale covering
of `X` by affine charts `U i`, a short complex `E ⟶ G ⟶ H` of `Coh(X, 𝓘)` is exact exactly when
its restriction `E|_{U i} ⟶ G|_{U i} ⟶ H|_{U i}` to `Coh(U i, 𝓘 · 𝒪_{U i})` is exact for every
`i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_forall_exact_coherentAdicChartRestriction {I : Type v}
    (U : I → SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (hU : ∀ i, IsAffine (chartScheme (U i)))
    (hcov : IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun i => (chartSpace B S hS X (U i)).1)
      (fun i => (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)).hom))
    (T : ShortComplex (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘)) :
    T.Exact ↔ ∀ i, (coherentAdicRestrictToChartShortComplex B S hS X 𝓘 hZ hN (U i)
      (pullbackIdealImage B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)) 𝓘) (hU i)
      (idealPowerMultipleCompatible_pullbackIdealImage B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)) 𝓘)
      T).Exact
declarations.comment: part (2): exactness can be checked on an étale covering by affine charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentAdicSystems_abelian_and_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 089P.**  Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S` and `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_X` a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.

1. `Coh(X, 𝓘)` is abelian.
2. Exactness in `Coh(X, 𝓘)` can be checked étale locally: on every étale covering of `X` by
   affine charts `U i`, a short complex is exact exactly when its restrictions to the categories
   `Coh(U i, 𝓘 · 𝒪_{U i})` are.
3. For every flat morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of Noetherian algebraic spaces the inverse image
   `f^* : Coh(X, 𝓘) ⥤ Coh(X', f⁻¹𝓘 · 𝒪_{X'})` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentAdicSystems_abelian_and_exact :
    Nonempty (Abelian (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘)) ∧
    (∀ {I : Type v} (U : I → SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (hU : ∀ i, IsAffine (chartScheme (U i))),
      IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun i => (chartSpace B S hS X (U i)).1)
          (fun i => (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)).hom) →
        ∀ T : ShortComplex (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘),
          T.Exact ↔ ∀ i, (coherentAdicRestrictToChartShortComplex B S hS X 𝓘 hZ hN (U i)
            (pullbackIdealImage B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)) 𝓘) (hU i)
            (idealPowerMultipleCompatible_pullbackIdealImage B S hS
              (chartToSpace B S hS X (U i)) 𝓘) T).Exact) ∧
    (∀ {X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X' ⟶ X) (hN' : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X'.1),
      IsFlat B S hS f.hom →
        exactFunctor (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘)
          (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS X'.1 X'.2 (pullbackIdealImage B S hS f 𝓘))
          (coherentAdicInverseImage B S hS f 𝓘 hN'.2.2))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_iff_epi_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 089Q.** A morphism between finite locally free sheaves of modules of the same
rank is an isomorphism if and only if it is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_iff_epi_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    [∀ U : Opens X, HasWeakSheafify ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [∀ U : Opens X, ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective
      AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (StrictlyPerfect.structureSheafOfRings X)} (r : ℕ)
    [@AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank _ _ _
      (StrictlyPerfect.structureSheafOfRings X) _ _ F r]
    [@AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank _ _ _
      (StrictlyPerfect.structureSheafOfRings X) _ _ G r] (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsIso f ↔ Epi f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.functor_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
