declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B0.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`,
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` a proper morphism of algebraic spaces and `F` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then
`Hᵖ(X, F) ⟶ lim_n Hᵖ(X, F / Iⁿ F)` is an isomorphism for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit [IsAdicComplete I A] :
    Function.Bijective
      (C1573.cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit (baseRingHom A B hA X.1 X.2) F I p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit_bijective_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B0.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring (`[IsNoetherianRing A]`), `I ⊆ A` an ideal
such that `A` is `I`-adically complete (`[IsAdicComplete I A]`), `f : X ⟶ Spec A` a proper
morphism of algebraic spaces and `F` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then for every `p ≥ 0` the
canonical map `Hᵖ(X, F) ⟶ lim_n Hᵖ(X, F / Iⁿ F)` is bijective, i.e.
`Hᵖ(X, F) = lim_n Hᵖ(X, F / Iⁿ F)`.

The objects in the statement, with the files that define them:
* `B : BigFppfSite` is a big fppf site and `hA : B.Contains (Spec A)` says that `Spec A` is one of
  its schemes; `AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec A) hA`
  (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Category.lean`) is the category of algebraic spaces over
  `Spec A`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseObject A B hA`
  (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FormalAlgebraization.lean`) is `Spec A` itself as an
  object of the big fppf site over `Spec A` (the identity of `Spec A`), and
  `AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace` (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SchemeAsSpace.lean`)
  regards it as an algebraic space, so `f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)` is a morphism
  `X ⟶ Spec A` of algebraic spaces over `Spec A`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsProper`
  (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/UniversallyClosed.lean`, Stacks 03ZM) is properness of a
  morphism of algebraic spaces: separated, of finite type and universally closed.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Modules` (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/RingedSite.lean`) is
  the category of `𝒪_X`-modules on the small étale site of `X`, and
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoherent`
  (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/CoherentModules.lean`, Stacks 07UA) says that such a
  module is coherent.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseRingHom A B hA X.1 X.2`
  (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SmallEtaleCohomology.lean`) is the canonical ring map
  from `A` to the global functions of `X`, through which `A` acts on cohomology.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit φ F I p` (the imported module)
  is the `A`-linear map `Hᵖ(X, F) ⟶ lim_n Hᵖ(X, F / Iⁿ F)` whose `n`-th component is the map on
  `Hᵖ` induced by the projection `F ⟶ F / Iⁿ F`.  Here `Hᵖ(X, -)` is the `p`-th right derived
  functor of global sections on `𝒪_X`-modules, as an `A`-module along `φ`
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cohomologyRes`,
  `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/IdealPowerCohomologyReesFinite.lean`); `F / Iⁿ F` is the
  cokernel of the inclusion of the submodule `Iⁿ F ⊆ F`, the image of multiplication by the
  elements of `Iⁿ` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealQuotient`,
  `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/IdealMultipleModule.lean`); and the limit is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.cohomologyIdealQuotientLimit` (same file as the map), the
  `A`-module of compatible families of the tower `n ↦ Hᵖ(X, F / Iⁿ F)` under the maps induced by
  `F / Iⁿ F ⟶ F / Iᵐ F`, `m ≤ n` (`Stacks.IntertwinedFiltration.towerLimit`,
  `StacksFrontier/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/IntertwinedFiltration.lean`).

The proof is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.bijective_cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit`: `Hᵖ(X, F)`
is a finite `A`-module (Stacks 08AS), hence `I`-adically complete, and the theorem on formal
functions (Stacks 08AZ) identifies its completion with the limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit_bijective_of_isAdicComplete {B : BigFppfSite.{u}}
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))}
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA} (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA))
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2)
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2 F] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] (p : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (C1573.cohomologyToIdealQuotientLimit (baseRingHom A B hA X.1 X.2) F I p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionIsoLimitOfQuotientsOverCompletion_geometricStalk
declarations.doc:
**The theorem on formal functions at a geometric point, [Stacks, Tag 08B1].**

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y` locally Noetherian, let
`F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module, `ȳ` a geometric point of `Y`, and let
`X_n = Spec (𝒪_{Y, ȳ} / 𝔪 ⁿ) ×_Y X` be the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the geometric fibre
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_geometricInfinitesimalNeighbourhood`), with `F_n` the
pullback of `F`.  Then

`(R ᵖ f_* F)_ȳ ^∧ ≅ lim_n H ᵖ (X_n, F_n)`

as modules over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ} ^∧`: there is an isomorphism of modules over
`R = Γ(Spec 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}, 𝒪) ≅ 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` from the `𝔪`-adic completion of the stalk to the limit,
whose `n`-th component on the image of the stalk is the map `(R ᵖ f_* F)_ȳ ⟶ H ᵖ (X_n, F_n)`, and
which is linear over the completion `R ^∧`, acting on `lim_n H ᵖ (X_n, F_n)` through
`R ^∧ ⟶ R / 𝔪 ⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completionIsoLimitOfQuotientsOverCompletion_geometricStalk (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F) (p : ℕ) :
    CompletionIsoLimitOfQuotientsOverCompletion (maximalIdeal Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
        (etaleLocalRingSpecObject (y := y) hY), ⊤))
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (etaleLocalRingSpecFunctionsEquiv y hY).toRingHom).obj
        (geometricModuleStalk B S hS Y y (moduleHigherPushforward B S hS f F p)))
      (fun n => geometricInfinitesimalNeighbourhoodCohomology f y hY F p n)
      (geometricInfinitesimalNeighbourhoodTransition f y hY F hF.toIsQuasicoherentOnSite p)
      (geometricInfinitesimalNeighbourhoodProj f y hY hf F hF.toIsQuasicoherentOnSite p)
      (geometricInfinitesimalNeighbourhoodCohomology_smul_eq_zero f y hY F
        hF.toIsQuasicoherentOnSite p)
declarations.comment: Y locally Noetherian, f proper, F coherent: the restriction maps assemble into an isomorphism (R^p f_* F)_ȳ^∧ ≅ lim_n H^p(X_n, F_n) of modules over the completion of 𝒪_{Y,ȳ}, deduced from Tag 08AZ by flat base change to Spec 𝒪_{Y,ȳ}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_of_isClosedImmersion_pullback_snd_of_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `i : Y' ⟶ Y` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`.
If `i` is a closed immersion, bijective on points, if the base change of `f` along `i` is a
closed immersion, and if either `f` is of finite type or `i` is of finite presentation, then `f`
is a closed immersion.

This is the registered form of Stacks 08B2. The 07VU step of the source's proof is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isClosedImmersion_of_bijective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_isClosedImmersion_pullback_snd_of_bijective
    {X Y Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : Y' ⟶ Y) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i)
    (hbij : Function.Bijective (pointsMap B S hS Y' i))
    (hbc : IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f i))
    (hfin : IsFiniteType B S hS f ∨ IsFinitePresentation B S hS i) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, with hypotheses (1)-(4) as in the source: `hi` (1), `hbij` (2), `hbc` (3) and `hfin` (4); the 07VU step of the proof is the proved `isRepresentable_of_isClosedImmersion_of_bijective`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_iff_epi_app_zero
declarations.doc:
A map of coherent adic systems on an algebraic space is surjective in `Coh(F, 𝓘)` exactly when
its component at the lowest level is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_iff_epi_app_zero {E E' : CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘} (f : E ⟶ E') :
    Epi f ↔ Epi (f.hom.app (op 0))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
The completion functor `Coh(𝒪_F) ⟶ Coh(F, 𝓘)` on a locally Noetherian algebraic space, for a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘`, sending a coherent `𝒪_F`-module `𝓖` to the coherent `𝓘`-adic
system `𝓖^∧ = (𝓖 / 𝓘 ^ (n + 1) 𝓖)_n`.
declarations.statement:
def completionFunctor
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (hI : 𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF ⥤ CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteColimits_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5, right exactness.**  The completion functor `Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` preserves
finite colimits.

No Noetherian hypothesis is needed: the term at `n` of a completion is the reflection of a
coherent module onto the modules annihilated by `𝓘 ^ (n + 1)`, and every term of a coherent
`𝓘`-adic system is so annihilated.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesFiniteColimits_completionFunctor :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI)
declarations.comment: right exactness: preservation of finite colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesMonomorphisms_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5, preservation of monomorphisms.**  On a Noetherian algebraic space the
completion functor `Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` carries a monomorphism to a monomorphism.

Let `f : M ⟶ N` be a monomorphism and let `c` be the Artin-Rees constant of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_completionTermProjection_eq_zero_of_mono`.  A morphism into
`M ^ ∧` killed by `f ^ ∧` is tested level by level; at level `n` the transition map down from
level `n + c` is an epimorphism, so it suffices to kill the morphism at level `n + c` after that
transition, and the quotient projection out of `M` is an epimorphism, so that in turn is the
Artin-Rees step.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesMonomorphisms_completionFunctor (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) :
    (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).PreservesMonomorphisms
declarations.comment: preservation of monomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5, left exactness.**  On a Noetherian algebraic space the completion functor
`Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` of Stacks 08B4 preserves finite limits.

It preserves homology by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesHomology_completionFunctor`, given
that every monomorphism of `Coh(F, 𝓘)` is a kernel; and that holds by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormalMonoCategory_coherentAdicSystems`, from part (1) of Stacks 089P,
since `𝓘` is cartesian on the affine charts by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`. The hypotheses are
the source's own: `F` is Noetherian — which is where Artin–Rees, Stacks 07UL, enters through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesMonomorphisms_completionFunctor` — and `𝓘` is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI)
declarations.comment: left exactness: the completion functor preserves finite limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5.**  On a Noetherian algebraic space the completion functor
`Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` of Stacks 08B4 is exact.

Right exactness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteColimits_completionFunctor` and needs
no Noetherian hypothesis; left exactness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_completionFunctor (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) :
    exactFunctor (CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘)
      (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI)
declarations.comment: exactness: the completion functor is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5, left exactness.**  On a Noetherian algebraic space the completion functor
`Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` of Stacks 08B4 preserves finite limits.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor`.
declarations.statement: alias preservesFiniteLimits_completionFunctor_of_isNoetherian
declarations.comment: left exactness: the completion functor preserves finite limits, over the source's own hypotheses that the algebraic space is Noetherian and the sheaf of ideals quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_completionFunctor_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B5.**  On a Noetherian algebraic space the completion functor
`Coh(𝒪_F) ⥤ Coh(F, 𝓘)` of Stacks 08B4 is exact.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_completionFunctor`.
declarations.statement: alias exactFunctor_completionFunctor_of_isNoetherian
declarations.comment: exactness of the completion functor over the source's own hypotheses that the algebraic space is Noetherian and the sheaf of ideals quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomSmallAdicEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B6.**  Let `F` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let
`𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_F` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and let `M`, `N` be coherent `𝒪_F`-modules.  Put
`𝓗 = 𝓗om_{𝒪_F}(M, N)`.  Then

`lim_n H⁰(F, 𝓗 / 𝓘 ^ n 𝓗) = Mor((M / 𝓘 ^ n M), (N / 𝓘 ^ n N))`,

the inverse limit of the global sections of the ideal-power quotients of `𝓗` being the
morphisms of inverse systems of `𝒪_F`-modules from the completion of `M` to the completion of
`N`; since `Coh(F, 𝓘)` is a full subcategory of the inverse systems of `𝒪_F`-modules, this is
`Mor_{Coh(F, 𝓘)}(M^∧, N^∧)`.  Here `𝓗` is the internal hom at the module universe of the
schemes, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomSmall`, whose universe lift is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHom`.  The source asks for `F` Noetherian; local
Noetherianity is all that is used.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleInternalHomSmallAdicEquiv :
    adicSections B S hS F hF
        (fun n => smallEtaleAdicQuotient B S hS F hF 𝓘 (n + 1)
          (smallEtaleInternalHomSmall B S hS F hF M N))
        (fun n => smallEtaleAdicQuotientTransition B S hS F hF 𝓘 (n + 1)
          (smallEtaleInternalHomSmall B S hS F hF M N)) ≃
      (smallEtaleAdicQuotientSystem B S hS F hF 𝓘 M ⟶
        smallEtaleAdicQuotientSystem B S hS F hF 𝓘 N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_adicSectionsMap_of_isSeqProIso
declarations.doc:
**A pro-isomorphism of inverse systems of `𝒪_F`-modules induces a bijection on the inverse
limits of their global sections.**  Pro-isomorphic systems therefore have the same
`lim_n H⁰(F, -)`, although they are nowhere isomorphic level by level.  The chartwise statement
is `bijective_adicSectionsMapAt_of_isSeqProIso` and the passage to global sections is the étale
descent of `bijective_adicSectionsMap_of_bijective_adicSectionsMapAt`.

This is the step by which Stacks 08B6 identifies its left-hand side
`lim_n H⁰(F, 𝓗 / 𝓘 ^ n 𝓗)` with `lim_n H⁰(F, 𝓗om(M, N / 𝓘 ^ n N))`: the comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomAdicComparisonApp` between those two systems is
not an isomorphism at any single level, and the source's Noetherian and coherence hypotheses
enter only to make it a pro-isomorphism.  Once that is known, this theorem turns it into the
identity of inverse limits, with no hypothesis on the systems at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_adicSectionsMap_of_isSeqProIso
    (hβ : ∀ n : ℕ, trX n ≫ β n = β (n + 1) ≫ trY n)
    (hpro : IsSeqProIso B S hS F hF X Y trX trY β) :
    Function.Bijective (adicSectionsMap B S hS F hF X Y trX trY β hβ)
declarations.comment:
the pro-isomorphism step: pro-isomorphic inverse systems of `𝒪_F`-modules have
the same inverse limit of global sections, which is what identifies the tag's two limits
`lim H⁰(𝓗 / 𝓘 ^ n 𝓗)` and `lim H⁰(𝓗om(M, N / 𝓘 ^ n N))` from a pro-isomorphism of the
comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomAdicEquivOfNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B6.**  Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_X` be
a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and let `M`, `N` be coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.  Put
`𝓗 = 𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(M, N)`.  Then

`lim_n H⁰(X, 𝓗 / 𝓘 ^ n 𝓗) = Mor((M / 𝓘 ^ n M), (N / 𝓘 ^ n N))`,

the inverse limit of the global sections of the ideal-power quotients of `𝓗` being the morphisms
of inverse systems of `𝒪_X`-modules from the completion of `M` to the completion of `N`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomAdicEquiv` with its assumed chartwise input
`h0882` discharged, so the hypotheses are exactly the source's: Noetherianness of `X`,
quasi-coherence of `𝓘`, coherence of `M` and of `N`.

The tag is registered here, bare, because this is where the source's identity is proved outright
under the source's own hypotheses and nothing else.  The two step registrations in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/CoherentAdicInternalHomProIso.lean` carry clause strings
naming the pro-isomorphism step and the morphism step.  No registration is placed on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHomAdicEquiv` itself, which takes `h0882` as a
hypothesis; this declaration is that one with `h0882` proved.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleInternalHomAdicEquivOfNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hI : 𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hM : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M) (hN : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 N) :
    adicSections B S hS X.1 X.2
        (fun n => smallEtaleAdicQuotient B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘 (n + 1)
          (smallEtaleInternalHom B S hS X.1 X.2 M N))
        (fun n => smallEtaleAdicQuotientTransition B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘 (n + 1)
          (smallEtaleInternalHom B S hS X.1 X.2 M N)) ≃
      (smallEtaleAdicQuotientSystem B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘 M ⟶
        smallEtaleAdicQuotientSystem B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘 N)

registrations.name: bijective_smallEtaleInternalHomAdicSection
registrations.comment:
the morphism step of the identity: morphisms of the inverse systems of
ideal-power quotients are exactly the compatible families of global sections of the internal
homs into those quotients, so that `Mor((M / 𝓘 ^ n M), (N / 𝓘 ^ n N))` is
`lim_n H⁰(F, 𝓗om(M, N / 𝓘 ^ n N))`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ExistenceSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B7.** The standing data of Grothendieck's existence theorem: a Noetherian
ring `A` complete with respect to an ideal `I`, together with a separated algebraic space
`X` of finite type over `Spec A`.
declarations.statement: structure ExistenceSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_idealPowerQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B8, the support condition.** The terms `M / 𝓘 ^ n M` of the completion of a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M` whose support is proper over `Y` again have support proper over `Y`.

A coherent module is of finite type, and `M / 𝓘 ^ n M` is a quotient of `M`, so this is the
quotient clause of Stacks 0CZK part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_idealPowerQuotient (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (𝓘 : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).O))).Submodule)
    (n : ℕ) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (hMcoh : IsCoherent B S hS X hX M)
    (hM : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj (idealPowerQuotient B S hS X hX 𝓘 n M))
declarations.comment: the support condition, by which equation 76.42.2.1 restricts to the two full subcategories constructed below: the completion M / 𝓘 ^ n M of a coherent module with support proper over the base again has support proper over the base. The arrow itself is the completion functor of Stacks 08B4, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionFunctor`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionFunctorProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B8, the arrow.**  The completion functor
`Coh_{support proper over Y}(𝒪_X) ⟶ Coh_{support proper over Y}(X, 𝓘)` of
equation 76.42.5.1, the restriction of the completion functor of Stacks 08B4 to the full
subcategories of objects whose support is proper over `Y`.

It is well defined because the completion of a coherent module with support proper over `Y`
has all of its terms supported inside the support of the module, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_idealPowerQuotient`.
declarations.statement:
def completionFunctorProperOver
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (hI : 𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    CoherentModulesProperOver B S hS hX hY g hg ⥤
      CoherentAdicSystemsProperOver B S hS hX hY g hg 𝓘
declarations.comment: the arrow, restricting the completion functor of Stacks 08B4 to the two full subcategories of objects with support proper over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_completionFunctor_map_of_isProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B9, the bijection on morphisms.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with
respect to an ideal `I`, let `X` be an algebraic space with a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` locally of finite type, and let `F`, `G` be coherent `𝒪_X`-modules such that the
intersection of their supports is proper over `Spec A`.  Then completion along `I 𝒪_X`
(Stacks 08B4) is a bijection
`Mor_{Coh(𝒪_X)}(F, G) ⟶ Mor_{Coh(X, I 𝒪_X)}(F^∧, G^∧)`.

The source's Situation 08B7 has `X` separated and of finite type over `Spec A`, so locally
Noetherian (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType` with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_baseObject` supply the `Fact`
instance the completion functor of Stacks 08B4 is stated with); neither separatedness nor
quasi-compactness is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_completionFunctor_map_of_isProperOver [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (F G : CoherentModules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2)
    (hcl : IsClosed (supportOfSheaf B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F.obj) ∩
      supportOfSheaf B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G.obj)))
    (hp : IsProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf _ hcl) :
    letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf
    Function.Bijective ((completionFunctor B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2
      (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
      (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).map
        (X := F) (Y := G))
declarations.comment: the bijection on morphisms; the source's Situation 08B7 asks X separated of finite type over Spec A, of which only local finite type is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionFunctorProperOverFullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B9, full faithfulness.**  In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_completionFunctor_map_of_isProperOver`, the completion functor
`Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_X) ⟶ Coh_{support proper over A}(X, I 𝒪_X)` of Stacks 08B8 is
fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
def completionFunctorProperOverFullyFaithful [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf
    (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1
      (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1 X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf
      (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
      (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: in particular, the completion functor of 08B8 is fully faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_completionFunctor_map_and_fullyFaithful_of_isProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08B9.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I` and let
`X` be an algebraic space with a morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec A` locally of finite type.

1. For coherent `𝒪_X`-modules `F`, `G` such that the intersection of their supports is proper
   over `Spec A`, completion along `I 𝒪_X` (Stacks 08B4) is a bijection
   `Mor_{Coh(𝒪_X)}(F, G) ⟶ Mor_{Coh(X, I 𝒪_X)}(F^∧, G^∧)`.
2. In particular, the completion functor
   `Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_X) ⟶ Coh_{support proper over A}(X, I 𝒪_X)` of Stacks 08B8 is
   fully faithful.

The source's Situation 08B7 has `X` separated and of finite type over `Spec A`, so locally
Noetherian (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject` supplies the
`Fact` instance the completion functor of Stacks 08B4 is stated with); neither separatedness nor
quasi-compactness is used.  The properness of `Supp F ∩ Supp G` is stated in the curried form
`IsProperOver … hcl` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsProperOver`, which takes the closedness `hcl`
of the subset as an argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_completionFunctor_map_and_fullyFaithful_of_isProperOver
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf
    (∀ (F G : CoherentModules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2)
      (hcl : IsClosed
        (supportOfSheaf B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F.obj) ∩
          supportOfSheaf B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G.obj))),
      IsProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf _ hcl →
      Function.Bijective ((completionFunctor B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2
        (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
        (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).map
          (X := F) (Y := G))) ∧
    Nonempty (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1
      (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1 X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf
      (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
      (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).FullyFaithful

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.bijective_completionFunctor_map_of_isProperOver
registrations.comment: the bijection on morphisms; the source's Situation 08B7 asks X separated of finite type over Spec A, of which only local finite type is used

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.completionFunctorProperOverFullyFaithful
registrations.comment: in particular, the completion functor of 08B8 is fully faithful

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_pow_le_annihilator_ker_and_coker_mapQ_pow_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08BA.** For a linear map `φ : M → N` of `I`-adically complete
modules, one positive power of `K` annihilates the kernels and the cokernels of all the
reductions `M / Iⁿ⁺¹ M → N / Iⁿ⁺¹ N` if and only if one positive power of `K` annihilates
`Ker(φ)` and `Coker(φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_ker_and_coker_mapQ_pow_iff (I K : Ideal A)
    [IsAdicComplete I M] [IsHausdorff I N] (φ : M →ₗ[A] N) :
    (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A
          ↑(LinearMap.ker (Submodule.mapQ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
            (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A N)) φ
            (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top _ φ))) ∧
        K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A
          (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range (Submodule.mapQ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
            (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A N)) φ
            (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top _ φ)))) ↔
      ∃ t : ℕ, 0 < t ∧ K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A ↑(LinearMap.ker φ) ∧
        K ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A (N ⧸ LinearMap.range φ)
declarations.comment: equivalence of the annihilation conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BA, the notion.** A map `α : (F_n) ⟶ (G_n)` of inverse systems of `𝒪_X`-modules
on an algebraic space is a *map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝓚`* if
one integer `t ≥ 1` works for every level: `𝓚 ^ t` annihilates `Ker(α_n)` and `Coker(α_n)` for
all `n`. This is condition (1) of the remark; its equivalence with condition (2), which is what
makes the notion the one the remark names, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_tfae`.

The systems are indexed from `0`, the term at `n` being the source's term at `n + 1`; the
condition quantifies over every level, so this is the source's condition for all `n ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
def IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower
    (𝓚 : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))).Submodule)
    {E E' : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (α : E ⟶ E') : Prop
declarations.comment: the notion named by the remark: condition (1), one power of K annihilating every levelwise kernel and cokernel

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08BA.** Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let
`𝓘, 𝓚 ⊆ 𝒪_X` be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals and let `α : (F_n) ⟶ (G_n)` be a morphism of
`Coh(X, 𝓘)`. For a surjective étale morphism `U = Spec(A) ⟶ X` write `I, K ⊆ A` for the ideals of
`𝓘|_U, 𝓚|_U` and `α_U : M ⟶ N` for the map of finite `A^∧`-modules attached to `α|_U` by Stacks
087W. The following are equivalent:

1. there is an integer `t ≥ 1` such that `Ker(α_n)` and `Coker(α_n)` are annihilated by `𝓚 ^ t`
   for all `n`;
2. for any such `U`, the modules `Ker(α_U)` and `Coker(α_U)` are annihilated by `K ^ t` for some
   integer `t ≥ 1`;
3. for some such `U`, the modules `Ker(α_U)` and `Coker(α_U)` are annihilated by `K ^ t` for some
   integer `t ≥ 1`.

A chart `U ⟶ X` is an object of the small étale site of `X`, so étale; "`U = Spec(A)`" is
affineness of its underlying scheme; surjectivity is surjectivity after every representable base
change. Such a chart exists, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_isNoetherianAffineChart`, which is what makes (3) follow
from (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_tfae
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (h𝓘 : 𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (h𝓚 : 𝓚.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {E E' : CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘} (α : E ⟶ E') :
    List.TFAE
      [IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS F hF 𝓚 α.hom,
        ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS F, IsAffine (chartScheme U) →
          (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf U.1.hom →
          IsChartKernelCokernelAnnihilated B S hS F hF 𝓘 𝓚 α.hom U,
        ∃ U : SmallEtale B S hS F, IsAffine (chartScheme U) ∧
          (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf U.1.hom ∧
          IsChartKernelCokernelAnnihilated B S hS F hF 𝓘 𝓚 α.hom U]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) with (2) for any, and for some, surjective etale affine chart U = Spec(A), with alpha_U the map of 087W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_algebraization_and_existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BB.**  Let `F` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and `𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_F` a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.  Let `G` be a coherent `𝒪_F`-module, `E` an object of
`Coh(F, 𝓘)` and `α : E ⟶ G^∧` a map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝓘`.
Then there exists a triple `(M, a, β)` where

1. `M` is a coherent `𝒪_F`-module,
2. `a : M ⟶ G` is an `𝒪_F`-module map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of
   `𝓘`,
3. `β : E ≅ M^∧` is an isomorphism, and
4. `α = a^∧ ∘ β`,

and it is unique up to unique isomorphism: for any two such triples `(M, a, β)` and
`(N, a', β')` there is exactly one isomorphism `e : M ≅ N` with `a' ∘ e = a` and
`e^∧ ∘ β = β'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraization_and_existsUnique_iso
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    {G : CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} {E : CoherentAdicSystems B S hS F hF 𝓘}
    (α : E ⟶ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).obj G)
    (hα : IsSystemKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS F hF 𝓘 α.hom) :
    (∃ (M : CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (a : M ⟶ G)
      (β : E ≅ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).obj M),
      IsMapKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS F hF 𝓘 a ∧
        α = β.hom ≫ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).map a) ∧
    ∀ {M N : CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (a : M ⟶ G) (a' : N ⟶ G)
      (β : E ≅ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).obj M)
      (β' : E ≅ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).obj N),
      IsMapKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS F hF 𝓘 a →
      IsMapKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS F hF 𝓘 a' →
      α = β.hom ≫ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).map a →
      α = β'.hom ≫ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).map a' →
      ∃! e : M ≅ N, e.hom ≫ a' = a ∧
        β.hom ≫ (completionFunctor B S hS F hF 𝓘 hI).map e.hom = β'.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_completionFunctorProperOver_of_auxiliaryIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BC.**  In Situation 08B7 — `A` Noetherian and `I`-adically complete,
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` of finite type and separated, `𝓘 = I 𝒪_X` — let `𝓚 ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and `(F_n)` an object of
`Coh_{support proper over A}(X, 𝓘)`.  Assume

1. for every `e ≥ 1`, the closed subspace `X_e` cut out by `𝓚^e` is such that completion along
   `𝓘_e = I 𝒪_{X_e}` is an equivalence
   `Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_{X_e}) ≌ Coh_{support proper over A}(X_e, 𝓘_e)`, and
2. there are an object `𝓗` of `Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_X)` and a map
   `α : (F_n) ⟶ 𝓗^∧` whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝓚`.

Then `(F_n)` is in the essential image of the completion functor of Stacks 08B8.

The closed subspace `X_e` of (1) is given as a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` whose ideal sheaf
`ker(𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_Z)` is `𝓚^e`. The proof follows the source: the systems `(F_n / 𝓚^(e+1) F_n)_n`
are algebraized on `X_(e+1)` and pushed to `X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.kTorsionEssSurj_of_essSurj`); the algebraizations `G_e` form a
coherent `𝓚`-adic system mapping to `𝓗^∧` with kernels and cokernels killed by `𝓚^(2t)` — the bound
the source leaves as "details omitted"
(`C1573.TorsionAlgebraization.isSystemKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower_γSystem`, a sharper exponent
than the source's `𝓚^(4t)`); Stacks 08BB along `𝓚` algebraizes this map to `a : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓗`; reducing
modulo `𝓘^(n+1)` identifies `𝓕 / 𝓘^(n+1) 𝓕` with `F_n`; and the kernel of `a` embeds into some
`G_e` by Artin–Rees, so `𝓕` has proper support by Stacks 0CZH
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.essImage_completionFunctorProperOver_of_kTorsionEssSurj`).
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_completionFunctorProperOver_of_auxiliaryIdeal [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    [IsAdicComplete I A] (X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)) (hf : IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (K : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1
        X.2).O))).Submodule) (hK : K.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (h1 : ∀ e : ℕ, 0 < e → ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (i : Z ⟶ X)
      (hi : IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of A)) hA i.hom),
      SheafOfModules.kerIdeal (structureSharp B (Spec (.of A)) hA i) =
        idealPowerMultiple B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2 K e (SheafOfModules.unit _) ∧
      letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject Z (i ≫ f)
        (C1573.isLocallyOfFiniteType_closedImmersion_comp i hi f hf.1)
      (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA Z.1 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1
        Z.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 (i ≫ f).hom
        (C1573.isLocallyOfFiniteType_closedImmersion_comp i hi f hf.1)
        (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule Z.1 Z.2 I)
        (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := Z.1) (hX := Z.2) I)).IsEquivalence)
    (E : CoherentAdicSystemsProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2
      f.hom hf.1 (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I))
    (H : CoherentModulesProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.2 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2
      f.hom hf.1)
    (α : E ⟶ letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf.1
      (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1 X.2
        (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf.1 (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
        (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).obj H)
    (hα : IsSystemKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2 K α.hom.hom) :
    letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf.1
    (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1 X.2
      (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf.1 (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
      (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).essImage E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_completionMap_kernel_cokernel_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a representable proper morphism of Noetherian algebraic
spaces over `S`, let `𝓙, 𝓚 ⊆ 𝒪_Y` be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals, and assume `f` is an
isomorphism over `Y ∖ V(𝓚)`.  Set `𝓘 = f⁻¹𝓙 𝒪_X`.  Let `(𝓖_n)` be an object of `Coh(Y, 𝓙)`,
`𝓕` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `β : (f^*𝓖_n) ≅ 𝓕^∧` an isomorphism in `Coh(X, 𝓘)`.  Then there
is a map `α : (𝓖_n) ⟶ (f_*𝓕)^∧` in `Coh(Y, 𝓙)` whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a
power of `𝓚` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower`, the notion of
Stacks 08BA: one exponent `t > 0` with `𝓚 ^ t` killing every levelwise kernel and cokernel).

`α` is the map whose composite with the comparison `(f_*𝓕)^∧ ⟶ f_*(𝓕^∧)` is the system of
adjunction maps followed by `f_*β`; it exists because that comparison is an isomorphism on limits
(the theorem on formal functions, checked on affine charts), and the annihilation is the scheme
case Stacks 088B on one surjective affine chart of `Y`, spread over `Y` by quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completionMap_kernel_cokernel_annihilated (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f.hom)
    (hfp : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (J K : (SheafOfModules.unit.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O))).Submodule)
    (hJ : J.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hK : K.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hiso : IsIso ((idealComplementSubfunctor B S hS Y K).fromPreimage f.hom))
    (G : CoherentAdicSystems B S hS Y.1 Y.2 J) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F) :
    letI : Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V)) :=
      ⟨hX.2.2⟩
    letI : Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V)) :=
      ⟨hY.2.2⟩
    ∀ _β : G.obj ⋙ modulePullback B S hS f ≅
        ((completionFunctor B S hS X.1 X.2 (pullbackIdealSubsheaf B S hS f hf J)
          (isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackIdealSubsheaf B S hS f hf J hJ)).obj ⟨F, hF⟩).obj,
      ∃ α : G ⟶ (completionFunctor B S hS Y.1 Y.2 J hJ).obj
          ⟨(modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F,
            isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isProper B S hS f hf hfp hY.2.2 F hF⟩,
        IsKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS Y.1 Y.2 K α.hom
declarations.comment: the full statement: for a representable proper morphism of Noetherian algebraic spaces which is an isomorphism over Y minus V(K), a map alpha from (G_n) to the completion of f_*F in Coh(Y, J) whose levelwise kernels and cokernels are all annihilated by one positive power of K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.directImageComparison
declarations.doc:
**The maps `γ_n : 𝓖_n ⟶ f_*f^*𝓖_n ⟶ f_*(𝓕/𝓘 ⁿ⁺¹𝓕)` of the proof of Stacks 08BD**, as a
morphism of inverse systems of `𝒪_Y`-modules on an algebraic space: the adjunction map followed
by `f_*β_n`.
declarations.statement:
def directImageComparison :
    G.obj ⟶ ((completionFunctor B S hS X.1 X.2 𝓘 hI).obj F).obj ⋙ modulePushforward B S hS f
declarations.comment: the maps gamma_n of the proof: the adjunction map followed by f_*beta_n. The map alpha into (f_*F)^ is a different declaration and is not constructed in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_pos_idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_directImageComparison_iff
declarations.doc:
**The reduction of the kernel–cokernel condition of Stacks 08BD to the adjunction maps.**
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let `𝓙, 𝓚 ⊆ 𝒪_Y` and
`𝓘 ⊆ 𝒪_X` be sheaves of ideals, let `(𝓖_n)` be an object of `Coh(Y, 𝓙)`, let `𝓕` be a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and let `β : (f^*𝓖_n) ⟶ 𝓕^∧` be an isomorphism in `Coh(X, 𝓘)`.  The maps

`γ_n : 𝓖_n ⟶ f_*f^*𝓖_n ⟶ f_*(𝓕/𝓘 ⁿ⁺¹𝓕)`

have their levelwise kernels and cokernels annihilated by one positive power of `𝓚` exactly when
the adjunction maps `𝓖_n ⟶ f_*f^*𝓖_n` do, because `γ_n` differs from the adjunction map by the
isomorphism `f_*β_n`.  This is the step of the source's proof which makes the isomorphism `β`
disappear from the annihilation statement, leaving the adjunction map that the closing paragraph
of the scheme case is about.

The map `α : (𝓖_n) ⟶ (f_*𝓕)^∧` which the source produces out of `γ` is not constructed; see the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pos_idealPowerMultiple_kernel_cokernel_directImageComparison_iff
    (𝓚 : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O))).Submodule) :
    (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < t ∧ ∀ k : ℕ,
        idealPowerMultiple B S hS Y.1 Y.2 𝓚 t
            (kernel ((directImageComparison B S hS f 𝓙 𝓘 hI G F β).app (op k))) = ⊥ ∧
          idealPowerMultiple B S hS Y.1 Y.2 𝓚 t
            (cokernel ((directImageComparison B S hS f 𝓙 𝓘 hI G F β).app (op k))) = ⊥) ↔
      ∃ t : ℕ, 0 < t ∧ ∀ k : ℕ,
        idealPowerMultiple B S hS Y.1 Y.2 𝓚 t
            (kernel ((pullbackPushforwardUnitSystem B S hS f G.obj).app (op k))) = ⊥ ∧
          idealPowerMultiple B S hS Y.1 Y.2 𝓚 t
            (cokernel ((pullbackPushforwardUnitSystem B S hS f G.obj).app (op k))) = ⊥
declarations.comment: the reduction of the lemma's kernel-cokernel condition from gamma to the adjunction maps. The map alpha into (f_*F)^ is not constructed in this library, which proves neither 08AR for a representable proper morphism nor the uniform Artin-Rees bounds 02OB behind the scheme case 088B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_hom_completion_modulePushforward_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BD.**  For a representable proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of Noetherian algebraic
spaces which is an isomorphism over the complement of the closed subspace `Z = V(𝒦)`, a coherent
`𝒥`-adic system `(𝒢_n)` on `Y`, a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` and an isomorphism
`β : (f^*𝒢_n) ≅ 𝓕^∧` of inverse systems on `X` (for the ideal `𝓘 = f⁻¹𝒥 𝒪_X`), the direct image
`f_*𝓕` is coherent and there is a map `α : (𝒢_n) ⟶ (f_*𝓕)^∧` of coherent `𝒥`-adic systems whose
kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝒦`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hom_completion_modulePushforward_annihilated
    (hZ0 : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ0 X.1) (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ0 Y.1)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f.hom) (hfp : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (J K : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O))).Submodule)
    (hJ : J.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hZ : definingIdealSheaf B S hS Y Z = K)
    (hiso : IsIso ((openComplement B S hS Z.1).fromPreimage f.hom))
    (G : CoherentAdicSystems B S hS Y.1 Y.2 J)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F)
    (β : G.obj ⋙ modulePullback B S hS f ≅
      adicQuotientSystem B S hS X.1 X.2 (C1573.inverseImageIdeal B S hS f hf J) F) :
    haveI : Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) := ⟨hY.2.2⟩
    ∃ hP : IsCoherent B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F),
      ∃ α : G ⟶ (completionFunctor B S hS Y.1 Y.2 J hJ).obj
          ⟨(modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F, hP⟩,
        IsSystemKernelCokernelAnnihilatedByPower B S hS Y.1 Y.2 K α.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BE, Grothendieck's existence theorem for algebraic spaces.**  Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, and let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be a separated
morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces (Situation 08B7, with `𝓘 = I 𝒪_X`).  Then the
completion functor

`Coh_{support proper over A}(𝒪_X) ⟶ Coh_{support proper over A}(X, 𝓘)`

of Stacks 08B8 is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_completionFunctorProperOver [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    [IsAdicComplete I A] (X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)) (hf : IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    letI := C1573.fact_isLocallyNoetherian_of_baseObject X f hf.1
    (completionFunctorProperOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).1 X.2
      (schemeSpace (baseObject A B hA)).2 f.hom hf.1 (C1573.baseIdealSubmodule X.1 X.2 I)
      (C1573.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseIdealSubmodule (X := X.1) (hX := X.2) I)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_adicFibreRestrictionProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BF.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, write
`S = Spec A` and `Sₙ = Spec(A/Iⁿ)`, and let `X ⟶ S` be a separated morphism of algebraic spaces of
finite type, with `Xₙ = X ×_S Sₙ`.  Then the completion functor `𝓕 ↦ (𝓕|_{Xₙ})ₙ`, from coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules with support proper over `A` to systems `(𝓕ₙ, φₙ)` of coherent
`𝒪_{Xₙ}`-modules `𝓕ₙ` with isomorphisms `φₙ : iₙ^* 𝓕ₙ₊₁ ≅ 𝓕ₙ` such that `Supp(𝓕₁)` is proper
over `S₁`, is an equivalence of categories.

The adic fibres are indexed from `0`: `adicFibreSpaceOf A I B hA X f n` is the source's `Xₙ₊₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_adicFibreRestrictionProperOver [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hf : IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    (adicFibreRestrictionProperOver I X f hf.1).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_adicFibreRestriction_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BF, the case of `X` proper over `A`.**  If `X ⟶ S = Spec A` is proper, the
completion functor `𝓕 ↦ (𝓕|_{Xₙ})ₙ` from all coherent `𝒪_X`-modules to all systems `(𝓕ₙ, φₙ)` of
coherent `𝒪_{Xₙ}`-modules with isomorphisms `φₙ : iₙ^* 𝓕ₙ₊₁ ≅ 𝓕ₙ` is an equivalence of
categories: the conditions on the supports can be omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_adicFibreRestriction_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    (adicFibreRestrictionOf I X f hf.2.1.1).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the special case of X proper over A, where the conditions on the supports are omitted

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedImmersion_adicFibre_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BG.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, write
`S = Spec A` and `S_n = Spec(A / I^{n+1})`, and let `X ⟶ S` be a separated morphism of finite
type of algebraic spaces, with adic fibres `X_n = X ×_S S_n`.  Let `Z_n` be algebraic spaces with
morphisms `j_n : Z_n ⟶ X_n` and `t_n : Z_n ⟶ Z_{n+1}` making every square
`Z_n ⟶ Z_{n+1}` over `X_n ⟶ X_{n+1}` cartesian.  If `Z_0 ⟶ X_0` is a closed immersion and
`Z_0 ⟶ S_0` is proper, then there is a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces with
`Z ⟶ S` proper and isomorphisms `Z_n ≅ Z ×_S S_n` over `X_n`, compatible with the transition
maps.

The index `n` stands for the source's `n + 1`: `Z 0 = Z_1`, `X 0 = X_1`, `S 0 = S_1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_adicFibre_iso [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hS X)
    (fX : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject A B hS)) (hft : IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hS fX)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hS fX)
    (Z : ℕ → (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hZ : ∀ n, IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hS (Z n))
    (j : ∀ n, Z n ⟶ adicFibre A I B hS hSn fX n) (t : ∀ n, Z n ⟶ Z (n + 1))
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (t n) (j n) (j (n + 1)) (adicFibreSucc A I B hS hSn fX n))
    (hj : IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of A)) hS (j 0))
    (hprop : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hS
      (j 0 ≫ pullback.snd fX (yoneda.map (adicThickeningMap A I B hS hSn 0)))) :
    ∃ (W : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hS W) (i : W ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of A)) hS i ∧ IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hS (i ≫ fX) ∧
      ∃ e : ∀ n, Z n ≅ adicFibre A I B hS hSn (i ≫ fX) n,
        (∀ n, (e n).hom ≫ adicFibreMap A I B hS hSn i rfl n = j n) ∧
        (∀ n, t n ≫ (e (n + 1)).hom = (e n).hom ≫ adicFibreSucc A I B hS hSn (i ≫ fX) n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAbsolutelySeparated_groupAlgebraicSpace_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BH.** A decent group algebraic space over the spectrum of a field is a separated
algebraic space.

By Stacks 06P6 separatedness of the structure morphism is the identity section being a closed
immersion, and the identity section is a section of the structure morphism, hence a closed
immersion because the space is decent. The base is separated because the spectrum of a field is
affine, so Stacks 04ZH part (1) upgrades separatedness of the structure morphism to
separatedness of the group space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_groupAlgebraicSpace_of_isDecentSpace (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hZ : C.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C S hS
      (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS)))
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda C S hS
        (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS))))
    (hG : IsDecentSpace C S hS G.obj.X.left) :
    IsAbsolutelySeparated C S hS hZ G.obj.X.left
declarations.comment: a decent group algebraic space over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isAbsolutelySeparated_arrows_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BH.** The arrow space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose object space is
the algebraic space of the spectrum of a field and whose arrow space is decent is a separated
algebraic space.

The unit of the groupoid is a section of the source morphism, hence a closed immersion because
the arrow space is decent; the target morphism is then separated, and the object space is
separated because the spectrum of a field is affine, so Stacks 04ZH part (1) applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_arrows_of_isDecentSpace (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hZ : C.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (hU : G.objects.obj =
      yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS)))
    (hR : Space.IsDecentSpace C S hS G.arrows.obj) :
    Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated C S hS hZ G.arrows.obj
declarations.comment: the arrows of a decent groupoid on a field

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BI**, the triple complex. Given a category `C` and three complex shapes `c₁`, `c₂`
and `c₃` on types `I₁`, `I₂` and `I₃`, a tricomplex `K : HomologicalComplex₃ C c₁ c₂ c₃` is a
complex `K : HomologicalComplex (HomologicalComplex₂ C c₂ c₃) c₁` of bicomplexes.
declarations.statement: abbrev HomologicalComplex₃ [HasZeroMorphisms C]
declarations.comment: the triple complex, as a complex of bicomplexes, for any three complex shapes

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.int₂₃
declarations.doc:
Given a tricomplex `K : HomologicalComplex₃ C c₁ c₂ c₃` and a complex shape `c₂₃` with
`TotalComplexShape c₂ c₃ c₂₃`, this is the bicomplex in `HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂₃` whose
column indexed by `i₁` is `(K.X i₁).total c₂₃`: Stacks' `Tot₂₃(A^{•, •, •})`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev int₂₃ [K.HasInt₂₃ c₂₃] : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂₃
declarations.comment: `Tot₂₃`, integrating the last two indices; termwise, for any shapes

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.int₁₂
declarations.doc:
Given a tricomplex `K : HomologicalComplex₃ C c₁ c₂ c₃` and a complex shape `c₁₂` with
`TotalComplexShape c₁ c₂ c₁₂`, this is the bicomplex in `HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁₂ c₃` whose row
indexed by `i₃` is `(K.X' i₃).total c₁₂`, the total complex of the slice at `i₃`, and whose second
differential is induced by the third differential of `K`: Stacks' `Tot₁₂(A^{•, •, •})`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev int₁₂ [K.HasInt₁₂ c₁₂] : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁₂ c₃
declarations.comment: `Tot₁₂`, integrating the first two indices; termwise, for any shapes

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.totalAssociator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BI**: the two ways of forming the total complex of a tricomplex agree,
`Tot(Tot₁₂(A)) ≅ Tot(Tot₂₃(A))`, by the isomorphism which is the identity on every summand.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def totalAssociator : K.total₁₂ c₁₂ c ≅ K.total₂₃ c₂₃ c
declarations.comment: `Tot(Tot₁₂) ≅ Tot(Tot₂₃)`, the identity on every summand, under `Associative`

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.ιTotal₁₂_d_up_ℤ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BI**, the tag's formula for the differential of the total complex of a `ℤ`-cochain
triple complex: on the summand `A^{p, q, r}` it is `d₁ + (-1)^p d₂ + (-1)^{p + q} d₃`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ιTotal₁₂_d_up_ℤ (p q r n : ℤ) (h : p + q + r = n) :
    A.ιTotal₁₂ (up ℤ) (up ℤ) p q r n h ≫ (A.total₁₂ (up ℤ) (up ℤ)).d n (n + 1) =
      ((A.d p (p + 1)).f q).f r ≫ A.ιTotal₁₂ (up ℤ) (up ℤ) (p + 1) q r (n + 1)
        (by
          change p + 1 + q + r = n + 1
          rw [← h, Int.add_right_comm p 1 q, Int.add_right_comm (p + q) 1 r]) +
        p.negOnePow •
          (((A.X p).d q (q + 1)).f r ≫ A.ιTotal₁₂ (up ℤ) (up ℤ) p (q + 1) r (n + 1)
            (by
              change p + (q + 1) + r = n + 1
              rw [← h, ← Int.add_assoc p q 1, Int.add_right_comm (p + q) 1 r])) +
        (p + q).negOnePow •
          (((A.X p).X q).d r (r + 1) ≫ A.ιTotal₁₂ (up ℤ) (up ℤ) p q (r + 1) (n + 1)
            (by
              change p + q + (r + 1) = n + 1
              rw [← h]; exact (Int.add_assoc (p + q) r 1).symm))
declarations.comment: the tag's `d₁ + (-1)^p d₂ + (-1)^{p + q} d₃` on `A^{p, q, r}`, over `ℤ`

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.total₁₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BI**, the total complex of a tricomplex `K : HomologicalComplex₃ C c₁ c₂ c₃`, formed
as the total complex of the bicomplex `K.int₁₂ c₁₂ : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁₂ c₃`. For
`ℤ`-cochain shapes its differential carries the tag's signs `d₁ + (-1)^p d₂ + (-1)^{p + q} d₃`,
see `ιTotal₁₂_d_up_ℤ`, so this is the tag's `Tot(A^{•, •, •})` itself, and also its
`Tot(Tot₁₂(A^{•, •, •}))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev total₁₂ : HomologicalComplex C c
declarations.comment: the tag's `Tot`, as `Tot(Tot₁₂)`; any shapes, signs from the `TotalComplexShape`s

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.total₁₂_d
declarations.doc: The differential of `Tot(Tot₁₂)` is `D₁ + D₂ + D₃`.
declarations.statement:
lemma total₁₂_d (j j' : J) :
    (K.total₁₂ c₁₂ c).d j j' = K.D₁ c₁₂ c j j' + K.D₂ c₁₂ c j j' + K.D₃ c₁₂ c j j'
declarations.comment: the differential of `Tot` is the sum of the three signed pieces

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₃.total₂₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BI**, `Tot(Tot₂₃(A^{•, •, •}))`: the total complex of a tricomplex
`K : HomologicalComplex₃ C c₁ c₂ c₃` as the total complex of the bicomplex
`K.int₂₃ c₂₃ : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂₃`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev total₂₃ : HomologicalComplex C c
declarations.comment: `Tot(Tot₂₃)`; any shapes

registrations.name: HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorAssociator
registrations.comment: the bifunctor case: `Tot(Tot(F₁₂(K₁, K₂)) ⊗ K₃) ≅ Tot(K₁ ⊗ Tot(G₂₃(K₂, K₃)))`

registrations.name: ComplexShape.Associative
registrations.comment: the sign compatibility under which `Tot(Tot₁₂)` and `Tot(Tot₂₃)` agree

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_mapHomologicalComplex_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BJ.** Adjoint criterion for K-injectivity, exactness form: let `u : A ⥤ B` and
`v : B ⥤ A` be additive functors between abelian categories such that `u` is right adjoint to `v`
and `v` is exact. Then `u` carries K-injective cochain complexes to K-injective cochain
complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_mapHomologicalComplex_of_exact
    (u : A ⥤ B) (v : B ⥤ A) [u.Additive] [v.Additive] (adj : v ⊣ u)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits v] [PreservesFiniteColimits v]
    (I : CochainComplex A ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective ((u.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.FlatEquationalCriterion.exists_local_factorization_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project Tag 08BK (Modules, Lemma 17.17.11).**

Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and `F` a flat `O_X`-module. Let `U ⊆ X` be open, `n ∈ ℕ`,
`f₁, …, fₙ ∈ O_X(U)` and `s₁, …, sₙ ∈ F(U)` such that the diagram
`O_U → O_U^{⊕n} → F|_U` is a complex, i.e. `∑ᵢ fᵢ • sᵢ = 0` in `F(U)`.

Then for every `x ∈ U` there exist an open neighbourhood `V ⊆ U` of `x`, an integer `m`,
sections `t₁, …, t_m ∈ F(V)` and scalars `a_{ji} ∈ O_X(V)` such that:
  - (Factorization)  `sᵢ|_V = ∑ⱼ a_{ji} • t_j`   for every `i`;
  - (Annihilation)   `∑ᵢ a_{ji} • fᵢ|_V = 0`      for every `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_factorization_of_isFlat {X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u}}
  (M : OXModule X) (hM : M.IsFlat)
    (U : Opens X) (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → OSections X U) (s : Fin n → M.sheaf.obj (op U))
    (hcomplex : ∑ i, f i • s i = 0)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x ∈ V) (iVU : V ≤ U) (m : ℕ)
      (t : Fin m → M.sheaf.obj (op V)) (a : Fin m → Fin n → OSections X V),
      (∀ i, M.res iVU (s i) = ∑ j, a j i • t j) ∧
      (∀ j, ∑ i, a j i • Ores X iVU (f i) = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_isFlat_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BL.** A flat sheaf of `O_X`-modules of finite presentation on a ringed space is,
locally on `X`, a direct summand of a finite free `O_X`-module.

This is Stacks 08FD on the site of opens of `X`: the covering sieve it produces on `⊤` is, by
`TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_grothendieckTopology`, a neighbourhood of each point of `X` carrying
the retraction, and the finite index type of the free module there is reindexed by `Fin n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_isFlat_of_isFinitePresentation
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    [hfp₀ : F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.sheaf) F) :
    IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.cechTotalComplexRefinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BM.** A refinement `t : V ⟶ U` induces, naturally in a complex of presheaves,
the restriction map `Tot(Č^•(U, F^•)) ⟶ Tot(Č^•(V, F^•))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechTotalComplexRefinement {I J : Type w} (U : I → C) (V : J → C)
    (t : FormalCoproduct.mk J V ⟶ FormalCoproduct.mk I U) :
    CechRefinementTransformation U V t

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.exists_cechToDerivedComparison_and_cechSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08BN.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, let `U : X = ⋃_{i ∈ I} U_i` be an open
covering and let `F^•` be a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules. Then

1. there is a canonical map `Tot(Č^•(U, F^•)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F^•)`, functorial in `F^•` -- it is a
   morphism of functors on bounded below complexes -- and compatible both with the augmentation
   of equation (20.25.0.1) ([Stacks, Tag 07M9]) and with the refinement map of equation
   (20.25.0.2) ([Stacks, Tag 08BM]); and
2. there is a cohomological spectral sequence with
   `E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Tot(Č^•(U, H^q(F^•))))` abutting to `H^{p+q}(X, F^•)`, where `H^q(F^•)` is
   the complex `n ↦ R^q i(F^n)` of cohomology presheaves of [Stacks, Tag 01ER].

Both halves are read off the library's wider statements: the comparison from the system of
comparisons for all coverings at once, `cechToDerivedGlobalSections`, and the spectral sequence
from `exists_cechSpectralSequence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechToDerivedComparison_and_cechSpectralSequence
    {I : Type u} (U : I → Opens X) (hU : ⊤ = iSup U)
    (K : CochainComplex.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} R)) :
    ((globalSectionsToCechDerived X R U).app K ≫
          ((cechToDerivedGlobalSections X R).map U hU).app K =
          globalSectionsToDerived X R K ∧
        ∀ (J : Type u) (V : J → Opens X) (hV : ⊤ = iSup V)
            (t : FormalCoproduct.mk J V ⟶ FormalCoproduct.mk I U),
          cechRefinementDerived X R U V t ≫ (cechToDerivedGlobalSections X R).map V hV =
            (cechToDerivedGlobalSections X R).map U hU) ∧
      ∃ E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 2,
        (∀ p q : ℤ,
          Nonempty ((E.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
            ((cechTotalComplexFunctor U).obj
              ((((underlyingPresheafFunctor X R).rightDerivedPlus q).mapHomologicalComplex
                (up ℤ)).obj K.1)).homology p)) ∧
          SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E (fun n =>
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
              ((derivedGlobalSectionsFunctor X R).obj K))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: the canonical map `Tot(Č(U, F)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F)`, functorial in `F` and compatible with the augmentation of (20.25.0.1) = Tag 07M9 and the refinement map of (20.25.0.2) = Tag 08BM, together with the spectral sequence `E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Tot(Č(U, H^q(F))))` abutting to `H^{p+q}(X, F)` -- for a ringed space, an open covering of `X` and a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules, which are the lemma's three inputs and all of them

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.exists_cechSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
For a ringed space `(X, O_X)`, an open covering `U : I → Opens X` of `X` and a bounded below
complex `F^•` of `O_X`-modules there is a cohomological spectral sequence, starting on page two,
with

```
E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Tot(Č^•(U, H^q(F^•))))
```

where `H^q(F^•)` is the complex `n ↦ R^q i(F^n)` of cohomology presheaves, abutting to
`H^{p+q}(X, F^•)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechSpectralSequence {I : Type u} (U : I → Opens X) (hU : ⊤ = iSup U)
    (K : CochainComplex.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} R)) :
    ∃ E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 2,
      (∀ p q : ℤ,
        Nonempty ((E.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
          ((cechTotalComplexFunctor U).obj
            ((((underlyingPresheafFunctor X R).rightDerivedPlus q).mapHomologicalComplex
              (up ℤ)).obj K.1)).homology p)) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E (fun n =>
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsFunctor X R).obj K))
declarations.comment: the tag's spectral sequence: `E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Tot(Č(U, H^q(F))))`, both coordinates ranging over `ℤ`, abutting to `H^{p+q}(X, F)`, for a ringed space, an open covering of `X` and a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules. The tag's comparison map `Tot(Č(U, F)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F)`, with its Tag 07M9 and Tag 08BM compatibilities, is `Stacks.Cech.cechToDerivedGlobalSections`, and the two halves are asserted together at the lemma's own three inputs by `Stacks.Cech.exists_cechToDerivedComparison_and_cechSpectralSequence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.cechToDerivedGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08BN, the comparison map.** For a ringed space `(X, O_X)` the total Čech complex of a
bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules has a canonical map to its derived global sections,
functorial in the complex, compatible with the augmentation of Tag 07M9 — hence independent of
the covering — and compatible with the refinement map of Tag 08BM.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechToDerivedGlobalSections
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) :
    CechToDerivedGlobalSectionsSystem X R
declarations.comment: the tag's comparison map: the total Čech complex of a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules maps canonically to its derived global sections, functorially in the complex -- the map is a morphism of functors on bounded below complexes -- and compatibly both with the Tag 07M9 augmentation and with the Tag 08BM refinement map, simultaneously for every open covering of `X`. The tag's spectral sequence `E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Tot(Č(U, H^q(F))))` abutting to `H^{p+q}(X, F)` is `Stacks.Cech.exists_cechSpectralSequence`, and the two halves are asserted together at the lemma's own three inputs by `Stacks.Cech.exists_cechToDerivedComparison_and_cechSpectralSequence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.Linear.cechToDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BN, the comparison map with module coefficients.**  For a ringed space `(X, O_X)`
and an open subset `U` the total Čech complex of a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules has a
canonical map to its derived sections over `U`, a morphism of `D(O_X(U))` functorial in the
complex and compatible with the augmentation of [Stacks, Tag 07M9] -- hence independent of the
covering.
declarations.statement: def cechToDerivedSections : CechToDerivedSectionsSystem X O U
declarations.comment: the tag's comparison map, generalised to module coefficients over an arbitrary open: for a ringed space `(X, O_X)` and an open `U`, the total Čech complex of a bounded below complex of `O_X`-modules maps canonically to its derived sections in `D(O_X(U))`, functorially in the complex and compatibly with the Tag 07M9 augmentation, simultaneously for every open covering of `U`. The tag's own statement -- the comparison over `X`, compatible with both the Tag 07M9 and the Tag 08BM maps, together with the tag's spectral sequence -- is `Stacks.Cech.cechToDerivedGlobalSections` and `Stacks.Cech.exists_cechSpectralSequence`, conjoined at the lemma's three inputs by `Stacks.Cech.exists_cechToDerivedComparison_and_cechSpectralSequence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.tor

declarations.statement: def tor (p : ℤ) (F G : OXMod.{u} X) : OXMod.{u} X

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.flat_iff_forall_isZero_tor
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08BQ: Tor measures the deviation of flatness.** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and
`ℱ` an `𝒪_X`-module. The following are equivalent:

1. `ℱ` is a flat `𝒪_X`-module, and
2. `Tor_1^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) = 0` for every `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢`.

Clause (1) is `OXModule.Flat`, Definition Tag 05ND: the genuine sheaf tensor endofunctor
`- ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ` preserves monomorphisms, hence is exact. Clause (2) is the source's own `Tor_1`,
the sheaf `Stacks.Cohomology.tor X 1 ℱ 𝒢` of Tag 08BP, which is `H^{-1}(ℱ ⊗^{L}_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)` —
not a stalkwise substitute for it.

*Proof.* Tag 05NE (`OXModule.flat_iff_flat_stalk`) replaces clause (1) by flatness of every
stalk, and `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.flat_stalk_ringCat_iff_commRingCat` reads that over
the stalk ring the derived tensor product is formed relative to. Over that ring
`OXModule.module_flat_iff_tor1` turns flatness of a stalk into the vanishing of the
module-theoretic `Tor_1` against every module over it, every such module being a stalk by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.stalkFunctor_essSurj`; and
`isZero_derivedTensorHomology_iff_forall_isZero_tor` turns the vanishing of those stalkwise
`Tor_1` into the vanishing of the sheaf `Tor_1`, which is clause (2).

No intermediate statement of stalkwise flatness over the `RingCat`-valued stalk ring is written
down, and that is deliberate: writing `Module.Flat Λ M` for that ring forces the `Semiring Λ`
inside the `Module` instance to be the one derived from
`StacksDraft.StalkTensor.commRing_stalk`, while the `ModuleCat Λ` that `M` lives in carries the
one derived from `RingCat`'s own `Ring`. The two are definitionally equal but not syntactically,
so instance synthesis fails on the resulting `Module Λ M` goal. Going through
`OXModule.module_flat_iff_tor1`, whose `ModuleCat` is formed from its own `CommRing` binder,
keeps the instances internally consistent.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_forall_isZero_tor (F : OXMod.{u, u} X) :
    OXModule.Flat F ↔ ∀ G : OXMod.{u, u} X, IsZero (tor X 1 F G)
declarations.comment:
(1) ⟺ (2) for a ringed space, with clause (2) stated in the source's own terms:
the vanishing of the sheaf Tor_1^{O_X}(F, G) = H^{-1}(F ⊗^L_{O_X} G) of Tag 08BP, for every
O_X-module G, and clause (1) sheaf-level flatness of Tag 05ND.

declarations.name: OXModule.flat_iff_tor1_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 08BQ — "Tor measures the deviation of flatness").**
Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and `F` an `O_X`-module.  Then `F` is flat
(Definition 2: the genuine tensor endofunctor `- ⊗_{O_X} F` is exact) if and
only if `Tor_1^{O_X}(F, G)` is the zero `O_X`-module for every `O_X`-module
`G`.

The tensor product (Definition 1) is formalized directly as the sheafification
of the presheaf tensor product, and `Flat` is the genuine sheaf-level exactness
of this tensor, so the left-hand side is the source's own notion (Tag 05ND).

The right-hand side is the **stalk-level** reading: `Tor1IsZero F G` says that
the classical module-theoretic `Tor_1^{O_{X,x}}(F_x, G_x)` vanishes at every
`x`.  It is not the expression `Stacks.Cohomology.tor X 1 F G` (Tag 08BP), the
genuine `H^{-1}(F ⊗^{L}_{O_X} G)`, which is what the tag's clause (2) is about;
and `tor1IsZero_iff_stalk` is `Iff.rfl`, so it supplies no part of the
comparison.

The two readings are nevertheless **the same statement**, and that is now a
theorem rather than a gap: `Stacks.Cohomology.flat_iff_forall_isZero_tor` in
`StacksFrontier/Topology/Sheaves/Cohomology/DerivedTensor/TorFlatness.lean` states
Tag 08BQ with clause (2) in the source's own terms, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorStalk.isZero_derivedTensorHomology_iff_forall_isZero_tor`
there is the identification itself: the sheaf `Tor_p` of Tag 08BP vanishes
exactly when the stalkwise module-theoretic `Tor_p` vanishes at every point.
Its four ingredients are
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isZero_iff_forall_isZero_stalkFunctor_obj`
(vanishing is stalkwise, Tag 01AG),
`CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyIso` (the exact stalk functor
commutes with `H^{-1}`),
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorStalk.derivedTensorStalkIso` (the derived
form of Tag 01CB) — all three of which already existed — and
`Stacks.DerivedTensor.homologyIsoTor`
(`StacksFrontier/Homology/Tor/DerivedTensorTor.lean`), the identification of
`H^{-p}` of a derived tensor product of two modules over a commutative ring
with their `Tor_p`, which is the one that had to be supplied.

So this declaration is the stalk-level half of the tag, kept because the rest of
this file is written in the stalkwise vocabulary; the tag's own statement is the
one in `StacksFrontier/Topology/Sheaves/Cohomology/DerivedTensor/TorFlatness.lean`.

*Proof.*  By `flat_iff_flat_stalk` (Tag 05NE) sheaf flatness is equivalent to
stalk-wise flatness `F.FlatStalkwise`, and by `flatStalkwise_iff_forall_tor1`
the latter is equivalent to the vanishing of all stalk-wise `Tor₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_tor1_eq_zero (F : OXModule X) :
    F.Flat ↔ ∀ G : OXModule X, F.Tor1IsZero G
declarations.comment:
(1) ⟺ (2) with clause (2) read stalkwise: Tor_1 here is the module-theoretic
Tor_1^{O_{X,x}}(F_x, G_x) at every point, not the sheaf Tor_1 of Tag 08BP. The tag's clause (2)
in the source's own terms — the vanishing of Stacks.Cohomology.tor X 1 F G — is
Stacks.Cohomology.flat_iff_forall_isZero_tor in
StacksFrontier/Topology/Sheaves/Cohomology/DerivedTensor/TorFlatness.lean, and the two readings are
identified there by isZero_derivedTensorHomology_iff_forall_isZero_tor.

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.exists_derivedJShriek_restriction_adjunction
declarations.doc:
For an open subset `U` of a ringed space `X`, extension by zero and restriction to `U` are
exact, and the functor on unbounded derived categories induced by extension by zero is left
adjoint to the functor induced by restriction to `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedJShriek_restriction_adjunction
    (X : SheafedSpace RingCat.{u}) (U : Opens X.carrier) :
    ∃ (h₁ : (jShriek00A7 X U).Additive)
      (h₂ : PreservesFiniteLimits (jShriek00A7 X U))
      (h₃ : PreservesFiniteColimits (jShriek00A7 X U))
      (h₄ : (restMod X U).Additive)
      (h₅ : PreservesFiniteLimits (restMod X U))
      (h₆ : PreservesFiniteColimits (restMod X U)),
      letI := h₁
      letI := h₂
      letI := h₃
      letI := h₄
      letI := h₅
      letI := h₆
      Nonempty ((jShriek00A7 X U).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ (restMod X U).mapDerivedCategory)

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.distinguished_extensionRestriction_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BU.** For a cover by two open subspaces, extension by zero of the
restrictions to their intersection and to the two opens forms a distinguished triangle,
naturally in the object of the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem distinguished_extensionRestriction_triangle {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (DU DV DUV : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (aU : homotopyExtensionRestriction O U ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DU)
    (aV : homotopyExtensionRestriction O V ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DV)
    (aUV : homotopyExtensionRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DUV)
    [DU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [DV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [DUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ (iU : DUV ⟶ DU) (iV : DUV ⟶ DV)
      (δ : 𝟭 (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶
        DUV ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (1 : ℤ)),
      (iU ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O U DU aU =
          derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O (U ⊓ V) DUV aUV) ∧
      (iV ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O V DV aV =
          -derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O (U ⊓ V) DUV aUV) ∧
      (∀ E, Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (iU.app E) (iV.app E))
        (biprod.desc ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O U DU aU).app E)
          ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O V DV aV).app E)) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)))
declarations.comment:
the whole statement: the distinguished triangle, for every choice of the three
derived functors `R(j_!j^*)` and their units — the degreewise one of Section 20.32 included — with
the two maps out of the intersection term pinned by the adjunction counits, the second with the
Mayer--Vietoris sign

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.distinguished_derivedExtensionRestriction_triangle
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space which is the union of two open subspaces `U` and `V`. Then there
are comparison maps out of `D(j_!)D(j^*)` for `U ∩ V` into the ones for `U` and for `V`, and a
connecting transformation, such that for every object of `D(𝒪_X)` the resulting triangle is
distinguished. The three derived functors are `derivedExtensionRestriction`, the maps to the
identity functor are the canonical derived adjunction counits
`derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit`, and the two comparison maps are determined by
composing them with those counits, the second with a sign.
declarations.statement:
public theorem distinguished_derivedExtensionRestriction_triangle {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (U V : Opens X)
    (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (iU : derivedExtensionRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ⟶ derivedExtensionRestriction O U)
      (iV : derivedExtensionRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ⟶ derivedExtensionRestriction O V)
      (δ : 𝟭 (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶
        derivedExtensionRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ⋙
          shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (1 : ℤ)),
      (iU ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O U =
          derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O (U ⊓ V)) ∧
      (iV ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O V =
          -derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O (U ⊓ V)) ∧
      (∀ E, Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (iU.app E) (iV.app E))
        (biprod.desc ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O U).app E)
          ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCanonicalCounit O V).app E)) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)))
declarations.comment:
the whole statement at the presentation built in this file: the three clauses of
`distinguished_extensionRestriction_triangle` for `derivedExtensionRestriction`,
`derivedExtensionRestrictionFactorsh` and the instance
`derivedExtensionRestriction_isRightDerivedFunctor`, with the maps to the identity functor the
canonical derived adjunction counits of Stacks 08BT and the two maps out of the intersection term
pinned by composing them with those counits, the second with the Mayer--Vietoris sign

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isMayerVietorisApex_restrictPushforward_sup
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08BV] for a scheme.** For opens `U`, `V` of a scheme `X` and any object `K` of
the unbounded derived category `D(𝒪_X)` there is a distinguished triangle
