`Rj_{U ∪ V,*}(K|_{U ∪ V}) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶`

in `D(𝒪_X)`, where `j_W : W → X` are the inclusions of the open subschemes.

This is `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_distTriang_restrictPushforward_sup`, read in the
vocabulary of `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.IsMayerVietorisApex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMayerVietorisApex_restrictPushforward_sup (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    IsMayerVietorisApex X U V K (restrictPushforward (U ⊔ V) K)
declarations.comment: the scheme-level form: `U`, `V` opens of a scheme inside their union, with the terms `Rj_{W,*}(K|_W)` of `D(𝒪_X)` at the locally small model

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isMayerVietorisApex_self
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08BV] for a scheme, in the form of the source.** If the opens `U`, `V` cover the
scheme `X`, then every object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` itself sits in a distinguished triangle

`K ⟶ Rj_{U,*}(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶ K⟦1⟧`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_distTriang_self`, read in the vocabulary of
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.IsMayerVietorisApex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMayerVietorisApex_self (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    IsMayerVietorisApex X U V K K
declarations.comment: the scheme-level form for a cover of the whole scheme, with `K` itself as the first term of the triangle

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MayerVietoris.exists_distinguished_triangle_of_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BV.** A two-open cover gives a distinguished Mayer--Vietoris triangle, naturally
in every object of the unbounded derived category of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distinguished_triangle_of_cover
    (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (RU RV RUV : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (aU : homotopyToDerived O U ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RU)
    (aV : homotopyToDerived O V ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RV)
    (aUV : homotopyToDerived O (U ⊓ V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RUV)
    [RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ (qU : homotopyToDerived O U ⟶ homotopyToDerived O (U ⊓ V))
      (qV : homotopyToDerived O V ⟶ homotopyToDerived O (U ⊓ V))
      (rU : (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶ RU)
      (rV : (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶ RV)
      (dU : RU ⟶ RUV) (dV : RV ⟶ RUV)
      (δ : RUV ⟶ (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
            DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⋙
        shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (1 : ℤ)),
      homotopyRestriction O U ≫ qU = homotopyRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ∧
      homotopyRestriction O V ≫ qV = homotopyRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ∧
      homotopyRestriction O U ≫ aU = Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh rU ∧
      homotopyRestriction O V ≫ aV = Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh rV ∧
      qU ≫ aUV = aU ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh dU ∧
      -(qV ≫ aUV) = aV ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh dV ∧
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (rU.app E) (rV.app E))
        (biprod.desc (dU.app E) (dV.app E)) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MayerVietoris.exists_distinguished_triangle_of_cover_rightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BV.** A two-open cover of a space carrying a sheaf of rings `O` gives a
distinguished Mayer--Vietoris triangle

`E ⟶ Rj_{U*}(E|_U) ⊞ Rj_{V*}(E|_V) ⟶ Rj_{(U ∩ V)*}(E|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶ E⟦1⟧`

naturally in the object `E` of the unbounded derived category of `O`-modules, where the three
derived pushforwards are the ones constructed by `rightDerivedRestrictPush`. The restriction maps
`rU`, `rV`, the two difference maps `dU`, `dV` and the connecting map `δ` are maps of functors on
`D(O)`, which is the naturality in `E`, and the equations preceding the triangle identify them
with the restriction and transition maps of the cover through the canonical comparisons, so that
the triangle's maps and its Mayer--Vietoris sign are retained rather than merely asserted to
exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distinguished_triangle_of_cover_rightDerived
    (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (qU : homotopyToDerived O U ⟶ homotopyToDerived O (U ⊓ V))
      (qV : homotopyToDerived O V ⟶ homotopyToDerived O (U ⊓ V))
      (rU : (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶ rightDerivedRestrictPush O U)
      (rV : (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⟶ rightDerivedRestrictPush O V)
      (dU : rightDerivedRestrictPush O U ⟶ rightDerivedRestrictPush O (U ⊓ V))
      (dV : rightDerivedRestrictPush O V ⟶ rightDerivedRestrictPush O (U ⊓ V))
      (δ : rightDerivedRestrictPush O (U ⊓ V) ⟶
        (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
            DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) ⋙
        shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (1 : ℤ)),
      homotopyRestriction O U ≫ qU = homotopyRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ∧
      homotopyRestriction O V ≫ qV = homotopyRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ∧
      homotopyRestriction O U ≫ rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O U =
        Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh rU ∧
      homotopyRestriction O V ≫ rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O V =
        Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh rV ∧
      qU ≫ rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O (U ⊓ V) =
        rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O U ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh dU ∧
      -(qV ≫ rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O (U ⊓ V)) =
        rightDerivedRestrictPushUnit O V ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh dV ∧
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (rU.app E) (rV.app E))
        (biprod.desc (dU.app E) (dV.app E)) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
declarations.comment: the ringed-space form with the three derived pushforwards constructed by `rightDerivedRestrictPush`, at the standard model of `D(O)`: no derived functor, comparison map or derived-functor hypothesis is taken as a parameter

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.exists_mayerVietoris_ext_longExactSequence
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space covered by two open subspaces `U` and `V`, and let `E` and `F` be
objects of `D(𝒪_X)`. There are restriction, difference and connecting homomorphisms making the
Mayer--Vietoris sequence

`⋯ ⟶ Ext^{n-1}(E|_{U∩V}, F|_{U∩V}) ⟶ Ext^n(E, F) ⟶
  Ext^n(E|_U, F|_U) × Ext^n(E|_V, F|_V) ⟶ Ext^n(E|_{U∩V}, F|_{U∩V}) ⟶ ⋯`

exact at each of its three kinds of spot and in every integer degree, the Ext groups of the
restrictions being taken in the derived categories of the open subspaces.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mayerVietoris_ext_longExactSequence {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
    ∃ (restriction : ∀ n : ℤ, (E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) →+
          (((derivedRestriction O U).obj E ⟶ ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F)⟦n⟧) ×
            ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E ⟶ ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F)⟦n⟧)))
      (difference : ∀ n : ℤ,
        (((derivedRestriction O U).obj E ⟶ ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F)⟦n⟧) ×
            ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E ⟶ ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F)⟦n⟧)) →+
          ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E ⟶
            ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F)⟦n⟧))
      (boundary : ∀ n : ℤ,
        ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E ⟶
          ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F)⟦n⟧) →+ (E ⟶ F⟦n + 1⟧)),
      ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Exact (restriction n) (difference n) ∧
        Function.Exact (difference n) (boundary n) ∧
        Function.Exact (boundary n) (restriction (n + 1))
declarations.comment: long exact sequence of the Ext groups on the two opens and their intersection

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.exists_mayerVietoris_hom_longExactSequence
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space covered by two open subspaces `U` and `V`, and let `E` and `F` be
objects of `D(𝒪_X)`. For every choice of the three derived functors of extension by zero of the
restrictions there are comparison maps `iU` and `iV` out of the functor attached to `U ∩ V`,
compatible with the canonical derived adjunction counits and carrying the Mayer--Vietoris sign,
and connecting homomorphisms, such that the Mayer--Vietoris sequence

`⋯ ⟶ Ext^{n-1}(j_{U∩V,!}E|_{U∩V}, F) ⟶ Ext^n(E, F) ⟶
  Ext^n(j_{U!}E|_U, F) × Ext^n(j_{V!}E|_V, F) ⟶ Ext^n(j_{U∩V,!}E|_{U∩V}, F) ⟶ ⋯`

is exact at each of its three kinds of spot and in every integer degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mayerVietoris_hom_longExactSequence {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (DU DV DUV : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (aU : homotopyExtensionRestriction O U ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DU)
    (aV : homotopyExtensionRestriction O V ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DV)
    (aUV : homotopyExtensionRestriction O (U ⊓ V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ DUV)
    [DU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [DV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [DUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ (iU : DUV ⟶ DU) (iV : DUV ⟶ DV)
      (boundary : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
        (DUV.obj E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) →+ (E ⟶ F⟦n + 1⟧)),
      (iU ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O U DU aU =
          derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O (U ⊓ V) DUV aUV) ∧
      (iV ≫ derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O V DV aV =
          -derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O (U ⊓ V) DUV aUV) ∧
      ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
        Function.Exact
            (fun x : E ⟶ F⟦n⟧ =>
              ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O U DU aU).app E ≫ x,
                (derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O V DV aV).app E ≫ x))
            (fun w : (DU.obj E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) × (DV.obj E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) =>
              iU.app E ≫ w.1 + iV.app E ≫ w.2) ∧
          Function.Exact
            (fun w : (DU.obj E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) × (DV.obj E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) =>
              iU.app E ≫ w.1 + iV.app E ≫ w.2)
            (boundary E F n) ∧
          Function.Exact (boundary E F n)
            (fun x : E ⟶ F⟦n + 1⟧ =>
              ((derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O U DU aU).app E ≫ x,
                (derivedExtensionRestrictionCounit O V DV aV).app E ≫ x))
declarations.comment: long exact sequence, extension-by-zero form of the Ext groups

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtensionByZero.exists_mayerVietoris_ext_longExactSequence_restrictions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BW, with every map of the sequence named.** For a ringed space covered by two
open subspaces `U` and `V` and objects `E`, `F` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the Mayer--Vietoris sequence

`⋯ ⟶ Ext^{n-1}(E|_{U∩V}, F|_{U∩V}) ⟶ Ext^n(E, F) ⟶
  Ext^n(E|_U, F|_U) × Ext^n(E|_V, F|_V) ⟶ Ext^n(E|_{U∩V}, F|_{U∩V}) ⟶ ⋯`

is exact at each of its three kinds of spot and in every integer degree, its first map is
the pair of the two restrictions and its second map is the difference of two further
restrictions to the intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mayerVietoris_ext_longExactSequence_restrictions (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (restriction : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          (E ⟶ F⟦n⟧) →+
            (ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O U).obj E) ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F) n ×
              ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E)
                ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F) n))
      (restrictionUW : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O U).obj E) ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F) n →+
            ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E)
              ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F) n)
      (restrictionVW : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E) ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F) n →+
            ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E)
              ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F) n)
      (difference : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          (ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O U).obj E) ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F) n ×
              ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E)
                ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F) n) →+
            ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E)
              ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F) n)
      (boundary : ∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj E)
              ((derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V)).obj F) n →+ (E ⟶ F⟦n + 1⟧)),
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ) (x : E ⟶ F⟦n⟧),
          restriction E F n x =
            (ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O U),
              ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O V))) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ) (x : E ⟶ F⟦n⟧),
          restrictionUW E F n (ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O U)) =
            ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V))) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ) (x : E ⟶ F⟦n⟧),
          restrictionVW E F n (ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O V)) =
            ShiftedHom.map x (derivedRestriction O (U ⊓ V))) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ)
          (xU : ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O U).obj E)
            ((derivedRestriction O U).obj F) n)
          (xV : ShiftedHom ((derivedRestriction O V).obj E)
            ((derivedRestriction O V).obj F) n),
          difference E F n (xU, xV) =
            restrictionUW E F n xU - restrictionVW E F n xV) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          Function.Exact (restriction E F n) (difference E F n)) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          Function.Exact (difference E F n) (boundary E F n)) ∧
      (∀ (E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (n : ℤ),
          Function.Exact (boundary E F n) (restriction E F (n + 1)))
declarations.comment: the long exact sequence, with its first map the pair of the restrictions to the two opens and its second map the difference of two restrictions to their intersection

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LinearMayerVietoris.linearUnboundedMayerVietoris_longExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BX, the long exact cohomology sequence.** Let `X` be a ringed space covered by
two open subsets `U` and `V`, and let `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.  There is a natural transformation
`δ : RΓ(U ∩ V, -) ⟶ RΓ(X, -)[1]` such that, for every object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)`,

* `RΓ(X, E) ⟶ RΓ(U, E) ⊕ RΓ(V, E) ⟶ RΓ(U ∩ V, E) ⟶ RΓ(X, E)[1]` is a distinguished
  triangle in `D(A)`, the first two maps being the restrictions with the usual sign;
* writing `H^n(W, E) = H^n(RΓ(W, E))`, the sequence
  `H^n(X, E) ⟶ H^n(U, E) ⊕ H^n(V, E) ⟶ H^n(U ∩ V, E) ⟶ H^{n+1}(X, E) ⟶
    H^{n+1}(U, E) ⊕ H^{n+1}(V, E)`
  is exact for every `n ∈ ℤ`, the connecting map being the one induced by `δ`; as `n` varies
  these windows make up the whole long exact Mayer--Vietoris sequence;
* every map of the long exact sequence is natural in `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearUnboundedMayerVietoris_longExact (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ δ : derivedLinearSections X (U ⊓ V) ⟶ derivedLinearSections X ⊤ ⋙
          shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) (1 : ℤ),
      (∀ E, Triangle.mk
        (biprod.lift ((derivedLinearRestriction X (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).app E)
          ((derivedLinearRestriction X (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).app E))
        (biprod.desc ((derivedLinearRestriction X (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)).app E)
          (-((derivedLinearRestriction X (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)).app E)))
        (δ.app E) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X)))) ∧
      (∀ E (n₀ n₁ : ℤ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁),
        (ComposableArrows.mk₄ (cohomologyToBiprod X U V n₀ E) (cohomologyFromBiprod X U V n₀ E)
          (cohomologyConnecting X U V δ n₀ n₁ h E) (cohomologyToBiprod X U V n₁ E)).Exact) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) {E E'} (φ : E ⟶ E'),
        cohomologyToBiprod X U V n E ≫
            biprod.map ((linearCohomology X U n).map φ) ((linearCohomology X V n).map φ) =
          (linearCohomology X ⊤ n).map φ ≫ cohomologyToBiprod X U V n E' ∧
        cohomologyFromBiprod X U V n E ≫ (linearCohomology X (U ⊓ V) n).map φ =
          biprod.map ((linearCohomology X U n).map φ) ((linearCohomology X V n).map φ) ≫
            cohomologyFromBiprod X U V n E') ∧
      (∀ (n₀ n₁ : ℤ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) {E E'} (φ : E ⟶ E'),
        cohomologyConnecting X U V δ n₀ n₁ h E ≫ (linearCohomology X ⊤ n₁).map φ =
          (linearCohomology X (U ⊓ V) n₀).map φ ≫ cohomologyConnecting X U V δ n₀ n₁ h E')
declarations.comment: the triangle and the long exact cohomology sequence, functorial in E, in D(A)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LinearMayerVietoris.linearUnboundedMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space covered by two open subsets `U` and `V`, and let `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
The restriction maps of the `A`-linear derived sections functors, with the usual sign on the
overlap, fit into a distinguished triangle in the derived category of `A`-modules, naturally in
the object of `D(𝒪_X)`: the connecting map is a natural transformation and the other four maps
are the right-derived restrictions.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearUnboundedMayerVietoris (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ δ : derivedLinearSections X (U ⊓ V) ⟶ derivedLinearSections X ⊤ ⋙
          shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) (1 : ℤ),
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk
        (biprod.lift ((derivedLinearRestriction X (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).app E)
          ((derivedLinearRestriction X (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).app E))
        (biprod.desc ((derivedLinearRestriction X (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)).app E)
          (-((derivedLinearRestriction X (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)).app E)))
        (δ.app E) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X)))
declarations.comment: the triangle, in D(A), A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceMayerVietoris.relativeUnboundedMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BX for a cover of an arbitrary open.** Let `X` be a ringed space and let
`W = U ∪ V` be an open subset written as the union of two open subsets.  For any choice of
derived sections functors over `W`, `U`, `V` and `U ∩ V` — that is, any right derived functors
of degreewise sections along the quasi-isomorphisms — the right-derived restriction maps, with
the usual sign on the overlap, fit into a distinguished triangle in the derived category of
abelian groups, naturally in the object of `D(𝒪_X)`: the connecting map is a natural
transformation and the other four maps are natural transformations of the given functors.
Applying the cohomological functors gives the functorial Mayer--Vietoris long exact
sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeUnboundedMayerVietoris (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (U V W : Opens X.carrier) (hUV : U ⊔ V = W)
    (RW RU RV RUV : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaves X) ⥤ DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (aW : sectionsComplexDerived X W ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RW)
    (aU : sectionsComplexDerived X U ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RU)
    (aV : sectionsComplexDerived X V ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RV)
    (aUV : sectionsComplexDerived X (U ⊓ V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RUV)
    [RW.IsRightDerivedFunctor aW
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ δ : RUV ⟶ RW ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (1 : ℤ),
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk
        (biprod.lift
          ((RW.rightDerivedNatTrans RU aW aU
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (le_sup_left.trans hUV.le : U ≤ W)))).app E)
          ((RW.rightDerivedNatTrans RV aW aV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (le_sup_right.trans hUV.le : V ≤ W)))).app E))
        (biprod.desc
          ((RU.rightDerivedNatTrans RUV aU aUV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)))).app E)
          (-((RV.rightDerivedNatTrans RUV aV aUV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)))).app E)))
        (δ.app E) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment:
the triangle, for a pair of opens covering an arbitrary open, not only the whole
space

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceMayerVietoris.unboundedMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BX.** Let `X` be a ringed space covered by two open subsets `U` and `V`.  For
any choice of derived sections functors over `X`, `U`, `V` and `U ∩ V` — that is, any right
derived functors of degreewise sections along the quasi-isomorphisms — the right-derived
restriction maps, with the usual sign on the overlap, fit into a distinguished triangle in the
derived category of abelian groups, naturally in the object of `D(𝒪_X)`: the connecting map is
a natural transformation and the other four maps are natural transformations of the given
functors.  The functorial Mayer--Vietoris long exact cohomology sequence obtained from the
triangle is `Stacks.Cohomology.LinearMayerVietoris.linearUnboundedMayerVietoris_longExact`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unboundedMayerVietoris (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (U V : Opens X.carrier)
    (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (RX RU RV RUV : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaves X) ⥤ DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (aX : sectionsComplexDerived X ⊤ ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RX)
    (aU : sectionsComplexDerived X U ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RU)
    (aV : sectionsComplexDerived X V ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RV)
    (aUV : sectionsComplexDerived X (U ⊓ V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RUV)
    [RX.IsRightDerivedFunctor aX
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ δ : RUV ⟶ RX ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (1 : ℤ),
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk
        (biprod.lift
          ((RX.rightDerivedNatTrans RU aX aU
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)))).app E)
          ((RX.rightDerivedNatTrans RV aX aV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)))).app E))
        (biprod.desc
          ((RU.rightDerivedNatTrans RUV aU aUV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)))).app E)
          (-((RV.rightDerivedNatTrans RUV aV aUV
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            (sectionsRestrictionDerived X (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)))).app E)))
        (δ.app E) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment: the triangle, in the derived category of abelian groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceInverseSystems.homology_isLimit_of_local_rlim_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BY.** Cohomology of the termwise inverse limit is the inverse limit of the
cohomology sheaves under local first-derived-limit vanishing and eventual stability.
declarations.statement:
theorem homology_isLimit_of_local_rlim_vanishing
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    (m : ℤ) (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (n₀ : ℕ)
    (hneg2 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ InverseLimits.sectionsComplexFunctor (structureSheafRing X) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval Ab.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 2))))
    (hneg1 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ InverseLimits.sectionsComplexFunctor (structureSheafRing X) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval Ab.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 1))))
    (hHneg1 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ InverseLimits.sectionsComplexFunctor (structureSheafRing X) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 1))))
    (hstable : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n₀ ≤ n), IsIso
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).map
        ((InverseLimits.sectionsComplexFunctor (structureSheafRing X) U).map
          (F.map (homOfLE hn).op)))) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).mapCone
          (limit.cone F)))
declarations.comment: canonical cohomology-limit comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceInverseSystems.homology_limit_projection_isIso_of_local_rlim_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08BY.** The projection from the limit of degree-`m` cohomology sheaves to the
stable stage is an isomorphism when the transition maps are locally isomorphisms on a
basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem homology_limit_projection_isIso_of_local_rlim_vanishing
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    (m : ℤ) (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (n₀ : ℕ)
    (hstable : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n₀ ≤ n), IsIso
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).map
        ((InverseLimits.sectionsComplexFunctor (structureSheafRing X) U).map
          (F.map (homOfLE hn).op)))) :
    IsIso (limit.π (F ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m) (op n₀))
declarations.comment: projection to the stable stage

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.globalSectionsToAlternatingCech
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08C0.** The functorial map from the complex of global sections to the
total alternating Čech complex: in each cohomological degree a section is sent, in Čech degree
zero, to its restrictions to the members of the family.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def globalSectionsToAlternatingCech :
    globalSectionsUliftComplexFunctor.{u, v, w} X ⟶ alternatingCechTotalComplexFunctor U

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.globalSectionsToAlternatingCech_app_f
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08C0.** In every cohomological degree the canonical map restricts a
global section into alternating Čech degree zero and includes that summand into the total
complex; in particular all of its positive Čech components vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma globalSectionsToAlternatingCech_app_f
    (K : CochainComplex ((Opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w}) ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    ((globalSectionsToAlternatingCech X U).app K).f n =
      globalSectionsAlternatingCechRestrictionInt X U (K.X n) ≫
        ((alternatingCechBicomplexFunctor U).obj K).ιTotal (up ℤ) 0 n n (by simp)
declarations.comment: degree-zero restrictions and vanishing higher components

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechToDerivedGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08C1.** For a ringed space `(X, O_X)` and a finite open covering `U`
of `X`, the total alternating Čech complex of an unbounded complex of `O_X`-modules has a
canonical map to its derived global sections, functorial in the complex and compatible with
the augmentation of Tag 08C0.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def alternatingCechToDerivedGlobalSections :
    AlternatingCechToDerivedGlobalSections X R

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.isIso_alternatingCechToDerivedComparison_of_acyclicBasis
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08C2]** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, let `U : I → Opens X` be a finite
open covering of `X` and let `F^•` be a complex of `O_X`-modules. Let `B` be a set of open
subsets of `X` such that every open of `X` is a union of members of `B`, such that every finite
intersection of members of the covering lies in `B`, and such that for every `W ∈ B` and every
`p > 0` the cohomology groups `H^p(W, F^q)`, `H^p(W, Coker(F^{q-1} → F^q))` and
`H^p(W, H^q(F))` all vanish. Then the comparison map
`Tot(Č_alt^•(U, F^•)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F^•)` of Tag 08C1 is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_alternatingCechToDerivedComparison_of_acyclicBasis
    {I : Type u} [Finite I] (U : I → Opens X) (hU : (⊤ : Opens X) = iSup U)
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} R) ℤ)
    (B : Set (Opens X)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (h_inter : ∀ (p : ℕ) (s : Fin (p + 1) → I), (⨅ k, U (s k)) ∈ B)
    (h_terms : ∀ W ∈ B, ∀ (q : ℤ) (p : ℕ), 0 < p →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation R (op W)).rightDerived p).obj (F.X q)))
    (h_cokernels : ∀ W ∈ B, ∀ (q : ℤ) (p : ℕ), 0 < p →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation R (op W)).rightDerived p).obj
        (cokernel (F.d (q - 1) q))))
    (h_homology : ∀ W ∈ B, ∀ (q : ℤ) (p : ℕ), 0 < p →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation R (op W)).rightDerived p).obj (F.homology q))) :
    IsIso ((alternatingCechToDerivedComparison X R U hU).app F)

declarations.name: StrictlyPerfect.isStrictlyPerfect_mappingCone
declarations.doc:
The cone on a morphism of strictly perfect complexes is strictly perfect.

The cone `C(f)` is `CochainComplex.mappingCone f`, whose `n`-th term is `L^n ⊕ K^{n+1}`. The
hypothesis `HasHomotopyCofiber f` is the (automatically satisfied, since the category has
binary biproducts) condition ensuring the mapping cone exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictlyPerfect_mappingCone {K L : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, w} X) ℤ}
    (f : K ⟶ L) [HomologicalComplex.HasHomotopyCofiber f]
    (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect K) (hL : IsStrictlyPerfect L) :
    IsStrictlyPerfect (CochainComplex.mappingCone f)

declarations.name: StrictlyPerfect.exists_over_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08C6.** Let `X` be a ringed space, `p : 𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` an epimorphism of `𝒪_X`-modules and
`f : ℰ ⟶ ℱ` a morphism out of a direct summand of a finite free `𝒪_X`-module. Then every point
of `X` has an open neighbourhood `U` and a morphism `l : ℰ|_U ⟶ 𝒢|_U` with `l ≫ p|_U = f|_U`.

The ring universe, the space universe and the module universe are independent; the price is the
two sheafification hypotheses, which are what make `Mod(𝒪_X)` abelian and are Stacks' standing
convention. See the module docstring for how the module universe is freed and for the two other
carriers of this tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_over_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree {E F G : OXMod.{u, w} X} (f : E ⟶ F)
    (p : G ⟶ F) [Epi p] (hE : IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree E) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ l : E.over U ⟶ G.over U, l ≫ p.over U = f.over U
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary module universe

declarations.name: StrictlyPerfect.exists_local_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree
declarations.doc:
Given `α : E ⟶ F` and an epimorphism `p : G ⟶ F` of `O_X`-modules with `E` a direct summand of
a finite free `O_X`-module, a factorisation of `α` through `p` exists locally on `X`: every point
has an open neighbourhood `U` and a morphism `β : E|_U ⟶ G|_U` with `β ≫ p|_U = α|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree {E F G : OXMod.{r, r} X}
    (hE : IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree E) (α : E ⟶ F) (p : G ⟶ F) [Epi p] (x : X.carrier) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ β : (restrictModules X U).obj E ⟶ (restrictModules X U).obj G,
        β ≫ (restrictModules X U).map p = (restrictModules X U).map α
declarations.comment: module universe = ring universe, space universe free, stated through `restrictModules`. Strictly more general than the collapsed form in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/PseudoCoherent/StrictlyPerfectLift.lean`, strictly less than the arbitrary-module-universe form in `StrictlyPerfectLiftModuleUniverse.lean`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08C6.** Let `X` be a ringed space, let `p : 𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` be an epimorphism of
`𝒪_X`-modules and let `f : ℰ ⟶ ℱ` be a map out of a direct summand of a finite free
`𝒪_X`-module. Then every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood over which `f` factors
through `p`.

Writing `ℰ` as a retract `(i, r)` of `𝒪_X^{⊕ n}`, it is enough to lift `r ≫ f` and compose
the lift with `i`, since `i ≫ r = 𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_lift_of_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree
    {E F G : StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X} (f : E ⟶ F) (p : G ⟶ F) [Epi p]
    (hE : StrictlyPerfect.IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree E) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ l : (restrictModules X U).obj E ⟶ (restrictModules X U).obj G,
        l ≫ (restrictModules X U).map p = (restrictModules X U).map f
declarations.comment: all three universes collapsed (space = ring = module), stated through `restrictModules`. The module-universe-free form is in `StacksFrontier/Algebra/Homology/StrictlyPerfectLiftModuleUniverse.lean`; neither subsumes the other.

declarations.name: StrictlyPerfect.LocalLifting.exists_local_lift
declarations.doc:
A map from a direct summand of a finite free module lifts locally through
any epimorphism of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_lift [Epi p] (hE : IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree E) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ l : E.over U ⟶ G.over U, l ≫ p.over U = f.over U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_isZero_homology
declarations.doc:
A map from a strictly perfect complex concentrated in degrees at least
`a` is locally null-homotopic if the target's cohomology vanishes in those
degrees.

This is the ringed-space-facing name for
`Stacks.Cohomology.LocalNullHomotopy.exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_isZero_homology`, which
carries the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_isZero_homology (a : ℤ)
    (hE : StrictlyPerfect.IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hE₀ : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hF : ∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero (F.homology i)) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_acyclic
declarations.doc:
A map from a strictly perfect complex to an acyclic complex is locally
null-homotopic.

This is the ringed-space-facing name for
`Stacks.Cohomology.LocalNullHomotopy.exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_acyclic`, which carries the
proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_acyclic
    (hE : StrictlyPerfect.IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hF : F.Acyclic) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_lift_homotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08C8.** Let `X` be a ringed space, let `α : ℰ ⟶ ℱ` be a morphism of complexes of
`𝒪_X`-modules with `ℰ` strictly perfect and `ℰ^j = 0` for `j < a`, and let `f : 𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` be a
morphism of complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules which is an isomorphism on cohomology in every degree
above `a` and an epimorphism on cohomology in degree `a`. Then every point of `X` has an open
neighbourhood `U` carrying a morphism `β : ℰ|_U ⟶ 𝒢|_U` with `β ≫ f|_U` homotopic to `α|_U`.

The mapping cone `C(f)` has vanishing cohomology in degrees at least `a`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isZero_homology_mappingCone`), so Stacks 08C7 makes the
composite `α ≫ inr f` null-homotopic over some open neighbourhood `U` of the given point. Hence
`α|_U` composed with the second map of the distinguished triangle `𝒢|_U ⟶ ℱ|_U ⟶ C(f|_U)` is
zero in the homotopy category over `U`, and `Triangle.coyoneda_exact₂` factors it through
`f|_U`; any representative `β` of that factorization satisfies the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_local_lift_homotopy
    {E F G : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ} (α : E ⟶ F) (f : G ⟶ F) (a : ℤ)
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hEa : ∀ j : ℤ, j < a → IsZero (E.X j))
    (hf_gt : ∀ j : ℤ, a < j → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f j))
    (hf_a : Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f a)) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ β : ((overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
          ((overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G,
        Nonempty (Homotopy
          (β ≫ ((overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
          (((overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α))

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherence.DerivedCharacterization.exists_local_lift_homotopy
declarations.doc:
A map from a strictly perfect complex lifts locally up to homotopy through a map that is
cohomologically an isomorphism above the lower bound and surjective at the lower bound.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_lift_homotopy (α : E ⟶ F) (f : G ⟶ F) (a : ℤ)
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hEa : ∀ j : ℤ, j < a → IsZero (E.X j))
    (hf_gt : ∀ j : ℤ, a < j → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f j))
    (hf_a : Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f a)) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ β : ((overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
          ((overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G,
        Nonempty (Homotopy
          (β ≫ ((overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
          (((overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_derived_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08C9, part (2).** Let `α : ℰ ⟶ ℱ` be a morphism of complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules with
`ℰ` strictly perfect whose image in the derived category of `X` is zero. Then every point of `X`
has an open neighbourhood over which `α` is homotopic to zero.

The image of `α` in the derived category vanishes, so its image in the homotopy category is
killed by a quasi-isomorphism `t : 𝒵 ⟶ ℰ`; that is, `t ≫ α` is null-homotopic. Stacks 08C8,
applied to the identity of `ℰ` and to `t`, produces over some open neighbourhood `U` a map
`β : ℰ|_U ⟶ 𝒵|_U` with `β ≫ t|_U` homotopic to the identity, and
`CochainComplex.nonempty_homotopy_zero_of_lift_homotopy_id` concludes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_local_homotopy_zero_of_derived_eq_zero
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] {E F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ}
    (α : E ⟶ F) (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hα : DerivedCategory.Q.map α = 0) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (structureSheafOfRings X) U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: local_null_homotopy

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_complex_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08C9, part (1).** Let `ℰ`, `ℱ` be complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules with `ℰ` strictly
perfect and let `α : ℰ ⟶ ℱ` be a morphism in the derived category of `X`. Then every point of `X`
has an open neighbourhood `U` over which `α` is induced by a morphism of complexes
`β : ℰ|_U ⟶ ℱ|_U`, the comparison being made through the canonical isomorphism
`CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors` of the exact functor `restrictModules X U`.

The exactness of restriction, which is what makes that comparison available, is part of the
assertion; the witnesses are the instances
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.restrictModules_additive`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.restrictModules_preservesFiniteLimits` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.restrictModules_preservesFiniteColimits`, and the content is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_local_complex_map_of_instances`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_local_complex_map [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    {E F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ} (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (hadd : (restrictModules.{u, u} X U).Additive)
        (hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits (restrictModules.{u, u} X U))
        (hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits (restrictModules.{u, u} X U)),
        letI := hadd
        letI := hlim
        letI := hcolim
        ∃ β : ((restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
            ((restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F,
          (restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫
              (restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app F =
            (restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app E ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map β
declarations.comment: local_representation

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.exists_local_complex_map
declarations.doc:
A derived morphism out of a strictly perfect complex is locally represented by a morphism of
complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_complex_map (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (hadd : (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).Additive)
        (hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U))
        (hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U)),
        letI := hadd
        letI := hlim
        letI := hcolim
        ∃ β : ((RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
            ((RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F,
          (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫
              (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app F =
          (RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X U).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app E ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map β
declarations.comment: local_representation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom
declarations.doc:
A complex of `𝒪_X`-modules is `m`-pseudo-coherent if every point of `X` has an open
neighbourhood on which the complex admits a strictly perfect approximation in degrees at
least `m`: a map from a strictly perfect complex which is an isomorphism on cohomology in every
degree above `m` and an epimorphism on cohomology in degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom
    (E : CochainComplex (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X) ℤ) (m : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentComplex
declarations.doc:
A complex of `𝒪_X`-modules is pseudo-coherent if it is `m`-pseudo-coherent for every
integer `m`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsPseudoCoherentComplex
    (E : CochainComplex (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X) ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
An object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules is `m`-pseudo-coherent if it is
represented by an `m`-pseudo-coherent complex.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsPseudoCoherentFrom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X)) (m : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3), m-pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
An object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules is pseudo-coherent if it is represented by
a pseudo-coherent complex.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsPseudoCoherent
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} X)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3), pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be an `m`-pseudo-coherent object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules. Then every
complex of `𝒪_X`-modules representing `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_local_derived_approximation
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be an object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules and suppose that every point of
`X` has an open neighbourhood `U` on which some strictly perfect complex `𝒫` maps to `E|_U` in
`D(𝒪_U)` by a morphism which is an isomorphism on cohomology above `m` and an epimorphism in degree
`m`. Then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent. Here `E|_U` is presented as `Q(𝒦|_U)` for a complex `𝒦`
representing `E`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_local_derived_approximation
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E)
    (h : ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ P : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)) ℤ,
        IsStrictlyPerfect P ∧
        ∃ α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex K U),
          (∀ j : ℤ, m < j → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).map α)) ∧
          Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map α)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherence.DerivedCharacterization.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_local_derived_approximation
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CC part (1).** Local strictly perfect approximations in the derived category make a
derived object `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_local_derived_approximation
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) (m : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u} X) ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E)
    (h : ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ P : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)) ℤ,
        IsStrictlyPerfect P ∧
        ∃ α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.restrictComplex K U),
          (∀ j : ℤ, m < j → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).map α)) ∧
          Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map α)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X) E m
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherence.DerivedCharacterization.isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CC part (2).** Every complex representing an `m`-pseudo-coherent derived object is
`m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_iso (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X) E m)
    (K : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u} X) ℤ) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom (X := X) K m
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₃_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CD, part (1).** If the first term of a distinguished triangle in the derived
category of `𝒪_X`-modules is `(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent and the second is `m`-pseudo-coherent,
then the third is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₃_of_distinguished (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ (m + 1)) (hL : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₂_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CD, part (2).** If the first and third terms of a distinguished triangle in the
derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules are `m`-pseudo-coherent, then so is the second.

Apply part (1) to the inverse rotation of the triangle, whose first two terms are `M[-1]` and
`K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₂_of_distinguished (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ m) (hM : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ m
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₁_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CD, part (3).** If the second term of a distinguished triangle in the derived
category of `𝒪_X`-modules is `(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent and the third is `m`-pseudo-coherent, then
the first is `(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent.

Apply part (1) to the rotation of the triangle, whose third term is `K[1]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₁_of_distinguished (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hL : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ (m + 1)) (hM : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ (m + 1)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064X on a ringed space: both summands of an `m`-pseudo-coherent binary biproduct in
`D(𝒪_X)` are `m`-pseudo-coherent.**

`m`-pseudo-coherence is local
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_local_restrict`), so it is enough to find,
around every point, an open `U` on which the restriction of the summand is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
Choose `U` so that `A ⊞ B` has no cohomology above some degree there
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_isZero_homology_gt_derivedRestrict`); restriction is
additive, so `(A ⊞ B)|_U ≅ A|_U ⊞ B|_U`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_biprod_of_isZero_homology_gt` applies on
`X|U`.

This is also **Stacks 08CE** for a fixed degree: the ringed-space statement of 08CE at a fixed
degree is literally this one, and both of its conclusions are proved here at once.
declarations.comment: m-pseudo-coherent, both summands

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_left_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08CE.** The first summand of an `m`-pseudo-coherent biproduct is
`m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_left_of_biprod
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (h : IsPseudoCoherentFrom (K ⊞ L) m) : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m
declarations.comment: m-pseudo-coherent, first summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_right_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08CE.** The second summand of an `m`-pseudo-coherent biproduct is
`m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_right_of_biprod
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (h : IsPseudoCoherentFrom (K ⊞ L) m) : IsPseudoCoherentFrom L m
declarations.comment: m-pseudo-coherent, second summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherent_left_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08CE.** The first summand of a pseudo-coherent biproduct is
pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_left_of_biprod
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (h : IsPseudoCoherent (K ⊞ L)) :
    IsPseudoCoherent K
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent, first summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherent_right_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08CE.** The second summand of a pseudo-coherent biproduct is
pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_right_of_biprod
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (h : IsPseudoCoherent (K ⊞ L)) :
    IsPseudoCoherent L
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent, second summand

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherence.Summands.isPseudoCoherent_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CE.** Both summands of a pseudo-coherent binary biproduct in `D(O_X)` are
pseudo-coherent.

Pseudo-coherence is `m`-pseudo-coherence in every degree, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherent_iff_forall`, and in each degree the two summands
are `m`-pseudo-coherent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_biprod`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_biprod {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    [∀ V : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict V.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (A B : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (A ⊞ B)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent A ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent B
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent, both summands

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasTorAmplitudeIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CG (1).** An object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` *has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`* if, for every
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` and every integer `i` outside `[a, b]`, the cohomology sheaf
`H^i(E ⊗^{L}_{𝒪_X} ℱ)` vanishes.

The derived tensor product is the one carried by `D`; see the implementation notes of this file
for what the certificate buys and for why the interval is not assumed nonempty.
declarations.statement:
public def HasTorAmplitudeIn (D : CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{d, u} X)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (a b : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: tor amplitude in an interval

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CG (2).** An object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` *has finite Tor dimension* if it has Tor
amplitude in some interval `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
public def HasFiniteTorDimension (D : CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{d, u} X)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite tor dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasTorDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**The last sentence of Stacks 08CG.** An `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` *has Tor dimension at most `n`* if
`ℱ[0]`, viewed in `D(𝒪_X)`, has Tor amplitude in `[-n, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
public def HasTorDimensionLE (D : CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{d, u} X)
    (F : OXMod.{u, u} X) (n : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: tor dimension of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CG (3).** An object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` *locally has finite Tor dimension* if there is
an open covering `X = ⋃ U i` such that `E|_{U i}` has finite Tor dimension for every `i`.

A derived tensor product is needed on each open subspace, so the certificate is a family `D`
indexed by the opens of `X`; `E|_{U i}` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.derivedRestrictModules`.
declarations.statement:
public def LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
    (D : ∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{d', u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) : Prop
declarations.comment: locally finite tor dimension

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.HasTorAmplitudeIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CG (1)**, for a derived tensor product given as a bifunctor on `D(A)`. An object
`E` of `D(A)` *has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`* when `H^i(E ⊗^{L} F) = 0` for every object `F` of
`A` and every `i` outside `[a, b]`, the object `F` being read in degree `0`.

On `A = OXMod X` this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasTorAmplitudeIn` with `T` the
certificate's `derivedTensor`, and the identification is `Iff.rfl`;
`hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_hasTorAmplitude` identifies it with the `TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude` of
Stacks 08CJ.

This form is stated for a bifunctor `T` on the derived category of an arbitrary abelian
category. `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasTorAmplitudeIn`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/TorDimension.lean`) is the same clause for a bundle that
also records an underived tensor product, a comparison and an `IsLeftDerivedFunctor` field, and
`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude`
(`StacksFrontier/Topology/Sheaves/Cohomology/TorAmplitude/OnARingedSpace.lean`) is the clause for
the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU.
declarations.statement:
public def HasTorAmplitudeIn
    (T : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory A)
    (E : DerivedCategory A) (a b : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: tor amplitude in an interval, for a derived tensor bifunctor T over an arbitrary abelian category: H^i(E ⊗^L F) = 0 for every object F in degree 0 and every i outside [a, b]; at the derivedTensor of AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring it is CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.HasTorAmplitudeIn by Iff.rfl

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(O_X)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` when its derived tensor product with
every `O_X`-module, placed in degree `0`, has vanishing cohomology in every degree outside
`[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
def HasTorAmplitude (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) (a b : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: tor amplitude in an interval, at the derived tensor product of Tag 06YU

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(O_X)` has finite Tor dimension when it has Tor amplitude in some interval
`[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasFiniteTorDimension (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite tor dimension, at the derived tensor product of Tag 06YU

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
An `O_X`-module `F` has Tor dimension at most `n` when `F[0]`, viewed in `D(O_X)`, has Tor
amplitude in `[-n, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
def HasTorDimensionLE (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
    (F : OXMod.{u} X) (n : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: tor dimension of a module, at the derived tensor product of Tag 06YU

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(O_X)` locally has finite Tor dimension when its restriction to each member of
some open cover has finite Tor dimension.
declarations.statement:
def LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) : Prop
declarations.comment: locally finite tor dimension, at the Tag 06YU tensor on each open subspace

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.FlatCokernel.isFlat_cokernel_of_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CH.** The cokernel of the differential into the lowest degree of the Tor-amplitude
interval of a bounded above complex of flat `O_X`-modules is a flat `O_X`-module.

The complex is K-flat by Tag 06YQ, so the Tor-amplitude hypothesis makes the three-term
complex `K^{a-2} ⊗ F ⟶ K^{a-1} ⊗ F ⟶ K^a ⊗ F` exact for every `O_X`-module `F`. Hence
`Coker(d^{a-1}) ⊗ -` preserves monomorphisms, and being right exact as well it is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_cokernel_of_hasTorAmplitude
    (K : CochainComplex (Modules X) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (hbound : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.sheaf) (K.X i))
    (hamp : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.sheaf)
      (cokernel (K.d (a - 1) a))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.BoundedFlatRepresentative.hasTorAmplitude_iff_exists_flat_representative
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(O_X)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` exactly when some complex
of flat `O_X`-modules vanishing in every degree outside `[a, b]` represents it.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_iff_exists_flat_representative (E : DerivedCategory (Modules X))
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X E a b ↔
      ∃ K : CochainComplex (Modules X) ℤ,
        (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
          (O := X.sheaf) (K.X i)) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, i ∉ Set.Icc a b → IsZero (K.X i)) ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.FlatOpcycles.hasTorAmplitude_obj₃
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CJ (1) at the ringed-space Tor-amplitude predicate.** In a distinguished triangle
`K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K[1]` of `D(O_X)`, if `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a + 1, b + 1]` and `L` has Tor
amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `M` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.

This is `TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₃` read through
`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.FlatOpcycles.tensorSingleFunctor`, exactly as
`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.FlatOpcycles.hasTorAmplitude_obj₁` reads part (3) through it; the
only content is the translation between the two encodings of "outside `[a, b]`".
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₃
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₁ (a + 1) (b + 1))
    (hL : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₂ a b) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₃ a b
declarations.comment: (1), at the ringed-space Tor-amplitude predicate

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.FlatOpcycles.hasTorAmplitude_obj₂
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08CJ] (2) at the ringed-space Tor-amplitude predicate.** In a distinguished
triangle `K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K[1]` of `D(O_X)`, if `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` and `M` has Tor
amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `L` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.

This is `TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₂` read through `tensorSingleFunctor`; the only content
is the translation between the two encodings of "outside `[a, b]`".
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₂ (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (Modules X)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₁ a b)
    (hM : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₃ a b) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X T.obj₂ a b
declarations.comment: (2), at the ringed-space Tor-amplitude predicate

declarations.name: TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₃
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 08CJ (1): in a distinguished triangle `K → L → M → K[1]`, if `K` has
tor-amplitude in `[a+1, b+1]` and `L` has tor-amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `M` has
tor-amplitude in `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₃ (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory M))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₁ (a + 1) (b + 1))
    (hL : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₂ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₃ a b

declarations.name: TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₂
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 08CJ (2): in a distinguished triangle `K → L → M → K[1]`, if `K` and `M`
both have tor-amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `L` has tor-amplitude in `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₂ (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory M))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₁ a b)
    (hM : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₃ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₂ a b

declarations.name: TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₁
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 08CJ (3): in a distinguished triangle `K → L → M → K[1]`, if `L` has
tor-amplitude in `[a+1, b+1]` and `M` has tor-amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `K` has
tor-amplitude in `[a+1, b+1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₁ (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory M))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (a b : ℤ)
    (hL : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₂ (a + 1) (b + 1))
    (hM : HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₃ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derTensor T.obj₁ (a + 1) (b + 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_biprod
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08CK], from the summands to the sum.** If `K` and `L` have Tor amplitude in
`[a, b]` then so does `K ⊞ L`.

The split triangle `K ⟶ K ⊞ L ⟶ L ⟶ K⟦1⟧` is distinguished, so this is clause (2) of
[Stacks, Tag 08CJ].
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_biprod (a b : ℤ) (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude X K a b) (hL : HasTorAmplitude X L a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude X (K ⊞ L) a b
declarations.comment: from the summands to the sum, at the ringed-space Tor-amplitude predicate

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.hasFiniteTorDimension_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Finite Tor dimension passes from two summands to their sum.** The two intervals are
merged.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteTorDimension_biprod (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))
    (hK : HasFiniteTorDimension X K) (hL : HasFiniteTorDimension X L) :
    HasFiniteTorDimension X (K ⊞ L)
declarations.comment: finite Tor dimension, from the summands to the sum

declarations.name: Stacks.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Tag 08CK / Lemma 20.48.8).**  Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space
and `a ≤ b`.  We work with THE derived tensor product `- ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} -` on
`D(𝒪_X)`: it is given as a bifunctor `derivedTensor` whose flips
`- ⊗^L F = derivedTensor.flip.obj (single F)` are, together with the comparison
natural transformation `derivedTensorComparison F`, the **total left derived
functors** (`IsLeftDerivedFunctor`) of the underived tensor products `- ⊗ F`.
This universal property determines `derivedTensor` up to canonical isomorphism, so
it is genuinely the derived tensor product (introduced here as hypotheses rather
than as `axiom`s).

If the direct sum `K ⊕ L` (categorical biproduct `K ⊞ L`) has tor-amplitude in
`[a,b]`, then both `K` and `L` have tor-amplitude in `[a,b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_of_biprod
    (derivedTensor : DOX X ⥤ DOX X ⥤ DOX X)
    (a b : ℤ)
    (K L : DOX X) (h : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor a b (K ⊞ L)) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor a b K ∧ HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor a b L

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfectComplex
declarations.doc:
A complex is perfect if an open cover admits strictly perfect complexes mapping to its
restrictions by quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
def IsPerfectComplex {X : RingedSpace.{u, v}}
    (E : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, v} X) ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: perfect complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
declarations.doc: An object of the derived category is perfect if represented by a perfect complex.
declarations.comment: perfect derived-category objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfect_of_strictlyPerfect_local_models
declarations.doc:
An object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules which is, on an open covering of `X`,
isomorphic in the derived category to a strictly perfect complex is perfect.

The hypothesis fixes a complex `F` representing the object, and asks the local strictly perfect
models to be isomorphic, in the derived categories of the members of the covering, to the
restrictions of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_strictlyPerfect_local_models (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier, HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))
    (h : ∃ F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ,
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K) ∧
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens X.carrier), (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i : I, ∃ P : CochainComplex
            (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding)) ℤ,
            IsStrictlyPerfect P ∧
              Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅
                DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex F (U i)))) :
    IsPerfect K
declarations.comment: local_criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfectComplex_of_isPerfect_representation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CN.** Every complex representing a perfect object of the derived category of
`𝒪_X`-modules is itself a perfect complex.

Perfectness of `K` provides one perfect representative `E`. The isomorphism `Q(E) ≅ Q(F)` with
the complex `F` at hand is a roof of quasi-isomorphisms between `E` and `F`, and perfectness of
complexes is invariant under roofs.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectComplex_of_isPerfect_representation
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    {K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)} (hK : IsPerfect K)
    {F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ}
    (hF : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K)) :
    IsPerfectComplex F
declarations.comment: representative_independence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectFromTorAmplitude.isPerfect_of_hasTorAmplitude_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CP.** An object of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space with Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, for
integers `a ≤ b`, which is `(a - 1)`-pseudo-coherent, is perfect.

The pseudo-coherence supplies a representative `C` and, near every point, a strictly perfect
approximation of `C|_U` in degrees above `a - 1` with no terms above `b`; its brutal truncation
`σ^{≥a-1}P` is concentrated in `[a-1, b]` and still approximates above `a - 1`, and the
Tor-amplitude hypothesis makes the degree-`a` opcycles of that truncation flat, hence locally a
direct summand of a finite free module. That is what the truncation criterion consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_hasTorAmplitude_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hamp : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X E a b)
    (hpc : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E (a - 1)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect E

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.isPseudoCoherent_and_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CQ, the forward implication.** A perfect object of `D(O_X)` is pseudo-coherent and
locally has finite Tor dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_and_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_of_isPerfect
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X)) (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect E) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) E ∧
      LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension X E
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.isPerfect_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CQ, the converse implication.** A pseudo-coherent object of `D(O_X)` which locally has
finite Tor dimension is perfect.

Perfectness is local on the space
(`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexTriangles.isPerfect_of_local_isPerfect`), which is what makes
the per-member Tor-amplitude intervals of `LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension` usable: over a member `U`
of the cover witnessing finite Tor dimension there is a *single* interval `[a, b]`, and the
restriction of `E` to `X|_U` is still pseudo-coherent, hence `(a-1)`-pseudo-coherent, so Tag 08CP
applies there. The interval is widened to `[min a b, max a b]` so that it is nonempty, which Tag
08CP requires.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X))
    (hpc : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) E)
    (htor : LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension X E) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect E
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexTriangles.isPerfect_obj₃_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CR, third object.** The third object of a distinguished triangle is perfect if the
first two are. With perfect complexes `E₁`, `E₂` representing the first two vertices, the third
vertex is `Q` of the mapping cone of a chain map `γ : E₁ ⟶ G` with `E₂ ⟶ G` a quasi-isomorphism
(`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexTriangles.exists_mappingCone_iso_obj₃`); `G` is perfect along
with `E₂`, and the mapping cone of a morphism of perfect complexes is perfect
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfectComplex_mappingCone`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_obj₃_of_distinguished [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
  (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
  (h₁ : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₁) (h₂ :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₂) :
  Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₃
declarations.comment: third object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexTriangles.isPerfect_obj₂_of_distinguished
declarations.doc: **Tag 08CR, second object.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_obj₂_of_distinguished [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
  (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
  (h₁ : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₁) (h₃ :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₃) :
  Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₂
declarations.comment: second object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexTriangles.isPerfect_obj₁_of_distinguished
declarations.doc: **Tag 08CR, first object.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_obj₁_of_distinguished [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X)]
  (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X))) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
  (h₂ : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₂) (h₃ :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₃) :
  Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect T.obj₁
declarations.comment: first object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.isPerfect_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08CS.** If a binary biproduct in `D(O_X)` is perfect, then so are both of its summands.

By Tag 08CQ the biproduct is pseudo-coherent and locally of finite Tor dimension; both properties
pass to the summands, pseudo-coherence by Tag 08CE and locally finite Tor dimension by Tag 08CK;
and Tag 08CQ turns the pair back into perfectness of each summand.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_biprod (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u} X))
    (h : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (K ⊞ L)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect K ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect L

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseLimits.homology_isLimit_of_local_rlim_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CT.** The canonical cone from the degree-`m` cohomology of the termwise
inverse limit of an inverse system of complexes of modules on a ringed site to the
degree-`m` cohomologies is a limit cone, provided the first derived limits of the sections
vanish in degrees `m - 2` and `m - 1` and on the degree `m - 1` cohomology over a generating
family, and the degree-`m` cohomology of sections is constant from stage `n₀` on.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homology_isLimit_of_local_rlim_vanishing
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{t}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (m : ℤ) (B : Set X.C) (hB : X.J.HasEnoughObjects (· ∈ B))
    (hneg2 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ sectionsComplexFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval Ab.{t} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 2))))
    (hneg1 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ sectionsComplexFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval Ab.{t} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 1))))
    (hHneg1 : ∀ U ∈ B, IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
      (F ⋙ sectionsComplexFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{t} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (m - 1))))
    (n₀ : ℕ)
    (hstable : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n₀ ≤ n), IsIso
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{t} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).map
