        ((sectionsComplexFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).map
          (F.map (homOfLE hn).op)))) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{t} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).mapCone (limit.cone F)))
declarations.comment: canonical cohomology-limit comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseLimits.homology_limit_projection_isIso_of_local_rlim_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08CT.** The limit of the degree-`m` cohomology sheaves of an inverse system of
complexes of modules on a ringed site projects isomorphically to any stage from which the
degree-`m` cohomology of sections over a generating family is constant.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homology_limit_projection_isIso_of_local_rlim_vanishing
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{t}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (m : ℤ) (B : Set X.C) (hB : X.J.HasEnoughObjects (· ∈ B)) (n₀ : ℕ)
    (hstable : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n₀ ≤ n), IsIso
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor Ab.{t} (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m).map
        ((sectionsComplexFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).map
          (F.map (homOfLE hn).op)))) :
    IsIso (limit.π (F ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{t} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m) (op n₀))
declarations.comment: projection to a stable stage

declarations.name: Koszul.koszulIdealComplexSystem
declarations.doc: The canonical inverse system `I^•(f) ← I^•(f²) ← I^•(f³) ← ⋯`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def koszulIdealComplexSystem {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) :
    KoszulIdealComplexSystem f

declarations.name: Koszul.CechSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08CZ.** The standing situation of the section on Koszul complexes:
a commutative ring `A` and a finite sequence `f₁, …, f_r` of elements of `A`. The affine
scheme `X = Spec(A)`, the open `U = D(f₁) ∪ ⋯ ∪ D(f_r)` and the covering `𝒰` of `U` by the
standard opens `D(fᵢ)` are derived from these data.
declarations.statement: structure CechSituation

declarations.name: Koszul.alternatingCechComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D0.** The canonical identification between the colimit of the
contragredient Koszul complexes and the alternating Čech complex of `M^~`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def alternatingCechComplexIso {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A) :
    colimit (koszulHomDiagram f M) ≅ moduleAlternatingCechComplex f M

declarations.name: Koszul.alternatingCechComplexIso_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 08D0.** The identification is natural in the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem alternatingCechComplexIso_naturality {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A)
    (M N : ModuleCat.{v} A) (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (alternatingCechComplexIso f M).hom ≫ moduleAlternatingCechMap f g =
      koszulHomColimitMap f g ≫ (alternatingCechComplexIso f N).hom

declarations.name: Koszul.alternatingCechComplexIso_ι_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D0.** On the stage-`e` linear form `t` the identification takes the
value `(-1)^p t([i₀, …, iₚ]) / ∏ⱼ f(iⱼ)^(e+1)` at the tuple `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem alternatingCechComplexIso_ι_apply {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A)
    (e p : ℕ) (t : (koszulIdealComplexPower f e).X p →ₗ[A] M) (i : Fin (p + 1) → Fin r) :
    (((colimit.ι (koszulHomDiagram f M) e ≫
        (alternatingCechComplexIso f M).hom).f p) t).1 i =
      koszulCechFraction f M e p t i

declarations.name: Koszul.koszulHomColimitIsoAlternatingCechTotal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D1.** The filtered colimit of the Hom complexes from the powers
of the truncated Koszul complex is canonically isomorphic to the total alternating Čech complex
of the associated sheaf complex, naturally in the coefficient complex.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def koszulHomColimitIsoAlternatingCechTotal
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) :
    koszulHomColimitFunctor f ⋙
        (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} A) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (up ℤ) ≅
      alternatingCechTotalFunctor f

declarations.name: Koszul.CechSituation.isIso_linearAlternatingCechToDerivedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D2.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 08CZ], for a complex `F^•`
of quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-modules the comparison map `Tot(Č_alt^•(𝒰, F^•)) ⟶ RΓ(U, F^•)` of
[Stacks, Tag 08C1], taken in `D(A)`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_linearAlternatingCechToDerivedComparison (F : CochainComplex S.scheme.Modules ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n, (F.X n).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cech.linearAlternatingCechToDerivedComparison (TopCat.of S.scheme)
      S.scheme.ringCatSheaf S.baseCenter S.coverUlift S.iSup_coverUlift).app F)
declarations.comment: the canonical map in D(A) is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Koszul.CechSituation.alternatingCechTotalNatIsoDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D2.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 08CZ], the canonical
isomorphism `Tot(Č_alt^•(𝒰, F^•)) ≅ RΓ(U, F^•)` in `D(A)`, natural in the complex `F^•` of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-modules: its components are the comparison maps of [Stacks, Tag 08C1].
declarations.statement:
def alternatingCechTotalNatIsoDerivedSections :
    S.QuasicoherentComplex.ι ⋙
        Stacks.Cech.linearAlternatingCechDerivedFunctor (TopCat.of S.scheme)
          S.scheme.ringCatSheaf S.baseCenter S.coverUlift ≅
      S.QuasicoherentComplex.ι ⋙
        Stacks.Cech.linearUnboundedDerivedGlobalSectionsFunctor (TopCat.of S.scheme)
          S.scheme.ringCatSheaf S.baseCenter
declarations.comment: the isomorphism in D(A), functorial in F^•

declarations.name: Koszul.DerivedSystem.isIso_alternatingCechToDerivedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D2, in `D(Ab)`.**  In Situation 08CZ, the comparison map
`Tot(Č_alt(𝒰, ℱ^•)) ⟶ RΓ(U, ℱ^•)` of Tag 08C1 for the covering `𝒰` of `U` by the basic opens
`D(fᵢ)` is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)` for every complex `ℱ^•` of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_U`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_alternatingCechToDerivedComparison (f : Fin r → A)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (unionRingSheaf f)) ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, (K.X n).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechToDerivedComparison (unionSpace f)
      (unionRingSheaf f) (unionSpaceCover f) (iSup_unionSpaceCover f)).app K)
declarations.comment: the comparison map is an isomorphism, in D(Ab)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D3.** A complex of `𝒪_X`-modules on a scheme whose cohomology sheaves are all
quasi-coherent is canonically isomorphic to the derived inverse limit of the tower of its
canonical lower truncations `n ↦ τ_{≥ -n} E`.

The derived limit is presented by a distinguished triangle whose second map is the canonical
difference of the projections, and the map `c` is pinned down by the requirement that its
composites with the projections are the canonical truncation maps; the conclusion is that this
map is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)) (c : E ⟶ L)
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶
      L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
          (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
            (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).map
              (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)))
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
        (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves are all
quasi-coherent. Then the canonical map from `E` to a derived limit `L` of the tower
`n ↦ τ_{≥ -n} E` of canonical truncations from below is an isomorphism.

The derived limit is presented by its structural morphism `p` to the product of the tower and the
distinguished triangle `hL` characterising it; the map `c` out of `E` is the canonical one because
its composites with the product projections are required to be the truncation maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (c : E ⟶ L)
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).map
            (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower X.Modules E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasicoherentAmplitude.isGE_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D4] part (3), lower bound.** A total right derived functor preserves a lower
cohomological bound on a complex with quasi-coherent cohomology.

No product hypothesis on `F` and no vanishing hypothesis are needed: the K-injective complexes
compute any total right derived functor out of a Grothendieck abelian category, and a bounded
below object is represented by a K-injective complex in the same range.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGE_obj {B : Type*} [Category* B] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory B]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (alpha : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (a : ℤ) (hE : E.IsGE a) : (RF.obj E).IsGE a
declarations.comment: part (3), lower bound

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasicoherentAmplitude.isLE_obj_of_isZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D4] part (3), upper bound.** If the higher derived functors vanish from degree
`N` onward on quasi-coherent modules, a total right derived functor shifts an upper cohomological
bound by at most `N - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLE_obj_of_isZero {B : Type*} [Category* B] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasProductsOfShape ℕ B] [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) B]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) F]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (alpha : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ (M : X.Modules), M.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ (p : ℤ), (N : ℤ) ≤ p →
      IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b : ℤ) (hE : E.IsLE b) : (RF.obj E).IsLE (b + (N : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.comment: part (3), upper bound

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasicoherentAmplitude.isIso_homology_map_truncLE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D4] part (1).** A total right derived functor agrees in degrees at most `a` on
a complex with quasi-coherent cohomology and its canonical truncation in degrees at most `a`.

The third vertex of the truncation triangle at `a` is `≥ a + 1`, so by part (3) lower bound its
image under `RF` has no cohomology in degrees `i` and `i - 1` for `i ≤ a`, and the long exact
sequence makes the comparison both mono and epi.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_map_truncLE {B : Type*} [Category* B] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory B]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (alpha : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (a i : ℤ) (hi : i ≤ a) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app E)))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasicoherentAmplitude.isIso_homology_map_truncGE_of_isZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D4] part (2).** If the higher derived functors vanish from degree `N` onward
on quasi-coherent modules, then in degrees at least `b` a total right derived functor agrees on a
complex with quasi-coherent cohomology and its canonical truncation in degrees at least
`b - N + 1`.

The first vertex of the truncation triangle at `a = b - N + 1` is `≤ a - 1`, so by part (3) upper
bound its image under `RF` is `≤ a - 1 + N - 1 = b - 1`, hence has no cohomology in degrees `i`
and `i + 1` for `i ≥ b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_map_truncGE_of_isZero {B : Type*} [Category* B] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasProductsOfShape ℕ B] [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) B]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) F]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (alpha : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ (M : X.Modules), M.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ (p : ℤ), (N : ℤ) ≤ p →
      IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b i : ℤ) (hi : b ≤ i) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - (N : ℤ) + 1)).app E)))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
A total right derived functor of an additive functor out of the `𝒪_X`-modules of a scheme
preserves the lower end of the range of degrees in which an object with quasi-coherent cohomology
lives.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (a : ℤ) (hE : E.IsGE a) : (RF.obj E).IsGE a
declarations.comment: part (3), lower bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncLEι
declarations.doc:
A total right derived functor of an additive functor out of the `𝒪_X`-modules of a scheme
agrees in degrees at most `a` on an object with quasi-coherent cohomology and on its canonical
truncation in degrees at most `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncLEι
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (a i : ℤ) (hi : i ≤ a) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app E)))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_of_isZero_rightDerivedPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D4, part (3), the upper bound.** Let `X` be a scheme, let `F` be an
additive functor out of the `𝒪_X`-modules which preserves countable products, and let `RF` be a
total right derived functor of `F` on `D(𝒪_X)`. Suppose the higher right derived functors `R^pF`
vanish on every quasi-coherent module in every degree `p ≥ N`. If an object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` has
quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves and lives in degrees `≤ b`, then `RF(E)` lives in degrees
`≤ b + N - 1`.

The canonical truncation triangle `τ_{≤ b-1}E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥ b}E` reduces the claim to its third
vertex, concentrated in degree `b` and so covered by the vanishing hypothesis, and to its first
vertex, where the bound `b - 1 + N` — one worse, which is why the triangle is used — is supplied
by the `E = R\lim \tau_{\geq -n}E` argument: `E` is the derived limit of its truncations from
below ([Stacks, Tag 08D3]), `RF` carries that derived limit to a derived limit
([Stacks, Tag 08U1]), each `RF(τ_{≥ -n}E)` lives in degrees `≤ b + N - 1` because `τ_{≥ -n}E` is
bounded, and a derived limit of such a tower lives in degrees `≤ b + N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_of_isZero_rightDerivedPlus (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf, M.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ p : ℤ, (N : ℤ) ≤ p → IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b : ℤ) (hE : E.IsLE b) : (RF.obj E).IsLE (b + (N : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.comment: part (3), upper bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncGEπ_of_isZero_rightDerivedPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D4, part (2).** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_of_isZero_rightDerivedPlus`, the canonical
comparison
`H^i(RF(E)) ⟶ H^i(RF(τ_{≥ b - N + 1}E))` is an isomorphism for every `i ≥ b`.

Write `a = b - N + 1`. The canonical truncation triangle
`τ_{≤ a-1}E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥ a}E` goes to a distinguished triangle under `RF`, which is exact; its
first vertex has `RF`-image in degrees `≤ a - 1 + N - 1 = b - 1` by part (3), so `H^i` and
`H^{i+1}` vanish there for `i ≥ b`, and the long exact homology sequence makes the second map
invertible on `H^i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncGEπ_of_isZero_rightDerivedPlus
    (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf, M.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ p : ℤ, (N : ℤ) ≤ p → IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b i : ℤ) (hi : b ≤ i) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - (N : ℤ) + 1)).app E)))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_addCommGrpCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D4, part (3), the upper bound.** Let `X` be a scheme, let `F` be an additive
functor out of the `𝒪_X`-modules commuting with countable products, and let `(RF, alpha)` be a
total right derived functor of `F` on `D(𝒪_X)`. If `R ᵖ F` vanishes on quasi-coherent modules for
every `p ≥ N`, then `RF` carries an object with quasi-coherent cohomology lying in degrees `≤ b`
to one lying in degrees `≤ b + N - 1`.

The object is split by the truncation triangle at `b` into a part concentrated in degree `b` and a
part in degrees `≤ b - 1`. The second is handled by the derived limit of its truncation tower:
each stage is bounded, so the bounded statement applies with `N - 1`, [Stacks, Tag 08U1] carries
the derived limit through `RF`, and the derived limit costs the one further degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_addCommGrpCat (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b : ℤ) (hE : E.IsLE b) : (RF.obj E).IsLE (b + (N : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.comment: part (3), upper bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncGEπ_addCommGrpCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D4, part (2).** With the hypotheses of the upper bound, in degrees at least `b` a
total right derived functor agrees on an object with quasi-coherent cohomology and on its
canonical truncation in degrees at least `b - N + 1`.

The truncation triangle at `a = b - N + 1` has first vertex in degrees `≤ a - 1`, so the upper
bound puts its `RF`-image in degrees `≤ a - 1 + N - 1 = b - 1`; the long exact homology sequence
then makes the second map invertible on `H^i` for every `i ≥ b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerivedFunctor_truncGEπ_addCommGrpCat
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (b i : ℤ) (hi : b ≤ i) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - (N : ℤ) + 1)).app E)))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isLE_derivedPushforward_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D5] part (2), in the duality spelling.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact
and quasi-separated morphism of schemes with `Y` quasi-compact. There is an integer `N`,
depending on `f` alone, such that `Rf_*E` lives in degrees `≤ b + N` for every object `E` of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` living in degrees `≤ b`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward` with `Rf_*` spelled
`Stacks.Duality.derivedPushforward` and the conclusion packaged as `DerivedCategory.IsLE`; the
degree drops by one in the repackaging because the source asserts vanishing *at* `b + N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLE_derivedPushforward_obj [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ E : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      (∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) →
      ∀ b : ℤ, E.IsLE b → ((derivedPushforward f).obj E).IsLE (b + N)
declarations.comment: part (2), in the duality spelling

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isLE_derivedPushforward_obj_anyModel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D5] part (2), at an arbitrary chosen model of the derived categories, in the
`IsLE` form.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes with `Y`
quasi-compact. There is an integer `N`, depending on `f` alone, such that `Rf_*E` lives in degrees
`≤ b + N` for every object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` with quasi-coherent cohomology living in degrees `≤ b`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.exists_isLE_derivedPushforward_obj` with the choice of derived category a
binder rather than a term; the degree drops by one in the repackaging because
`Stacks.Duality.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_anyModel` asserts vanishing *at*
`b + N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLE_derivedPushforward_obj_anyModel
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ E : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      (∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) →
      ∀ b : ℤ, E.IsLE b → ((derivedPushforward.{w} f).obj E).IsLE (b + N)
declarations.comment: part (2), at an arbitrary derived category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_uniform_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D5, part (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of schemes with `S` quasi-compact. There is an integer `N`, depending only on `f`, such that for
every morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` the base change `f' : X ×_S S' ⟶ S'` satisfies `H^q(Rf'_* E) = 0`
for every `q ≥ N` and every object `E` of `D(𝒪_{X ×_S S'})` with quasi-coherent cohomology
sheaves and vanishing cohomology in positive degrees.

The covering data of `f` is extracted once, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_cover_data`, and
`isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_commSq` is applied to the cartesian square, whose
affineness hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_inf_preimage`. The degree `N` is read
off the covering data alone, so it does not depend on `g`.

This is one of the three declarations carrying [Stacks, Tag 08D5]; the other two are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward` (part (1)) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isLE_zero` (part (2)).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace S] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S)
      (E : DerivedCategory.{u + 1} (pullback f g).Modules),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (pullback f g).Modules i).obj
        E).IsQuasicoherent) →
      E.IsLE 0 → ∀ q : ℤ, N ≤ q →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor S'.Modules q).obj
          ((derivedPushforward (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E))
declarations.comment: uniform_bound_after_base_change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isLE_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes with `S`
quasi-compact. There is an integer `N`, depending only on `f`, such that every object `E` of
`D(𝒪_X)` with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves and vanishing cohomology in positive degrees has
`H^m(Rf_* E) = 0` for all `m ≥ N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isLE_zero
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace S] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ E : DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules,
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) →
      E.IsLE 0 → ∀ m : ℤ, N ≤ m →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor S.Modules m).obj
          ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E))
declarations.comment: bounded_cohomological_dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D5, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes. The unbounded derived direct image `Rf_*` carries `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`: the
cohomology sheaves of `Rf_* E` are quasi-coherent for every object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` whose
cohomology sheaves are.

Quasi-coherence is local on the target and `Rf_*` commutes with restriction to an open, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward_of_compactTarget`; the affine case is
`preservesQuasicoherentOnCompactTarget`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf)
      ((RingedSpace.derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E.obj)
declarations.comment: quasi_coherent_direct_image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward_affineLocal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D5], part (1).** For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ S` the unbounded derived direct image `Rf_*` carries `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`:
the cohomology sheaves of `Rf_*E` are quasi-coherent whenever those of `E` are.

The question is local on `S`, and over an affine open of `S` it is the quasi-compact-target case
`AlgebraicGeometry.preservesQuasicoherentOnCompactTarget`; the name records that affine-local
route, the same statement being reached by the compact-target route in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_derivedPushforward_affineLocal
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf)
      ((RingedSpace.derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E.obj)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D5], part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
morphism of schemes with `S` quasi-compact. There is an integer `N`, depending on `X`, `S` and `f`
alone, such that every object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `H^m(E) = 0` for `m > 0` has
`H^m(Rf_*E) = 0` for `m ≥ N`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward` at `b = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isLE (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace S] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X, E.obj.IsLE 0 → ∀ m : ℤ, N ≤ m →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor S.Modules m).obj
        ((RingedSpace.derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E.obj))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedPushforward_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D7.** Comparison with an arbitrary right derived pushforward of all
sheaves of modules. This is the commutative square of the source, up to the unique natural
isomorphism whose inverse agrees with the derivation unit `α` on every homotopy complex of
quasi-coherent modules, after the canonical termwise identifications.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineDerivedPushforward_comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory Y.Modules)
    (α : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    let I : Scheme.QuasicoherentModules X ⥤ X.Modules :=
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).ι
    let J : Scheme.QuasicoherentModules Y ⥤ Y.Modules :=
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).ι
    letI : I.Additive := CategoryTheory.Functor.fullSubcategoryInclusion_additive _
    letI : J.Additive := CategoryTheory.Functor.fullSubcategoryInclusion_additive _
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits I :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.isQuasicoherent_ι_preservesFiniteLimits X
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits I :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.isQuasicoherent_ι_preservesFiniteColimits X
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits J :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.isQuasicoherent_ι_preservesFiniteLimits Y
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits J :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.isQuasicoherent_ι_preservesFiniteColimits Y
    let F := quasicoherentPushforward f
    let G := Scheme.Modules.pushforward f
    ∃! e : (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparison X ⋙
          affineRightDerivedPushforward f RF α) ≅
        (F.mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparison Y),
      ∀ K : HomotopyCategory (Scheme.QuasicoherentModules X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
        (e.inv.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K)).hom ≫
            RF.map (I.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app K) =
          J.mapDerivedCategory.map (F.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app K) ≫
            J.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app
              ((F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Qh.map
              ((Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl (F ⋙ J))
                  (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom.app K ≫
                (Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl (I ⋙ G))
                  (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inv.app K) ≫
            α.app ((I.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)
declarations.comment: comparison square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineRightDerivedPushforward_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D7.** The derived direct image along an affine morphism of schemes
takes a complex of `𝒪_X`-modules with quasi-coherent cohomology to a complex of `𝒪_Y`-modules
with quasi-coherent cohomology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineRightDerivedPushforward_mem {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f]
    (RF : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory Y.Modules)
    (α : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)) (RF.obj E.obj)
declarations.comment: quasi-coherent cohomology of derived pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePushforwardPreservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D7.** Pushforward along an affine morphism preserves finite limits
of quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
public instance affinePushforwardPreservesFiniteLimits {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f] : PreservesFiniteLimits (quasicoherentPushforward f)
declarations.comment: exactness, kernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePushforwardPreservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08D7.** Pushforward along an affine morphism preserves finite colimits
of quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
public instance affinePushforwardPreservesFiniteColimits {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f] : PreservesFiniteColimits (quasicoherentPushforward f)
declarations.comment: exactness, cokernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRightDerivedFunctor_quasicoherentPushforward_mapDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Pushforward along an affine morphism defines a derived functor
`D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D(QCoh(𝒪_Y))`.** This is the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 08D7]: the functor
induced on unbounded derived categories by the exact functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentPushforward`, namely
`CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategory`, is a total right derived functor of it, so no
resolutions are involved and the derived functor is computed by applying `f_*` to a representative
complex.

The structure map is `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv`, which exhibits the
induced functor as a lift through the localization `DerivedCategory.Qh`; a lift of a functor that
inverts the quasi-isomorphisms is a right derived functor for the inverse of the lifting
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRightDerivedFunctor_quasicoherentPushforward_mapDerivedCategory
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f] :
    (quasicoherentPushforward f).mapDerivedCategory.IsRightDerivedFunctor
      (quasicoherentPushforward f).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Scheme.QuasicoherentModules X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
declarations.comment: the derived functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08D7, the commuting square.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` an affine morphism of schemes the
square
`D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, `D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⟶ D(QCoh(𝒪_Y)) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`
commutes: the comparison functor of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] carries the derived functor of direct image
on quasi-coherent modules to the restriction of the unbounded derived direct image.

The two edges are compared after the fully faithful inclusion `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_Y)`, where the
comparison functor becomes the derived inclusion
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonCompι`) and the
square becomes `AlgebraicGeometry.mapDerivedCategoryQuasicoherentPushforwardCompιIso`, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0G9N] for an affine morphism.
declarations.comment: the commuting square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatPushforwardCoheratorIso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated and flat morphism of schemes. Let `Rf_*`
be a total right derived functor of pushforward of all modules, let `RQ_X`, `RQ_Y` be total right
derived functors of the coherators, and let `Φ` be a total right derived functor of pushforward
restricted to quasi-coherent modules. Then `Rf_* ⋙ RQ_Y ≅ RQ_X ⋙ Φ`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def flatPushforwardCoheratorIso : Rf ⋙ RQY ≅ RQX ⋙ Φ

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.coheratorSpecIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D9] part (1).** On the affine scheme `X = Spec R` the coherator
`Q_X : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` sends a module `F` to the quasi-coherent module `Γ(X, F)^~` attached
to the `R`-module of global sections of `F`.

Both `Q_X` and `Γ(X, -) ⋙ ~` are right adjoint to the inclusion of the quasi-coherent modules:
for the second, compose the sheafification–sections adjunction `~ ⊣ Γ(X, -)` with the equivalence
`Mod(R) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_X)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv`. A right adjoint is unique up to a unique
natural isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def coheratorSpecIso :
    coherator (Spec R) ≅ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R) ⋙ (tildeEquiv (R := R)).functor
declarations.comment: part (1): the coherator on an affine scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoheratorIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D9] part (2).** On the affine scheme `X = Spec R` the derived coherator
`RQ_X : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(QCoh(𝒪_X))` sends an object `E` to the complex of quasi-coherent modules
attached to the object `RΓ(X, E)` of `D(R)`.

Both sides are right derived functors of the two isomorphic functors of
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.coheratorSpecIso`: the right-hand side because derived sheafification
`D(R) ≌ D(QCoh(𝒪_X))` is an equivalence, hence a left adjoint, and postcomposing a right derived
functor with a left adjoint again gives a right derived functor. A right derived functor is unique
up to a unique natural isomorphism.
declarations.comment: part (2): the derived coherator

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoheratorEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08D9] part (3).** On the affine scheme `X = Spec R` the derived coherator,
restricted to the complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, is a quasi-inverse to the comparison
functor `D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 06VT]: the two are the two halves of an
equivalence of categories.

The comparison functor is an equivalence by
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence`, and
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoheratorComparisonAdjunction` exhibits the restricted derived coherator
as its right adjoint; a right adjoint of an equivalence is its quasi-inverse.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCoheratorEquivalence :
    DerivedCategory (Scheme.QuasicoherentModules (Spec R)) ≌
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: part (3): quasi-inverse to the comparison functor

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNonvanishing.exists_quasicoherentComplex_iso_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08DB] at the hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0BQR].** On a scheme carrying an ample
invertible `𝒪_X`-module every object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is isomorphic in `D(𝒪_X)` to the class
of a cochain complex `G` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.

This is `Stacks.AmpleNonvanishing.exists_quasicoherentComplex_iso` with its two hypotheses — `X`
quasi-compact and `X` of affine diagonal — supplied by ampleness, which is the first line of the
proof of [Stacks, Tag 0BQR]. No hypothesis beyond the tag's is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasicoherentComplex_iso_of_isAmple (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L)
    (K : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ G : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ℤ,
      Nonempty (K.1 ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).ι.mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G))
declarations.comment: on a scheme carrying an ample invertible module, which is the form Tag 0BQR consumes: quasi-compactness and the affine diagonal both come from ampleness

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_affineDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08DB].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal. Then the
comparison functor `i_X : D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] is an equivalence.

A scheme with affine diagonal is quasi-separated, and the inclusion of one of its affine opens is
an affine morphism, so the square of [Stacks, Tag 09T6] is the square of [Stacks, Tag 08D7]; that
is `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.affineOpenPushforwardCompatible`, which discharges the hypothesis of
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_compatible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_affineDiagonal (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))] :
    (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{u} X).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoherator_isoInv_of_affineDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08DB], the quasi-inverse.** On a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal the
quasi-inverse of the comparison functor of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] is the derived coherator `RQ_X`,
restricted to the complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology.

The comparison functor is an equivalence by
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_affineDiagonal`, and
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoherator_isoInv` — the quasi-inverse clause of [Stacks, Tag 09T6] —
identifies the inverse of an equivalent comparison functor with any total right derived functor
of the coherator, here `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedCoheratorOfScheme`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCoherator_isoInv_of_affineDiagonal (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))] :
    letI := derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_affineDiagonal X
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).ι ⋙ derivedCoheratorOfScheme X ≅
      (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{u} X).inv
declarations.comment: quasi-inverse

declarations.name: Koszul.DerivedSystem.cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of Stacks 08DC.** For every object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` the maps
`Iₑ → 𝒪_X`, which become isomorphisms after restriction to `U = D(f₁) ∪ ⋯ ∪ D(f_r)`, induce a
canonical homomorphism

`colimₑ Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(Iₑ, E) ⟶ H⁰(U, E)`,

sending the class of `α : Iₑ → E` to the restriction of `α` to `U` precomposed with the inverse
of the restriction of `Iₑ → 𝒪_X`, read as a degree-zero hypercohomology class over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public def cohomologyComparison (f : Fin r → A) (E : derivedCat A) :
    ↥(colimit (homGroupSystem f E)) →+ ↥((sectionsOnUnion f).obj E)

declarations.name: Koszul.DerivedSystem.cohomologyComparison_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DD.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 08CZ] — `A` a commutative ring, `f` a
finite sequence in `A`, `X = Spec A` and `U = D(f₁) ∪ ⋯ ∪ D(f_r)` — the comparison map of
[Stacks, Tag 08DC]

`colimₑ Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(Iₑ, E) ⟶ H⁰(U, E)`

is an isomorphism for every object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MixedDerivedTensorOnARingedSpace.derivedLinearMixedTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DE, through the one-sided K-flat descent of the mixed tensor product.**  The
canonical bifunctorial isomorphism

`F ⊗^L_{O_X} Lf^*G ≅ F ⊗^L_{f⁻¹O_Y} f⁻¹G`

in `D(O_X)`, for a morphism `f : (X, O_X) ⟶ (Y, O_Y)` of ringed spaces, `F` in `D(O_X)` and
`G` in `D(O_Y)`.  The right-hand side is the derived tensor product over `f⁻¹O_Y` of `F` and
`f⁻¹G`, an object of `D(O_X)` through `F`.  It is stated between the two uncurried bifunctors on
`D(O_X) × D(O_Y)`, so that bifunctoriality is part of its type, and the left-hand one is written
with the ringed-space derived pullback of Tag 06YJ.
declarations.statement:
def derivedLinearMixedTensorIso :
    spaceLinearDerivedTensorPullback f ≅ spaceDerivedMixedTensorInverseImage f
declarations.comment: the canonical bifunctorial isomorphism, in D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.isIso_derivedOpenPushforward_restrictionUnit_app_of_supported
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08DF, part (1).** Let `j : U → X` be the inclusion of an open
subspace of a ringed space and `T ⊆ U` a closed subset of `X`. If every cohomology sheaf of
`E ∈ D(O_X)` is supported on `T`, then the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedOpenPushforward_restrictionUnit_app_of_supported
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (U : Opens X) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTU : T ⊆ U)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (hE : CohomologySupportedOn O T E) :
    IsIso ((derivedPushforwardRestrictionUnit O U (derivedOpenPushforward O U)
      (derivedOpenPushforwardUnit O U)).app E)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.isIso_extensionByZeroToDerivedOpenPushforward_app_of_supported
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08DF, part (2).** Let `j : U → X` be the inclusion of an open
subspace of a ringed space and `T ⊆ U` a closed subset of `X`. If every cohomology sheaf of
`F ∈ D(O_U)` is supported on `T`, then the canonical map `j_! F ⟶ Rj_* F` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_extensionByZeroToDerivedOpenPushforward_app_of_supported
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (U : Opens X) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTU : T ⊆ U)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O))]
    (F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O)))
    (hF : CohomologySupportedOn (resRing U O)
      ((fun x : Usp U ↦ x.1) ⁻¹' T) F) :
    IsIso ((extensionByZeroToDerivedPushforward O U (derivedOpenPushforward O U)
      (derivedOpenPushforwardUnit O U)).app F)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlueingComplexes.exists_glueing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08DG.** Let `X` be a ringed space, let `jU : U ⟶ X` and `jV : V ⟶ X`
be open immersions and let `W` be their intersection. An object `A` of `D(𝒪_U)`, an object `B`
of `D(𝒪_V)` and an isomorphism `c : A|_W ≅ B|_W` come from an object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

No hypothesis that `U` and `V` cover `X` is needed for the glued object to exist; a cover is
what makes it unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_glueing {X U V W : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (jU : U ⟶ X) (jV : V ⟶ X) (iU : W ⟶ U)
    (iV : W ⟶ V) [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion jU] [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion jV]
    (h : IsPullback iU iV jU jV) (A : DerivedModules U) (B : DerivedModules V)
    (c : (derivedRestrict iU).obj A ≅ (derivedRestrict iV).obj B) :
    Nonempty (Glueing jU jV iU iV h.w A B c)
declarations.comment: existence of a glueing

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlueingComplexes.exists_hom_of_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08DG.** Let `X` be a ringed space covered by the images of two open
immersions `jU : U ⟶ X` and `jV : V ⟶ X`, let `W` be their intersection, and let `F` be a
glueing of the glueing data `(A, B, c)`, with identifications `f : F|_U ≅ A` and
`g : F|_V ≅ B`. Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `a : A ⟶ E|_U` and `b : B ⟶ E|_V`
agree on `W` through `c`. Then there is a morphism `F ⟶ E` restricting to `a ∘ f` on `U` and
to `b ∘ g` on `V`.

Unlike the existence of the glued object, this needs `U` and `V` to cover `X`: it is
Mayer--Vietoris for `Hom`, and the covering hypothesis enters only through
`isIso_of_restrict_isIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hom_of_compatible {X U V W : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (jU : U ⟶ X) (jV : V ⟶ X)
    (iU : W ⟶ U) (iV : W ⟶ V) [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion jU]
    [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion jV] (h : IsPullback iU iV jU jV)
    (cover : Set.range jU.hom.base ∪ Set.range jV.hom.base = Set.univ)
    {A : DerivedModules U} {B : DerivedModules V}
    {c : (derivedRestrict iU).obj A ≅ (derivedRestrict iV).obj B}
    (G : Glueing jU jV iU iV h.w A B c) (E : DerivedModules X)
    (a : A ⟶ (derivedRestrict jU).obj E) (b : B ⟶ (derivedRestrict jV).obj E)
    (hab : (derivedRestrict iU).map a ≫ (overlapIso jU jV iU iV h.w).hom.app E =
      c.hom ≫ (derivedRestrict iV).map b) :
    ∃ φ : G.F ⟶ E, (derivedRestrict jU).map φ = G.f.hom ≫ a ∧
      (derivedRestrict jV).map φ = G.g.hom ≫ b
declarations.comment: a compatible pair of maps comes from the glued object

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomTensorEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DI.** For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space, morphisms into the
derived internal hom are canonically identified with morphisms out of the derived tensor
product,

`Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, RSheafHom(L, M)) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K ⊗^L_{O_X} L, M)`,

as an isomorphism of abelian groups.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedCurryingData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DJ.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K`, `L`, `M` be objects of
`D(O_X)`. There is a canonical isomorphism

`RSheafHom(K, RSheafHom(L, M)) ≅ RSheafHom(K ⊗^L_{O_X} L, M)`

in `D(O_X)`, functorial in `K`, `L` and `M`, which recovers the tensor--internal-Hom bijection
of Stacks 08DI on taking `H⁰(X, -)`.
declarations.statement: def derivedCurryingData : DerivedCurryingData Rc

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DK globally.** For objects `L`, `M` of `D(O_X)` the degree-zero global
hypercohomology of the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(L, M)` is the group of morphisms
`L ⟶ M` in the derived category of `O_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv (L M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (ringedSite Rc)).obj (op L)).obj M)) :
        Type u) ≃+ (L ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DK over an open.** For objects `L`, `M` of `D(O_X)` and an open `U ⊆ X` the
degree-zero hypercohomology over `U` of the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(L, M)` is the group
of morphisms `L|_U ⟶ M|_U` in the derived category of `O_U`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv (L M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedSectionsOverObject (ringedSite Rc) U).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (ringedSite Rc)).obj (op L)).obj M)) :
        Type u) ≃+
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheaf Rc) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj L ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheaf Rc) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)
declarations.comment: sections over an open

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DL.** For objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_X)` the derived internal Hom commutes with
restriction to an open `U`: restricting `RSheafHom(K, L)` to the opens contained in `U` gives the
derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(K|_U, L|_U)` of the restrictions.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    (derivedRestrict Rc U).obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (ringedSite Rc)).obj (op K)).obj L) ≅
      ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor ((ringedSite Rc).over U)).obj
          (op ((derivedRestrict Rc U).obj K))).obj ((derivedRestrict Rc U).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_natural_left
declarations.doc:
The comparison of Stacks 08DL is natural in the contravariant variable: restricting the map
`RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K', L)` induced by `f : K' ⟶ K` gives the map induced by `f|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_natural_left
    {K K' L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (f : K' ⟶ K) :
    (derivedRestrict Rc U).map
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (ringedSite Rc)).map f.op).app L) ≫
        (derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso Rc U K' L).hom =
      (derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso Rc U K L).hom ≫
        ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor ((ringedSite Rc).over U)).map
          ((derivedRestrict Rc U).map f).op).app ((derivedRestrict Rc U).obj L)
declarations.comment: functoriality in the first variable

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_natural_right
declarations.doc:
The comparison of Stacks 08DL is natural in the covariant variable: restricting the map
`RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, L')` induced by `g : L ⟶ L'` gives the map induced by `g|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_natural_right
    {K L L' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (g : L ⟶ L') :
    (derivedRestrict Rc U).map
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (ringedSite Rc)).obj (op K)).map g) ≫
        (derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso Rc U K L').hom =
      (derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso Rc U K L).hom ≫
        ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor ((ringedSite Rc).over U)).obj
          (op ((derivedRestrict Rc U).obj K))).map ((derivedRestrict Rc U).map g)
declarations.comment: functoriality in the second variable

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomRestrictionComplexMap_isRestriction
declarations.doc:
On every local homogeneous cochain, the chain-level comparison of Stacks 08DL is the
canonical restriction isomorphism of internal Homs of modules. This is what pins the comparison
down: a cochain over `V ⊆ U` is sent to the cochain it already is, read along the identification
of `Opens X / V` with the opens contained in `V` inside `Opens X / U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomRestrictionComplexMap_isRestriction
    (A B : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) :
    RingedSite.IsInternalHomRestrictionMap (ringedSite Rc) U A B
      (sheafHomRestrictionComplexMap Rc U A B)
declarations.comment: restriction of internal-Hom complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_model
declarations.doc:
On the classes of complexes `A` and `B` with `B` K-injective, both sides of Stacks 08DL are
the class of an internal Hom complex, and the comparison is the class of the chain-level
restriction map. Together with naturality this determines the comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso_model
    (A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite Rc).O)) ℤ)
    [B.IsKInjective] :
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite Rc).O) U) :=
      ‹PreservesFiniteLimits (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheaf Rc) U)›
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite Rc).O) U) :=
      ‹PreservesFiniteColimits (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheaf Rc) U)›
    (derivedSheafHomRestrictionIso Rc U
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)).hom ≫
        (RingedSite.restrictionTargetComparison (ringedSite Rc) U A B).hom =
      (RingedSite.restrictionSourceComparison (ringedSite Rc) U A B).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (sheafHomRestrictionComplexMap Rc U A B)
declarations.comment: canonical model characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.strictlyPerfectHomDegreeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DM, the degreewise description.** The degree-`n` term of the internal Hom complex
`SheafHom(E, F)` of a bounded complex `E` is the finite direct sum `⊕_q Hom_{O_X}(E^{-q},
F^{n-q})`, that is `⊕_{n = p + q} Hom_{O_X}(E^{-q}, F^p)`.
declarations.comment: finite direct-sum terms and Hom differential

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DM.** For `E` strictly perfect — bounded, with every term a direct summand of a
finite free `O_X`-module — the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(E, F)` is represented by the
ordinary internal Hom complex `SheafHom(E, F)` of Stacks 0A8Z, for every complex `F`, the
comparison being the canonical one. No injective resolution of `F` is needed.

The comparison is an isomorphism exactly when the map of internal Hom complexes induced by the
K-injective augmentation of `F` is a quasi-isomorphism, and strict perfectness of `E` makes it
one: the statement holds for a source concentrated in one degree whose term is the structure
sheaf, hence for finite free terms by direct sums, hence for direct summands of those by
retracts, and the stupid filtration of the bounded complex `E` assembles the terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso
    (hE : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (E.X i)}.Finite)
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ, RingedSite.IsFiniteFreeSummand (ringedSite Rc) (E.X i)) :
    IsIso (strictlyPerfectHomComparison Rc E F)
declarations.comment: representation by the finite direct-sum Hom complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isFinitePresentation_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space and let `K` be an `m`-pseudo-coherent object of the derived category
of `𝒪_X`-modules with `H^i(K) = 0` for `i > m + 1`. Then `H^{m+1}(K)` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFinitePresentation_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m + 1 < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) i).obj K)) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := structureSheafOfRings X)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) (m + 1)).obj K)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isFiniteType_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DN, part (1).** Let `X` be a ringed space and let `K` be an `m`-pseudo-coherent
object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules with `H^i(K) = 0` for `i > m`. Then `H^m(K)` is an
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type.

Finite type is a local condition, so it is enough to produce, around each point of `X`, an
epimorphism onto `H^m(K)` from a finite free module. Let `E` be a complex representing `K` which
is `m`-pseudo-coherent as a complex, and let `𝒫 ⟶ E|_U` be a strictly perfect approximation on an
open neighbourhood `U` of the given point: it is an isomorphism on cohomology above `m` and an
epimorphism in degree `m`. Since restriction is exact and `H^i(K)` vanishes above `m`, the
cohomology of `𝒫` vanishes above `m` too, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_isDirectSummandOfFiniteFree_restrict_cycles` makes `Z^m(𝒫)`
a direct summand of a finite free module after restriction to a smaller `W`. Composing the
retraction with `Z^m(𝒫) ⟶ H^m(𝒫) ⟶ H^m(E|_U) ≅ H^m(E)|_U` gives the required epimorphism, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_epi_free_over_of_epi_finiteFree` reads in the slice idiom in
which finite type is phrased.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteType_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) i).obj K)) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (R := structureSheafOfRings X)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) m).obj K)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ClosedSupportPerfect.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_closedSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DP.** The derived pushforward of a perfect object on an open subspace is perfect
if its cohomology is supported on a subset closed in the ambient space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_closedSupport
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (U : Opens X) (T : Set (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).carrier)
    (hT : IsClosed ((X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding).hom.base '' T))
    (Rj : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing
      (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (αj : (modulePushforward (X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rj)
    [hRj : Rj.IsRightDerivedFunctor αj
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing
      (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) E)
    (hET : CohomologySupportedOn
      (structureSheafRing (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)) T E) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X) (Rj.obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedBidualIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, second assertion.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O_X)`. Then `K` is reflexive: the canonical map `K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` of
`derivedBidualMap` is an isomorphism, so `(K^∨)^∨ ≅ K`.

This is the isomorphism form of `isIso_derivedBidualMap`; its `.symm` is the orientation
`(K^∨)^∨ ≅ K` in which the source states the assertion. The three factors are the left unitor,
the trivialisation `O_X ≅ RSheafHom(O_X, O_X)` and the derived evaluation morphism of
Stacks 0A8U, the last being invertible by Stacks 0G40.

Perfectness is the site-level notion of Stacks 08G5 read at the site of opens of the space, as in
`StacksFrontier.Topology.Sheaves.Cohomology.InternalHomEvaluation.PerfectEvaluation`, whose section
"Perfectness model" records why that notion and not the ringed-space one of Stacks 08CM.
declarations.comment: the second assertion: `(K^∨)^∨ ≅ K` for a perfect `K`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedBidualMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, second assertion.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O_X)`. The canonical map

`K = RSheafHom(O_X, O_X) ⊗^L_{O_X} K ⟶ RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, O_X), O_X) = (K^∨)^∨`

of `derivedBidualMap` is an isomorphism; equivalently `(K^∨)^∨ ≅ K`, which is
`derivedBidualIso`.

Perfectness of `K` is the only hypothesis. Its two outer factors are isomorphisms by
construction, and its middle factor — the derived evaluation morphism of Stacks 0A8U at
`L = M = O_X` — is an isomorphism by Stacks 0G40, which holds for every value of the two
variables specialised here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBidualMap (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedBidualMap Rc K)
declarations.comment: the second assertion: the canonical map `K = RSheafHom(O_X, O_X) ⊗^L K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` of Stacks 0A8U is an isomorphism for a perfect `K`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isPerfect_derivedDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, first assertion.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O_X)`. Then the dual `K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O_X)` is perfect as well.

Perfectness is local, so it is enough to model `K^∨` above a covering of each open. Over a
member `V` on which `K` is modelled by a strictly perfect complex `E`, the restriction of `K^∨`
is `RSheafHom(K|_V, O_V)`, which is the class of the internal Hom complex `SheafHom(E, O_V)`;
and that complex is strictly perfect because the dual of a direct summand of a finite free
module is again one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedDual (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect (derivedDual Rc K)
declarations.comment: the dual of a perfect object is perfect

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isPerfect_derivedDual_of_isPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K` be a perfect object of `D(O_X)` in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 08CM]. Then the dual `K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O_X)` is perfect in that same sense.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedDual_of_isPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) (derivedDual X.sheaf K)
declarations.comment: the first assertion with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM on both sides, rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isPerfect_derivedDual` uses; the two are equivalent by `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_of_ringedSite` and `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_ringedSite_of_isPerfect`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedBidualMap_of_isPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08CM] the canonical map
`K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedBidualMap` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBidualMap_of_isPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    IsIso (derivedBidualMap X.sheaf K)
declarations.comment: the second assertion with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedBidualMap` uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedBidualIsoOfIsPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08CM], the isomorphism
`K ≅ (K^∨)^∨`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBidualIsoOfIsPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    K ≅ derivedDual X.sheaf (derivedDual X.sheaf K)
declarations.comment: the second assertion as an isomorphism, with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedBidualIso` uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08CM] and any object `M`, the
canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 08I1]

`M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X.sheaf K M)
declarations.comment: the third assertion with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect` uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.bijective_derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_of_isPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08CM] and any object `M`, the
canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 08I1] on degree-zero global hypercohomology

`H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)`

is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_of_isPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    Function.Bijective (derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap X.sheaf K M)
declarations.comment: the fourth assertion with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.bijective_derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_of_isPerfect` uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsAddEquivOfIsPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08CM] and any object `M`,
`H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)` as abelian groups, the identification being the
canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 08I1].
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsAddEquivOfIsPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
          (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj M).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf K))) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: the fourth assertion as an isomorphism of abelian groups, with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsAddEquiv` uses; functoriality in `M` is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualSections_naturality` together with `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.bijective_derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, fourth assertion.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O_X)` and let `M` be any object. The canonical map of Stacks 08I1 on degree-zero
global hypercohomology

`H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)`

is bijective.

Perfectness of `K` is in the site-level reading of Stacks 08G5, and `M` is arbitrary. The proof is
the source's: by Stacks 08I1 the assertion reduces to invertibility of the canonical map
`M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)`, which is the third assertion of the tag,
`isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_of_isPerfect
    (K M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    Function.Bijective (derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap Rc K M)
declarations.comment: the fourth assertion: the canonical map `H⁰(X, M ⊗^L K^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)` of Stacks 08I1 is bijective for a perfect `K`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, fourth assertion**, in the equality form the source states it in: for a
perfect object `K` of `D(O_X)` and any object `M`,

`H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)`

as abelian groups, the identification being the canonical map of Stacks 08I1.

Functoriality of this identification in `M` is *not* claimed; see the section "What is still
missing" of this file.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsAddEquiv
    (K M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((derivedTensor Rc).obj M).obj (derivedDual Rc K))) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: the fourth assertion: `H⁰(X, M ⊗^L K^∨) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M)` for a perfect `K`, as an isomorphism of abelian groups along the canonical map of Stacks 08I1; not its functoriality in `M`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, third assertion.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O_X)` and let `M` be any object. The canonical map of Stacks 08I1

`Φ : M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)`

is an isomorphism.

The only hypothesis is perfectness of `K`, in the site-level reading of Stacks 08G5: there is a
complex of `O_X`-modules representing `K` and a covering of the space on each member of which the
restriction of that complex receives a quasi-isomorphism from a strictly perfect complex. The
object `M` is arbitrary.

This is the ringed-site statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect` read at the site of
opens of the space, for the canonical derived tensor product. The section "How it is proved" of
this file sets out the argument.

The instances in the ambient variable block are setup, not hypotheses on the lemma: a ringed
space whose slice sites admit sheafification and on which the tensor product of sheaves of
modules is additive and totalisable is what it takes for the objects in the statement — the
derived tensor product, the derived dual, and their restrictions to the slices appearing in the
definition of perfection — to exist at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect
    (K M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom Rc K M)
declarations.comment: the third assertion: the canonical map `M ⊗^L K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)` of Stacks 08I1 is an isomorphism for a perfect `K`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, third assertion, as a natural isomorphism.** For a perfect object `K` of
`D(O_X)` the canonical maps `M ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)` of [Stacks, Tag 08I1] assemble
into an isomorphism of functors

`(- ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨) ≅ RSheafHom(K, -)`,

which is the source's assertion that the identification is functorial in `M`. Its component at
`M` is the canonical map, invertible by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect`; the naturality square is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualNatIso (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    (derivedTensor Rc).flip.obj (derivedDual Rc K) ≅ (derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)
declarations.comment: the third assertion as a natural isomorphism of functors on D(O_X), i.e. together with the FUNCTORIALITY in M that the source asserts; its component at M is the canonical map of Tag 08I1 and is the content of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIsoOfIsPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, third assertion, as a natural isomorphism, at the ringed-space hypothesis.**
As `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIso`, with perfectness of `K` read as
`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect`, the notion of [Stacks, Tag 08CM].
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualNatIsoOfIsPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    (derivedTensor X.sheaf).flip.obj (derivedDual X.sheaf K) ≅
      (derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op K)
declarations.comment: the third assertion as a natural isomorphism of functors, with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIso` uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeft
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, third assertion, with the dual in the left tensor slot.** For a perfect
object `K` of `D(O_X)` there is an isomorphism of functors

`(K^∨ ⊗^L_{O_X} -) ≅ RSheafHom(K, -)`

on `D(O_X)`, which is the source's assertion that the identification is functorial in the
second variable, written with the dual tensored on the left.

It is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIso`, the same assertion with the dual in the
right slot, precomposed with the commutativity constraint of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorBraidingNatIso`. Unlike the right-slot form, it is not
claimed to be carried by the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 08I1]; see the implementation
notes.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeft (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    (derivedTensor Rc).obj (derivedDual Rc K) ≅ (derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)
declarations.comment: the third assertion as a natural isomorphism of functors on D(O_X), with the dual in the LEFT tensor slot rather than the right one in which Tag 08I1 writes the canonical map and in which `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIso` states it; the two differ by the commutativity constraint of Tag 0FPT, so this one is NOT claimed to be carried by the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeftOfIsPerfectSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08DQ, third assertion in the left tensor slot, at the ringed-space hypothesis.**
As `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeft`, with perfectness of `K` read as
`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect`, the notion of [Stacks, Tag 08CM].
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeftOfIsPerfectSpace
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    (derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf K) ≅
      (derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op K)
declarations.comment: the third assertion as a natural isomorphism with the dual in the LEFT tensor slot, with perfectness in the RINGED-SPACE reading of Tag 08CM rather than the site reading of Tag 08G5 that `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualNatIsoLeft` uses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangeOverAffineBase_of_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
**The induction of Stacks 0DJ9 over the quasi-compact opens of `X`.**  Granted the affine
case and the Mayer--Vietoris step, the conclusion holds for every cartesian square over an affine
base: an affine base makes `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the induction principle of
Stacks 08DR carries the property from the affine opens to all of `X`.
declarations.comment: the induction of Stacks 0DJ9 from the affine opens of X to X itself

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CompactOpenInduction.of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08DR], the induction principle.** Let `X` be a quasi-separated scheme and let
`P` be a property of its open subsets such that `P` holds for every affine open, and such that
`P (U ⊔ V)` holds whenever `U` is quasi-compact open, `V` is affine open and `P U`, `P V`,
`P (U ⊓ V)` hold. Then `P` holds for every quasi-compact open of `X`.

Only the hypothesis `P (U ⊓ V)` has to be produced beyond what
`AlgebraicGeometry.compact_open_induction_on` already supplies, and `U ⊓ V` is a quasi-compact
open of the affine open `V`, so `of_le_isAffineOpen` produces it.
