`f : X ⟶ Y`, an `E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and a `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, the projection-formula morphism
of [Stacks, Tag 0B53]

`Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} Lf^*K)`

is an isomorphism.

The hypotheses are the source's and no others: quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f`,
and quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves of `E` and of `K`.  No boundedness, no flatness,
no perfectness, no affineness, no Noetherian or separatedness assumption, and no choice of model
for either derived category beyond the one the whole file works in.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_of_isDQCoh {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)))
    (hE : Stacks.DerivedQCoh.IsDQCoh (R := structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hK : Stacks.DerivedQCoh.IsDQCoh (R := structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace) K) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom E K)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y, E in D_QCoh(𝒪_X) and K in D_QCoh(𝒪_Y), the projection-formula morphism Rf_*E ⊗ᴸ K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗ᴸ Lf^*K) of Tag 0B53 is invertible. The proof is the source's dévissage: locality on Y, the affine equivalence D(A) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) of Tag 06Z0 with the resolution of Tag 09PB, direct sums through Tag 08DZ, two-out-of-three on distinguished triangles, and the shifts of the structure sheaf as the base case

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_quasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08EU].**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes.  For `E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` the projection-formula morphism of
[Stacks, Tag 0B53]

`R f_* E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} K ⟶ R f_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} L f^* K)`

is an isomorphism.

Invertibility is local on `Y`, the affine opens cover `Y`, and over an affine open the statement
is `isIso_projectionFormulaMap_of_isAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_quasiCoherent
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)))
    (hK : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)) j).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom E K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_unitObject_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08EU] at `K = 𝒪_Y[0]`.**  For an arbitrary
morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and an arbitrary `E` in `D(𝒪_X)`, the derived
projection-formula morphism

`Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} Lf^*𝒪_Y)`

is an isomorphism.

This is the base case of the source's dévissage for [Stacks, Tag 08EU].  The inputs of
`isIso_projectionFormulaMap_unitObject` are: the two right unitors and the
naturality of the one on `X` by `Stacks.RingedSpace.derivedTensorRightUnitorNatIso`, the unit
comparison by `derivedPullbackUnitIso`, and the right-unitor coherence of [Stacks, Tag 079U] by
`rightUnitorCoherence_unitObject`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_unitObject_unconditional
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f E (singleUnit Y))
declarations.comment: the case K = 𝒪_Y[0]: for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces f and an arbitrary E in D(𝒪_X), the projection-formula morphism Rf_*E ⊗ᴸ 𝒪_Y ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗ᴸ Lf^*𝒪_Y) is invertible; the right unitors are derivedTensorRightUnitorNatIso, the unit comparison is derivedPullbackUnitIso and the right-unitor coherence of Tag 079U is rightUnitorCoherence_unitObject

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_unitShift_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08EU] at `K = 𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧`, for every integer `m`.**
For an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and an arbitrary `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, the derived
projection-formula morphism of [Stacks, Tag 0B53]

`Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧ ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} Lf^*(𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧))`

is an isomorphism.

This is the case the source's proof calls clear — "the statement of the lemma is clear for shifts
of the structure sheaf" — and it is the whole base case of the source's dévissage in `K`.  At
`m = 0` it is the case `K = 𝒪_Y[0]` of [Stacks, Tag 08EU] up to the isomorphism `Z⟦0⟧ ≅ Z`.

The morphism `f` is an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces and `E` is arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_unitShift_unconditional
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (m : ℤ) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f E ((singleUnit Y)⟦m⟧))
declarations.comment: the case K = 𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧, every shift of the structure sheaf: for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces and an arbitrary E in D(𝒪_X), Rf_*E ⊗ᴸ 𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧ ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗ᴸ Lf^*(𝒪_Y[0]⟦m⟧)) is invertible for every integer m

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSupportCoherent.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_isProperOver_supp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08EV].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism locally of
finite type and `E` an object of `D(𝒪_X)` such that

1. `E` is in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`: it is bounded, `E ∈ D^{≥ a} ∩ D^{≤ b}`, and its cohomology sheaves
   are coherent;
2. the support of `H^i(E)` is proper over `S` for every `i`;
3. `E` has finite Tor dimension as an object of `D(f⁻¹𝒪_S)`.

Then `Rf_*E` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)`.

`Rf_*` is `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardModules`, the total right derived functor of
degreewise pushforward, and clause (3) is Tor dimension over the inverse-image ringed space
`(X, f⁻¹𝒪_S)` for its canonical derived tensor product. As in the source, the proof splits the
conclusion by [Stacks, Tag 08CQ]: pseudo-coherence comes from [Stacks, Tag 08E2] and
[Stacks, Tag 08E8], and locally finite Tor dimension from
`AlgebraicGeometry.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_derivedPushforward_of_isProperOver`. That second
half follows the source's reduction — one closed subset proper over `S` carrying all the
cohomological support ([Stacks, Tag 0CYR]), and a quasi-compact open neighbourhood of it over each
affine open of `S` — and then replaces the source's appeal to [Stacks, Tag 08EU] and
[Stacks, Tag 08EA] by a Mayer--Vietoris induction from the affine case, where the statement is
commutative algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_isProperOver_supp {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (a b : ℤ) (hGE : E.IsGE a) (hLE : E.IsLE b)
    (hcoh : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsCoherent)
    (hsupp : ∀ j : ℤ, IsProperOver f
      ⟨SheafOfModules.supp ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E),
        @SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp _ _ _ (hcoh j).isFiniteType⟩)
    (htor : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasFiniteTorDimension
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)
      ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction f).obj E)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPushforwardModules f).obj E)
declarations.comment: the source's statement and hypotheses: S Noetherian, f locally of finite type, E bounded with coherent cohomology sheaves whose supports are proper over S and of finite Tor dimension over f⁻¹𝒪_S for its canonical derived tensor product; Rf_* is the total right derived functor of degreewise pushforward. The Tor-dimension half is proved by a Mayer–Vietoris induction from the affine case rather than through Tag 08EU and Tag 08EA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_tfae
declarations.doc:
Nine criteria for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` to be flat: pointwise flatness,
flatness of every base change to a scheme or to an affine scheme or to one surjective étale chart
of the target, flatness of the composite with one surjective étale chart of the source, flatness
of the morphism of schemes in every — or in one surjective — commuting square of étale charts, or
over a pair of Zariski coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsFlat B S hS f,
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, IsFlatAt B S hS f x,
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) → IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
        IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧ IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS p ∧ IsFlat B S hS (p ≫ f),
      ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS q → p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q →
          IsFlat B S hS (yoneda.map a),
      ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS p ∧
          p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q ∧ IsFlat B S hS (yoneda.map a),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (Yopen : I → Subfunctor Y) (J : I → Type u)
        (Xopen : ∀ i, J i → Subfunctor (pullback f (Yopen i).ι)),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yopen ∧ (∀ i, IsZariskiCover B S hS (J i) (Xopen i)) ∧
          ∀ i j, IsFlat B S hS ((Xopen i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f (Yopen i).ι)
    ]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2): flat iff flat at every point of |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cohomologyAffineChartIsoSectionsHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08EX.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `V` be an affine
étale chart of `Y`.  Then the cohomology of `F` over `U = V ×_Y X` agrees with the module of
sections over `V` of the degree-`q` higher direct image `R^q f_*F`, in every degree:

`H^q(V ×_Y X, F) = H^0(V, R^q f_*F)`.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyAffineChartIsoSectionsHigherDirectImage (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) (hV : IsAffineChart B S hS Y.1 V) (q : ℕ) :
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS (chartBaseChangeSpace B S hS f V).1
      (chartBaseChangeSpace B S hS f V).2
    have := enoughInjectives_modules B S hS (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).1
      (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).2
    ((modulePushforward B S hS (chartBaseChangeProjection B S hS f V) ⋙
            globalSectionsFunctor.{u + 1, u, u, u}
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
                (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).1
                (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).2).O))).rightDerived q).obj
        ((chartBaseChangeModulePullback B S hS f V).obj F) ≅
      (globalSectionsFunctor.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
            (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).1
            (chartBaseChangeTarget B S hS V).2).O))).obj
        ((etaleModulePullback B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS Y V)
            (isEtale_chartToSpace B S hS Y V)).obj
          (((modulePushforward B S hS f).rightDerived q).obj F))
declarations.comment:
the complete statement at the source's own data, with no extra hypothesis: f
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, F quasi-coherent, V an affine object of Y_etale. The three
inputs of the source's proof (03F3(1) for the etale inclusion, 072Z via 0731(3), and 0720 with
01XB on the small etale site) are theorems of the library, applied here. The cohomology over
V times_Y X is read as the right derived functor of the composite Gamma(V, f'_* -), as in the
library's form of Stacks 0D2U. The degree q ranges over the natural numbers, which loses
nothing: in the right-derived-functor convention both sides vanish in negative degrees. This is
the sole registration of 08EX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedComparisonSchemeUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F1**, the comparison functor `D(QCoh(𝒪_F)) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` of an algebraic space,
with its `𝒪_F`-modules taken at the universe of the schemes, where the source assumes them.

It has no open input.  What the functor needs of Properties of Spaces, Lemma 03M1 — the lemma
Stacks 08F1 points at for the comparison to make sense — is the closure of quasi-coherence under
kernels, under cokernels and under finite direct sums, and all three hold at this universe: the
kernel clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels_quasicoherentSheaves_schemeUniverse`, the cokernel
clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderCokernels_quasicoherentSheaves`, and the
direct-sum clause is the instance
`SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_isClosedUnderFiniteProducts`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedComparisonSchemeUniverse :
    letI := isClosedUnderKernels_quasicoherentSheaves_schemeUniverse B S hS F hF
    letI := isClosedUnderCokernels_quasicoherentSheaves B S hS F hF
    DerivedCategory (QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS F hF) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F2.**  Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic space `X`.  The following
are equivalent: `E` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`; `Lφ^*E` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_U)` for every étale scheme
chart `φ : U → X` with `U` affine; the same for every étale scheme chart; the same for one étale
scheme chart surjective on points; and `Lf^*E` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` for one étale morphism
`f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces surjective on points.

All five are the corresponding conditions of Stacks 03M0 applied to the cohomology sheaves of
`E`, the passage between `Hⁿ(Lf^*E)` and `f^*(HⁿE)` being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherentPullback_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_tfae (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) :
    List.TFAE
      [DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))) E,
        ∀ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj A)) →
          DerivedQuasicoherentPullback B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X A)
            (isEtale_chartToSpace B S hS X A) E,
        ∀ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
          DerivedQuasicoherentPullback B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X A)
            (isEtale_chartToSpace B S hS X A) E,
        ∃ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, IsSurjective B S hS A.1.hom ∧
          DerivedQuasicoherentPullback B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X A)
            (isEtale_chartToSpace B S hS X A) E,
        ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : Z ⟶ X) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom),
          IsSurjective B S hS g.hom ∧ DerivedQuasicoherentPullback B S hS g hg E]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCoproducts_quasicoherentDerivedCategory_ringUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F3.**  Let `F` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf
site `B`.  Then `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`, the derived category of `𝒪_F`-modules with quasi-coherent
cohomology, has direct sums.

The tag lands at the module universe `u` of the structure rings, because the `←` direction of
Descent, Proposition 03DX(2) is available only there, and at a free module universe the
direct-sum clause of Stacks 03M1 would have to be assumed instead of proved.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCoproducts_quasicoherentDerivedCategory` with its hypothesis
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_sigma_of_h03DX`, fed with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCoproducts_quasicoherentDerivedCategory_ringUniverse :
    HasCoproducts.{u} (QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_etaleModulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F4 for an étale morphism of algebraic spaces.**  If `E` is an object of `D(𝒪_X)`
all of whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent and `f : Y ⟶ X` is étale, then every
cohomology sheaf of `Lf^*E` is quasi-coherent.

The étale pullback is exact, so `Hⁿ(Lf^*E) ≅ f^*(HⁿE)`, and `f^*` preserves quasi-coherence of a
module by the `(1) ⟹ (2)` direction of Stacks 03M0.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_etaleModulePullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))) E) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O)))
      ((etaleModulePullback B S hS f hf).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
declarations.comment: for étale morphisms of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedEtalePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F4 for an étale morphism of algebraic spaces, as a functor.**  The derived
pullback along an étale morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` restricts to a functor
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` between the derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedEtalePullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2
declarations.comment: for étale morphisms of algebraic spaces, the restriction D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback
declarations.doc:
Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.  The derived pullback `Lf^*`,
the total left derived functor `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback` of
degreewise pullback along the morphism of small étale ringed topoi of `f`, sends `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
into `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`: if every cohomology sheaf of `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` is quasi-coherent, then so is
every cohomology sheaf of `Lf^*E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))) E) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O)))
      ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS f).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
The derived pullback `Lf^*` along an arbitrary morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces
restricts to a functor `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` between the full subcategories of complexes
with quasi-coherent cohomology (Stacks 071X).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedPullback (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))) :
      ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))).FullSubcategory ⥤
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O))) :
      ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)))).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: the restriction D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) of Lf^*, for an arbitrary morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F5 for two quasi-coherent modules placed in degree zero, the left one K-flat.**
Let `X` be an algebraic space, let `T` be a derived tensor product on `𝒪_X`, and let `M` and `N`
be quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with `M[0]` K-flat.  Then `M[0] ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} N[0]` lies in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Membership in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is the object property `DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB` for
quasi-coherence that `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentDerivedCategory` of Stacks 071X is
the full subcategory on, so no new predicate appears.  The content is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_tensor_single` on the
small étale ringed site of `X`; the general case of Stacks 08F5 is not proved, and the module
docstring records the four missing inputs.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor_single
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, d} (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (hM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) 0).obj M))
    (hMq : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hNq : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)))
      ((T.tensor.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) 0).obj M)).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) 0).obj N))
declarations.comment: the case of two quasi-coherent modules placed in degree zero, the left one K-flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor_single'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F5 for two quasi-coherent modules placed in degree zero, the right one K-flat.**
The mirror of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor_single`, read through

declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor_single'

          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) 0).obj M)).obj

declarations.comment: the case of two quasi-coherent modules placed in degree zero, the right one K-flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F5.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`.  For objects `K`, `L` of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the derived tensor product `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} L` is in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Here `𝒪_X`-modules are the sheaves of modules on the small étale ringed site of `X`,
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentDerivedCategory` of Stacks 071X, the full
subcategory of the unbounded derived category on the objects with quasi-coherent cohomology
sheaves, and `⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X}` is an arbitrary derived tensor product datum `T` on that ringed site —
for instance the canonical one, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct` of
Stacks 06YU.  `K` and `L` are arbitrary objects of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, with no boundedness.

The proof represents `K` by a K-flat complex `P` (Stacks 06YS) and `L` by any complex `L'`, so
that `K ⊗^𝐋 L ≅ Q(Tot(P ⊗ L'))` by the K-flat comparison of `T`, and concludes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_tensorComplex`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherent_derivedTensor
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1}
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (K L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)))
      ((T.tensor.obj K.obj).obj L.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.qcohDerived_smallEtaleDerivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F5.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`. For objects `K`, `L` of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the derived tensor product `K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} L` is in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem qcohDerived_smallEtaleDerivedTensor (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hK : QcohDerived B S hS X K) (hL : QcohDerived B S hS X L) :
    QcohDerived B S hS X (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_ringUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08F6.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and
let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.  Then the canonical map from `E` to a derived limit `L` of
the tower `n ↦ τ_{≥ -n} E` of canonical truncations from below is an isomorphism.

The derived limit is presented by its structural morphism `p` to the product of the tower together
with the distinguished triangle `hL` characterising it, and the map `c` out of `E` is the canonical
one because its composites with the product projections are required to be the truncation maps.
The product exists by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProductsOfShape_nat_derivedCategory_modules`, so
the only hypothesis is the quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves of `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_ringUniverse
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hE : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) q).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (c : E ⟶ L)
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
          (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
            (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)))
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c
declarations.comment: the source's statement: E in D_QCoh is the derived limit of its truncations τ_{≥ -n} E. The source's two inputs are theorems of this library: the affine étale charts cover the small étale site (04JS) and a quasi-coherent module has no higher cohomology on an affine étale chart (the étale-site analogue of 01XB); the countable product of the tower exists in D(𝒪_X). The module universe is the universe of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_homology_rightDerived_of_isZero_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F7, the `i < a` half of assertion (3).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an
algebraic space over `S`, let `F : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Ab` be an additive functor and let `(RF, α)` be a
right derived functor of `F` on `D(𝒪_X)`.  Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with
`H ^ j (E) = 0` for `j < a`.  Then `H ^ i (RF E) = 0` for `i < a`.

This is the half of assertion (3) that bounds `RF E` from below.  The source gets it from
assertion (1); here it is the left t-exactness of a right derived functor out of a Grothendieck
abelian category with enough injectives,
`Stacks.SmallDerivedCategory.isGE_obj_of_isGE`, which is Stacks 05TC part (1).

Neither the quasi-coherence of `E`, nor the source's hypotheses (2) and (3) on `F`, nor the
integer `N` is used: `N` governs only the upper bound `b + N - 1`, which is the other half of
assertion (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_rightDerived_of_isZero_lt
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX))
    (hqc : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX) q).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (a : ℤ)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, j < a → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX) j).obj E))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i < a) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{m} i).obj (RF.obj E))
declarations.comment: the i < a half of assertion (3); the upper bound b + N - 1, where the integer N and the hypotheses (2), (3) on F enter, is not proved — it needs the clause q > 0 of Stacks 03DW, which this repository does not carry

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerived_truncLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F7, assertion (1).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`,
let `F : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Ab` be an additive functor and let `(RF, α)` be a right derived functor of
`F` on `D(𝒪_X)`.  Then for every object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and every `i ≤ a` the canonical
truncation map `τ_{≤ a} E ⟶ E` induces an isomorphism
`H ^ i (RF (τ_{≤ a} E)) ⟶ H ^ i (RF E)`.

The argument is the source's, which cites Derived Categories, Lemma [Stacks, Tag 05TC].  The
functor `RF` is triangulated, so it carries the canonical truncation triangle
`τ_{≤ a} E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥ a + 1} E` to a distinguished triangle; its third vertex lies in degrees
`≥ a + 1` by left t-exactness of `RF`, so `H ^ i` and `H ^ (i - 1)` vanish on it for `i ≤ a`,
and the long exact homology sequence makes the first map invertible on `H ^ i`.

Neither the quasi-coherence of `E`, nor the source's hypotheses (2) and (3) on `F`, nor the
integer `N` is used — none of them occurs in Tag 05TC either.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerived_truncLE
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX))
    (hqc : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX) q).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (a i : ℤ) (hi : i ≤ a) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{m} i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app E)))
declarations.comment: assertion (1), as the source proves it, by citing Derived Categories 05TC; the hypotheses (2), (3) on F and the integer N play no part in that assertion and are not binders

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_homology_rightDerived_of_isZero_gt_unbounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F7, assertion (3), the upper bound, for every `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.** Let `S` be a
scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `F : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Ab` be an additive functor
commuting with countable direct products and let `(RF, α)` be a right derived functor of `F` on
`D(𝒪_X)`.  Let `N ≥ 0` be an integer such that `R^pF(ℱ) = 0` for every quasi-coherent `ℱ` and
every `p ≥ N`, which is the source's hypothesis (3).  Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with
`H ^ j (E) = 0` for `j > b`.  Then `H ^ i (RF E) = 0` for `i > b + N - 1`.

Nothing is assumed about the lower endpoint `a` of the source's range `-∞ ≤ a ≤ b ≤ ∞`, so this
is the case `a = -∞` as well; the vanishing for `i < a` when `a` is finite is the other half of
assertion (3) and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_homology_rightDerived_of_isZero_lt`.  The source's hypothesis (2)
on `F` is the binder `[PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) F]`; it is used, unlike in the bounded
statements, because the proof passes through the derived limit `E = R lim τ_{≥ -n} E`.

This is the sole registration of the upper bound of assertion (3); no form of that clause
assuming in addition that `E` is bounded below is stated in the library, the bounded case being
confined to the `private` ingredient
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLE_rightDerived_obj_of_bounded`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_rightDerived_of_isZero_gt_unbounded (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX, M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
      ∀ p : ℤ, (N : ℤ) ≤ p → IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hqc : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) q).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (b : ℤ)
    (hEb : ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) j).obj E))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : b + (N : ℤ) - 1 < i) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj (RF.obj E))
declarations.comment: assertion (3), the upper bound b + N - 1, and the sole registration of that half: H^i(RF E) = 0 for i > b + N - 1 once H^j(E) = 0 for j > b, for every E of D_QCoh with no boundedness hypothesis, so for a = -infinity too. Hypothesis (2) on F is the binder PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete N) F, hypothesis (3) is hRF, hypothesis (1) is unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerived_truncGE_unbounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08F7, assertion (2), for every `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X`
be an algebraic space over `S`, let `F : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Ab` be an additive functor commuting with
countable direct products and let `(RF, α)` be a right derived functor of `F` on `D(𝒪_X)`.  Let
`N ≥ 0` be an integer such that `R^pF(ℱ) = 0` for every quasi-coherent `ℱ` and every `p ≥ N`, the
source's hypothesis (3).  Then for every object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and every `i ≥ b` the
canonical truncation map `E ⟶ τ_{≥ b - N + 1} E` induces an isomorphism
`H ^ i (RF E) ⟶ H ^ i (RF (τ_{≥ b - N + 1} E))`.

No boundedness hypothesis on `E` is made.  The canonical truncation triangle
`τ_{≤ b - N} E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥ b - N + 1} E` is carried by `RF` to a distinguished triangle, `RF`
being triangulated; its first vertex lies in degrees `≤ b - 1` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLE_rightDerived_obj_of_isLE`, which needs no lower bound, so `H ^ i`
and `H ^ (i + 1)` vanish on it for `i ≥ b`, and the long exact homology sequence makes the second
map invertible on `H ^ i`.

This is the sole registration of assertion (2); no form of it assuming in addition that `E` is
bounded below is stated in the library, the bounded case being confined to the `private`
ingredient `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLE_rightDerived_obj_of_bounded`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyFunctor_map_rightDerived_truncGE_unbounded (N : ℕ)
    (hRF : ∀ M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX, M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
      ∀ p : ℤ, (N : ℤ) ≤ p → IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj M))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hqc : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) q).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (b i : ℤ) (hi : b ≤ i) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).map
      (RF.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - (N : ℤ) + 1)).app E)))
declarations.comment: assertion (2), and the sole registration of it: H^i(RF E) -> H^i(RF(tau_{>= b - N + 1} E)) is an isomorphism for i >= b, for every E of D_QCoh with no boundedness hypothesis. Hypothesis (2) on F is the binder PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete N) F, hypothesis (3) is hRF, hypothesis (1) is unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isZero_homology_derivedModulePushforward_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FA, part (3).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` quasi-compact.  There is an integer `N` such that for every
morphism of algebraic spaces `Y' ⟶ Y`, with base change `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` of `f`, and every `E` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{X'})` with `H^m(E) = 0` for `m > 0`, we have `H^m(Rf'_*E) = 0` for `m ≥ N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_homology_derivedModulePushforward_baseChange {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ (Y' X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y'),
      IsPullback g' f' f g →
      ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X'.1 X'.2), QcohDerived B S hS X' E →
        (∀ m : ℤ, 0 < m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).obj E)) →
        ∀ m : ℤ, N ≤ m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).obj
          ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f').obj E))
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isZero_homology_derivedModulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FA, part (2).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` quasi-compact.  There is an integer `N` such that for every
`E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `H^m(E) = 0` for `m > 0`, we have `H^m(Rf_*E) = 0` for `m ≥ N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_homology_derivedModulePushforward {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2), QcohDerived B S hS X E →
      (∀ m : ℤ, 0 < m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).obj E)) →
      ∀ m : ℤ, N ≤ m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).obj
        ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj E))
declarations.comment: part (2)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.qcohDerived_derivedModulePushforward_obj
registrations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlat_iff_hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FC, parts (1) and (2).**  A sheaf of modules on a ringed site is flat exactly
when every single finite relation among its sections locally factors through a finite free
module by a matrix annihilating that relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max v w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O)) :
    IsFlat F ↔ HasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations O F
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_of_isFlat_freeUniverse
declarations.doc:
A flat sheaf of modules satisfies the single-relation form of the local equational criterion:
every relation `∑ᵢ aᵢ • sᵢ = 0` among its sections over an object `U` admits, on a covering sieve
of `U`, a factorisation of the restricted sections through a finite free module by a matrix
annihilating the restricted relation. The universe `w` of the sections of the structure sheaf is
independent of the universes of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_of_isFlat_freeUniverse
    {F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O)} (hF : IsFlat F) :
    HasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations O F
declarations.comment: part (1) implies part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlat_of_hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_freeUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FC, (2) implies (1).** A sheaf of modules satisfying the single-relation form of
the local equational criterion is flat: every relation `∑ᵢ aᵢ • sᵢ = 0` among its sections
factoring locally through a finite free module annihilating the relation forces the tensor
endofunctor `- ⊗ F` on sheaves of modules to be exact.

This is the universe-general form of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlat_of_hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations`, which proves the same
implication for a structure sheaf `O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max v w}` on a site with morphisms
in `Type v`. Here the section universe `w` is independent of `u` and `v`, and `HasWeakSheafify`
is assumed in place of `HasSheafify`. A ringed site whose sections are unrelated to its
morphisms cannot be fed to the `max v w` form, because `w =?= max v u` is not a solvable
universe constraint. The proof sheafifies the local injectivity of the presheaf-level tensor map
through `Stacks.SheafOfModules.mono_shf_map_of_isLocallyInjective`.

Together with `Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_of_isFlat_freeUniverse`
this gives the equivalence of parts (1) and (2) of the source at those universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_freeUniverse
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O))
    (hF : HasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations O F) : IsFlat F
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_iff_finite
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of modules on a ringed site, the single-relation and the finite-matrix forms of
the local equational criterion for flatness are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations_iff_finite
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O)) :
    HasLocalSingleRelationFactorizations O F ↔ HasLocalFiniteRelationFactorizations O F
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_coveringSieve_retract_free
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site, a sheaf of modules which is flat and locally of finite presentation is,
locally on the site, a direct summand of a finite free sheaf of modules: every object `U`
carries a covering sieve on each member `f : V ⟶ U` of which `F|_V` is a retract of
`O_V^{⊕ I}` for some finite `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_retract_free
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max v w} RingCat.{max v w})]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max v w}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max v w}]
    [∀ T : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over T) AddCommGrpCat.{max v w}]
    [∀ T : C, (J.over T).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max v w}]
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max v w})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max v w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hF : IsFlat F) (U : C) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧ ∀ {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
      ∃ I : Type (max v w), Finite I ∧
        ∃ (i : F.over V ⟶ _root_.SheafOfModules.free
            (R := (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O).over V) I)
          (r : _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O).over V) I ⟶
            F.over V), i ≫ r = 𝟙 (F.over V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.isIso_quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictBaseChangeSquare
declarations.doc:
**The comparison `(Rf_*K)|_V ⟶ Rf'_*(K|_U)` of [Stacks, Tag 08FE] is invertible on the
quasi-coherent derived categories.**  This is the slot that
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Duality.OpenImmersion.TwistedInverseImageRestrictionConjugate`
leaves open; see the module documentation for the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictBaseChangeSquare (sq : IsPullback j' f' f j) :
    IsIso (quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictBaseChangeSquare j' f' f j hpushj' hpushf hpushf' hpushj
      (fun K i => derivedCategoryB_derivedRestrict j K.obj K.property i)
      (fun K i => derivedCategoryB_derivedRestrict j' K.obj K.property i) sq.w)
declarations.comment: invertibility of Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictBaseChangeSquare, the mate of Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPushforwardSquareIso across the two restriction adjunctions, on the quasi-coherent derived categories of a cartesian square of schemes whose vertical arrows are open immersions, at the locally small model. The isomorphism of functors itself is Stacks.Cohomology.derivedPushforwardRestrictIso, for ringed spaces; what is added here is that this particular canonical map is the invertible one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedChow.derivedPushforwardRestrictOpenIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08FE] at an open of the target of a morphism of schemes.**  Restricting the
derived direct image along `q` to an open `V` of the target is the derived direct image along
`q ∣_ V` of the restriction to `q ⁻¹ᵁ V`: "forming the total direct image commutes with
localization".
declarations.comment: for the standard derived direct image and derived pullback of [Stacks, Tag 079W], at the inclusion of an open subscheme of the target of a morphism of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.schemeDerivedPushforwardRestrictOpenIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08FE] for schemes.** For a Cartesian square of schemes
```
X' --f'--> T
|          |
g'         g
v          v
X ---f---> S
```
whose vertical sides are open immersions, the restriction to `T` of `Rf_*E` is the derived direct
image along `f'` of the restriction of `E` to `X'`.

Restriction along an open immersion is exact, so both restriction edges are the functors induced
on derived categories and carry no derivation.
declarations.statement:
def schemeDerivedPushforwardRestrictOpenIso {X S X' T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ S)
    [IsOpenImmersion g] (f' : X' ⟶ T) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    letI : IsOpenImmersion g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip inferInstance
    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor g).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((schemeDerivedPushforward f).obj E) ≅
      (schemeDerivedPushforward f').obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor g').mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
declarations.comment: for schemes, at the derived direct image of Tag 079W, with restriction to an open subscheme on the restriction edges

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.schemeDerivedPushforwardRestrictOpensIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08FE] for schemes, at an open of the base.** The restriction to an open
`U ⊆ S` of `Rf_*E` is the derived direct image along `f ∣_ U : f ⁻¹ᵁ U ⟶ U` of the restriction of
`E` to `f ⁻¹ᵁ U`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.schemeDerivedPushforwardRestrictOpenIso` at the Cartesian square of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_morphismRestrict`.
declarations.statement:
def schemeDerivedPushforwardRestrictOpensIso {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (U : S.Opens)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((schemeDerivedPushforward f).obj E) ≅
      (schemeDerivedPushforward (f ∣_ U)).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
declarations.comment: for schemes, at the restriction of f to the preimage of an open of the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedPushforwardRestrictIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FE.** In a Cartesian square of ringed spaces
```
U ----g---> V
|           |
i           j
|           |
v           v
X ----f---> Y
```
in which `i` and `j` are open immersions, restricting the derived direct image along `j` is
naturally isomorphic to taking the derived direct image along `g` after restriction along `i`.

The four functors are arbitrary choices of right derived functors equipped with their canonical
units; hence the result applies in particular to the standard choices of `Rf_*`, `Rg_*`, and the
exact restriction functors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedPushforwardRestrictIso
    {X Y U V : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : U ⟶ X) (j : V ⟶ Y) (g : U ⟶ V)
    [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion i] [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion j]
    (h : IsPullback i g f j)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V))]
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)))
    (Rg : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V)))
    (Ri : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U)))
    (Rj : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V)))
    (αf : (modulePushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    (αg : (modulePushforward g).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rg)
    (αi : (modulePullback i).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Ri)
    (αj : (modulePullback j).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rj)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rg.IsRightDerivedFunctor αg
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Ri.IsRightDerivedFunctor αi
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rj.IsRightDerivedFunctor αj
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    Rf ⋙ Rj ≅ Ri ⋙ Rg

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedPushforwardRestrictIso_isCanonical
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `derivedPushforwardRestrictIso` is the canonical one: on a
K-injective representative it is induced by the fixed adjunction mate
`pushforwardRestrictHomotopyMap` and by the four specified derived-functor units.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardRestrictIso_isCanonical
    {X Y U V : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : U ⟶ X) (j : V ⟶ Y) (g : U ⟶ V)
    [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion i] [SheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion j]
    (h : IsPullback i g f j)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V))]
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)))
    (Rg : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V)))
    (Ri : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U)))
    (Rj : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing V)))
    (alpha_f : (modulePushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    (alpha_g : (modulePushforward g).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rg)
    (alpha_i : (modulePullback i).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Ri)
    (alpha_j : (modulePullback j).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rj)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha_f
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rg.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha_g
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Ri.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha_i
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rj.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha_j
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ) (_hI : I.IsKInjective) :
    alpha_j.app (((modulePushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I)) ≫
        Rj.map (alpha_f.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I)) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardRestrictIso f i j g h Rf Rg Ri Rj
          alpha_f alpha_g alpha_i alpha_j).hom.app
            (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I)) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((pushforwardRestrictHomotopyMap f i j g h.w).app
            ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I)) ≫
        alpha_g.app (((modulePullback i).mapHomotopyCategory
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I)) ≫
        Rg.map (alpha_i.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I))
declarations.comment: canonicality

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.tor
declarations.doc:
**The Tor's of two `O`-modules on a ringed site.** The `O`-module
`Tor_p^O(F, G) = H^{-p}(F ⊗_O^{L} G)`.
declarations.statement: def tor (p : ℤ) (F G : Modules R) : Modules R

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.isFlat_iff_isZero_tor_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08FG.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `F` be an `O`-module.
Then `F` is a flat `O`-module if and only if `Tor_1^O(F, G) = 0` for every `O`-module `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_isZero_tor_one (F : Modules R) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := R) F ↔
      ∀ G : Modules R, IsZero (tor R 1 F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.isKInjective_overMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FI for the slice-to-slice restriction.** Restriction of sheaves of modules along
`Over.map f`, for an arrow `f : V ⟶ U` of the site, carries K-injective complexes to K-injective
complexes.

Restriction along `Over.map f` is restriction to the slice of `C/U` at `Over.mk f` followed by the
transport of that iterated slice to `C/V`. The first preserves K-injectivity by the library's form
of Stacks 08FI for `SheafOfModules.overFunctor`, extension by zero being an exact left adjoint of
it, and the second by `isKInjective_sliceBackward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_overMap
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over U)) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      ((((_root_.SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} O f)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)
declarations.comment: for the restriction between two slices, along `Over.map`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.isKInjective_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FI.** Restriction to the slice site over an object preserves K-injective
complexes of sheaves of modules. Extension by zero is an exact left adjoint of the restriction,
so the adjoint criterion for K-injectivity applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_over {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (U : C)
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} R) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} R U).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedExtensionByZeroRestrictionAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FJ.** On the unbounded derived categories of modules over a ringed site,
extension by zero along the localization at an object is left adjoint to restriction to the
localized site. The adjunction is the canonical one: it is obtained by localizing the
degreewise underived adjunction, so its unit and counit are the images of the underived unit
and counit under the localization comparisons.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedExtensionByZeroRestrictionAdjunction
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    [HasDerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))] :
    let R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
    let jShriek := SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := Over.forget U) (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U))
    let restriction := SheafOfModules.overFunctor R U
    jShriek.mapDerivedCategory ⊣ restriction.mapDerivedCategory

registrations.name: IsStrictlyPerfect
registrations.comment: a complex of `O`-modules is strictly perfect

declarations.name: mappingCone_isStrictlyPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 08FM).**
Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, and let `f : A ⟶ B` be a morphism of complexes of
`O`-modules. If `A` and `B` are both strictly perfect (Definition 2), then the cone
`C(f) = CochainComplex.mappingCone f` (Definition 4) is strictly perfect.

Proof sketch (Tag 08FM, "immediate from the definitions"):
* Boundedness. By `CochainComplex.mappingCone.isZero_X_iff`,
  `IsZero ((mappingCone f).X i) ↔ IsZero (A.X (i+1)) ∧ IsZero (B.X i)`, so
  `{i | ¬ IsZero ((mappingCone f).X i)} ⊆ {i | ¬ IsZero (A.X (i+1))} ∪ {i | ¬ IsZero (B.X i)}`.
  The second set is `hB.bounded`; the first is the preimage of `hA.bounded` under
  `i ↦ i+1`, hence finite. A finite union of finite sets is finite.
* Term condition. Fix `i`. We have `(mappingCone f).X i ≅ A.X (i+1) ⊞ B.X i` via
  `HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.XIsoBiprod f i (i+1) rfl` (`mappingCone f` is
  definitionally `homotopyCofiber f`, and for `CochainComplex … ℤ` the relation `c.Rel i j`
  is `i+1 = j`). By Helper 2, `A.X (i+1) ⊞ B.X i` is a direct summand of a finite free
  module (since `A.X (i+1)` and `B.X i` are, by `hA.termDirectSummand`,
  `hB.termDirectSummand`); by Helper 1 (transport along that iso) so is
  `(mappingCone f).X i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mappingCone_isStrictlyPerfect
    {A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} R) ℤ} (f : A ⟶ B)
    [HomologicalComplex.HasHomotopyCofiber f]
    (hA : IsStrictlyPerfect R A) (hB : IsStrictlyPerfect R B) :
    IsStrictlyPerfect R (CochainComplex.mappingCone f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FN.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, `U` an object of `C`, and let
`p : G ⟶ F` be an epimorphism of `O|_U`-modules. A map `e : E ⟶ F` whose source is a direct
summand of a finite free `O|_U`-module lifts through `p` locally on `U`: there is a covering
sieve `S` of `U` such that for every `f : V ⟶ U` in `S` the restriction of `e` to `C/V`
factors through the restriction of `p`.

The lift is produced one coordinate at a time. Writing `E` as a retract of `O|_U^{⊕n}` by
`j : E ⟶ O|_U^{⊕n}` and `r : O|_U^{⊕n} ⟶ E` with `j ≫ r = 𝟙`, the composite `q = r ≫ e` is
determined by `n` global sections of `F` over `U`. Each of them lifts through `p` on a
covering sieve, since `p` is locally surjective; the intersection of those `n` sieves is still
covering, and over it the chosen lifts assemble, by the universal property of the free module,
into a map `O|_U^{⊕n}|_V ⟶ G|_V` over `p`. Precomposing with `j|_V` gives the lift of `e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_lift (X : RingedSite.{u, t, 0}) (U : X.C)
    [HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [(X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    (E F G : SheafOfModules.{0} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
    (e : E ⟶ F) (p : G ⟶ F) [Epi p]
    (hE : IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, (S ∈ X.J U) ∧
      (∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        ∃ l : E.over (Over.mk f) ⟶ G.over (Over.mk f),
          l ≫ p.over (Over.mk f) = e.over (Over.mk f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_acyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FP (1).** A map from a strictly perfect complex of `O|_U`-modules to an acyclic
complex is null-homotopic after restriction along every arrow of a covering sieve of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_acyclic
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E)
    (hF : F.Acyclic) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        Nonempty (Homotopy
          (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
            (Over.mk f)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_isZero_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FP (2).** A map from a strictly perfect complex of `O|_U`-modules supported in
degrees `≥ a` is null-homotopic after restriction along every arrow of a covering sieve of `U`,
provided the target has vanishing cohomology in those degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_isZero_homology (a : ℤ)
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E)
    (hE₀ : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hF : ∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero (F.homology i)) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        Nonempty (Homotopy
          (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
            (Over.mk f)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_lift_homotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FQ.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and `U` an object of `C`. Given a solid
diagram of complexes of `O|_U`-modules
```
E --α--> F
     ↗
    G
```
with `E` strictly perfect, `Eʲ = 0` for `j < a`, `Hʲ(f)` an isomorphism for `j > a` and an
epimorphism for `j = a`, there is a covering sieve of `U` such that over each of its arrows a
dotted arrow exists making the diagram commute up to homotopy.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_lift_homotopy (α : E ⟶ F) (f : G ⟶ F) (a : ℤ)
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E)
    (hEa : ∀ j : ℤ, j < a → IsZero (E.X j))
    (hf_gt : ∀ j : ℤ, a < j → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f j))
    (hf_a : Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f a)) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (g : V ⟶ U), S g →
        ∃ β : ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
              (Over.mk g)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
              (Over.mk g)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G,
          Nonempty (Homotopy
            (β ≫ ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
              (Over.mk g)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
            (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
              (Over.mk g)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_derived_zero_overMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FR (2), with the restriction to the slice over an arrow `V ⟶ U` of the covering
sieve expressed by `SheafOfModules.overMap`** rather than by restriction to an iterated slice.

This is the same statement as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_derived_zero_general`, in
the presentation of the restriction that Stacks 08FR (1) and pseudo-coherence use. The general
form of 08FR (2) is the one read here, the module sections living in the ring universe `w`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_derived_zero_overMap
    {E F : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) ℤ}
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E) (α : E ⟶ F)
    (hα : DerivedCategory.Q.map α = 0) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧ ∀ ⦃V : X.C⦄ (g : V ⟶ U), S g →
      Nonempty (Homotopy (((SheafOfModules.overMap.{w}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) g).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: local_null_homotopy, along an arrow of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_derived_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and `U` an object of `C`. Let
`α : E ⟶ F` be a map of complexes of `O|_U`-modules with `E` strictly perfect, and suppose the
image of `α` in `D(O|_U)` is zero. Then there is a covering sieve of `U` such that the
restriction of `α` along each of its arrows is homotopic to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_homotopy_zero_of_derived_zero
    {E F : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{0} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) ℤ}
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E) (α : E ⟶ F)
    (hα : DerivedCategory.Q.map α = 0) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        Nonempty (Homotopy
          (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)
            (Over.mk f)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0)
declarations.comment: local_null_homotopy

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_complexMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FR (1).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and `U` an object of `C`. Let `E`, `F` be
complexes of `O|_U`-modules with `E` strictly perfect. Any morphism `α : E ⟶ F` of `D(O|_U)` is,
after restriction along the arrows of a covering sieve of `U`, the image under the localisation
functor of a morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_complexMap
    {E F : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) ℤ}
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U) E)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        let H := SheafOfModules.overMap (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) f
        ∃ (hsheaf : HasSheafify (X.J.over V) AddCommGrpCat.{w})
          (hlocal : (X.J.over V).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}),
          letI := hsheaf
          letI := hlocal
          letI : HasDerivedCategory
              (SheafOfModules.{w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over V)) :=
            HasDerivedCategory.standard _
          ∃ (hadd : H.Additive)
            (hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits H)
            (hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits H),
            letI := hadd
            letI := hlim
            letI := hcolim
            ∃ β : (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E ⟶
                (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F,
              H.mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫ H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app F =
                H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app E ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map β
declarations.comment: local_representation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FT, part (1).** A complex `E` of `O`-modules is `m`-*pseudo-coherent* if every
object `U` of the site admits a covering `{V → U}` over each member of which there are a
strictly perfect complex `P` of `O|_V`-modules and a map `P ⟶ E|_V` inducing isomorphisms on
cohomology in every degree `> m` and an epimorphism on cohomology in degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom
    (E : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (m : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FT, part (2).** A complex of `O`-modules is *pseudo-coherent* if it is
`m`-pseudo-coherent for every integer `m`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsPseudoCoherentComplex
    (E : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FT, part (3), first clause.** An object of `D(O)` is `m`-*pseudo-coherent* if
it is isomorphic to the image of an `m`-pseudo-coherent complex.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsPseudoCoherentFrom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (m : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3), m-pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FT, part (3), second clause.** An object of `D(O)` is *pseudo-coherent* if it
is isomorphic to the image of a pseudo-coherent complex.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsPseudoCoherent
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    Prop
declarations.comment: part (3), pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherent_derivedRestriction_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FU, part (3), all degrees at once, in the direction which restricts
pseudo-coherence to a slice**, at independent universes. If an object `E` of `D(O)` is
pseudo-coherent, then its restriction to the localized ringed site over any object `V` of `C` is
pseudo-coherent there.

This is not the fixed-degree statement read in each degree: the all-degrees clause of Stacks
08FT (3) asks for **one** complex which is `m`-pseudo-coherent for every `m`, and a family of
degreewise statements does not provide it.  What the proof restricts is the single complex that
pseudo-coherence of `E` already provides, and it stays `m`-pseudo-coherent for every `m` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_restrictComplex_general`, which is
itself stated at one complex and an arbitrary degree; so no quantifier swap is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedRestriction_general
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hE : X.IsPseudoCoherent E) (V : X.C) :
    (X.over V).IsPseudoCoherent
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
declarations.comment: part (3), all degrees, restriction to a slice

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_locally
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FU, part (3).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `E` be an object of
`D(O)`. If every object `U` of `C` admits a covering `{V → U}` over each member of which the
restriction of `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent, then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_locally
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (h : ∀ U : X.C, ∃ S : Presieve U, Sieve.generate S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ ⦃V : X.C⦄ (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        (X.over V).IsPseudoCoherentFrom
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{0}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) m) :
    X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FU, part (2).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `E` be an object of `D(O)`
which is `m`-pseudo-coherent. Then every complex of `O`-modules representing `E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_iso
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (hE : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E) :
    X.IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom K m
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FU, part (3), in the direction which restricts pseudo-coherence to a slice.** If
an object `E` of `D(O)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent, then its restriction to the localized ringed
site over any object `V` of `C` is `m`-pseudo-coherent there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedRestriction
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (hE : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) (V : X.C) :
    (X.over V).IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) m
declarations.comment: part (3), restriction to a slice

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_covering_of_terminal
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, let `E` be an object of `D(O)` and let `T` be a final object of
`C`. If a covering `{V → T}` of `T` carries over each of its members a strictly perfect complex `P`
of `O|_V`-modules and a morphism `P ⟶ E|_V` of `D(O|_V)` which is an isomorphism on cohomology in
every degree `> m` and an epimorphism on cohomology in degree `m`, then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_covering_of_terminal
    (T : X.C) (hT : IsTerminal T)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (S : Presieve T) (hS : Sieve.generate S ∈ X.J T)
    (hdata : ∀ ⦃V : X.C⦄ (f : V ⟶ T), S f →
      ∃ P : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{0} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over V)) ℤ,
        IsStrictlyPerfect ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over V) P ∧
        ∃ α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{0}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E,
          (∀ j : ℤ, m < j → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).map α)) ∧
          Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map α)) :
    X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_distinguished_one_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FV, part (1)**, with the site, its morphisms and the sections of the structure
sheaf at independent universes. Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let
`K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K[1]` be a distinguished triangle of `D(O)`. If `K` is `(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent
and `L` is `m`-pseudo-coherent, then `M` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_distinguished_one_general (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_homology_general
declarations.doc:
The degree-`m` cohomology of an `m`-pseudo-coherent object of the derived category of modules
over a ringed site `RingedSite.{u, v, w}`, whose cohomology vanishes above `m`, is of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_homology_general (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, HasSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) i).obj K)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) m).obj K).IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: finite_type_top_cohomology, at independent universes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FX**, finite type of the top cohomology. The degree-`m` cohomology of an
`m`-pseudo-coherent object of the derived category whose higher cohomology vanishes is of
finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_homology (X : RingedSite.{u, u, 0})
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{0} RingCat.{0})]
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [∀ U : X.C, HasSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{0} AddCommGrpCat.{0})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) i).obj K)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) m).obj K).IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: finite_type_top_cohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFinitePresentation_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08FX**, finite presentation of the top cohomology. The degree-`m + 1` cohomology
of an `m`-pseudo-coherent object of the derived category whose cohomology vanishes above
`m + 1` is finitely presented.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_homology (X : RingedSite.{u, u, 0})
