    HasTorAmplitude T' ((derivedPullback (toZariskiSmallModelHom B S hS)).obj E) a b ↔
      HasTorAmplitude T E a b
declarations.comment:
clause (1): `E` has tor amplitude in `[a, b]` ⟺ `ε^*E` has tor amplitude in
  `[a, b]`, for `ε` the comparison morphism of Equation 75.4.0.1 (Stacks 08H7) read on the
  `Type u`-presented model `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.smallModelRingedTopos` of the small
  étale ringed topos, and `ε^*` its derived pullback.  Stated for an arbitrary derived tensor
  product datum on either side rather than for the canonical one.  Clause (2) is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasFiniteTorDimension_derivedPullback_of_hasFiniteTorDimension`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasFiniteTorDimension_derivedPullback_of_hasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HF, clause (2).**  An object `E` of `D(𝒪_S)` has finite Tor dimension for a
derived tensor product datum `T` on the small Zariski ringed site of `S` **if and only if** its
derived pullback `Lε^*E` has finite Tor dimension for a derived tensor product datum `T'` on the
model.  Both data are arbitrary.

This is clause (1) with the interval existentially quantified: an interval containing the Tor
amplitude of one of the two objects contains that of the other.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFiniteTorDimension_derivedPullback_of_hasFiniteTorDimension
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct S.zariskiRingedTopos.toRingedSite)
    (T' : DerivedTensorProduct (smallModelRingedTopos B S hS).toRingedSite)
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules S.zariskiRingedTopos.toRingedSite) :
    HasFiniteTorDimension T' ((derivedPullback (toZariskiSmallModelHom B S hS)).obj E) ↔
      HasFiniteTorDimension T E
declarations.comment:
clause (2): `E` has finite tor dimension ⟺ `ε^*E` has finite tor dimension, for
  `ε` the comparison morphism of Equation 75.4.0.1 (Stacks 08H7) read on the `Type u`-presented
  model `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.smallModelRingedTopos` of the small étale ringed topos, and
  `ε^*` its derived pullback.  Stated for an arbitrary derived tensor product datum on either
  side rather than for the canonical one.  Clause (1) is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasTorAmplitude_derivedPullback_of_hasTorAmplitude`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isPerfectZariski_iff_isPerfectSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HG.** Let `S` be a scheme and `E` an object of `D(𝒪_S)`. Then `E` is a perfect
object of `D(𝒪_S)` if and only if `ε^*E` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_étale)`, where
`ε : (S_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` is the morphism of ringed sites of Stacks 08H7 and `ε^*` its
pullback on the derived category — the termwise associated-module functor, `ε` being flat
(Stacks 08H8).

Perfectness on either side is Stacks 08G5. The direction `E` perfect ⟹ `ε^*E` perfect is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.perfectToAssociatedModule_of_slice_exact`; the converse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isPerfectZariski_of_isPerfectSmallEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectZariski_iff_isPerfectSmallEtale
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.zariskiRingedSite.O))) :
    IsPerfectZariski S E ↔ IsPerfectSmallEtale B S hS E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.perfectToAssociatedModule_of_slice_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HG, the direction `E` perfect ⟹ `ε^*E` perfect.**

If `E` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)` then `ε^*E` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_étale)`, `ε` being
the morphism of ringed sites of Stacks 08H7 and `ε^*` the termwise associated-module functor on the
derived category, which is what `ε` being flat means.

Left exactness of the associated-module functor on a slice over an open of `S` is the exactness
assertion of Stacks 08H8 localized at that open, proved by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.preservesFiniteLimits_pullback_sliceStructureMap`.  Everything else
is available: the transfer engine
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_mapDerivedCategory_of_hypotheses`, the localization square
of Stacks 03DV (`associatedModuleOverIso`), the unit comparison, and the covering
(`coversTop_obj_opensToSmallEtale`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfectToAssociatedModule_of_slice_exact
    (E : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.zariskiRingedSite.O)))
    (hE : IsPerfectZariski S E) :
    IsPerfectSmallEtale B S hS E
declarations.comment:
the direction `E` perfect ⟹ `ε^*E` perfect ONLY. Left exactness of
  `SheafOfModules.pullback (SmallEtale.sliceStructureMap B S hS V)` -- the exactness assertion of
  Stacks 08H8 localized at an open `V` of `S` -- is supplied by
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.preservesFiniteLimits_pullback_sliceStructureMap`, which localizes
  the whole-site 08H8 (`preservesFiniteLimits_associatedModule`) along the open immersion. The
  converse
  direction `ε^*E` perfect ⟹ `E` perfect is NOT proved: the source derives it from Stacks 08G8
  together with the converses of Stacks 08HE and Stacks 08HF, and of those the converse of
  Stacks 08HE does not exist in this tree.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ApproximationHolds
declarations.doc:
*Approximation holds* for the triple `(T, E, m)`: some perfect object of `D(𝒪_F)` supported on
`T` maps to `E` by a map inducing isomorphisms on cohomology in every degree above `m` and a
surjection in degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev ApproximationHolds (T : Set (points B S hS F))
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, m} B S hS F hF) (m : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ApproximationByPerfectComplexes
declarations.doc:
*Approximation by perfect complexes holds* on `F`: for every closed `T ⊆ |F|` whose open
complement has quasi-compact inclusion there is an integer `r` such that approximation holds for
every triple `(T, E, m)` in which `E` is `(m - r)`-pseudo-coherent and `Hⁱ(E)` is supported on `T`
for every `i ≥ m - r`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev ApproximationByPerfectComplexes : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_derivedModulePushforward_of_cohomologySupportedOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HK.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `(U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary
distinguished square of algebraic spaces over `S`, and set `T = |X| \ |U|`.  Let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_V)` supported on `j^{-1}T`.  Then `Rj_*E` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)`.

Perfectness is local on `X_étale` along the two morphisms of the square, and `Rj_*E` is `j_!E`,
whose restriction to `U` vanishes and whose restriction to `V` is the perfect `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedModulePushforward_of_cohomologySupportedOn
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1
      (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2))
    (hperf : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1
      (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2).IsPerfect E)
    (hE : CohomologySupportedOn B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2
      (edsEtalePreimageComplementPoints B S hS hsq) E) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS W.1 W.2).IsPerfect
      ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)).obj E)
declarations.comment: Rj_*E is perfect in D(O_X) for an elementary distinguished square and E perfect on V supported on j^{-1}T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_rightAdjoint_edsDerivedRestrictEtale_of_cohomologySupportedOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HK.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `(U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary
distinguished square of algebraic spaces over `S`, and set `T = |X| \ |U|`.  Let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_V)` supported on `j⁻¹(T)`.  Then `Rj_*E` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)`.

`Rj_*` is a right adjoint of derived restriction `(-)|_V`, given together with its adjunction,
as in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_cohomologySupportedOn`; this
determines it up to a unique compatible isomorphism.  The proof is the source's: perfectness is
local on `X_étale` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_of_isPerfect_eds`), the restriction of
`Rj_*E` to `U` vanishes and its restriction to `V` is `E` (Stacks 08GG (2)(b)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_rightAdjoint_edsDerivedRestrictEtale_of_cohomologySupportedOn
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2))
    (hperf : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1
      (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2).IsPerfect E)
    (hE : CohomologySupportedOn B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2
      (edsEtalePreimageComplementPoints B S hS hsq) E) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS W.1 W.2).IsPerfect (RpushD.obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HL.**  Let `(U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square of
algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let `T ⊆ |X| \ |U|` and let `(T, E, m)` be a triple as in
Stacks 08HI.  If

1. approximation holds for `(j^{-1}T, E|_V, m)`, and
2. the sheaves `Hⁱ(E)` for `i ≥ m` are supported on `T`,

then approximation holds for `(T, E, m)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationHolds_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
    (T : Set (points B S hS W.1)) (hTU : T ⊆ edsComplementPoints B S hS Uo)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (m : ℤ)
    (happrox : ApproximationHolds B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2
      (pointsMap B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq).hom ⁻¹' T)
      ((quasicoherentDerivedEtalePullback B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
        (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)).obj E) m)
    (hsupp : ∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
      supportOfSheaf B S hS W.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (etaleRingSheaf B S hS W)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) i).obj E.obj)) ⊆ T) :
    ApproximationHolds B S hS W.1 W.2 T E m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_approximationHolds_edsEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HL.**  Let `(U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square of
algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let `T ⊆ |X| \ |U|` and let `(T, E, m)` be a triple as in
Stacks 08HI.  If

1. approximation holds for `(j^{-1}T, E|_V, m)`, and
2. the sheaves `Hⁱ(E)` for `i ≥ m` are supported on `T`,

then approximation holds for `(T, E, m)`.

The approximation produced is `j_!P ⟶ j_!(E|_V) ⟶ E` for an approximation `P ⟶ E|_V` of the
restricted triple; `j_!P = Rj_*P` by Stacks 08GG part (2) clause (c).
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationHolds_of_approximationHolds_edsEtale
    (T : Set (points B S hS W.1)) (hTU : T ⊆ edsComplementPoints B S hS Uo)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (m : ℤ)
    (happrox : ApproximationHolds B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2
      (pointsMap B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1 (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq).hom ⁻¹' T)
      ((quasicoherentDerivedEtalePullback B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
        (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)).obj E) m)
    (hsupp : ∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
      supportOfSheaf B S hS W.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS W.1 W.2).O))).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) i).obj E.obj)) ⊆ T) :
    ApproximationHolds B S hS W.1 W.2 T E m
declarations.comment:
for an elementary distinguished square (U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X), T ⊆ |X| \ |U| and a
triple (T, E, m): approximation for (j^{-1}T, E|_V, m) with E|_V = quasicoherentDerivedEtalePullback
of E, together with H^i(E) supported on T for i ≥ m, gives approximation for (T, E, m); nothing
else is bound. T is any subset of |X| \ |U|, closedness being unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_affineCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HM.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is
representable by an affine scheme.  Then approximation holds (Stacks 08HI) for every triple
`(T, E, m)` for which there exists an integer `r ≥ 0` such that

1. `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent,
2. `Hⁱ(E)` is supported on `T` for `i ≥ m - r + 1`,
3. `X ∖ T` is the union of `r` affine opens `V₁, …, V_r` of `X`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_isAffineSpace`, applied to the integer and
the affine opens provided.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationHolds_of_affineCover (hXa : IsAffineSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (m : ℤ)
    (h : ∃ r : ℕ,
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E.obj m ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, m - (r : ℤ) + 1 ≤ i →
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).O))).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) i).obj E.obj)) ⊆ T) ∧
      ∃ V : Fin r → {G : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G},
        (∀ k, IsAffineSpace B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor) ∧
        ⋃ k, Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor (V k).1.ι) = Tᶜ) :
    ApproximationHolds B S hS X hX T E m
declarations.comment:
first assertion: for X an algebraic space representable by an affine scheme,
approximation holds for every triple (T, E, m) such that there exists an integer r ≥ 0 with E
m-pseudo-coherent, H^i(E) supported on T for i ≥ m - r + 1 and X \ T a union of r affine
opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**The "in particular" of Stacks 08HM**: approximation by perfect complexes (Stacks 08HJ)
holds on an algebraic space representable by an affine scheme.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isAffineSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_affine (hXa : IsAffineSpace B S hS X) :
    ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS X hX
declarations.comment:
second assertion: approximation by perfect complexes holds on an algebraic space
representable by an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_isAffineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HM.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is
representable by an affine scheme.  Then approximation holds (Stacks 08HI) for every triple
`(Z, E, m)` for which there is an integer `r ≥ 0` with

1. `E` `m`-pseudo-coherent,
2. `Hⁱ(E)` supported on `Z` for `i ≥ m - r + 1`,
3. `X ∖ Z` the union of `r` affine opens `V₁, …, V_r` of `X`.

The case `X = h_U` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_isAffine_represented`; the
general case is transported along an isomorphism `X ≅ h_U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_of_iso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationHolds_of_isAffineSpace (hXa : IsAffineSpace B S hS F)
    (Z : Set (points B S hS F))
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (m : ℤ) (r : ℕ)
    (hpc : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E.obj m)
    (hsupp : ∀ i : ℤ, m - (r : ℤ) + 1 ≤ i →
      supportOfSheaf B S hS F
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E.obj)) ⊆ Z)
    (V : Fin r → {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G})
    (hV : ∀ k, IsAffineSpace B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor)
    (hcover : ⋃ k, Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor (V k).1.ι) = Zᶜ) :
    ApproximationHolds B S hS F hF Z E m
declarations.comment:
first assertion: approximation holds for every triple (T, E, m) with E
m-pseudo-coherent, H^i(E) supported on T for i ≥ m - r + 1 and X \ T a union of r affine opens,
for X an algebraic space representable by an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isAffineSpace
declarations.doc:
**The "in particular" of Stacks 08HM**: approximation by perfect complexes (Stacks 08HJ)
holds on an algebraic space representable by an affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isAffineSpace (hXa : IsAffineSpace B S hS F) :
    ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS F hF
declarations.comment:
second assertion: approximation by perfect complexes holds on an algebraic space
representable by an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationHolds_and_approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isAffineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HM.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is
representable by an affine scheme.  Then

1. approximation holds (Stacks 08HI) for every triple `(Z, E, m)` for which there is an integer
   `r ≥ 0` with
   1. `E` `m`-pseudo-coherent,
   2. `Hⁱ(E)` supported on `Z` for `i ≥ m - r + 1`,
   3. `X ∖ Z` the union of `r` affine opens `V₁, …, V_r` of `X`;
2. in particular, approximation by perfect complexes (Stacks 08HJ) holds for `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationHolds_and_approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isAffineSpace
    (hXa : IsAffineSpace B S hS F) :
    (∀ (Z : Set (points B S hS F))
      (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (m : ℤ) (r : ℕ),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E.obj m →
      (∀ i : ℤ, m - (r : ℤ) + 1 ≤ i →
        supportOfSheaf B S hS F
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E.obj)) ⊆ Z) →
      ∀ (V : Fin r → {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G}),
      (∀ k, IsAffineSpace B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor) →
      ⋃ k, Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (V k).1.toFunctor (V k).1.ι) = Zᶜ →
      ApproximationHolds B S hS F hF Z E m) ∧
    ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS F hF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HN.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `(U ⊆ X, j : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary
distinguished square of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `U` quasi-compact, `V` affine and
`U ×_X V` quasi-compact.  If approximation by perfect complexes holds on `U`, then approximation
by perfect complexes holds on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
    {X V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (f : V ⟶ X)
    (hsq : IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hX U f)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.toFunctor)
    (hVaff : IsAffineSpace B S hS V)
    (hUVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (U.preimage f).toFunctor)
    (hU : ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS U.toFunctor hsq.isOpenSubspace.1) :
    ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS X hX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HP.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S`.  Then approximation by perfect complexes holds on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem approximationByPerfectComplexes_of_qcqs (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    ApproximationByPerfectComplexes.{u, u} B S hS X hX

declarations.name: existsUnique_algHom_henselian_of_residue_datum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 08HQ** (map into henselian). Let `R → S` be a ring map with `S`
henselian local, `p = R ∩ m_S` the contraction of the maximal ideal. Given an
etale `R`-algebra `A`, a prime `q` of `A` lying over `p`, and a
`κ(p)`-algebra map `τ : κ(q) → κ(m_S)`, there is a unique `R`-algebra map
`f : A → S` with `q = f⁻¹(m_S)` inducing `τ` on residue fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_algHom_henselian_of_residue_datum
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [HenselianLocalRing S]
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.Etale R A]
    -- `q` is a prime of `A` lying over `p = R ∩ m_S`.
    (𝔮 : Ideal A) [𝔮.IsPrime]
    (hlo : 𝔮.comap (algebraMap R A) = (maximalIdeal S).comap (algebraMap R S))
    -- `τ : κ(q) → κ(m_S)` is a `κ(p)`-algebra map: the triangle over `κ(p)` commutes.
    (τ : 𝔮.ResidueField →+* (maximalIdeal S).ResidueField)
    (hτ : τ.comp (Ideal.ResidueField.map _ 𝔮 (algebraMap R A) hlo.symm)
        = Ideal.ResidueField.map _ (maximalIdeal S) (algebraMap R S) rfl) :
    -- There is a unique `R`-algebra map `f : A → S` with `q = f⁻¹(m_S)` inducing `τ`.
    ∃! f : A →ₐ[R] S,
      ∃ (h : (maximalIdeal S).comap f.toRingHom = 𝔮),
        Ideal.ResidueField.map 𝔮 (maximalIdeal S) f.toRingHom h.symm = τ

declarations.name: Stacks.Henselian.EtaleLifting.algHom
declarations.doc:
**The lift of a residue datum along an ind-étale algebra into a henselian local ring**
(Stacks Tag 08HR, Lemma 10.154.6). Let `R → S` be a ring map with `S` henselian local, let `A` be
ind-étale over `R`, let `q` be a prime of `A` lying over `p = R ∩ 𝔪 S`, and let
`τ : κ(q) → κ(S)` be a `κ(p)`-algebra map. This is the `R`-algebra map `A → S` with
`q = f⁻¹(𝔪 S)` inducing `τ` on residue fields; `algHom_spec` is those two properties and
`algHom_unique` says it is the only such map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algHom
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {S : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R S]
    [HenselianLocalRing S]
    (hA : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} A)))
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : p = (maximalIdeal S).comap (algebraMap R S))
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R A))
    (τ : q.ResidueField →+* ResidueField S)
    (hτ : τ.comp (residueFieldMapFib p q hpq) = residueFieldMapBase p hp) :
    A →ₐ[R] S
declarations.comment:
the map itself; `algHom_spec` is its two defining properties and `algHom_unique`
its uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.Henselian.EtaleLifting.algHom_spec
declarations.doc: `algHom` pulls the maximal ideal of `S` back to `q` and induces `τ` on residue fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem algHom_spec
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {S : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R S]
    [HenselianLocalRing S]
    (hA : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} A)))
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : p = (maximalIdeal S).comap (algebraMap R S))
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R A))
    (τ : q.ResidueField →+* ResidueField S)
    (hτ : τ.comp (residueFieldMapFib p q hpq) = residueFieldMapBase p hp) :
    q = (maximalIdeal S).comap (algHom hA p hp q hpq τ hτ : A →+* S) ∧
      InducesResidueMap q (algHom hA p hp q hpq τ hτ : A →+* S) τ
declarations.comment: the two defining properties of `algHom`

declarations.name: Stacks.Henselian.EtaleLifting.algHom_unique
declarations.doc:
`algHom` is the only `R`-algebra map `A → S` pulling `𝔪 S` back to `q` and inducing `τ` on
residue fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem algHom_unique
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {S : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R S]
    [HenselianLocalRing S]
    (hA : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} A)))
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : p = (maximalIdeal S).comap (algebraMap R S))
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R A))
    (τ : q.ResidueField →+* ResidueField S)
    (hτ : τ.comp (residueFieldMapFib p q hpq) = residueFieldMapBase p hp)
    (f : A →ₐ[R] S)
    (hf : q = (maximalIdeal S).comap (f : A →+* S) ∧
      InducesResidueMap q (f : A →+* S) τ) :
    f = algHom hA p hp q hpq τ hτ
declarations.comment: uniqueness of `algHom`

declarations.name: CommRingCat.ind_etale_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**A filtered colimit of étale algebras over a filtered colimit of étale algebras.** Let
`R → A → B` be ring maps. If `A` and `B` are filtered colimits of étale `R`-algebras, then `B` is
a filtered colimit of étale `A`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem ind_etale_of_comp {R A B : CommRingCat.{u}} (f : R ⟶ A) (g : A ⟶ B)
    (hf : ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : Under R ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale) (Under.mk f))
    (hfg : ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : Under R ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale) (Under.mk (f ≫ g))) :
    ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : Under A ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale) (Under.mk g)
declarations.comment:
"`Λ` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras" is
`ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : Under R ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale) Λ`, as in Lemma `07C3`; the source's
`R`-algebra map `A → B` is a map `g` together with the composite `f ≫ g` as the `R`-algebra
structure of `B`, so the triangle commutes by construction. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.ind_etale_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**A filtered colimit of étale algebras over a filtered colimit of étale algebras.** Let
`A → B → C` be ring maps. If `B` and `C` are filtered colimits of étale `A`-algebras, then `C` is
a filtered colimit of étale `B`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem ind_etale_of_comp {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hB : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} A).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of A B))
    (hC : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} A).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of A C)) :
    (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} B).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of B C)
declarations.comment:
"`Λ` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras" is
`(CommAlgCat.etale R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R Λ)`, as in Lemma `04GN`, and the source's
`A → B → C` is an `IsScalarTower A B C`. Tagged jointly with `CommRingCat.ind_etale_of_comp`,
which is this lemma for ring maps and the `ObjectProperty.ind` spelling on `Under R`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: HenselianLocalRing.existsUnique_algEquiv_of_ind_etale
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the henselization** (Stacks 08HT). Let `R` be a ring, let `S` and `S'` be
henselian local `R`-algebras that are filtered colimits of étale `R`-algebras, and let
`p : S →ₐ[R] K` and `p' : S' →ₐ[R] K` be surjections onto a field `K`, so that `K` is the residue
field of both. Then there is an `R`-algebra isomorphism `e : S ≃ₐ[R] S'` such that an `R`-algebra
map `f : S → S'` satisfies `p' ∘ f = p` if and only if `f = e`; in particular `e` is the unique
`R`-algebra isomorphism `S → S'` compatible with the maps to `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem HenselianLocalRing.existsUnique_algEquiv_of_ind_etale
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R S'] [HenselianLocalRing S] [HenselianLocalRing S']
    (hS : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R S))
    (hS' : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R S'))
    {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra R K] (p : S →ₐ[R] K) (p' : S' →ₐ[R] K)
    (hp : Function.Surjective p) (hp' : Function.Surjective p') :
    ∃ e : S ≃ₐ[R] S', ∀ f : S →ₐ[R] S', p'.comp f = p ↔ f = (e : S →ₐ[R] S')
declarations.comment:
"`S` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras" is
`(CommAlgCat.etale R).ind (CommAlgCat.of R S)`, as in Lemma 04GN; the source's commutative square
is the two `R`-algebra maps to `K`; and "the arrows identify `K` with the residue field" is their
surjectivity, `K` being a field. Uniqueness is stated among all `R`-algebra maps `S → S'`, which is
stronger than the source's uniqueness among isomorphisms. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_unique_prime_isHenselization_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**The henselization after a ring map** (Stacks 08HU). Let `R → S` be a ring map and let
`q ⊆ S` lie over `p ⊆ R`. Let `Rh` and `Sh` be henselizations of `R_p` and `S_q`. The local
ring map `f : Rh → Sh` of Lemma 04GS (the unique local map over `R_p → S_q`) identifies `Sh` with
the henselization of `Rh ⊗[R] S` at the unique prime `Q` lying over `𝔪_Rh` and `q`: here `Q` is the
inverse image of `𝔪_Sh` under the map `g : Rh ⊗[R] S → Sh` induced by `f`, and `Sh` is a
henselization of `(Rh ⊗[R] S)_Q` through an algebra structure extending `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_prime_isHenselization_tensorProduct [Algebra R Sq] [Algebra Rp Sq]
    [IsScalarTower R S Sq] [IsScalarTower R Rp Sq] [IsHenselization Rp (ResidueField Rp) Rh]
    [Algebra Rp Sh] [IsScalarTower Rp Sq Sh] [IsHenselization Sq (ResidueField Sq) Sh] :
    ∃ f : Rh →ₐ[R] Sh, IsLocalHom f ∧
      f.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap Rp Rh) = algebraMap Rp Sh ∧
      (∀ f' : Rh →ₐ[R] Sh, IsLocalHom f' →
        f'.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap Rp Rh) = algebraMap Rp Sh → f' = f) ∧
      let g : Rh ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R] Sh :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S Sh) fun _ _ => .all _ _
      ∃ (Q : Ideal (Rh ⊗[R] S)) (_ : Q.IsPrime),
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)) =
          maximalIdeal Rh ∧
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)).toRingHom = q ∧
        Q = (maximalIdeal Sh).comap g.toRingHom ∧
        (∀ Q' : Ideal (Rh ⊗[R] S), Q'.IsPrime →
          Q'.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)) =
            maximalIdeal Rh →
          Q'.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)).toRingHom =
            q → Q' = Q) ∧
        ∃ _ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh,
          IsLocalHom (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh) ∧
          IsHenselization (Localization.AtPrime Q) (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) Sh ∧
          (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh).comp
            (algebraMap (Rh ⊗[R] S) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) = g.toRingHom
declarations.comment:
The map `R^h → S^h` of 04GS is pinned as the unique local `R`-algebra map `f`
compatible with `R_p → S_q`. The prime is characterized by its two contractions, with uniqueness,
and equals `g⁻¹(𝔪_{S^h})` for the map `g` induced by `f`; that `S^h` is the henselization of
`(R^h ⊗_R S)_Q` is `IsHenselization` with residue field `κ(Q)`, through an algebra structure
extending `g`. All rings share one universe, as `IsHenselization` requires.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.henselization_tensorProduct_at_unique_prime
declarations.doc:
**Henselization after a ring map** (Stacks 08HU), at six independent universes. For primes
`q` over `p`, the canonical local map between henselizations of `R_p` and `S_q` identifies the
latter with the henselization of `Rh ⊗[R] S` at its unique prime lying over both the maximal
ideal of `Rh` and `q`. The final equality says that the henselization map is induced by the
canonical map from the tensor product.

This is the source-strength form of tag 08HU, and the provider of that tag. The weaker
single-universe statement
`IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_unique_prime_isHenselization_tensorProduct` pins all six
rings to one `Type u`; its `@[stacks 08HU]` attribute is dropped in favour of this one. See the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselization_tensorProduct_at_unique_prime
    {R : Type uR} {Rp : Type uRp} {Rh : Type uRh}
    {S : Type uS} {Sq : Type uSq} {Sh : Type uSh}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [CommRing Rp] [IsLocalRing Rp] [Algebra R Rp] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rp p]
    [CommRing Sq] [IsLocalRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q]
    [Algebra R Sq] [Algebra Rp Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq] [IsScalarTower R Rp Sq]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh] [Algebra Rp Rh]
    [IsScalarTower R Rp Rh] [IsHenselization Rp (ResidueField Rp) Rh]
    [CommRing Sh] [IsLocalRing Sh] [Algebra R Sh] [Algebra S Sh] [Algebra Rp Sh]
    [Algebra Sq Sh] [IsScalarTower R S Sh] [IsScalarTower S Sq Sh]
    [IsScalarTower Rp Sq Sh] [IsHenselization Sq (ResidueField Sq) Sh] :
    ∃ f : Rh →ₐ[R] Sh,
      IsLocalHom f ∧
      f.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap Rp Rh) = algebraMap Rp Sh ∧
      (∀ f' : Rh →ₐ[R] Sh, IsLocalHom f' →
        f'.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap Rp Rh) = algebraMap Rp Sh → f' = f) ∧
      let g : Rh ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R] Sh :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S Sh)
          (fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _)
      ∃ (Q : Ideal (Rh ⊗[R] S)) (_hQ : Q.IsPrime),
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)) =
            maximalIdeal Rh ∧
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)).toRingHom = q ∧
        Q = (maximalIdeal Sh).comap g.toRingHom ∧
        (∀ (Q' : Ideal (Rh ⊗[R] S)), Q'.IsPrime →
          Q'.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)) =
              maximalIdeal Rh →
          Q'.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rh) (B := S)).toRingHom =
              q → Q' = Q) ∧
        ∃ alg : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh,
          letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh := alg
          ∃ _ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh),
            IsHenselization (Localization.AtPrime Q)
                (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) Sh ∧
              (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Sh).comp
                  (algebraMap (Rh ⊗[R] S) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) = g.toRingHom
declarations.comment:
Stated over six independent universes, as the source requires: the tag's six
rings `R`, `R_p`, `R^h`, `S`, `S_q`, `S^h` are unconstrained relative to one another.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_prime_isStrictHenselization_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**The strict henselization after a ring map** (Stacks 08HV). Let `R → S` be a ring map and
let `q ⊆ S` lie over `p ⊆ R`. Let `Rsh` and `Ssh` be strict henselizations of `R_p` and `S_q`,
with respect to the separable algebraic closures `κ(Rsh)` of `κ(p)` and `κ(Ssh)` of `κ(q)`, and
let `φ : κ(Rsh) → κ(Ssh)` be compatible with the residue maps out of `R`. The local map
`f : Rsh → Ssh` of Lemma 04GU inducing `φ` identifies `Ssh` with the strict henselization of
`Rsh ⊗[R] S` at the prime `Q = g⁻¹(𝔪_Ssh)`, where `g : Rsh ⊗[R] S → Ssh` is induced by `f`; `Q`
lies over `𝔪_Rsh` and over `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_prime_isStrictHenselization_tensorProduct [Algebra R Sq] [Algebra Rp Sq]
    [IsScalarTower R S Sq] [IsScalarTower R Rp Sq] [Algebra Rp Ssh] [IsScalarTower R Rp Ssh]
    [IsScalarTower Rp Sq Ssh] (phi : ResidueField Rsh →+* ResidueField Ssh)
    (hphi : phi.comp ((residue Rsh).comp (algebraMap R Rsh)) =
      (residue Ssh).comp (algebraMap R Ssh)) :
    ∃ f : Rsh →ₐ[R] Ssh, IsLocalHom f ∧
      (residue Ssh).comp f.toRingHom = phi.comp (residue Rsh) ∧
      (∀ f' : Rsh →ₐ[R] Ssh, IsLocalHom f' →
        (residue Ssh).comp f'.toRingHom = phi.comp (residue Rsh) → f' = f) ∧
      let g : Rsh ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R] Ssh :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S Ssh) fun _ _ => .all _ _
      ∃ (Q : Ideal (Rsh ⊗[R] S)) (_ : Q.IsPrime),
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rsh) (B := S)) =
          maximalIdeal Rsh ∧
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rsh) (B := S)).toRingHom = q ∧
        Q = (maximalIdeal Ssh).comap g.toRingHom ∧
        ∃ _ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh,
          IsLocalHom (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh) ∧
          ∃ _ : Algebra (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh),
            IsSepClosure (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh) ∧
            IsHenselization (Localization.AtPrime Q) (ResidueField Ssh) Ssh ∧
            (∀ x, algebraMap (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh)
              (residue (Localization.AtPrime Q) x) =
                residue Ssh (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh x)) ∧
            (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh).comp
              (algebraMap (Rsh ⊗[R] S) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) = g.toRingHom
declarations.comment:
The separable algebraic closures are the residue fields of `R^sh` and `S^sh`, and
the commutative square is the compatibility `hphi` of `φ` with the residue maps out of `R`. The map
of 04GU is pinned as the unique local `R`-algebra map inducing `φ`. The prime is `g⁻¹(𝔪_{S^sh})`
with its two contractions; that `S^sh` is the strict henselization of `(R^sh ⊗_R S)_Q` is
`IsHenselization` with residue field `κ(S^sh)`, separably closed over `κ(Q)`. All rings share one
universe, as `IsHenselization` requires.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.strictHenselization_tensorProduct_at_induced_prime
declarations.doc:
**Strict henselization after a ring map** (Stacks 08HV), at six independent universes. For
primes `q` over `p` and compatible separable closures of their residue fields, the canonical local
map between strict henselizations identifies the target with the strict henselization of
`Rsh ⊗[R] S` at the prime induced by that map.

This is the source-strength form of tag 08HV, and the provider of that tag. The weaker
single-universe statement
`IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_prime_isStrictHenselization_tensorProduct` pins all six rings
to one `Type u`; its `@[stacks 08HV]` attribute is dropped in favour of this one. See the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictHenselization_tensorProduct_at_induced_prime
    {R : Type uR} {Rp : Type uRp} {Rsh : Type uRsh}
    {S : Type uS} {Sq : Type uSq} {Ssh : Type uSsh}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [CommRing Rp] [IsLocalRing Rp] [Algebra R Rp] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rp p]
    [CommRing Sq] [IsLocalRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q]
    [Algebra R Sq] [Algebra Rp Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq] [IsScalarTower R Rp Sq]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh] [Algebra Rp Rsh]
    [IsScalarTower R Rp Rsh]
    [Algebra (ResidueField Rp) (ResidueField Rsh)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Rp) (ResidueField Rsh)]
    [IsHenselization Rp (ResidueField Rsh) Rsh]
    [CommRing Ssh] [IsLocalRing Ssh] [Algebra R Ssh] [Algebra S Ssh] [Algebra Rp Ssh]
    [Algebra Sq Ssh] [IsScalarTower R S Ssh] [IsScalarTower S Sq Ssh]
    [IsScalarTower R Rp Ssh] [IsScalarTower Rp Sq Ssh]
    [Algebra (ResidueField Sq) (ResidueField Ssh)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Sq) (ResidueField Ssh)]
    [IsHenselization Sq (ResidueField Ssh) Ssh]
    (phi : ResidueField Rsh →+* ResidueField Ssh)
    (hphi : phi.comp ((residue Rsh).comp (algebraMap R Rsh)) =
      (residue Ssh).comp (algebraMap R Ssh)) :
    ∃ f : Rsh →ₐ[R] Ssh,
      IsLocalHom f ∧
      (residue Ssh).comp f.toRingHom = phi.comp (residue Rsh) ∧
      (∀ f' : Rsh →ₐ[R] Ssh, IsLocalHom f' →
        (residue Ssh).comp f'.toRingHom = phi.comp (residue Rsh) → f' = f) ∧
      let g : Rsh ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R] Ssh :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S Ssh)
          (fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _)
      ∃ (Q : Ideal (Rsh ⊗[R] S)) (_hQ : Q.IsPrime),
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := Rsh) (B := S)) =
            maximalIdeal Rsh ∧
        Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Rsh) (B := S)).toRingHom = q ∧
        Q = (maximalIdeal Ssh).comap g.toRingHom ∧
        ∃ alg : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh,
          letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh := alg
          ∃ _ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh),
            ∃ algRes : Algebra (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh),
              letI : Algebra (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh) := algRes
              IsSepClosure (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh) ∧
                IsHenselization (Localization.AtPrime Q) (ResidueField Ssh) Ssh ∧
                (∀ x : Localization.AtPrime Q,
                  algebraMap (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (ResidueField Ssh)
                      (residue (Localization.AtPrime Q) x) =
                    residue Ssh (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh x)) ∧
                (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime Q) Ssh).comp
                    (algebraMap (Rsh ⊗[R] S) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) = g.toRingHom
declarations.comment:
Stated over six independent universes, as the source requires: the tag's six
rings `R`, `R_p`, `R^sh`, `S`, `S_q`, `S^sh` are unconstrained relative to one another.

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.isIso_torExtensionMap_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HW.** If `R'` is flat over `R`, `A'` is flat over `A ⊗[R] R'`, and
`B'` is flat over `R' ⊗[R] B`, the canonical scalar-extended change-of-rings map on
ordinary Tor is an isomorphism. The diagram is lifted to the maximum of its six independent
universes so that Mathlib's categorical Tor and extension-of-scalars constructions apply.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_torExtensionMap_of_flat
    (R : Type uR) (R' : Type uS) (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB)
    (A' : Type uC) (B' : Type uD)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B']
    [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R A'] [Algebra R B']
    [Algebra R' A'] [Algebra R' B'] [IsScalarTower R R' A'] [IsScalarTower R R' B']
    (fA : A →ₐ[R] A') (fB : B →ₐ[R] B')
    (hR' : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap R R'))
    (hA' : RingHom.Flat (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift fA
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R R' A') (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _)).toRingHom)
    (hB' : RingHom.Flat (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R R' B') fB (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _)).toRingHom)
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsIso (TorChangeOfRings.extensionMap TorChangeOfRings.canonicalSystem_nonempty
      (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} R) (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} R')
      (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} A) (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} B)
      (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} A') (ULift.{max uR uS uA uB uC uD} B')
      i fA.ulift fB.ulift)

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.torIndependent_localizations_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem torIndependent_localizations_tfae
    (R A B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] :
    List.TFAE [
      TorIndependent R A B,
      (∀ (r : PrimeSpectrum R) (p : PrimeSpectrum A) (q : PrimeSpectrum B)
        (hp : r.asIdeal = p.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R A))
        (hq : r.asIdeal = q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R B)),
        letI : p.asIdeal.LiesOver r.asIdeal := ⟨hp⟩
        letI : q.asIdeal.LiesOver r.asIdeal := ⟨hq⟩
        letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal)
            (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) :=
          Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver r.asIdeal p.asIdeal
        letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal)
            (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) :=
          Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver r.asIdeal q.asIdeal
        TorIndependent (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal)
          (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)),
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < i → ∀ s : PrimeSpectrum (A ⊗[R] B),
        letI := TorChangeOfRings.moduleStructure
          TorChangeOfRings.canonicalSystem_nonempty R A B i
        Subsingleton
          (LocalizedModule s.asIdeal.primeCompl (TorChangeOfRings.torObj R i A B)))]

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.localizedModuleTorEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HX**, the displayed identification. Let `s` be a prime of `A ⊗[R] B` and let
`p = A ∩ s`, `q = B ∩ s` lie over the prime `r` of `R`. Then
`Tor_i^R(A, B)_s ≃ Tor_i^{R_r}(A_p, B_q)_s` as `A ⊗[R] B`-modules, where `Tor_i^{R_r}(A_p, B_q)`
is regarded as an `A ⊗[R] B`-module along the canonical map `A ⊗[R] B → A_p ⊗[R_r] B_q`.
It is the localization at `s` of the canonical change-of-rings map, and comes from the
isomorphism of Stacks 08HW.
declarations.statement:
public def localizedModuleTorEquiv
    (R A B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (s : PrimeSpectrum (A ⊗[R] B))
    (r : PrimeSpectrum R) (p : PrimeSpectrum A) (q : PrimeSpectrum B)
    [p.asIdeal.LiesOver r.asIdeal] [q.asIdeal.LiesOver r.asIdeal]
    [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)]
    [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)]
    [Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra r.asIdeal p.asIdeal]
    [Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra r.asIdeal q.asIdeal]
    (hp : p.asIdeal = s.asIdeal.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : A →ₐ[R] A ⊗[R] B))
    (hq : q.asIdeal = s.asIdeal.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[R] A ⊗[R] B))
    (i : ℕ) :
    letI := TorChangeOfRings.moduleStructure TorChangeOfRings.canonicalSystem_nonempty R A B i
    letI := TorChangeOfRings.moduleStructure TorChangeOfRings.canonicalSystem_nonempty
      (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
      (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) i
    letI : Module (A ⊗[R] B) (TorChangeOfRings.torObj (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) i
        (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) :=
      Module.compHom _ (TorChangeOfRings.tensorProductMap R (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) A B
        (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A _) (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R B _))
    LocalizedModule s.asIdeal.primeCompl (TorChangeOfRings.torObj R i A B) ≃ₗ[A ⊗[R] B]
      LocalizedModule s.asIdeal.primeCompl
        (TorChangeOfRings.torObj (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) i
          (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
declarations.comment: the identification Tor_i^R(A,B)_s = Tor_i^{R_r}(A_p,B_q)_s displayed in part (3) of the lemma, as a linear equivalence of localized A ⊗_R B-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**The derived base change map** `Lg^* (Rf_* K) ⟶ Rf'_* (Lg'^* K)` of a commutative square
of ringed spaces, at an object of the unbounded derived category.  It is adjoint to the derived
pullback along `g'` of the derived counit `Lf^* (Rf_* K) ⟶ K`, after identifying the two
iterated derived pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBaseChangeMap (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g).obj
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K) ⟶
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f').obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g').obj K)
declarations.comment: derived_base_change_map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap_adjoint
declarations.doc:
Under the derived adjunction `Lf'^* ⊣ Rf'_*`, the base change map is the derived pullback
of the counit, transported across the two composition isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeMap_adjoint
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction f').homEquiv
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g).obj
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K))
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g').obj K)).symm
        (derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq K) =
      (derivedPullbackCompIsoLeft g' f' f g sq).hom.app
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K) ≫
        (derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical g' f).inv.app
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K) ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g').map
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction f).counit.app K)
declarations.comment: adjoint characterization of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.canonicalPushforwardTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
The relative Mayer--Vietoris triangle built from the canonical derived functors and the
canonical relative Mayer--Vietoris sequence is distinguished at every object of the unbounded
derived category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalPushforwardTriangle_distinguished
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    canonicalPushforwardTriangle f iU iV iW cover intersection E ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)))
declarations.comment: the triangle with no choices: the canonical derived functors of `canonicalRightDerived` and the canonical sequence of Tag 01EC, which is the form in which two such triangles can be compared

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.unboundedRelativeMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08HZ.** For a morphism of ringed spaces and a cover of its source by two open
subsets, the four derived pushforwards attached to the cover fit into a distinguished triangle,
naturally in the object of the unbounded derived category.  The four derived pushforwards are
hypothesised only through `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightDerivedFunctor`, so the statement
applies to every choice of them; applying a cohomological functor to the triangle gives the
relative Mayer--Vietoris long exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unboundedRelativeMayerVietoris (f : X ⟶ Y) (U V : Opens X) (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (Rf RU RV RUV : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)))
    (af : homotopyToDerived (modulePushforward f) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    (aU : homotopyToDerived (restrictedPushforward f U) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RU)
    (aV : homotopyToDerived (restrictedPushforward f V) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RV)
    (aUV : homotopyToDerived (restrictedPushforward f (U ⊓ V)) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RUV)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor af (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aV (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RUV.IsRightDerivedFunctor aUV (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ (rU : Rf ⟶ RU) (rV : Rf ⟶ RV) (dU : RU ⟶ RUV) (dV : RV ⟶ RUV)
      (δ : RUV ⟶ Rf ⋙ shiftFunctor
        (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) (1 : ℤ)),
      ∀ E, Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (rU.app E) (rV.app E))
        (biprod.desc (dU.app E) (dV.app E)) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.pushforwardTriangleMap
declarations.doc:
The relative Mayer--Vietoris triangle is functorial in the derived object: a morphism
`e : E ⟶ E'` induces a morphism of triangles whose components are the four derived functors
applied to `e`.
declarations.statement:
public def pushforwardTriangleMap
    {E E' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))} (e : E ⟶ E') :
    pushforwardTriangle f iU iV iW S Rf RU RV RUV af aU aV aUV E ⟶
      pushforwardTriangle f iU iV iW S Rf RU RV RUV af aU aV aUV E'
declarations.comment: functoriality of the triangle in `E`: the lemma's second assertion, which the existential form above cannot express because it hides the morphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isTriangulated_derivedSheafHom_flip
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I0, first variable.**  On a ringed space `(X, O_X)`, for every `L` in `D(O_X)` the
derived internal hom `RSheafHom(-, L) : D(O_X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ D(O_X)` is a triangulated functor: with the
commutation datum `commShift_derivedSheafHom_flip` it carries every distinguished triangle to a
distinguished triangle, the third map of the image being the image of the third map composed
with the commutation isomorphism (Stacks 014V).  A distinguished triangle of `D(O_X)ᵒᵖ` is the
opposite of a distinguished triangle `K₁ ⟶ K₂ ⟶ K₃ ⟶ K₁[1]` of `D(O_X)`, and its image is the
triangle `RSheafHom(K₃, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K₂, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K₁, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K₃, L)[1]`.
declarations.statement:
instance isTriangulated_derivedSheafHom_flip (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((derivedSheafHom Rc).flip.obj L).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: first variable: `RSheafHom(-, L)` is a triangulated functor `D(O_X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ D(O_X)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isTriangulated_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I0, second variable.**  On a ringed space `(X, O_X)`, for every `K` in `D(O_X)`
the derived internal hom `RSheafHom(K, -) : D(O_X) ⥤ D(O_X)` is a triangulated functor: with the
commutation datum `commShift_derivedSheafHom` it carries every distinguished triangle
`M₁ ⟶ M₂ ⟶ M₃ ⟶ M₁[1]` to the distinguished triangle
`RSheafHom(K, M₁) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M₂) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M₃) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M₁)[1]` whose third map
is the image of the third map composed with the commutation isomorphism (Stacks 014V).

The proof is not the source's: `RSheafHom(K, -)` is right adjoint to the triangulated functor
`- ⊗^L_{O_X} K` (Stacks 08DI, 06YU), compatibly with the shifts, and the right adjoint of a
triangulated functor is triangulated.
declarations.statement:
instance isTriangulated_derivedSheafHom (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: second variable: `RSheafHom(K, -)` is a triangulated functor `D(O_X) ⥤ D(O_X)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I1: the canonical map `M ⊗^L_{O_X} L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)`.** It is the derived
composition morphism of Stacks 0A8V, taken at intermediate object the structure sheaf, after the
left tensor factor `M` has been identified with `RSheafHom(O_X, M)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualToSheafHom
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))) :
    ((derivedTensor Rc).obj M).obj (derivedDual Rc L) ⟶
      ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).obj M
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 08I1 is functorial in `M`.** This is the covariant naturality
of the derived composition morphism of Stacks 0A8V in its target, together with the naturality
of the identification of `M` with `RSheafHom(O_X, M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_naturality
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))} (m : M ⟶ M') :
    ((derivedTensor Rc).map m).app (derivedDual Rc L) ≫
        derivedTensorDualToSheafHom Rc L M' =
      derivedTensorDualToSheafHom Rc L M ≫ ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).map m
declarations.comment: functoriality in M of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_naturality_tensorMap
declarations.doc:
Functoriality in `M` of the canonical map of Stacks 08I1, in the `derivedTensorMap` and
`derivedSheafHomMap` spelling of the induced maps on the derived tensor product and the derived
internal Hom.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_naturality_tensorMap
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))} (m : M ⟶ M') :
    derivedTensorMap Rc m (𝟙 (derivedDual Rc L)) ≫ derivedTensorDualToSheafHom Rc L M' =
      derivedTensorDualToSheafHom Rc L M ≫ derivedSheafHomMap Rc (𝟙 L) m
declarations.comment: functoriality in M of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I1: the induced map on degree-zero global cohomology.** The canonical map
`M ⊗^L_{O_X} L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)` induces a map of abelian groups

`H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} L^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O_X)}(L, M)`,

namely its degree-zero global hypercohomology followed by the identification
`H⁰(X, RSheafHom(L, M)) ≅ Hom_{D(O_X)}(L, M)` of Stacks 08DK.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((derivedTensor Rc).obj M).obj (derivedDual Rc L))) : Type u) →+ (L ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: the induced map on degree-zero global cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I1: the induced map `H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{O_X} L^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O_X)}(L, M)` is functorial
in `M`.** For `m : M ⟶ M'` the degree-zero global hypercohomology of `m ⊗ 1` carries the induced
map at `M` to the induced map at `M'` followed by postcomposition with `m`.

This is the ringed-site statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality`, read along
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite` for the canonical derived tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality
    (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (m : M ⟶ M')
    (z : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj
        (((derivedTensor Rc).obj M).obj (derivedDual Rc L))) : Type u)) :
    derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap Rc L M'
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).map
            (((derivedTensor Rc).map m).app (derivedDual Rc L))) z) =
      derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap Rc L M z ≫ m
declarations.comment: functoriality in M of the induced map on degree-zero global cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality_tensorMap
declarations.doc:
Functoriality in `M` of the induced map of Stacks 08I1, in the `derivedTensorMap` spelling of
the map induced on the derived tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality_tensorMap
    (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (m : M ⟶ M')
    (z : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj
        (((derivedTensor Rc).obj M).obj (derivedDual Rc L))) : Type u)) :
    derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap Rc L M'
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).map
            (derivedTensorMap Rc m (𝟙 (derivedDual Rc L)))) z) =
      derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap Rc L M z ≫ m
declarations.comment: functoriality in M of the induced map on degree-zero global cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08I3: the canonical map `Lh^*R𝓗om(K, L) ⟶ R𝓗om(Lh^*K, Lh^*L)`** for a morphism of
ringed spaces `h : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and objects `K, L` of `D(𝒪_Y)`.

By the tensor–internal-hom bijection of Tag 08DI it is the same datum as a map
`Lh^*R𝓗om(K,L) ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} Lh^*K ⟶ Lh^*L`, and that is the derived pullback of the evaluation
`R𝓗om(K,L) ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} K ⟶ L` preceded by the monoidality comparison of Tag 079U.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackSheafHomMap :
    (derivedPullbackFunctor h).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj L) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj
          (op ((derivedPullbackFunctor h).obj K))).obj
        ((derivedPullbackFunctor h).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08I4: the base change map for a derived internal hom.**  For a commutative square of
ringed spaces with `h : X' ⟶ X` over `g : S' ⟶ S` and objects `K, L` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the canonical
map

`Lg^* Rf_* R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, L) ⟶ R(f')_* R𝓗om_{𝒪_{X'}}(Lh^*K, Lh^*L)`

in `D(𝒪_{S'})`.  It is the derived base change map of Tag 08HY at `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, L)` followed
by `R(f')_*` of the canonical map of Tag 08I3, which is the adjoint of the three-step
composition the source describes.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap :
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj L)) ⟶
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f').obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X'.sheaf).obj
            (op ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback h).obj
              K))).obj
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback h).obj L))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homMap_quasiIso_of_boundedAbove_isFiniteFreeSummand
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I5**, the quasi-isomorphism invariance. Let `E` be a complex of `O`-modules which
is bounded above and all of whose terms are direct summands of finite free `O`-modules. Then the
internal Hom complex out of `E` carries a quasi-isomorphism between two complexes vanishing in
all degrees below a common bound `a` to a quasi-isomorphism.

This is the whole content of the tag; the representation statement
`strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove` is obtained from it by the formal reduction
`strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_iff`.

Unlike `homMap_quasiIso_of_isFiniteFreeSummand` (Stacks 08JH) the source is not assumed to have
finitely many nonzero terms, and in exchange the targets are assumed bounded below. The proof is
degreewise: `quasiIsoAt_homMap_of_boundedAbove` at `k = a - n - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homMap_quasiIso_of_boundedAbove_isFiniteFreeSummand (a : ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ i, i < a → IsZero (F.X i))
    (hG : ∀ i, i < a → IsZero (G.X i))
    (hE : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i, b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hterm : ∀ i, IsFiniteFreeSummand X (E.X i))
    (f : F ⟶ G) [QuasiIso f] :
    QuasiIso (homMap X (𝟙 E) f)
declarations.comment: invariance of the internal Hom complex under quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I5**, the representation statement. Let `E` be a complex of `O`-modules which is
bounded above and all of whose terms are direct summands of finite free `O`-modules, and let `F`
vanish in all degrees below `a`. Then the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(E, F)` is represented
by the ordinary internal Hom complex `SheafHom(E, F)` of Stacks 0A8Z, the comparison being the
canonical one of `strictlyPerfectHomComparison`.

By `strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_iff` the claim is the quasi-isomorphy of the map of
internal Hom complexes induced by the K-injective augmentation `F ⟶ I` of the target. The
chosen resolution `I` carries no lower bound, so the invariance is applied instead to a
degreewise injective resolution `u : F ⟶ I₀` which is again zero below `a`, and transported to
the augmentation of `F` along the naturality square of the augmentation; the two maps between
K-injective complexes occurring there are handled by `homMap_quasiIso` (Stacks 0A95). See the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove (a : ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ i, i < a → IsZero (F.X i))
    (hE : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i, b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hterm : ∀ i, IsFiniteFreeSummand X (E.X i)) :
    IsIso (strictlyPerfectHomComparison X D E F)
declarations.comment: representation of derived internal Hom by the ordinary Hom complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MixedDerivedTensor.derivedMixedTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I6, read after restriction of scalars to `f⁻¹O'`.**  The bifunctorial
isomorphism

`(F ⊗^L_O Lf^*G)|_{f⁻¹O'} ≅ F|_{f⁻¹O'} ⊗^L_{f⁻¹O'} f⁻¹G`

in `D(f⁻¹O')`, for a site-presented morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')`,
`F` in `D(O)` and `G` in `D(O')`.  It is stated between the two uncurried bifunctors on
`D(O) × D(O')`, so that naturality in both variables is part of its type.  The tag itself, in
`D(O)` and for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, is
`Stacks.Cohomology.MixedDerivedTensor.OfToposHom.derivedMixedTensorIso`.

Its value at a complex of `O`-modules and a K-flat complex of `O'`-modules with flat terms is
the chain of the source (`derivedMixedTensorModelIso`): there both sides are computed by total
tensor complexes and the identity is the underived one of the source, applied in each bidegree.
The passage to arbitrary objects is the descent of that value along the localization of pairs
of models.
declarations.statement:
def derivedMixedTensorIso :
    mixedDerivedTensorPullback f ≅ mixedDerivedTensorInverseImage f
declarations.comment:
variant: the isomorphism read in D(f⁻¹O') after restriction of scalars, for a
site-presented morphism; the tag in D(O) for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi is
Stacks.Cohomology.MixedDerivedTensor.OfToposHom.derivedMixedTensorIso

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MixedDerivedTensor.OfToposHom.derivedMixedTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08I6.**  For a morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')` — a
morphism of the underlying topoi together with the structure map, with no hypothesis on the
underlying sites — the canonical bifunctorial isomorphism

`F ⊗^L_O Lf^*G ≅ F ⊗^L_{f⁻¹O'} f⁻¹G`

in `D(O)`, for `F` in `D(O)` and `G` in `D(O')`.  The right-hand side is the derived tensor
product over `f⁻¹O'` (`coeffMixedDerivedTensor` along the structure map `f⁻¹O' ⟶ O`) of `F` and
the inverse image `f⁻¹G` (`derivedInverseImage`), an object of `D(O)` through `F`.  It is stated
between the two uncurried bifunctors on `D(O) × D(O')`, so that bifunctoriality is part of its
type.

At a complex `F` of `O`-modules and a K-flat complex `G` of `O'`-modules with flat terms both
sides are total complexes and the isomorphism is the underived identity
`F ⊗_{f⁻¹O'} f⁻¹G ≅ F ⊗_O f^*G` in each bidegree (`modelIso`); the passage to arbitrary objects
is the descent along the localization of pairs of models.
declarations.statement:
def derivedMixedTensorIso :
    derivedTensorPullback f ≅ derivedMixedTensorInverseImage f
declarations.comment:
the canonical bifunctorial isomorphism in D(O), for an arbitrary morphism of
ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_basicOpen_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A meromorphic function on a quasi-compact open which vanishes on the basic open of a
regular function there is annihilated by a power of that regular function.
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_basicOpen_eq_zero
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {W : X.Opens} (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X)) (h : Γ(X, W))
    (f : X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op W))
    (hf : X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.map
      (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le h)).op f = 0) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      (X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op W)).hom h ^ n * f = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pow_mul_eq_zero_of_restrict_basicOpen_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A meromorphic function vanishing on the basic open of a global regular function is
annihilated by a power of that regular function.
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_mul_eq_zero_of_restrict_basicOpen_eq_zero
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] (h : Γ(X, ⊤))
    (f : X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
    (hf : X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.map
      (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le h)).op f = 0) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      (X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op ⊤)).hom h ^ n * f = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.reflectsIsomorphisms_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_specMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I8] for a morphism of affine schemes.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` and let
`f = Spec φ : Spec S ⟶ Spec R`. Then `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S}) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})` reflects
isomorphisms: a map of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology is invertible as soon as its
derived pushforward is.

Derived sheafification is an equivalence `D(S) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S})` [Stacks, Tag 06Z0] carrying
`Rf_*` to derived restriction of scalars along `φ` [Stacks, Tag 0DJK], and that functor reflects
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem reflectsIsomorphisms_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_specMap :
    (derivedQuasicoherentPushforward (Spec.map φ)).ReflectsIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: a morphism Spec φ of affine schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.reflectsIsomorphisms_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I8].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of schemes, with `Y` an
arbitrary scheme. Then `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` reflects isomorphisms.

`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentPushforward` is by construction the lift of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_Y)` through the inclusion of `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, so a map of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose derived direct image is invertible in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has invertible derived
direct image in `D(𝒪_Y)`;
`AlgebraicGeometry.AnyModel.isIso_of_isIso_derivedPushforward_map_of_isAffineHom` makes it
invertible in `D(𝒪_X)`, and the inclusion of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is fully faithful, hence reflects
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem reflectsIsomorphisms_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward [IsAffineHom f] :
    (derivedQuasicoherentPushforward f).ReflectsIsomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforwardTExactness.isIso_of_isIso_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I8].**  Let `f : W ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of schemes and let
`α : E ⟶ F` be a morphism of `D(𝒪_W)` between complexes whose cohomology sheaves are
quasi-coherent.  If the derived direct image `Rf_*α` is invertible in `D(𝒪_Y)`, then `α` is
invertible.  This is the assertion that `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_W) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` reflects
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isIso_derivedPushforward (f : W ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    {E F : DerivedCategory W.Modules}
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor W.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hF : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor W.Modules i).obj F).IsQuasicoherent)
    (α : E ⟶ F)
    (h : IsIso ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).map α)) : IsIso α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineProjectionFormula.isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 08I9.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be an affine morphism of schemes and let `E` be an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`, that is, an object of `D(𝒪_S)` all of whose cohomology sheaves are
quasi-coherent.  Then the canonical morphism

`Rf_*𝒪_X ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} E ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*E`

is an isomorphism.  The derived pullback is the genuine `Lf^*` of [Stacks, Tag 06YJ], the tensor
product is the genuine `⊗^𝐋`, and there is no boundedness, flatness or finiteness hypothesis on
`E` and no hypothesis on `S`.

The proof is the source's.  The question is local on `S`, which is
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_of_openCover` over
the cover of `S` by its affine opens; each restriction `f|_U` is an affine morphism over an affine
scheme, and the restricted complex still has quasi-coherent cohomology by
`isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback_of_isOpenImmersion`, so
`isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_of_isAffine` applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_unconditional {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffineHom f] (E : DerivedCategory S.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor S.Modules n).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso (pullbackPushforwardTensorMap' f.toLRSHom.toShHom E)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism Rf_*O_X ⊗^L E ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*E is invertible for every affine morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ S and every object E of D_QCoh(O_S), with the genuine derived pullback Lf^* and the genuine derived tensor product ⊗^L, no boundedness, flatness or finiteness hypothesis on E and no hypothesis on S

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforwardTExactness.derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
For an affine morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and a complex `E` on `S` with quasi-coherent
cohomology,

`f_*𝒪_X ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} E ≅ Rf_* Lf^* E`,

with the derived tensor product and with no boundedness hypothesis on `E`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso (f : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom f]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)) j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          ((modulePushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))))).obj E ≅
      (derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedAffinePushforward.derivedPushforwardPullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I9] for `E` a quasi-coherent module in degree zero, with the underived
inverse image and tensor product**: for an affine morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `H`,

`Rf_*((f^*H)[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0]`

in `D(𝒪_S)`. Unconditional.

The source states `Rf_*Lf^*E ≅ E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} f_*𝒪_X`; here both derived functors on the
right-hand side of that identity are replaced by their underived counterparts `f^*` and `⊗`.
See the module documentation for what that costs. The proof is
`pushforwardStructureSheafTensorIso` followed by [Stacks, Tag 01XC] in the form
`derivedPushforwardSingleIso`: `f^*H` is quasi-coherent and `f` is affine, so the ordinary direct
image of `f^*H` in degree zero is already its derived direct image.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardPullbackTensorIso [IsAffineHom f] (H : S.Modules)
    (hH : H.IsQuasicoherent) :
    (Stacks.Duality.derivedPushforward f).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj H)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj
        (((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            ⟨((S.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((S.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩))).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf : X.Modules),
            H))
declarations.comment: a SPECIAL CASE of the general statement, which is proved — the tag is closed by AlgebraicGeometry.AffineProjectionFormula.isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_unconditional. The degree-zero clause: Rf_*((f^*H)[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0] for H a quasi-coherent 𝒪_S-module, with the underived f^* and ⊗ in place of the general statement's Lf^* and ⊗ᴸ and E restricted to a module in degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedAffinePushforward.derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I9] for `E` a flat quasi-coherent module in degree zero, with the genuine
derived pullback**: for an affine morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and a flat quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `H`,

`Rf_*Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0]`,

with nothing assumed beyond those restrictions on `f` and `H`. Flatness of `H` makes `H[0]`
K-flat, so the degree-zero comparison `Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f^*H)[0]` is
`derivedPullbackSingleIsoOfFlat`; the tensor product on the right-hand side is still the
underived one.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso [IsAffineHom f] (H : S.Modules)
    (hH : H.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hHflat : SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.toRingedSpace.sheaf) H) :
    (Stacks.Duality.derivedPushforward f).obj
        ((Stacks.Duality.derivedPullback f).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj H)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj
        (((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            ⟨((S.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((S.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩))).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf : X.Modules),
            H))
declarations.comment: a SPECIAL CASE of the general statement, which is proved — the tag is closed by AlgebraicGeometry.AffineProjectionFormula.isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_unconditional. E = H[0] for f affine and H a flat quasi-coherent 𝒪_S-module, with the genuine Lf^* and nothing carried: Rf_*Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0]; the right-hand tensor product is the underived ⊗, not ⊗ᴸ, and E is restricted to a module in degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedAffinePushforward.derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIsoOfExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I9] for a flat affine morphism and `E` a quasi-coherent module in degree
zero**: for `f : X ⟶ S` affine with `f^*` exact and `H` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module,

`Rf_*Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0]`

in `D(𝒪_S)`, with no hypothesis carried. Flatness of `f` replaces the flatness of `H` asked by
`derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso`: it supplies the degree-zero comparison
`Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f^*H)[0]` through `derivedPullbackSingleIsoOfExact` instead.

Both sides are the source's, except that the tensor product on the right is the ordinary one
rather than `⊗^𝐋`; for `f` flat the two agree, but that identification is not proved here.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIsoOfExact [IsAffineHom f]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback f)] (H : S.Modules)
    (hH : H.IsQuasicoherent) :
    (Stacks.Duality.derivedPushforward f).obj
        ((Stacks.Duality.derivedPullback f).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj H)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj
        (((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            ⟨((S.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((S.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩))).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf : X.Modules),
            H))
declarations.comment: a SPECIAL CASE of the general statement, which is proved — the tag is closed by AlgebraicGeometry.AffineProjectionFormula.isIso_pullbackPushforwardTensorMap_unconditional. E = H[0] for f affine with f^* exact (f flat) and H quasi-coherent, with the genuine Rf_* and Lf^* and nothing carried: Rf_*Lf^*(H[0]) ≅ (f_*𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_S} H)[0]; the right-hand tensor product is the underived ⊗, not ⊗ᴸ, and E is restricted to a module in degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePullbackPushforwardTensor.derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08I9].**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be an affine morphism of schemes.  For every `K`
in `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`,

`f_*𝒪_X ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} K ≅ Rf_*Lf^*K`,

with the *ordinary* direct image of the structure sheaf placed in degree zero on the left and
