the *derived* tensor product.  The left-hand factor is `(f_*𝒪_X)[0]` rather than `Rf_*(𝒪_X[0])`
by [Stacks, Tag 01XC] for an affine morphism, which is the first step of the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardDerivedPullbackTensorIso (f : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom f]
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
    (hK : Stacks.DerivedQCoh.IsDQCoh (R := structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace) K) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          ((modulePushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSpace.sheaf))))).obj K ≅
      (derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: for an affine morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ S and every K in D_QCoh(𝒪_S), the canonical map f_*𝒪_X ⊗ᴸ K ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*K is invertible. The tensor factors are written in the opposite order from the source, the derived tensor product of a ringed space being symmetric

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorIndependent
declarations.doc:
Two schemes over a common base are Tor independent if their local rings at
every pair of points with the same image are Tor independent over the local
ring of the base.
declarations.statement: def TorIndependent {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeChart.isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0661 on a Cartesian affine-open chart.** If `X` and `S'` are Tor independent over
`S`, then for every chart the canonical comparison

`K ⊗ᴸ_R R' ⟶ K ⊗ᴸ_A A'`

of Stacks 065Z is an isomorphism on the whole unbounded derived category of `A`-modules, for
every choice of models of the two total derived extension-of-scalars functors.

The pushout hypothesis of Stacks 0661 is the chart's own square `A' = A ⊗_R R'`, and the Tor
independence hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeChart.torIndependent`.

This is the Tor-independence input of Stacks 08IB, not its conclusion: it does not say that the
derived base-change map `Lg^*Rf_*K ⟶ Rf'_*L(g')^*K` of Stacks 08HY is an isomorphism. Passing
from the chartwise comparison to that map is Stacks 0DJ9.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison (hTor : TorIndependent f g)
    (ch : BaseChangeChart f g f' g')
    (L_g : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ch.R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ch.R'))
    (L_h : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ch.A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ch.A'))
    (alpha_g : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L_g ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} ch.b.hom).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    (alpha_h : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L_h ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} ch.c.hom).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    [L_g.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_g
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} ch.R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [L_h.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_h
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} ch.A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (RingTheory.TorIndependence.derivedBaseChangeComparison.{u, u, u, u, u}
      ch.a.hom ch.b.hom ch.c.hom ch.d.hom ch.isPushout_hom L_g L_h alpha_g alpha_h).2.1
declarations.comment: the Tor-independence input of the proof: on every Cartesian affine-open chart of the square the coordinate rings are Tor independent, so the ring-level derived base-change comparison of Stacks 065Z is invertible there. The global statement is isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08IB].**  Let

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
S' --g---> S
```

be a Cartesian square of schemes with `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `X` and `S'` Tor
independent over `S`, and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` with quasi-coherent cohomology
sheaves.  Then the derived base-change map

`Lg^*(Rf_*K) ⟶ Rf'_*(L(g')^*K)`

of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] is an isomorphism.

`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent_of_overAffineBase` — the source's
reduction to an affine base — at `derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOverAffineBase`.
declarations.statement: theorem derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent : DerivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
Let `g : S' ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and `X' = X ×_S S'` with projections `g' : X' ⟶ X` and `f' : X' ⟶ S'`. If `X` and `S'` are Tor
independent over `S`, then for every `E ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the canonical arrow
`Lg^*Rf_*E ⟶ Rf'_*L(g')^*E` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (hTor : TorIndependent f g)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toSheafedSpace)))
    (hE : ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso (derivedBaseChangeMap g'.toLRSHom.toShHom f'.toLRSHom.toShHom f.toLRSHom.toShHom
      g.toLRSHom.toShHom (comp_toShHom_of_comm sq.w) E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.isIso_quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChangeSquare_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08IB] for base change along an open immersion of the base**, on the
quasi-coherent derived categories at the locally small model: the derived base change map
`β : Rf_* ⋙ Lj^* ⟶ L(j')^* ⋙ Rf'_*` of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] is invertible.

This is the companion of
`isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_isOpenImmersion` under
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_iff`, and it is the localization
step of [Stacks, Tag 0DJ9] at this model — `β` here is the mate of
`Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPushforwardSquareIso`, not the comparison of
`Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictBaseChangeSquare`, so nothing identifies
derived pullback with the exact restriction along the way.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChangeSquare_of_isOpenImmersion
    [(Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f hpushf).IsLeftAdjoint]
    [(Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f' hpushf').IsLeftAdjoint]
    (sq : IsPullback j' f' f j) :
    IsIso (Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChangeSquare j' f' f j hpushj' hpushf hpushf'
      hpushj (Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' j)
      (Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' j') sq.w)
declarations.comment: for base change along an OPEN IMMERSION of the base, hence flat, hence Tor independent of f: invertibility of Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChangeSquare, the derived base change map of Stacks 08HY on the quasi-coherent derived categories at the locally small model. The general Tor-independent case is not proved in this repository; see Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_isOpenImmersion

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ExtPerfectProjection.extIso_qcoh_boundary
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08ID].**  Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type,
`E` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over
`S`, with support proper over `S`, and let `K = Rf_* RSheafHom(E, 𝒢)` as in [Stacks, Tag 0DJR].
Then there are isomorphisms

`Φᵢ : H^i(S, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_S} ℱ) ⟶ Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*ℱ) = Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(E, (𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ)[i])`,

functorial in the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `ℱ` (a natural isomorphism of functors on
quasi-coherent modules for every `i`), compatible with boundary maps: for a short exact sequence
`0 → ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃ → 0` of `𝒪_S`-modules with `ℱ₁`, `ℱ₃` quasi-coherent and every class `y` in
`H^i(S, K ⊗^L ℱ₃)`,

`Φᵢ₊₁(∂ y) = Φᵢ(y) ∘ δ`,

where `∂ : H^i(S, K ⊗^L ℱ₃) ⟶ H^{i+1}(S, K ⊗^L ℱ₁)` is the connecting morphism of the
distinguished triangle `K ⊗^L ℱ₁ → K ⊗^L ℱ₂ → K ⊗^L ℱ₃ → (K ⊗^L ℱ₁)[1]` (the image under
`K ⊗^L -` of the triangle of the sequence) and `δ : 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ ⟶ (𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₁)[1]` is the
connecting morphism of the distinguished triangle of the short exact sequence of complexes
`0 → 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₁ → 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₂ → 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ → 0`, composed as an element of `Ext¹`.

`H^i(S, -)` is the `i`-th cohomology of the unbounded derived global sections; it is a group of
`Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`-modules, read as an abelian group and lifted to the universe of the morphism groups of
`D(𝒪_X)`.  `f^*` is the pullback of modules and `𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ` the complex with terms
`𝒢^p ⊗ f^*ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extIso_qcoh_boundary [IsNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hG : PerfectPushforward.FlatProperSupportComplex f G) :
    ∃ Φ : ∀ i : ℤ, (qcModules S).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModS S) 0 ⋙
          tensorSheafHomK f E G ⋙ sectionsS (S := S) ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i ⋙
          forgetLift (Y := S.toRingedSpace) ≅
        (qcModules S).ι ⋙ Ψ f G ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ shiftFunctor _ i ⋙
          preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op E),
      ∀ (T : ShortComplex (ModS S)) (hT : T.ShortExact) (h₁ : qcModules S T.X₁)
        (h₃ : qcModules S T.X₃) (i : ℤ)
        (y : ((qcModules S).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModS S) 0 ⋙
          tensorSheafHomK f E G ⋙ sectionsS (S := S) ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i ⋙
          forgetLift (Y := S.toRingedSpace)).obj ⟨T.X₃, h₃⟩),
        (Φ (i + 1)).hom.app ⟨T.X₁, h₁⟩
            ((forgetLift (Y := S.toRingedSpace)).map ((H0 (S := S)).homologySequenceδ
              ((sectionsS (S := S)).mapTriangle.obj
                ((tensorSheafHomK f E G).mapTriangle.obj hT.singleTriangle)) i (i + 1) rfl) y) =
          ((Φ i).hom.app ⟨T.X₃, h₃⟩ y : E ⟶ _) ≫
            (DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ
              (Stacks.Cohomology.ExtProjectionFormulaBoundary.shortExact_Ψ f G hG T hT))⟦i⟧' ≫
            (shiftFunctorAdd' _ 1 i (i + 1) (by omega)).inv.app _
declarations.comment: the functorial isomorphisms for every i, Ext^i read as Hom_{D(O_X)}(E, -[i]), and their compatibility with the boundary maps of every short exact sequence of quasi-coherent modules (with ℱ₂ an arbitrary O_S-module): the class of a boundary is the Yoneda composite with the connecting morphism of the triangle of 0 → G ⊗ f^*F₁ → G ⊗ f^*F₂ → G ⊗ f^*F₃ → 0; H^i(S, -) is H^i of unbounded RΓ(S, -) with its Γ(S, O_S)-module structure forgotten

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 08IE**:

`Lg^*Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_{X'}}(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢^•)`.

It is the derived base-change map of Stacks 08HY at `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢^•)`, followed by `Rf'_*`
of the base-change comparison for a derived internal hom of Stacks 0DJA, taken at the
derived-to-ordinary comparison `L(g')^*𝒢^• ⟶ (g')^*𝒢^•`.

On the right-hand side the complex `𝒢^•` is pulled back by the **ordinary** functor `(g')^*`,
which is what the source's boldface insists on; the derived-to-ordinary comparison that makes
this possible is the `φ` of the second factor, and it is never assumed invertible.
declarations.statement:
public def sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : g'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ f.toLRSHom.toShHom =
      f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) :
    (derivedPullback g.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          (((derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj G))) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (((derivedSheafHom X'.sheaf).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E))).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((pullbackComplex g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)))
declarations.comment: the canonical map whose invertibility is the tag's conclusion: the derived base-change map of Stacks 08HY at R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•), followed by Rf'_* of the base-change comparison of Stacks 0DJA taken at the derived-to-ordinary comparison L(g')^*𝒢^• ⟶ (g')^*𝒢^•. The target uses the ORDINARY pullback (g')^*𝒢^•, which the source sets in bold, and the derived-to-ordinary comparison is not assumed invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IE, case (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of schemes, let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `𝒢^•` be a bounded above complex of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose terms are flat over `S`. For every cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
S' --g---> S
```

the canonical map

`Lg^*Rf_*R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*R𝓗om(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢^•)`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap`, with the **ordinary** pullback `(g')^*𝒢^•` on
the right as the source insists, is an isomorphism: the formation of `Rf_*R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•)`
commutes with arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPerfect
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hqc : QuasiCompact f) (hqs : QuasiSeparated f)
    (sq : g'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ f.toLRSHom.toShHom =
      f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hGminus : CochainComplex.minus X.Modules G)
    (hGqcoh : ∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (G.X n)) :
    IsIso (sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq E G)
declarations.comment: case (1): E perfect, 𝒢^• bounded above with terms quasi-coherent and flat over S, f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, an arbitrary cartesian square; the canonical map of the source's proof, with the ORDINARY pullback (g')^*𝒢^• on the right, is an isomorphism. Case (2) is false as stated (errata.md, entry 08IE(2)); its corrected form, for g of finite Tor dimension, is `isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IE, case (2), corrected.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
morphism of schemes, let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `𝒢^•` be a bounded
complex of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose terms are flat over `S`. For every cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
S' --g---> S
```

in which `g` has finite Tor dimension at the stalks — every local ring `𝒪_{S', s'}` has finite Tor
dimension over `𝒪_{S, g(s')}`, the correction of case (2) recorded in `errata.md` (entry
**08IE(2)**) — the canonical map

`Lg^*Rf_*R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*R𝓗om(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢^•)`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap`, with the **ordinary** pullback `(g')^*𝒢^•` on
the right, is an isomorphism. Without the condition on `g` the statement is false:
`not_forall_isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent` in
`Stacks.Examples.SheafHomCounterexample`.

The condition on `g` is the stalkwise form of "`𝒪_{S'}` has finite Tor dimension over
`g⁻¹𝒪_S`": it is implied by that condition, and also by its local version (Tor amplitude is a
stalkwise condition, Stacks 09U9).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hqc : QuasiCompact f) (hqs : QuasiSeparated f)
    (hg : ∀ s' : S', HasFiniteTorDimensionRingHom (g.stalkMap s').hom)
    (sq : g'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ f.toLRSHom.toShHom =
      f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (hGge : G.IsStrictlyGE a)
    (hGle : G.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hGqcoh : ∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (G.X n)) :
    IsIso (sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq E G)
declarations.comment: case (2), with the correction of errata.md (entry 08IE(2)): f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, E pseudo-coherent, 𝒢^• bounded with terms quasi-coherent and flat over S, and g of finite Tor dimension, read at the stalks (each 𝒪_{S', s'} of finite Tor dimension over 𝒪_{S, g(s')}, which finite Tor dimension of g implies); the canonical map of the source's proof, with the ORDINARY pullback (g')^*𝒢^• on the right, is an isomorphism. Without the condition on g case (2) is false (the counterexample over ℤ/4 of the erratum)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension_appLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IE, case (2), corrected, with the condition on `g` on affine opens.** This is
`isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension` with the correction
of `errata.md` (entry **08IE(2)**) read on affine opens as the erratum spells it out: for all affine
opens `V ⊆ S` and `V' ⊆ g⁻¹(V)` the ring `𝒪_{S'}(V')` has finite Tor dimension over `𝒪_S(V)`. The
hypotheses on `f`, `E` and `𝒢^•` are those of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasFiniteTorDimension_appLE
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hqc : QuasiCompact f) (hqs : QuasiSeparated f)
    (hg : ∀ (V : S.Opens) (V' : S'.Opens), IsAffineOpen V → IsAffineOpen V' →
      ∀ hle : V' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V, HasFiniteTorDimensionRingHom (g.appLE V V' hle).hom)
    (sq : g'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ f.toLRSHom.toShHom =
      f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (hGge : G.IsStrictlyGE a)
    (hGle : G.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hGqcoh : ∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (G.X n)) :
    IsIso (sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq E G)
declarations.comment: case (2), with the correction of errata.md (entry 08IE(2)) in the affine-open form the erratum spells out: for affine opens V ⊆ S and V' ⊆ g⁻¹(V), 𝒪_{S'}(V') has finite Tor dimension over 𝒪_S(V); f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, E pseudo-coherent, 𝒢^• bounded with terms quasi-coherent and flat over S; the canonical map, with the ORDINARY pullback (g')^*𝒢^•, is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.SheafHomCounterexample.not_forall_isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
It is not true that for every quasi-compact
and quasi-separated `f : X ⟶ S`, every pseudo-coherent `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, every bounded complex
`𝒢^•` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules flat over `S` and every cartesian square, the canonical map
`Lg^*Rf_*R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*R𝓗om(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢^•)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isIso_sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent :
    ¬ ∀ {X X' S S' : Scheme.{0}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
      (_ : IsPullback g' f' f g) (_ : QuasiCompact f) (_ : QuasiSeparated f)
      (sq : g'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ f.toLRSHom.toShHom =
        f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ≫ g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
      (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (_ : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
      (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (_ : G.IsStrictlyGE a) (_ : G.IsStrictlyLE b)
      (_ : ∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
      (_ : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (G.X n)),
      IsIso (sheafHomFlatBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq E G)
declarations.comment: the erratum's counterexample: case (2) for an ARBITRARY base change is false; it fails for S = X = Spec ℤ/4, f = id, E = (ℤ/2)~, 𝒢^• = 𝒪_X and g : Spec ℤ/2 ⟶ Spec ℤ/4

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeExt.exists_perfect_relativeExt_comparison
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism locally of finite type,
`E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with
support proper over `S`. For every `m` there are a perfect object `K` of `D(𝒪_S)` and maps

`α^i_ℱ : Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*ℱ) ⟶ H^i(S, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_S} ℱ)`

for quasi-coherent `ℱ` (with `H^i(S, -) = Ext^i_{𝒪_S}(𝒪_S, -)`), which are additive, functorial in
`ℱ`, compatible with the boundary maps of short exact sequences `0 ⟶ ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂ ⟶ ℱ₃ ⟶ 0` of
quasi-coherent modules (on the left, the connecting morphism of
`0 ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₁ ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₂ ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ ⟶ 0`, exact because `𝒢` is flat over `S`; on the right,
that of the distinguished triangle `K ⊗^L ℱ₁ ⟶ K ⊗^L ℱ₂ ⟶ K ⊗^L ℱ₃ ⟶`), and bijective for
`i ≤ m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_perfect_relativeExt_comparison (E : DStd X) (hE : IsBoundedAboveCoherent E)
    (G : CochainComplex (TModules X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hG : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.FlatProperSupportComplex f G) (m : ℤ) :
    ∃ K : DStd S, IsPerfectObject K ∧
      ∃ α : ∀ (i : ℤ) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)),
          F.IsQuasicoherent → (relativeExtGroup f G E F i →+ baseTensorGroup K F i),
        (∀ (i : ℤ) (F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace))
            (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherent) (v : F ⟶ F')
            (y : relativeExtGroup f G E F i),
          α i F' hF' (relativeExtMap f G E i v y) = baseTensorMap i K v (α i F hF y)) ∧
        (∀ (A : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
            (hA : A.ShortExact) (h₁ : A.X₁.IsQuasicoherent) (h₃ : A.X₃.IsQuasicoherent)
            (n m' : ℤ) (h : 1 + n = m') (y : relativeExtGroup f G E A.X₃ n),
          α m' A.X₁ h₁ (relativeExtBoundaryMap E
              (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG) hA n m' h y) =
            baseTensorBoundaryMap K hA n m' h (α n A.X₃ h₃ y)) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℤ), i ≤ m → ∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace))
            (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent), Function.Bijective (α i F hF))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeExt.exists_pseudoCoherent_relativeExt_representative
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08IF] (B).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism locally of
finite type, `E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over
`S`, with support proper over `S`. There is a pseudo-coherent object `L` of `D(𝒪_S)` and
isomorphisms

`Ext^i_{𝒪_S}(L, ℱ) ≅ Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*ℱ)`

for all `i` and all quasi-coherent `ℱ`, functorial in `ℱ` and compatible with the boundary maps of
short exact sequences `0 ⟶ ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂ ⟶ ℱ₃ ⟶ 0` of quasi-coherent modules (on the left, composition
with the connecting morphism `ℱ₃ ⟶ ℱ₁[1]`; on the right, with that of
`0 ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₁ ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₂ ⟶ 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ ⟶ 0`, exact because `𝒢` is flat over `S`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pseudoCoherent_relativeExt_representative (E : DStd X)
    (hE : IsBoundedAboveCoherent E) (G : CochainComplex (TModules X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hG : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.FlatProperSupportComplex f G) :
    ∃ L : DStd S, IsPseudoCoherentObject L ∧
      ∃ β : ∀ (i : ℤ) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)),
          F.IsQuasicoherent → (baseExtGroup L F i ≃+ relativeExtGroup f G E F i),
        (∀ (i : ℤ) (F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace))
            (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherent) (v : F ⟶ F')
            (z : baseExtGroup L F i),
          β i F' hF' (baseExtMap L i v z) = relativeExtMap f G E i v (β i F hF z)) ∧
        (∀ (A : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
            (hA : A.ShortExact) (h₁ : A.X₁.IsQuasicoherent) (h₃ : A.X₃.IsQuasicoherent)
            (n m : ℤ) (h : 1 + n = m) (z : baseExtGroup L A.X₃ n),
          β m A.X₁ h₁ (baseExtBoundaryMap L hA n m h z) =
            relativeExtBoundaryMap E (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG) hA n m
              h (β n A.X₃ h₃ z))

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.compatiblePairs_adjunctionMap_surjective_and_not_injective_in_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08IG.** For a fibre product `B' = B ×_A A'` with `A' → A`
surjective, the adjunction map from any `B'`-module to the compatible pairs of its scalar
extensions to `B` and `A'` is surjective. In general this map is not injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem compatiblePairs_adjunctionMap_surjective_and_not_injective_in_general :
    (∀ (A A' B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B]
      (toBase : B →+* A) (surjection : A' →+* A) (I : Ideal A')
      (s : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I),
      let toB : s.fibreProduct →+* B := s.pullbackCone.fst.hom
      let toA' : s.fibreProduct →+* A' := s.pullbackCone.snd.hom
      let comm : toBase.comp toB = surjection.comp toA' := by
        exact congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom s.pullbackCone.condition
      ∃ (F : CategoricalPullback (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} toBase)
            (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} surjection) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} s.fibreProduct)
        (e : ∀ X, F.obj X ≃ CompatiblePairs toBase surjection X)
        (adj : extensionOfScalarsToPullback toB toA' toBase surjection comm ⊣ F),
        (∀ (L : ModuleCat.{u} s.fibreProduct) (X) (h : L ⟶ F.obj X) (l : L),
          (e X (h l)).1.1 =
              ((adj.homEquiv L X).symm h).fst
                ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[s.fibreProduct,toB] l) ∧
            (e X (h l)).1.2 =
              ((adj.homEquiv L X).symm h).snd
                ((1 : A') ⊗ₜ[s.fibreProduct,toA'] l)) ∧
          IsIso adj.counit ∧ ∀ L, Function.Surjective (adj.unit.app L)) ∧
      ∃ (A A' B : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : CommRing B)
        (toBase : B →+* A) (surjection : A' →+* A) (I : Ideal A')
        (s : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I),
        let toB : s.fibreProduct →+* B := s.pullbackCone.fst.hom
        let toA' : s.fibreProduct →+* A' := s.pullbackCone.snd.hom
        let comm : toBase.comp toB = surjection.comp toA' := by
          exact congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom s.pullbackCone.condition
        ∃ (F : CategoricalPullback (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} toBase)
              (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} surjection) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} s.fibreProduct)
          (e : ∀ X, F.obj X ≃ CompatiblePairs toBase surjection X)
          (adj : extensionOfScalarsToPullback toB toA' toBase surjection comm ⊣ F)
          (L : ModuleCat.{u} s.fibreProduct),
          (∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} s.fibreProduct) (X) (h : N ⟶ F.obj X) (l : N),
            (e X (h l)).1.1 =
                ((adj.homEquiv N X).symm h).fst
                  ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[s.fibreProduct,toB] l) ∧
              (e X (h l)).1.2 =
                ((adj.homEquiv N X).symm h).snd
                  ((1 : A') ⊗ₜ[s.fibreProduct,toA'] l)) ∧
            IsIso adj.counit ∧ ¬ Function.Injective (adj.unit.app L)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.finite_relativeRightAdjoint_obj_of_finite_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08IH.** In a relative module fibre-product situation, the
compatible-pairs module associated to a finite `D`-module and a finite `C'`-module is
finite over `D'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_relativeRightAdjoint_obj_of_finite_components
    {A A' B D' : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing D']
    {toBase : B →+* A} {surjection : A' →+* A} {I : Ideal A'}
    {base : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I}
    (s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := D') base)
    (F : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation.CompatibleModules s ⥤
      ModuleCat.{u} D')
    (adj : (letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct D' := s.toD'.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct B := (toBase.pullbackFst surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A' := (toBase.pullbackSnd surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A := (toBase.comp (toBase.pullbackFst surjection)).toAlgebra
       extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback (D' := D')
         ({ toBase with commutes' := fun _ => rfl } : B →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)
         ({ surjection with commutes' := fun r => r.property.symm } : A' →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)) ⊣
           F)
    (hCounit : IsIso adj.counit)
    (X : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation.CompatibleModules s) :
    Module.Finite s.D X.fst → Module.Finite s.C' X.snd →
      Module.Finite D' (F.obj X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reflectsIsomorphisms_affineQuasicoherentDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08II].**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`.  Then `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` reflects isomorphisms.

Here `Rf_*` is any total right derived functor of the direct image of `𝒪_X`-modules, with its
derivation unit `α`, restricted to `D_QCoh` as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineQuasicoherentDerivedPushforward`.  The proof is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isIso_derivedModulePushforward_map_of_isAffineHom`: the cone `C`
of a morphism `E ⟶ F` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, `Rf_*C = 0` when `Rf_*` of the
morphism is invertible, and `H^i(Rf_*C) = f_*H^i(C)` with `f_*` conservative on quasi-coherent
modules forces `C = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reflectsIsomorphisms_affineQuasicoherentDerivedPushforward :
    (affineQuasicoherentDerivedPushforward B S hS f hf Rf α).ReflectsIsomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_affinePullPushMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IJ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`. For `E`
in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` the canonical map `E ⊗^L f_*𝒪_X ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*E` is an isomorphism, so
`Rf_*Lf^*E = E ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} f_*𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_affinePullPushMap (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)))
    (hE : QcohDerived B S hS Y E) :
    IsIso (affinePullPushMap f hf E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IK, the coherence clause of (1) derived from (2).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F`
be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`.  If `E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent then `Hⁱ(E)` is coherent for every `i ≥ m`.

The remaining clause of (1), that `Hⁱ(E)` vanishes for `i ≫ 0`, and the converse implication
(1) ⇒ (2) are not proved in this development; the module documentation names the missing
substrate for each.

Only local Noetherianity of `F` is used, which is the third component of Stacks 03EA; the
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness components are not.  The underlying statement with
that hypothesis alone is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom`.

The quasi-coherence hypothesis is the hypothesis `E ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` of the source, read in the
single degree in which it is used, and it is needed only in the degree `i = m`:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_lt` is the same
conclusion for `i > m` with no hypothesis on `E` beyond pseudo-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (m i : ℤ)
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) (hi : m ≤ i)
    (hqc : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)
declarations.comment: (2) gives the coherence clause of (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IK, the coherence half of the final statement.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be
a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_F)`.  Then
`Hⁱ(E)` is a coherent `𝒪_F`-module in every degree.

This is the half of "`E` is an object of `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_F)`" that does not mention boundedness; the
boundedness half is not proved here, and neither is the converse.  No quasi-coherence hypothesis
is needed: a pseudo-coherent object lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` by Stacks 08JL,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_of_isPseudoCoherent_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherent E) (i : ℤ) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent gives coherent cohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isCoherent_homology_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian algebraic space, an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology is coherent in
degrees `≥ m` and zero in degrees `> b` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isCoherent_homology_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hXN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (m b : ℤ)
    (hqc : ∀ i : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj
        E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
      IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj E))
    (hb : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj E)) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_of_isCoherent_homology_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian algebraic space an object of `D(𝒪_X)` with coherent cohomology sheaves
vanishing in large degrees is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_isCoherent_homology_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hXN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ℤ, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj E))
    (hb : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E
declarations.comment: in particular: an object of D⁻_Coh is pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_and_isPseudoCoherent_iff_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IK.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and
let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`. For every `m ∈ ℤ` the following are equivalent:

1. `Hⁱ(E)` is coherent for `i ≥ m` and zero for `i ≫ 0`, and
2. `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.

In particular, `E` is pseudo-coherent if and only if `E` is an object of `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_F)`, that
is, its cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently large degrees and is coherent in every degree.

The first conjunct is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_of_isNoetherian` and the
second `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_iff_of_isNoetherian`. Noetherianity of `F` is
Stacks 03EA: quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian. `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` is the
condition whose full subcategory is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentDerivedCategory`
(Stacks 071X).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_and_isPseudoCoherent_iff_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))) E) :
    (∀ m : ℤ,
      ((∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i → SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)) ∧
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E) ↔
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) ∧
      ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherent E ↔
        (DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E ∧
          ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_and_isBoundedAbove_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `E` be an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`.  If `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent then `Hⁱ(E)` is coherent for every
`i ≥ m` and `Hⁱ(E)` vanishes for `i ≫ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_homology_and_isBoundedAbove_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (m : ℤ)
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m)
    (hqc : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i → SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)) ∧
      DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E
declarations.comment: (2) gives (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_homology_and_isBoundedAbove_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `E` be a
pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_F)`.  Then `E` is an object of `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_F)`: its cohomology
vanishes in all sufficiently large degrees and is coherent in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_homology_and_isBoundedAbove_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_isNoetherian
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hFN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherent E) :
    DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E)
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent gives D⁻_Coh

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_homology_iff_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IK.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and `E` an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. For `m ∈ ℤ` the following are equivalent:
1. `Hⁱ(E)` is coherent for `i ≥ m` and zero for `i ≫ 0`, and
2. `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_homology_iff_isPseudoCoherentFrom (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (m : ℤ) :
    ((∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i → IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E.obj)) ∧
      ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E.obj)) ↔
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E.obj m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_iff_isCoherent_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IK, the final statement.** Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S`. An
object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is pseudo-coherent if and only if it lies in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)`: its
cohomology sheaves are coherent and vanish in all sufficiently large degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_iff_isCoherent_homology (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E.obj ↔
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E.obj)) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E.obj)
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent objects of D_QCoh are those of D⁻_Coh

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_iff_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_standardModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IL.**  Let `X` be a quasi-separated algebraic space and `E` an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.  Then `E` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if and only if
`Hⁱ(E ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} ℱ) = 0` for `i ∉ [a, b]` and every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`.

This is the form at the standard model of `D(𝒪_X)`, with no hypothesis on the tensor product of
sheaves.  The derived tensor product is any `T`; Tor amplitude and condition (2) do not depend on
it.  The hypothesis `a ≤ b` of the source is not needed.  For (2) ⟹ (1), Tor amplitude is checked
on the affine étale charts `j : U ⟶ X`; condition (2) passes to `Lj^*E` because `X` is
quasi-separated (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_chart`), `Lj^*E` lies in
`D_QCoh`, and the affine case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_of_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_representedAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_iff_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_standardModel
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (hE : QcohDerived B S hS X E)
    (a b : ℤ) :
    DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude T E a b ↔
      HasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent B S hS X.2 T E a b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_of_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
If an object of `D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic space `X` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then its
derived tensor product with every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module has vanishing cohomology outside
`[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_of_hasTorAmplitude
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, d} (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u + 1, u, u, d} (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (a b : ℤ)
    (hE : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude T E a b) :
    HasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent B S hS hF T E a b
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_iff_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IL.**  Let `X` be a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `E` be an object
of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, and let `T` be a derived tensor product on `D(𝒪_X)`.  The following are
equivalent:

1. `E` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`;
2. `Hⁱ(E ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} ℱ) = 0` for `i ∉ [a, b]` and every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`.

The source assumes `a ≤ b`; neither direction uses it, as in the scheme case Stacks 08EA, so it is
not assumed.  (1) ⟹ (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_of_hasTorAmplitude`.  For (2) ⟹ (1) the
converse `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_of_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent_ofSlices` is
applied at the standard derived categories of `X` and of its slices, and carried to the given
derived category of `X` and the given datum `T` along the identity of `Mod(𝒪_X)`, which carries
Tor tests to Tor tests
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.isZero_homology_tensor_single_iff_of_equivalence`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_iff_hasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F)
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, d} (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u + 1, u, u, d} (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)) E)
    (a b : ℤ) :
    HasTorAmplitude T E a b ↔ HasTorAmplitudeOnQuasicoherent B S hS hF T E a b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleProjectionFormulaMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IN.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces, `E ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.  Then the projection formula map
`Rf_*(E) ⊗^L K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^L Lf^*K)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleProjectionFormulaMap (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (hE : QcohDerived B S hS X E)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)))
    (hK : QcohDerived B S hS Y K) :
    IsIso (smallEtaleProjectionFormulaMap B S hS f E K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.TorIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IP.** Two algebraic spaces are Tor independent over a base when the geometric
étale local rings at every compatible pair of points are Tor independent
for the homomorphisms induced on germs by their structure morphisms.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_iff_forall_etale_diagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IQ, (1) ⟺ (2).**  Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space
`B`.  Then `X` and `Y` are Tor independent over `B` if and only if for every commutative
diagram
```
U ⟶ W ⟵ V
↓    ↓    ↓
X ⟶ B ⟵ Y
```
with étale vertical arrows, `U` and `V` are Tor independent over `W`.

Condition (3), which asks for a single such diagram in which `W ⟶ B` is surjective and the
two upper terms are étale surjective over the base changes `X ×_B W` and `Y ×_B W`, is
equivalent to condition (1): it implies it by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_isEtale_surjective_diagram` and follows from it by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtale_surjective_diagram_of_torIndependent`.  Condition (4),
which reads the conclusion for `U`, `V` and `W` schemes in the sense of Stacks 08IA, that is on
ordinary local rings, implies condition (1) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_torIndependent_scheme_diagram` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.TorIndependenceSchemeComparison`, and follows from
condition (1) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_torIndependent_scheme_diagram_of_torIndependent` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.TorIndependenceSchemeConverse`.  So the four conditions
of Stacks 08IQ are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torIndependent_iff_forall_etale_diagram {Bs X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (fX : X ⟶ Bs) (gY : Y ⟶ Bs) :
    TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Bs.2 fX.hom gY.hom ↔
      ∀ (U V W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (a : U ⟶ X) (b : V ⟶ Y) (c : W ⟶ Bs)
        (uw : U ⟶ W) (vw : V ⟶ W), IsEtale B S hS a.hom → IsEtale B S hS b.hom →
        IsEtale B S hS c.hom → uw.hom ≫ c.hom = a.hom ≫ fX.hom →
        vw.hom ≫ c.hom = b.hom ≫ gY.hom → TorIndependent U.2 V.2 W.2 uw.hom vw.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_isEtale_surjective_diagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IQ, (3) ⟹ (1).**  Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space
`Bs`.  Suppose given one commutative diagram
```
U ⟶ W ⟵ V
↓    ↓    ↓
X ⟶ Bs ⟵ Y
```
with étale vertical arrows in which `W ⟶ Bs` is surjective and in which `U` and `V` are étale
and surjective over the fibre products `X ×_{Bs} W` and `Y ×_{Bs} W`.  If `U` and `V` are Tor
independent over `W`, then `X` and `Y` are Tor independent over `Bs`.

The two fibre products are presented as arbitrary cartesian squares of the underlying
presheaves, which is how a fibre product of algebraic spaces is formed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torIndependent_of_isEtale_surjective_diagram
    {Bs X Y U V W PX PY : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (fX : X ⟶ Bs) (gY : Y ⟶ Bs) (c : W ⟶ Bs)
    (a : U ⟶ X) (uw : U ⟶ W) (b : V ⟶ Y) (vw : V ⟶ W)
    (pX : PX ⟶ X) (pW : PX ⟶ W) (qY : PY ⟶ Y) (qW : PY ⟶ W)
    (u' : U ⟶ PX) (v' : V ⟶ PY)
    (sqX : IsPullback pX.hom pW.hom fX.hom c.hom)
    (sqY : IsPullback qY.hom qW.hom gY.hom c.hom)
    (hu'X : u' ≫ pX = a) (hu'W : u' ≫ pW = uw)
    (hv'Y : v' ≫ qY = b) (hv'W : v' ≫ qW = vw)
    (hcEtale : IsEtale B S hS c.hom) (hcSurj : IsSurjective B S hS c.hom)
    (haEtale : IsEtale B S hS a.hom) (hbEtale : IsEtale B S hS b.hom)
    (huEtale : IsEtale B S hS u'.hom) (huSurj : IsSurjective B S hS u'.hom)
    (hvEtale : IsEtale B S hS v'.hom) (hvSurj : IsSurjective B S hS v'.hom)
    (h : TorIndependent U.2 V.2 W.2 uw.hom vw.hom) :
    TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Bs.2 fX.hom gY.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtale_surjective_diagram_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IQ, (1) ⟹ (3).**  Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space
`Bs` which are Tor independent over `Bs`.  Then there is a commutative diagram
```
U ⟶ W ⟵ V
↓    ↓    ↓
X ⟶ Bs ⟵ Y
```
with étale vertical arrows in which `W ⟶ Bs` is surjective, in which `U` and `V` are étale and
surjective over the fibre products `X ×_{Bs} W` and `Y ×_{Bs} W`, and in which `U` and `V` are
Tor independent over `W`: this is the existence asserted by condition (3).

The witness is the diagram of identities, `W = Bs`, `U = X` and `V = Y`, whose two fibre
products are `X` and `Y` themselves by `CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_id_fst`; the Tor
independence asked of the diagram is then the hypothesis on the nose.  The converse implication
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_isEtale_surjective_diagram`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isEtale_surjective_diagram_of_torIndependent
    {Bs X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (fX : X ⟶ Bs) (gY : Y ⟶ Bs)
    (h : TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Bs.2 fX.hom gY.hom) :
    ∃ (U V W PX PY : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (c : W ⟶ Bs) (a : U ⟶ X) (uw : U ⟶ W)
      (b : V ⟶ Y) (vw : V ⟶ W) (pX : PX ⟶ X) (pW : PX ⟶ W) (qY : PY ⟶ Y) (qW : PY ⟶ W)
      (u' : U ⟶ PX) (v' : V ⟶ PY),
      IsPullback pX.hom pW.hom fX.hom c.hom ∧ IsPullback qY.hom qW.hom gY.hom c.hom ∧
        u' ≫ pX = a ∧ u' ≫ pW = uw ∧ v' ≫ qY = b ∧ v' ≫ qW = vw ∧
        IsEtale B S hS c.hom ∧ IsSurjective B S hS c.hom ∧
        IsEtale B S hS a.hom ∧ IsEtale B S hS b.hom ∧
        IsEtale B S hS u'.hom ∧ IsSurjective B S hS u'.hom ∧
        IsEtale B S hS v'.hom ∧ IsSurjective B S hS v'.hom ∧
        TorIndependent U.2 V.2 W.2 uw.hom vw.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_torIndependent_scheme_diagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IQ, (4) ⟹ (1).**  Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space
`Bs`.  Suppose given one commutative diagram
```
U ⟶ W ⟵ V
↓    ↓    ↓
X ⟶ Bs ⟵ Y
```
in which `U`, `V` and `W` are *schemes*, the vertical arrows are étale, `W ⟶ Bs` is surjective
and `U` and `V` are étale and surjective over the fibre products `X ×_{Bs} W` and `Y ×_{Bs} W`.
If `U` and `V` are Tor independent over `W` in the sense of Stacks 08IA, that is on their
ordinary local rings, then `X` and `Y` are Tor independent over `Bs`.

This is condition (4) of Stacks 08IQ: a diagram as in condition (3) whose three upper terms are
schemes, with Tor independence read in the sense of Derived Categories of Schemes, Definition
08IA.  The passage from the ordinary local rings of the three schemes to the étale local rings
of the algebraic spaces they represent is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_yoneda_of_torIndependent_scheme`; condition (3) then
gives condition (1) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_isEtale_surjective_diagram`.
declarations.statement:
theorem torIndependent_of_torIndependent_scheme_diagram
    {Bs X Y PX PY : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (fX : X ⟶ Bs) (gY : Y ⟶ Bs)
    {U₀ V₀ W₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (c : yoneda.obj W₀ ⟶ Bs.1) (a : yoneda.obj U₀ ⟶ X.1) (uw : U₀ ⟶ W₀)
    (b : yoneda.obj V₀ ⟶ Y.1) (vw : V₀ ⟶ W₀)
    (pX : PX ⟶ X) (pW : PX.1 ⟶ yoneda.obj W₀) (qY : PY ⟶ Y) (qW : PY.1 ⟶ yoneda.obj W₀)
    (u' : yoneda.obj U₀ ⟶ PX.1) (v' : yoneda.obj V₀ ⟶ PY.1)
    (sqX : IsPullback pX.hom pW fX.hom c) (sqY : IsPullback qY.hom qW gY.hom c)
    (hu'X : u' ≫ pX.hom = a) (hu'W : u' ≫ pW = yoneda.map uw)
    (hv'Y : v' ≫ qY.hom = b) (hv'W : v' ≫ qW = yoneda.map vw)
    (hcEtale : IsEtale B S hS c) (hcSurj : IsSurjective B S hS c)
    (haEtale : IsEtale B S hS a) (hbEtale : IsEtale B S hS b)
    (huEtale : IsEtale B S hS u') (huSurj : IsSurjective B S hS u')
    (hvEtale : IsEtale B S hS v') (hvSurj : IsSurjective B S hS v')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.TorIndependent ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map uw)
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map vw)) :
    TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Bs.2 fX.hom gY.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_torIndependent_scheme_diagram_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IQ, (1) ⟹ (4).**  Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over an algebraic space
`Bs` which are Tor independent over `Bs`.  Then there is a commutative diagram
```
U ⟶ W ⟵ V
↓    ↓    ↓
X ⟶ Bs ⟵ Y
```
in which `U`, `V` and `W` are *schemes*, the vertical arrows are étale, `W ⟶ Bs` is surjective,
`U` and `V` are étale and surjective over the fibre products `X ×_{Bs} W` and `Y ×_{Bs} W`, and
`U` and `V` are Tor independent over `W` in the sense of Stacks 08IA — that is, on their
*ordinary* local rings.  This is the existence asserted by condition (4).

The diagram is the atlas tower: a scheme chart `W ⟶ Bs` of the base, then scheme charts of the
two fibre products, which are algebraic spaces.  Condition (2) of Stacks 08IQ gives Tor
independence of the étale local rings over that diagram, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_scheme_of_torIndependent_yoneda` turns it into Tor
independence of the ordinary local rings.  The converse implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torIndependent_of_torIndependent_scheme_diagram`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_torIndependent_scheme_diagram_of_torIndependent
    {Bs X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (fX : X ⟶ Bs) (gY : Y ⟶ Bs)
    (h : TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Bs.2 fX.hom gY.hom) :
    ∃ (U₀ V₀ W₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS) (PX PY : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
      (c : yoneda.obj W₀ ⟶ Bs.1) (a : yoneda.obj U₀ ⟶ X.1) (uw : U₀ ⟶ W₀)
      (b : yoneda.obj V₀ ⟶ Y.1) (vw : V₀ ⟶ W₀)
      (pX : PX ⟶ X) (pW : PX.1 ⟶ yoneda.obj W₀) (qY : PY ⟶ Y) (qW : PY.1 ⟶ yoneda.obj W₀)
      (u' : yoneda.obj U₀ ⟶ PX.1) (v' : yoneda.obj V₀ ⟶ PY.1),
      IsPullback pX.hom pW fX.hom c ∧ IsPullback qY.hom qW gY.hom c ∧
        u' ≫ pX.hom = a ∧ u' ≫ pW = yoneda.map uw ∧ v' ≫ qY.hom = b ∧
        v' ≫ qW = yoneda.map vw ∧
        IsEtale B S hS c ∧ IsSurjective B S hS c ∧
        IsEtale B S hS a ∧ IsEtale B S hS b ∧
        IsEtale B S hS u' ∧ IsSurjective B S hS u' ∧
        IsEtale B S hS v' ∧ IsSurjective B S hS v' ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.TorIndependent ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map uw)
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map vw)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IR.**  Let `g : Y' ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces and `f : X ⟶ Y` a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated one, with base change `f' : X' ⟶ Y'`, `g' : X' ⟶ X`.  If `X`
and `Y'` are Tor independent over `Y`, then the base change map
`Lg^*Rf_*E ⟶ Rf'_*L(g')^*E` is an isomorphism for every `E ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hTor : TorIndependent X.2 Y'.2 Y.2 f.hom g.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (hE : QcohDerived B S hS X E) :
    IsIso (smallEtaleDerivedModuleBaseChangeMap B S hS f g f' g' sq.w E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_derivedModulePushforward_of_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**Perfect direct images.**  Let `S` be a scheme, `Y` a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and
`f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type and quasi-separated.
Let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be such that

1. `E ∈ D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`,
2. the support of `Hⁱ(E)` is proper over `Y` for all `i`,
3. `E` has finite tor dimension as an object of `D(f⁻¹𝒪_Y)`.

Then `Rf_*E` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_Y)`.

`Rf_*` is the total right derived functor of the direct image of modules, and the tor dimension
of `E`, read in `D(f⁻¹𝒪_Y)` by restriction of scalars along `f♯ : f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X`, is measured
against any derived tensor product `T` on `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-modules (they all agree, being characterized
by their values on K-flat complexes).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedModulePushforward_of_hasProperSupport
    (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop Y.1)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : derivedCategoryBBounded (isCoherent.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) E)
    (hsupp : ∀ i : ℤ, HasProperSupport B S hS X.2 Y.2 f.hom hf
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E)))
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1}
      (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f))
    (hTor : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasFiniteTorDimension.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1} T
      ((derivedScalarRestriction B S hS f).obj E)) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).IsPerfect
      ((Stacks.DerivedFunctor.totalRightDerived (modulePushforward B S hS f)).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.canonicalBaseChangedSituation
declarations.doc:
The standing data of Stacks 082M obtained by changing the base algebraic space along
`p : B' ⟶ B`: source `X' = X ×_B B'`, morphism the second projection, module the pullback `F'` of
`F`, quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement: abbrev canonicalBaseChangedSituation : QuotientSituation B S hS
declarations.comment: the base-changed situation F'/X'/B'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.canonicalBaseChangeQuotientModuleIso
declarations.doc:
**The quotients themselves correspond**, at the canonical pseudofunctoriality datum: the
quotient `F'_T/K'` named by the subobject corresponding to `K` is the inverse image along
`X'_T ≅ X_T` of the quotient `F_T/K`.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalBaseChangeQuotientModuleIso (T : SchemesOver Y')
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T))) :
    (D.canonicalBaseChangedSituation p).quotientModule T
        (D.baseChangeSubobjectEquiv p (D.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseChangedSourceModule p)
          (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) T K) ≅
      (modulePullback B S hS
          (D.baseChangeFiberIso p (D.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseChangedSourceModule p) T).hom).obj
        (D.quotientModule ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T) K)
declarations.comment: the identification of the quotients themselves, F'_T/K' = F_T/K under X'_T ≅ X_T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.mem_quotients_canonicalBaseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
For a test scheme `T` over `B'` a subobject of `F'_T` is an element of `Q_{F'/X'/B'}(T)`
exactly when the corresponding subobject of `F_T` is an element of `Q_{F/X/B}(T)`, where on the
right `T` is read as a scheme over `B` through `T ⟶ B' ⟶ B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_quotients_canonicalBaseChange_iff (T : SchemesOver Y')
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T))) :
    D.baseChangeSubobjectEquiv p (D.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseChangedSourceModule p)
        (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) T K ∈
        (D.canonicalBaseChangedSituation p).quotients T ↔
      K ∈ D.quotients ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T)
declarations.comment: the identification Q(F'/X'/B')(T) = Q(F/X/B)(T), in membership form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotients_canonicalBaseChange
declarations.doc:
`Q_{F'/X'/B'}(T) = Q_{F/X/B}(T)`: the canonical bijection of the two lattices of subobjects
carries the set of quotients of Stacks 082M for `F/X/B` at `T`, read as a scheme over `B`, onto the
one for `F'/X'/B'` at `T`, read as a scheme over `B'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotients_canonicalBaseChange (T : SchemesOver Y') :
    (D.canonicalBaseChangedSituation p).quotients T =
      D.baseChangeSubobjectEquiv p (D.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseChangedSourceModule p)
          (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) T ''
        D.quotients ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T)
declarations.comment: the identification Q(F'/X'/B')(T) = Q(F/X/B)(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientsCanonicalBaseChangeEquiv
declarations.doc: The equality `Q_{F'/X'/B'}(T) = Q_{F/X/B}(T)` read as a bijection of the two sets.
declarations.comment: the bijection Q(F'/X'/B')(T) ≃ Q(F/X/B)(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.mem_finitePresentationQuotients_canonicalBaseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
The same identification for `Q^{fp}`, in membership form: a subobject of `F'_T` is an element
of `Q^{fp}_{F'/X'/B'}(T)` exactly when the corresponding subobject of `F_T` is an element of

declarations.statement:
theorem mem_finitePresentationQuotients_canonicalBaseChange_iff (T : SchemesOver Y')
    (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule ((CostructuredArrow.map p).obj T))) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijOn_quotientRestrict_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IU.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site, let
`F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `{f i : X i ⟶ X}` be an fpqc covering and for each
`i, j` let `{g i j k : X ijk ⟶ X i ×_X X j}` be an fpqc covering.  Then restriction along the
members of the covering is a bijection from the quotients `F ⟶ Q` with `Q` quasi-coherent onto
the families of quotients `f i ^* F ⟶ Q i` with `Q i` quasi-coherent such that `Q i` and `Q j`
restrict to the same quotient on every `X ijk`.

A quotient is recorded by its kernel, a subobject of the module, as in Situation 082M; the
restriction of a quotient of `F` along `f i` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientRestrict`, and
the restrictions of `Q i` and `Q j` to `X ijk` are compared as quotients of the single inverse
image of `F` along `X ijk ⟶ X`, through `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientRestrictOver`.

Injectivity is the faithfulness clause of Stacks 04W8 applied to the kernels, which are
quasi-coherent.  For surjectivity, agreement on the `X ijk` gives agreement on `X i ×_X X j`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientRestrict_pairFst_eq_of_refinement`), and the family descends
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_quotientRestrict_eq_of_isFpqcCovering`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_quotientRestrict_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v} {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {Xi : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (f i).hom)
    {J : I → I → Type w} {Xijk : ∀ i j, J i j → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (g : ∀ i j k, Xijk i j k ⟶ QuasiCoherentDescent.pair B S hS Xi f i j)
    (hg : ∀ i j, IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun k ↦ (g i j k).hom) :
    Set.BijOn (fun (K : Subobject F) i ↦ quotientRestrict (f i) K)
      {K | (cokernel K.arrow).IsQuasicoherentOnSite}
      {Q | (∀ i, (cokernel (Q i).arrow).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
        ∀ i j k, quotientRestrictOver (g i j k ≫ QuasiCoherentDescent.pairFst B S hS Xi f i j)
            rfl F (Q i) =
          quotientRestrictOver (g i j k ≫ QuasiCoherentDescent.pairSnd B S hS Xi f i j)
            (pair_comp_condition f i j (g i j k)) F (Q j)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IV.**  In Situation 082M, let `{a i : W i ⟶ X}` be an fpqc covering of the source,
let `P i j` be the fibre product `W i ×_X W j` and let `{Z i j k ⟶ P i j}` be fpqc coverings.
For every scheme `T` over `Y` the diagram

`Q_{F/X/Y}(T) ⟶ ∏_i Q_{F i/W i/Y}(T) ⇉ ∏_{ijk} Q_{F ijk/Z i j k/Y}(T)`

presents the first arrow as the equalizer of the other two: restriction is a bijection from
`Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` onto the set of families `(Q i)` whose two restrictions to each `Z i j k` agree.

The three halves of this are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.restrictQuotientToMember_mem_quotients` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.restrictQuotientBetweenMembers_toMember`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.eq_of_restrictQuotientToMember_eq` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.exists_mem_quotients_restrictQuotientToMember_eq`.

Nothing beyond Situation 082M and the two coverings is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember
    {I : Type v} {κ : I → I → Type v} {W : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {P : I → I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ∀ i j, κ i j → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (a : ∀ i, W i ⟶ D.X) {c₀ : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ W i} {c₁ : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ W j}
    {d : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ D.X} (q : ∀ i j k, Z i j k ⟶ P i j) {e : ∀ i j k, Z i j k ⟶ D.X}
    (hcov : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (a i).hom)
    (hP : ∀ i j, IsPullback (c₀ i j) (c₁ i j) (a i) (a j))
    (hd₀ : ∀ i j, c₀ i j ≫ a i = d i j) (hd₁ : ∀ i j, c₁ i j ≫ a j = d i j)
    (hqcov : ∀ i j, IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun k ↦ (q i j k).hom)
    (he₀ : ∀ i j k, (q i j k ≫ c₀ i j) ≫ a i = e i j k)
    (he₁ : ∀ i j k, (q i j k ≫ c₁ i j) ≫ a j = e i j k) (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    Set.BijOn (fun K i ↦
        D.restrictQuotientToMember (a i) T K)
      (D.quotients T)
      {Q | (∀ i, Q i ∈ (D.sourceRestricted (a i)).quotients T) ∧
        ∀ i j k, D.restrictQuotientBetweenMembers (q i j k ≫ c₀ i j) (he₀ i j k) T (Q i) =
          D.restrictQuotientBetweenMembers (q i j k ≫ c₁ i j) (he₁ i j k) T (Q j)}
declarations.comment: the full bijection onto the matching families, every T, with nothing assumed beyond Situation 082M and the two coverings: 03LU for commutativity, 04W8 faithfulness and 03DO kernels for injectivity, 03GA and 05VW along the flat members of the covering for the restrictions, Remark 08IT (04W8 fullness and effectivity, at the quasi-coherent module of the situation) and 05VY for surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IV for the finite-presentation subfunctor.**  The diagram of Stacks 08IV presents
the first arrow as the equalizer of the other two for `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}` as well: restriction is a
bijection from `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}(T)` onto the set of families of elements of
`Q^{fp}_{F i/W i/Y}(T)` whose two restrictions to each `Z i j k` agree.

Only the two outer halves change: the restriction maps preserve finite presentation, which is
`restrictQuotientToMember_mem_finitePresentationQuotients` of this namespace, and the quotient
descended by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.exists_mem_quotients_restrictQuotientToMember_eq` is
of finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePresentationOnSiteDescendsAlongFpqcCovering`, Stacks 060V on the
site.

Nothing beyond Situation 082M and the two coverings is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_finitePresentation
    {I : Type v} {κ : I → I → Type v} {W : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {P : I → I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Z : ∀ i j, κ i j → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (a : ∀ i, W i ⟶ D.X) {c₀ : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ W i} {c₁ : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ W j}
    {d : ∀ i j, P i j ⟶ D.X} (q : ∀ i j k, Z i j k ⟶ P i j) {e : ∀ i j k, Z i j k ⟶ D.X}
    (hcov : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (a i).hom)
    (hP : ∀ i j, IsPullback (c₀ i j) (c₁ i j) (a i) (a j))
    (hd₀ : ∀ i j, c₀ i j ≫ a i = d i j) (hd₁ : ∀ i j, c₁ i j ≫ a j = d i j)
    (hqcov : ∀ i j, IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun k ↦ (q i j k).hom)
    (he₀ : ∀ i j k, (q i j k ≫ c₀ i j) ≫ a i = e i j k)
    (he₁ : ∀ i j k, (q i j k ≫ c₁ i j) ≫ a j = e i j k) (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    Set.BijOn (fun K i ↦
        D.restrictQuotientToMember (a i) T K)
      (D.finitePresentationQuotients T)
      {Q | (∀ i, Q i ∈ (D.sourceRestricted (a i)).finitePresentationQuotients T) ∧
        ∀ i j k, D.restrictQuotientBetweenMembers (q i j k ≫ c₀ i j) (he₀ i j k) T (Q i) =
          D.restrictQuotientBetweenMembers (q i j k ≫ c₁ i j) (he₁ i j k) T (Q j)}
declarations.comment: the same equalizer property for the finite-presentation subfunctor Q^{fp}, again with nothing assumed and no weakening: the inputs of bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember together with Section 05VR for the restriction maps and 060V on the site for surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
In Situation 082M, let `{a i : W i ⟶ X}` be an fpqc covering of the source, let `P i j` be the
fibre product `W i ×_X W j` and let `{Z i j k ⟶ P i j}` be fpqc coverings. For every scheme `T`
over `Y` the diagram

`Q_{F/X/Y}(T) ⟶ ∏_i Q_{F i/W i/Y}(T) ⇉ ∏_{ijk} Q_{F ijk/Z i j k/Y}(T)`

presents the first arrow as the equalizer of the other two: restriction is a bijection from
`Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` onto the set of families `(Q i)` of elements of the `Q_{F i/W i/Y}(T)` whose two
restrictions `pr₀^*`, `pr₁^*` to each `Z i j k` agree.  Being a bijection onto that set is the
commutativity `pr₀^* ∘ res = pr₁^* ∘ res`, the injectivity of `res`, and the surjectivity of
`res` onto the equalizer.

Here `F i` is the inverse image of `F` along `a i` and `F ijk` the inverse image of `F` along the
single morphism `e i j k : Z i j k ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement: alias bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_of_isFpqcCovering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_finitePresentation_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
The diagram of Stacks 08IV presents the first arrow as the equalizer of the other two for
`Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}` as well: restriction is a bijection from `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}(T)` onto the set of
families of elements of the `Q^{fp}_{F i/W i/Y}(T)` whose two restrictions to each `Z i j k`
agree.
declarations.statement: alias bijOn_restrictQuotientToMember_finitePresentation_of_isFpqcCovering

infinite-dimensional affine space need not be quasi-separated.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_lqcohSheafFbc_algebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IY.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒪_𝒳)`, the
derived category of the sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on the fppf site of `𝒳`, whose cohomology
sheaves are locally quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WJ**) and have the flat base change property of
**Stacks 0762**, read with the inverse image of sheaves of modules.  Then there is a distinguished
triangle

`K ⟶ ∏_{n ≥ 0} τ_{≥ -n}K ⟶ ∏_{n ≥ 0} τ_{≥ -n}K ⟶ K[1]`

in `D(𝒪_𝒳)`: the product of the tower `n ↦ τ_{≥ -n}K` exists and `K` is its derived limit
(`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit`, **Stacks 08TC**), the second arrow being
`1 - shift`.

As in the source: the higher cohomology of a module in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` vanishes over the
objects lying over an affine scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isZero_rightDerived_evaluation_of_sheafFlatBaseChange_algebraicStack`),
those objects cover `𝒳_fppf`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEnoughObjects_isAffineOver_of_essentiallySmall`), and the
convergence criterion of **Stacks 0D6P** with `d = 0` applies
(`Stacks.Cohomology.AcyclicCover.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_acyclic`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_lqcohSheafFbc_algebraicStack
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (K : DerivedCategory (fppfSiteModules B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange.{u, _, _, u} B E h S hS
      𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (fppfSiteModules B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) i).obj K).val) :
    ∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
        (fppfTruncGETower B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids K).obj ⟨n⟩,
      IsDerivedLimit (fppfTruncGETower B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids K) K
declarations.comment: K is the derived limit of its canonical truncations from below: the distinguished triangle K → ∏ τ_{≥ -n}K → ∏ τ_{≥ -n}K → K[1] in D(𝒪_𝒳), for an algebraic stack 𝒳 and a complex of fppf 𝒪_𝒳-modules whose cohomology sheaves are locally quasi-coherent with the flat base change property of 0762, read with the inverse image of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_coproductToProduct_shiftedSingleFamily_algebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08IZ.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `ℱ_n`, `n ≥ 0`, be sheaves of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules on its big fppf site which are locally quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WJ**) and have
the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762**, read with the inverse image of sheaves of
modules.  Then the canonical map

`⊕_n ℱ_n[n] ⟶ ∏_n ℱ_n[n]`

is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_𝒳)`.

As in the source, this is **Stacks 08IY** for the sum: the higher cohomology of each `ℱ_n`
vanishes over the objects lying over an affine scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isZero_rightDerived_evaluation_of_sheafFlatBaseChange_algebraicStack`),
those objects cover `𝒳_fppf`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEnoughObjects_isAffineOver_of_essentiallySmall`), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_coproductToProduct_shiftedSingleFamily_of_isZero_rightDerived`
concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coproductToProduct_shiftedSingleFamily_algebraicStack
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (F : ℕ → fppfSiteModules B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℕ, IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange.{u, _, _, u} B E h S hS
      𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (F n).val) :
    IsIso (Pi.lift (Sigma.π (shiftedSingleFamily B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F)))
declarations.comment: for an algebraic stack 𝒳 and a family (ℱ_n)_{n ≥ 0} of locally quasi-coherent fppf 𝒪_𝒳-modules with the flat base change property of 0762 (read with the inverse image of sheaves of modules), the canonical map ⊕_n ℱ_n[n] → ∏_n ℱ_n[n] is an isomorphism in D(𝒪_𝒳); the index n runs over n ≥ 0, the case the section applies

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.ProjectivityNotLocalOnBase.not_isZariskiLocalAtTarget
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08J1], granted Hironaka's example and the two comparisons of Tags 07RL and
0BCL.** Neither projectivity nor quasi-projectivity is Zariski local on the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isZariskiLocalAtTarget (hH : ProperLocallyProjectiveNotProjective.{u})
    (hRL : ProjectiveIsQuasiProjective.{u}) (hBCL : ProperQuasiProjectiveIsProjective.{u}) :
    ¬ IsZariskiLocalAtTarget projectiveProperty.{u} ∧
      ¬ IsZariskiLocalAtTarget quasiProjectiveProperty.{u}
declarations.comment: the tag's two assertions REDUCED TO HIRONAKA'S EXAMPLE, which is NOT proved.  The witness is the named hypothesis `ProperLocallyProjectiveNotProjective` (:220) -- a proper, Zariski-locally projective, non-projective morphism -- and it carries the whole content of the tag; `hRL` and `hBCL` are the source's own Tags 07RL and 0BCL (1), also carried. What IS proved unconditionally, and is the reason the reduction is exact rather than circular: `isLocallyProjective_iff_isProjective` (:192) shows that Zariski-locality of projectivity is precisely the collapse of Tag 01W8 (1) onto Tag 01W8 (3), i.e. of `IsProjective` onto `IsLocallyProjective`, so refuting locality is exactly exhibiting a morphism separating those two notions -- nothing more is needed and nothing less suffices. The fpqc assertions follow from the Zariski ones at :293, :301, :310 via `zariskiPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage`. Of the construction, step 3 is fully proved over any domain in `Examples/HironakaConicIntersection.lean`: the two conics meet exactly in the two points `P` and `Q` (`conicIdealC_sup_conicIdealD_eq_inf`, :366) and that intersection is reduced (`isRadical_conicIdealC_sup_conicIdealD`, :372). Absent: the conics as smooth closed subschemes of `P^3`, the two iterated blow-up towers and their gluing over `Y - P - Q`, Tags 01OE and 0BCL (1) for 01W8-projectivity, and the rational equivalences on the exceptional surface. Tag 02TI, which the degree argument consumes, IS present (`Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapFactorsEverywhere_iff_killsPrincipalDivisor`)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.ProjectivityNotLocalOnBase.not_isZariskiLocalAtTarget_and_not_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
The properties "`f` is projective" and "`f` is quasi-projective" are not Zariski local on
the base; a fortiori, they are not fpqc local on the base.

The witness is Hironaka's example,
`Stacks.Examples.ProjectivityNotLocalOnBase.properLocallyProjectiveNotProjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isZariskiLocalAtTarget_and_not_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (¬ IsZariskiLocalAtTarget projectiveProperty.{u} ∧
      ¬ IsZariskiLocalAtTarget quasiProjectiveProperty.{u}) ∧
    (¬ projectiveProperty.{u}.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
      ¬ quasiProjectiveProperty.{u}.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.no_derived_base_change
declarations.doc:
In general, derived base change of `A`-modules to `R'` does not factor
through the derived category of the ordinary tensor-product algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem no_derived_base_change :
    ∃ (R : Type u), ∃ (hR : CommRing R),
      letI : CommRing R := hR
      ∃ (A : Type u), ∃ (hA : CommRing A),
        letI : CommRing A := hA
        ∃ (R' : Type u), ∃ (hR' : CommRing R'),
          letI : CommRing R' := hR'
          ∃ (f : R →+* A) (g : R →+* R'),
            letI : Algebra R A := f.toAlgebra
            letI : Algebra R R' := g.toAlgebra
            letI : Algebra R' (A ⊗[R] R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
            ¬ ∃ (T : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
                DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] R'))),
              ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A),
                Nonempty
                  (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
                      (algebraMap R' (A ⊗[R] R'))).mapDerivedCategory.obj
                        (T.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M))) ≅
                    ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} g).functor.obj
                      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.obj
                        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M))))

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.triangleTruncLETruncGE_distinguished
declarations.doc:
