`τ_{≤a} K ⟶ K ⟶ τ_{≥a+1} K ⟶ (τ_{≤a} K)[1]` on the canonical truncations of `K`, with the
canonical maps, is distinguished in `D(C)`.

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.triangleTruncLETruncLESucc_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08J5** (2). For a complex `K` and an integer `a`, the triangle
`τ_{≤a} K ⟶ τ_{≤a+1} K ⟶ H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1] ⟶ (τ_{≤a} K)[1]`, whose first map is the canonical
inclusion of truncations and whose second map is the canonical projection onto the cohomology in
degree `a + 1`, is distinguished in `D(C)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleTruncLETruncLESucc_distinguished (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (a : ℤ) :
    triangleTruncLETruncLESucc K a ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory C)
declarations.comment: (2) the triangle τ_{≤a}K → τ_{≤a+1}K → H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1] → (τ_{≤a}K)[1] on the truncations of the complex K, with the canonical maps

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.triangleTruncGETruncGESucc_distinguished

**Stacks Project, Tag 08J5** (3). For a complex `K` and an integer `a`, the triangle
`H^a(K)[-a] ⟶ τ_{≥a} K ⟶ τ_{≥a+1} K ⟶ (H^a(K)[-a])[1]`, whose first map is the canonical
inclusion of the cohomology in degree `a` and whose second map is the canonical projection of

declarations.statement:
theorem triangleTruncGETruncGESucc_distinguished (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (a : ℤ) :
    triangleTruncGETruncGESucc K a ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory C)
declarations.comment: (3) the triangle H^a(K)[-a] → τ_{≥a}K → τ_{≥a+1}K → H^a(K)[-a+1] on the truncations of the complex K, with the canonical maps

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.derivedGlobalSectionsPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J6**, read in abelian groups: `RΓ(C, F) = RΓ(D, Rf_*F)`.

The source's remark observes that [Stacks, Tag 015M] applies to the composition
`Γ(C, -) = Γ(D, -) ∘ f_*`, because the direct image of an injective module is totally acyclic
(Stacks 072Z) and a totally acyclic module is acyclic for global sections (Stacks 0731). This
is that application: the canonical map `R(Γ(D, -) ∘ f_*) ⟶ RΓ(D, -) ∘ Rf_*` is invertible, and
`Γ(C, -) ≅ Γ(D, -) ∘ f_*` carries the left hand side to `RΓ(C, -)`. The statement is an
isomorphism of functors on `D⁺(Mod(O_C))`, so it holds in particular at a single module placed
in degree zero, which is the form the remark displays.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsPushforwardIso :
    (globalSectionsAb X).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ≅
      (pushforwardModules f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        (globalSectionsAb Y).rightDerivedFunctorPlus
declarations.comment: the identification RΓ(D, Rf_*F) = RΓ(C, F), read in abelian groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurrySectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] over an object `U` of the site.**
Morphisms `K|_U ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)|_U` are morphisms `(K ⊗^L_O B)|_U ⟶ Z|_U`.

It is the derived currying isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 08J9] read on degree-zero hypercohomology
over `U`, with both sides identified with groups of morphisms between restrictions by
[Stacks, Tag 08JA].  The tensor product is the one taken on `C`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCurrySectionsEquiv
    (K B Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z)) ≃+
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj B) ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            U).mapDerivedCategory.obj Z)
declarations.comment: the bijection of morphism groups over an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurrySectionsEquiv_restriction
declarations.doc:
**The bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] over `U` is the restriction of the bijection over
`C`.**  For `g : K ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)` the morphism `(K ⊗^L_O B)|_U ⟶ Z|_U` matched with `g|_U`
over `U` is the restriction of the morphism `K ⊗^L_O B ⟶ Z` matched with `g` over `C`.

This is the compatibility of [Stacks, Tag 08JA] globally and over `U` under restriction of
hypercohomology, applied at the two ends of the bijection, with the naturality of that
restriction at the derived currying isomorphism in between.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurrySectionsEquiv_restriction
    (K B Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (g : K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z) :
    derivedCurrySectionsEquiv X U K B Z
        ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            U).mapDerivedCategory.map g) =
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          U).mapDerivedCategory.map
        (derivedCurryHomEquiv X K B Z g)
declarations.comment: the bijection over an object of the site restricts the global one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurrySectionsEquiv_naturality_source
declarations.doc:
**The bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] over `U` is natural in its source variable.**  For a
morphism `u : K' ⟶ K` of `D(O)`, precomposing a morphism `K|_U ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)|_U` with `u|_U`
corresponds to precomposing the matched morphism `(K ⊗^L_O B)|_U ⟶ Z|_U` with the restriction of
`u ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurrySectionsEquiv_naturality_source
    (K K' B Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (u : K' ⟶ K)
    (h : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z)) :
    derivedCurrySectionsEquiv X U K' B Z
        ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            U).mapDerivedCategory.map u ≫ h) =
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          U).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map u).app B) ≫
        derivedCurrySectionsEquiv X U K B Z h
declarations.comment: functoriality in the source, over an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The tensor–internal-Hom isomorphism of morphism groups**, Stacks 08J8 as 08J9 gives it:
morphisms `K ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)` in `D(O)` are morphisms `K ⊗^L_O L ⟶ M`.

It is the derived currying isomorphism read on degree-zero global hypercohomology, with both
sides identified with groups of morphisms by Stacks 08JA.
declarations.comment: the tensor-internal-Hom bijection of morphism groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**The tensor–internal-Hom bijection is tensoring and then evaluating.** For objects `K`, `A`,
`B` of `D(O)` it carries `g : K ⟶ RSheafHom(A, B)` to

`(g ⊗^𝐋_O 1_A) ≫ e`,

with `e : RSheafHom(A, B) ⊗^𝐋_O A ⟶ B` the evaluation morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomCounit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_apply
    (K A B : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (g : K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor Y).obj (op A)).obj B) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv Y K A B g =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y).map g).app A ≫
        derivedSheafHomCounit Y A B
declarations.comment: the bijection is tensoring with the identity followed by the evaluation morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08J8 is natural in all three objects.** For
morphisms `k : K' ⟶ K`, `l : L' ⟶ L` and `m : M ⟶ M'` of `D(O)`, the bijection carries a
morphism `θ : K ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)` precomposed with `k` and postcomposed with
`RSheafHom(l, m)` to its transpose precomposed with the derived tensor product of `k` and `l`
and postcomposed with `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality
    {K K' L L' M M' :
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (k : K' ⟶ K) (l : L' ⟶ L) (m : M ⟶ M')
    (θ : K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X K' L' M'
        (k ≫ θ ≫ (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map l.op).app M ≫
          ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L')).map m)) =
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map k).app L' ≫
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).map l) ≫
        derivedCurryHomEquiv X K L M θ ≫ m
declarations.comment: naturality of the tensor-internal-Hom bijection in all three objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_dinaturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J8, dinaturality in the internal-Hom variable.** Postcomposing a morphism
`h : A ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)` with the map `RSheafHom(B, Z) ⟶ RSheafHom(B', Z)` induced by
`v : B' ⟶ B` corresponds, under the tensor–internal-Hom bijection, to precomposing the morphism
`A ⊗^L_O B ⟶ Z` matched with `h` with `1 ⊗ v`.

The variable `B` is contravariant on the left of the bijection and covariant on the right, so
this is a dinaturality identity and not a naturality square.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_dinaturality
    {B B' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (A Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (v : B' ⟶ B)
    (h : A ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X A B' Z
        (h ≫ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map v.op).app Z) =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj A).map v ≫
        derivedCurryHomEquiv X A B Z h
declarations.comment: dinaturality of the bijection of morphism groups in the internal-Hom variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J8 is natural in its source variable.** Precomposing a morphism
`h : A ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)` with `u : A' ⟶ A` corresponds, under the tensor-internal-Hom
bijection `derivedCurryHomEquiv`, to precomposing the morphism `A ⊗^L_O B ⟶ Z` matched with
`h` by `u ⊗ 1`.

The bijection is the derived currying isomorphism of Stacks 08J9 read on degree-zero global
hypercohomology with both sides identified with morphism groups by Stacks 08JA, so this is the
object-level naturality `derivedCurryIso_natural` together with the naturality of Stacks 08JA
in its source variable,
`derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_source`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_source
    {A A' B Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (u : A' ⟶ A)
    (h : A ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X A' B Z (u ≫ h) =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map u).app B ≫
        derivedCurryHomEquiv X A B Z h
declarations.comment: the tensor-internal-Hom bijection is natural in the source variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J8 is natural in its target variable.** Postcomposing a morphism
`h : A ⟶ RSheafHom(B, Z)` with `RSheafHom(B, w)`, for `w : Z ⟶ Z'`, corresponds under the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection `derivedCurryHomEquiv` to postcomposing the morphism
`A ⊗^L_O B ⟶ Z` matched with `h` by `w`.

The bijection is the derived currying isomorphism of Stacks 08J9 read on degree-zero global
hypercohomology with both sides identified with morphism groups by Stacks 08JA, so this is the
object-level naturality `derivedCurryIso_natural` together with the naturality of Stacks 08JA
in its target variable, `derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target_globalMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_target
    {A B Z Z' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (w : Z ⟶ Z')
    (h : A ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).obj Z) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X A B Z'
        (h ≫ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)).map w) =
      derivedCurryHomEquiv X A B Z h ≫ w
declarations.comment: the tensor-internal-Hom bijection is natural in the target variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorSheafHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J8 as an adjunction.** For an object `B` of `D(O)`, the derived tensor product
with `B` is left adjoint to the derived internal Hom out of `B`:

`Hom_{D(O)}(A ⊗^L_O B, Z) ≅ Hom_{D(O)}(A, RSheafHom(B, Z))`,

naturally in `A` and `Z`. The bijection is `derivedCurryHomEquiv`, its naturality in `A` is
`derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_source` and its naturality in `Z` is
`derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_target`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorSheafHomAdjunction
    (B : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).flip.obj B ⊣
      (derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op B)
declarations.comment: the tensor-internal-Hom bijection as an adjunction, at a fixed middle object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.tensorHomEquivDinatural_ringedSpace
declarations.doc:
**The bijection of Tag 08DI on a ringed space is dinatural in its internal-hom variable.**
This is `Transpose.TensorHomEquivDinatural` for the bijection of Tag 08DI, the companion of
`tensorHomEquivNaturalLeft_ringedSpace`, and it is the clause the assembly of
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomStalk.InternalHomComparison` and the dévissage of Tag 0GM7
in the perfect variable both ask for.

The bijection is presented as the site-level `RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv` of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Z.sheaf` rather than as
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomTensorEquiv Z.sheaf`, which is the same family of additive
equivalences; see the implementation notes of this file.  `convert … using 1` rather than `exact`
for the reason recorded on `tensorHomEquivNaturalLeft_ringedSpace`: what is left to settle lives
inside the `FunLike` instance of the coercion, where the two spellings of the derived tensor
product and of the derived internal hom appear as instance arguments, and the congruence `convert`
builds settles those argument by argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquivDinatural_ringedSpace :
    Transpose.TensorHomEquivDinatural (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Z.sheaf)
      (internalHomTensorUncurried Z)
      (fun A B C => (RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Z.sheaf) A B C).toEquiv)
declarations.comment: dinaturality of the bijection of morphism groups of Tag 08DI in its internal-hom variable, read on a ringed space at the uncurried spelling of the derived tensor product; the companion clause in the source variable is tensorHomEquivNaturalLeft_ringedSpace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism of morphism groups is the derived currying isomorphism on global
hypercohomology.** This is the last assertion of Stacks 08J9: taking degree-zero global
hypercohomology of `derivedCurryIso` and identifying both sides with morphism groups by
Stacks 08JA gives `derivedCurryHomEquiv`, the bijection (21.35.0.1) of Stacks 08J8.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_globalSections
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).obj
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M))) : Type u)) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X K L M
        (derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X K
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M) x) =
      derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L) M
        (derivedCurryGlobalEquiv X K L M x)
declarations.comment: recovers the morphism-group bijection on H^0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_globalSections_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
`derivedCurryHomEquiv_globalSections` with the additive equivalence
`derivedCurryGlobalEquiv` spelled out as the map induced by `derivedCurryIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryHomEquiv_globalSections_homologyMap
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).obj
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M))) : Type u)) :
    derivedCurryHomEquiv X K L M
        (derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X K
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M) x) =
      derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L) M
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).map (derivedCurryIso X K L M).hom) x)
declarations.comment: recovers the morphism-group bijection on H^0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08J9: the derived currying isomorphism is a natural isomorphism.** The canonical
isomorphism

`RSheafHom(K, RSheafHom(L, M)) ≅ RSheafHom(K ⊗^L_O L, M)`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryIso`, bundled as an isomorphism between the
trifunctor `(K, L, M) ↦ RSheafHom(K, RSheafHom(L, M))` and the trifunctor
`(K, L, M) ↦ RSheafHom(K ⊗^L_O L, M)` on `D(O)ᵒᵖ × D(O)ᵒᵖ × D(O)`. It is obtained by extending
the comparison on models.
declarations.statement: def derivedCurryNatIso : iteratedHomFunctor X ≅ tensorHomFunctor X
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryIso_natural
declarations.doc:
**Functoriality of the derived currying isomorphism in all three objects.** For morphisms
`k : K' ⟶ K`, `l : L' ⟶ L` and `m : M ⟶ M'` of `D(O)` the square formed by `derivedCurryIso`
at `(K, L, M)` and at `(K', L', M')` commutes: the derived currying isomorphism is natural
contravariantly in the source and in the middle object and covariantly in the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryIso_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' :
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (k : K' ⟶ K) (l : L' ⟶ L) (m : M ⟶ M') :
    ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map k.op).app
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M) ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K')).map
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map l.op).app M ≫
            ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L')).map m) ≫
        (derivedCurryIso X K' L' M').hom =
      (derivedCurryIso X K L M).hom ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map
            ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map k).app L' ≫
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).map l).op)).app M ≫
          ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj
            (op (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K').obj L'))).map
              m
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryIso_comparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of Stacks 08J9 with the currying isomorphism of complexes of Stacks
0A90.** For complexes `A`, `B`, `I` with `B` K-flat and `I` K-injective, `derivedCurryIso` on
the classes of `A`, `B`, `I` is, after the two identifications

`RSheafHom(QA, RSheafHom(QB, QI)) ≅ Q SheafHom(A, SheafHom(B, I))` and
`RSheafHom(QA ⊗^L_O QB, QI) ≅ Q SheafHom(Tot(A ⊗_O B), I)`,

the class of the complex-level currying isomorphism `SheafHom(A, SheafHom(B, I)) ≅
SheafHom(Tot(A ⊗_O B), I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCurryIso_comparison
    (A B I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hB : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O B) [I.IsKInjective] :
    (derivedCurryIso X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)).hom ≫
        (tensorHomRepresentativeIso X A B I hB).hom =
      (iteratedHomRepresentativeIso X A B I hB).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (sheafHomTensorCurryIso X A B I).hom
declarations.comment: comparison with currying of complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA globally is natural in the source variable, for an arbitrary morphism of
`D(O)`**: the identification of the degree-zero global hypercohomology of `RSheafHom(L, M)`
with `Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` carries the map induced by `u : L' ⟶ L` to precomposition with `u`.

This is the global half of the naturality of Stacks 0A94 read at arbitrary objects of `D(O)`:
the two sides are compared at the chosen K-flat representative of the source and the chosen
K-injective representative of the target, where it is
`derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquivOfKFlat_naturality_derived`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_source
    {A A' W : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (u : A' ⟶ A)
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op A)).obj W)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X A' W (derivedHomGlobalMap X u (𝟙 W) x) =
      u ≫ derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X A W x
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality in the source variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target_globalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA globally is natural in the target variable, for an arbitrary morphism of
`D(O)`**: the identification of the degree-zero global hypercohomology of `RSheafHom(A, W)`
with `Hom_{D(O)}(A, W)` carries the map induced by `v : W ⟶ W'` to postcomposition with `v`.

This is the target half of the naturality of Stacks 0A94 read at arbitrary objects of `D(O)`:
the two sides are compared at the chosen K-flat representative of the source and the chosen
K-injective representatives of the two targets, where it is
`derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquivOfKFlat_naturality_derived_snd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target_globalMap
    {A W W' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (v : W ⟶ W')
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op A)).obj W)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X A W' (derivedHomGlobalMap X (𝟙 A) v x) =
      derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X A W x ≫ v
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality in the target variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_bifunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA globally is natural in both variables.** For arbitrary morphisms `f : L' ⟶ L`
and `g : M ⟶ M'` of `D(O)`, the identification of the degree-zero global hypercohomology of
`RSheafHom(L, M)` with `Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` carries the derived internal Hom of `f` and `g` to
precomposition with `f` and postcomposition with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_bifunctor
    {L L' M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (f : L' ⟶ L) (g : M ⟶ M')
    (z : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L' M'
        ((derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsFunctor X).map
          ((f.op, g) : ((op L, M) :
            (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))ᵒᵖ ×
              DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) ⟶
            (op L', M')) z) =
      f ≫ derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L M z ≫ g
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality in both variables

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA globally.** For arbitrary objects `L`, `M` of `D(O)` the degree-zero global
hypercohomology of the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(L, M)` is the group of morphisms
`L ⟶ M` in the derived category of `O`-modules.

A K-injective complex representing `M` and a K-flat complex representing `L` are chosen; the
internal Hom complex between them is K-injective by Stacks 0A96, so global sections compute
derived global sections and the degree-zero cohomology is the group of derived-category
morphisms, by Stacks 0A94.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u) ≃+ (L ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA over an object of the site.** For arbitrary objects `L`, `M` of `D(O)` the
degree-zero hypercohomology over `U` of the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(L, M)` is the
group of morphisms `L|_U ⟶ M|_U` in the derived category of `O|_U`-modules.

A K-injective complex representing `M` and a K-flat complex representing `L` are chosen; the
internal Hom complex between them is K-injective by Stacks 0A96, so sections compute derived
sections and the degree-zero cohomology is the group of derived-category morphisms between
the restrictions, by Stacks 0A94.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u) ≃+
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj L ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)
declarations.comment: sections over an object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA over an object of the site is natural in both variables.** For arbitrary
morphisms `f : L' ⟶ L` and `g : M ⟶ M'` of `D(O)`, the identification of the degree-zero
hypercohomology over `U` of `RSheafHom(L, M)` with `Hom_{D(O|_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)` carries the
derived internal Hom of `f` and `g` to precomposition with `f|_U` and postcomposition with
`g|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv_naturality
    {L L' M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (f : L' ⟶ L) (g : M ⟶ M')
    (z : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv X U L' M'
        ((derivedSheafHomSectionsFunctor X U).map
          ((f.op, g) : ((op L, M) :
              (DerivedCategory
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))ᵒᵖ ×
              DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) ⟶
              (op L', M')) z) =
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        U).mapDerivedCategory.map f ≫
        derivedSheafHomSectionsEquiv X U L M z ≫
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            U).mapDerivedCategory.map g
declarations.comment: sections over an object, naturality in both variables

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_source_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA, naturality in the source variable.** For objects `L'`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` and
an arbitrary morphism `u : L' ⟶ L`, the identification of the degree-zero global
hypercohomology of `RSheafHom(L, M)` with `Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` carries the contravariant
functoriality of the derived internal Hom to precomposition with `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_source_homologyMap
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (u : L' ⟶ L)
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L' M
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).map
            (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map u.op).app M)) x) =
      u ≫ derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L M x
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JA, naturality in the target variable.** For objects `L`, `M`, `M'` of `D(O)` and
an arbitrary morphism `φ : M ⟶ M'`, the identification of the degree-zero global
hypercohomology of `RSheafHom(L, M)` with `Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` carries the covariant
functoriality of the derived internal Hom to postcomposition with `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (φ : M ⟶ M')
    (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M)) : Type u)) :
    derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L M'
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).map
            (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).map φ)) x) =
      derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv X L M x ≫ φ
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality in the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E, the cohomology of the global derived hom in every degree.** The degree-`n`
cohomology of `RHom_O(K, L)` is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ L[n]` in `D(O)`, that is the
`Ext`-group `Ext^n_{D(O)}(K, L)`. This is the abelian-group-valued reading
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHom` of the global derived hom.

The degree is moved into the covariant variable: the homology functors of the derived category
form a shift sequence, derived global sections commute with the translation, and the derived
internal Hom commutes with the translation in its covariant variable by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomTargetShiftIso`; in degree zero the cohomology is
the morphism group by Stacks 08JA, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        (((globalDerivedHom X).obj (op K)).obj L) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: global sections in every degree, via the translation in the covariant variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Hypercohomology in every degree is morphisms out of the structure sheaf.** For an object
`Z` of `D(O)` the hypercohomology group `H^n(C, Z)`, the degree-`n` homology of unbounded derived
global sections, is the group `Hom_{D(O)}(O[0], Z[n])`.

This is Tag 08JA at source the structure sheaf in every degree: derived global sections of the
identification `RSheafHom(O[0], Z) ≅ Z` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafHomIso` turn `H^n(C, Z)` into the degree-`n`
cohomology of the global derived hom `RHom_O(O[0], Z)`, which is `Hom(O[0], Z[n])` by Tag 0B6E
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv`). In degree zero it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
    (Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O))) (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj Z) : Type u) ≃+
      (derivedStructureSheaf X ⟶ Z⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: hypercohomology out of the structure sheaf in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Hypercohomology of a ringed space in every degree is morphisms out of the structure
sheaf.** For an object `Z` of `D(O_X)` the hypercohomology group `H^n(X, Z)`, the degree-`n`
homology of unbounded derived global sections, is `Hom_{D(O_X)}(O_X[0], Z[n])`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv` read at the
site of opens of `X`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
    (Z : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite Rc)).obj Z) : Type u) ≃+
      (RingedSite.derivedStructureSheaf (ringedSite Rc) ⟶ Z⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: hypercohomology of a ringed space out of the structure sheaf in every degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.DerivedHomRestriction.complexMap_apply
declarations.doc:
The component of the complex map restricts each local homogeneous map
along the iterated slice, as in the canonical comparison of Tag 0E8H.
declarations.statement:
theorem DerivedHomRestriction.complexMap_apply
    (r : DerivedHomRestriction X U)
    (A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (V : (Over U)ᵒᵖ) (W : (Over V.unop)ᵒᵖ)
    (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q)
    (s : ((sheafHomComplex X A B).obj.X n).val.obj (op V.unop.left))
    (x : ((restrictComplex (X.over U)
      (restrictComplex X A U) V.unop).X p).val.obj W) :
    (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
      (((sheafHomComplex (X.over U)
        (restrictComplex X A U) (restrictComplex X B U)).sectionsIso V.unop).hom.f n)
      (((r.complexMap A B).f n).val.app V s)).v p q hpq).val.app W x) =
      (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
        (((sheafHomComplex X A B).sectionsIso V.unop.left).hom.f n) s).v p q hpq).val.app
          (op (Over.mk W.unop.hom.left)) x)
declarations.comment: restriction on local homogeneous cochains

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedHom_restriction_exists
declarations.doc:
Derived internal Hom commutes, naturally in both arguments, with
restriction to the slice site over any object.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHom_restriction_exists :
    Nonempty (DerivedHomRestriction X U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedHomRestriction_complexMap_isRestriction
declarations.doc:
Restriction of internal-Hom complexes is induced on every homogeneous
component by the canonical internal-Hom restriction isomorphism of Tag 0E8H.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomRestriction_complexMap_isRestriction
    (A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    IsInternalHomRestrictionMap X U A B
      ((derivedHomRestriction X U).complexMap A B)
declarations.comment: restriction of internal-Hom complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedHomRestriction_model
declarations.doc:
Under the fixed K-injective and exact-restriction comparisons, the full
derived comparison is the localization of the restriction map of internal-Hom
complexes induced by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.internalHomOverIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomRestriction_model
    (A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) [B.IsKInjective] :
    ((derivedHomRestriction X U).iso
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)).hom ≫
        (restrictionTargetComparison X U A B).hom =
      (restrictionSourceComparison X U A B).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((derivedHomRestriction X U).complexMap A B)
declarations.comment: canonical model characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JC, contravariant variable.**  The derived internal Hom into a fixed object carries
a distinguished triangle of `D(O)` to a distinguished triangle: for any distinguished `T` and any
`E`, the two morphisms `RSheafHom(T.obj₃, E) ⟶ RSheafHom(T.obj₂, E) ⟶ RSheafHom(T.obj₁, E)`
induced by `T.mor₂` and `T.mor₁` extend by a connecting morphism to a distinguished triangle.

Every distinguished triangle is presented by a termwise split short exact sequence of complexes,
so this follows from
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom_of_ses_obj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (T : Triangle
      (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang
      (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    ∃ δ : ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).obj (op T.obj₁) ⟶
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).obj (op T.obj₃))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).map T.mor₂.op)
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).map T.mor₁.op)
        δ ∈ distTriang
          (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
declarations.comment: contravariant variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom_second
declarations.doc:
The derived internal Hom out of a fixed object carries a distinguished triangle of `D(O)` to
a distinguished triangle: for any distinguished `T` and any `E`, the two morphisms
`RSheafHom(E, T.obj₁) ⟶ RSheafHom(E, T.obj₂) ⟶ RSheafHom(E, T.obj₃)` induced by `T.mor₁` and
`T.mor₂` extend by a connecting morphism to a distinguished triangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom_second
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (T : Triangle
      (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang
      (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    ∃ δ : ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op E)).obj T.obj₃ ⟶
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op E)).obj T.obj₁)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op E)).map T.mor₁)
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op E)).map T.mor₂)
        δ ∈ distTriang
          (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
declarations.comment: covariant variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The map of Stacks 08JD on degree-zero global hypercohomology is natural in `M`.** For
`m : M ⟶ M'` the map `H⁰(C, M ⊗^L_O L^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap` carries the map induced by `m`
on the left to postcomposition with `m` on the right.

That map is the degree-zero global hypercohomology of the canonical map
`M ⊗^L_O L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)` followed by Stacks 08JA, so this is the naturality in `M` of
those two pieces: `derivedTensorDualSectionsMap_naturality` for the first, and
`derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv_naturality_target` above for the second. No bijectivity of the
map, hence no perfectness of `L`, is involved: this is functoriality of the comparison of Stacks
08JD, not Stacks 08DQ.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap_naturality
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (m : M ⟶ M')
    (z : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
        ((T.tensor.obj M).obj (derivedDual X L))) : Type u)) :
    derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap X T L M'
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).map
            ((T.tensor.map m).app (derivedDual X L))) z) =
      derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap X T L M z ≫ m
declarations.comment: functoriality in M of the map on degree-zero derived global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JD: the canonical map `M ⊗^L_O L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)`.** It is the composition
morphism of derived internal Homs of Stacks 0A98, taken at intermediate object the structure
sheaf, after the left tensor factor `M` has been identified with `RSheafHom(O, M)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualToSheafHom
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (T.tensor.obj M).obj (derivedDual X L) ⟶
      ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj M
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JD: the canonical map on degree-zero global hypercohomology.** The canonical map
`M ⊗^L_O L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)` induces a map of abelian groups

`H⁰(C, M ⊗^L_O L^∨) ⟶ Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)`,

namely its degree-zero global hypercohomology followed by the identification
`H⁰(C, RSheafHom(L, M)) ≅ Hom_{D(O)}(L, M)` of Stacks 08JA.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
          ((T.tensor.obj M).obj (derivedDual X L))) : Type u) →+ (L ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: map on degree-zero derived global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JF: the canonical map `Lh^* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(Lh^* K, Lh^* L)`** in
`D(O)`, for a morphism of ringed topoi `h : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')` and objects `K`, `L` of
`D(O')`. It is the arrow corresponding to `derivedPullbackSheafHomPairing` under the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08J8 on the source topos.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackSheafHomMap :
    (derivedPullback h).obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
          (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).obj (op K)).obj L) ⟶
      ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj
        (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JF: the canonical map `Lh^* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(Lh^* K, Lh^* L)`** in
`D(O)`, for a morphism of ringed topoi `h : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')` in the sense of
Stacks 01D3, part (2), and objects `K`, `L` of `D(O')`. It is the arrow corresponding to
`derivedPullbackSheafHomPairing` under the tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08J8.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackSheafHomMap :
    (derivedPullback h).obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
          (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).obj (op K)).obj L) ⟶
      ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj
        (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of ringed topoi in the sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) -- a morphism
of the underlying topoi together with the map of structure sheaves, with no functor between the
underlying sites

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOnTopoi.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
The base change map for the internal hom in the derived category (Stacks 08JG), for a square
of morphisms of sites.  For a
commutative square of ringed topoi with `h : (Sh(C'), O_{C'}) ⟶ (Sh(C), O_C)` over
`g : (Sh(D'), O_{D'}) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` and objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_C)`, the canonical map

`Lg^* Rf_* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ R(f')_* RSheafHom(Lh^* K, Lh^* L)`

in `D(O_{D'})`.  It is the derived base change map of Stacks 07A7 at `RSheafHom(K, L)` followed
by `R(f')_*` of the canonical map of Stacks 08JF, which is the adjoint of the three-step
composition the source describes.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap :
    (derivedPullback g).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f').obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C')).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L))
declarations.comment:
derived_base_change_sheaf_hom_map, variant: the special case of a square of
morphisms of ringed topoi presented by morphisms of sites; the tag for an arbitrary commutative
square of morphisms of ringed topoi is
Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOnTopoi.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The adjoint characterization of the base change map (Stacks 08JG), for a square of morphisms
of sites.  Under the derived adjunction
`L(f')^* ⊣ R(f')_*` of Stacks 07A6, the base change map for the internal hom is the three-step
composition the source prescribes: the two identifications of the iterated derived pullbacks
around the square with the derived pullback along its common composite, then the derived
pullback along `h` of the derived counit `Lf^* Rf_* ⟶ id` at `RSheafHom(K, L)`, then the
canonical map of Stacks 08JF.

Since transposition is a bijection this determines the map.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint :
    ((derivedAdjunction f' hmosf').homEquiv
        ((derivedPullback g).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)))
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C')).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L))).symm
        (derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap f h f' g hmosf hmosh hmosf' hmosg sq K L) =
      (derivedPullbackCompIsoLeft f' g hmosf' hmosg).hom.app
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj
            (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
              (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        (derivedPullbackCompIsoRight f h f' g hmosf hmosh sq).inv.app
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj
            (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
              (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        (derivedPullback h).map ((derivedAdjunction f hmosf).counit.app
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        RingedToposSiteHom.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap h hmosh K L
declarations.comment:
derived_base_change_sheaf_hom_map: adjoint characterization, variant: the special
case of a square of morphisms of ringed topoi presented by morphisms of sites; the tag for an
arbitrary commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi is
Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JG: the base change map for the internal hom in the derived category.**  For a
commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi, with `h : (Sh(C'), O_{C'}) ⟶ (Sh(C), O_C)`
over `g : (Sh(D'), O_{D'}) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)`, and objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_C)`, the canonical map

`Lg^* Rf_* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ R(f')_* RSheafHom(Lh^* K, Lh^* L)`

in `D(O_{D'})`: the derived base change map of Stacks 07A7 at `RSheafHom(K, L)` followed by
`R(f')_*` of the canonical map of Stacks 08JF.  Its transpose is the three-step composition of
the source, `derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap :
    (derivedPullback g).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f').obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C')).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L))
declarations.comment:
for a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi in the sense of Tag 01D3,
part (2), with no hypothesis beyond commutativity

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JG, the adjoint characterization.**  Under the derived adjunction
`L(f')^* ⊣ R(f')_*` of Stacks 07A6, the base change map for the internal hom is the composition
the source prescribes: the identification `L(f')^* Lg^* = Lh^* Lf^*` of the iterated derived
pullbacks around the square (through the derived pullback along its common composite), then
`Lh^*` of the derived counit `Lf^* Rf_* ⟶ id` at `RSheafHom(K, L)`, then the canonical map of
Stacks 08JF.  Since transposition is a bijection this determines the map.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap_adjoint :
    ((derivedAdjunction f').homEquiv
        ((derivedPullback g).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)))
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C')).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback h).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback h).obj L))).symm
        (derivedBaseChangeSheafHomMap f h f' g sq K L) =
      (derivedPullbackCompIsoLeft f' g).hom.app
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj
            (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
              (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        (derivedPullbackCompIsoRight f h f' g sq).inv.app
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj
            (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
              (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        (derivedPullback h).map ((derivedAdjunction f).counit.app
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite C)).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        RingedToposHom.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap h K L
declarations.comment:
adjoint characterization, for a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi in
the sense of Tag 01D3, part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JH**, the representation statement. For `E` strictly perfect — bounded, with
every term a direct summand of a finite free `O`-module — the derived internal Hom
`RSheafHom(E, F)` is represented by the ordinary internal Hom complex `SheafHom(E, F)` of
Stacks 0A8Z, the comparison being the canonical one.

By `strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_iff` this is the quasi-isomorphy of the map of internal
Hom complexes induced by the K-injective augmentation of the target, which is
`homMap_quasiIso_of_isFiniteFreeSummand`.

The degreewise direct-sum description of that complex, the other half of Stacks 08JH, is
`strictlyPerfectHomDegreeIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso
    (hbdd : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (E.X i)}.Finite)
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteFreeSummand X (E.X i)) :
    IsIso (strictlyPerfectHomComparison X D E F)
declarations.comment: representation by the finite direct-sum Hom complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.strictlyPerfectHomDegreeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JH**, degreewise statement. For `E` bounded, the `n`-th term of the internal Hom
complex `SheafHom(E, F)` of Stacks 0A8Z is the direct sum, over `q : ℤ`, of the internal Hom
sheaves `SheafHom(E^{-q}, F^{n-q})`.

By `homDegreeIsLimit` the term is the *product* of those sheaves, with no hypothesis on `E`.
Boundedness makes `E^{-q}` vanish outside a finite set of `q`, hence each summand vanish there
by `internalHomSheaf_isZero_of_isZero`, and `productCoproductIsoOfFiniteSupport` then
identifies the product with the coproduct.

The source lemma assumes `E` strictly perfect; boundedness is the `bounded` field of that
condition and the only part used, so this is the source statement generalized. See the
implementation notes for why the strict-perfectness predicate cannot be named at these
universes.

The differential needs no separate description: that it is the standard Hom-complex
differential is part of the data of `SheafHomComplex`, whose `sectionsIso` is an isomorphism
of complexes onto `CochainComplex.HomComplex` on every slice site.
declarations.statement:
def strictlyPerfectHomDegreeIso
    (E F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hE : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (E.X i)}.Finite) (n : ℤ) :
    ((sheafHomComplex X E F).obj.X n) ≅
      ∐ (fun q : ℤ => internalHomSheaf X (E.X (-q)) (F.X (n - q)))
declarations.comment: finite direct-sum terms and Hom differential

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.boundedAboveHomRepresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JI**, the whole statement. Let `E` be a complex of `O`-modules vanishing above
`b` all of whose terms are direct summands of finite free `O`-modules, and let `F` be a complex
of `O`-modules vanishing below `a`. Then the derived internal Hom `RSheafHom(E, F)` is
represented by the internal Hom complex `H = SheafHom(E, F)` of Stacks 0A8Z — the comparison
being the canonical `strictlyPerfectHomComparison` — and that complex has
`H^n = ⨁_{n = p + q} SheafHom(E^{-q}, F^p)` in every degree.

The two components are exactly the two assertions of the source, and neither is restated here:
the first is `strictlyPerfectHomComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove`, the library's Stacks 08I5, at
exactly the hypotheses of Stacks 08JI; the second is `boundedAboveHomDegreeIso`. The differential
needs no separate component; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
def boundedAboveHomRepresentation (D : DerivedInternalHom.{u, d} X) (a b : ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (F.X i)) (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteFreeSummand X (E.X i)) :
    Σ' _ : IsIso (strictlyPerfectHomComparison X D E F),
      ∀ n : ℤ, (sheafHomComplex X E F).obj.X n ≅
        ∐ (fun q : ℤ => internalHomSheaf X (E.X (-q)) (F.X (n - q)))
declarations.comment: derived internal Hom represented by the Hom complex, with finite direct-sum terms

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_tensorDualToSheafHom_of_localSummand
declarations.doc:
**Step (5) of the proof of Stacks 08JJ.** Let `(C, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `E` be a sheaf of
`𝒪`-modules which is locally a direct summand of a finite free sheaf of modules, and let `F` be an
arbitrary sheaf of `𝒪`-modules. Then the canonical map

`F ⊗_𝒪 SheafHom(E, 𝒪) ⟶ SheafHom(E, F)`

is an isomorphism.

The map is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToSheafHom`, pinned down on local sections by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToSheafHom_toTensorSheafSection`. At `E = F` this is the first
assertion of Tag 0FNY, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism_of_localSummand`.

The hypothesis is the one of Tag 0FNY, that `E` is a summand of a finite free module *locally*;
Stacks 08JJ's step (5) asks for a global summand, which is a special case.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorDualToSheafHom_of_localSummand
    (hE : IsLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree 𝒪 h𝒪 E) :
    IsIso (tensorDualToSheafHom 𝒪 h𝒪 E F)
declarations.comment:
step (5) of the proof only: the canonical map
`F ⊗_𝒪 SheafHom(E, 𝒪) ⟶ SheafHom(E, F)` is an isomorphism for `E` locally a summand of a finite
free module and `F` arbitrary. None of the tag's four assertions is proved here; in particular
the derived statement `M ⊗^L_𝒪 K^∨ ≅ RSheafHom(K, M)` for perfect `K` is not, and still needs a
complex-level comparison with its Koszul signs, the tensor-side analogue of Tag 08JH, locality
of the derived tensor product on a slice, and a K-flat representative on a ringed site.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedSheafHomEvaluation_of_coversTop
declarations.doc:
**Invertibility of the evaluation morphism of derived internal Homs is local on the site.**
Let `V : ι → C` be a family of objects covering the final object of the site, let `A` be a K-flat
complex representing `K`, and let `B` and `C` be K-injective complexes representing `L` and `M`.
If the evaluation morphism of internal Hom complexes of Stacks 0A92 formed over each `V i`, at
the restrictions of `A`, `B` and `C`, is a quasi-isomorphism, then the evaluation morphism of
derived internal Homs of Stacks 0A97 at `K`, `L`, `M` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedSheafHomEvaluation_of_coversTop
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {A B C : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    (hA : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O A) [B.IsKInjective] [C.IsKInjective]
    (eA : DerivedCategory.Q.obj A ≅ K) (eB : DerivedCategory.Q.obj B ≅ L)
    (eC : DerivedCategory.Q.obj C ≅ M)
    {ι : Type*} {V : ι → X.C} (hV : X.J.CoversTop V)
    (h : ∀ i, QuasiIso (evaluationMap (X.over (V i)) (restrictComplex X A (V i))
      (restrictComplex X B (V i)) (restrictComplex X C (V i)))) :
    IsIso (derivedSheafHomEvaluation X T Hd K L M)
declarations.comment: the locality step for the evaluation morphism of Tag 0A97 only: invertibility of `ev : RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_O K ⟶ RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, L), M)`, and hence of the bidual map `K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedBidual`, may be checked after restriction to the slices over a family of objects covering the final object, where it becomes quasi-isomorphy of the evaluation morphism of internal Hom complexes of Tag 0A92. NONE of the four assertions of Tag 08JJ is proved here and in particular the bidual map is NOT shown to be invertible for a perfect K: quasi-isomorphy over each member of the covering family is a HYPOTHESIS below. The base case that discharges it — that `evaluationMap` is a quasi-isomorphism when its source complex is strictly perfect (Tag 08FL) — is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.quasiIso_evaluationMap_of_isStrictlyPerfect`, and the second assertion of Tag 08JJ follows from the two together, in `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedBidual_of_isPerfect`. The reduction performed here is the same one `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_of_coversTop_mapDerivedCategory` performs for an arbitrary morphism of `D(Mod(O))`, but carried out at the chain level, because the derived evaluation morphism has no restriction compatibility of its own; the chain-level square it uses is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.evaluationMap_restrict_square`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedBidual_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**The bidual map of a perfect object is an isomorphism.** For a perfect object
`K` of `D(O)` the canonical map

`K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedBidual` is an isomorphism, where `K^∨` is the derived
dual `RSheafHom(K, O)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBidual_of_isPerfect
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedBidual X T K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` is an isomorphism for a perfect object `K` of `D(O)`, where `K^∨` is the derived dual `RSheafHom_O(K, O)`; this is one of the four assertions of the tag, and the hypothesis is perfection of `K` alone

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_derivedDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JJ, first assertion.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `K` be a perfect
object of `D(O)`. Then the dual `K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O)` is perfect as well.

Perfectness is local, so it is enough to model `K^∨` above a covering of each object of the
site. Over a member `V` on which `K` is modelled by a strictly perfect complex `E`, the
restriction of `K^∨` is `RSheafHom(K|_V, O|_V)` by Stacks 08JB, which is the class of the
internal Hom complex `SheafHom(E, O|_V)` by Stacks 08JH; and that complex is strictly perfect
because the dual of a direct summand of a finite free module is again one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedDual
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) : X.IsPerfect (derivedDual X K)
declarations.comment: the dual of a perfect object is perfect

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JJ: tensoring with the dual of a perfect object is derived internal Hom.** Let
`(C, O)` be a ringed site, let `K` be a perfect object of `D(O)` with dual
`K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O)`, and let `M` be an arbitrary object of `D(O)`. Then

`M ⊗^L_O K^∨ ≅ RSheafHom_O(K, M)`.

It is the diagonal morphism of Stacks 0BYS at tensor factor `M`, internal-Hom source `K` and
target the structure sheaf in degree zero — invertible by Stacks 0ATN because `K` is perfect,
its source being `M ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(K, O) = M ⊗^L_O K^∨` — followed by the internal Hom out of
`K` of the right unit constraint `M ⊗^L_O O ≅ M` of Stacks 0FPT.
declarations.statement:
def derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj M).obj (derivedDual X K) ≅
      ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).obj M
declarations.comment: the isomorphism M ⊗^L_O K^∨ ≅ RSheafHom_O(K, M) for perfect K; not the invertibility of the canonical map of Stacks 08JD, which is a different morphism of the same type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JJ: the isomorphism is functorial in `M`.** This is the functoriality the source
asserts: the diagonal of Stacks 0BYS is natural in its tensor factor and the right unit
constraint of Stacks 0FPT is natural, so the composite of the two is.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso_naturality
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K)
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (f : M ⟶ M') :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map f).app (derivedDual X K) ≫
        (derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso X K M' hK).hom =
      (derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso X K M hK).hom ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).map f
declarations.comment: that isomorphism is functorial in M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualTensorGlobalSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JJ: `H⁰(C, M ⊗^L_O K^∨) = Hom_{D(O)}(K, M)` for perfect `K`.** The degree-zero
global hypercohomology of `M ⊗^L_O K^∨` is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ M` in `D(O)`.

It is the degree-zero global hypercohomology of `derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso`, which is an
isomorphism of abelian groups because derived global sections and the degree-zero cohomology
functor both preserve isomorphisms, followed by the identification
`H⁰(C, RSheafHom(K, M)) = Hom_{D(O)}(K, M)` of Stacks 08JA.
declarations.statement:
def derivedDualTensorGlobalSectionsEquiv
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj M).obj
            (derivedDual X K))) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: the identification H⁰(C, M ⊗^L_O K^∨) = Hom_{D(O)}(K, M) for perfect K, as an isomorphism of abelian groups; not the bijectivity of the induced map of Stacks 08JD

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JJ, third assertion, for the canonical map of Stacks 08JD.** Let `(C, O)` be a
ringed site, let `L` be a **perfect** object of `D(O)` with dual `L^∨ = RSheafHom(L, O)` and let
`M` be an arbitrary object of `D(O)`. Then the canonical map

`M ⊗^L_O L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(L, M)`

of Stacks 08JD, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom`, is an isomorphism.

The isomorphism itself was already in the library as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualTensorSheafHomIso`, the diagonal of Stacks 0BYS at
target object the structure sheaf; what is proved here is that the *canonical* map of
Stacks 08JD is that diagonal, so that the invertibility supplied by Stacks 0ATN applies to it.
The comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_comp_derivedSheafHomComparison`, whose
chain-level content is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorHomInterchange_comp_homMap`: the
interchange morphism of Stacks 0BYR is the diagonal of Stacks 0A93 tensored with the identity
followed by the composition morphism of Stacks 0A91, so no Koszul sign separates the two
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect_canonical
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hL : X.IsPerfect L) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X) L M)
declarations.comment: the canonical map M ⊗^L_O L^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom_O(L, M) of Stacks 08JD is an isomorphism for a perfect L

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_of_coversTop_mapDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Invertibility in the derived category of sheaves of modules is local on the site.** Let
`V : ι → C` be a family of objects covering the final object of the site. A morphism of
`D(Mod(R))` whose image under restriction to the slice site over each `V i` is an isomorphism
is itself an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_coversTop_mapDerivedCategory {ι : Type*} {V : ι → C} (hV : J.CoversTop V)
    {K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} R)} (f : K ⟶ L)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{w} R (V i)).mapDerivedCategory.map f)) :
    IsIso f
declarations.comment:
the locality step of the proof only: invertibility of a morphism of `D(Mod(O))`
may be checked after restriction to the slices over a family of objects covering the final
object. Stacks 08JJ uses this reduction twice, for the bidual map `K ⟶ (K^∨)^∨` and for the
canonical map `M ⊗^L_O K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom_O(K, M)`; neither of those maps is shown to be an
isomorphism here, and none of the tag's four assertions is proved here.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JK, the distinguished triangle.**  This declaration is the `@[stacks 08JK]`
registration of the first of the tag's two assertions, and it takes no hypothesis.

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let
`(U ⊆ X, j_V : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square on `X`, let `P = U ×_X V` and let
`a = f|_U`, `b = f|_V`, `c = f|_P` be the restrictions of `f` to the three.  Let `Rf_*`,
`Ra_*((-)|_U)`, `Rb_*((-)|_V)` and `Rc_*((-)|_P)` be right derived functors of `f_*`,
`a_*((-)|_U)`, `b_*((-)|_V)` and `c_*((-)|_P)`, with their comparisons.  Then every object `E`
of `D(𝒪_X)` sits in a distinguished triangle

`Rf_*E ⟶ Ra_*(E|_U) ⊕ Rb_*(E|_V) ⟶ Rc_*(E|_{U ×_X V}) ⟶ (Rf_*E)[1]`

in `D(𝒪_Y)`.

The conclusion is that of the untagged
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris` verbatim, with that
statement's one hypothesis discharged by a route the source does not take.  The source
deduces the direct-image Mayer–Vietoris sequence of Stacks 08GW part (1) at every module, and
gets surjectivity on the right from the étale-local vanishing of an obstruction class.  Only the
sequence at an *injective* module is used here — the representative of `E` may be taken
termwise injective, by Stacks 079P — and there the obstruction vanishes for a formal reason:
`CategoryTheory.PushforwardMayerVietoris.epi_conjugate_of_injective` splits the sequence by
extending a counit along the monomorphism that part (1) of Stacks 08GV provides
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_edsShriekMayerVietoris`).  So nothing beyond Stacks 08GV
part (1), which the library proves, and Stacks 079P is needed.

The three extensions by zero are the ones the library constructs,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleLowerShriek`, with their adjunctions; nothing about them is
assumed, and they do not appear in the statement.  The five morphisms are existentially
quantified at each `E`; the tag's second assertion, that the triangle is in addition
*functorial in `E`*, is registered on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_natTrans_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_`
`unconditional` in the sibling module.  Those two declarations are the only two
`@[stacks 08JK]` registrations.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional
    (RX RU RV RP : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2))
    (αX : (modulePushforward B S hS f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RX)
    (αU : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsOpenHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RU)
    (αV : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RV)
    (αP : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsInterHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsInterHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsInterHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RP)
    (hRX : RX.IsRightDerivedFunctor αX
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRU : RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor αU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRV : RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor αV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRP : RP.IsRightDerivedFunctor αP
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2)) :
    ∃ (fU : RX.obj E ⟶ RU.obj E) (fV : RX.obj E ⟶ RV.obj E) (gU : RU.obj E ⟶ RP.obj E)
      (gV : RV.obj E ⟶ RP.obj E) (δ : RP.obj E ⟶ (RX.obj E)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk (biprod.lift fU fV) (biprod.desc gU (-gV)) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2))
declarations.comment:
FIRST ASSERTION: for every E of D(O_X) a distinguished triangle
Rf_*E -> Ra_*(E|_U) ⊕ Rb_*(E|_V) -> Rc_*(E|_{U x_X V}) -> (Rf_*E)[1] in D(O_Y), with no
hypothesis beyond the square, f and the four derived functors. The SECOND ASSERTION,
functoriality in E, is exists_natTrans_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional in
the sibling module. Proof route and provenance are in this theorem's docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_natTrans_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JK, the functoriality in `E`.**

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let
`(U ⊆ X, j_V : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square on `X`, let `P = U ×_X V`, and let
`Rf_*`, `Ra_*((-)|_U)`, `Rb_*((-)|_V)`, `Rc_*((-)|_P)` be right derived functors of the four
functors of the square, with their comparisons.  Then the five morphisms of the Mayer–Vietoris
triangle

`Rf_*E ⟶ Ra_*(E|_U) ⊕ Rb_*(E|_V) ⟶ Rc_*(E|_{U ×_X V}) ⟶ (Rf_*E)[1]`

are **natural transformations** of the four derived functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_Y)`, and the triangle
is distinguished at every object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)`.  So a morphism `φ : E ⟶ E'` induces a
morphism of the two triangles.

The direct-image Mayer–Vietoris sequence is used only at *injective* modules — the functorial
resolution of Stacks 079P is termwise injective — where it is proved from part (1) of
Stacks 08GV: `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_edsRestrictPushMayerVietoris_of_injective`.  The
first assertion of Stacks 08JK is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_natTrans_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional
    (RX RU RV RP : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2))
    (αX : (modulePushforward B S hS f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RX)
    (αU : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsOpenHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RU)
    (αV : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RV)
    (αP : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (edsInterHom B S hS hsq)
          (isEtale_edsInterHom B S hS hsq) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS (edsInterHom B S hS hsq ≫ f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RP)
    (hRX : RX.IsRightDerivedFunctor αX
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRU : RU.IsRightDerivedFunctor αU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRV : RV.IsRightDerivedFunctor αV
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hRP : RP.IsRightDerivedFunctor αP
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ (fU : RX ⟶ RU) (fV : RX ⟶ RV) (gU : RU ⟶ RP) (gV : RV ⟶ RP)
      (δ : RP ⟶ RX ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2)) (1 : ℤ)),
      ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2),
        Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (fU.app E) (fV.app E))
            (biprod.desc (gU.app E) (-(gV.app E))) (δ.app E) ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2))
declarations.comment:
SECOND ASSERTION: the distinguished triangle is FUNCTORIAL IN E. The five
morphisms are natural transformations of the four right derived functors D(O_X) -> D(O_Y) and
the triangle is distinguished at EVERY E, with no hypothesis beyond the square, f and those
functors. The FIRST ASSERTION is exists_mem_distTriang_edsRelativeMayerVietoris_unconditional in
the sibling module. Proof route and provenance are in this theorem's docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JL, first assertion.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be an algebraic space over
`S` and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_F)`.  If `E` is `n`-pseudo-coherent, then `Hⁱ(E)` is a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-module for every `i > n`.

The second assertion of the tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_of_isPseudoCoherent_unconditional`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom` with
its two closure hypotheses discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels_over` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderCokernels_over`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_unconditional
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (n i : ℤ)
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E n) (hi : n < i) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: cohomology above the approximation degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_of_isPseudoCoherent_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JL, second assertion.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be an algebraic space over
`S` and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_F)`.  If `E` is pseudo-coherent, then `E` lies in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`, that is, every cohomology sheaf of `E` is quasi-coherent.

The conclusion is the object property whose full subcategory is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentDerivedCategory`, the `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` of Stacks 071X.  The
first assertion of the tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom_unconditional`.

Apply the first assertion in degree `i` using a strictly perfect approximation from degree
`i - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_of_isPseudoCoherent_unconditional
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).IsPseudoCoherent E) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))) E
declarations.comment: pseudo-coherent objects lie in the quasi-coherent derived category
