declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap_and_not_forall_isIso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces,
`E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢^•` a complex of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, each `𝒢^n` flat over `Y`. For
every cartesian square, the base change map
`Lg^*Rf_*R𝓗om(E, 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*R𝓗om(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢^•)` is an isomorphism if

1. `E` is perfect and `𝒢^•` is bounded above (the source's part (1), at its hypotheses), or
2. `E` is pseudo-coherent, `𝒢^•` is bounded, and `g` has finite Tor dimension.

Part (2) as printed, for an arbitrary base change `g`, is false, and the third conjunct proves
it: it fails for `X = Y = Spec ℤ/4`, `f = id`, `E = (ℤ/4 ⧸ 2)^~`, `𝒢^• = 𝒪_X` and
`g = g' : Spec ℤ/2 ⟶ Spec ℤ/4`, where the source of the map lies in `D^{≤ 0}` (`ℤ/4` is
self-injective) and the target has nonzero cohomology in degree `1`
(`not_forall_isIso_smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent`, in the namespace
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafHomBaseChangeCounterexample`). The source proves (2) through
Stacks 0DKH and 0DKI (3); Stacks 0DKI (3) needs `g` of finite Tor dimension, and with that
condition the proof goes through
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap_of_isPseudoCoherent`). The
morphism `Spec ℤ/2 ⟶ Spec ℤ/4` of the counterexample does not have finite Tor dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap_and_not_forall_isIso
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)) ℤ)
    (hq : ∀ n, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hfl : ∀ n, IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom (G.X n)) :
    (RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E →
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i, b < i → IsZero (G.X i)) →
      ∀ {X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso (smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq.w E G)) ∧
    (RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E →
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i, (i < a ∨ b < i) → IsZero (G.X i)) →
      ∀ {X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g), HasFiniteTorDimension g →
        IsIso (smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq.w E G)) ∧
    ¬ ∀ {B : BigFppfSite.{0}} {S : Scheme.{0}} {hS : B.Contains S} {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
      (f : X ⟶ Y), IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom → IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom →
      ∀ (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X))),
        RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E →
      ∀ (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{0} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)) ℤ),
        (∀ n, (G.X n).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) → (∀ n, IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom (G.X n)) →
        (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i, (i < a ∨ b < i) → IsZero (G.X i)) →
      ∀ {X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso (smallEtaleDerivedSheafHomBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq.w E G)
declarations.comment: erratum: as printed, part (2) (E pseudo-coherent, G bounded and flat over Y, an arbitrary base change g) is false, refuted for X = Y = Spec Z/4, f = id, E = (Z/4/2)~, G = O_X and g the closed point Spec Z/2 -> Spec Z/4 (third conjunct); it holds when g has finite Tor dimension (second conjunct); part (1) holds as printed (first conjunct)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPseudoCoherent_extAddEquiv_tensorPullbackComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JR, part (B).**  Let `S` be a scheme and `f : X ⟶ B` a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` with `B` Noetherian and `f` locally of finite type and quasi-separated.  Let
`E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` (coherent cohomology sheaves, bounded above) and let `𝒢^•` be a bounded
complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `B`, with support proper over `B`.  Then there is a
pseudo-coherent `L ∈ D(𝒪_B)` with isomorphisms
`Ext^i_{𝒪_B}(L, ℱ) ≅ Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢^• ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*ℱ)` for quasi-coherent `𝒪_B`-modules `ℱ`,
functorial in `ℱ` and compatible with the boundary maps: for a short exact sequence
`0 → ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃ → 0` of quasi-coherent modules, the boundary map of the distinguished triangle
of `ℱ₁[0] → ℱ₂[0] → ℱ₃[0]` on the left corresponds to the boundary map of the distinguished
triangle of the short exact sequence of complexes
`0 → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₁ → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₂ → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ → 0` on the right.

Here `Ext^i(A, C) = Hom(A, C[i])` in the derived categories of the small étale ringed sites,
`ℱ[0]` is `DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0`, and `𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorPullbackComplex` at `ℱ` placed in degree `0`; the sequence of
complexes is written `ShortComplex.mk (ℱ₁[0] → ℱ₂[0]) (ℱ₂[0] → ℱ₃[0])` mapped by
`𝒢^• ⊗ f^*(-)`, exact by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_tensorPullbackComplex_map_single`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPseudoCoherent_extAddEquiv_tensorPullbackComplex (hTop : B.Contains
    (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop Y.1) (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hEcoh : ∀ q : ℤ, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj E))
    (hEb : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E)
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)) ℤ)
    (hG : FlatProperSupportComplex B S hS f hf G) :
    ∃ (L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2))
      (_ : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).IsPseudoCoherent L)
      (Φ : ∀ (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (i : ℤ),
        (L ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) 0).obj F)⟦i⟧) ≃+
          ShiftedHom E (tensorPullbackComplexDerived f G ((HomologicalComplex.single
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y))
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)) i),
      (∀ {F F' : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2} (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
        (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (q : F ⟶ F') (i : ℤ)
        (e : L ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) 0).obj F)⟦i⟧),
        Φ F' hF' i (e ≫ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) 0).map q)⟦i⟧') =
          Φ F hF i e ≫ (DerivedCategory.Q.map ((tensorPullbackComplex f G).map
            ((HomologicalComplex.single (SheafOfModules.{u}
            (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).map q)))⟦i⟧') ∧
      (∀ (T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)) (hT : T.ShortExact)
        (h₁ : T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite), T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        ∀ (h₃ : T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (i : ℤ)
        (e : ShiftedHom L ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) 0).obj T.X₃) i),
        Φ T.X₁ h₁ (i + 1) (e.comp hT.singleδ (add_comm 1 i)) =
          (Φ T.X₃ h₃ i e).comp (DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ
            (S := (ShortComplex.mk ((HomologicalComplex.single (SheafOfModules.{u}
            (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).map T.f)
            ((HomologicalComplex.single (SheafOfModules.{u}
            (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).map T.g)
            (single_map_comp_map_eq_zero B S hS T)).map (tensorPullbackComplex f G))
              (shortExact_tensorPullbackComplex_map_single
                (FlatProperSupportComplex.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS hG) hT))
              (add_comm 1 i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_tensorPullbackExtGroup_smallEtaleTensorCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JR, part (A).**  Let `S` be a scheme and `f : X ⟶ B` a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` with `B` Noetherian and `f` locally of finite type and quasi-separated.  Let
`E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` (coherent cohomology sheaves, bounded above) and let `𝒢^•` be a bounded
complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `B`, with support proper over `B`.  Then for every
`m ∈ ℤ` there are a perfect `K ∈ D(𝒪_B)` and maps
`α^i_ℱ : Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢^• ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*ℱ) ⟶ H^i(B, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_B} ℱ)` for quasi-coherent
`𝒪_B`-modules `ℱ`, functorial in `ℱ`, compatible with the boundary maps of short exact sequences
`0 → ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃ → 0` of quasi-coherent modules (on the left the boundary map of the
distinguished triangle of `0 → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₁ → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₂ → 𝒢^• ⊗ f^*ℱ₃ → 0`, on the right the
connecting map of the cohomology of `RΓ(B, K ⊗^L -)` of the triangle of `ℱ₁[0] → ℱ₂[0] → ℱ₃[0]`),
and invertible for `i ≤ m`.

Here `Ext^i(E, -) = Hom(E, -[i])` in `D(𝒪_X)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorPullbackExtGroup`),
`H^i(B, K ⊗^L ℱ)` is the `i`-th cohomology of derived global sections of `K ⊗^L ℱ[0]`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleTensorCohomology`), and the maps are morphisms of abelian
groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_tensorPullbackExtGroup_smallEtaleTensorCohomology
    (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop Y.1) (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hEcoh : ∀ q : ℤ, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj E))
    (hEb : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E)
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)) ℤ)
    (hG : FlatProperSupportComplex B S hS f hf G) (m : ℤ) :
    ∃ (K : smallEtaleModulesDerived B S hS Y) (_ : SmallEtaleIsPerfect B S hS K)
      (α : ∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y))
        (_ : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (i : ℤ),
        tensorPullbackExtGroup B S hS E f G F i ⟶ smallEtaleTensorCohomology B S hS K F i),
      (∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y))
        (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (i : ℤ), i ≤ m → IsIso (α F hF i)) ∧
      (∀ {F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)}
        (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (q : F ⟶ F') (i : ℤ),
        tensorPullbackExtGroupMap B S hS E f G q i ≫ α F' hF' i =
          α F hF i ≫ smallEtaleTensorCohomologyMap B S hS K q i) ∧
      (∀ (T : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)))
        (hT : T.ShortExact) (h₁ : T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
        (i j : ℤ) (h : i + 1 = j),
        tensorPullbackExtGroupDelta B S hS E f G T (shortExact_tensorPullbackComplex_map_single
            (FlatProperSupportComplex.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS hG) hT) i j h ≫
            α T.X₁ h₁ j =
          α T.X₃ h₃ i ≫ smallEtaleTensorCohomologyDelta B S hS K T hT i j h)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homSchemeFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JT.**  The relative Hom functor `Hom(F, G) : (Sch/base)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`: its value at a
test scheme `T` over the base is `Hom_{𝒪_{X_T}}(F_T, G_T)`, the homomorphisms of the two modules
pulled back to `X_T = X ×_{base} T`, and its action on a morphism of test schemes is pullback of
homomorphisms.  It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homOverSpaceFunctor` restricted to
the test schemes over the base; the pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU that
makes it a functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`.
declarations.statement: def homSchemeFunctor : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Hom functor on the schemes over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homSchemeFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JT.**  The value of the relative Hom functor at a test scheme `T` over the base
is the set of `𝒪_{X_T}`-module homomorphisms `F_T ⟶ G_T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homSchemeFunctor_obj (T : s.SchemesOver) :
    s.homSchemeFunctor.obj (Opposite.op T) = s.homAt T
declarations.comment: the value of the Hom functor at a scheme over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homSchemeFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JT.**  The action of the relative Hom functor on a morphism of test schemes is
pullback of homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem homSchemeFunctor_map {U T : s.SchemesOver} (g : U ⟶ T) :
    s.homSchemeFunctor.map (Opposite.op g) = TypeCat.ofHom (s.homMap g)
declarations.comment: the action of the Hom functor on a morphism of schemes over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homOverSpaceFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The relative Hom functor of Stacks 08JT, indexed by the algebraic spaces over the
base.**  Its value at `T ⟶ base` is `Hom_{𝒪_{X_T}}(F_T, G_T)` and its action is pullback of
homomorphisms.  The relative Hom functor on the test *schemes* over the base is this one
restricted along the inclusion of those into the algebraic spaces over the base.

The pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU, which makes pullback of
homomorphisms functorial, is supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`
and so is not a hypothesis.
declarations.statement: def homOverSpaceFunctor : (Over s.base)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Hom functor indexed by the algebraic spaces over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JT.**  The standing data of the relative Hom functor: a morphism `f : X ⟶ base`
of algebraic spaces over `S` and two quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement: structure HomSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.existsUnique_homMap_of_restrictionsAgree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JV.**  In the standing data of Stacks 08JT the relative Hom functor
`Hom(F, G)` satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology: for an fpqc covering
`{U i ⟶ T}` of test schemes over the base, a family of homomorphisms `F_{U i} ⟶ G_{U i}` whose
restrictions agree on the overlaps `X_{U i} ×_{X_T} X_{U j}` comes from a unique
homomorphism `F_T ⟶ G_T`.

This is the proof of the source.  The base changes `{X_{U i} ⟶ X_T}` form an fpqc covering of
`X_T` by Stacks 03MR, part (3), in the form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFpqcCovering_baseChangeMap`, and a compatible family of
homomorphisms of the inverse images of two quasi-coherent modules along an fpqc covering glues
uniquely, which is the gluing half of Stacks 04W8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_restrictPullbackHom_eq_of_isFpqcCovering`.  The
base-changed modules `F_T`,
`G_T` are quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_homMap_of_restrictionsAgree
    {I : Type v} {T : s.SchemesOver} {U : I → s.SchemesOver} (g : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).map (g i).left).hom)
    (α : ∀ i, s.homAt (U i))
    (hα : RestrictionsAgree (s.projection T) (fun i ↦ baseChangeMap s.f (g i))
      (fun i ↦ s.projection (U i)) (fun i ↦ baseChangeMap_comp_projection s.f (g i))
      (fun i ↦ s.toModuleHom (α i))) :
    ∃! β : s.homAt T, ∀ i, s.homMap (g i) β = α i
declarations.comment: the sheaf property elementwise, for an fpqc covering of test schemes; the same property as CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor is isSheafFor_homFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isSheafFor_homFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JV, as the sheaf condition for a presieve.**  In the standing data of
Stacks 08JT the relative Hom functor `Hom(F, G)` is a sheaf for the presieve generated by an
fpqc covering `{U i ⟶ T}` of test schemes over the base: every compatible family of sections
has a unique amalgamation.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.existsUnique_homMap_of_restrictionsAgree` with
the compatibility of the family transported to the overlaps `X_{U i} ×_{X_T} X_{U j}` of the
base changes.  That transport is the content added here: the overlap `U i ×_T U j` of two test
schemes is again a test scheme, so a compatible family restricts compatibly to it, and the
fibre product of the two base changes maps to the base change of that overlap by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.overlapTestComparison`, which carries the two projections
of the fibre product to the base changes of the two projections of the overlap.

This is the form of the sheaf property that Stacks 08K8 consumes, as the hypothesis `hHom` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isSheafFor_isomFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_homFunctor (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    {I : Type v} {T : s.SchemesOver} {U : I → s.SchemesOver} (g : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).map (g i).left).hom) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor (s.homFunctor hc) (Presieve.ofArrows U g)
declarations.comment: the sheaf property for the presieve of an fpqc covering of test schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isSheaf_homFunctor_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JV.**  In Situation 08JT the relative Hom functor `Hom(F, G)`, sending a scheme
`T` over the base to `Hom_{𝒪_{X_T}}(F_T, G_T)`, satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc
topology on the schemes over the base.

Its functoriality is the pseudofunctoriality of Stacks 03LU, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`, proved with no hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_homFunctor_fpqc :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology s.base) (s.homFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.baseChangedSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JW.**  The relative Hom situation obtained by changing the base algebraic space
along `p : base' ⟶ base`: its source is `X' = X ×_base base'`, its morphism the second
projection, and its two modules the pullbacks of `F` and `G` along the first projection.
declarations.statement: def baseChangedSituation : HomSituation B S hS
declarations.comment: the base-changed situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.homFunctorBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JW.**  For a test scheme `T` over `base'` the two relative Hom sets agree:
`Hom(F', G')(T) = Hom(F, G)(T)`, where on the right `T` is read as a scheme over `base`
through `T ⟶ base' ⟶ base`.  The identification is natural in `T`, so it is an isomorphism of
the two relative Hom functors.

It has no hypotheses.  The coherence data for the direct images, which the Hom functor of
either situation is formed from, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`, and
the quasi-coherence of the two pullbacks, which forming the base-changed situation needs, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.comment: the identification Hom(F',G')(T) = Hom(F,G)(T), natural in T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver_degreeZeroSectionsFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JX, part (1).**  Let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic
space `X` such that `H⁻¹(Lg^*K) = 0` for every scheme `g : T → X`.  Then the functor
`(g : T → X) ↦ H⁰(T, H⁰(Lg^*K))` on the schemes over `X` is an algebraic space affine and of
finite presentation over `X`.

The functor is the degree-zero sections functor of any K-flat complex `P₀` with flat terms
representing `K`; its value at `g` is `H⁰(T, H⁰(Lg^*K))` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degreeZeroSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver_degreeZeroSectionsFunctor
    (K : derivedModules B S hS X) (hK : IsPseudoCoherentObject K)
    (hvan : HasVanishingDegreeNegOneDerivedPullback (hasDerivedModulePullbacks B S hS) K)
    (P₀ : CochainComplex (toposModules B S hS X) ℤ)
    (hP₀ : IsKFlat (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P₀))
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P₀ ≅ K) :
    IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver X
      (degreeZeroSectionsFunctor (schemesOverCone X) P₀)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPullbackSectionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero hypercohomology functor of Stacks 08JX, part (2)**: the functor sending a
test scheme `g : T → B` to `H⁰(T, Lg^*K)`, read as the derived Hom out of the pulled-back
structure sheaf.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPullbackSectionFunctor_obj_equiv` identifies its value at `T`
with `Hom_{D(𝒪_T)}(𝒪_T, Lg^*K)`, which is that degree-zero hypercohomology group.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackSectionFunctor (hc : DerivedPullbackCoherence B S hS hL)
    (K : derivedModules B S hS X) : (SchemesOver X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the functor of part (2), `(g : T → B) ↦ H⁰(T, Lg^*K)`, on the test schemes over `B`; its value is `Hom_{D(𝒪_T)}(𝒪_T, Lg^*K)` by `derivedPullbackSectionFunctor_obj_equiv`. The datum `hc` -- Stacks 0D6D and the unit law for `L(-)^*` -- is built with no hypothesis by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPullbackCoherence`. Its representability is `isAffineFinitePresentationSectionFunctor_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback` and the two conclusions about `K` are `isPerfect_and_locally_hasTorAmplitude_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degreeZeroPullbackSections
declarations.doc:
**The value at a test scheme of the functor of Stacks 08JX, part (1)**: the group
`H⁰(T, H⁰(Lg^*K))` of global sections of the degree-zero cohomology sheaf of the derived pullback
of `K` along `g : T → B`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev degreeZeroPullbackSections (hL : BottomRankStratum.HasDerivedModulePullbacks B S hS)
    (K : derivedModules B S hS X) (T : SchemesOver X) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the value at a test scheme `g : T → B` of the functor of part (1), the group `H⁰(T, H⁰(Lg^*K))`. Its restriction maps are not constructed here, for want of a comparison `g^*H⁰(E) ⟶ H⁰(Lg^*E)`; part (1) is proved on the degree-zero sections functor of a K-flat complex representing `K`, which takes these values by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degreeZeroSectionsEquiv`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasVanishingDegreeNegOneDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**The hypothesis of Stacks 08JX, part (1)**: for every test scheme `g : T → B` the
cohomology sheaf `H⁻¹(Lg^*K)` is zero.
declarations.statement:
def HasVanishingDegreeNegOneDerivedPullback
    (hL : BottomRankStratum.HasDerivedModulePullbacks B S hS)
    (K : derivedModules B S hS X) : Prop
declarations.comment: the hypothesis of part (1): `H⁻¹(Lg^*K) = 0` for every test scheme `g : T → B`. The hypothesis of part (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**The hypothesis of Stacks 08JX, part (2)**: for every test scheme `g : T → B` the
cohomology sheaves `Hⁱ(Lg^*K)` are zero for every `i < 0`.
declarations.statement:
def HasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
    (hL : BottomRankStratum.HasDerivedModulePullbacks B S hS)
    (K : derivedModules B S hS X) : Prop
declarations.comment: the hypothesis of part (2): `Hⁱ(Lg^*K) = 0` for every test scheme `g : T → B` and every `i < 0`. The hypothesis of part (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasVanishingDegreeNegOneDerivedPullback`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineFinitePresentationSectionFunctor_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JX, part (2), the functor.**  Let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` on
an algebraic space `X` such that `Hⁱ(Lg^*K) = 0` for every scheme `g : T → X` and every `i < 0`.
Then the functor `(g : T → X) ↦ H⁰(T, Lg^*K)` on the schemes over `X` is an algebraic space
affine and of finite presentation over `X`.

As in the source, under this hypothesis `H⁰(T, Lg^*K) = H⁰(T, H⁰(Lg^*K))`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPullbackSectionFunctorIso`), so the statement is part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFinitePresentationSectionFunctor_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (K : derivedModules B S hS X) (hK : IsPseudoCoherentObject K)
    (hvan : HasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback (hasDerivedModulePullbacks B S hS) K) :
    IsAffineFinitePresentationSectionFunctor (derivedPullbackCoherence B S hS) K
declarations.comment: part (2), the conclusion that `(g : T → B) ↦ H⁰(T, Lg^*K)` is an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over `B`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfect_and_locally_hasTorAmplitude_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JX, part (2), the first two conclusions.**  Let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of
`D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic space `X` such that `Hⁱ(Lg^*K) = 0` for every scheme `g : T → X` and
every `i < 0`.  Then `K` is perfect, and `K` locally has tor amplitude in `[0, b]`: every étale
chart of `X` is covered by charts `V` over which `K|_V` has tor amplitude in `[0, b_V]` for some
`b_V ≥ 0`, against any derived tensor product on the slices.

The proof is the source's: near every point a strictly perfect approximation of `K` has a free
cokernel `Coker(P⁻¹ → P⁰)` (Stacks 068U, from the vanishing of `H⁻¹` on the fibres), so its
canonical truncation `τ_{≥ 0}` is strictly perfect, and it represents `K` there because `K` has
no cohomology in negative degrees
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_covering_slice_models`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_locally_hasTorAmplitude_of_hasVanishingNegativeDerivedPullback
    (T : ∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).C,
      DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1} ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).over U)) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect K ∧
      ∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).C,
        ∃ P : Presieve U, Sieve.generate P ∈ (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J U ∧
          ∀ ⦃V : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).C⦄ (f : V ⟶ U), P f →
            ∃ b : ℤ, 0 ≤ b ∧ DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude (T V)
              ((RingedSite.derivedRestriction.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ V).obj K) 0 b
declarations.comment: part (2), the conclusions that K is perfect and locally has tor amplitude in [0, b]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOverBase_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
In Situation 08JT assume that the base `B` is a Noetherian algebraic space, that `f : X ⟶ B` is
locally of finite type and quasi-separated, that `𝓕` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type, and that
`𝒢` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type, flat over `B`, with support proper over `B`. Then the
functor `Hom(𝓕, 𝒢)` is an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOverBase_of_isNoetherian
    (s : HomSituation B S hS) (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hB : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop s.base.1) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS s.f.hom) (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite s.F)
    (hG : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite s.G) (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS s.X.2 s.f.hom s.G)
    (hproper : HasProperSupportOver s.f s.G) :
    s.IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOverBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.naiveCotangentComplex_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08JZ, the formation of the naive cotangent complex commutes with localization at an
element.** Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `g ∈ B`, let `B_g` be a localization of `B` away from
`g`, let `α : P = A[x_i, i ∈ ι] → B` be a presentation with kernel `I` and let `f ∈ P` be an
element mapped to `g` by `α`. Then `β = (localizationAway T g).comp P : P[x] → B_g` is a
presentation of `B_g` over `A` extending `α` and sending `x` to `1/g`, and

* its kernel `J` is generated by `I` and `f x - 1`;
* (1) `J/J² = (I/I²)_g ⊕ B_g (f x - 1)`: there is an isomorphism `J/J² ≅ (I/I²) ⊗_B B_g ⊕ B_g`
  restricting to the canonical map on the first summand and sending `(0, 1)` to the class of
  `f x - 1`;
* (2) `Ω_{P[x]/A} ⊗ B_g = Ω_{P/A} ⊗ B_g ⊕ B_g dx`: there is an isomorphism
  `Ω_{P[x]/A} ⊗ B_g ≅ (Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B) ⊗_B B_g ⊕ B_g` restricting to the canonical map on the first
  summand and sending `(0, 1)` to `dx`;
* (3) `NL(β) ≅ NL(α) ⊗_B B_g ⊕ (B_g --g--> B_g)`: isomorphisms in both degrees which intertwine
  the differential of `NL(β)` with the direct sum of the base changed differential of `NL(α)` and
  multiplication by `g` on `B_g`, and restrict to the canonical maps on the first summands;
* hence, for any presentations `P'` of `B` and `Q` of `B_g` over `A` (for example the canonical
  ones, whose complexes are `NL_{B/A}` and `NL_{B_g/A}`) and any morphism `φ` of presentations,
  the induced map `NL(P') ⊗_B B_g → NL(Q)` is a homotopy equivalence: a chain map with a chain
  homotopy inverse `(ψ₁, ψ₀)` and homotopies `s`, `t`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangentComplex_localizationAway
    (g : S) [IsLocalization.Away g T] {ι : Type*} (P : Generators R S ι) (f : P.Ring)
    (hf : algebraMap P.Ring S f = g) :
    (∀ i, ((localizationAway T g).comp P).val (Sum.inr i) = algebraMap S T (P.val i)) ∧
      ((localizationAway T g).comp P).val (Sum.inl ()) = IsLocalization.Away.invSelf g ∧
      ((localizationAway T g).comp P).ker =
        Ideal.map ((localizationAway T g).toComp P).toAlgHom P.ker ⊔
          Ideal.span {rename Sum.inr f * X (Sum.inl ()) - 1} ∧
      (∃ e : ((localizationAway T g).comp P).toExtension.Cotangent ≃ₗ[T]
          T ⊗[S] P.toExtension.Cotangent × T,
        e.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl T _ _ =
            (Extension.Cotangent.map
              ((localizationAway T g).toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange T ∧
          ∃ h : rename Sum.inr f * X (Sum.inl ()) - 1 ∈ ((localizationAway T g).comp P).ker,
            e.symm (0, 1) = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨_, h⟩) ∧
      (∃ e : ((localizationAway T g).comp P).toExtension.CotangentSpace ≃ₗ[T]
          T ⊗[S] P.toExtension.CotangentSpace × T,
        e.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl T _ _ =
            (Extension.CotangentSpace.map
              ((localizationAway T g).toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange T ∧
          e.symm (0, 1) = ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[((localizationAway T g).comp P).Ring]
            KaehlerDifferential.D R ((localizationAway T g).comp P).Ring (X (Sum.inl ())) :)) ∧
      (∃ (e₁ : ((localizationAway T g).comp P).toExtension.Cotangent ≃ₗ[T]
          T ⊗[S] P.toExtension.Cotangent × T)
        (e₀ : ((localizationAway T g).comp P).toExtension.CotangentSpace ≃ₗ[T]
          T ⊗[S] P.toExtension.CotangentSpace × T),
        e₀.toLinearMap ∘ₗ ((localizationAway T g).comp P).toExtension.cotangentComplex =
            (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T).prodMap
              (algebraMap S T g • LinearMap.id) ∘ₗ e₁.toLinearMap ∧
          e₁.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl T _ _ =
            (Extension.Cotangent.map
              ((localizationAway T g).toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange T ∧
          e₀.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl T _ _ =
            (Extension.CotangentSpace.map
              ((localizationAway T g).toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange T) ∧
      ∀ {ι' κ : Type*} (P' : Generators R S ι') (Q : Generators R T κ)
        (φ : P'.toExtension.Hom Q.toExtension),
        Q.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ (Extension.Cotangent.map φ).liftBaseChange T =
            (Extension.CotangentSpace.map φ).liftBaseChange T ∘ₗ
              P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T ∧
          ∃ (ψ₁ : Q.toExtension.Cotangent →ₗ[T] T ⊗[S] P'.toExtension.Cotangent)
            (ψ₀ : Q.toExtension.CotangentSpace →ₗ[T] T ⊗[S] P'.toExtension.CotangentSpace)
            (s : T ⊗[S] P'.toExtension.CotangentSpace →ₗ[T] T ⊗[S] P'.toExtension.Cotangent)
            (t : Q.toExtension.CotangentSpace →ₗ[T] Q.toExtension.Cotangent),
            P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T ∘ₗ ψ₁ =
                ψ₀ ∘ₗ Q.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∧
              LinearMap.id - ψ₁ ∘ₗ (Extension.Cotangent.map φ).liftBaseChange T =
                s ∘ₗ P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T ∧
              LinearMap.id - ψ₀ ∘ₗ (Extension.CotangentSpace.map φ).liftBaseChange T =
                P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T ∘ₗ s ∧
              LinearMap.id - (Extension.Cotangent.map φ).liftBaseChange T ∘ₗ ψ₁ =
                t ∘ₗ Q.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∧
              LinearMap.id - (Extension.CotangentSpace.map φ).liftBaseChange T ∘ₗ ψ₀ =
                Q.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ t
declarations.comment:
The whole statement: the presentation `β` (its values on the variables), the
generators `I`, `f x - 1` of its kernel (Mathlib's `Algebra.Generators.comp_localizationAway_ker`),
items (1) (from Mathlib's `Algebra.Generators.cotangentCompLocalizationAwayEquiv` and
`Algebra.Generators.basisCotangentAway`), (2) (from Mathlib's
`Algebra.Generators.CotangentSpace.compEquiv`) and (3), and the homotopy equivalence
`NL_{B/A} ⊗_B B_g → NL_{B_g/A}`, for the map induced by any morphism between any presentations.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFlatOver_baseChange_of_chartLimitsInSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K0, flatness of a module, with no bound on the index.** Let `(B_i)` be a
cofiltered inverse system of algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms, let `i`
be a stage with `B_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `B_i`. Let `F₀` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation. Suppose the pullback of `F₀` to `lim B_j ×_{B_i} X` is flat
over `lim B_j ×_{B_i} Y`, and `f` is locally of finite presentation. Then for some stage `j ⟶ i`
the pullback of `F₀` to `B_j ×_{B_i} X` is flat over `B_j ×_{B_i} Y`.

This strengthens `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isFlatOver_mapAt`. The
bound `MorphismDescentSystem.indexSize` on the index is replaced by `hconv`. `hconv` is the
chapter's convention 07SD: the limits of the base changes of the stages to the affine objects of
the site lie in the site. It is not an assumption beyond the source. It is equivalent to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits`, which it states unfolded, and the index
bound implies it (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartLimitsInSite_of_lt_cof`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlatOver_baseChange_of_chartLimitsInSite
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (D : I ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hconv : ∀ (i : I) (Z : BigAffineFppf B S hS)
      (g : yoneda.obj ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj Z) ⟶ D.obj i)
      (W : Over i ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS),
      (W ⋙ (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙ yoneda) ≅
        (Over.post (X := i) D ⋙ Over.pullback g) ⋙
          Over.forget (yoneda.obj ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj Z))) →
      ∀ c : Cone (((W ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS) ⋙
          BigFppfOver.forget B S hS) ⋙ B.inclusion),
        IsLimit c → B.Contains c.pt)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hAffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map f))
    (i : I) (hB₀qc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hB₀qs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (D.obj i))
    {X Y : Over (D.obj i)} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y.left)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.left) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.left)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.left) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.left)
    (F₀ : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.left hX)
    [F₀.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [F₀.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (flat : IsFlatOver B S hS
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS (limit.π D i) X.hom
        (isAlgebraicSpace_limit_of_chartLimitsInSite B S hS D hconv hD hAffine i hB₀qc) hX (hD i))
      (pullback.map (limit.π D i) X.hom (limit.π D i) Y.hom (𝟙 _) f.left (𝟙 _) (by simp)
        (by simp))
      ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd (limit.π D i) X.hom) :
          (⟨pullback (limit.π D i) X.hom,
            isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS (limit.π D i) X.hom
              (isAlgebraicSpace_limit_of_chartLimitsInSite B S hS D hconv hD hAffine i hB₀qc) hX
              (hD i)⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨X.left, hX⟩)).obj F₀))
    (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.left) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i), IsFlatOver B S hS
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS (D.map e) X.hom (hD j) hX (hD i))
      (pullback.map (D.map e) X.hom (D.map e) Y.hom (𝟙 _) f.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp))
      ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd (D.map e) X.hom) :
          (⟨pullback (D.map e) X.hom,
            isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS (D.map e) X.hom (hD j) hX (hD i)⟩ :
              AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨X.left, hX⟩)).obj F₀)
declarations.comment: flatness of a module, with no bound on the index: the 07SD convention in place of the index bound of MorphismDescentSystem, which exists_isFlatOver_mapAt carries

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSituation.exists_isFlat_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K0**, flatness of the morphism. In the situation of Stacks 084W, if `f₀` is locally
of finite presentation and its base change `f : X ⟶ Y` to the limit is flat, then its base change
`f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_i` to some stage `i ≥ 0` is flat.

This is the statement under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD), which asks
nothing of the index.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlat_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
    (D : MorphismDescentSituation B S hS hZ I) (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base)
        (flat : IsFlat B S hS D.mapLimit)
    (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), IsFlat B S hS (D.mapAt i le)
declarations.comment: in particular: flatness of the morphism, under the convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD) and with no condition on the index

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isFlat_mapAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K0**, flatness of the morphism. In the situation of Stacks 084W, if `f₀` is locally
of finite presentation and its base change `f : X ⟶ Y` to the limit is flat, then its base change
`f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_i` to some stage `i ≥ 0` is flat.

The index of the system is bounded by `MorphismDescentSystem.indexSize`; the statement under the
chapter's convention 07SD, with no condition on the index, is
`MorphismDescentSituation.exists_isFlat_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlat_mapAt
    (D : MorphismDescentSystem B S hS hZ I) (flat : IsFlat B S hS D.mapLimit)
    (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), IsFlat B S hS (D.mapAt i le)
declarations.comment: in particular: flatness of the morphism, with the index bounded by indexSize

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isFlatOver_mapAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K0**, flatness of a module. In the situation of Stacks 084W, let `F₀` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X₀}`-module, with pullbacks `F_i` to `X_i` and `F` to `X`. If `F` is flat over
`Y`, `F₀` is of finite presentation and `f₀` is locally of finite presentation, then `F_i` is flat
over `Y_i` for some stage `i ≥ 0`.

The index of the system is bounded by `MorphismDescentSystem.indexSize`; the statement with no
condition on the index is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFlatOver_baseChange_of_chartLimitsInSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlatOver_mapAt (D : MorphismDescentSystem B S hS hZ I)
    (F₀ : Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.source₀ D.source₀_isAlgebraicSpace)
    [F₀.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [F₀.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (flat : IsFlatOver B S hS D.sourceLimit_isAlgebraicSpace D.mapLimit
      ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (pullback.snd (limit.π D.base (op D.initial)) D.sourceToBase) :
          (⟨D.sourceLimit, D.sourceLimit_isAlgebraicSpace⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
            ⟨D.source₀, D.source₀_isAlgebraicSpace⟩)).obj F₀))
    (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), IsFlatOver B S hS (D.sourceAt_isAlgebraicSpace i le)
      (D.mapAt i le) ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (pullback.snd (D.baseAtToInitial i le) D.sourceToBase) :
          (⟨D.sourceAt i le, D.sourceAt_isAlgebraicSpace i le⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
            ⟨D.source₀, D.source₀_isAlgebraicSpace⟩)).obj F₀)
declarations.comment: flatness of a module, with the index bounded by indexSize

registrations.name: C1573.exists_isFlatOver_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
registrations.comment: flatness of a module, under the convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD) and with no condition on the index

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentData.exists_isProper_mapAt
declarations.doc:
In Situation 084W, under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2, if `f` is
proper and `f₀` is locally of finite type, then `f_i` is proper for some `i ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_mapAt (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).mapLimit)
    (hf₀ : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.initial ≤ i),
      IsProper B S hS ((D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).mapAt i hi)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentData.exists_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_moduleAt
declarations.doc:
In Situation 084W, under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2, let `F₀`
be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X₀}`-module of finite type and let `F` and `F_i` be its pullbacks to `X`
and `X_i`. If `f₀` is locally of finite type and the scheme-theoretic support of `F` is proper
over `Y`, then the scheme-theoretic support of `F_i` is proper over `Y_i` for some `i ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_moduleAt
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base)
    (F₀ : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).source₀Space.1
      (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).source₀Space.2)
    (hqc : F₀.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hf₀ : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS D.map₀)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F₀)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS
      ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).sourceLimitSpace
        ((D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).moduleLimit F₀)).ι ≫
          (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).mapLimit)) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.initial ≤ i), IsProper B S hS
      ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS ((D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).sourceAtSpace i hi)
        ((D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).moduleAt F₀ i hi)).ι ≫
          (D.toMorphismDescentSituation hconv).mapAt i hi)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.tripleRestrictionsAgree_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K3, the first half of the exactness.**  The restrictions of a global
homomorphism `F_T ⟶ G_T` to the base changes `X_{i, T}` of the members of a covering of the
source satisfy the overlap condition: the two parallel arrows of the diagram agree on the image
of the first arrow.

Both restrictions are the restriction of the global homomorphism along the projection
`X_{ijk, T} ⟶ X_T`, because both parallel arrows are morphisms over `X_T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleRestrictionsAgree_restrict (β : s.homAt T) :
    s.TripleRestrictionsAgree a T b
      (fun i ↦ restrictPullbackHom (s.memberInclusion a T i) (s.memberInclusion_comp a T i)
        (s.toModuleHom β))
declarations.comment: the two parallel arrows agree on the image of the first arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.existsUnique_sourceHom_of_tripleRestrictionsAgree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K3, the second half of the exactness.**  In the standing data of Stacks 08JT let
`{X_i ⟶ X}` be an fppf covering and for all `i`, `j` let `{X_{ijk} ⟶ X_i ×_X X_j}` be an fppf
covering.  For every test scheme `T` over the base, a family of homomorphisms
`F_i ⟶ G_i` over the base changes `X_{i, T}` whose restrictions agree on the `X_{ijk, T}` comes
from a unique homomorphism `F_T ⟶ G_T`.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.tripleRestrictionsAgree_restrict` this is
the exactness of the diagram displayed by the source: the first arrow lands in the equalizer of
the other two, is injective, and hits every element of that equalizer.

This is the proof of the source.  The base change of an fppf covering is an fppf covering, so
`{X_{i, T} ⟶ X_T}` and `{X_{ijk, T} ⟶ X_{i, T} ×_{X_T} X_{j, T}}` are fppf, hence fpqc,
coverings — Stacks 03Y9 and Stacks 03MR, part (3).  Applying Stacks 04W8 to the second reduces
the overlap condition to the overlaps themselves, and applying it to the first, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_restrictPullbackHom_eq_of_isFpqcCovering`, produces the
unique global
homomorphism.  The base-changed modules `F_T`, `G_T` are quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_sourceHom_of_tripleRestrictionsAgree
    (hrepr : QuasiCoherentDescent.ReprFpqcHomInjective.{u, v} B S hS)
    (ha : IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun i ↦ (Xi i).1) fun i ↦ (a i).hom)
    (hb : ∀ i j, IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun k ↦ (Xijk i j k).1) fun k ↦ (b i j k).hom)
    (α : ∀ i, (modulePullback B S hS (s.memberToSource a T i)).obj s.F ⟶
      (modulePullback B S hS (s.memberToSource a T i)).obj s.G)
    (hα : s.TripleRestrictionsAgree a T b α) :
    ∃! β : s.homAt T, ∀ i, restrictPullbackHom (s.memberInclusion a T i)
      (s.memberInclusion_comp a T i) (s.toModuleHom β) = α i
declarations.comment: the first arrow is injective with image the equalizer of the other two

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.tripleRestrictionsAgree_iff_existsUnique_sourceHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K3.**  In Situation 08JT let `{X_i ⟶ X}` be an fppf covering and for all `i`, `j`
let `{X_{ijk} ⟶ X_i ×_X X_j}` be an fppf covering, and write `F_i`, `G_i`, `F_{ijk}`,
`G_{ijk}` for the pullbacks of `F` and `G`.  For every scheme `T` over the base, the diagram
`Hom(F, G)(T) ⟶ ∏_i Hom(F_i, G_i)(T) ⇉ ∏_{ijk} Hom(F_{ijk}, G_{ijk})(T)` presents the first
arrow as the equalizer of the other two: a family `(α i)` of homomorphisms over the base
changes `X_{i, T}` is taken to the same element by the two parallel arrows exactly when it is
the image of a unique `β : F_T ⟶ G_T`.

The backward direction says that the first arrow lands in the equalizer; together with it the
forward direction says that the first arrow is injective and its image is the equalizer.

This is the proof of the source.  The base changes `{X_{i, T} ⟶ X_T}` and
`{X_{ijk, T} ⟶ X_{i, T} ×_{X_T} X_{j, T}}` are fppf, hence fpqc, coverings (Stacks 03Y9);
Stacks 04W8 applied to the second, in the form of its faithfulness half, reduces the condition
to the overlaps themselves, and applied to the first, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gluesModuleHomAlongFpqcCovering`, produces the unique global
homomorphism.  The base-changed modules `F_T`, `G_T` are quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleRestrictionsAgree_iff_existsUnique_sourceHom
    (ha : IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun i ↦ (Xi i).1) fun i ↦ (a i).hom)
    (hb : ∀ i j, IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun k ↦ (Xijk i j k).1) fun k ↦ (b i j k).hom)
    (α : ∀ i, (modulePullback B S hS (s.memberToSource a T i)).obj s.F ⟶
      (modulePullback B S hS (s.memberToSource a T i)).obj s.G) :
    s.TripleRestrictionsAgree a T b α ↔
      ∃! β : s.homAt T, ∀ i, restrictPullbackHom (s.memberInclusion a T i)
        (s.memberInclusion_comp a T i) (s.toModuleHom β) = α i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isLimitPreservingHom_of_isEqualizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K4, reduced to an equalizer presentation of the relative Hom functor.**  The
relative Hom functor of Stacks 08JT is limit preserving as soon as it is cut out, at every test
scheme over the base, as the equalizer of two maps between limit-preserving presheaves.

Stacks 08K3 supplies such a presentation from an affine scheme surjective and étale over the
source and an affine scheme surjective and étale over its self-overlap, which exist because the
structure morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Stacks 03H6), the two presheaves being
the relative Hom functors of those charts; their limit preservation is the affine case, which is
Stacks 05LI.  Neither the presentation nor the affine case is proved here, so both are asked for
as data; accordingly the three hypotheses of Stacks 08K4 are not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreservingHom_of_isEqualizer (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    (s : HomSituation B S hS) {Q R : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
    (a : s.homFunctor hc ⟶ Q) (b₁ b₂ : Q ⟶ R)
    (hinj : ∀ T, Function.Injective (a.app T))
    (hequalizes : ∀ (T : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ) (α : (s.homFunctor hc).obj T),
      b₁.app T (a.app T α) = b₂.app T (a.app T α))
    (hlift : ∀ (T : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ) (q : Q.obj T),
      b₁.app T q = b₂.app T q → ∃ α, a.app T α = q)
    (hQ : LimitPreserving.{u, u + 1, w, w', u + 1} s.testSchemeFunctor Q)
    (hR : LimitPreserving.{u, u + 1, w, w', u + 1} s.testSchemeFunctor R) :
    IsLimitPreservingHom.{u, w, w'} hc s
declarations.comment: reduced to the equalizer presentation of Stacks 08K3; that presentation and the affine case, Stacks 05LI, are not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.limitPreserving_homFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K4.**  In Situation 08JT, if `F` is of finite presentation and `f` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then the relative Hom functor `Hom(F, G)` is limit
preserving: for every directed limit `T = lim T_i` of affine schemes over the base,
`Hom(F, G)(T) = colim Hom(F, G)(T_i)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_homFunctor (s : HomSituation B S hS)
    (hF : s.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS s.f.hom) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u + 1, u, u} s.testSchemeFunctor
      (s.homFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.homFunctorClosedImmersionIso_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K5.**  Let `i : X' ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over an
algebraic space `Y` over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `G'` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X'}`-module.  Then

`Hom(F, i_*G') = Hom(i^*F, G')`

as functors on the test schemes over `Y`: the relative Hom functor of Stacks 08JT of the
situation `(X ⟶ Y, F, i_*G')` is isomorphic to the one of the situation `(X' ⟶ Y, i^*F, G')`,
both formed with the pseudofunctoriality `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`
of Stacks 03LU.

The two situations are formed with the quasi-coherence of `i_*G'` (Stacks 03M9) and of `i^*F`
(Stacks 03GA), and the comparison is bijective by the base-change clause of Stacks 07U8 for
the affine morphism `i`.
declarations.statement:
def homFunctorClosedImmersionIso_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite (p : X ⟶ Y) (i : X' ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (G' : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X'.1 X'.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hG' : G'.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (pushforwardHomSituation p i F G' hF
        (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion B S hS i hi G'
          hG')).homFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) ≅
      (pullbackHomSituation p i F G'
        (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isClosedImmersion B S hS i hi F hF)
        hG').homFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
declarations.comment: The whole statement, under exactly the source's hypotheses.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isAffineAlgebraicSpaceOverBase_and_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K6.** In Situation 08JT let `f : X ⟶ B` be of finite presentation and let `G` be an
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `B`, with support proper over `B`.  Then
`Hom(F, G)` is an algebraic space affine over `B` for every quasi-coherent `F` étale-locally
generated by fewer than `μ` sections, `μ` below the cutoff of the site; and if `F` is of finite
presentation, then `Hom(F, G)` is an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over `B`.

The bound on `F` in the first assertion corrects the source (Stacks erratum): for an arbitrary
quasi-coherent `F` the first assertion is false on every big fppf site, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_homSituation_not_isAffineAlgebraicSpaceOverBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineAlgebraicSpaceOverBase_and_finitePresentation
    (s : HomSituation B S hS)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hG : s.G.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS s.X.2 s.f.hom s.G)
    (hproper : HasProperSupportOver s.f s.G) :
    ((∃ μ < B.cutoff, IsEtaleLocallyGeneratedBelow B S hS μ s.F) →
        s.IsAffineAlgebraicSpaceOverBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)) ∧
      (s.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite →
        s.IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOverBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS))
declarations.comment: both assertions: Hom(F, G) is an algebraic space affine over B for F étale-locally generated by fewer sections than the cutoff of the site (Stacks erratum: false for an unbounded quasi-coherent F), and affine of finite presentation over B for F of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isomSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K7.**  The relative Isom functor `Isom(F, G) ⊆ Hom(F, G)` as a subfunctor of the
relative Hom functor of Stacks 08JT: its sections at a test scheme `T` over the base are the
invertible `𝒪_{X_T}`-homomorphisms `F_T ⟶ G_T`.

It is a subfunctor because invertibility is stable under pullback,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isIsomAt_homMap`.  The ambient relative Hom functor is
taken at the pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`.
declarations.statement: def isomSubfunctor : Subfunctor (s.homFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS))
declarations.comment: the Isom functor as a subfunctor of the Hom functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isomFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K7.**  The relative Isom functor `Isom(F, G) : (Sch/base)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`, whose value
at a test scheme `T` over the base is the set of invertible `𝒪_{X_T}`-homomorphisms
`F_T ⟶ G_T` and whose action on a morphism of test schemes is pullback of homomorphisms.  Its
inclusion into the relative Hom functor is `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.ι`.
declarations.statement: def isomFunctor : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Isom functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isSheafFor_isomFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08K8.**  In Situation 08JT the relative Isom functor `Isom(F, G)` satisfies the
sheaf property for the fpqc topology: for every fpqc covering `{U i ⟶ T}` of schemes over the
base, every compatible family of invertible homomorphisms `F_{U i} ⟶ G_{U i}` has a unique
amalgamation, an invertible homomorphism `F_T ⟶ G_T`.

This is the proof of the source.  `Hom(F, G)` satisfies the sheaf property, Stacks 08JV in the
form of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isSheafFor_homFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering`, so it
remains that a homomorphism `F_T ⟶ G_T` whose base changes to the `U i` are isomorphisms is an
isomorphism; the base changes `{X_{U i} ⟶ X_T}` form an fpqc covering of `X_T` by Stacks 03MR,
and invertibility descends along it by Stacks 04W8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reflectsIsoAlongFpqcCovering`, the base-changed modules being
quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_isomFunctor_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v} {T : s.SchemesOver}
    {U : I → s.SchemesOver} (g : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).map (g i).left).hom) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor s.isomFunctor (Presieve.ofArrows U g)
declarations.comment: the functor Isom(F, G) of Situation 08JT satisfies the sheaf property for every fpqc covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver_isomFunctor_of_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
In Situation 08JT assume that `f : X ⟶ B` is of finite presentation and that `𝓕` and `𝒢`
are finitely presented `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `B`, with support proper over `B`. Then the
functor `Isom(𝓕, 𝒢)` is an algebraic space affine of finite presentation over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver_isomFunctor_of_hasProperSupport
    (s : HomSituation B S hS) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hF : s.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) (hG : s.G.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hFflat : IsFlatOver B S hS s.X.2 s.f.hom s.F)
    (hGflat : IsFlatOver B S hS s.X.2 s.f.hom s.G)
    (hFsupp : HasProperSupport B S hS s.X.2 s.base.2 s.f.hom
      (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hfp.1)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj s.F))
    (hGsupp : HasProperSupport B S hS s.X.2 s.base.2 s.f.hom
      (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hfp.1)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj s.G)) :
    IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver s.base s.isomFunctor
declarations.comment: Isom(F, G) is an algebraic space affine of finite presentation over B, for f of finite presentation and F, G of finite presentation, flat over B, with support proper over B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08KB, the standing data.**  A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` of
finite presentation: the relative algebraic space whose coherent sheaves with proper support
the category `Coh_{X/Y}` classifies.
declarations.statement: structure CoherentSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the relative algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08KB, the objects.**  An object of `Coh_{X/Y}`: a scheme `T` of the site over `Y`
together with a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X_T}`-module of finite presentation which is flat over `T`
and whose support is proper over `T`.
declarations.statement: structure CoherentObject (D : CoherentSituation B S hS)
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08KB, the morphisms.**  A morphism of `Coh_{X/Y}`: a morphism `h : T ⟶ T'` of
test schemes over `Y` together with an isomorphism `(X_h)^*F' ⟶ F` of `𝒪_{X_T}`-modules.
declarations.statement: structure CoherentHom {D : CoherentSituation B S hS} (A A' : CoherentObject D)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.categoryData
declarations.doc:
**`Coh_{X/Y}` is a category**, for the canonical pseudofunctoriality datum
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence` of the direct images of Stacks 03LU.
declarations.statement: def categoryData : CoherentCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) D
declarations.comment:
the category structure on Coh_{X/Y}: the identity and associativity laws, which
Stacks 08KB asserts by designation and this library had left unverified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08KC.**  In Situation 08KB the projection `Coh_{X/Y} ⟶ (Sch/S)_fppf`,
`(T, g, F) ↦ T`, makes the category `Coh_{X/Y}` of Stacks 08KB a stack in groupoids over the big
fppf site of `S`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.isLimitPreserving_coherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08KD.** In Situation 08KB, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite presentation of
algebraic spaces over `S` and assume `Y` locally of finite presentation over `S`. Then
`Coh_{X/Y}` is limit preserving in the sense of Artin's Axioms, Definition 07XL: for every
cofiltered inverse system of affine schemes `T_j` of the big fppf site, indexed by a category in
the scheme universe, whose limit `T` in schemes lies in the site, the comparison functor
`colim Coh_{X/Y, T_j} ⥤ Coh_{X/Y, T}` is an equivalence.

The index category is taken in the scheme universe, which is the smallness the source's
directed sets have, as in `AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPreservingPolarizedUnconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_coherent
    (hY : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (terminal.from D.Y.1)) :
    Deformation.Artin.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u} B S hS D.coherentCFG
declarations.comment: at a small index category

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonEffectiveProjectiveDescent.exists_etale_descentData_projective_not_isEffective
declarations.doc:
**There is a non-effective projective descent datum along an étale covering.** There are an
étale covering of a scheme consisting of a single morphism `f : X ⟶ S` and a descent datum
relative to `f` whose scheme over `X` is projective over `X` and which is not effective in the
category of schemes. This is [Stacks, Tag 08KF] with no hypothesis; the witness is built over
`ULift ℚ` by
`HironakaInvolution.exists_etale_descentData_projective_not_isEffective_of_two_ne_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_descentData_projective_not_isEffective :
    ∃ (S X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ S)
      (D : DescentData (S := S) (X := fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f)),
      Presieve.singleton f ∈ Scheme.etalePrecoverage S ∧
        IsProjective (D.obj ()).hom ∧ ¬ D.IsEffective
declarations.comment:
The source's construction over ℚ: the involution [x:y:z:w] ↦ [y:x:w:z] of ℙ³
acts freely on Y = ℙ³ minus two lines, Y → S = Y/G is an étale double cover, Hironaka's threefold
over ℙ³ carries the lifted involution, and its restriction gives the descent datum. Two choices
differ from the text: the étale covering is the single open Y − {Q} → S (a member of the source's
covering (Y − P) ⊔ (Y − Q), already surjective onto S), and non-effectivity is derived from
χ(H|L₀) + χ(H|g(L₀)) = 2 for invertible H (the Euler-characteristic form of L₀ + g(L₀) ∼ 0) applied
to the divisor of a function on the would-be quotient, instead of degrees of 1-cycles

declarations.name: RingFibreProduct.Situation
declarations.doc:
The setup for a ring fibre product `B ×_A A'` in which `A' → A` is surjective and
has the specified ideal `I` as its kernel.
declarations.statement:
public structure Situation (toBase : B →+* A) (surjection : A' →+* A)
    (I : Ideal A') : Prop

declarations.name: RingFibreProduct.Situation.pullbackCone
declarations.doc: The canonical cone whose point is `B ×_A A'` and whose legs are the two projections.

declarations.name: RingFibreProduct.Situation.pullbackConeIsLimit
declarations.doc: The canonical square defining `B ×_A A'` is cartesian.

declarations.name: ModuleGlueing.extensionOfScalarsToPullback
declarations.doc:
A commutative square of commutative rings induces the
extension-of-scalars functor
`Mod B' ⟶ Mod B ×_(Mod A) Mod A'`. Its value at `L'` consists of the two scalar
extensions of `L'` and their canonical identification after extending scalars to `A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionOfScalarsToPullback.{u, uB', uB, uA', uA}
    {B' : Type uB'} {B : Type uB} {A' : Type uA'} {A : Type uA}
    [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [CommRing A]
    (toB : B' →+* B) (toA' : B' →+* A') (BtoA : B →+* A) (A'toA : A' →+* A)
    (comm : BtoA.comp toB = A'toA.comp toA') :
    ModuleCat.{max u uB uA' uA} B' ⥤
      CategoricalPullback (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uB, uA, max u uB uA' uA} BtoA)
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uA', uA, max u uB uA' uA} A'toA)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.fibreProdMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag `08KJ`, Lemma 15.6.6).**  If both component maps
`a : N₁ → N₂` and `b : M'₁ → M'₂` of a morphism in the fibre product category are
surjective, then the induced `B'`-linear map `F(a, b)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreProdMap_surjective
    (φ₁ : StructIso π B N₁ M₁') (φ₂ : StructIso π B N₂ M₂')
    (a : N₁ →ₗ[B] N₂) (b : M₁' →ₗ[A'] M₂') (hab : IsMorphism π B N₁ N₂ M₁' M₂' φ₁ φ₂ a b)
    (ha : Function.Surjective a) (hb : Function.Surjective b) :
    Function.Surjective (Fmor π B N₁ N₂ M₁' M₂' φ₁ φ₂ a b hab)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KK.** The relative fibre-product situation consists of a
fibre-product square `B' = B ×_A A'` as in Tag 08KH and an additional ring map
`B' → D'`.
declarations.statement:
public structure RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation
    (base : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KL.** After base change along a `B'`-algebra `D'`, extension
of scalars gives the functor
`Mod D' \longrightarrow Mod (D' \otimes_{B'} B) \times_{Mod (D' \otimes_{B'} A)}
Mod (D' \otimes_{B'} A')`.

It sends a module `L'` to its scalar extensions to `D' \otimes_{B'} B` and
`D' \otimes_{B'} A'`, equipped with the canonical identification after extending both
once more to `D' \otimes_{B'} A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback
    {B' : Type uB'} {B : Type uB} {A' : Type uA'} {A : Type uA} {D' : Type uD'}
    [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [CommRing A]
    [CommRing D'] [Algebra B' B] [Algebra B' A'] [Algebra B' A] [Algebra B' D']
    (BtoA : B →ₐ[B'] A) (A'toA : A' →ₐ[B'] A) :
    ModuleCat.{max v uD' uB uA' uA} D' ⥤
      CategoricalPullback
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{_, _, max v uD' uB uA' uA}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id B' D') BtoA).toRingHom)
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{_, _, max v uD' uB uA' uA}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id B' D') A'toA).toRingHom)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.relativeCompatiblePairsRightAdjoint_counit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KM.** In the relative fibre-product situation, extension of
scalars from `D'` to compatible `D`- and `C'`-modules has a right adjoint.  Its value on
`(N, M', φ)` is naturally the fibre product `N ×_{M' / I M'} M'`.  The counit is an
isomorphism, so extending this fibre-product module back to `D` and to `C'` canonically
and naturally recovers `N` and `M'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeCompatiblePairsRightAdjoint_counit_isIso
    (s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := D') base) :
    ∃ (F : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation.CompatibleModules s ⥤
          ModuleCat.{u} D')
      (e : ∀ X, F.obj X ≃ RelativeCompatiblePairs s X)
      (adj : (letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct D' := s.toD'.toAlgebra
         letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct B := (toBase.pullbackFst surjection).toAlgebra
         letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A' := (toBase.pullbackSnd surjection).toAlgebra
         letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A := (toBase.comp (toBase.pullbackFst
           surjection)).toAlgebra
         extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback (D' := D')
           ({ toBase with commutes' := fun _ => rfl } : B →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)
           ({ surjection with commutes' := fun r => r.property.symm } : A' →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A))
             ⊣ F),
      (∀ (L : ModuleCat.{u} D') (X) (h : L ⟶ F.obj X) (l : L),
          (e X (h l)).1.1 =
              ((adj.homEquiv L X).symm h).fst
                ((1 : s.D) ⊗ₜ[D',s.toD] l) ∧
            (e X (h l)).1.2 =
              ((adj.homEquiv L X).symm h).snd
                ((1 : s.C') ⊗ₜ[D',s.toC'] l)) ∧
        IsIso adj.counit

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.image_extendedKernel_eq_extendedIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KN.** If `J` is the kernel of `B' → B`, then the
canonical map from `J D'` to `I C'` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem image_extendedKernel_eq_extendedIdeal
    (s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := D') base) :
    s.toC' ''
        (↑((RingHom.ker (toB (base := base))).map s.toD') : Set D') =
      (↑(I.map s.A'toC') : Set s.C')

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.finitePresentation_rightAdjoint_obj_of_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KP.** In a relative module fibre-product situation, the
compatible-pairs module is finitely presented over `D'` if its `D`-component and
`C'`-component are finitely presented and flat over `B` and `A'`, respectively, and
the map `B' → D'` factors as a flat map followed by a finitely presented map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_rightAdjoint_obj_of_factorization
    {A A' B D' : Type u} {D'' : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing D'] [CommRing D'']
    {toBase : B →+* A} {surjection : A' →+* A} {I : Ideal A'}
    {base : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I}
    (s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := D') base)
    (F : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation.CompatibleModules s ⥤
      ModuleCat.{u} D')
    (adj : (letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct D' := s.toD'.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct B := (toBase.pullbackFst surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A' := (toBase.pullbackSnd surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A := (toBase.comp (toBase.pullbackFst surjection)).toAlgebra
       extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback (D' := D')
         ({ toBase with commutes' := fun _ => rfl } : B →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)
         ({ surjection with commutes' := fun r => r.property.symm } : A' →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)) ⊣
           F)
    (_ : IsIso adj.counit)
    (X : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation.CompatibleModules s)
    (_ : Module.FinitePresentation s.D X.fst)
    (_ : Module.Flat B ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars s.BtoD).obj X.fst))
    (_ : Module.FinitePresentation s.C' X.snd)
    (_ : Module.Flat A' ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars s.A'toC').obj X.snd))
    (toD'' : base.fibreProduct →+* D'') (fromD'' : D'' →+* D')
    (_ : fromD''.comp toD'' = s.toD')
    (_ : @Module.Flat base.fibreProduct D'' _ _ (Module.compHom D'' toD''))
    (_ : fromD''.FinitePresentation) :
    Module.FinitePresentation D' (F.obj X)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.ringHom_properties_pullback_iff_and_flatAlgebra_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KQ.** Properties of an algebra obtained by gluing algebras over a
fibre product are detected on its two base changes. Every flat algebra over the fibre product
is canonically reconstructed from those base changes, and base change induces an equivalence
with the category of compatible systems of flat algebras.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringHom_properties_pullback_iff_and_flatAlgebra_equivalence
    {A A' B : Type u} {D : Type v} {C' : Type w} {C : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [CommRing C'] [CommRing C]
    (toBase : B →+* A) (surjection : A' →+* A) (I : Ideal A')
    (base : RingFibreProduct.Situation toBase surjection I)
    (BtoD : B →+* D) (A'toC' : A' →+* C') (AtoC : A →+* C)
    (DtoC : D →+* C) (C'toC : C' →+* C)
    (hD : ringPushout BtoD toBase DtoC AtoC)
    (hC' : ringPushout A'toC' surjection C'toC AtoC) :
    let toB : base.fibreProduct →+* B := base.pullbackCone.fst.hom
    let toA' : base.fibreProduct →+* A' := base.pullbackCone.snd.hom
    let toD' : base.fibreProduct →+* RingHom.pullback DtoC C'toC :=
      RingHom.codRestrict ((BtoD.comp toB).prod (A'toC'.comp toA'))
        (RingHom.pullback DtoC C'toC) (fun x ↦ by
          change DtoC (BtoD (toB x)) = C'toC (A'toC' (toA' x))
          have hd : DtoC.comp BtoD = AtoC.comp toBase := ringPushout_comm hD
          have hc : C'toC.comp A'toC' = AtoC.comp surjection := ringPushout_comm hC'
          calc
            _ = AtoC (toBase (toB x)) := DFunLike.congr_fun hd (toB x)
            _ = AtoC (surjection (toA' x)) := congrArg AtoC
              (DFunLike.congr_fun
                (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom base.pullbackCone.condition) x)
            _ = _ := (DFunLike.congr_fun hc (toA' x)).symm)
    let flat := CommRingCat.flat
    let BtoA := MorphismProperty.Under.pushout flat ⊤ (CommRingCat.ofHom toBase)
    let A'toA := MorphismProperty.Under.pushout flat ⊤ (CommRingCat.ofHom surjection)
    let B'toB := MorphismProperty.Under.pushout flat ⊤ (CommRingCat.ofHom toB)
    let B'toA' := MorphismProperty.Under.pushout flat ⊤ (CommRingCat.ofHom toA')
    (toD'.FiniteType ↔ BtoD.FiniteType ∧ A'toC'.FiniteType) ∧
      (toD'.Flat ↔ BtoD.Flat ∧ A'toC'.Flat) ∧
      (toD'.Flat ∧ toD'.FinitePresentation ↔
        (BtoD.Flat ∧ BtoD.FinitePresentation) ∧
          (A'toC'.Flat ∧ A'toC'.FinitePresentation)) ∧
      (toD'.Smooth ↔ BtoD.Smooth ∧ A'toC'.Smooth) ∧
      (toD'.Etale ↔ BtoD.Etale ∧ A'toC'.Etale) ∧
      (∀ (E : Type u) [CommRing E] (f : base.fibreProduct →+* E), f.Flat →
        let s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := E) base := ⟨f⟩
        Function.Bijective s.toRelativePullback) ∧
      ∃ q : (flat.Under ⊤ (CommRingCat.of base.fibreProduct)) ≌
          CategoricalPullback BtoA A'toA,
        Nonempty (q.functor ⋙ CategoricalPullback.π₁ BtoA A'toA ≅ B'toB) ∧
          Nonempty (q.functor ⋙ CategoricalPullback.π₂ BtoA A'toA ≅ B'toA')

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.relativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotientsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KR.** If `B' → D'` is of finite presentation, the
finitely presented quotients of a `D'`-module which are flat over `B'` correspond to
pairs of finitely presented quotients after base change to `D` and `C'`, flat over `B`
and `A'`, and agreeing as quotients after base change to `C`.

The forward correspondence is extension of scalars.  The inverse target module is the
fibre product of the two quotient modules over their common quotient over `C`; the final
formula records the prescribed quotient map from `L`.

Scalar extension and the compatible-pairs construction give the canonical equivalence of
finitely presented relatively flat quotient categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotientsEquivalence
    (s : RelativeModuleFibreProductSituation (D' := D') base)
    (hfp : s.toD'.FinitePresentation) (L : ModuleCat.{u} D') :
    let E := (letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct D' := s.toD'.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct B := (toBase.pullbackFst surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A' := (toBase.pullbackSnd surjection).toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra base.fibreProduct A := (toBase.comp (toBase.pullbackFst surjection)).toAlgebra
       extensionOfScalarsToTensorProductPullback (D' := D')
         ({ toBase with commutes' := fun _ => rfl } : B →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A)
         ({ surjection with commutes' := fun r => r.property.symm } : A' →ₐ[base.fibreProduct] A))
    let source := (RelativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotient s L).FullSubcategory
    let target := (CompatibleRelativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotient s L).FullSubcategory
    ∃ e : source ≌ target,
      Nonempty
          ((RelativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotient s L).ι ⋙ Under.post E ≅
            e.functor ⋙ (CompatibleRelativeFlatFinitelyPresentedQuotient s L).ι) ∧
        ∀ q : target,
          ∃ glueEquiv : (e.inverse.obj q).obj.right ≃
              RelativeCompatiblePairs s q.obj.right,
            ∀ l : L,
              (glueEquiv ((e.inverse.obj q).obj.hom l)).1.1 =
                  q.obj.hom.fst
                    ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj s.toD).unit.app L l) ∧
                (glueEquiv ((e.inverse.obj q).obj.hom l)).1.2 =
                  q.obj.hom.snd
                    ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj s.toC').unit.app L l)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag08KS.modulePushforward_fullyFaithful

spaces whose underlying continuous map is a closed embedding and whose comorphism of structure

right adjoint.

spaces whose underlying continuous map is a closed embedding is right exact.

Together with `preservesFiniteLimits_modulePushforward` this says that the functor is exact.
