declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.fullyFaithfulModulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08KS], full faithfulness.** The direct image
`i_* : Mod(𝒪_Z) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_X)` along a homeomorphism onto a closed subset with surjective
comorphism is fully faithful.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fullyFaithfulModulePushforward : (modulePushforward S.i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.modulePushforward_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08KS], the essential image.** An `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` is a direct image
`i_* ℱ` exactly when `ℐ𝒢 = 0`, i.e. when every section of the kernel ideal `ℐ = ker i^♯` over
an open `U` annihilates every section of `𝒢` over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePushforward_essImage_iff (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)) :
    (modulePushforward S.i).essImage M ↔
      ∀ (U : Opens S.X) (a : (structureSheafRing S.X).obj.obj (op U)), a ∈ S.kernelIdeal U →
        ∀ m : M.val.obj (op U), a • m = 0
declarations.comment: the essential image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_iff
declarations.doc:
**The essential-image clause of Stacks 08KS for algebraic spaces.** For a closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S`, an `𝒪_X`-module is isomorphic to a direct image along
`i` exactly when the ideal `ℐ = ker(i♯)` cutting out `Z` annihilates it.

This is the one statement carrying the tag for the essential-image clause on the algebraic-space
substrate: it states the clause as the source does, so neither inclusion does. The forward one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_le_annihilatedByKerIdeal` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionModulePushforwardExactness.lean`, in its
containment form, and the reverse one is the previous statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_modulePushforward_iff (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (modulePushforward B S hS i).essImage M ↔ AnnihilatedByKerIdeal B S hS i M
declarations.comment: essential image of the direct image: exactly the annihilated modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulModulePushforward
declarations.doc:
Direct image of `𝒪`-modules along a closed immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is
fully faithful.

The two inputs of `Stacks.ToposBridge.fullyFaithfulPushforwardModules` are part (1) of
Stacks 04E5, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSmallEtalePushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion`, and
the surjectivity clause of Stacks 03MB,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharp`. This is Stacks 04CJ, part (2) in
its full-faithfulness form; the Stacks 04CJ tag is carried by the counit statements below, which
are the form the source asserts.

It is at the same time the **full-faithfulness clause of Stacks 08KS for algebraic spaces**: that
tag asserts of the direct image along a closed immersion that it is exact, fully faithful, and has
the `𝓘`-annihilated modules for essential image, and this is the second of those three. The first
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_modulePushforward` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionModulePushforwardExactness.lean` for its
left-exactness half; the third is the pair of annihilation statements below for one inclusion, the
other being `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_of_annihilatedByKerIdeal` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionModuleEssentialImage.lean`, which needs no
hypothesis beyond the closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulModulePushforward (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f.hom) :
    (modulePushforward B S hS f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness of the direct image, for algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion_viaAlmostCocontinuity
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08KS], the exactness clause, for algebraic spaces, unconditionally.** The
direct image `i_* : Mod(𝒪_Z) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_X)` of Stacks 03LU along a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces is an exact functor.

Left exactness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_modulePushforward` and needs no
hypothesis on `i`; right exactness is the previous statement. It replaces
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_modulePushforward_of_essSurj`, which assumes the
essential-image assertion of Stacks 04E5.

This is the one statement carrying the tag for the exactness clause on the algebraic-space
substrate: it states the clause as the source does, so neither half does.

The name records the route: right exactness comes from almost cocontinuity, the space-level
analogue of [Stacks, Tag 04DX], part (7), rather than from the finite case of
[Stacks, Tag 04C2].
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion_viaAlmostCocontinuity (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    exactFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2) (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (modulePushforward B S hS i)
declarations.comment: the exactness clause of the direct image, for algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
An `O_X`-module is flat over `Y` at `x : X` if its stalk at `x`, regarded
as an `O_{Y,f(x)}`-module through the stalk map of `f`, is flat.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev IsFlatOverAt {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf))
    (x : X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver
declarations.doc:
An `O_X`-module is flat over `Y` if it is flat over `Y` at every point of
`X`.
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isEquivalence_flatBaseChangeTripleFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KU, the equivalence of the first clause.**  For a thickening
`i : X ⟶ X'`, an affine morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, the pushout `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` and any
`g : V' ⟶ Y'`, the comparison functor of the tag — a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{V'}`-module flat over
`Y'` goes to its restrictions to `V = Y ×_{Y'} V'` and to `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'` together with the
canonical isomorphism of their restrictions to `U = X ×_{Y'} V'` — is an **equivalence of
categories** onto the triples `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)` with `𝒢` quasi-coherent on `V` and flat over `Y`,
`ℱ'` quasi-coherent on `U'` and flat over `X'`, and `φ` an isomorphism of their restrictions
to `U`.

The pushout `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` is not assumed to exist: for a thickening `i` and an affine `f` it
does, by the first assertion of [Stacks Project, Tag 07RT],
`Stacks.Pushout.hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom`, whose [Stacks Project, Tag 06AD]
hypothesis is discharged by `Stacks.Thickenings.forall_isAffine_of_isThickening`; that is the
instance the statement binds for itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_flatBaseChangeTripleFunctor (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ g : V' ⟶ pushout i f, (flatBaseChangeTripleFunctor i f g hi).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the first clause

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.baseChangeTripleFunctor
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor, sending a module on `V'` to its two restrictions to `V` and to `U'`
together with the canonical isomorphism `Stacks.Pushout.overlapComparison` between their
restrictions to `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeTripleFunctor (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ g : V' ⟶ pushout i f, V'.Modules ⥤ GluingTriple i f g
declarations.comment: the comparison functor of the tag, on all modules on V'

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isFiniteType_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
If a module on `V'` is of finite type, then both components of its comparison triple, its
restrictions to `V` and to `U'`, are of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f) (M : V'.Modules) [M.IsFiniteType],
      ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M).target.IsFiniteType ∧
        ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M).ambient.IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: the finite type clause, for an arbitrary module on V'

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isFinitePresentation_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
If a module on `V'` is of finite presentation, then both components of its comparison
triple, its restrictions to `V` and to `U'`, are of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f) (M : V'.Modules) [M.IsFinitePresentation],
      ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M).target.IsFinitePresentation ∧
        ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M).ambient.IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: the finite presentation clause, for an arbitrary module on V'

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isFiniteType_iff_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on `V'` flat over `Y'` is of finite type if and only if both
components of its comparison triple, its restrictions to `V` and to `U'`, are of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_iff_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f) (M : FlatQuasicoherentModule g),
      M.obj.IsFiniteType ↔
        ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M.obj).target.IsFiniteType ∧
          ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M.obj).ambient.IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: the finite type clause

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isFinitePresentation_iff_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
If `V' ⟶ Y'` is locally of finite presentation, a quasi-coherent module on `V'` flat over `Y'`
is of finite presentation if and only if both components of its comparison triple, its
restrictions to `V` and to `U'`, are of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_iff_baseChangeTripleFunctor_obj (hi : IsThickening i)
    [IsAffineHom f] :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom forall_isAffine_of_isThickening i f hi
    ∀ (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f), LocallyOfFinitePresentation g →
      ∀ M : FlatQuasicoherentModule g,
        M.obj.IsFinitePresentation ↔
          ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M.obj).target.IsFinitePresentation ∧
            ((baseChangeTripleFunctor i f hi g).obj M.obj).ambient.IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: the finite presentation clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isFiniteType_iff_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KV (a).**  Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be a thickening and `f : X ⟶ Y` an affine
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` be their pushout (Stacks 07VX) and
`g : V' ⟶ Y'` a morphism, with `V = Y ×_{Y'} V'` and `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'`.  If a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_{V'}`-module `𝒢'` flat over `Y'` corresponds to the triple `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)` under the equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor`, so that
`𝒢 = (V ⟶ V')^*𝒢'` and `ℱ' = (U' ⟶ V')^*𝒢'`, then `𝒢'` is of finite type if and only if `𝒢` and
`ℱ'` are of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_iff_restrict :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom B S hS i f hi hf
    ∀ {V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f)
      (M : (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory),
      M.obj.IsFiniteType ↔
        (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
          (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
            (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
            (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
          fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
            M.property).obj M).obj.target.IsFiniteType ∧
        (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
          (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
            (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
            (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
          fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
            M.property).obj M).obj.ambient.IsFiniteType

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KV (b).**  Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be a thickening and `f : X ⟶ Y` an affine
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` be their pushout (Stacks 07VX) and
`g : V' ⟶ Y'` a morphism **locally of finite presentation**, with `V = Y ×_{Y'} V'` and
`U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'`.  If a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{V'}`-module `𝒢'` flat over `Y'` corresponds to the
triple `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)` under the equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor`, so that
`𝒢 = (V ⟶ V')^*𝒢'` and `ℱ' = (U' ⟶ V')^*𝒢'`, then `𝒢'` is of finite presentation if and only if
`𝒢` and `ℱ'` are of finite presentation
(Stacks 03DL (7), `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_restrict :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom B S hS i f hi hf
    ∀ {V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f),
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom →
      ∀ M : (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory,
      (SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite M.obj ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite
          (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
            (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
              (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
              (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
            fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj M.property).obj M).obj.target ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite
          (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
            (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
              (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
              (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
            fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
              M.property).obj M).obj.ambient)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KV, the equivalence.**  Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be a thickening and
`f : X ⟶ Y` an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` be their pushout
(Stacks 07VX) and let `g : V' ⟶ Y'` be a morphism, with `V = Y ×_{Y'} V'`, `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'`
and `U = X ×_{Y'} V'`.  The functor `𝒢' ↦ ((V ⟶ V')^*𝒢', (U' ⟶ V')^*𝒢', can)` is an
**equivalence of categories** from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_{V'}`-modules flat over `Y'` onto the
triples `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)` of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_V`-module `𝒢` flat over `Y`, a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_{U'}`-module `ℱ'` flat over `X'` and an isomorphism `φ : (U ⟶ V)^*𝒢 ≅ (U ⟶ U')^*ℱ'`.

The source writes "`ℱ'` … flat over `X`": `ℱ'` lives on `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'`, which lies over
`X'`, so the condition is flatness over `X'`, as in the scheme case Stacks 08KU.  The pushout is
not assumed: it exists by Stacks 07VX
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom`), which is the instance
the statement binds.  The functor is written out as the lift to the two full subcategories of
`CategoryTheory.TripleGluing.restrictFunctor` at the canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.squareOverlap`; a quasi-inverse is the gluing functor
`(𝒢, ℱ', φ) ↦ (V ⟶ V')_*𝒢 ×_{(U ⟶ V')_*ℱ} (U' ⟶ V')_*ℱ'`
(`isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor_of_hasPushout`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom B S hS i f hi hf
    ∀ {V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f),
      ((((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
      (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g) (targetRestriction i f g)
      (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
        fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj M.property) :
        (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).FullSubcategory)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor_and_finiteness_iff_restrict
declarations.doc:
Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be a thickening and `f : X ⟶ Y` an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`, let `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` be their pushout (Stacks 07VX) and let `g : V' ⟶ Y'` be a morphism, with
`V = Y ×_{Y'} V'`, `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'` and `U = X ×_{Y'} V'`.

* The functor `𝒢' ↦ ((V ⟶ V')^*𝒢', (U' ⟶ V')^*𝒢', can)` is an **equivalence of categories**
  from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_{V'}`-modules flat over `Y'` onto the triples `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)` of a
  quasi-coherent `𝒪_V`-module `𝒢` flat over `Y`, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{U'}`-module `ℱ'` flat over
  `X'` and an isomorphism `φ : (U ⟶ V)^*𝒢 ≅ (U ⟶ U')^*ℱ'`.
* Suppose `𝒢'` corresponds to the triple `(𝒢, ℱ', φ)`, so that `𝒢 = (V ⟶ V')^*𝒢'` and
  `ℱ' = (U' ⟶ V')^*𝒢'`. Then
  (a) `𝒢'` is of finite type if and only if `𝒢` and `ℱ'` are of finite type;
  (b) if `g` is locally of finite presentation, then `𝒢'` is of finite presentation if and only
  if `𝒢` and `ℱ'` are of finite presentation (Stacks 03DL (7),
  `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite`).

The source writes "`ℱ'` … flat over `X`": `ℱ'` lives on `U' = X' ×_{Y'} V'`, which lies over
`X'`, so the condition is flatness over `X'`, as in the scheme case Stacks 08KU.  The pushout is
not assumed: it exists by Stacks 07VX
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom`), which is the instance
the statement binds.  The functor is written out as the lift to the two full subcategories of
`CategoryTheory.TripleGluing.restrictFunctor` at the canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PushoutModules.squareOverlap`; a quasi-inverse is the gluing functor
`(𝒢, ℱ', φ) ↦ (V ⟶ V')_*𝒢 ×_{(U ⟶ V')_*ℱ} (U' ⟶ V')_*ℱ'`
(`isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor_of_hasPushout`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_flatRestrictionFunctor_and_finiteness_iff_restrict :
    letI := hasPushout_of_isThickeningHom_of_isAffineHom B S hS i f hi hf
    ∀ {V' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : V' ⟶ pushout i f),
      ((((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
          (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
            (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
            (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
        fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj M.property) :
        (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory ⥤
          (FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).FullSubcategory)).IsEquivalence ∧
      (∀ (M : (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory),
        M.obj.IsFiniteType ↔
          (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
            (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
              (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
              (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
            fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
              M.property).obj M).obj.target.IsFiniteType ∧
          (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
            (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
              (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
              (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
            fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
              M.property).obj M).obj.ambient.IsFiniteType) ∧
      (IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom →
        ∀ M : (FlatQuasicoherentOver g).FullSubcategory,
        (SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite M.obj ↔
          SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite
            (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
              (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
                (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
                (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
              fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj M.property).obj M).obj.target ∧
          SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite
            (((FlatQuasicoherentTriple i f g).lift ((FlatQuasicoherentOver g).ι ⋙
              (TripleGluing.restrictFunctor (squareOverlap (commonToTarget i f g)
                (targetRestriction i f g) (commonToAmbient i f g) (ambientRestriction i f g)
                (commonToAmbient_comp_eq i f g))))
              fun M => flatQuasicoherentTriple_restrict i f g M.obj
                M.property).obj M).obj.ambient))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings
declarations.doc:
A morphism of thickenings: a commutative square of ringed spaces whose horizontal arrows are
thickenings.
declarations.statement: structure MorphismOfThickenings
declarations.comment: the commutative square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.idealMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `(f')^* J ⟶ I`: after inclusion into `𝒪_{X'}`, it is the restriction of
`(f')^♯` to the pullback of `J`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def idealMap (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u}) :
    { g : (modulePullback D.f').obj D.idealJ ⟶ D.idealI //
      g ≫ kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit (structureSheafHom D.i)) =
        D.ambientIdealMap }
declarations.comment: the canonical ideal map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.firstOrderSurjection
declarations.doc:
The canonical reduction map `(f')^* J ⟶ i_* f^* t^* J`: the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*`, followed by
the pushforward of `reducedPullbackComparison`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def firstOrderSurjection (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u})
    (_hi : IsFirstOrderThickening D.i) (_ht : IsFirstOrderThickening D.t) :
    (modulePullback D.f').obj D.idealJ ⟶ D.reducedPullbackIdeal
declarations.comment: the first-order canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.firstOrderSurjection_epi
declarations.doc:
When both thickenings are first order, the canonical reduction map
`(f')^* J ⟶ i_* f^* t^* J` is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstOrderSurjection_epi (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u})
    (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening D.i) (ht : IsFirstOrderThickening D.t) :
    Epi (D.firstOrderSurjection hi ht)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the first-order canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.firstOrderIdealMap
declarations.doc:
If both thickenings are first order, the canonical ideal map `(f')^* J ⟶ I` factors uniquely
through the reduction `(f')^* J ⟶ i_* f^* J`, giving a map `f^* J ⟶ I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def firstOrderIdealMap (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u})
    (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening D.i) (ht : IsFirstOrderThickening D.t) :
    { g : D.reducedPullbackIdeal ⟶ D.idealI //
      D.firstOrderSurjection hi ht ≫ g = D.idealMap.1 ∧
        ∀ g' : D.reducedPullbackIdeal ⟶ D.idealI,
          D.firstOrderSurjection hi ht ≫ g' = D.idealMap.1 → g' = g }
declarations.comment: the first-order factorization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.exists_factorization_of_comp_idealι_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08KZ.** Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be a thickening and `f : Y ⟶ X'` a morphism
of ringed spaces whose comorphism kills the kernel ideal `ℐ = ker(i^♯)`. Then `f` factors
through `i`.

The factorization of sheaves of modules exists because `i^♯` is an epimorphism killed by `ℐ`,
which is what `Abelian.epiDesc` supplies; `exists_ringHom_of_additive_factorization` upgrades
its underlying additive map to a map of sheaves of rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_comp_idealι_eq_zero
    {X Y X' : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (i : X ⟶ X') (f : Y ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsThickening i)
    (h : kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit (structureSheafHom i)) ≫
      SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit (structureSheafHom f) = 0) :
    ∃ p : Y ⟶ X, p ≫ i = f
declarations.comment: factoring through a thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.epi_baseToSourceIdeal
declarations.doc:
For a strict morphism of thickenings the reduced canonical ideal map `f^* t^* J ⟶ i^* I` is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_baseToSourceIdeal (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u}) (hs : D.IsStrict) :
    Epi D.baseToSourceIdeal
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the reduced canonical ideal map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.IsStrict
declarations.doc:
A morphism of thickenings is *strict* when the canonical map `(f')^* J ⟶ I` of ideal sheaves
is surjective, i.e. an epimorphism of sheaves of `𝒪_{X'}`-modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev IsStrict (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: strict morphism of thickenings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.isStrict_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L2.** A cartesian square of thickenings is strict.

For a point `x` of `X'` the test object `testPoint x` maps to `X'`, and its composite with `f'`
factors through the thickening `t`; the square, being cartesian, therefore lifts it to `X`, and
the lift forces the comorphism of `testPoint x` to kill `I`. So the germ at `x` of a section of
`I` is a germ of a section in the range of the ambient ideal map, and `(f')^* J ⟶ I` is locally
surjective.
declarations.statement: theorem isStrict_of_isPullback (hc : IsPullback D.i D.f D.f' D.t) : D.IsStrict
declarations.comment: a cartesian square is strict

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.isStrict_iff_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L2.** A morphism of thickenings of ringed spaces is strict if and
only if its square is cartesian in the category of ringed spaces. The forward implication is
`isPullback_of_isStrict`; the converse is `isStrict_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement: theorem isStrict_iff_isPullback : D.IsStrict ↔ IsPullback D.i D.f D.f' D.t
declarations.comment: strict iff cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.MorphismOfThickenings.isPullback_of_isStrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L2.** A strict morphism of thickenings has a cartesian square: both
thickenings are monomorphisms, so uniqueness of a lift is automatic, and existence is the
factorization of a test morphism through `i` supplied by
`exists_factorization_of_comp_idealι_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_of_isStrict (D : MorphismOfThickenings.{u}) (hs : D.IsStrict) :
    IsPullback D.i D.f D.f' D.t
declarations.comment: a strict morphism has a cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.firstOrderExtensionAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L4.** The canonical map `c_{ℱ'} : i^* ℐ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ ⟶ 𝒦` of an
extension `0 ⟶ i_* 𝒦 ⟶ ℱ' ⟶ i_* ℱ ⟶ 0` of `𝒪_{X'}`-modules across a first order thickening
`i`.

The bundled equation is the local lifting characterisation from the source: on an open set of
`X'` over which a section `s` of `i_* ℱ` lifts to a section `s'` of `ℱ'`, the image in `ℱ'` of
`c_{ℱ'}(a ⊗ s)` is the scalar multiple `a · s'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def firstOrderExtensionAction
    (F K : SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩))
        (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
      ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0) :
    { c : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
        ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj ((idealSheafPullback i))).obj (F)) ⟶ K //
      ∀ (U : Opens X') (a : (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.idealSheaf i).val.obj (op U))
        (s : ((modulePushforward i).obj F).val.obj (op U)) (s' : E.Z.left.val.obj (op U)),
        (E.g.val.app (op U)).hom s' = s →
          (E.f.val.app (op U)).hom
              ((((modulePushforward i).map c).val.app (op U)).hom
                (((extensionTensorComparison i F).val.app (op U)).hom
                  (toTensorSheafSection X' (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.idealSheaf i)
                    ((modulePushforward i).obj F) (op U)
                    (a ⊗ₜ[X'.presheaf.obj (op U)] s)))) =
            (show ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u}
                ⟨X'.presheaf, X'.IsSheaf⟩).obj.obj (op U) : Type u) from
              ((idealSheafι i).val.app (op U)).hom a) • s' }
declarations.comment: the canonical map

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
registrations.comment: the short exact sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.ExtensionPair.extensionAction_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L5**, part (1). If the middle terms of two extensions across a
first order thickening are linked by a map `φ'` compatible with `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` and `ψ : 𝒦 ⟶ ℒ`,
then the canonical maps of the two extensions commute with `1 ⊗ φ` and `ψ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionAction_naturality (S : ExtensionPair.{u}) (c : CompatibleMap S) :
    (firstOrderExtensionAction S.i S.F S.K S.firstOrder S.firstExtension).val ≫ S.kernelMap =
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((S.X)).presheaf,
          ((S.X)).IsSheaf⟩)).map (((𝟙 (idealSheafPullback S.i)), S.quotientMap) : (_, _) ⟶
          (_, _))) ≫
        (firstOrderExtensionAction S.i S.G S.L S.firstOrder S.secondExtension).val
declarations.comment: part (1): compatibility of the canonical maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.ExtensionPair.exists_compatibleMap_translate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L5.** Translating a compatible map `φ'` by a map `α : ℱ ⟶ ℒ`, that
is adding the composite `ℱ' ⟶ i_* ℱ ⟶ i_* ℒ ⟶ 𝒢'`, again gives a compatible map. This is the
action of `Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ℒ)` on the set of compatible maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_compatibleMap_translate (c : CompatibleMap S) (α : S.F ⟶ S.L) :
    ∃ d : CompatibleMap S,
      d.hom = c.hom +
        S.firstExtension.g ≫ (modulePushforward S.i).map α ≫ S.secondExtension.f
declarations.comment: the action on compatible maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.ExtensionPair.existsUnique_translate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L5.** Any two compatible maps differ by a unique
`α : ℱ ⟶ ℒ`. Together with `exists_compatibleMap_translate` this says that the set of
compatible maps is, when nonempty, a principal homogeneous space under
`Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ℒ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_translate (c d : CompatibleMap S) :
    ∃! α : S.F ⟶ S.L,
      d.hom = c.hom +
        S.firstExtension.g ≫ (modulePushforward S.i).map α ≫ S.secondExtension.f
declarations.comment: freeness and transitivity of the action

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.mapLiftingObstruction
declarations.doc:
The obstruction `o(φ, ψ) ∈ Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ℒ)` to lifting a pair of maps `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` and
`ψ : 𝒦 ⟶ ℒ`, compatible with the canonical maps of two extensions across a first order
thickening, to a map of the extensions themselves: the class vanishes exactly when an
`𝒪_{X'}`-module map `φ' : ℱ' ⟶ 𝒢'` inducing `ψ` on kernels and `φ` on quotients exists.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def mapLiftingObstruction
    [HasExt (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (F K G L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
      ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0)
    (E' : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
      ((modulePushforward i).obj G) ((modulePushforward i).obj L) 0)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) (ψ : K ⟶ L)
    (hcompat : (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E).val ≫ ψ =
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩)).map (((𝟙 (idealSheafPullback i)), φ) :
          ((idealSheafPullback i), F) ⟶ ((idealSheafPullback i), G))) ≫
        (firstOrderExtensionAction i G L hi E').val) :
    { o : CategoryTheory.Abelian.zExt F L 1 //
      o = 0 ↔ ∃ φ' : E.Z.left ⟶ E'.Z.left,
        E.f ≫ φ' = (modulePushforward i).map ψ ≫ E'.f ∧
          φ' ≫ E'.g = E.g ≫ (modulePushforward i).map φ }
declarations.comment: the obstruction class and its vanishing criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.extensionClassesWithAction_principalHomogeneous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08L7.** Let `i : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (X', 𝒪_{X'})` be a first order thickening of ringed
spaces, `ℱ`, `𝒦` two `𝒪_X`-modules and `c : ℐ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ ⟶ 𝒦` an `𝒪_X`-linear map. The
isomorphism classes of extensions `0 ⟶ i_* 𝒦 ⟶ ℱ' ⟶ i_* ℱ ⟶ 0` of `𝒪_{X'}`-modules with
`c_{ℱ'} = c` (the set `extensionClassesWithAction i F K hi c ⊆ Ext¹_{𝒪_{X'}}(i_* ℱ, i_* 𝒦)`)
form a principal homogeneous space under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)`, acting by `ξ • η = η + i_* ξ`:

* the action preserves the set;
* it is an action of the group `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)`: `0` acts trivially and `ξ + ξ'` acts as
  `ξ` followed by `ξ'`;
* it is simply transitive: any two elements `η`, `η'` of the set satisfy `η' = η + i_* ξ` for
  exactly one `ξ ∈ Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)`.

So as soon as the set is nonempty (the source's hypothesis that some sequence (08L4) with
`c_{ℱ'} = c` exists, `hc`), every point `η₀` of it identifies it with `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` via
`ξ ↦ η₀ + i_* ξ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionClassesWithAction_principalHomogeneous
    {X X' : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (F K : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    [HasExt.{e} (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasExt.{e} (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X'))]
    (c : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj
      ((idealSheafPullback i))).obj (F)) ⟶ K)
    (hc : ∃ E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
        ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0,
      (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E).val = c) :
    haveI := preservesFiniteColimits_modulePushforward i hi.1
    haveI := preservesFiniteLimits_modulePushforward i
    (extensionClassesWithAction.{e} i F K hi c).Nonempty ∧
      (∀ η ∈ extensionClassesWithAction.{e} i F K hi c, ∀ ξ : Abelian.Ext.{e} F K 1,
        η + ξ.mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i) ∈ extensionClassesWithAction.{e} i F K hi c) ∧
      (∀ η : Abelian.Ext.{e} ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 1,
        η + (0 : Abelian.Ext.{e} F K 1).mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i) = η ∧
          ∀ ξ ξ' : Abelian.Ext.{e} F K 1,
            η + (ξ + ξ').mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i) =
              (η + ξ.mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i)) +
                ξ'.mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i)) ∧
      ∀ η ∈ extensionClassesWithAction.{e} i F K hi c,
        ∀ η' ∈ extensionClassesWithAction.{e} i F K hi c,
          ∃! ξ : Abelian.Ext.{e} F K 1, η + ξ.mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i) = η'
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, for a first order thickening of ringed spaces: the isomorphism classes of extensions as in 08L4 with `c_{ℱ'} = c`, represented by their classes in `Ext¹_{𝒪_{X'}}(i_* ℱ, i_* 𝒦)`, form a principal homogeneous space under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` acting through `i_*` by Baer sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.exists_extClass_add_of_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08L7, the action.** Adding to an extension one whose middle term is a direct
image does not change the canonical map: such an extension has vanishing canonical map
(**Stacks 08KS**) and the canonical map is additive for Baer sums
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.exists_baerSum_firstOrderExtensionAction`).

This is the source's "conversely, given such an extension `ℰ` we can add the extension `ℰ` to
the `𝒪_{X'}`-extension `ℱ'` without affecting the map `c_{ℱ'}`". By **Stacks 08KS** the
extensions whose middle term is a direct image are exactly the extensions of `𝒪_X`-modules,
which is how `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` acts.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extClass_add_of_essImage (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (E₀ D : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
      ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0)
    (hD : (modulePushforward i).essImage D.Z.left) :
    ∃ E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
        ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0,
      (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact E).extClass =
          (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact E₀).extClass +
            (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact D).extClass ∧
        (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E).val =
          (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E₀).val
declarations.comment: the action of `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)`: adding an extension of `𝒪_X`-modules, read on `X'` as one whose middle term is a direct image, does not change the canonical map. SCOPE: this clause only; the simple transitivity of the action is `existsUnique_extClass_sub_of_firstOrderExtensionAction_eq`, and the identification of the subgroup of such classes with `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` itself is not formalized here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.existsUnique_extClass_sub_of_firstOrderExtensionAction_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08L7, simple transitivity.** Two extensions across the thickening with the same
canonical map differ, in `Ext¹_{𝒪_{X'}}(i_* ℱ, i_* 𝒦)`, by the class of exactly one extension
whose middle term is a direct image — hence, by **Stacks 08KS**, by the class of an extension of
`𝒪_X`-modules.

This is the source's "the difference is an extension `0 → 𝒦 → ℰ → ℱ → 0` where `ℰ` is
annihilated by `ℐ`, hence is an extension of `𝒪_X`-modules". Uniqueness is uniqueness of a
difference in the group `Ext¹_{𝒪_{X'}}(i_* ℱ, i_* 𝒦)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_extClass_sub_of_firstOrderExtensionAction_eq (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (E₀ E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
      ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0)
    (h : (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E).val =
      (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E₀).val) :
    ∃! ξ : CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.{w}
        ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 1,
      (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact E).extClass =
          (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact E₀).extClass + ξ ∧
        ∃ D : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
            ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0,
          (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact D).extClass = ξ ∧
            (modulePushforward i).essImage D.Z.left
declarations.comment: simple transitivity: two extensions with the same canonical map differ by the class of exactly one extension whose middle term is a direct image, i.e. of an extension of `𝒪_X`-modules. SCOPE: this clause only; the identification of the group of such classes with `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` itself is not formalized here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.existsUnique_ext_mapExactFunctor_eq
declarations.doc:
The classes in `Ext¹_{𝒪_{X'}}(i_* ℱ, i_* 𝒦)` whose extensions have a direct image as middle
term are exactly the images of `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` under `i_*`, each attained by exactly one
class.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_ext_mapExactFunctor_eq (hi : IsThickening i)
    (ξ' : CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.{w}
      ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 1)
    (h : ∃ D : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
        ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0,
      (CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension.shortExact D).extClass = ξ' ∧
        (modulePushforward i).essImage D.Z.left) :
    ∃! ξ : CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.{w} F K 1,
      ξ.mapExactFunctor (modulePushforward i) = ξ'
declarations.comment: the identification of the group of classes whose extensions have a direct image as middle term with `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` itself: such a class is `i_*` of exactly one class on `X`. SCOPE: this clause only; the action of those classes is `exists_extClass_add_of_essImage` and the simple transitivity is `existsUnique_extClass_sub_of_firstOrderExtensionAction_eq`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.extensionExistenceObstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08L8.** The obstruction `o(ℱ, 𝒦, c) ∈ Ext²_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒦)` to the
existence of an extension of `𝒪_{X'}`-modules `0 ⟶ i_* 𝒦 ⟶ ℱ' ⟶ i_* ℱ ⟶ 0` as in Tag 08L4 whose
canonical map `c_{ℱ'}` is a prescribed `𝒪_X`-linear map `c : ℐ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ ⟶ 𝒦`.

The class is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.obstructionClass`, and the bundled property
is the content of the lemma: it vanishes exactly when such an extension exists.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionExistenceObstruction
    [HasExt (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (F K : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (c : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} ⟨((X)).presheaf,
        ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj ((idealSheafPullback i))).obj (F)) ⟶ K) :
    { o : CategoryTheory.Abelian.zExt F K 2 //
      o = 0 ↔ ∃ E : CategoryTheory.Abelian.YonedaExtension
          ((modulePushforward i).obj F) ((modulePushforward i).obj K) 0,
        (firstOrderExtensionAction i F K hi E).val = c }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.structureSheafSplitEpi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08L9.** A trivialization of a thickening splits its structure-sheaf map: the
structure-sheaf map `𝒪_X ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{X'}` of the retraction, reindexed along
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.retraction_opens_obj`, is a section of
`i^♯ : 𝒪_{X'} ⟶ i_* 𝒪_X`.

This is the step the source phrases as "using `π^♯` to split the surjection
`𝒪_{X'} ⟶ 𝒪_X`". It is the converse of `Deformation.RingThickening.retractionFromSplitting`,
and it supplies the `CategoryTheory.SplitMono` that
`Deformation.RingThickening.splittingFromTrivialization` takes as a hypothesis — so the two
together, and neither alone, give the source's "given `π` we obtain a splitting".
declarations.statement: noncomputable def structureSheafSplitEpi : SplitEpi i.hom.c
declarations.comment: a trivialization splits the structure-sheaf map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.trivializedThickeningEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The category of trivialized first order thickenings of a ringed space `(X, 𝒪_X)` is
equivalent to the opposite of the category of `𝒪_X`-modules.

A trivialization `π` of a first order thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` splits the surjection
`𝒪_{X'} ⟶ 𝒪_X`, giving `𝒪_{X'} = 𝒪_X ⊕ ℐ` as sheaves of algebras on `X`, and conversely such a
splitting determines `π`. The equivalence sends an `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` to the trivial square-zero
extension `(X, 𝒪_X ⋉ 𝒢)` with the zero section as trivialization, and a trivialized thickening
back to its ideal read along the trivialization.

It is contravariant for the source's own convention for morphisms: `TrivializedThickening X`
has its Hom in the geometric direction, a morphism of thickenings of `(X, 𝒪_X)` being a
morphism `X'₁ ⟶ X'₂` of ringed spaces (Stacks 08LD), and that is a morphism
`𝒪_{X'₂} ⟶ 𝒪_{X'₁}` of sheaves of algebras on `X`, hence a morphism `ℐ₂ ⟶ ℐ₁` of the ideals
(Stacks 08LC).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def trivializedThickeningEquivalence (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) :
    (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))ᵒᵖ ≌ TrivializedThickening X
declarations.comment: the category of trivialized first order thickenings of (X, 𝒪_X) is equivalent to the category of 𝒪_X-modules; morphisms of thickenings run in the geometric direction (X'₁ ⟶ X'₂ of ringed spaces, Stacks 08LD), so the module side carries ᵒᵖ

declarations.name: Deformation.RingThickening.splittingFromTrivialization
declarations.doc:
A trivialization identifies a first order thickening with the trivial square-zero extension
by its kernel ideal.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def splittingFromTrivialization
    (split : A ⟶ A') (π : SplitMono split)
    (h_sq : ∀ U : C, RingHom.ker (π.retraction.app U).hom ^ 2 = ⊥) :
  PresheafTrivialSquareZeroEquiv A' A π.retraction split
declarations.comment: splitting_from_trivialization

declarations.name: Deformation.RingThickening.retractionFromSplitting
declarations.doc:
The section of the structure-sheaf map, transported along the inverse homeomorphism of the
base map, defines a morphism of ringed spaces in the opposite direction.
declarations.comment: trivialization_from_splitting

declarations.name: Deformation.RingThickening.retractionFromSplitting_comp
declarations.doc:
The morphism induced by a splitting of the structure-sheaf map retracts the original
morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem retractionFromSplitting_comp {X X' : RingedSpace.{u, v}}
    (i : X ⟶ X') [IsIso i.hom.base]
    (splitting : SplitEpi i.hom.c) :
    i ≫ retractionFromSplitting i splitting = 𝟙 X
declarations.comment: trivialization_from_splitting

registrations.comment: trivial_thickening_and_trivialization

registrations.comment: the splitting determined by a trivialization
