    (hX : IsSliceStandardEndofunctor A B X) :
    Nonempty
      (((SimplicialObject.Augmented.whiskeringObj _ _ (Over.forget B)).obj
        ((SimplicialObject.Augmented.whiskeringObj _ _
        ((evaluation (Over B) (Over B)).obj (Over.mk (𝟙 B)))).obj X)) ≅
        standardResolution A B)
declarations.comment: comparison of standard resolutions

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.postAdjunctionRight
registrations.comment: the adjunction

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.post_forget_eq_forget_comp
registrations.comment: the commutative square

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The site `C_{B/A}`: the opposite of the category of polynomial `A`-algebras
augmented to `B`. Its topology is the chaotic one, recorded through the ringed point below.
declarations.statement: abbrev polynomialSite
declarations.comment: the site C_{B/A}

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialTopology_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The topology of `C_{B/A}` is the chaotic topology: its only coverings are
the maximal sieves, so every presheaf on `C_{B/A}` is a sheaf.
declarations.statement: theorem polynomialTopology_eq_bot : polynomialTopology A B = ⊥
declarations.comment: the chaotic topology on C_{B/A}

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The tautological sheaf of rings `𝒪` on `C_{B/A}`, which sends the object
`(P, α)` to `P`. It is a sheaf because the topology of `C_{B/A}` is chaotic.
declarations.statement: def polynomialStructureSheaf : Sheaf (polynomialTopology A B) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf 𝒪

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialConstantSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The constant sheaf of rings `B` on `C_{B/A}`, written with an underline in
the source. By Tag 08PF it is the inverse image along `π` of the ring on the point.
declarations.statement: def polynomialConstantSheaf : Sheaf (polynomialTopology A B) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: the constant sheaf B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialConstantSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The constant sheaf of rings `B` of Tag 08PF is the constant presheaf with
value `B`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialConstantSheafIso :
    (polynomialConstantSheaf A B).obj ≅ polynomialConstantPresheaf A B
declarations.comment: the constant sheaf B is constant

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAugmentation
declarations.doc: **Stacks 08PR.** The map of sheaves of rings `𝒪 → B` given by the augmentations.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialAugmentation :
    polynomialStructureSheaf A B ⟶ polynomialConstantSheaf A B
declarations.comment: the augmentation 𝒪 ⟶ B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAugmentation_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** On sections over the object `(P, α)` of `C_{B/A}`, the augmentation of
sheaves of rings is `α`, read through the identification of the constant sheaf with the constant
presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialAugmentation_app (X : polynomialSite A B) :
    (polynomialAugmentation A B).hom.app (Opposite.op X) ≫
        (polynomialConstantSheafIso A B).hom.app (Opposite.op X) =
      (polynomialAugmentationPresheaf A B).app (Opposite.op X)
declarations.comment: the augmentation is given by α

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The morphism of ringed topoi `i : (Sh(C_{B/A}), B) ⟶ (Sh(C_{B/A}), 𝒪)`:
the identity on underlying topoi, with `i♯ : 𝒪 ⟶ i_*B` the augmentation.
declarations.comment: the morphism i of ringed topoi

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialInclusion_toToposHom
declarations.doc: **Stacks 08PR.** The geometric morphism underlying `i` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialInclusion_toToposHom :
    (polynomialInclusion A B).toToposHom = polynomialIdentityTopos A B
declarations.comment: i is the identity on topoi

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PR.** The morphism of ringed topoi `π : (Sh(C_{B/A}), B) ⟶ (Sh(*), B)`, the
projection of the chaotic site to its ringed point.
declarations.statement: abbrev polynomialProjection
declarations.comment: the morphism π of ringed topoi

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.boundedPolynomialSite
declarations.doc:
The site `C_{B/A}` cut down to the polynomial algebras on at most `κ` variables: the opposite
of `CommAlgCat.BoundedPolynomialAugmentation`. For `κ = #B` this is the site of the source,
footnote included; `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite` is the same construction with the footnote
omitted.
declarations.statement: abbrev boundedPolynomialSite
declarations.comment: the site C_{B/A} with the section's footnote in force, restricting the sets of variables to cardinality at most κ. The unrestricted version is `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite`; only this one is essentially small

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_homotopyEquivalences_resolutionMor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PS**. Let `P_•` be a simplicial `A`-algebra endowed with an augmentation
`ε : P_• ⟶ B`, assume every `P_n` is a polynomial algebra over `A` and that `ε` is a trivial Kan
fibration on underlying simplicial sets. Then for every object `W = (Q, β)` of the site `C_{B/A}`
the simplicial set `Mor_{C_{B/A}}((P_•, ε), W)` is homotopy equivalent to the constant simplicial
set on a singleton, which is the hypothesis the criterion of Tag 08Q9 asks of the cosimplicial
object `CommAlgCat.resolutionCosimplicialObject` of the resolution.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyEquivalences_resolutionMor
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A))))
    (W : polynomialSite A B) :
    ∃ f : (resolutionCosimplicialObject ε hP).op ⋙ yoneda.obj W ⟶
        (Functor.const SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ).obj PUnit.{u + 1},
      SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type u) f
declarations.comment: the hypothesis of the criterion of Tag 08Q9 for the cosimplicial object of a resolution: each `Mor_C((P_•, ε), W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. The conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)`, resp. `D(B)`, functorially in `ℱ`, is not asserted: the criterion as formalized asks for a small site, and `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite` is large — see the first implementation note

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)`, functorially in `ℱ`, at the site `C_{B/A}`.**
Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a simplicial `A`-algebra endowed with an augmentation to `B`, assume every
`P_n` is a polynomial algebra over `A` and that `ε` is a trivial Kan fibration on underlying
simplicial sets. Then the extended Moore complex of the simplicial abelian group `ℱ(P_•, ε)` is
`Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(Ab)`, as an **isomorphism of functors** of the abelian sheaf `ℱ` on the site
`C_{B/A}` of Tag 08PR -- the abelian presheaves being its abelian sheaves, the topology being
chaotic.

This is the abelian half of the conclusion of Tag 08PS. The hypothesis of the criterion of
Tag 08Q9 is `CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_resolutionCosimplicialObject`, and
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge` is that criterion in
its derived form, natural in the coefficient presheaf and with no smallness hypothesis on the
site.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialSiteResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A)))) :
    Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainComplex'
          (resolutionCosimplicialObject ε hP) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single ((polynomialSite A B)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          totalDerivedColimit' (polynomialSite A B) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Ab(C_{B/A})`, at `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite` -- the site of Tag 08PR itself, not a restriction of it -- as an isomorphism in the derived category, with `π_!` in its colimit presentation of Tag 08PF and the coefficients at the universe `u + 1` of the site's objects

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteResolutionModuleDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)`, functorially in `ℱ`, at the site `C_{B/A}`.**
Under the hypotheses of Tag 08PS, the extended Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module
`ℱ(P_•, ε)` is `Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(B)`, as an **isomorphism of functors** of the sheaf of `B`-modules
`ℱ` on the site `C_{B/A}` of Tag 08PR -- the diagrams of `B`-modules on the site being its
`B̲`-modules, the topology being chaotic.

This is the module half of the conclusion of Tag 08PS, beside the abelian half
`CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso`: the same hypothesis
`CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_resolutionCosimplicialObject` -- which does not mention the
coefficients -- is fed to
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge`. The coefficient ring is
`ULift.{u + 1} B`, the ring of the site's ringed point
`CommAlgCat.polynomialRingedPoint`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialSiteResolutionModuleDerivedColimitNatIso
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A)))) :
    Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainComplex'
          (resolutionCosimplicialObject ε hP)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single
          ((polynomialSite A B)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u)))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          totalDerivedColimit' (polynomialSite A B)
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u)))
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, at `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite` -- the site of Tag 08PR itself, not a restriction of it -- as an isomorphism in the derived category, with the coefficient ring read as `ULift.{u+1} B` exactly as the site's own ringed point `CommAlgCat.polynomialRingedPoint` reads it

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a resolution of `B` over `A` whose terms are polynomial algebras on at
most `κ` variables. For every sheaf of `B`-modules `ℱ` on the small model of the restricted site
`C_{B/A}`, the sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)` are the degree `n` homology of the Moore
complex of the simplicial `B`-module `ℱ(P_•, ε)`, naturally in `ℱ`; here `π` is the point
morphism of the small model.
declarations.statement:
def smallResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A))))
    (n : ℕ) :
    (modulePointLowerShriek (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)
          (B : Type u)).leftDerived n ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ))
          (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ⋙
        moduleCosimplicialMooreComplex (smallResolutionCosimplicialObject ε κ hPκ) ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))
            (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site, for the same reason as recorded for the abelian half in `StacksFrontier/Cotangent/ResolutionPointCriterionSmall.lean`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08PT] at module coefficients.** Let `C` be a small
category with the chaotic topology, `B` a ring, and `U_•` a cosimplicial object of `C` such that
every simplicial set `Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. Then for every
diagram `ℱ` of `B`-modules on `Cᵒᵖ` — that is, every `B̲`-module on the chaotic site — the
extended Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module `ℱ(U_•)` computes derived lower shriek:

`Q(ℱ(U_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(B)`.

Here `Lπ_!` is `Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit`, the total left derived functor of
the colimit over `Cᵒᵖ`, which is `π_!` on the chaotic site by [Stacks, Tag 08PF]. The proof
compares the two filtrations of the double complex obtained by evaluating a projective resolution
of `ℱ` on `U_•`.

The isomorphism depends on the chosen projective resolution and is not asserted to be natural in
`ℱ`; see the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
def mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit (hU : IsPointResolution U) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((mooreCochainComplex U).obj F) ≅
      (totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((HomologicalComplex.single (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F))
declarations.comment: derived form at module coefficients, for one module over the constant sheaf of rings: the extended Moore complex of the evaluation on a point resolution is derived lower shriek in D(B), derived lower shriek being the total left derived functor of the colimit over the index category. Not asserted natural in the coefficient module

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08PT] at module coefficients is independent of the point
resolution**, compatibly with morphisms of point resolutions. For a morphism `v : U_• ⟶ V_•` of
cosimplicial objects of `C`, both point resolutions, and a diagram `ℱ` of `B`-modules on `Cᵒᵖ`,
the triangle

`Q(ℱ(V_•)) ⟶ Q(ℱ(U_•)) ⟶ Lπ_!(ℱ)`

commutes, the second arrow being
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit` at `U_•` and the composite being
the same isomorphism at `V_•`. This is the totalized form of the canonical map of
[Stacks, Tag 08Q6]: the comparison of the extended Moore complex of a point resolution with
derived lower shriek does not depend on the point resolution.

The projective resolution of `ℱ` chosen by
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit` is built from `ℱ` alone, so one
and the same resolution serves both point resolutions and the statement is
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimitOfResolution_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit_naturality (v : U ⟶ V) (hU : IsPointResolution U)
    (hV : IsPointResolution V) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map ((mooreCochainMap v).app F) ≫
        (mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit U F hU).hom =
      (mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit V F hV).hom
declarations.comment: the derived form at module coefficients is natural in the point resolution: a morphism of cosimplicial objects between two point resolutions carries the comparison at one to the comparison at the other. Still not asserted natural in the coefficient module

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionAbelianDerivedLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PT, in `D(Ab)`.** Let `A → B` be a ring map and let `ε : P_• → B` be the standard
resolution of `B` over `A`. Let `π` be as in Tag 08PR. Then

`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)`, functorially in `ℱ` in `Ab(C)`.

Here `C = C_{B/A}` is the site of Tag 08PR (`CommAlgCat.polynomialSite`), whose topology is chaotic
so that `Ab(C)` is the category of abelian presheaves on it, with coefficients in
`Type (u + 1)`, the universe in which colimits over `C` exist; `Lπ_!` is
`CommAlgCat.polynomialDerivedLowerShriek`; and `ℱ(P_•, ε)` is the extended Moore complex of
the simplicial abelian group obtained by evaluating `ℱ` on the cosimplicial object of `C` given
by the standard resolution. The standard resolution satisfies the hypotheses of Tag 08PS by
Tag 08QI: its terms are polynomial algebras, and its augmentation is a homotopy equivalence of
underlying simplicial sets (Tag 08ND), hence a quasi-isomorphism of associated complexes
(Tag 08P2), hence a trivial Kan fibration (Tag 08P1).
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionAbelianDerivedLowerShriekIso :
    polynomialMooreCochain A B
        (resolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
          (standardResolution_isResolution.{u, u} A B).isPolynomialAlgebra)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single ((polynomialSite A B)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
        polynomialDerivedLowerShriek A B AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Ab(C)`, on the site `C_{B/A}` of 08PR, with coefficients in the universe above that of `A` and `B`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionModuleDerivedLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PT, in `D(B)`.** Let `A → B` be a ring map and let `ε : P_• → B` be the standard
resolution of `B` over `A`. Let `π` be as in Tag 08PR. Then

`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)`, functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`.

Here `C = C_{B/A}` is the site of Tag 08PR (`CommAlgCat.polynomialSite`), whose topology is chaotic
so that a `B̲`-module is a diagram of `B`-modules on it, with sections in `Type (u + 1)`, the
universe in which colimits over `C` exist, `B` being lifted to that universe as the ring on the
point of `π` is; `Lπ_!` is `CommAlgCat.polynomialDerivedLowerShriek`; and `ℱ(P_•, ε)` is the
extended Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module obtained by evaluating `ℱ` on the
cosimplicial object of `C` given by the standard resolution. The standard resolution satisfies
the hypotheses of Tag 08PS by Tag 08QI, as recorded at
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionAbelianDerivedLowerShriekIso`.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionModuleDerivedLowerShriekIso :
    polynomialMooreCochain A B
        (resolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
          (standardResolution_isResolution.{u, u} A B).isPolynomialAlgebra)
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single
          ((polynomialSite A B)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u)))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
        polynomialDerivedLowerShriek A B (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u)))
declarations.comment: `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, on the site `C_{B/A}` of 08PR, with module sections in the universe above that of `A` and `B`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_homotopyEquivalences_standardResolutionMor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PT**. Let `A → B` be a ring map and let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be the standard resolution of
`B` over `A`. Then for every object `W` of the site `C_{B/A}` the simplicial set
`Mor_{C_{B/A}}((P_•, ε), W)` is homotopy equivalent to the constant simplicial set on a singleton,
which is the hypothesis the criterion of Tag 08Q9 asks of the cosimplicial object of the standard
resolution. The two hypotheses of Tag 08PS hold for it by Tag 08QI: its terms are polynomial
algebras, and its augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration because it is a homotopy equivalence of
underlying simplicial sets (Tag 08ND), hence a quasi-isomorphism of associated complexes
(Tag 08P2), hence — being degreewise surjective — a trivial Kan fibration (Tag 08P1).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyEquivalences_standardResolutionMor (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (B : CommAlgCat.{u} A) (W : polynomialSite A B) :
    ∃ f : (resolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
          (standardResolution_isResolution.{u, u} A B).isPolynomialAlgebra).op ⋙
        yoneda.obj W ⟶ (Functor.const SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ).obj PUnit.{u + 1},
      SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type u) f
declarations.comment: the hypothesis of the criterion of Tag 08Q9 for the cosimplicial object of the standard resolution: each `Mor_C((P_•, ε), W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. The conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)`, resp. `D(B)`, functorially in `ℱ`, is not asserted, for the reason recorded at Tag 08PS in this file

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)` for the standard resolution**, functorially in the abelian
sheaf `ℱ` on the small model of the site restricted to polynomial algebras on at most
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionVarCardinal A B` variables.

This is the abelian half of the conclusion of Tag 08PT in the derived category. The two
hypotheses of Tag 08PS hold for the standard resolution by Tag 08QI — its terms are polynomial
algebras and its augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration — and its terms are boundedly many
variables wide by `CommAlgCat.standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebraBelow`, so nothing is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso :
    Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainComplex
          (smallResolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)
            (standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebraBelow A B)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single
          ((smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))ᵒᵖ ⥤
            AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          totalDerivedColimit (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(Ab)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Ab(C_{B/A})`, for the standard resolution, as an isomorphism in the derived category rather than degreewise, read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site — for the reason recorded at Tag 08PS in this file

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionModuleDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` for the standard resolution**, functorially in the sheaf of
`B`-modules `ℱ` on the small model of the site restricted to polynomial algebras on at most
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionVarCardinal A B` variables.

This is the module half of the conclusion of Tag 08PT in the derived category, beside the abelian
half `CommAlgCat.standardResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso`; as there, the hypotheses of Tag 08PS are
discharged for the standard resolution by Tag 08QI.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionModuleDerivedColimitNatIso :
    Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainComplex (B := (B : Type u))
          (smallResolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)
            (standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebraBelow A B)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single
          ((smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))ᵒᵖ ⥤
            ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          totalDerivedColimit (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, for the standard resolution, as an isomorphism in the derived category rather than degreewise, read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site — for the reason recorded at Tag 08PS in this file

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso
declarations.doc:
For every sheaf of `B`-modules `ℱ` on the small model of the site `C_{B/A}` restricted to
polynomial algebras on at most `CommAlgCat.standardResolutionVarCardinal A B` variables, the
sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)` are the degree `n` homology of the Moore complex of the
simplicial `B`-module `ℱ(P_•, ε)` for `P_•` the standard resolution of `B` over `A`, naturally
in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso (n : ℕ) :
    (modulePointLowerShriek
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))
          (B : Type u)).leftDerived n ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)))
          (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ⋙
        moduleCosimplicialMooreComplex
            (smallResolutionCosimplicialObject (standardResolution.{u, u} A B).hom
              (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)
              (standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebraBelow A B)) ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))
            (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: the conclusion `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, for the standard resolution, read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site, for the reason recorded at Tag 08PS in this file

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.free_kaehlerDifferential_polynomialSite
declarations.doc:
**The differentials of each object of `C_{B/A}` are free over it.** Every object `(P, α)` of
the site has `P` a polynomial algebra over `A`, so `Ω[P⁄A]` is free on the variables. This is the
first sentence of the proof of Tag 08PU, the objectwise input to its step `Li^* = i^*`; the
sheaf-level flatness is `CommAlgCat.polynomialRelativeDifferentials_isFlat`, and the step itself,
`Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} ≅ i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` in `D(B̲)`, is `CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialDerivedPullbackDifferentialsIso`
of `StacksFrontier/Cotangent/PolynomialAlgebraSiteDerivedPullbackDifferentials.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_kaehlerDifferential_polynomialSite (X : polynomialSite A B) :
    Module.Free (X.unop.obj.left : Type u) Ω[(X.unop.obj.left : Type u)⁄A]
declarations.comment: the first sentence of the proof: for each object P → B of C_{B/A} the module Ω_{P/A} is a free P-module; this is the input to the step Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}, which is CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialDerivedPullbackDifferentialsIso

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentMooreComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**The Moore complex of `(i^*Ω_{𝒪/A})(P_•, ε)` is the complex of `L_{B/A}`.** For the
standard resolution of `B` over `A`, the Moore complex of the simplicial abelian group obtained
by evaluating `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` on the cosimplicial object of the small model is the complex
underlying the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, namely the alternating face map complex of
`CommAlgCat.cotangentSimplicialModule` with its `B`-module structures forgotten.

This is the heart of Tag 08PU: an isomorphism of complexes, not merely of their homology.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionCotangentMooreComplexIso :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.cosimplicialMooreComplex
          (standardResolutionSmallCosimplicialObject A B)).obj
        (smallPolynomialCotangentSheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)).obj ≅
      ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj
        ((alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj
          (cotangentSimplicialModule.{u, u} A B).object)
declarations.comment: the step Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) = (Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)(P_•, ε): the evaluation of i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} on the standard resolution is the simplicial module whose complex is L_{B/A}, as an isomorphism of complexes

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionLeftDerivedCotangentComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08PU at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`.** The sections at the point
of `L_nπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` are the degree `-n` cohomology of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` of
Tag 08PN, with its `B`-module structure forgotten; here `π` is the point morphism of the small
model of the footnote-restricted site and `Lπ_!` is read degreewise, as the left derived functors
of the `π_!` of Tag 08PF.

The proof is the source's: Tag 08PT computes `L_nπ_!` on the standard resolution
(`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso`), the evaluation of
`Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` there is the simplicial module defining `L_{B/A}`
(`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentMooreComplexIso`), and the cotangent complex is the
reindexing of that simplicial module's alternating face map complex. The step
`Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` of the source is the flatness of `Ω_{𝒪/A}` over `𝒪`,
`CommAlgCat.polynomialRelativeDifferentials_isFlat`; see the implementation notes for what
separates this statement from the source's isomorphism in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionLeftDerivedCotangentComplexIso (n : ℕ) :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
                (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).leftDerived n).obj
          (smallPolynomialCotangentSheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) ≅
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        ((cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B).homology (-(n : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the identification L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲), for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A} and with Lπ_! read degreewise, as the left derived functors of the π_! of Tag 08PF at abelian coefficients: the sections at the point of L_nπ_! are the degree -n cohomology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN. The source's isomorphism in D(B) needs the module-level Lπ_!, which is absent from this library

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialDerivedPullbackDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**`Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}`** in `D(B̲)`, on the small model of the footnote-restricted site
`C_{B/A}`: the total left derived functor of the module pullback along `i`, evaluated at
`Ω_{𝒪/A}` in degree zero, is the underived pullback in degree zero. This is the comparison
`Li^* ⟶ i^*` at `Ω_{𝒪/A}[0]`, invertible by
`CommAlgCat.isIso_derivedExtendScalarsCounit_singleDifferentials`, read between the two
single-degree embeddings.
declarations.statement:
def smallPolynomialDerivedPullbackDifferentialsIso :
    (smallPolynomialDerivedModulePullback A B κ).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (smallPolynomialDifferentials A B κ)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        ((smallPolynomialModulePullback A B κ).obj (smallPolynomialDifferentials A B κ))
declarations.comment: the step Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} in D(B̲), on the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A}, where i^* is extension of scalars along the augmentation 𝒪 ⟶ B̲ and Li^* its total left derived functor

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexIsoDerivedLowerShriekDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08PU] as the full chain, in `D(Ab)`**: on the small model of the
footnote-restricted site `C_{B/A}`, at the cardinal bounding the standard resolution,

`L_{B/A} ≅ Lπ_!(Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A})`,

with `Lπ_!` the derived colimit of the underlying abelian presheaves
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianDerivedColimitOfModules`). The isomorphism is the composite of the
source's three steps: `Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}`
(`CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialDerivedPullbackDifferentialsIso`); `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲`, the
sheaf `(P, α) ↦ B ⊗_{P,α} Ω_{P/A}` (`CommAlgCat.extendScalarsDifferentialsIso`); and
`Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) = L_{B/A}`, computed on the standard resolution
(`CommAlgCat.derivedLowerShriekCotangentIso`).
declarations.statement:
def cotangentComplexIsoDerivedLowerShriekDerivedPullback :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B)) ≅
      (Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianDerivedColimitOfModules
          (smallPolynomialConstantPresheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).obj
        ((smallPolynomialDerivedModulePullback A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            (smallPolynomialDifferentials A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))))
declarations.comment: the chain L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A}) = Lπ_!(i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}) = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲), read in D(Ab), on the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A}

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionModuleLeftDerivedCotangentComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08PU at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`, with `B`-linear
coefficients.** The sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` are the degree `-n`
cohomology of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` of Tag 08PN, as `B`-modules; here `π` is the point
morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site and `Lπ_!` is read degreewise, as
the left derived functors of the `π_!` of Tag 08PF on sheaves of `B`-modules.

The proof is the source's: Tag 08PT at linear coefficients computes `L_nπ_!` on the standard
resolution (`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso`), the evaluation of
`Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` there is the simplicial `B`-module defining `L_{B/A}`
(`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentModuleMooreComplexIso`), and the cotangent complex is the
reindexing of that simplicial module's alternating face map complex.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionModuleLeftDerivedCotangentComplexIso (n : ℕ) :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.modulePointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))
              (B : Type u)).leftDerived n).obj
          (smallPolynomialCotangentModuleSheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) ≅
      (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B).homology (-(n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) at linear coefficients, for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A} and with Lπ_! read degreewise, as the left derived functors of the π_! of Tag 08PF on sheaves of B-modules: the sections at the point of L_nπ_! are the degree -n cohomology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, as B-modules. The source's isomorphism in D(B) needs the derived form of Tag 08PT

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)`, at module coefficients and on the small model of the
footnote-restricted site `C_{B/A}`.** The cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 08PN] is
derived lower shriek of the sheaf of `B̲`-modules `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲`, as an object of
`D(B)`:

`Q(L_{B/A}) ≅ Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)`.

Here `Lπ_!` is `CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialModuleDerivedLowerShriek`, the total left derived
functor of the colimit over the index category of `B̲`-modules, which is the `π_!` of
[Stacks, Tag 08PF].

The proof is the source's. The standard resolution is a point resolution of the small model
(`CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_standardResolutionSmallCosimplicialObject`), so the derived form
of [Stacks, Tag 08PT] at module coefficients
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit`) computes `Lπ_!` of
`i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` as the extended Moore complex of its evaluation on that resolution, and that
complex is the cotangent complex. The step `Li^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` of the source is the
flatness of `Ω_{𝒪/A}` over `𝒪`, which is why `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` may be used underived.
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients: Q(L_{B/A}) = L pi_!(Omega ⊗ B) for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A}, with L pi_! the total left derived functor of the colimit on D(B-underline)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)` for an arbitrary bounded resolution.** Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a
resolution of `B` over `A` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08QI] whose terms are polynomial algebras
on at most `κ` variables. Then the complex `Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B` of that resolution, read in
cohomological degrees `≤ 0`, is derived lower shriek of the sheaf of `B̲`-modules
`i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲`, as an object of `D(B)`:

`Q(Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B) ≅ Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)`.

Here `Lπ_!` is `CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialModuleDerivedLowerShriek`, the total left derived
functor of the colimit over the index category of `B̲`-modules, which is the `π_!` of
[Stacks, Tag 08PF].

The proof is the source's, with the standard resolution replaced by `P_•`: the resolution is a
point resolution of the small model of the footnote-restricted site
(`CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_smallResolutionCosimplicialObject`), so the derived form of
[Stacks, Tag 08PT] at module coefficients
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit`) computes `Lπ_!` of
`i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` as the extended Moore complex of its evaluation on `P_•`, and that evaluation is
`Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B`. Since the right-hand side does not mention the resolution, this is also
the assertion of [Stacks, Remark 08QI] that any resolution computes `L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
def smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A)))) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))).obj
            (resolutionOver ε ⋙ overDifferentialsFunctor)).extend
          (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE (0 : ℤ))) ≅
      smallPolynomialCotangentDerivedLowerShriek A B κ
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients, for an arbitrary resolution whose terms have at most κ variables: Q of the complex of that resolution is L pi_!(Omega ⊗ B-underline) for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A}. Combined with the same statement at the standard resolution this is Remark 08QI, that any resolution computes L_{B/A}

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIsoOfLE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)` at an arbitrary cardinal bound.** The cotangent complex
`L_{B/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 08PN] is derived lower shriek of the sheaf of `B̲`-modules
`i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` on the small model of the site restricted to polynomial algebras
on at most `κ` variables, for any bound `κ` containing the standard resolution:

`Q(L_{B/A}) ≅ Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso` at the standard resolution,
whose complex `Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B` is the cotangent complex by
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionOverDifferentialsIso`. At
`κ = CommAlgCat.standardResolutionVarCardinal A B` it is
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso`; the point of the free bound is
that a second resolution may need a larger one.
declarations.statement:
def standardResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIsoOfLE
    (hκ : standardResolutionVarCardinal A B ≤ κ) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B) ≅
      smallPolynomialCotangentDerivedLowerShriek A B κ
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients, at an arbitrary cardinal bound κ containing the standard resolution: Q(L_{B/A}) = L pi_!(Omega ⊗ B-underline) for the point morphism of the small model of the site restricted to at most κ variables

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso_naturality
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)` is functorial in the resolution.** Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` and
`ε' : P'_• ⟶ B` be resolutions of `B` over `A` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08QI] whose terms are
polynomial algebras on at most `κ` variables, and let `w : P_• ⟶ P'_•` be a morphism of simplicial
`A`-algebras over `B`. Then the triangle

`Q(Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B) ⟶ Q(Ω[P'_•⁄A] ⊗_{P'_•} B) ⟶ Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)`

commutes: the comparison of `CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso` at `ε'`,
precomposed with the map `CommAlgCat.resolutionCotangentComplexMap` induced by `w`, is the
comparison at `ε`.

In particular the isomorphism between the complexes of two resolutions that the two instances of
[Stacks, Tag 08PU] produce is the map induced by any morphism between the resolutions — which is
the content of [Stacks, Remark 08QI] beyond the object-level statement, and what a comparison of
two presentations consumes.

The proof is the naturality of the derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08PT] in the point resolution
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit_naturality`), applied at
`CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCosimplicialObjectMap`, together with
`CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentMooreCochainIso_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso_naturality (w : P ⟶ P') (hw : w ≫ ε' = ε)
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A))))
    (hε' : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε' (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A)))) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map (resolutionCotangentComplexMap ε ε' w hw) ≫
        (smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso ε' κ hP'κ hε').hom =
      (smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso ε κ hPκ hε).hom
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients: the identification of the complex of a resolution with L pi_!(Omega ⊗ B-underline) is functorial in the resolution, so the isomorphism it gives between the complexes of two resolutions is the map induced by a morphism between them. This is the arrow-level form of Remark 08QI

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.leftDerivedColimPolynomialCotangentIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08PU at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`, at linear coefficients.**
The `n`th homology of `C_{B/A}` with coefficients in `Ω = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` — the `n`th left
derived functor of the colimit over the opposite of the small model, which is Tag 08PF's
definition — is the degree `-n` cohomology of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` of Tag 08PN, as
`B`-modules.

This is the linear-coefficient refinement of
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionLeftDerivedCotangentComplexIso`, which is its image under the
forgetful functor to abelian groups. The proof is the same: the module half of Tag 08Q9
computes `L_n colim` on the standard resolution, and the evaluation of `Ω` there is the
simplicial module defining `L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedColimPolynomialCotangentIso (n : ℕ) :
    ((colim :
          ((smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))ᵒᵖ ⥤
            ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B).leftDerived n).obj
        (smallPolynomialCotangentModulePresheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) ≅
      (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B).homology (-(n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the identification L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) read degreewise at LINEAR coefficients: for every n, the nth left derived functor of the colimit over the opposite of the small model of the footnote-restricted site, applied to Ω, is the degree -n cohomology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, as an isomorphism of B-modules. L_n colim is Tag 08PF's definition of H_n(C_{B/A}, -); the identification with the sections at the point of L_nπ_! is Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.moduleLeftDerivedPointLowerShriekNatIso. Proved for every ring map A → B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.finiteType_succ_of_trivialKanFibration_of_isCoskeletal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PW**. For a finite type algebra `B` over a Noetherian ring `A`, an
`n`-coskeletal simplicial `A`-algebra over `B` whose canonical augmentation is a trivial Kan
fibration and whose terms through degree `n` are of finite type has a finite type term in degree
`n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_succ_of_trivialKanFibration_of_isCoskeletal
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (P : SimplicialObject (Over (CommAlgCat.of A B))) (n : ℕ)
    (_hkan : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (underlyingAugmentation A B P))
    (hcosk : IsIso ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app P))
    (hfinite : ∀ k ≤ n,
      Algebra.FiniteType A (P.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk k))).left) :
    Algebra.FiniteType A (P.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1)))).left

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_trivialKanFibration_from_finiteType_polynomial_simplicialAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PX.** A finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring has a simplicial resolution by
polynomial algebras of finite type whose augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration on underlying
simplicial sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_trivialKanFibration_from_finiteType_polynomial_simplicialAlgebra
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] :
    ∃ (P : SimplicialObject (CommAlgCat.{u} A))
      (ε : P ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of A B)),
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ k : ℕ,
        Nonempty ((P.obj (op ⦋n⦌) : Type u) ≃ₐ[A] MvPolynomial (Fin k) A)) ∧
      SSet.trivialKanFibrations
        (Functor.whiskerRight ε (CategoryTheory.forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A)))

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallResolutionLeftDerivedMooreHomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` for a presheaf of `B`-modules, with the module structure forgotten.**
The sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)` are the degree `n` homology of the `B`-module Moore
complex of `ℱ(P_•, ε)`, read as an abelian group.

This is `CommAlgCat.smallResolutionLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso` — the conclusion of Tag 08PT at
the small model of the restricted site — followed by the two identifications that move the
computation from abelian groups to `B`-modules: the Moore complex of the underlying abelian
presheaf is the image of the `B`-module Moore complex, and `forget₂` preserves homology.
declarations.statement:
def smallResolutionLeftDerivedMooreHomologyIso (n : ℕ) :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)).leftDerived n).obj
          (smallPolynomialModuleSheaf A B κ ℱ)) ≅
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        ((smallResolutionMooreComplex ε κ hPκ ℱ).homology n)
declarations.comment: the half of the statement that says which modules the conclusion is about: the cohomology of Lπ_!(ℱ) for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site, read degreewise at abelian coefficients, is the homology of the B-module Moore complex of ℱ(P_•, ε). The finiteness of those modules is `CommAlgCat.finite_homology_smallResolutionMooreComplex`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.finite_homology_smallResolutionMooreComplex
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08PY for a bounded resolution.** Let `B` be Noetherian, let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a
resolution of `B` over `A` whose terms are polynomial algebras on at most `κ` variables, and let
`ℱ` be a presheaf of `B`-modules on the small model of the restricted site whose sections on the
terms of the resolution are finite `B`-modules. Then the Moore homology of `ℱ(P_•, ε)` — which by
`CommAlgCat.smallResolutionLeftDerivedMooreHomologyIso` is the sections at the point of
`L_nπ_!(ℱ)` — is a finite `B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_homology_smallResolutionMooreComplex [IsNoetherianRing (B : Type u)]
    (hfin : ∀ p : SimplexCategory,
      Module.Finite B (ℱ.obj (op ((smallResolutionCosimplicialObject ε κ hPκ).obj p))))
    (n : ℕ) : Module.Finite B ((smallResolutionMooreComplex ε κ hPκ ℱ).homology n)
declarations.comment: the conclusion for a resolution satisfying the cardinality bound of the small model of the footnote-restricted site, and with the cohomology of Lπ_! read as the homology of the B-module Moore complex of ℱ(P_•, ε), which is what identifies it here (`CommAlgCat.smallResolutionLeftDerivedMooreHomologyIso`): the module-level Lπ_! is absent from this library. The finiteness hypothesis is carried for the terms of the resolution, not for every object of the site

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.finite_moduleLeftDerivedPointLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08PY.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `A → B` be a finite type ring map and let
`π`, `B̲` be as in Tag 08PR. If `ℱ` is a `B̲`-module such that `ℱ(P, α)` is a finite `B`-module
for every augmentation `α : P → B` whose `P` is of finite type over `A`, then every cohomology
module of `Lπ_!(ℱ)` is a finite `B`-module.

By Tag 08PX there is a resolution `ε : P_• ⟶ B` of `B` over `A` all of whose terms are
*finite type* polynomial algebras, and by the module half of Tag 08PS the sections at the point
of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)` are the degree `n` homology of the Moore complex of `ℱ(P_•, ε)`. Each term of that
complex is `ℱ` evaluated at a finite type polynomial augmentation, hence a finite `B`-module, and
`B` is Noetherian because it is of finite type over the Noetherian ring `A`; so each homology
module is a subquotient of a finite module over a Noetherian ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_moduleLeftDerivedPointLowerShriek (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : Cardinal.aleph0.{u} ≤ κ)
    (ℱ : Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ))
      (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)))
    (hℱ : ∀ W : smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ,
      Algebra.FiniteType A (smallBoundedPolynomialAlgebra A B κ W : Type u) →
        Module.Finite (B : Type u) (ℱ.obj.obj (op W)))
    (n : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite (B : Type u)
      (((modulePointLowerShriek (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)
            (B : Type u)).leftDerived n ⋙
          Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u}
            (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))).obj ℱ)
declarations.comment: read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site, for the reason recorded for Tag 08PS in `StacksFrontier/Cotangent/ResolutionPointCriterionSmallOfModules.lean`; the cardinal bound `κ` of the footnote is a parameter, required only to be infinite so that the finite type resolution of Tag 08PX is an object of the site

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.finite_homology_cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08PZ.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and let `A → B` be a finite type ring map. Then
`H^n(L_{B/A})` is a finite `B`-module for every `n : ℤ`.

In positive degrees the cotangent complex vanishes, so there is nothing to prove; the content is
`CommAlgCat.finite_homology_cotangentComplex_of_resolution` fed with the finite type resolution
of Tag 08PX.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_homology_cotangentComplex (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (m : ℤ) :
    Module.Finite B ((cotangentComplex.{u, u} A (CommAlgCat.of A B)).homology m)

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.isHomotopyEquiv_toKaehlerChainMap_of_algEquiv_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**The naive cotangent complex of a polynomial algebra** (Stacks 08Q1). Let `R → S` be a
polynomial algebra, that is `S ≅ R[x_i : i ∈ ι]` as `R`-algebras for some set of variables `ι`.
Then the canonical naive cotangent complex `NL_{S/R}` is homotopy equivalent to the complex
`(0 → Ω_{S/R})` with `Ω_{S/R}` in degree `0`, the homotopy equivalence being the augmentation
`toKaehlerChainMap R S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomotopyEquiv_toKaehlerChainMap_of_algEquiv_mvPolynomial {ι : Type*}
    (e : MvPolynomial ι R ≃ₐ[R] S) : IsHomotopyEquiv (toKaehlerChainMap R S)
declarations.comment:
the homotopy equivalence `NL_{S/R} → (0 → Ω_{S/R})`, for the canonical naive
cotangent complex of any `R`-algebra `S` isomorphic to a polynomial algebra `R[x_i : i ∈ ι]`

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.isQuasiIso_toKaehlerChainMap_of_algEquiv_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Homology of the naive cotangent complex of a polynomial algebra** (Stacks 08Q1). For an
`R`-algebra `S` isomorphic to a polynomial algebra `R[x_i : i ∈ ι]`, the augmentation
`NL_{S/R} → (0 → Ω_{S/R})` is a quasi-isomorphism: `H₁(NL_{S/R}) = 0` and `H₀(NL_{S/R}) = Ω_{S/R}`
through it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiIso_toKaehlerChainMap_of_algEquiv_mvPolynomial {ι : Type*}
    (e : MvPolynomial ι R ≃ₐ[R] S) : IsQuasiIso (toKaehlerChainMap R S)
declarations.comment:
the quasi-isomorphism `NL_{S/R} → (0 → Ω_{S/R})` deduced from the homotopy
equivalence, for any `R`-algebra `S` isomorphic to a polynomial algebra `R[x_i : i ∈ ι]`

declarations.name: main_covariant
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (covariant case). If `H^i(K 0) = 0` for `i > 0` and the induced
map `H^{-j}(f j)` vanishes for each `0 ≤ j ≤ n-1`, then the composite
`K 0 ⟶ K n`, viewed in the derived category, factors through the canonical map
`ι : τ_{≤ -n} (K n) ⟶ K n`.

PROOF.  Induction on `n`.
* `n = 0`: `chainComp K f 0 = 𝟙`, and `covariant_base` makes `Q(ιTruncLE 0)`
  invertible, so `h = inv (Q(ιTruncLE 0))` works.
* `n → n+1`: `chainComp K f (m+1) = chainComp K f m ≫ f m`.  The induction
  hypothesis factors `Q(chainComp K f m)` through `Q(ιTruncLE (-m))`; apply
  `covariant_step m (K m) (K (m+1)) (f m)` (its `H^{-m}(f m) = 0` hypothesis is
  `h2 m`), then rewrite `-(↑m+1) = -(↑(m+1))` by `push_cast` to match.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_covariant
    (n : ℕ) (K : ℕ → CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : ∀ j, K j ⟶ K (j + 1))
    (h1 : ∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → Limits.IsZero ((K 0).homology i))
    (h2 : ∀ j : ℕ, j < n → HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (f j) (-(j : ℤ)) = 0) :
    ∃ h : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (K 0) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((K n).truncLE (-(n : ℤ))),
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (chainComp K f n) =
        h ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((K n).ιTruncLE (-(n : ℤ)))

declarations.name: main_contravariant
declarations.doc:
Statement 2 (contravariant / dual case). If `H^i(K 0) = 0` for `i < 0` and
the induced map `H^{j}(g j)` vanishes for each `0 ≤ j ≤ n-1`, then the composite
`K n ⟶ K 0`, viewed in the derived category, factors through the canonical map
`π : K n ⟶ τ_{≥ n} (K n)`.

PROOF.  Dual of `main_covariant`, by induction on `n` using `contravariant_base`
(base) and `contravariant_step` (step).
declarations.statement:
theorem main_contravariant
    (n : ℕ) (K : ℕ → CochainComplex A ℤ) (g : ∀ j, K (j + 1) ⟶ K j)
    (h1 : ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → Limits.IsZero ((K 0).homology i))
    (h2 : ∀ j : ℕ, j < n → HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (g j) (j : ℤ) = 0) :
    ∃ h : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((K n).truncGE (n : ℤ)) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (K 0),
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (chainCompOp K g n) =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((K n).πTruncGE (n : ℤ)) ≫ h

declarations.name: SSet.stdSimplex.homotopyEquivalences_hom_obj₀
declarations.doc:
The standard simplex `Δ[m]` is homotopy equivalent to `Δ[0]`. The unique morphism
`f : Δ[m] ⟶ Δ[0]` is a homotopy equivalence of simplicial objects ([Stacks, Tag 019N]): a
homotopy inverse is the inclusion `g : Δ[0] ⟶ Δ[m]` of the last `0`-simplex of `Δ[m]`, for
which `g ≫ f = 𝟙 Δ[0]` and, as the second conjunct records, `𝟙 Δ[m]` is homotopic to
`f ≫ g = SSet.const (obj₀Equiv.symm (Fin.last m))` by a homotopy in that direction, namely
`(φ, α) ↦ (k ↦ if α k = 0 then φ k else m)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalences_hom_obj₀ (m : ℕ) :
    (∀ f : (Δ[m] : SSet.{u}) ⟶ Δ[0],
        SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type u) f) ∧
      Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (𝟙 (Δ[m] : SSet.{u}))
        (SSet.const (obj₀Equiv.symm (Fin.last m))))
declarations.comment: the homotopy equivalence, with the homotopy `𝟙 ⟹ f ≫ g` for `g` the last vertex; `g ≫ f = 𝟙` is `SSet.stdSimplex.ext₀`, as `Δ[0]` is terminal

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.nonempty_homotopy_and_homotopyEquivalences_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
Products of homotopies and of homotopy equivalences of simplicial objects. Let `X t`, `Y t`
(`t : T`) be families of simplicial objects of a category `C`, and let `p t : P ⟶ X t` and
`q t : Q ⟶ Y t` exhibit `P` and `Q` as the products `∏_t X t` and `∏_t Y t`, that is, degreewise
products in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 016Q]. Let `a t, b t : X t ⟶ Y t` be morphisms and let
`f, g : P ⟶ Q` be their products, pinned by `f ≫ q t = p t ≫ a t` and `g ≫ q t = p t ≫ b t`. Then:
* if there is a homotopy from `a t` to `b t` for every `t`, there is a homotopy from `f` to `g`
  (part (2), no finiteness needed);
* if `a t` and `b t` are homotopic for every `t` and `a t = b t` for all but finitely many `t`,
  then `f` and `g` are homotopic (part (3));
* if `T` is finite and every `a t` is a homotopy equivalence, then `f` is a homotopy
  equivalence, so `∏_t X t` and `∏_t Y t` are homotopy equivalent (part (1)).
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_homotopy_and_homotopyEquivalences_of_isLimit
    {T : Type w} {X Y : T → SimplicialObject C} {P Q : SimplicialObject C}
    (p : ∀ t, P ⟶ X t) (q : ∀ t, Q ⟶ Y t)
    (hP : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, IsLimit (Fan.mk (P.obj n) fun t => (p t).app n))
    (hQ : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, IsLimit (Fan.mk (Q.obj n) fun t => (q t).app n))
    {a b : ∀ t, X t ⟶ Y t} {f g : P ⟶ Q}
    (hf : ∀ t, f ≫ q t = p t ≫ a t) (hg : ∀ t, g ≫ q t = p t ≫ b t) :
    ((∀ t, Nonempty (Homotopy (a t) (b t))) → Nonempty (Homotopy f g)) ∧
      ({t | a t ≠ b t}.Finite →
        (∀ t, Relation.EqvGen (fun u v : X t ⟶ Y t => Nonempty (Homotopy u v)) (a t) (b t)) →
          Relation.EqvGen (fun u v : P ⟶ Q => Nonempty (Homotopy u v)) f g) ∧
      (Finite T → (∀ t, homotopyEquivalences C (a t)) → homotopyEquivalences C f)
declarations.comment: the three conjuncts are parts (2), (3), (1), in that order. The products are pinned degreewise by limit fans, as in [Stacks, Tag 016Q], instead of by `HasProduct` in `SimplicialObject C`, and `f = ∏ a_t`, `g = ∏ b_t` by their characterizing equations. Part (1) is stated in the stronger form that the product of homotopy equivalences is one, the source's `homotopy equivalent` following by choice; part (3) is stated with the weaker hypothesis that only finitely many coordinates differ. See the module docstring

declarations.name: SSet.isStableUnderFilteredColimits_trivialKanFibrations
declarations.doc:
**A filtered colimit of trivial Kan fibrations is a trivial Kan fibration.** If `J` is a
filtered category and `f : X₁ ⟶ X₂` is a morphism of diagrams `J ⥤ SSet` whose components
`f.app j` are all trivial Kan fibrations, that is, all have the right lifting property with
respect to every boundary inclusion `∂Δ[n].ι`, then so is the induced morphism
`colim X₁ ⟶ colim X₂` between any colimits of `X₁` and of `X₂`.
declarations.comment: stability under filtered colimits is stated for arbitrary colimit cocones over an arbitrary filtered index category, as `IsStableUnderFilteredColimits` for the class of Tag 08NL; the source's `colim X₁ → colim X₂` is the case of `colimMap`, and the index category is in arbitrary universes, the hypothesis `HasColimitsOfSize` being what makes the colimits degreewise as in the source's hint

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)`.** For a complex `F^•` of diagrams on `Cᵒᵖ` and an
object `U` of `C`, the canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)` in the unbounded derived category,
natural in `F^•`. For `D = AddCommGrpCat` this is a map in `D(Ab)`, and for `D = ModuleCat B` it
is the same map read in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
def evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit (U : C) :
    ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C D
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map is the colimit cocone.** After the canonical comparisons of the total
left derived functor with the degreewise colimit, the map of `evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit` is
the colimit cocone of the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit_comp_counit (U : C) (K : CochainComplex (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ℤ) :
    (evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit C D U).app K ≫
      (totalDerivedColimit C D).map ((DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso _).inv.app K) ≫
      (totalDerivedColimitCounit C D).app
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map
        (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).mapHomotopyCategoryFactors
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom.app K) ≫
      (DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso _).hom.app
        (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) =
    DerivedCategory.Q.map
      ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (sectionsToColimit C D U) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).app K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit'
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)`.** For a complex `F^•` of diagrams on `Cᵒᵖ` and an
object `U` of `C`, the canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)` in the unbounded derived category,
natural in `F^•`. For `D = AddCommGrpCat` this is a map in `D(Ab)`, and for `D = ModuleCat B` it
is the same map read in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
def evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit' (U : C) :
    ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit' C D
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit_comp_counit'
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map is the colimit cocone.** After the canonical comparisons of the total
left derived functor with the degreewise colimit, the map of `evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit'`
is the colimit cocone of the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit_comp_counit' (U : C) (K : CochainComplex (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ℤ) :
    (evaluationToTotalDerivedColimit' C D U).app K ≫
      (totalDerivedColimit' C D).map ((DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso _).inv.app K) ≫
      (totalDerivedColimitCounit' C D).app
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map
        (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).mapHomotopyCategoryFactors
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom.app K) ≫
      (DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso _).hom.app
        (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) =
    DerivedCategory.Q.map
      ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (sectionsToColimit' C D U) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).app K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToDerivedColimitOfAbelianDiagrams
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map for abelian presheaves.** The canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)` in
`D(Ab)`, for a complex `F^•` of abelian presheaves — equivalently, of abelian sheaves for the
chaotic topology — on a small category.
declarations.comment: ab_map

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.evaluationToDerivedColimitOfModuleDiagrams
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map for modules.** The canonical map `F^•(U) ⟶ Lπ_!(F^•)`, read in `D(B)`,
for a complex of modules over the constant sheaf of rings `B̲` on a small chaotic site.
declarations.statement:
def evaluationToDerivedColimitOfModuleDiagrams (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C]
    (B : Type w) [Ring B] (U : C) :
    ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{max u w} B)).obj (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{max u w} B)
declarations.comment: module_map

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianDerivedLowerShriekInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08Q7 for a functor with a fully faithful right adjoint.** Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a functor
between categories carrying the chaotic topology and let `g` be the induced morphism of topoi, so
that `g⁻¹` is restriction along `u`. If `u` has a fully faithful right adjoint, then inverse image
followed by derived lower shriek is the identity of `D(Ab(D))`: for any left derived functor `L`
of lower shriek, presented by a comparison `α`, and any derived functor `G` of inverse image,
presented by `e`, there is a natural isomorphism `G ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭`.
declarations.statement:
def abelianDerivedLowerShriekInverseImageIso (adj : uf ⊣ sf) [sf.Full] [sf.Faithful]
    (hJ : J = ⊥) (hK : K = ⊥)
    [HasSheafify J A] [HasSheafify K A]
    [uf.IsContinuous J K] [sf.IsContinuous K J]
    [(uf.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K).IsRightAdjoint]
    (L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (Sheaf K A))
    (α : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶
      (uf.sheafPullback A J K).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    [L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Sheaf J A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (G : DerivedCategory (Sheaf K A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (Sheaf J A))
    (e : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ G ≅
      (uf.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh) :
    G ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: for a functor of chaotic sites with a fully faithful right adjoint, of which the projection to the point of a category with a final object is the case in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedConstCompColimitIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q7, unconditionally.** In the colimit presentation of lower shriek on a chaotic
site — `π_! = colim_{Cᵒᵖ}` and `π^{-1} = const` — the identity `Lπ_! ∘ π^{-1} = id` holds with no
hypothesis on the existence of the derived functor: the total left derived colimit of
`Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit` exists for any coefficient category with enough
projectives and exact countable filtered colimits.
declarations.statement:
def derivedConstCompColimitIso (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C]
    (Dc : Type uA) [Category.{vA} Dc] [Abelian Dc]
    [EnoughProjectives (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dc)] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ Dc]
    [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ Dc] [HasColimitsOfShape Cᵒᵖ Dc]
    (hC : HasInitial C ∨ HasTerminal C) :
    (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ : Dc ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dc)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
      Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit C Dc ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: derived colimit presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedConstCompColimitIso'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q7, unconditionally, for a category that need not be small.** In the colimit
presentation of lower shriek on a chaotic site — `π_! = colim_{Cᵒᵖ}` and `π^{-1} = const` — the
identity `Lπ_! ∘ π^{-1} = id` holds with no hypothesis on the existence of the derived functor: the
total left derived colimit of `Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit'` exists for any
coefficient category with enough projectives and exact countable filtered colimits.

No smallness is asked of the site either: the objects of `C` and its morphisms may live in
different universes, as they do at the site of [Stacks, Tag 08PR]. Everything the proof consumes
is size-general — `Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit'` and its two companions
carry only instance hypotheses, and the abstract form `derivedCompositeOfConstant` is stated for
an arbitrary category.
declarations.statement:
def derivedConstCompColimitIso' (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
    (Dc : Type uA) [Category.{vA} Dc] [Abelian Dc]
    [EnoughProjectives (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dc)] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ Dc]
    [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ Dc] [HasColimitsOfShape Cᵒᵖ Dc]
    (hC : HasInitial C ∨ HasTerminal C) :
    (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ : Dc ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dc)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
      Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit' C Dc ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: derived colimit presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q7 for abelian sheaves.** On the chaotic site of a category with an initial or a
final object, inverse image from the point followed by derived lower shriek is the identity of
`D(Ab)`: for any left derived functor `L` of lower shriek, presented by a comparison `α`, and
any derived functor `G` of inverse image, presented by `e`, there is a natural isomorphism
`G ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭`.
declarations.statement:
def abelianDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
    (hC : HasInitial C ∨ HasTerminal C)
    [HasSheafify (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C) AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}]
    [HasSheafify (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))
      AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}]
    [((Functor.star C).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))).IsRightAdjoint]
    [((Functor.star C).sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))).Additive]
    [((Functor.star C).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
      (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))).Additive]
    (L : DerivedCategory
      (Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C) AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))
        AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}))
    (α : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶
      ((Functor.star C).sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}
        (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
        (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))).mapHomotopyCategory
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    [L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
        (Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C) AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v})
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (G : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))
        AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}))
    (e : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ G ≅
      ((Functor.star C).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max w (u + 1) v}
        (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C)
        (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))).mapHomotopyCategory
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) :
    G ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: abelian groups

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.moduleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q7 for sheaves of modules.** The same identity for sheaves of modules over the
constant coefficient ring of a ringed-point situation whose category has an initial or a final
object.
declarations.statement:
def moduleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
    (hC : HasInitial s.C ∨ HasTerminal s.C)
    [HasSheafify (GrothendieckTopology.trivial s.C) AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v}]
    [HasSheafify (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1}))
      AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v}]
    [(GrothendieckTopology.trivial s.C).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v}]
    [(GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})).WEqualsLocallyBijective
      AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v}]
    [(SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 (pointSituationConstantRing s))).IsRightAdjoint]
    [(SheafOfModules.pullback (𝟙 (pointSituationConstantRing s))).Additive]
    [(SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 (pointSituationConstantRing s))).Additive]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max w u v} (pointSituationConstantRing s)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max w u v} (pointRing s)))
    (α : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.pullback (𝟙 (pointSituationConstantRing s))).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    [L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (G : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max w u v} (pointRing s)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max w u v} (pointSituationConstantRing s)))
    (e : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ G ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 (pointSituationConstantRing s))).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) :
    G ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: modules over a ring

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitExtendScalarsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q8.** For a ring map `f : B ⟶ B'` and the resulting commutative square of
ringed topoi over a chaotic site, derived lower shriek to the point commutes with derived
extension of coefficients: `Lπ'_! ∘ Lh^* ≅ Lf^* ∘ Lπ_!`.

Both sides are left adjoint to the degreewise derived functor of the constant diagram of the
restriction of scalars, so they agree by uniqueness of left adjoints.

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedColimitIsoMooreComplexHomology
declarations.doc:
Let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of a small category `C` such that every simplicial set
`Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. The homology `L_nπ_!` of `C` with
coefficients the free abelian presheaf `j_{W!}ℤ_W` on a representable is the homology of the
Moore complex of `j_{W!}ℤ_W(U_•)`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedColimitIsoMooreComplexHomology (hU : IsPointResolution U) (W : C) (n : ℕ) :
    ((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n).obj
        (freeRepresentablePresheaf W) ≅
      ((cosimplicialMooreComplex U).obj (freeRepresentablePresheaf W)).homology n
declarations.comment: for the abelian sheaves `ℱ = j_{W!}ℤ_W`, the free abelian presheaves on representables, which are the projective generators the source's proof reduces to; `Lπ_!` is read degreewise as the left derived functors `L_nπ_! = H_n(C, -)` of the colimit over `Cᵒᵖ` of Tag 08PF, and `ℱ(U_•)` as the Moore complex of the simplicial abelian group obtained by evaluating `ℱ` on `U_•`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of a small category `C` such that every simplicial set
`Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. For every abelian presheaf `ℱ` the
homology `L_nπ_!` of `C` with coefficients `ℱ` is the homology of the Moore complex of `ℱ(U_•)`,
naturally in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedColimitNatIso (hU : IsPointResolution U) (n : ℕ) :
    (colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n ≅
      cosimplicialMooreComplex U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.moduleLeftDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of a small category `C` such that every simplicial set
`Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent to a singleton, and let `B` be a ring. For every `B̲`-module
`ℱ` on the chaotic site `C` — that is, every diagram of `B`-modules on `Cᵒᵖ` — the homology
`L_nπ_!` of `C` with coefficients `ℱ` is the homology of the Moore complex of `ℱ(U_•)`, naturally
in `ℱ`, as `B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def moduleLeftDerivedColimitNatIso (hU : IsPointResolution U) (n : ℕ) :
    (colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B).leftDerived n ≅
      moduleCosimplicialMooreComplex U ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: module half: `Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(U_•)` in `D(B)` functorially in `ℱ` in `Mod(B̲)`, read degreewise as `L_nπ_! = L_n colim` of Tag 08PF and as the Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module obtained by evaluating `ℱ` on `U_•`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] at abelian coefficients, as an isomorphism of
functors.** Let `C` be a small category with the chaotic topology and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial
object of `C` which is a point resolution. Then

`Q(ℱ(U_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(Ab)`,

**naturally in the abelian presheaf `ℱ`**, where the left side is the extended Moore complex of
the simplicial abelian group `ℱ(U_•)` and `Lπ_!` is the total left derived functor of the colimit
over `Cᵒᵖ`, which is `π_!` on the chaotic site by [Stacks, Tag 08PF].
declarations.comment: derived-category form at abelian coefficients, natural in the coefficient presheaf: the extended Moore complex of the evaluation on a point resolution is derived lower shriek as an isomorphism of functors. The degreewise form `Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedColimitNatIso` gives only the cohomology of the two sides and cannot transport a morphism of coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] at abelian coefficients, for a site that need not be
small.** Let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C` which is a point resolution. Then

`Q(ℱ(U_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(Ab)`,

**naturally in the abelian presheaf `ℱ`**, where the left side is the extended Moore complex of
the simplicial abelian group `ℱ(U_•)` and `Lπ_!` is the total left derived functor of the colimit
over `Cᵒᵖ`, which is `π_!` on the chaotic site by [Stacks, Tag 08PF].

The objects of `C` and its morphisms may live in different universes; the coefficients are read
at `max v u`, the smallest universe in which `Cᵒᵖ` has colimits of abelian groups. The form
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit` asks for a small site, and so
does not apply to the site of [Stacks, Tag 08PR].
declarations.comment: derived-category form at abelian coefficients, natural in the coefficient presheaf, with the smallness hypothesis on the site removed: the site's objects and its morphisms may live in different universes, the coefficients being read at their maximum. The lemma `Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit` is this statement for a small site

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] at linear coefficients, for a site that need not be
small.** Let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C` which is a point resolution and let `B` be a
ring. Then

`Q(ℱ(U_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(B)`,

**naturally in the diagram of `B`-modules `ℱ`** -- equivalently, in the `B̲`-module `ℱ`, the
topology being chaotic. This is the module half beside
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge`, and as there the
objects of `C` and its morphisms may live in different universes.
declarations.statement:
def mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimitOfLarge (hU : IsPointResolution U) :
    GeneralValued.mooreCochainComplex' U (ModuleCat.{max v u} B) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max v u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit' C (ModuleCat.{max v u} B)
declarations.comment: derived-category form at module coefficients, natural in the coefficient module, with the smallness hypothesis on the site removed. The lemma `Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit` is this statement for a small site

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit
declarations.doc:
**The derived form of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] at module coefficients, as an isomorphism of
functors.** Let `C` be a small category with the chaotic topology, `B` a ring, and `U_•` a
cosimplicial object of `C` which is a point resolution. Then

`Q(ℱ(U_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(ℱ)` in `D(B)`,

**naturally in the diagram `ℱ` of `B`-modules**, where the left side is the extended Moore complex
of the simplicial `B`-module `ℱ(U_•)` and `Lπ_!` is the total left derived functor of the colimit
over `Cᵒᵖ`, which is `π_!` on the chaotic site by [Stacks, Tag 08PF].
declarations.statement:
def mooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit (hU : IsPointResolution U) :
    mooreCochainComplex (B := B) U ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} B)
