declarations.comment: derived-category form at module coefficients, natural in the coefficient module: the extended Moore complex of the evaluation on a point resolution is derived lower shriek as an isomorphism of functors. Neither the degreewise form `Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedColimitNatIso` nor the object-level `Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.mooreCochainQIsoDerivedColimit` provides this

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.simplexCategoryLeftDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q9 at `C = Δ`.** For a simplicial abelian group `ℱ`, the homology `L_nπ_!` of `Δ`
with coefficients `ℱ` is the `n`th homology of the alternating-face-map complex of `ℱ`, naturally
in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def simplexCategoryLeftDerivedColimitNatIso (n : ℕ) :
    (colim : (SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{0}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{0}).leftDerived n ≅
      alternatingFaceMapComplex AddCommGrpCat.{0} ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{0} (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: at C = Δ with U_• = 𝟭: L_n of the colimit over Δᵒᵖ is the homology of the alternating-face-map complex of the simplicial abelian group itself, there being no cosimplicial object left in the statement. Abelian coefficients in the universe of Δ, which is 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.categoryHomology_simplexCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q9 at `C = Δ`, in the `categoryHomology` spelling.** The homology of `Δ` with
coefficients in a simplicial abelian group is the Moore homology of that simplicial abelian
group. This is the form the fibrewise machinery of Stacks 08PI and 08PJ consumes.
declarations.comment: at C = Δ, written with `Stacks.CategoryHomology.categoryHomology`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.simplexCategoryMooreCochainNatIsoDerivedColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q9 at `C = Δ`, in the derived category.** The extended alternating-face-map complex
of a simplicial abelian group is derived lower shriek of that simplicial abelian group placed in
degree zero, as an isomorphism of functors into `D(Ab)`.
declarations.comment: at C = Δ, derived-category form, natural in the coefficient presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.simplexCategoryModuleLeftDerivedColimitNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08Q9 at `C = Δ`, module coefficients.** For a simplicial `B`-module `ℱ`, the homology
`L_nπ_!` of `Δ` with coefficients `ℱ` is the `n`th homology of the alternating-face-map complex of
`ℱ`, naturally in `ℱ`, as `B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def simplexCategoryModuleLeftDerivedColimitNatIso (n : ℕ) :
    (colim : (SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{0} B) ⥤ ModuleCat.{0} B).leftDerived n ≅
      alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{0} B) ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} B) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: at C = Δ with U_• = 𝟭, module coefficients: L_n of the colimit over Δᵒᵖ is the homology of the alternating-face-map complex of the simplicial B-module itself. The ring and the module sections lie in the universe of Δ, which is 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedColimitPresheafRestrictionNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QA.** Let `f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories and let `U_•` be a
cosimplicial object of `C'` such that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then the
homology of `C'` with coefficients the restriction of an abelian presheaf `ℱ` on `C` along `f` is
the homology of `C` with coefficients `ℱ`, in every degree and naturally in `ℱ`: that is,
`L_nπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = L_nπ_!`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedColimitPresheafRestrictionNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) (n : ℕ) :
    Stacks.CategoryHomology.presheafRestriction.{u, u, u} f ⋙
        (colim : (C'ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n ≅
      (colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n
declarations.comment: the identification `L_nπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = L_nπ_!` degreewise, for the left derived functors of `colim` at abelian coefficients. The derived-category forms at a single module of coefficients are `Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionNatIso` and `Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageNatIso`, and at an arbitrary bounded above COMPLEX of coefficients — the form the source states — `Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionComplexNatIso` and `Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageComplexNatIso`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories with their chaotic topologies, let
`g^{-1}` be restriction of abelian presheaves along `f`, and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of
`C'` such that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then the derived lower shriek on
`C'` of the restriction of an abelian presheaf `ℱ` on `C` is the derived lower shriek of `ℱ` on
`C`, as an isomorphism of functors into `D(Ab)` and naturally in `ℱ`: that is,
`Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    Stacks.CategoryHomology.presheafRestriction.{u, u, u} f ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.single (C'ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C' AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(Ab)`, at abelian coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors whose domain is the category of abelian presheaves on `C` — the heart. The same identification for an arbitrary bounded above COMPLEX of abelian presheaves, which is what the source's `D(C) ⥤ D(Ab)` says, is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionComplexNatIso`; the unbounded case is open and the implementation note says what it needs

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories with their chaotic topologies, let `B`
be a ring, let `g^{-1}` be the inverse image of the induced morphism of ringed topoi — restriction
of diagrams of `B`-modules along `f` — and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C'` such that
both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then the derived lower shriek on `C'` of the
inverse image of a `B̲`-module `ℱ` on `C` is the derived lower shriek of `ℱ` on `C`, as an
isomorphism of functors into `D(B)` and naturally in `ℱ`: that is, `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitInverseImageNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    inverseImageAlongAFunctor C C' f B ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.single (C'ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C' (ModuleCat.{u} B) ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} B)
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(B)`, at module coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors whose domain is the category of `B̲`-modules on `C` — the heart. The same identification for an arbitrary bounded above COMPLEX of `B̲`-modules, which is what the source's `D(C, B̲) ⥤ D(B)` says, is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageComplexNatIso`; the unbounded case is open and the implementation note says what it needs

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageComplexNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QA in `D(B)` for bounded above complexes, as an isomorphism of functors.** Let
`f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories with their chaotic topologies, let `B` be a
ring, let `g^{-1}` be the inverse image of the induced morphism of ringed topoi — restriction of
diagrams of `B`-modules along `f` — and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C'` such that both
`U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then

`Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!`

as functors from the complexes of `B̲`-modules on `C` strictly bounded above by `0` to `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitInverseImageComplexNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    (strictlyLEZero (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B)).ι ⋙
        (inverseImageAlongAFunctor C C' f B).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C' (ModuleCat.{u} B) ≅
      (strictlyLEZero (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B)).ι ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} B)
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(B)`, at module coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors of a COMPLEX of coefficients strictly bounded above by `0`, whose domain contains the complexes concentrated in degree `0`, so that the statement specialises to the form at the heart (the two isomorphisms are not compared). The source states the identification on the unbounded `D(C, B̲)`; the module docstring records what the unbounded case needs, namely the dévissage along the compact generators, the total complex of the double complex of an unbounded complex not being `Lπ_!` of it

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionComplexNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QA in `D(Ab)` for bounded above complexes, as an isomorphism of functors.** Let
`f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories with their chaotic topologies, let `g^{-1}` be
restriction of abelian presheaves along `f`, and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C'` such
that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then

`Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!`

as functors from the complexes of abelian presheaves on `C` strictly bounded above by `0` to
`D(Ab)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionComplexNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    (strictlyLEZero (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})).ι ⋙
        (Stacks.CategoryHomology.presheafRestriction.{u, u, u} f).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C' AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      (strictlyLEZero (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})).ι ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit C AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(Ab)`, at abelian coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors of a COMPLEX of coefficients strictly bounded above by `0`, whose domain contains the complexes concentrated in degree `0`, so that the statement specialises to the form at the heart (the two isomorphisms are not compared). The source states the identification on the unbounded `D(C)`; the module docstring records what the unbounded case needs, namely the dévissage along the compact generators, the total complex of the double complex of an unbounded complex not being `Lπ_!` of it

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.isIso_derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedComparison
declarations.doc:
For a functor `f : C' ⥤ C` between small categories with their chaotic topologies and a
cosimplicial object `U_•` of `C'` such that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions, the
comparison `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} ⟶ Lπ_!` of
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedComparison` is an
isomorphism of functors `D(C, B̲) ⥤ D(B)` on the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem ModuleValued.isIso_derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedComparison
    {U : CosimplicialObject C'} (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    IsIso (ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedComparison (B := B) f)
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(B)`, at module coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors on the UNBOUNDED derived category `D(C, B̲)`, which is what the source's `resp. D(C, B̲) ⥤ D(B)` says. The other half of the source's `resp.`, the unbounded statement with values in `D(Ab)`, is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.isIso_derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedComparison` in `DerivedColimitUnboundedIsIsoAbelian.lean`: the same mechanism at `AddCommGrpCat`, whose separating family of projective compact objects is `ULift ℤ`.

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedNatIso
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism of functors `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} ≅ Lπ_!` from `D(C, B̲)` to `D(B)` on the
unbounded derived category, when `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions.
declarations.statement:
def ModuleValued.derivedColimitInverseImageUnboundedNatIso
    {U : CosimplicialObject C'} (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    (inverseImageAlongAFunctor C C' f B).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        totalDerivedColimit C' (ModuleCat.{u} B) ≅
      totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} B)
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(B)` as an ISOMORPHISM OF FUNCTORS on the unbounded derived category `D(C, B̲)`, packaged from the invertibility of the comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.isIso_derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedComparison
declarations.doc:
For a functor `f : C' ⥤ C` between small categories with their chaotic
topologies and a cosimplicial object `U_•` of `C'` such that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point
resolutions, the comparison `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} ⟶ Lπ_!` of
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedComparison` is an
isomorphism of functors `D(C) ⥤ D(Ab)` on the unbounded derived category `D(C)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem AbelianValued.isIso_derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedComparison
    {U : CosimplicialObject C'} (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    IsIso (AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedComparison f)
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(Ab)`, at abelian coefficients, as an isomorphism of functors on the UNBOUNDED derived category `D(C)`, which is what the source's `as functors D(C) ⥤ D(Ab)` says

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedNatIso
declarations.doc:
For a functor `f : C' ⥤ C` between small categories with their chaotic topologies and a
cosimplicial object `U_•` of `C'` such that both `U_•` and `f(U_•)` are point resolutions, the
isomorphism of functors `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} ≅ Lπ_!` from `D(C)` to `D(Ab)` on the unbounded derived
category.
declarations.statement:
def AbelianValued.derivedColimitPresheafRestrictionUnboundedNatIso
    {U : CosimplicialObject C'} (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) :
    (Stacks.CategoryHomology.presheafRestriction.{u, u, u} f).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        totalDerivedColimit C' AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      totalDerivedColimit C AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the identification `Lπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = Lπ_!` with values in `D(Ab)` as an ISOMORPHISM OF FUNCTORS on the unbounded derived category `D(C)`, packaged from the invertibility of the comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPresheafRestrictionNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08QA for `Lπ_!`.** Let `f : C' ⥤ C` be a functor between small categories with their
chaotic topologies and let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C'` such that both `U_•` and
`f(U_•)` are point resolutions. Then the sections at the point of `L_nπ'_!` applied to the
inverse image of an abelian sheaf `ℱ` on `C` are the sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)`, in
every degree and naturally in `ℱ`: that is, `L_nπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = L_nπ_!`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPresheafRestrictionNatIso (f : C' ⥤ C) (U : CosimplicialObject C')
    (hU : IsPointResolution U) (hfU : IsPointResolution (U ⋙ f)) (n : ℕ) :
    f.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C')
          (GrothendieckTopology.trivial C) ⋙
        (abelianPointLowerShriek C').leftDerived n ⋙
          pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      (abelianPointLowerShriek C).leftDerived n ⋙
        pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the identification `L_nπ'_! ∘ g^{-1} = L_nπ_!` for the sheaf-theoretic lower shriek along the point morphism, read through the sections at the point

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.isIso_derivedExternalTensorComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QB.**  Let `C₁` and `C₂` be categories, `g_i` the morphisms of ringed topoi
induced by the two projections of `C₁ × C₂`, and `R` a ring.  For `K_i ∈ D(C_i, R)` the canonical
comparison

`L(π₁ × π₂)_!(g₁^{-1}K₁ ⊗^L_{R̲} g₂^{-1}K₂) ⟶ Lπ_{1,!}K₁ ⊗^L_R Lπ_{2,!}K₂`

is an isomorphism in `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedExternalTensorComparison
    (K₁ : DerivedCategory (C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (K₂ : DerivedCategory (C₂ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    IsIso (derivedExternalTensorComparison C₁ C₂ R exists_kFlat_quasiIso_diagrams K₁ K₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.colimExternalTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QB, the identity with the derived functors replaced by the underived ones.** The
colimit over the product of two opposite categories of an external tensor product of diagrams is
the tensor product of the two colimits.
declarations.statement:
def colimExternalTensorIso (F : C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B)
    (G : C₂ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B) :
    (colim : ((C₁ × C₂)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B) ⥤ _).obj (externalTensor F G) ≅
      (colim : (C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B) ⥤ _).obj F ⊗
        (colim : (C₂ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B) ⥤ _).obj G
declarations.comment: the identity with both derived functors replaced by the underived ones, `π_!(g₁⁻¹F ⊗_B̲ g₂⁻¹G) ≅ π_{1,!}F ⊗_B π_{2,!}G` for diagrams of `B`-modules, with `π_!` the colimit over the site of Tag 08PF; the derived identity is not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryHomology.externalTensorFreeYonedaIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QB, the computation of its proof on the generators.** For `U` an object of `C₁`
and `V` an object of `C₂`, the external tensor product of the free diagram on `U` with
coefficients `P` and the free diagram on `V` with coefficients `Q` is the free diagram on
`(U, V)` with coefficients `P ⊗_B Q`.
declarations.statement:
def externalTensorFreeYonedaIso (U : C₁) (V : C₂)
    (P Q : ModuleCat.{max u₁ u₂ w} B) :
    externalTensor (C₂ := C₂) (Presheaf.freeYoneda U P) (Presheaf.freeYoneda V Q) ≅
      Presheaf.freeYoneda ((U, V) : C₁ × C₂) (P ⊗ Q)
declarations.comment: the computation `g₁⁻¹j_{U!}B̲_U ⊗_B̲ g₂⁻¹j_{V!}B̲_V = j_{(U,V)!}B̲_{(U,V)}` made in the proof, for arbitrary coefficient modules in place of `B̲`; the derived identity that it is used to prove is not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.totalDerivedColimitTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08QC].**  Let `C` be a small category with the chaotic topology and `R` a
commutative ring, as in Example 08PF, and suppose `C` carries a cosimplicial object `U_•` to which
Tag 08Q9 applies: for every object `W` the simplicial set `Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent
to a point.  Then derived lower shriek to the point preserves derived tensor products:

`Lπ_!(K₁ ⊗^L_{R̲} K₂) ≅ Lπ_!(K₁) ⊗^L_R Lπ_!(K₂)`

for all `K₁, K₂ ∈ D(R̲)`, naturally in both, as an isomorphism of bifunctors
`D(Cᵒᵖ ⥤ R-Mod) × D(Cᵒᵖ ⥤ R-Mod) ⥤ D(R)`.

It is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.totalDerivedColimitTensorIsoOfExternal` (Tags 07A4, 08Q4 and 08QA along
the diagonal) applied to [Stacks, Tag 08QB] on `C × C`,
`Stacks.CategoryHomology.isIso_derivedExternalTensorComparisonNatTrans`.
declarations.statement:
def totalDerivedColimitTensorIso (U : CosimplicialObject C) (hU : IsPointResolution U) :
    letI := derivedMonoidal (ModuleCat.{u} R)
      (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.OneSided.exists_kFlat_quasiIso R)
    letI := derivedMonoidal (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R) (exists_kFlat_quasiIso_diagrams (J := Cᵒᵖ))
    MonoidalCategory.tensor (DerivedCategory (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R)) ⋙
        totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} R) ≅
      (totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} R)).prod (totalDerivedColimit C (ModuleCat.{u} R)) ⋙
        MonoidalCategory.tensor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.quasiIso_alexanderWhitney
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QD.** The Alexander–Whitney map of two simplicial modules is a
quasi-isomorphism. This is the Eilenberg–Zilber theorem: the Moore complex
`s(M ⊗_B N)` of the degreewise tensor product is computed, through the canonical comparison,
by the total complex `s(M) ⊗_B s(N)` of the double complex of the two Moore complexes.
declarations.statement: public instance quasiIso_alexanderWhitney : QuasiIso (alexanderWhitney M N)
declarations.comment: flat_eilenberg_zilber

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.simplexCategoryModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QD, `Mod(B̲)` on `Δ`.** For the chaotic site `Δ` and a ring `B`, the category
`Mod(B̲)` of modules over the constant sheaf of rings `B̲` is the category of simplicial
`B`-modules.
declarations.comment: `Mod(B̲)` is the category of simplicial `B`-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.simplexCategoryMooreNatIsoDerivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QD, `Lπ_!` of a simplicial module is its associated complex.** For the chaotic
site `Δ` and a ring `B`, the derived lower shriek `Lπ_! : D(B̲) ⥤ D(B)` sends a simplicial
`B`-module `M_•`, placed in degree zero, to its associated complex `s(M_•)`, the
alternating-face-map complex, read as a cochain complex in nonpositive degrees:

`Q(s(M_•)) ≅ Lπ_!(M_•)` in `D(B)`, naturally in `M_•`.

Here `Lπ_!` is the total left derived functor of the colimit over `Δᵒᵖ`, which is `π_!` on the
chaotic site by Example 08PF, and a `B̲`-module is a simplicial `B`-module by
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.simplexCategoryModuleEquivalence`. The proof is Lemma 08Q9 for the point
resolution `U_• = 𝟭 Δ`, at which the evaluation `M(U_•)` is `M_•` itself.
declarations.statement:
def simplexCategoryMooreNatIsoDerivedLowerShriek :
    alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{w} B) ⋙
        (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE (0 : ℤ)).extendFunctor (ModuleCat.{w} B) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      HomologicalComplex.single (SimplicialObject (ModuleCat.{w} B)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ totalDerivedColimit SimplexCategory (ModuleCat.{w} B)
declarations.comment: `Lπ_!` sends a simplicial `B`-module `M_•` to its associated complex `s(M_•)`, as an isomorphism in `D(B)` natural in `M_•`

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.flatEilenbergZilber
declarations.doc:
**The Eilenberg–Zilber comparison holds for every commutative ring.** For two degreewise flat
simplicial `B`-modules the Moore complex of the degreewise tensor product is quasi-isomorphic to
the total tensor product of the Moore complexes, the quasi-isomorphism being the
Alexander–Whitney map `AlgebraicTopology.alexanderWhitney` (Stacks 08QD,
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.quasiIso_alexanderWhitney`, which needs no flatness).
declarations.statement:
theorem flatEilenbergZilber.{t, s} (B : Type s) [CommRing B] :
    FlatEilenbergZilber.{t, s} B
declarations.comment: flat_eilenberg_zilber: for flat simplicial `B`-modules `M_•`, `M'_•`, the complex `s(M_• ⊗_B M'_•)` is quasi-isomorphic to the total complex of `s(M_•) ⊗_B s(M'_•)`

registrations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.isPointResolution_id_simplexCategory
registrations.comment: the identity functor of `Δ` is a point resolution, which is the hypothesis of Lemma 08Q9 for `C = Δ`

registrations.name: SSet.stdSimplex.homotopyEquivalences_hom_obj₀
registrations.comment: simplex_contractible

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.atiyahModuleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08QE] at the site `C_{B/A}` itself.** Derived lower shriek of the inverse
image of a `B`-module is that module: `Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M` in `D(B)`, naturally in `M`. Here
`π^{-1}` is the constant diagram and `Lπ_!` the total left derived functor of the colimit over
the index category, which is the `π_!` of [Stacks, Tag 08PF]; the coefficient ring is
`ULift B`, the ring of the site's own ringed point `CommAlgCat.polynomialRingedPoint`.

The proof is the source's: the augmentation `A → B` is a terminal object of the site
(`CommAlgCat.isTerminal_atiyahBaseObj`), so `π^{-1}` has the exact right adjoint "sections over
`A → B`" and `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedConstCompColimitIso` applies with no hypothesis on the
existence of the derived functor. The statement at the footnote-restricted site is
`CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialModuleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso`; that is a statement
about different coefficients, the restriction to a full subcategory changing both `Mod(B̲)` and
`Lπ_!`.
declarations.statement:
def atiyahModuleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso :
    (Functor.const (atiyahSite A B)ᵒᵖ :
          ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u)) ⥤ _).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        totalDerivedColimit (atiyahSite A B)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))) ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients: Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M at `CommAlgCat.polynomialSite` -- the site of Tag 08PR itself, not a restriction of it, read on its `AsSmall` model -- with Lπ_! the total left derived functor of the colimit on D(B̲), π^{-1} the constant diagram, and the coefficient ring read as `ULift.{u+1} B` exactly as the site's own ringed point `CommAlgCat.polynomialRingedPoint` reads it

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialLeftDerivedZeroLowerShriekInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08QE at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`, in degree zero.** The
sections at the point of `L_0π_!(π^{-1}M)` are the sections of `M`, for every abelian sheaf `M`
on the point; here `π` is the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site.

This is the source's proof: Tag 08PT computes `Lπ_!(π^{-1}M)` by `(π^{-1}M)(P_•, ε)` for the
standard resolution, and that is the constant simplicial object on `M`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialLeftDerivedZeroLowerShriekInverseImageIso
    (M : Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
                (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).leftDerived 0).obj
          ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointInverseImage
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
              (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).obj M)) ≅
      (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj M
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M in degree zero, for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A} at abelian coefficients

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isZero_polynomialLeftDerivedSuccLowerShriekInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08QE at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`, in positive degrees.** The
sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(π^{-1}M)` vanish for `n > 0`, so together with
`CommAlgCat.polynomialLeftDerivedZeroLowerShriekInverseImageIso` this is the source's
`Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M`, read degreewise.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_polynomialLeftDerivedSuccLowerShriekInverseImage
    (M : Sheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (n : ℕ) :
    IsZero ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
      (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
              (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).leftDerived (n + 1)).obj
        ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointInverseImage
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).obj M)))
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M in positive degrees: L_nπ_!(π^{-1}M) = 0 for n > 0

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.smallPolynomialModuleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08QE in `D(B)` at the small model of the restricted site `C_{B/A}`.** Derived lower
shriek of the inverse image of a `B`-module is that module: `Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M` in `D(B)`,
naturally in `M`. Here `π^{-1}` is the constant diagram and `Lπ_!` the total left derived
functor of the colimit, and the proof is that the augmentation `A → B` is a terminal object of
the site, so that `π^{-1}` has the exact right adjoint "sections over `A → B`".
declarations.statement:
def smallPolynomialModuleDerivedInverseImageCompLowerShriekIso :
    (Functor.const (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)ᵒᵖ :
          ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u) ⥤ _).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        Stacks.CategoryHomology.totalDerivedColimit (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)
          (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: in D(B), at module coefficients: Lπ_!(π^{-1}M) = M for the point morphism of the small model of the footnote-restricted site C_{B/A}, with Lπ_! the total left derived functor of the colimit on D(B̲) and π^{-1} the constant diagram

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QF.** The degree-zero homology of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` is
the module of Kähler differentials `Ω[B⁄A]`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso :
    (cotangentComplex A B).homology 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of B (KaehlerDifferential A B)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialEvaluationLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QG.** For `B` a polynomial algebra over `A`, evaluation at the identity
augmentation `B → B` is left adjoint to `π^{-1}`: it *is* a lower shriek.
declarations.comment: evaluation at B → B is a lower shriek

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAbelianLowerShriekEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QG.** For `B` a polynomial algebra over `A`, the lower shriek `π_!` of Stacks 08PR
is canonically evaluation at the identity augmentation `B → B`.
declarations.comment: π_! is evaluation at B → B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_pointSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QG.** `π_!ℱ = ℱ(B → B)`: the sections of `π_!ℱ` at the point are the sections of
`ℱ` over the identity augmentation, naturally in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_pointSectionsIso (hB : IsPolynomialAlgebra A B) :
    polynomialAbelianLowerShriek.{m} A B ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) m} ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (polynomialTopology A B) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) m} ⋙
        (evaluation (polynomialSite A B)ᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) m}).obj
          (polynomialIdentityObj A B hB)
declarations.comment: π_!F = F(B → B)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QG.** For `B` a polynomial algebra over `A`, `π_!` preserves finite limits. With
`CommAlgCat.polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_preservesColimitsOfShape` this is the exactness of `π_!`
asserted by the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_preservesFiniteLimits (hB : IsPolynomialAlgebra A B) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (polynomialAbelianLowerShriek.{m} A B)
declarations.comment: π_! is exact: finite limits

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_preservesColimitsOfShape
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QG.** `π_!` preserves all colimits, being a left adjoint; no hypothesis on `B` is
needed for this half of exactness.
declarations.statement:
instance polynomialAbelianLowerShriek_preservesColimitsOfShape {K : Type*} [Category* K] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape K (polynomialAbelianLowerShriek.{m} A B)
declarations.comment: π_! is exact: colimits

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_iso_kaehlerDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QH.** If `B` is a polynomial algebra over the ring `A`, then the
cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` is quasi-isomorphic to `Ω[B⁄A][0]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cotangentComplex_iso_kaehlerDifferential (hB : Algebra.IsPolynomialAlgebra A B) :
    Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex A B) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of B (KaehlerDifferential A B)))

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.IsResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QI.**

An augmentation `ε : P• ⟶ B` of a simplicial commutative `A`-algebra is a resolution of `B` over
`A` if every `Pₙ` is a polynomial algebra over `A` and the underlying augmentation of simplicial
sets is a trivial Kan fibration.
declarations.statement:
structure IsResolution (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (P : SimplicialObject (CommAlgCat.{v} A))
    (ε : P ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of A B)) : Prop
declarations.comment: resolution

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isResolution_quasiIso_homotopyEquivalence_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QI.**

For an augmentation `ε : P• ⟶ B` which is degreewise surjective and whose terms are polynomial
`A`-algebras, the following are equivalent: `ε` is a resolution, the induced map of associated
complexes is a quasi-isomorphism, and the underlying map of simplicial sets is a homotopy
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
lemma isResolution_quasiIso_homotopyEquivalence_tfae
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (P : SimplicialObject (CommAlgCat.{v} A))
    (ε : P ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of A B))
    (hP : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, IsPolynomialAlgebra A (P.obj n))
    (hε : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective (ε.app n).hom) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsResolution A B P ε,
       QuasiIso ((alternatingFaceMapComplex AddCommGrpCat.{v}).map
         (Functor.whiskerRight ε
           (forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{v} A) (AlgCat.{v} A) ⋙
            forget₂ (AlgCat.{v} A) (ModuleCat.{v} A) ⋙
            forget₂ (ModuleCat.{v} A) AddCommGrpCat.{v}))),
       SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type v)
         (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{v} A)))]
declarations.comment: resolution_criteria

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_isResolution
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Remark 08QI]: resolutions exist.** Every commutative `A`-algebra `B` admits a
resolution over `A`: the standard resolution of `B` over `A` is one, by
`CommAlgCat.standardResolution_isResolution`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResolution (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] :
    ∃ (P : SimplicialObject (CommAlgCat.{max u v} A))
      (ε : P ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const (CommAlgCat.{max u v} A)).obj (CommAlgCat.of A B)),
      IsResolution A B P ε
declarations.comment: existence of resolutions: every A-algebra B admits a resolution, namely the standard resolution

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexIsoOfResolution
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Remark 08QI]: any resolution computes the cotangent complex.** Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be
a resolution of `B` over `A` — every `P_n` a polynomial algebra over `A`, `ε` a trivial Kan
fibration of the underlying simplicial sets — with no bound on the number of variables. Then the
cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 08PN], which is built from the *standard* resolution,
is the complex of base-changed differentials of `P_•`, as objects of `D(B)`:

`Q(L_{B/A}) ≅ Q(Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•, ε} B)`.

The proof is the source's. At the cardinal `CommAlgCat.resolutionVarCardinal`, which bounds the
terms of `P_•` and those of the standard resolution at once, both resolutions lie on the small
model of the footnote-restricted site, so the two instances of [Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)` —
`CommAlgCat.standardResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIsoOfLE` and
`CommAlgCat.smallResolutionCotangentDerivedLowerShriekIso` — identify both complexes with
`Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)`, which mentions no resolution.
declarations.comment: in D(B): for an arbitrary resolution of B over A, with no bound on the number of variables, Q(L_{B/A}) = Q(Omega[P_bullet/A] ⊗_{P_bullet} B); the cardinal bound of the two instances of Tag 08PU this composes is supplied by the resolution itself

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.resolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(ℱ) = ℱ(P_•, ε)` in `D(B)` for an arbitrary resolution.** Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a
resolution of `B` over `A`, with no bound on the number of variables. For every sheaf of
`B`-modules `ℱ` on the small model of the site `C_{B/A}` restricted to polynomial algebras on at
most `CommAlgCat.resolutionVarCardinal A B hε.isPolynomialAlgebra` variables — a bound the
resolution supplies — the sections at the point of `L_nπ_!(ℱ)` are the degree `n` homology of the
Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module `ℱ(P_•, ε)`, naturally in `ℱ`.

This is `CommAlgCat.smallResolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso` at that cardinal. A bound
cannot be dispensed with altogether here, as it can in
`CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexIsoOfResolution`: the site, and with it `π_!`, is the one restricted
by the bound.
declarations.statement:
def resolutionModuleLeftDerivedLowerShriekNatIso (n : ℕ) :
    (modulePointLowerShriek
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (resolutionVarCardinal A B hε.isPolynomialAlgebra))
          (B : Type u)).leftDerived n ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (GrothendieckTopology.trivial
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (resolutionVarCardinal A B hε.isPolynomialAlgebra)))
          (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u)) ⋙
        moduleCosimplicialMooreComplex (smallResolutionCosimplicialObject ε
            (resolutionVarCardinal A B hε.isPolynomialAlgebra)
            (isPolynomialAlgebraBelow_resolutionVarCardinal A B hε.isPolynomialAlgebra)) ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))
            (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n
declarations.comment: the cosimplicial object of a resolution and the conclusion Lpi_!(F) = F(P_bullet, ε) in D(B) functorially in F, for an arbitrary resolution with no bound on the number of variables, read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site for the reason recorded in `StacksFrontier/Cotangent/ResolutionPointCriterionSmall.lean`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.quasiIso_alternatingFaceMapComplex_map_of_isResolution
declarations.doc:
**Remark 08QI at the arrow level.** Let `ε : P_• ⟶ B` and `ε' : P'_• ⟶ B` be resolutions of
`B` over `A` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 08QI]. Every morphism `ψ` of the attached simplicial
objects of `Over B` — equivalently, every morphism `P_• ⟶ P'_•` of simplicial `A`-algebras
compatible with the augmentations — induces a quasi-isomorphism

`Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B ⟶ Ω[P'_•⁄A] ⊗_{P'_•} B`.

So any resolution computes the cotangent complex, and the isomorphism is the one a morphism of
resolutions induces; no cardinal bound appears, the terms of the two resolutions being bounded by
a single cardinal.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_alternatingFaceMapComplex_map_of_isResolution
    (hres : IsResolution A (B : Type u) P ε) (hres' : IsResolution A (B : Type u) P' ε')
    (ψ : resolutionOver ε ⟶ resolutionOver ε') :
    QuasiIso ((alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))).map
      (Functor.whiskerRight ψ (overDifferentialsFunctor (A := A) (B := B))))
declarations.comment: the remark's payoff, at the arrow level: for any two resolutions of B over A and any morphism between them, the induced map of the complexes Omega[-/A] ⊗ B is a quasi-isomorphism, so any resolution computes L_{B/A} and the comparison is the induced map

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.resolutionCotangentComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Remark 08QI at the object level.** The complex `Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗_{P_•} B` of an arbitrary
resolution of `B` over `A`, read in cohomological degrees `≤ 0`, is the cotangent complex
`L_{B/A}` in `D(B)`. Both are identified with `Lπ_!(i^*Ω_{𝒪/A})` by [Stacks, Tag 08PU] in `D(B)`,
read at a bound containing both the given resolution and the standard one.
declarations.statement:
def resolutionCotangentComplexIso (hres : IsResolution A (B : Type u) P ε) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (B : Type u))).obj
            (resolutionOver ε ⋙ overDifferentialsFunctor)).extend
          (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE (0 : ℤ))) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B)
declarations.comment: the remark's payoff, at the object level: for any resolution of B over A the complex Omega[P_./A] ⊗_{P_.} B is L_{B/A} in D(B)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolution_isResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QI.** The standard augmented simplicial algebra of a commutative
`A`-algebra `B` is a resolution of `B` over `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardResolution_isResolution (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A) :
    IsResolution A B (standardResolution A B).left (standardResolution A B).hom
declarations.comment: standard_qualifies

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_smallPolynomialAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**The change of coefficients of [Stacks, Tag 08QJ].** Let `A → B` be a ring map and let
`𝒪`, `B̲` and `π` be as in [Stacks, Tag 08PR], read on the small model of `C_{B/A}` at the
cardinal `CommAlgCat.standardResolutionVarCardinal A B` bounding the standard resolution. Then
for every `𝒪`-module `ℱ`, placed in cohomological degree zero, the canonical comparison

`Lπ_!(ℱ) ⟶ Lπ_!(ℱ ⊗^L_𝒪 B̲)`

is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)`.

The source states the right-hand side as `Lπ_!(Li^*ℱ)` for the morphism of topoi `i` attached to
the ring map `B ⟶ B`; on a chaotic site that morphism is the identity on topoi, so `Li^*ℱ` and
`ℱ ⊗^L_𝒪 B̲` are one and the same object of `D(Mod(B̲))` and the two readings of the statement
coincide. The comparison itself is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitTensorComparison`: derived
lower shriek applied to the unit of the derived change-of-coefficients adjunction, followed by
the identification of `Lπ_!` on `B̲`-modules with `Lπ_!` on their underlying `𝒪`-modules, which
is an isomorphism because restriction of scalars does not change the underlying abelian
presheaf.

Both hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 08RX] are discharged, so nothing is assumed:
`CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_standardResolutionSmallCosimplicialObject` is [Stacks, Tag 08PS]
at this model, and
`CommAlgCat.isIso_leftDerivedColimit_map_smallPolynomialAugmentationAbelian` is
`Lπ_!(𝒪) = Lπ_!(B̲)` read degreewise. The dévissage from those two to an arbitrary `𝒪`-module
is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_app_single`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_smallPolynomialAugmentation
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u}
      (smallPolynomialStructurePresheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitTensorComparison
        (smallPolynomialAugmentation A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).app
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (PresheafOfModules.{u}
          (smallPolynomialStructurePresheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)))
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)))
declarations.comment: for an `𝒪`-module in cohomological degree zero, on the small model of the site `C_{B/A}`; on a chaotic site `Li^*ℱ` and `ℱ ⊗^L_𝒪 B̲` are the same object

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekDifferentialsBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A}) = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` in `D(Ab)` at the site `C_{B/A}` itself**, the last
identification of [Stacks, Tag 08QK], as the isomorphism **induced by the base-change unit**
`Ω_{𝒪/A} ⟶ Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲`.

Here `Ω_{𝒪/A}` is the sheaf of relative differentials of [Stacks, Tag 08PR]'s site, read on its
underlying abelian sheaf, `Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` is its base change along the augmentation `𝒪 ⟶ B̲` of
that tag, `π` is the point morphism of the site `C_{B/A}` -- not of a restriction of it -- and
`Lπ_!` is the total left derived functor of the colimit over the index category, which is the
`π_!` of [Stacks, Tag 08PF]. There is no hypothesis on `A → B` beyond its being a ring map, and no
cardinal bound on the sets of variables.

The two inputs are the criterion of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] with no smallness hypothesis on the site,
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.isIso_totalDerivedColimit_single_map_iff_of_large`, and the
quasi-isomorphism of Moore complexes
`CommAlgCat.quasiIso_mooreCochain_polynomialSiteDifferentialsBaseChangeUnit`, which is the
Δ-instance of [Stacks, Tag 08RX] rather than [Stacks, Tag 08QJ].
declarations.statement:
def polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekDifferentialsBaseChangeIso :
    polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekSingle A B
        (polynomialSiteAbelianRelativeDifferentials A B) ≅
      polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekSingle A B
        (polynomialSiteAbelianDifferentialsBaseChange A B)
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A}) in D(Ab), as the isomorphism induced by the base-change unit Ω_{𝒪/A} ⟶ Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲, for the point morphism of the site C_{B/A} of Tag 08PR itself -- not of the footnote-restricted site nor of a small model of it -- with Ω_{𝒪/A} the sheaf of relative differentials of that site and Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲ its base change along the augmentation 𝒪 ⟶ B̲ of Tag 08PR, under no hypothesis on A → B and no cardinal bound

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekConstantIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(B̲) = B` in `D(Ab)` at the site `C_{B/A}` itself**, the second identification of
[Stacks, Tag 08QK]. Here `B̲` is the constant sheaf of rings with value `B` of
[Stacks, Tag 08PR] read on its underlying abelian sheaf, `π` is the point morphism of the site
`C_{B/A}` of that tag -- not of a restriction of it -- and `Lπ_!` is the total left derived
functor of the colimit over the index category, which is the `π_!` of [Stacks, Tag 08PF].

The proof is the source's: the polynomial algebra on no variables, augmented by `A → B`, is a
terminal object of the site (`CommAlgCat.isTerminal_polynomialBaseObj`), so `π^{-1}` is the
constant diagram and has an exact right adjoint, and [Stacks, Tag 08Q7] in the form
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedConstCompColimitIso'` gives `Lπ_! ∘ π^{-1} = id`.
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(B̲) = B in D(Ab), for the point morphism of the site C_{B/A} of Tag 08PR itself -- not of the footnote-restricted site nor of a small model of it -- with Lπ_! the total left derived functor of the colimit over the index category, which is the π_! of Tag 08PF, and with B read as the abelian group ULift.{u+1} B exactly as the site's own ringed point CommAlgCat.polynomialRingedPoint reads it

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekStructureConstantIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(𝒪) = Lπ_!(B̲)` in `D(Ab)` at the site `C_{B/A}` itself**, the first identification of
[Stacks, Tag 08QK], as the isomorphism **induced by the augmentation `𝒪 ⟶ B̲`** of
[Stacks, Tag 08PR].

The two inputs are the criterion of [Stacks, Tag 08Q9] with no smallness hypothesis on the site,
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.AbelianValued.isIso_totalDerivedColimit_single_map_iff_of_large`, and the
quasi-isomorphism of Moore complexes
`CommAlgCat.quasiIso_mooreCochain_polynomialSiteAbelianAugmentation`, whose own input is
[Stacks, Tag 08QI].
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(𝒪) = Lπ_!(B̲) in D(Ab), as the isomorphism induced by the augmentation 𝒪 ⟶ B̲ of Tag 08PR, for the point morphism of the site C_{B/A} of Tag 08PR itself -- not of the footnote-restricted site nor of a small model of it

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekStructureIso
declarations.doc:
**`Lπ_!(𝒪) = B` in `D(Ab)` at the site `C_{B/A}` itself**, the composite of the two
identifications `Lπ_!(𝒪) = Lπ_!(B̲)` and `Lπ_!(B̲) = B` of [Stacks, Tag 08QK].
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(𝒪) = B in D(Ab), for the point morphism of the site C_{B/A} of Tag 08PR itself -- not of the footnote-restricted site nor of a small model of it

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteDerivedLowerShriekCotangentIso
declarations.doc:
**`L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` in `D(Ab)` at the site `C_{B/A}` itself**, the third
identification of [Stacks, Tag 08QK]. The left-hand side is the cotangent complex of
[Stacks, Tag 08PN] with its `B`-module structures forgotten, read at the coefficient universe of
the site; the right-hand side is `Lπ_!` of the abelian sheaf `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A} = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲`.

The two inputs are [Stacks, Tag 08PS] at `C_{B/A}` itself,
`CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteResolutionDerivedColimitNatIso`, which computes `Lπ_!` by the extended
Moore complex of the evaluation on the standard resolution, and
`CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteCotangentMooreComplexIso`, which is [Stacks, Tag 08PU] identifying that
Moore complex with the complex of `L_{B/A}`.
declarations.comment: L_{B/A} = Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) in D(Ab), for the point morphism of the site C_{B/A} of Tag 08PR itself -- not of the footnote-restricted site nor of a small model of it: the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, read in D(Ab) at the coefficient universe of the site, is Lπ_! of the sheaf i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.isTransport_coefficientSquareComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison is the canonical one.** It is the identity of the restriction functor along
`C ⥤ *`, not some other automorphism of it; this is what makes
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.coefficientSquare_commutes` a statement about the square rather than about a
choice.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTransport_coefficientSquareComparison :
    Stacks.IsTransport (coefficientSquareComparison.{w} C φ).hom
declarations.comment: change-of-coefficients square: the comparison is the canonical one

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.coefficientSquare_commutes
declarations.doc:
**The change-of-coefficients square commutes.** The structure map of the one composite,
transported along the adjoint mate of the canonical comparison, is the structure map of the
other; see `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.SquareCommutes`, which is that equation.
declarations.statement:
theorem coefficientSquare_commutes :
    SquareCommutes (X := constantRingedTopos C R')
      (Y := constantRingedTopos (Discrete PUnit.{u₁ + 1}) R)
      (coefficientSquareDownAcross.{w} C φ) (coefficientSquareAcrossDown.{w} C φ)
      (coefficientSquareComparison.{w} C φ)
declarations.comment: the change-of-coefficients square of constant-coefficient ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.isTransport_functorialitySquareComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison is the canonical one**, hence a transport: it is built from the
identification `u ⋙ star = star` of the two functors to the point and nothing else.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTransport_functorialitySquareComparison :
    Stacks.IsTransport (functorialitySquareComparison.{w} C D u R).hom
declarations.comment: functoriality triangle: the comparison is the canonical one

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.functorialitySquare_commutes
declarations.doc:
**The functoriality triangle commutes.** Every edge is a transport, so the structure map of
`π_C ∘ g` transported along the adjoint mate of the canonical comparison is the structure map of
`π_D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem functorialitySquare_commutes :
    (constantRingedTopos (Discrete PUnit.{u₁ + 1}) R).forgetRing.map
        (functorialitySquareAcrossDown.{w} C D u R).fSharp ≫
      (((functorialitySquareAcrossDown.{w} C D u R).toToposHom.adj.ofNatIsoLeft
            (functorialitySquareComparison.{w} C D u R)).rightAdjointUniq
          (constantProjection.{w} D R).toToposHom.adj).hom.app
        ((constantRingedTopos D R).forgetRing.obj (constantRingedTopos D R).O) =
      (constantRingedTopos (Discrete PUnit.{u₁ + 1}) R).forgetRing.map
        (constantProjection.{w} D R).fSharp
declarations.comment: the functoriality triangle of constant-coefficient ringed topoi

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.baseChangeAugmentation_tmul
declarations.doc: The augmentation of `A' ⊗_A P` sends `a' ⊗ p` to `a' · b(α(p))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeAugmentation_tmul (X : Over B) (a' : A') (p : (X.left : Type u)) :
    baseChangeAugmentation b X (a' ⊗ₜ[A] p) =
      algebraMap A' (B' : Type u) a' * b (X.hom.hom p)
declarations.comment: base-change augmentation on a pure tensor

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.baseChangeMap_tmul
declarations.doc: Extension of scalars of a morphism `f` of augmented algebras sends `a' ⊗ p` to `a' ⊗ f(p)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeMap_tmul {X Y : Over B} (f : X ⟶ Y) (a' : A') (p : (X.left : Type u)) :
    baseChangeMap f (a' ⊗ₜ[A] p) = a' ⊗ₜ[A] f.left.hom p
declarations.comment: base change of a morphism on a pure tensor

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isPolynomialAlgebra_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Extension of scalars takes a polynomial `A`-algebra to a polynomial `A'`-algebra:
`A' ⊗_A A[S] = A'[S]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPolynomialAlgebra_baseChange (P : CommAlgCat.{u} A)
    (hP : IsPolynomialAlgebra A P) :
    IsPolynomialAlgebra A' (baseChangeObj (A' := A') P)
declarations.comment: base change preserves polynomial algebras

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The functor of sites `C_{B/A} ⟶ C_{B'/A'}` induced by a commutative square of rings,
given by extension of scalars on polynomial algebras augmented to `B`.
declarations.statement: def polynomialBaseChange : polynomialSite A B ⥤ polynomialSite A' B'
declarations.comment: polynomial-site base change

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialBaseChange_obj_hom
declarations.doc:
The augmentation of the image of `X` under `polynomialBaseChange b` is
`baseChangeAugmentation b X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialBaseChange_obj_hom (X : polynomialSite A B) :
    ((polynomialBaseChange b).obj X).unop.obj.hom =
      CommAlgCat.ofHom (baseChangeAugmentation b X.unop.obj)
declarations.comment: polynomial-site base change on objects

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialBaseChange_map_left
declarations.doc:
The underlying algebra map of the image of `f` under `polynomialBaseChange b` is
`baseChangeMap f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialBaseChange_map_left {X Y : polynomialSite A B} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ((polynomialBaseChange b).map f).unop.hom.left =
      CommAlgCat.ofHom (baseChangeMap f.unop.hom)
declarations.comment: polynomial-site base change on morphisms

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.boundedPolynomialBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The base-change functor of sites `C_{B/A} ⟶ C_{B'/A'}`, between the sites restricted to
polynomial algebras on at most `κ` variables.
declarations.statement:
def boundedPolynomialBaseChange :
    boundedPolynomialSite A B κ ⥤ boundedPolynomialSite A' B' κ
declarations.comment: polynomial-site base change, with the section's footnote in force: the functor between the sites restricted to at most κ variables. The unrestricted version is `CommAlgCat.polynomialBaseChange`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIso
declarations.doc:
Let
```
A  --→  A'
|       |
B  --→  B'
```
be a commutative square of rings, let `C_{B/A}` and `C_{B'/A'}` be the sites of polynomial
algebras augmented to `B`, resp. to `B'`, of Tag 08PR, and let `g` be the morphism of topoi
induced by the base-change functor of Tag 08QN, so that `g^{-1}` is restriction along it. Let
`ε : P_• ⟶ B` be a resolution of `B` over `A` whose terms are polynomial algebras on at most
`κ` variables, and assume that the base-changed augmentation `A' ⊗_A P_• ⟶ B'` is again a
resolution of `B'` over `A'`. Then

`Lπ_!(g^{-1}ℱ') = Lπ'_!(ℱ')`

in every degree `n` and naturally in the abelian sheaf `ℱ'` on `C_{B'/A'}`, read through the
sections at the point. Both sites are read at the small model of their restriction to at most `κ`
variables.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIso
    (hε : SSet.trivialKanFibrations (Functor.whiskerRight ε (forget (CommAlgCat.{u} A))))
    (hres : IsResolution A' (B' : Type u)
      (simplicialBaseChange b ε) (augmentationBaseChange b ε))
    (n : ℕ) :
    (smallPolynomialBaseChange b κ).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ))
          (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A' B' κ)) ⋙
        (Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)).leftDerived n ⋙
          Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      (Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A' B' κ)).leftDerived n ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: a GENERALIZATION of the lemma: the identification `Lπ_!(g^{-1}ℱ') = Lπ'_!(ℱ')` under the weaker hypothesis that the base change `A' ⊗_A P_• ⟶ B'` of the chosen resolution is again a resolution, which is what the source's proof derives from `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'`. The source's own statement is `CommAlgCat.leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIsoOfTorIndependent`, proved from this one. Both are read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site `C_{B/A}` and through the sections at the point

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIsoOfTorIndependent
declarations.doc:
Let
```
A  --→  A'
|       |
B  --→  B'
```
be a commutative square of rings which induces a quasi-isomorphism `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'` — that is,
`Tor_i^A(A', B) = 0` for `i > 0` and the canonical map `A' ⊗_A B → B'` is bijective. Let
`C_{B/A}` and `C_{B'/A'}` be the sites of polynomial algebras augmented to `B`, resp. to `B'`, of
Tag 08PR, and let `g` be the morphism of topoi induced by the base-change functor of Tag 08QN, so
that `g^{-1}` is restriction along it. Then

`Lπ_!(g^{-1}ℱ') = Lπ'_!(ℱ')`

in every degree `n` and naturally in the abelian sheaf `ℱ'` on `C_{B'/A'}`, read through the
sections at the point. Both sites are read at the small model of their restriction to at most `κ`
variables, for any `κ` bounding the variables of a chosen resolution `ε : P_• ⟶ B` of `B` over
`A`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIsoOfTorIndependent
    (hres : IsResolution A (B : Type u) P ε)
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hφ : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b))
    (n : ℕ) :
    (smallPolynomialBaseChange b κ).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ))
          (GrothendieckTopology.trivial (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A' B' κ)) ⋙
        (Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
            (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B κ)).leftDerived n ⋙
          Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      (Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A' B' κ)).leftDerived n ⋙
        Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the lemma as stated: the identification `Lπ_!(g^{-1}ℱ') = Lπ'_!(ℱ')` from the source's own hypothesis that the square induce a quasi-isomorphism `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'`, written out as vanishing of the positive `Tor_i^A(A', B)` together with bijectivity of `A' ⊗_A B → B'`. Read at the small model of the footnote-restricted site `C_{B/A}` and through the sections at the point; the generalization assuming only that the base-changed augmentation is a resolution is `CommAlgCat.leftDerivedPointLowerShriekPolynomialBaseChangeNatIso`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_eq_counit
declarations.doc:
**The two shapes of the functoriality map agree, on the cotangent complexes.** The adjoint
map `L_{B/A} ⊗_B B' ⟶ L_{B'/A'}` of [Stacks, Tag 08QQ] is extension of scalars along `B → B'` of
the `B`-linear map `L_{B/A} ⟶ L_{B'/A'}` of [Stacks, Tag 08PN], followed by the counit
`B' ⊗_B L_{B'/A'} ⟶ L_{B'/A'}`.

This is `CommAlgCat.cotangentExtendScalarsMooreMap_eq_counit` transported through the reindexing
which places simplicial degree `n` in cohomological degree `-n`, by
`ModuleCat.extendMap_comp_extendRestrictScalarsAdjCounitComplex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_eq_counit :
    cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap b =
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars b.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
          (squareCotangentComplexMap.{u, u, u} (algebraSquareOfAlgHom b)) ≫
        ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdjCounitComplex b.toRingHom (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
          (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A' B')
declarations.comment: the arrow of the lemma is the functoriality map of Tag 08PN: the adjoint map out of extension of scalars is extension of scalars of the B-linear map of Tag 08PN followed by the counit, as an equality of maps of cotangent complexes

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsMooreMap_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QQ on the Moore complexes.** If the square induces `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'`, the
functoriality map of Tag 08PN is a quasi-isomorphism of the alternating face map complexes.
This is `CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsMooreMap` with Remark 08QI supplied by
`CommAlgCat.cotangentComputedByEveryResolution`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsMooreMap_unconditional
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hpush : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    QuasiIso (cotangentExtendScalarsMooreMap b)
declarations.comment: on the alternating-face-map complexes: under the source's own hypothesis and with no other, the functoriality map of Tag 08PN is a quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QQ.** If the commutative square `A → B`, `A → A'`, `B → B'`, `A' → B'` induces a
quasi-isomorphism `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'`, then the functoriality map `L_{B/A} ⊗_B B' ⟶ L_{B'/A'}` of
Tag 08PN is a quasi-isomorphism of cotangent complexes. This is
`CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap` with Remark 08QI supplied by
`CommAlgCat.cotangentComputedByEveryResolution`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_unconditional
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hpush : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    QuasiIso (cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap b)
declarations.comment: on the cotangent complexes, under the source's own hypothesis B ⊗_A^L A' = B' and no other: THE functoriality map of Tag 08PN is a quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isIso_Q_map_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QQ in the derived category.** Under the hypothesis `B ⊗_A^L A' = B'` the
functoriality map becomes an isomorphism `L_{B/A} ⊗_B^L B' ⟶ L_{B'/A'}` in `D(B')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_Q_map_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_unconditional
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hpush : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap b))
declarations.comment: the lemma as an isomorphism in D(B'): the image of the functoriality map of Tag 08PN under the localization D(B') is invertible, under the source's own hypothesis and no other

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentBaseChangeIsoUnconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QQ, the base-change isomorphism.** The isomorphism
`L_{B/A} ⊗_B^L B' ≅ L_{B'/A'}` in `D(B')` whose underlying morphism is the functoriality map of
the square.
declarations.statement:
def cotangentBaseChangeIsoUnconditional
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hpush : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars b.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A' B')
declarations.comment: the base-change isomorphism itself, as data: an isomorphism in D(B') whose underlying morphism is the functoriality map of Tag 08PN, under the source's own hypothesis and no other

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08QQ].** Let
```
A  --→  A'
|       |
B  --→  B'
```
be a commutative square of rings which induces a quasi-isomorphism `B ⊗_A^𝐋 A' = B'` — that is,
`Tor_i^A(A', B) = 0` for `i > 0` and the canonical map `A' ⊗_A B → B'` is bijective. Then the
functoriality map induces an isomorphism

`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B' ⟶ L_{B'/A'}`

in `D(B')`, where `- ⊗^𝐋_B B'` is the total derived extension-of-scalars functor of
`StacksFrontier.Homology.Tor.DerivedExtensionScalars`.

The arrow is the source's. The cotangent complex is a bounded above complex of free modules, so
`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B'` is the degreewise base change `B' ⊗_B L_{B/A}`
(`CommAlgCat.derivedExtensionScalarsCotangentComplexIso`), and on that the functoriality map of
[Stacks, Tag 08PN] after extension of scalars is
`CommAlgCat.cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap`, a quasi-isomorphism by
`CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap_unconditional`. That the isomorphism built
here is induced by the functoriality map and not merely some isomorphism between the two objects is
`CommAlgCat.derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso_hom`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hφ : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    (CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral
          b.toRingHom).functor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A' B')
declarations.comment: the lemma, with the arrow the source names: under the source's own hypothesis that the square induce a quasi-isomorphism B ⊗_A^L A' = B' — written out as vanishing of the positive Tor_i^A(A', B) together with bijectivity of A' ⊗_A B → B' — THE functoriality map of Tag 08PN induces an isomorphism L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B' ≅ L_{B'/A'} in D(B'), the derived tensor product being the chapter's total derived extension-of-scalars functor. That the underlying morphism is that functoriality map is CommAlgCat.derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso_hom below. No hypothesis beyond the source's is carried: Remark 08QI is proved, not assumed (CommAlgCat.cotangentComputedByEveryResolution)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism of Tag 08QQ is the one the functoriality map induces.** Its underlying
morphism is the image in `D(B')` of `CommAlgCat.cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap` — the
`B'`-linear adjoint of the `B`-linear map `L_{B/A} ⟶ L_{B'/A'}` of [Stacks, Tag 08PN] — read
after the identification of `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B'` with the degreewise base change `B' ⊗_B L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso_hom
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent A A' (B : Type u))
    (hφ : Function.Bijective (baseChangeUnit b)) :
    (derivedCotangentComplexBaseChangeFunctorialityIso b hTor hφ).hom =
      (derivedExtensionScalarsCotangentComplexIso b).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap b)
declarations.comment: that the isomorphism is induced by THE functoriality map of Tag 08PN: its underlying morphism in D(B') is the image of the chain-level map CommAlgCat.cotangentExtendScalarsComplexMap, read after the canonical identification of L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B' with the degreewise base change

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QS.**

The first displayed morphism `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C ⟶ L_{C/A}` of the triangle, for arbitrary ring
maps `A → B → C`: the functoriality map of Tag 08PN for the square `(𝟙_A, B → C)` after
extension of scalars along `B → C`, read through the identification of the derived base change
`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C` with the degreewise one `C ⊗_B L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
def fundamentalMor₁ :
    fundamentalVertex₁.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} A B C ⟶ fundamentalVertex₂.{u, u, u + 1} A C
declarations.comment: the first displayed morphism `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C ⟶ L_{C/A}`, canonical and with no hypothesis on the two ring maps: the functoriality map of Tag 08PN for the square (1_A, B → C) after extension of scalars. It is the first morphism of the distinguished triangle of Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`, whose third morphism is `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QS.**

The second displayed morphism `L_{C/A} ⟶ L_{C/B}` of the triangle, for arbitrary ring maps
`A → B → C`: the functoriality map of Tag 08PN for the square `(A → B, 𝟙_C)`, read in `D(C)`.
declarations.statement:
def fundamentalMor₂ :
    fundamentalVertex₂.{u, u, u + 1} A C ⟶ fundamentalVertex₃.{u, u, u + 1} B C
declarations.comment: the second displayed morphism `L_{C/A} ⟶ L_{C/B}`, canonical and with no hypothesis on the two ring maps: the functoriality map of Tag 08PN for the square (A → B, 1_C). It is the second morphism of the distinguished triangle of Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`, whose third morphism is `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QS.**

The first vertex `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C` of the displayed triangle, as an object of `D(C)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev fundamentalVertex₁ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} C)
declarations.comment: the first vertex of the displayed triangle, `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C`. The display's three morphisms are `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂` and `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`, and that the six form a distinguished triangle is Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QS.**

The second vertex `L_{C/A}` of the displayed triangle, as an object of `D(C)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev fundamentalVertex₂ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} C)
declarations.comment: the second vertex of the displayed triangle, `L_{C/A}`, the target of the first displayed morphism `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁` and the source of the second, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QS.**

The third vertex `L_{C/B}` of the displayed triangle, as an object of `D(C)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev fundamentalVertex₃ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} C)
declarations.comment: the third vertex of the displayed triangle, `L_{C/B}`, the target of the second displayed morphism `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂` and the source of the third, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`, which lands in `(L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C)[1]`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃
declarations.doc:
**The third displayed morphism of [Stacks, Tag 08QS], for arbitrary ring maps
`A → B → C`.** It is the connecting morphism of the fundamental triangle of
`A → B → B × C`, base changed along the flat ring map `B × C → C` and read between the display's
own vertices `L_{C/B}` and `(L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C)⟦1⟧`.
declarations.comment: the third displayed morphism `L_{C/B} → (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C)[1]`, for arbitrary ring maps `A → B → C`: the connecting morphism of the fundamental triangle of `A → B → B × C` base changed along `B × C → C`, read between the display's own two vertices. The display is a distinguished triangle on these three morphisms by `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08QX, and the distinguishedness asserted by the display of Tag 08QS.**
Let `A → B → C` be ring maps. Then

`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C ⟶ L_{C/A} ⟶ L_{C/B} ⟶ (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C)[1]`

is a distinguished triangle in `D(C)`, on the three vertices of the display of
[Stacks, Tag 08QS], with the display's own first two morphisms
`CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁` and `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂` — the two functoriality maps of
[Stacks, Tag 08PN] for the two commutative squares of the tower — and with
`CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃` for its third.

The display of Tag 08QS is written as a triangle, and what makes it one is exactly this
statement, so the display's distinguishedness clause is registered here as well: the three
objects and the three arrows of the display are named by
`CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₂`,
`CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₃`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂` and
`CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`, and that they form a triangle at all is Proposition 08QX.

The proof is the one of [Stacks, Remark 08SD]: the triangle for `A → B → B × C`, where the map
is the split injection `b ↦ (b, f b)`, base changed along the flat projection `B × C → C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished :
    Triangle.mk (fundamentalMor₁.{u} A B C) (fundamentalMor₂.{u} A B C)
        (productFundamentalMor₃ A B C) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} C))
declarations.comment: the distinguishedness asserted by the display: Equation 92.7.0.1 is written as a triangle, and that the display's three objects and three arrows form a DISTINGUISHED triangle in `D(C)` is the remaining clause of the display, for arbitrary ring maps `A → B → C` with no hypothesis on them. The display's three vertices are `CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₂` and `CommAlgCat.fundamentalVertex₃` and its three morphisms are `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂` and `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`, each of which carries the tag for its own constituent. That the triangle is distinguished is Proposition 08QX, which this declaration also carries

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialTowerSite
declarations.doc:
The site `C_{C/B/A}`: the opposite of the category of polynomial towers `(P → B, Q → C)`,
so that an object corresponds to the commutative diagram of spectra in which
`Spec C → Spec Q` lies over `Spec B → Spec P` over `Spec A`.

declarations.doc:

sieves, so every presheaf on `C_{C/B/A}` is a sheaf.
declarations.statement: theorem polynomialTowerTopology_eq_bot : polynomialTowerTopology A B C = ⊥
declarations.comment: the chaotic topology on C_{C/B/A}

declarations.comment: the functor u₁

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isPolynomialAlgebra_towerRightAlgebra

The `A`-algebra `Q` of a polynomial tower is a polynomial algebra over `A`: it is a
polynomial algebra over the polynomial `A`-algebra `P`, and

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isPolynomialAlgebra_towerBaseChangeAlgebra

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.boundedPolynomialTowerSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08QT** with the footnote's restriction. The site `C_{C/B/A}` cut down to the towers
whose two polynomial layers have at most `κ`, resp. `μ`, variables: the opposite of
`CommAlgCat.BoundedPolynomialTower`. `CommAlgCat.polynomialTowerSite` is the same construction
with the footnote omitted.
declarations.statement: abbrev boundedPolynomialTowerSite
declarations.comment: the site C_{C/B/A} with the section's footnote in force, restricting the two layers of variables to cardinality at most κ, resp. μ. The unrestricted version is `CommAlgCat.polynomialTowerSite`; only this one is essentially small

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isPolynomialAlgebraBelow_towerRightAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The `A`-algebra `Q` of a restricted polynomial tower is a polynomial algebra over `A` on at
most `μ + κ` variables: it is `A[ι][τ] = A[τ ⊕ ι]` with `#ι ≤ κ` and `#τ ≤ μ`. This is what
makes `u₂` land in the restricted site `C_{C/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPolynomialAlgebraBelow_towerRightAlgebra (Y : BoundedPolynomialTower A B C κ μ) :
    IsPolynomialAlgebraBelow A (μ + κ) (towerRightAlgebra Y.obj)
declarations.comment: u₂ lands in C_{C/A}, for the small model of the footnote-restricted tower site: the bound on the two layers gives the bound μ + κ on the variables of Q over A

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isPolynomialAlgebraBelow_towerBaseChangeAlgebra
declarations.doc:
`Q ⊗_P B` is a polynomial algebra over `B` on at most `μ` variables: if `Q = P[τ]` then
`Q ⊗_P B = B[τ]`, with the same set of variables. This is what makes `u₃` land in the restricted
site `C_{C/B}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPolynomialAlgebraBelow_towerBaseChangeAlgebra (Y : BoundedPolynomialTower A B C κ μ) :
    IsPolynomialAlgebraBelow B μ (towerBaseChangeAlgebra Y.obj)
declarations.comment: u₃ lands in C_{C/B}, for the small model of the footnote-restricted tower site: the base change Q ⊗_P B has the same set of variables as Q over P, so the bound μ is kept

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.towerDifferential_shortExact_extendScalars
declarations.doc:
For a tower `R → P → Q` with `Q` formally smooth over `P`, the differential sequence
`0 → Q ⊗_P Ω_{P/R} → Ω_{Q/R} → Ω_{Q/P} → 0` of Algebra, Lemma 10.138.9 is split, so it stays
short exact after extending scalars along an arbitrary ring map `ε : Q → S`. This is the
objectwise input to the exactness of the sequence of Tag 08QU.
declarations.statement:
theorem towerDifferential_shortExact_extendScalars
    (R P Q S : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing P] [CommRing Q] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R P] [Algebra P Q] [Algebra R Q] [IsScalarTower R P Q]
    [Algebra.FormallySmooth P Q] (ε : Q →+* S) :
    ((ShortComplex.moduleCatMk (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange R P Q)
        (KaehlerDifferential.map R P Q Q) (by
          apply LinearMap.ext
          intro x
          exact (KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map R P Q).apply_apply_eq_zero x)).map
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars ε)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the objectwise split differential sequence after base change: the exactness input of the lemma, at an object of the site

`g₂⁻¹Ω₂`, a presheaf of `C̲`-modules on `C_{C/B/A}`: the inverse image along `g₂` is
restriction along `u₂`, and the inverse image of `C̲` is `C̲`.
declarations.statement: def towerSecondTerm : PresheafOfModules.{u + 1} (towerConstantRingSheaf A B C).obj
declarations.comment: the second term g₂⁻¹Ω₂ of the sequence

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.towerThirdTerm
declarations.doc: `g₃⁻¹Ω₃`, a presheaf of `C̲`-modules on `C_{C/B/A}`.
declarations.statement: def towerThirdTerm : PresheafOfModules.{u + 1} (towerConstantRingSheaf A B C).obj
declarations.comment: the third term g₃⁻¹Ω₃ of the sequence

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.towerFirstTerm
declarations.doc: `g₁⁻¹Ω₁ ⊗_{B̲} C̲`, a presheaf of `C̲`-modules on `C_{C/B/A}`.
