The six conjuncts are the array's six regions: zero strictly below the antidiagonal p + q = 0 (negative homological degree); zero strictly above the diagonal -p - q = p, by the final clause of Theorem 08RF; B at the top of the column p = 0; zero down the rest of that column, which Theorem 08RF's vanishing does not give since it is vacuous at p = 0; H^{-i}(L_{B/A}) down the column p = 1, by Tag 08PU together with Sym¹(Ω) = Ω, which at the position (1, -2) is the I/I² of the display's third row by the remark's opening clause; and ∧^p_B(I/I²) at the diagonal position (p, -2p), by the remark's second clause. The entries strictly inside the triangle with p ≥ 2, which the display writes as H_3(C_{B/A}, Sym²(Ω)) and H_4(C_{B/A}, Sym²(Ω)), the remark leaves unidentified and so does this statement. The display's parenthetical `with horizontal differential` is Theorem 08RF's clause that d_r has bidegree (r, -r + 1), at r = 1, which holds by definition of the type CohomologicalSpectralSequence _ 1 carried by CommAlgCat.QuillenSpectralSequenceData.sequence. I/I² is (CommAlgCat.surjectionExtension A B h).Cotangent, the conormal module of the presentation of B by A itself, which CommAlgCat.surjectionConormalAddEquiv identifies with Ideal.Cotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)). No hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity of A → B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteHomologyOneCotangentNegOneIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RG**, the first equality of the remark's opening clause, which is Tag 08PU in
degree `n = 1`: the sections at the point of `L₁π_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` are the degree `-1`
cohomology of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}`. The remark states it for a surjective `A → B`; it
holds for every ring map.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialSiteHomologyOneCotangentNegOneIso :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
                (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).leftDerived 1).obj
          (smallPolynomialCotangentSheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) ≅
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ↥B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        ((cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B).homology (-1))
declarations.comment: the first equality of the opening clause, H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω), as the degree n = 1 case of Tag 08PU: the sections at the point of L₁π_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) are the degree -1 cohomology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN. As in Tag 08PU, Lπ_! is read degreewise at abelian coefficients, as the left derived functors of the π_! of Tag 08PF, on the small model of the footnote-restricted site, so this is an isomorphism of abelian groups; the B-module statement H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = I/I² is Tag 08RA, CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_homologyNegOneIso. Proved for every ring map A → B, hence in particular for the surjective one of the remark

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteHomologyOneConormalIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RG**, the opening clause `H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω) = I/I²` for a
surjective ring map `A → B` with kernel `I`: the sections at the point of
`L₁π_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲)` are the conormal module `I/I²`. The isomorphism is the composite of
`CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteHomologyOneCotangentNegOneIso` with Tag 08RA's
`CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_homologyNegOneIso`, so it factors through `H^{-1}(L_{B/A})` exactly
as the remark says.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialSiteHomologyOneConormalIso :
    (Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointSections.{u, u + 1, u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (((Stacks.ChaoticSite.abelianPointLowerShriek
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B
                (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))).leftDerived 1).obj
          (smallPolynomialCotangentSheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) ≅
      AddCommGrpCat.of (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A ↥B)).Cotangent
declarations.comment: the second equality of the opening clause, H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω) = I/I² for I = ker(A → B), as the composite of the first equality with Tag 08RA: for a surjective A → B the sections at the point of L₁π_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲) are Ideal.Cotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)), by way of H^{-1}(L_{B/A}), so the whole opening clause is covered by this declaration together with CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteHomologyOneCotangentNegOneIso. As in Tag 08PU, Lπ_! is read degreewise at abelian coefficients, so this is an isomorphism of abelian groups; the B-module statement H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = I/I² is Tag 08RA itself. This declaration carries no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity of A → B. It states the opening clause and that clause alone; the section `Where the rest of 08RG stands` of this module's docstring says where each of the remark's other clauses stands

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.torToCotangentEdge
declarations.doc:
**The first family of edge maps of Stacks Remark 08RG**: for every `i > 0` a map

`Tor_i^A(B, B) ⟶ H^{-i}(L_{B/A})`.

It is the remark's own map, read off the filtration `… ⊆ 𝒦² ⊆ 𝒦 ⊆ Ō` of the abutment: the
composite

`Tor^A_i(B, B) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, Ō) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) ⟶ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦/𝒦²) ≅ H^{-i}(L_{B/A})`

of `CommAlgCat.torToCotangentHomologyEdge` with
`CommAlgCat.siteHomologyGradedOneCotangentIso`.  The first identification is
`CommAlgCat.leftDerivedColimQuotientTorIso`, the second
`CommAlgCat.leftDerivedColimAugmentationIdealIsoOfPos` — available because `H_j(C_{B/A}, B̲)`
vanishes for `j > 0` — the arrow is induced by the projection onto the first graded piece, and
the last identification is `Ω ≅ 𝒦/𝒦²` followed by Tag 08PU.

The remark states these maps for a surjective `A → B`; they exist for every ring map.
declarations.statement:
def torToCotangentEdge (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    (RingTheory.TorProducts.torBaseChange.{u, u, u} A (B : Type u) i).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (B : Type u)) ⟶
      (cotangentComplex.{u, u} A B).homology (-(i : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the first family of edge maps, Tor_i^A(B, B) → H^{-i}(L_{B/A}) for every i > 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B). These are the remark's own edge maps, read -- as the remark reads them -- off the filtration … ⊆ 𝒦² ⊆ 𝒦 ⊆ Ō of the abutment, where Ō = 𝒪 ⊗_A B̲ and 𝒦 = ker(Ō → B̲) are presheaves on C_{B/A}: the composite Tor^A_i(B,B) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, Ō) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) ⟶ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦/𝒦²) ≅ H^{-i}(L_{B/A}). Tor^A_i(B, B) is RingTheory.TorProducts.torBaseChange, the i-th left derived functor of extension of scalars along A → B, which is the spelling in which this development identifies the abutment H_i(C_{B/A}, Ō) of Theorem 08RF; H^{-i}(L_{B/A}) is the degree -i cohomology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, reached by Tag 08PU at linear coefficients; and H_i(C_{B/A}, -) = L_i colim over the opposite of the small model of the footnote-restricted site is Tag 08PF's definition of the homology of a category. No spectral sequence is involved, and no hypothesis is carried: the construction holds for every ring map A → B, hence in particular for the surjective one of the remark. The remark's SECOND family, ∧^i_B(I/I²) → Tor_i^A(B, B), is not this declaration; it needs the footnote vanishing of Theorem 08RF and is recorded separately

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.symmetricPowerToTorEdge_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The second family of edge maps of Stacks Remark 08RG**, for a surjective `A → B` and on no
other hypothesis: for every `i > 0` a map

`∧^i_B(I/I²) = H_i(C_{B/A}, Sym^i_{B̲}(Ω)) ⟶ Tor_i^A(B, B)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.symmetricPowerToTorEdge` with its hypothesis `hvan` discharged by
`isZero_leftDerivedColim_smallPolynomialAugmentationIdealPow_of_surjective_unconditional`,
the footnote vanishing of [Stacks, Tag 08RF]. The map itself is the remark's own, read off the
filtration `… ⊆ 𝒦² ⊆ 𝒦 ⊆ Ō` of the abutment.
declarations.statement:
def symmetricPowerToTorEdge_of_surjective
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A (B : Type u))) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    (siteHomologyFunctor A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B) i).obj
        (Stacks.ChaoticSite.symmetricPowerDiagram
          (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) (B : Type u)
          (smallPolynomialCotangentModulePresheaf A B
            (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) i) ⟶
      (RingTheory.TorProducts.torBaseChange.{u, u, u} A (B : Type u) i).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (B : Type u))
declarations.comment: the second family of edge maps, ∧^i_B(I/I²) → Tor_i^A(B, B) for every i > 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B). It is the remark's own map, read -- as the remark reads it -- off the filtration … ⊆ 𝒦² ⊆ 𝒦 ⊆ Ō of the abutment, where Ō = 𝒪 ⊗_A B̲ and 𝒦 = ker(Ō → B̲) are presheaves on C_{B/A}: the composite H_i(C_{B/A}, Sym^i(Ω)) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁱ/𝒦ⁱ⁺¹) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁱ) ⟶ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, Ō) ≅ Tor_i^A(B, B), whose middle isomorphism is the diagonal identification H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁱ) ≅ H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁱ/𝒦ⁱ⁺¹) and whose arrow is induced by the inclusion 𝒦ⁱ ⊆ 𝒦. Tor_i^A(B, B) is RingTheory.TorProducts.torBaseChange, the i-th left derived functor of extension of scalars along A → B, in which this development identifies the abutment H_i(C_{B/A}, Ō) of Theorem 08RF; and H_i(C_{B/A}, -) = L_i colim over the opposite of the small model of the footnote-restricted site is Tag 08PF's definition of the homology of a category. The source is written ∧^i_B(I/I²) by the remark and H_i(C_{B/A}, Sym^i_{B̲}(Ω)) here; they are the same object by the remark's own second clause, which this library has unconditionally as CommAlgCat.exteriorPower_conormal_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPower_of_surjective, and that clause is the other declaration of this part's covering set. It is stated at the symmetric power because the clause produces its linear equivalence inside a Nonempty -- Remark 08SG is reached by décalage, which chooses an isomorphism rather than constructing a canonical one -- so there is no canonical map out of ∧^i_B(I/I²) to be had. The construction needs the footnote vanishing H_j(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁿ) = 0 for j < n of the proof of Theorem 08RF, which is a theorem here for every surjective A → B, so no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity is carried

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The five term exact sequence of Stacks Remark 08RG, exactness at `H^{-3}(L_{B/A})`**, for
a surjective `A → B` and on no other hypothesis: the image of the edge map
`Tor_3^A(B, B) → H^{-3}(L_{B/A})` is the kernel of the middle map `H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree` with its hypothesis `hvan` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree_of_surjective
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A (B : Type u))) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (torToCotangentEdge A B 3 (by norm_num))
      (fiveTermConnecting_of_surjective A B hsurj)
      (torToCotangentEdge_comp_fiveTermConnecting A B
        (isZero_leftDerivedColim_smallPolynomialAugmentationIdealPow_of_surjective_unconditional
          A B hsurj))).Exact
declarations.comment: the five term exact sequence of low degree terms, Tor_3^A(B, B) → H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B) -- exactness at H^{-3}(L_{B/A}). The sequence is the five term segment of the long exact sequence of 0 → 𝒦² → 𝒦 → 𝒦/𝒦² → 0 on C_{B/A} read through the remark's identifications H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) = Tor_i^A(B, B) for i ≥ 1, H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦/𝒦²) = H^{-i}(L_{B/A}) and H_2(C_{B/A}, 𝒦²) = H_2(C_{B/A}, Sym²(Ω)) = ∧²_B(I/I²), the last of these being the remark's second clause (CommAlgCat.exteriorPower_conormal_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPower_of_surjective); its first and fourth maps are the first family of edge maps, CommAlgCat.torToCotangentEdge, its third is the second family, CommAlgCat.symmetricPowerToTorEdge_of_surjective, and its second is CommAlgCat.fiveTermConnecting_of_surjective. The covering set of this part is this declaration together with CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare_of_surjective, CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_torTwo_of_surjective and CommAlgCat.epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two_of_surjective, which state exactness at the other two interior terms and the final → 0. No spectral sequence is involved. The footnote vanishing H_j(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁿ) = 0 for j < n of the proof of Theorem 08RF, which the sequence needs, is a theorem here for every surjective A → B, so no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity is carried

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The five term exact sequence of Stacks Remark 08RG, exactness at `∧²_B(I/I²)`**, for a
surjective `A → B` and on no other hypothesis: the image of the middle map
`H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²)` is the kernel of the second edge map `∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare` with its hypothesis `hvan` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare_of_surjective
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A (B : Type u))) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (fiveTermConnecting_of_surjective A B hsurj)
      (symmetricPowerToTorEdge_of_surjective A B hsurj 2 (by norm_num))
      (fiveTermConnecting_comp_symmetricPowerToTorEdge A B
        (isZero_leftDerivedColim_smallPolynomialAugmentationIdealPow_of_surjective_unconditional
          A B hsurj))).Exact
declarations.comment: the five term exact sequence of low degree terms, Tor_3^A(B, B) → H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B) -- exactness at ∧²_B(I/I²), the term the remark writes ∧²_B(I/I²) and this development spells H_2(C_{B/A}, Sym²_{B̲}(Ω)), the two being the same object by the remark's second clause (CommAlgCat.exteriorPower_conormal_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPower_of_surjective). The sequence is the five term segment of the long exact sequence of 0 → 𝒦² → 𝒦 → 𝒦/𝒦² → 0 on C_{B/A} read through the remark's identifications H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) = Tor_i^A(B, B) for i ≥ 1 and H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦/𝒦²) = H^{-i}(L_{B/A}). The covering set of this part is this declaration together with CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree_of_surjective, CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_torTwo_of_surjective and CommAlgCat.epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two_of_surjective. The footnote vanishing H_j(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁿ) = 0 for j < n of the proof of Theorem 08RF, which the sequence needs, is a theorem here for every surjective A → B, so no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity is carried

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_torTwo_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The five term exact sequence of Stacks Remark 08RG, exactness at `Tor_2^A(B, B)`**, for a
surjective `A → B` and on no other hypothesis: the image of the second edge map
`∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B)` is the kernel of the first edge map
`Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A})`.

This is `CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_torTwo` with its hypothesis `hvan` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_fiveTerm_torTwo_of_surjective
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A (B : Type u))) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (symmetricPowerToTorEdge_of_surjective A B hsurj 2 (by norm_num))
      (torToCotangentEdge A B 2 (by norm_num))
      (symmetricPowerToTorEdge_comp_torToCotangentEdge A B
        (isZero_leftDerivedColim_smallPolynomialAugmentationIdealPow_of_surjective_unconditional
          A B hsurj))).Exact
declarations.comment: the five term exact sequence of low degree terms, Tor_3^A(B, B) → H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B) -- exactness at Tor_2^A(B, B), which is RingTheory.TorProducts.torBaseChange in degree 2, the second left derived functor of extension of scalars along A → B applied to B, in which this development identifies the abutment H_2(C_{B/A}, Ō) of Theorem 08RF. The sequence is the five term segment of the long exact sequence of 0 → 𝒦² → 𝒦 → 𝒦/𝒦² → 0 on C_{B/A} read through the remark's identifications H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦) = Tor_i^A(B, B) for i ≥ 1, H_i(C_{B/A}, 𝒦/𝒦²) = H^{-i}(L_{B/A}) and H_2(C_{B/A}, 𝒦²) = ∧²_B(I/I²). The covering set of this part is this declaration together with CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree_of_surjective, CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare_of_surjective and CommAlgCat.epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two_of_surjective. The footnote vanishing H_j(C_{B/A}, 𝒦ⁿ) = 0 for j < n of the proof of Theorem 08RF, which the sequence needs, is a theorem here for every surjective A → B, so no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity is carried

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The five term exact sequence of Stacks Remark 08RG ends in zero**, for a surjective
`A → B` and on no other hypothesis: the first edge map `Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A})` is
surjective.

This is `CommAlgCat.epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two` with its hypothesis `hvan`
discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_fiveTerm_torToCotangentEdge_two_of_surjective
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A (B : Type u))) :
    Epi (torToCotangentEdge A B 2 (by norm_num))
declarations.comment: the five term exact sequence of low degree terms, Tor_3^A(B, B) → H^{-3}(L_{B/A}) → ∧²_B(I/I²) → Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0, for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B) -- the final → 0, i.e. surjectivity of the last map Tor_2^A(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}), which is the first family of edge maps (CommAlgCat.torToCotangentEdge) in degree 2. It holds because H_1(C_{B/A}, 𝒦²) = 0, the footnote vanishing of the proof of Theorem 08RF at j = 1 < 2 = n, which is a theorem here for every surjective A → B; so no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity is carried. The covering set of this part is this declaration together with CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_cotangentNegThree_of_surjective, CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_exteriorSquare_of_surjective and CommAlgCat.exact_fiveTerm_torTwo_of_surjective, which state exactness at the sequence's three interior terms

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.leftDerivedColimOneConormalLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RG**, the opening clause `H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω) = I/I²` for a
surjective ring map `A → B` with kernel `I`, as an isomorphism of `B`-modules: the first
homology of `C_{B/A}` with coefficients in `Ω = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` is the conormal module `I/I²` of
the presentation of `B` by `A` itself.

The first equality is Tag 08PU in degree `n = 1`, at linear coefficients
(`CommAlgCat.leftDerivedColimPolynomialCotangentIso`); the second is Tag 08RA
(`CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_homologyNegOneIso`). The abelian-group form of the same clause is
`CommAlgCat.polynomialSiteHomologyOneConormalIso`, which reads `H_1` as the sections at the
point of `L₁π_!`.
declarations.statement:
def leftDerivedColimOneConormalLinearEquiv :
    ↥(((colim :
            ((smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))ᵒᵖ ⥤
              ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B).leftDerived 1).obj
        (smallPolynomialCotangentModulePresheaf A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))) ≃ₗ[B]
      (surjectionExtension.{u, u} A B h).Cotangent
declarations.comment: the opening clause H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω) = I/I² for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B), as an isomorphism of B-MODULES: the first left derived functor of the colimit over the opposite of the small model of the footnote-restricted site, applied to Ω = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲, is the conormal module I/I² of the presentation of B by A itself. H_1(C_{B/A}, -) = L_1 colim at linear coefficients is Tag 08PF's definition; the first equality is Tag 08PU in degree 1 and the second is Tag 08RA. I/I² is (CommAlgCat.surjectionExtension A B h).Cotangent, which CommAlgCat.surjectionConormalAddEquiv identifies with Ideal.Cotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)). No hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity of A → B

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exteriorPower_conormal_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPower_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RG**, the second clause `H_k(C_{B/A}, Sym^k(Ω)) = ∧^k_B(I/I²)`, which the remark
gets from Remark 08SG applied to `Ω`.

Let `A → B` be surjective with kernel `I` and let `Ω = Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 B̲` on `C_{B/A}`. Then the
`k`-th homology of `C_{B/A}` with coefficients in the `k`-th sectionwise symmetric power of `Ω`
is the `k`-th exterior power of `I/I²` over `B`, for every `k`.

The deduction is the remark's own: `Ω` is a flat `B̲`-module
(`CommAlgCat.flat_smallPolynomialCotangentModulePresheaf_obj`) with `H_0(C_{B/A}, Ω) = 0`
(`CommAlgCat.isZero_leftDerivedColimZero_polynomialCotangentModulePresheaf_of_surjective`) on a
site with a point resolution
(`CommAlgCat.isPointResolution_standardResolutionSmallCosimplicialObject`), so Remark 08SG
applies and gives `H_k(C_{B/A}, Sym^k(Ω)) = ∧^k_B(H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω))`; the remark's opening clause
`leftDerivedColimOneConormalLinearEquiv` then replaces `H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω)` by `I/I²`.

No hypothesis is placed on `B`; in particular `2` need not be invertible. Remark 08SG is used in
the form `Stacks.ChaoticSite.nonempty_linearEquiv_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPowerDiagram`, which
holds over every commutative ring by décalage, and not through 08SG's own sign-twisted
coinvariants step, which `Stacks.ChaoticSite.not_quillenSignedCoinvariants_int` refutes over
`ℤ`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_conormal_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPower_of_surjective (k : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (↥(((colim :
              ((smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B))ᵒᵖ ⥤
                ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B).leftDerived k).obj
            (Stacks.ChaoticSite.symmetricPowerDiagram
              (smallBoundedPolynomialSite A B (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) (B : Type u)
              (smallPolynomialCotangentModulePresheaf A B
                (standardResolutionVarCardinal A B)) k)) ≃ₗ[B]
        ⋀[(B : Type u)]^k (surjectionExtension.{u, u} A B h).Cotangent)
declarations.comment: the second clause H_k(C_{B/A}, Sym^k_{B̲}(Ω)) = ∧^k_B(I/I²) for a surjective A → B with I = ker(A → B), as an isomorphism of B-modules, for every k, over an arbitrary commutative ring B and with no hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity of A → B; in particular 2 need not be invertible. H_k(C_{B/A}, -) = L_k colim over the opposite of the small model of the footnote-restricted site at linear coefficients is Tag 08PF's definition of the homology of a category, Sym^k_{B̲} is the sectionwise symmetric power, which is the sheaf symmetric power because the topology of C_{B/A} is chaotic, and I/I² is (CommAlgCat.surjectionExtension A B h).Cotangent, the conormal module of the presentation of B by A itself, which CommAlgCat.surjectionConormalAddEquiv identifies with Ideal.Cotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)). The deduction is the remark's own: Remark 08SG applied to ℱ = Ω, which is a flat B̲-module with H_0(C_{B/A}, Ω) = 0 on a site with a point resolution, composed with the remark's opening clause H_1(C_{B/A}, Ω) = I/I². Remark 08SG enters in the form Stacks.ChaoticSite.nonempty_linearEquiv_leftDerivedColim_symmetricPowerDiagram, which holds over every commutative ring by Illusie's and Quillen's décalage; 08SG's own sign-twisted S_k-coinvariants step is a proof erratum, refuted over ℤ by Stacks.ChaoticSite.not_quillenSignedCoinvariants_int, and plays no role here

declarations.name: RingHom.torOneSelfIsoCotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RG**, the clause `Tor_1^A(B, B) = I/I²`: for a surjective ring map `f : A → B`
with kernel `I`, the first Tor of `B` with itself over `A` is the conormal module `I/I²`.

The route is the vanishing of `Tor_1^A(B, A)`, the long exact sequence of
`0 → I → A → B → 0` tensored with `B`, and the identification `B ⊗_A I = I/I²`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def torOneSelfIsoCotangent
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 1).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A B)).obj (ModuleCat.of A B) ≅
        ModuleCat.of A (RingHom.ker f).Cotangent
declarations.comment: the clause Tor_1^A(B, B) = I/I² for a surjective ring map f : A → B with I = ker f: the first Tor of B with itself over A is Ideal.Cotangent I, which is Mathlib's I/I². Tor is Mathlib's monoidal Tor on ModuleCat A, the left derived functor of the tensor product, so both sides are read as A-modules; each is annihilated by I and hence a B-module. The route is the vanishing of Tor_1^A(B, A), the long exact sequence of 0 → I → A → B → 0 tensored with B, and B ⊗_A I = I/I². No hypothesis beyond the remark's own surjectivity of A → B

declarations.name: exists_factorThrough_mappingCone
declarations.doc:
If the composite `f ≫ g` is null-homotopic then `g` factors
through the mapping cone of `f`, via the canonical inclusion `mappingCone.inr f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorThrough_mappingCone
    {K L M : CochainComplex C ℤ} (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M)
    (H : Homotopy (f ≫ g) 0) :
    ∃ gbar : mappingCone f ⟶ M, mappingCone.inr f ≫ gbar = g

declarations.name: exists_factor_through_shifted_mappingCone
declarations.doc:
If the composite `f ≫ g` is null-homotopic then `f` factors through the shifted mapping cone
`C(g)[-1]`, via the shifted projection `pShift g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factor_through_shifted_mappingCone
    {K L M : CochainComplex C ℤ} (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M)
    (H : Homotopy (f ≫ g) 0) :
    ∃ fbar : K ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (CochainComplex C ℤ) (-1 : ℤ)).obj (mappingCone g),
      fbar ≫ pShift g = f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.congruence_homotopic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RJ**.
Let `C` be any category. Being homotopic — the equivalence relation on morphisms of simplicial
objects of `C` generated by the existence of a simplicial homotopy — is a congruence: if `a` and
`a'` are homotopic then so are `b ∘ a` and `b ∘ a'` for any `b : V ⟶ W`, and so are `a ∘ c` and
`a' ∘ c` for any `c : X ⟶ U`. Hence `CategoryTheory.Quotient` of this relation is the source's
`hSimp(C)`, the category whose objects are the simplicial objects of `C` and whose morphisms are
the homotopy classes of morphisms of simplicial objects, and `CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor` is
the canonical functor `Simp(C) ⟶ hSimp(C)`, essentially surjective and surjective on sets of
morphisms.

declarations.name: Quasiregular.cotangent_finite_projective_of_quasiregular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08RK**.
If `I \subseteq R` is a quasi-regular ideal, then `I/I^2` is a finite projective `R/I`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangent_finite_projective_of_quasiregular
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsQuasiregularIdeal' I) :
    Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent ∧ Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.universalDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08RM.** Postcomposition with the universal
derivation gives the unique morphism from the module of relative
differentials to any coefficient sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleOfDifferentials
declarations.doc: The sheaf of relative differentials representing derivations along `φ`.
declarations.comment: the module of differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.universalDerivation
declarations.doc: The universal relative derivation into `moduleOfDifferentials φ`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.pullbackDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification between the inverse image of the module of relative
differentials and the module of relative differentials of the inverse-image morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackDifferentialsIso (phi : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDerivation
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of a relative derivation, specified by its action on the images of local
sections under the inverse-image units.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageDerivation
    {M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (underlyingRingSheaf O₂)}
    (d : SheafDerivation phi M) :
    {δ : SheafDerivation ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map phi)
        (inverseImageModule f O₂ M) //
      ∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (b : O₂.obj.obj U),
        δ.d (((inverseImageRingHom f O₂).hom.app U) b) =
          ((inverseImageModuleUnit f O₂ M).val.app U).hom (d.d b)}
declarations.comment: inverse image of the derivation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc: The inverse image of the universal derivation remains universal.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageDerivation_isUniversal (phi : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :
    IsUniversal (inverseImageDerivation f (universalDerivation phi)).val
declarations.comment: universality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.pullbackDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification between the inverse image of the module of relative
differentials and the module of relative differentials of the inverse-image morphism.
declarations.statement:

    inverseImageModule f O₂ (moduleOfDifferentials phi) ≅
      moduleOfDifferentials ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map phi)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.pullbackDifferentialsIso_compatible
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification carries the inverse image of the universal derivation to the
universal derivation.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDifferentialsIso_compatible (phi : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :
    (inverseImageDerivation f (universalDerivation phi)).val.postcomp
        (pullbackDifferentialsIso f phi).hom.val =
      universalDerivation ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map phi)
declarations.comment: compatibility with universal derivations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.pullbackDifferentialsIso_unique
declarations.doc:
Compatibility with universal derivations uniquely characterizes the canonical
identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDifferentialsIso_unique (phi : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    (e : inverseImageModule f O₂ (moduleOfDifferentials phi) ≅
      moduleOfDifferentials ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map phi))
    (he : (inverseImageDerivation f (universalDerivation phi)).val.postcomp e.hom.val =
      universalDerivation ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map phi)) :
    e = pullbackDifferentialsIso f phi
declarations.comment: canonicity

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DifferentialsFunctorial.compDeriv
declarations.doc:
Given a commutative square of sheaves of commutative rings
```
  O₂ --φ--> O₂'
  ↑ι        ↑ι'
  O₁ --ψ--> O₁'
```
and a relative `ι'`-derivation `d'` with values in a sheaf of `O₂'`-modules `F`, the
composite `d' ∘ φ` is a relative `ι`-derivation with values in `F` regarded as a sheaf of
`O₂`-modules by restriction of scalars along `φ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compDeriv {F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Differentials.underlyingRingSheaf O₂')}
    (d' : Differentials.SheafDerivation O₁' O₂' ι' F) (φ : O₂ ⟶ O₂') (ψ : O₁ ⟶ O₁')
    (hcomm : ι ≫ φ = ψ ≫ ι') :
    Differentials.SheafDerivation O₁ O₂ ι (restrictAlong φ F)
declarations.comment: the composite of O_2 -> O_2' with d is an O_1-derivation

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DifferentialsFunctorial.differentialMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism of sheaves of modules between the sheaves of relative
differentials attached to a commutative square
```
  O₂ --φ--> O₂'
  ↑ι        ↑ι'
  O₁ --ψ--> O₁'
```
of sheaves of commutative rings. It goes from `Ω_{O₂/O₁}` to `Ω_{O₂'/O₁'}` regarded as a
sheaf of `O₂`-modules by restriction of scalars along `φ`, and is characterized by
`differentialMap_comp_d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialMap (ι : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (ι' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (φ : O₂ ⟶ O₂')
    (ψ : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (hcomm : ι ≫ φ = ψ ≫ ι') :
    Differentials.moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ ι ⟶
      restrictAlong φ (Differentials.moduleOfDifferentials O₁' O₂' ι')
declarations.comment: the canonical map of O_2-modules Omega_{O_2/O_1} -> Omega_{O_2'/O_1'}

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DifferentialsFunctorial.differentialMap_comp_d
declarations.doc:
The characterizing property of `differentialMap`: on local sections it sends `d a` to
`d' (φ a)`, where `d` and `d'` are the universal derivations of `Ω_{O₂/O₁}` and
`Ω_{O₂'/O₁'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialMap_comp_d (ι : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (ι' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (φ : O₂ ⟶ O₂')
    (ψ : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (hcomm : ι ≫ φ = ψ ≫ ι') {U : Cᵒᵖ} (a : O₂.obj.obj U) :
    ((differentialMap ι ι' φ ψ hcomm).val.app U).hom
        ((Differentials.universalDerivation O₁ O₂ ι).d a)
      = (Differentials.universalDerivation O₁' O₂' ι').d ((φ.hom.app U).hom a)
declarations.comment: the characterizing property d(f) |-> d(phi f) on local sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DifferentialsFunctorial.differentialMap_unique
declarations.doc:
Uniqueness: a morphism of sheaves of modules satisfying the characterizing property of
`differentialMap` is `differentialMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialMap_unique (ι : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (ι' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (φ : O₂ ⟶ O₂')
    (ψ : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (hcomm : ι ≫ φ = ψ ≫ ι')
    (β : Differentials.moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ ι ⟶
      restrictAlong φ (Differentials.moduleOfDifferentials O₁' O₂' ι'))
    (hβ : ∀ {U : Cᵒᵖ} (a : O₂.obj.obj U), (β.val.app U).hom
        ((Differentials.universalDerivation O₁ O₂ ι).d a)
      = (Differentials.universalDerivation O₁' O₂' ι').d ((φ.hom.app U).hom a)) :
    β = differentialMap ι ι' φ ψ hcomm
declarations.comment: the canonical map is uniquely characterized by that property

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DifferentialsFunctorial.differentialsArrowFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08RS.** The relative differentials as a functor on the category of
arrows of sheaves of commutative rings: an arrow `ι : O₁ ⟶ O₂` is sent to `Ω_{O₂/O₁}` and a
commutative square to the canonical map `differentialMap`, the identity and composition laws
being `differentialMap_id` and `differentialMap_comp`.

The target is the total category `ArrowModules` rather than a fixed category of modules,
because the sheaf of rings over which `Ω_{O₂/O₁}` is linear is `O₂`, which varies with the
arrow.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialsArrowFunctor :
    CategoryTheory.Arrow (Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) ⥤ ArrowModules J
declarations.comment: a functor on the category of arrows of sheaves of rings

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceDifferentials.SDerivation
declarations.doc:
`Der_S(𝒪_X, F)`, the type of *`S`-derivations* of a morphism of ringed spaces
`h : X ⟶ S` with values in a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F`: a derivation of `𝒪_X` relative to
`h⁻¹ 𝒪_S`, that is, an `inverseImageStructureMap h`-derivation in the sense of Tag 01UN.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev SDerivation (h : X ⟶ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
declarations.comment: S-derivations into an O_X-module: the set Der_S(O_X, F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceDifferentials.moduleOfDifferentials
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{X/S}` of a morphism of ringed spaces `h : X ⟶ S`:
the sheaf of differentials of `𝒪_X` relative to `h⁻¹ 𝒪_S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleOfDifferentials (h : X ⟶ S) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)
declarations.comment: the sheaf of differentials Omega_{X/S} of X over S

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceDifferentials.universalDerivation
declarations.doc: The universal relative derivation `d_{X/S} : 𝒪_X ⟶ Ω_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def universalDerivation (h : X ⟶ S) :
    SDerivation h (moduleOfDifferentials h)
declarations.comment: the universal S-derivation d_{X/S} with which Omega_{X/S} is endowed

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceDifferentials.differentialMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison map `c : f^* Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}` of sheaves of `𝒪_{X'}`-modules
attached to a commutative diagram of morphisms of ringed spaces
```
  X' --f--> X
  |         |
  h'        h
  v         v
  S' --g--> S
```
It is the morphism adjoint to `pushforwardDifferentialMap`, and
`differentialMap_isDifferentialMap` together with `differentialMap_unique` say that it is
the unique morphism carrying the pullback of `d a` to `d (f^♯ a)` on local sections.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialMap :
    (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj (moduleOfDifferentials h) ⟶
      moduleOfDifferentials h'
declarations.comment: the canonical map c_f : f^*Omega_{X/S} -> Omega_{X'/S'}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.existsUnique_compositeDerivation
declarations.doc:
The composite of `f^♯` with the pushforward of the universal derivation is an
`S`-derivation, and it is the unique one whose value on every local section `a` is the
universal derivation of `f^♯ a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_compositeDerivation {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    ∃! D : SheafDerivation (inverseImageStructureMap h)
      ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).obj
        (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h'))),
      ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (a : X.presheaf.obj (.op U)),
        D.d a = (universalDerivation
          (inverseImageStructureMap h')).d ((f.hom.c.app (.op U)).hom a)
declarations.comment: composite derivation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.pushforwardDifferentialMap
declarations.doc: The universal map `Ω_{X/S} ⟶ f_* Ω_{X'/S'}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardDifferentialMap {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h) ⟶
      (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).obj
        (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h'))
declarations.comment: map to pushforward differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.existsUnique_differentialMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism of differentials for a commutative square of ringed spaces exists
and is uniquely determined by its action on differentials of local sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_differentialMap {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    ∃! c : (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj
        (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h)) ⟶
      moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h'),
      IsDifferentialMap f h h' c
declarations.comment: canonical map and uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialMap_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The pullback map on differentials is adjoint to the canonical map into
pushforward differentials.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialMap_adjoint {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homEquiv f
      (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h'))
      (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h)))
        (differentialMap f h h' g hcomm) =
      pushforwardDifferentialMap f h h' g hcomm
declarations.comment: agreement under adjunction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDifferentialMapOfFunctoriality
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08RU, the map `f⁻¹Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}` built from Tags 08RR and 08RS.** For a
commutative square of ringed spaces
```
  X' --f--> X
  |h'       |h
  v         v
  S' --g--> S
```
this is the identification `f⁻¹Ω_{X/S} ≅ Ω_{f⁻¹𝒪_X/f⁻¹h⁻¹𝒪_S}` of Tag 08RR
(`pullbackDifferentialsIso`), followed by the map of Tag 08RS
(`inverseImageRingsDifferentialMap`) for the square of sheaves of rings
`f⁻¹h⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ h'⁻¹𝒪_{S'}`, `f⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_{X'}`. It is a map of `f⁻¹𝒪_X`-modules, the target
carrying its scalars restricted along `f⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_{X'}`, and it is constructed without
reference to the canonical map `c_f = differentialMap`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageDifferentialMapOfFunctoriality {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    inverseImageModule f.hom.base X.sheaf
      (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h)) ⟶
        inverseImageDifferentialTarget f h'
declarations.comment: the map f^{-1}Omega_{X/S} -> Omega_{X'/S'} from 08RR and 08RS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageToPullback_comp_differentialMap
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08RU, agreement of the inverse-image map with `c_f`.** Under the identification
`f^*Ω_{X/S} = f⁻¹Ω_{X/S} ⊗ 𝒪_{X'}`, the canonical map `c_f = differentialMap` corresponds to
the map `f⁻¹Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}` built from Tags 08RR and 08RS: the composite
`f⁻¹Ω_{X/S} ⟶ f^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}` of the tensor-unit map with `c_f` is
`inverseImageDifferentialMapOfFunctoriality`. The proof is by the universal property of
`f⁻¹Ω_{X/S}`: both maps send the inverse image of `d a` to `d (f^♯ a)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageToPullback_comp_differentialMap {X' X S' S : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ S) (h' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (hcomm : f ≫ h = h' ≫ g) :
    inverseImageToPullback f (moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageStructureMap h)) ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (inverseImageStructureRingMap f)).map
          (differentialMap f h h' g hcomm) =
      inverseImageDifferentialMapOfFunctoriality f h h' g hcomm
declarations.comment: agreement of the 08RR/08RS map with c_f under f^*Omega = f^{-1}Omega ⊗ O_{X'}

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.isIso_leftDerivedColimit_map_extensionByZero
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a small category with the chaotic topology,
let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C` which is a point resolution, and let `a : 𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪'` be a
morphism of abelian presheaves such that `L_nπ_!(a)` is invertible. Then for every object `W` of
`C` the induced morphism `j_{W!}𝒪_W ⟶ j_{W!}𝒪'_W` of extensions by zero is also inverted by
`L_nπ_!`.

Evaluated on `U_•` the two extensions by zero are the products of the simplicial set
`Mor_C(U_•, W)` with the simplicial abelian groups `𝒪(U_•)` and `𝒪'(U_•)`, and `Mor_C(U_•, W)` is
homotopy equivalent to a singleton; so the projections to `𝒪(U_•)` and `𝒪'(U_•)` are inverted by
the homology of the Moore complex, which reduces the claim to the hypothesis on `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_leftDerivedColimit_map_extensionByZero (hU : IsPointResolution U)
    {P P' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}} (a : P ⟶ P') (W : C) (n : ℕ)
    (ha : IsIso (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n).map a)) :
    IsIso (((colim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).leftDerived n).map
      (extensionByZeroPresheafMap a W))
declarations.comment: the generators `j_{U!}O_U`; see the scope paragraph in the module docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**Tag 08RX.** Let `C` be a small category with the chaotic topology and let `a : 𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪'` be a
morphism of presheaves of rings on `C` (on a chaotic site, of sheaves of rings). Assume

1. there is a cosimplicial object `U_•` of `C` as in Tag 08Q9, i.e. a point resolution: every
   `Mor_C(U_•, W)` is homotopy equivalent to the constant simplicial set on a singleton, and
2. `Lπ_!(𝒪) ⟶ Lπ_!(𝒪')` is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)`, where `Lπ_!` is derived lower shriek of
   abelian sheaves applied to the underlying morphism of abelian presheaves placed in degree zero.

Then for **every** object `K` of the unbounded derived category `D(𝒪) = D(Mod(𝒪))` the canonical
comparison

`Lπ_!(K) ⟶ Lπ_!(K ⊗^L_𝒪 𝒪')`

of `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitTensorComparison` (induced by `K ⟶ K ⊗^L_𝒪 𝒪'`) is an
isomorphism in `D(Ab)`.

The comparison is `Lπ_!` applied to the unit of the derived change-of-coefficients adjunction,
followed by the identification `Stacks.ChaoticSite.restrictScalarsDerivedColimitIso` of `Lπ_!` on
`𝒪'`-modules with `Lπ_!` on their underlying `𝒪`-modules
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_app_iff`); so the assertion is the
invertibility of the whiskered unit, which is a morphism of exact direct-sum-preserving functors
on `D(Mod(𝒪))` compatible with the shift. The free presheaves of modules on the representables —
the generators `j_{W!}𝒪_W` of the source's proof — are projective, separating and compact, so the
dévissage along compact generators of
`StacksDraft.CompactDevissage.isIso_of_isIso_app_single_anyModel` reduces the assertion to those
generators placed in degree zero, where it is
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_app_single`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedColimitTensorComparison_app (hU : IsPointResolution U)
    (ha : IsIso ((totalDerivedColimit C AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) 0).map
        (Functor.whiskerRight a (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})))))
    (K : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{u} O)) :
    IsIso ((derivedColimitTensorComparison a).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacement
declarations.doc: The functorial cosimplicial cochain replacement of an abelian presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cochainReplacement
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] :
    {K : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) ⥤ CosimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} //
      IsCochainReplacement C K}
declarations.comment: the cochain replacement

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementComplex_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc: The cochain replacement preserves finite limits, degree by degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementComplex_preservesFiniteLimits
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (cochainReplacementComplex C)
declarations.comment: left exactness of the replacement

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementComplex_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc: The cochain replacement preserves finite colimits, degree by degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementComplex_preservesFiniteColimits
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (cochainReplacementComplex C)
declarations.comment: right exactness of the replacement

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementDeltaFunctor
declarations.doc:
The homology functors of the replacement, with their natural connecting
morphisms, form a cohomological delta functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cochainReplacementDeltaFunctor
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] :
    {D : DeltaFunctor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} //
      ∀ n, D.functor n = cochainReplacementComplex C ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n}
declarations.comment: cohomological delta functor

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementZeroHomologyIsoLimit
declarations.doc:
The zeroth cohomology of the replacement is naturally the limit of the
presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementZeroHomologyIsoLimit
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] :
    Nonempty
      (cochainReplacementComplex C ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 ≅
        (lim : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}))
declarations.comment: degree-zero cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.pointSimplicialReplacement_contractible
declarations.doc:
The simplicial set of chains `U₀ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Uₙ` equipped with a map
`U ⟶ U₀` is the nerve of the under-category of `U`, and is simplicially
homotopy equivalent to a point.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSimplicialReplacement_contractible
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] (U : C) :
    ∃ f : nerve (Under U) ⟶ ⊤_ SSet.{u},
      SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type u) f
declarations.comment: contractibility of the point simplicial replacement

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementPointIsoNerve
declarations.doc:
The degree-`n` replacement of the point-pushforward of `A` is the group
of maps from the `n`-simplices of the nerve of `Under U` to `A`. These
identifications intertwine every coface with precomposition by the
corresponding simplicial face, hence identify the cochain complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementPointIsoNerve
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] (U : C) (A : AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) :
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (((cochainReplacement C).1.obj
          ((sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
            ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot U).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj A))).obj (.mk n)) ≅
          AddCommGrpCat.of (ComposableArrows (Under U) n → A),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (x : ComposableArrows (Under U) (n + 1))
          (s : ((cochainReplacement C).1.obj
            ((sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
              ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot U).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj A))).obj (.mk n)),
        ((e (n + 1)).hom
          (((cochainReplacement C).1.obj
            ((sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
              ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot U).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj A))).δ i s)) x =
          ((e n).hom s) ((nerve (Under U)).δ i x)
declarations.comment: point-pushforward replacement as maps from the nerve

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementPointAcyclic
declarations.doc:
Pushforward from a point of the chaotic site is acyclic for the cochain
replacement in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementPointAcyclic
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] (U : C) (A : AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n).obj
      ((cochainReplacementComplex C).obj
        ((sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
          ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot U).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj A))))
declarations.comment: point-pushforward acyclicity

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementPointProductAcyclic
declarations.doc: A product of pushforwards from points is acyclic in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementPointProductAcyclic
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] (I : Type u)
    (U : I → C) (A : I → AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n).obj
      ((cochainReplacementComplex C).obj
        (∏ᶜ fun i : I ↦
          (sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
            ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot (U i)).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj (A i)))))
declarations.comment: product acyclicity

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.presheafEmbedsInPointProduct
declarations.doc: Every abelian presheaf embeds in a product of point-pushforwards.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafEmbedsInPointProduct
    (C : Type u) [SmallCategory C] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (A : I → AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}),
      ∃ f : F ⟶
        (∏ᶜ fun i : I ↦
          (sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).functor.obj
            ((GrothendieckTopology.pointBot (U i)).skyscraperSheafFunctor.obj (A i))),
        Mono f
declarations.comment: embedding into a product of point pushforwards

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryCohomology.cochainReplacementHomologyIsoSiteCohomology
declarations.doc:
The cohomology of the cochain replacement computes the right-derived
functors of global sections on the chaotic site.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainReplacementHomologyIsoSiteCohomology
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (cochainReplacementComplex.{u, u} C ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n ≅
        (sheafBotEquivalence (C := C) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).inverse ⋙
          Stacks.Cohomology.CompositeRightDerived.siteCohomology
            (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) n)
declarations.comment: right-derived global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extCochainComplexBifunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S0.** The cochain complex computing homomorphisms of `O`-modules, as a bifunctor
contravariant in the source module and covariant in the target module.
declarations.comment: the cochain bifunctor

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extCochainComplex_d_apply
declarations.doc: The differential of `K^•(G, F)` is the alternating sum of the coface maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma extCochainComplex_d_apply (n : ℕ) (φ : extCochain G F n)
    (x : ComposableArrows C (n + 1)) (s : G.obj (op (x.obj (Fin.last (n + 1))))) :
    (extCochainComplex G F).d n (n + 1) φ x s =
      ∑ i : Fin (n + 2), ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ)) •
        (extCochainSimplexMap G F (SimplexCategory.δ i) φ x s)
declarations.comment: the alternating differential

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extCochainComplex_d_zero_apply
declarations.doc:
The degree-zero differential of `K^•(G, F)`: on an arrow `U₀ ⟶ U₁` it is
`ρ^{U₁}_{U₀} ∘ φ_{U₁} - φ_{U₀} ∘ ρ^{U₁}_{U₀}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma extCochainComplex_d_zero_apply (φ : extCochain G F 0) (x : ComposableArrows C 1)
    (s : G.obj (op (x.obj (Fin.last 1)))) (p q : F.obj (op (x.obj 0)))
    (hp : p = F.restrictₛₗ (stringSpine x).op (φ ((nerve C).δ 0 x) s))
    (hq : q = φ ((nerve C).δ 1 x) (G.restrictₛₗ (stringSpine x).op s)) :
    (extCochainComplex G F).d 0 1 φ x s = p - q
declarations.comment: the degree-zero differential

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extCochainComplex_d_one_apply
declarations.doc:
The degree-one differential of `K^•(G, F)`: on a string `U₀ ⟶ U₁ ⟶ U₂` it is
`φ_{U₀ → U₁} ∘ ρ^{U₂}_{U₁} - φ_{U₀ → U₂} + ρ^{U₁}_{U₀} ∘ φ_{U₁ → U₂}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma extCochainComplex_d_one_apply (φ : extCochain G F 1) (x : ComposableArrows C 2)
    (s : G.obj (op (x.obj (Fin.last 2)))) (p q r : F.obj (op (x.obj 0)))
    (hp : p = φ ((nerve C).δ 2 x) (G.restrictₛₗ (x.map' 1 2).op s))
    (hq : q = φ ((nerve C).δ 1 x) s)
    (hr : r = F.restrictₛₗ (x.map' 0 1).op (φ ((nerve C).δ 0 x) s)) :
    (extCochainComplex G F).d 1 2 φ x s = p - q + r
declarations.comment: the degree-one differential

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extCochainComplexHomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S0.** The degree-zero cohomology of `K^•(G, F)` is the group of homomorphisms
of `O`-modules from `G` to `F`.
declarations.statement:
def extCochainComplexHomologyZeroIso (G F : PresheafOfModules.{m} O) :
    (extCochainComplex G F).homology 0 ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of (G ⟶ F)
declarations.comment: degree-zero cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.shortExact_extCochainComplexShortComplexRight
declarations.doc:
Exactness in the second variable: if `G` is projective at every object, the
cochain complex carries a short exact sequence of targets to a short exact sequence of
complexes.
declarations.statement:
lemma shortExact_extCochainComplexShortComplexRight
    (hG : ∀ U : C, Projective (G.obj (op U))) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (extCochainComplexShortComplexRight G S).ShortExact
declarations.comment: exactness in the second variable

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.shortExact_extCochainComplexShortComplexLeft
declarations.doc:
Exactness in the first variable: if the target stays injective after
restriction of scalars along every arrow, the cochain complex carries a short exact sequence of
sources to a short exact sequence of complexes.
declarations.statement:
lemma shortExact_extCochainComplexShortComplexLeft
    (hF : ∀ {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V),
      Injective ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (O.map f.op).hom).obj (F.obj (op U))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (extCochainComplexShortComplexLeft F S).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
exactness in the first variable, when F(U) is injective over O(V) for every
arrow U ⟶ V

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extAddEquivCohomology_of_objectwiseProjective
declarations.doc:
Case (1): if the first module is projective at every object, the cochain
complex computes all its `Ext` groups: `Ext^n_O(G, F) ≅ H^n(K^•(G, F))` for every `n`.
declarations.comment: objectwise-projective case, every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.extAddEquivCohomology_of_arrowwiseInjective
declarations.doc:
Case (2): if each section of the second module remains injective after
restriction of scalars along every arrow, the cochain complex computes all `Ext` groups into it:
`Ext^n_O(G, F) ≅ H^n(K^•(G, F))` for every `n`.

Injectivity of each `F(U)` over `O(U)` alone does not suffice:
`Stacks.CategoryExt.ArrowCounterexample.injective_obj_and_not_nonempty_extAddEquiv_two` is a
counterexample in degree two.
declarations.statement:
def extAddEquivCohomology_of_arrowwiseInjective (G F : PresheafOfModules.{max u v m} O)
    (hF : ∀ {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V),
      Injective ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (O.map f.op).hom).obj (F.obj (op U))))
    (n : ℕ) :
    Abelian.zExt G F (n : ℤ) ≃+ (extCochainComplex G F).homology n

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.ArrowCounterexample.injective_obj_and_not_nonempty_extAddEquiv_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S0**, the counterexample to case (2) with objectwise injectivity. On the category
`false ⟶ true` with `O(true) = ℤ`, `O(false) = ℤ/2`, the module `F = target` has
`F(true) = 0` and `F(false) = ℤ/2`, so each `F(U)` is an injective `O(U)`-module; yet for
`G = source`, with `G(true) = ℤ/2` and `G(false) = 0`, the groups `Ext²_O(G, F)` and
`H²(K^•(G, F))` are not isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_obj_and_not_nonempty_extAddEquiv_two :
    (∀ U : Bool, Injective (target.obj (op U))) ∧
      ¬ Nonempty (Abelian.zExt source target ((2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≃+
        (extCochainComplex source target).homology 2)
declarations.comment: the counterexample: objectwise injectivity of F does not suffice in case (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.isLimitExtCochainComplexFanOfDirectSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S0.** The cochain bifunctor transforms direct sums in the first variable into
products: if the cofan `c` exhibits its point as the direct sum of a family `Gι` of `O`-modules,
then the maps which the bifunctor induces from the inclusions `Gι i ⟶ c.pt` exhibit
`K^•(c.pt, F)` as the product of the complexes `K^•(Gι i, F)`.
declarations.statement:
def isLimitExtCochainComplexFanOfDirectSum {ι : Type t} [Small.{m} ι]
    {Gι : ι → PresheafOfModules.{m} O} (c : Cofan Gι) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m} O) :
    IsLimit (Fan.mk (f := fun i ↦ extCochainComplex (Gι i) F) (extCochainComplex c.pt F)
      (fun i ↦ (extCochainComplexBifunctor C O).map ((c.inj i).op, 𝟙 F)))
declarations.comment: direct sums in the first variable become products

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryExt.isLimitExtCochainComplexFanOfProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S0.** The cochain bifunctor commutes with products in the second variable: if the
fan `c` exhibits its point as the product of a family `Fι` of `O`-modules, then the maps which
the bifunctor induces from the projections `c.pt ⟶ Fι i` exhibit `K^•(G, c.pt)` as the product of
the complexes `K^•(G, Fι i)`.
declarations.statement:
def isLimitExtCochainComplexFanOfProduct {ι : Type t} [Small.{m} ι]
    (G : PresheafOfModules.{m} O) {Fι : ι → PresheafOfModules.{m} O}
    (c : Fan Fι) (hc : IsLimit c) :
    IsLimit (Fan.mk (f := fun i ↦ extCochainComplex G (Fι i)) (extCochainComplex G c.pt)
      (fun i ↦ (extCochainComplexBifunctor C O).map (𝟙 (op G), c.proj i)))
declarations.comment: products in the second variable

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag08S2Assembly.relativeDifferentialsIsoDiagonalConormal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08S2].** The canonical isomorphism from the sheaf of relative differentials
of `X` over `S` to the conormal sheaf of its diagonal in `X ×_S X`.

This is `Stacks.LeibnizDerivation.diagonalConormalIso`, whose single hypothesis
`IsIso (Stacks.LeibnizDerivation.toConormal f)` is now discharged by `isIso_toConormal` and so
is carried by no argument here: `f` is an arbitrary morphism of schemes, and nothing is affine,
separated, Noetherian or quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeDifferentialsIsoDiagonalConormal :
    Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f ≅
      Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag08S2Assembly.relativeDifferentialsIsoDiagonalConormal_apply
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08S2], the canonical quotient formula.** The comparison isomorphism sends
`d b` to the image of `p₂^♯ b - p₁^♯ b` under the canonical quotient map from the ideal sheaf of
the diagonal to its conormal sheaf, on any open `V` of the coborder neighbourhood admitting the
tag's two containments.

This is `Stacks.LeibnizDerivation.diagonalConormalIso_hom_d_eq_quotientMap`, again with its
hypothesis discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDifferentialsIsoDiagonalConormal_apply
    (V : (pullback.diagonal f).coborderRange.toScheme.Opens)
    (h₁ : (pullback.diagonal f).coborderRange.ι ''ᵁ V ≤
      (pullback.fst f f) ⁻¹ᵁ ((pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    (h₂ : (pullback.diagonal f).coborderRange.ι ''ᵁ V ≤
      (pullback.snd f f) ⁻¹ᵁ ((pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    (b : Γ(X, (pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    (x : (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
      (pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom).val.obj (.op V))
    (hx : (kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit (structureSheafHom
        (pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom))).val.app (.op V) x =
      ((pullback.snd f f).appLE _ _ h₂).hom b - ((pullback.fst f f).appLE _ _ h₁).hom b) :
    ((relativeDifferentialsIsoDiagonalConormal f).hom.val.app
          (.op ((pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder ⁻¹ᵁ V))).hom
        ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d b) =
      (Stacks.Conormal.conormalQuotientMap (pullback.diagonal f)
        (pullback.diagonal f).coborderRange (pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder
        (pullback.diagonal f).liftCoborder_ι).val.app (.op V) x
declarations.comment: canonical quotient formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension
declarations.doc:
A solution of a square-zero extension problem.

The map `toB` and its kernel give the exact upper row
`0 → N → B' → B → 0`; `kernelEquiv` supplies the displayed identification
with `N`, and `map_I` says that the left square is the prescribed map `c`.
declarations.statement: public structure CompatibleExtension (S : SquareZeroExtensionProblem)

declarations.name: Deformation.RingThickening.fittingMap_addTorsor_kaehlerDifferentialHom
declarations.doc:
If a map filling a compatible square-zero deformation diagram exists, all such maps
form a principal homogeneous space under `Hom_{B₁}(Ω_{B₁/A₁}, N₂)`. Subtracting
two fitting maps gives the unique differential map whose value on `d b` is the
difference of their values on any lift of `b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingMap_addTorsor_kaehlerDifferentialHom
    (D : CompatibleSquareZeroDeformationDiagram.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄,
      v₁, v₂, v₃, v₄, w₁, w₂})
    (h : Nonempty D.FittingMap) :
    Nonempty
      {t : AddTorsor
          (KaehlerDifferential D.S₁.A D.S₁.B →ₗ[D.S₁.B] D.S₂.N)
          D.FittingMap //
        letI : AddTorsor
            (KaehlerDifferential D.S₁.A D.S₁.B →ₗ[D.S₁.B] D.S₂.N)
            D.FittingMap := t
        ∀ (φ ψ : D.FittingMap) (b' : D.X₁.B'),
          ((D.X₂.kernelEquiv
            ((φ -ᵥ ψ) (KaehlerDifferential.D D.S₁.A D.S₁.B (D.X₁.toB b'))) :
              RingHom.ker D.X₂.toB.toRingHom) : D.X₂.B') =
            φ.toRingHom b' - ψ.toRingHom b'}
declarations.comment: torsor

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.obstructionClass
declarations.doc:
The canonical obstruction to filling a compatible square-zero deformation diagram.

Its value lies in `Ext¹_{B₁}(NL_{B₁/A₁}, N₂)`.  The subtype records the characteristic
property of the obstruction: it is zero precisely when a fitting map `B'₁ → B'₂` exists.
declarations.statement:
public def obstructionClass
    (D : CompatibleSquareZeroDeformationDiagram.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄,
      v₁, v₂, v₃, v₄, w₁, w₂}) :
    let K := ((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{v₄} D.S₁.B).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj (Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex D.S₁.A D.S₁.B)
    {o : DerivedCategory.Ext
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (HomologicalComplex.double (K.d 1 0)
            (show (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel (-1) 0 from rfl)))
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u₂ u₃ v₄} D.S₁.B) 0).obj
          ((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max u₂ u₃} D.S₁.B).obj
            (ModuleCat.of D.S₁.B D.S₂.N))) 1 //
      o = 0 ↔ Nonempty D.FittingMap}
declarations.comment: obstruction

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.nonempty_compatibleExtension_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08S6.**  If `A → B` is a local complete intersection ring map, then every
square-zero extension problem over `A' → A` with target `B` and prescribed kernel map
`c : I → N` has a solution.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_compatibleExtension_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    (S : SquareZeroExtensionProblem.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    (h : (algebraMap S.A S.B).IsLocalCompleteIntersection) :
    Nonempty (S.CompatibleExtension.{max u₁ (max u₂ (max u₃ u₄))})

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.isomorphismClassesTorsor
declarations.doc:
If a square-zero extension problem has a solution, this is the canonical principal
homogeneous-space structure on its isomorphism classes under `Ext¹_B(NL_{B/A}, N)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def isomorphismClassesTorsor
    (S : SquareZeroExtensionProblem.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    (h : Nonempty (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.{v} S)) :
    AddTorsor (naiveCotangentExtOne S.A S.B S.N)
      (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄, v}
        S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.isomorphismClasses_vsub_eq_obstructionClass
declarations.doc:
In the canonical torsor of solutions, the difference `[Y] -ᵥ [X]` is the obstruction
class `o(X, Y)` to a map from `X` to `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isomorphismClasses_vsub_eq_obstructionClass
    (S : SquareZeroExtensionProblem.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    (h : Nonempty (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.{v} S))
    (X Y : S.CompatibleExtension.{v}) :
    (@VSub.vsub
      (naiveCotangentExtOne S.A S.B S.N)
      (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses S)
      (isomorphismClassesTorsor S h).toVSub
      (Quotient.mk
          (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid S) Y :
          SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses S)
      (Quotient.mk
          (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid S) X :
          SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses S) =
      (obstructionClass (comparisonDiagram X Y)).1)
declarations.comment: canonical difference

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isDirectedColimitOfTypes_cotangentComplexAb
declarations.doc:
Let `A i → B i` be a system of ring maps over a directed index set `I`, with `Ainf` the
colimit of the `A i` and `Binf` the colimit of the `B i`. Then in every degree the canonical
maps induced by the comparison squares exhibit `L_{Binf⁄Ainf}` as the directed colimit of the
cotangent complexes `L_{B i⁄A i}`, the transition maps of the system being those induced by
the squares of the system; that is, `colim L_{B i⁄A i} = L_{colim B i⁄colim A i}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem CommAlgCat.isDirectedColimitOfTypes_cotangentComplexAb
    (hA : IsDirectedColimitOfTypes (fun _ _ h a => (sq h).base a)
      (fun i a => (cocone i).base a))
    (hB : IsDirectedColimitOfTypes (fun _ _ h b => (sq h).map b)
      (fun i b => (cocone i).map b))
    (n : ℤ) :
    IsDirectedColimitOfTypes
      (fun _ _ h a => (CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexAbMap (sq h)).f n a)
      (fun i a => (CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexAbMap (cocone i)).f n a)
declarations.comment: degreewise

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isColimit_cotangentComplexAbCocone
declarations.doc:
Cotangent complexes commute with directed colimits of ring maps: the cocone of canonical
maps `L_{B i⁄A i} → L_{Binf⁄Ainf}` on the system of canonical maps `L_{B i⁄A i} → L_{B j⁄A j}`
is a colimit cocone.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def CommAlgCat.isColimit_cotangentComplexAbCocone :
    IsColimit (CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexAbCocone sq cocone hA hB)
declarations.comment: the colimit of complexes

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_distTriang_derivedExtensionScalars_cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08SA.** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps. If `B` is a polynomial algebra
over `A`, then there is a distinguished triangle

`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C)[1]`

in `D(C)`. This is the lemma as stated.

The proof is the source's. The standard resolution `P_•` of `C` over `B` is, read over `A`, also
a resolution of `C` over `A` (`CommAlgCat.standardResolution_isResolution_restrictScalars`); the
differentials of the tower `A → B → Pₙ` form a split short exact sequence because `Pₙ` is a
polynomial algebra over `B`, and base changing it to `C` gives a short exact sequence of
complexes of `C`-modules
`Ω[B⁄A] ⊗[B] C → Ω[P_•⁄A] ⊗[P_•] C → Ω[P_•⁄B] ⊗[P_•] C`
(`CommAlgCat.restrictedCotangentComplexShortComplex_shortExact`) whose distinguished triangle is
the one asserted. Its last term is `L_{C/B}` by definition; its first term is `Ω[B⁄A] ⊗[B] C` in
degree `0`, which is `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B C` by Tag 08QH and the projectivity of `Ω[B⁄A]`
(`CommAlgCat.nonempty_derivedExtensionScalars_cotangentComplex_iso_of_isPolynomialAlgebra`); and
its middle term is `L_{C/A}` because `P_•` and the standard resolution of `C` over `A` are two
resolutions of `C` over `A`, so by Tag 08PU both compute derived lower shriek of `i^*Ω_{𝒪/A}` on
the site `C_{C/A}`
(`CommAlgCat.nonempty_q_restrictedCotangentComplex_iso_cotangentComplex`).

The triangle is stated existentially, as in the source: the identifications of the first and
middle terms are isomorphisms of objects of `D(C)`, which transport a distinguished triangle to
one with the named objects. The three rings are taken in one universe, which is no restriction:
three rings with maps between them always live in a common universe. The conditional form at two
universes, with the identification of the middle term as a hypothesis, is
`CommAlgCat.exists_distTriang_derivedExtensionScalars_of_isPolynomialAlgebra`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_distTriang_derivedExtensionScalars_cotangentComplex
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hB : Algebra.IsPolynomialAlgebra A B) :
    ∃ (f : (CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral
            (algebraMap B C)).functor.obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} A B)) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} A C))
      (g : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} A C) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} B C))
      (h : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} B C) ⟶
        ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral
            (algebraMap B C)).functor.obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexOfAlgebra.{u, u} A B)))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk f g h ∈
        Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles (C := DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} C))

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_homotopy_squareCotangentComplexMap_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08SB.** Let `A → A'`, `B → B'` be a commutative square of ring maps
compatible with the algebra structures `A → B` and `A' → B'`. If there is a ring map
`κ : B → A'` which agrees with `A → A'` on the image of `A` and which recovers `B → B'` after
`A' → B'`, then the induced map of cotangent complexes `L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'}` is homotopic to
zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_homotopy_squareCotangentComplexMap_zero
    (sq : AlgebraSquare.{u, v, u} A A' B B') (κ : B →+* A')
    (hκ : ∀ a : A, κ (algebraMap A B a) = sq.base a)
    (hκ' : ∀ b : B, algebraMap A' B' (κ b) = sq.map b) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy (squareCotangentComplexMap.{u, v, u} sq) 0)
declarations.comment: the conclusion of the remark: the induced map on cotangent complexes is homotopic to zero. The claim of the remark itself, that the functoriality map of standard resolutions is homotopic to the composition through `κ`, is `CommAlgCat.eqvGen_homotopy_squareResolutionRingMap_baseMap` of `StacksFrontier.Cotangent.SquareResolutionBaseHomotopy`; the proof here does not pass through it, factoring the square through the identity of `A'` instead.

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentTermDifferential_squareResolutionRingBaseMap
declarations.doc:
The composition `P_• → B → A' → P'_•` lands in the image of `A'`, so it kills differentials:
the pure differential `1 ⊗ d` of each of its values vanishes. This is the step by which the
source passes from the homotopy below to the vanishing, up to homotopy, of the induced map on
cotangent complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cotangentTermDifferential_squareResolutionRingBaseMap
    (κ : B →+* A') (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ)
    (p : (standardResolution.{u, max u v} A B).left.obj n) :
    cotangentTermDifferential.{u, max u v} A' B' n
      ((squareResolutionRingBaseMap.{u, v} (B' := B') κ).app n p) = 0
declarations.comment: the remark's observation that the composition through `κ` induces the zero map on differentials, read degreewise on the pure differentials `1 ⊗ d p` which generate the terms of the cotangent complex.

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.eqvGen_homotopy_squareResolutionRingMap_baseMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08SB.** Let `A → A'`, `B → B'` be a commutative square of ring maps
compatible with the algebra structures `A → B` and `A' → B'`, and let `κ : B → A'` be a ring map
which agrees with `A → A'` on the image of `A` and which recovers `B → B'` after `A' → B'`. Then
the functoriality map `P_• → P'_•` of the two standard resolutions is homotopic, as a map of
simplicial commutative rings, to the composition `P_• → B → A' → P'_•`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eqvGen_homotopy_squareResolutionRingMap_baseMap
    (sq : AlgebraSquare.{u, v, u} A A' B B') (κ : B →+* A')
    (hκ : ∀ a : A, κ (algebraMap A B a) = sq.base a)
    (hκ' : ∀ b : B, algebraMap A' B' (κ b) = sq.map b) :
    Relation.EqvGen
      (fun f g : resolutionRing.{u, v} A B ⟶ resolutionRing.{u, v} A' B' =>
        Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy f g))
      (squareResolutionRingMap.{u, v} sq) (squareResolutionRingBaseMap.{u, v} (B' := B') κ)
declarations.comment: the claim of the remark: the functoriality map of standard resolutions is homotopic to the composition through `κ`. The consequence drawn from it, that the induced map of cotangent complexes is homotopic to zero, is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_homotopy_squareCotangentComplexMap_zero`.

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexProductMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 08SC].** For ring maps `A → B` and `A → C`, the pair of
the functoriality maps of the two projections `B × C → B` and `B × C → C` is a map of complexes of
`B × C`-modules

`L_{B×C/A} → L_{B/A} ⊕ L_{C/A}`,

the two summands being read over `B × C` along the projections. Tag 08SC asserts that
`DerivedCategory.Q` of this map is an isomorphism in `D(B × C)`; that is
`CommAlgCat.isIso_Q_map_cotangentComplexProductMap` of
`StacksFrontier/Cotangent/ProductDecompositionBase.lean`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cotangentComplexProductMap :
    cotangentComplex.{u, v} A (CommAlgCat.of A (B × C)) ⟶
      (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (productFstSquare.{u, v} A B C).map).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (cotangentComplex.{u, v} A B)) ⊞
        (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (productSndSquare.{u, v} A B C).map).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (cotangentComplex.{u, v} A C))
declarations.comment: the canonical map `L_{B×C/A} → L_{B/A} ⊕ L_{C/A}` of the lemma, at chain level: the pair of the functoriality maps of the two projections, whose `DerivedCategory.Q` is the map in `D(B × C)` of the statement. That this map is an isomorphism in `D(B × C)` is `CommAlgCat.isIso_Q_map_cotangentComplexProductMap` of `StacksFrontier/Cotangent/ProductDecompositionBase.lean`, over an arbitrary base

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isIso_Q_map_cotangentComplexProductMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08SC.** Let `A → B` and `A → C` be ring maps. Then the canonical map

`L_{B×C/A} ⟶ L_{B/A} ⊕ L_{C/A}`

is an isomorphism in `D(B × C)`.

The map is `CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexProductMap`, the pair of the functoriality maps of
[Stacks, Tag 08PN] for the two projections; it is a quasi-isomorphism by
`CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentComplexProductMap`, and the localization `DerivedCategory.Q`
inverts exactly the quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_Q_map_cotangentComplexProductMap (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (B C : CommAlgCat.{u} A) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (cotangentComplexProductMap.{u, u} A B C))
declarations.comment: the lemma: for ring maps `A → B` and `A → C` the canonical map `L_{B×C/A} → L_{B/A} ⊕ L_{C/A}` -- the pair of the functoriality maps of the two projections, `CommAlgCat.cotangentComplexProductMap` -- is an isomorphism in `D(B × C)`, over an arbitrary base `A`. The chain-level form, that the map is a quasi-isomorphism, is `CommAlgCat.quasiIso_cotangentComplexProductMap`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.baseChangedStandardResolution
declarations.doc:
The standard resolution of `C` over `A`, base changed along the standard
resolution of `B` to give an augmented simplicial `B`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangedStandardResolution
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    {B C : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A} (f : B ⟶ C) :
    SimplicialObject.Augmented (CommAlgCat.{max u v} B)
declarations.comment: base_changed_standard_resolution

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebra
declarations.doc:
Every term of the standard resolution of `C` is a polynomial algebra over
the corresponding term of the standard resolution of `B`, when `B → C` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardResolution_isPolynomialAlgebra
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    {B C : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A} (f : B ⟶ C)
    (hf : Function.Injective f.hom) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    let P := (standardResolution A B).left.obj n
    let Q := (standardResolution A C).left.obj n
    letI : Algebra P Q :=
      (((standardResolutionFunctor A).map f).left.app n).hom.toAlgebra
    IsPolynomialAlgebra P (CommAlgCat.of P Q)
declarations.comment: polynomiality

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.fundamentalTriangle_of_injective
