**Stacks Project, Tag 08TE.** The stalk of the sheaf of relative differentials of a
morphism of sheaves of commutative rings is the module of Kähler differentials of its stalk
map: `Ω_{O₂/O₁, x} = Ω_{O₂,x / O₁,x}`.

It is also Stacks Tag 01V0 at a point: the sheaf of relative differentials commutes with taking
stalks.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def stalkModuleOfDifferentialsKaehlerLinearEquiv (x : X)
    [DecidableEq (OrderDual (TopologicalSpace.OpenNhds x))] :
    letI := algebraStalk φ.hom x
    ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
        (moduleOfDifferentials.{u, u, u} φ).val.presheaf x)
      ≃ₗ[ToType (O₂.presheaf.stalk x)]
      KaehlerDifferential (ToType (O₁.presheaf.stalk x)) (ToType (O₂.presheaf.stalk x))
declarations.comment: the identification

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeDifferentialStalk.stalkModuleOfDifferentialsKaehlerLinearEquiv_germ_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TE.** The identification of the stalk of the sheaf of relative
differentials with the Kähler differentials of the stalk map carries universal differentials to
universal differentials.

The germ at `x` of the universal relative differential of a section of `O₂` over a neighbourhood
of `x` goes to the universal differential of the germ of that section. This is what makes the
identification canonical.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkModuleOfDifferentialsKaehlerLinearEquiv_germ_d (x : X)
    [DecidableEq (OrderDual (TopologicalSpace.OpenNhds x))]
    (i : OrderDual (TopologicalSpace.OpenNhds x)) (a : nhdRing O₂.presheaf i) :
    letI := algebraStalk φ.hom x
    stalkModuleOfDifferentialsKaehlerLinearEquiv φ x
        (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          (moduleOfDifferentials.{u, u, u} φ).val.presheaf (nhdOpen i) x (mem_nhdOpen i)
          ((universalDerivation.{u, u, u} φ).d a)) =
      KaehlerDifferential.D (ToType (O₁.presheaf.stalk x)) (ToType (O₂.presheaf.stalk x))
        (O₂.presheaf.germ (nhdOpen i) x (mem_nhdOpen i) a)
declarations.comment: compatibility with the universal derivations

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence
declarations.doc:
The conormal sequence `I/I² ⟶ B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} ⟶ Ω_{B/R} ⟶ 0`, with its middle and right
terms expressed by the sheaves of relative differentials that corepresent derivations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialSequence :
    ShortComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max w u v z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))
declarations.comment: canonical conormal sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_exact
declarations.doc: The transported sequence is exact at the extension of scalars of `Ω_{A/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_exact :
    (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_epi
declarations.doc: The transported sequence surjects onto `Ω_{B/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_epi :
    Epi (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_f_class
declarations.doc:
The left-hand map carries the conormal class of a local section of the kernel to the
source's `d x ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_f_class (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : kernelIdeal φ.hom X) :
    ((differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).f.val.app X)
      (conormalClass.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ X x) =
      ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
          (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
        ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x.1)
declarations.comment: formula on local kernel sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_g_differential
declarations.doc: The right-hand map carries `d x ⊗ 1` to the universal differential of the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_g_differential (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : A.obj.obj X) :
    ((differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g.val.app X)
      (((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
          (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
        ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x)) =
      (universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R B (a ≫ φ)).d (φ.hom.app X x)
declarations.comment: right map on differentials

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_g_eq_mapDifferentials
declarations.doc:
Under extension/restriction of scalars, the right-hand map is exactly the canonical map
on relative differentials attached to the square `R → A → B` by Stacks 08TR.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_g_eq_mapDifferentials :
    (_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
      (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).homEquiv
      (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)
        (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R B (a ≫ φ))
        (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g =
      mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, z} a (a ≫ φ) (𝟙 R) φ (by simp)
declarations.comment: canonical right-hand map

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_f_unique
declarations.doc: The formula on local conormal classes determines the left-hand map.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_f_unique
    (g : (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).X₁ ⟶
      (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).X₂)
    (hg : ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : kernelIdeal φ.hom X),
      g.val.app X (conormalClass.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ X x) =
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
          (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
            (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
          ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x.1)) :
    g = (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).f
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the conormal map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationNaiveCotangentDerivedIso
declarations.doc:
For a presentation `α : ℰ ⟶ ℬ` of `ℬ` as a quotient of a polynomial algebra over `𝒜`, the
isomorphism `𝖭𝖫(α) ≅ 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ/𝒜}` in `D(ℬ)` given by the comparison quasi-isomorphism
`𝖭𝖫(α) ⟶ 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ/𝒜}`.
declarations.comment: the presentation-independence assertion

registrations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.polynomialAlgebraSheaf
registrations.comment: the polynomial algebra sheaf 𝒜[ℰ] of the section's notation

registrations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.canonicalPolynomialPresentation

registrations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.canonicalPolynomialPresentation_surjective

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationNaiveCotangentComplex
registrations.comment: the complex 𝖭𝖫(α) attached to a presentation α : ℰ ⟶ ℬ

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare
registrations.comment: the canonical ℬ-linear map of complexes 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ/𝒜} ⟶ 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ'/𝒜'} attached to a commutative square of sheaves of rings

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare_comp

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplexComparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.polynomialAlgebraSheaf
declarations.doc: The sheaf `A[B]`: the sheafification of `U ↦ A(U)[B(U)]`.
declarations.comment: the polynomial algebra sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.polynomialAlgebraMap
declarations.doc:
The structural morphism `A ⟶ A[B]`, obtained from the coefficient inclusions and the
sheafification unit.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def polynomialAlgebraMap
    (A B : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}) :
    A ⟶ polynomialAlgebraSheaf A B
declarations.comment: the coefficient map

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.canonicalPolynomialPresentation
declarations.doc: The canonical presentation `A[B] ⟶ B`, induced by `[b] ↦ b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalPolynomialPresentation
    {A B : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B) :
    polynomialAlgebraSheaf A B ⟶ B
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.polynomialAlgebraMap_comp_canonicalPolynomialPresentation
declarations.doc:
Evaluation `A[B] ⟶ B` is compatible with the structural maps from `A`, hence is a morphism
of `A`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialAlgebraMap_comp_canonicalPolynomialPresentation
    {A B : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B) :
    polynomialAlgebraMap A B ≫ canonicalPolynomialPresentation f = f
declarations.comment: compatibility with coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PolynomialAlgebra.canonicalPolynomialPresentation_surjective
declarations.doc:
The canonical polynomial presentation `A[B] ⟶ B` is locally surjective on underlying
sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalPolynomialPresentation_surjective
    {A B : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (Functor.whiskerRight (canonicalPolynomialPresentation f).hom
        (forget CommRingCat))
declarations.comment: surjectivity

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex
registrations.comment: the displayed two-term complex `I/I² ⟶ Ω_{A[B]/A} ⊗_{A[B]} B`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TK.** The canonical `B`-linear chain map `NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'}` attached to a
commutative square of sheaves of commutative rings on a topological space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare :
    naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, u, u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a ⟶
      ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u, u, u, u} (underlyingRingHomOfSite.{u, u, u} β)
        ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, u, u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A' B' a')
declarations.comment: the canonical B-linear map of complexes NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'}

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TK.** The canonical chain map attached to a commutative square of sheaves of
commutative rings on a topological space is compatible with compositions: given a commutative
diagram
```
B ──β──▸ B' ──β'──▸ B''
▲         ▲          ▲
a         a'         a''
│         │          │
A ──f──▸ A' ──f'──▸ A''
```
the composition `NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'} ⟶ NL_{B''/A''}` is the map attached to the outer
rectangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare_comp :
    spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare A A' B B' a a' f β hsq ≫
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u, u, u, u}
            (underlyingRingHomOfSite.{u, u, u} β)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
          (spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare A' A'' B' B'' a' a'' f' β' hsq') =
      spaceNaiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare A A'' B B'' a a'' (f ≫ f') (β ≫ β')
        (square_comp hsq hsq')
declarations.comment: compatibility of the canonical map of complexes with compositions

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison chain map `NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A}` from the naive cotangent complex of
an arbitrary polynomial presentation `α : E ⟶ B` to the one of the canonical presentation. It
is the map of the morphism of presentations `α : (E, α) ⟶ (B, id)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplexComparison :
    presentationNaiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E α ⟶
      naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, w, z} J A B a
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationNaiveCotangentDerivedIso
declarations.doc:
For a presentation `α : ℰ ⟶ ℬ` of `ℬ` as a quotient of a polynomial algebra over `𝒜`, the
isomorphism `𝖭𝖫(α) ≅ 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ/𝒜}` in `D(ℬ)` given by the comparison quasi-isomorphism
`𝖭𝖫(α) ⟶ 𝖭𝖫_{ℬ/𝒜}`.
declarations.comment: the isomorphism in D(ℬ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplexComparison
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `a : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of commutative rings on a topological space and a
family of generators `α : E ⟶ B` presenting `B`, the canonical comparison map
`NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A}` is a quasi-isomorphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_trivialNaiveCotangentComplexComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TL for the trivial presentation.**  For a locally surjective morphism
`a : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of commutative rings on a topological space, the comparison map
`NL(a) ⟶ NL_{B/A}` from the naive cotangent complex of the trivial presentation of `B` over `A`
— that is, of `a` itself, presenting `B` as a quotient of the `A`-algebra `A` — to the naive
cotangent complex of the canonical polynomial presentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

Quasi-isomorphy is a stalkwise condition, and at every point `x` the two stalk complexes are
the naive cotangent complexes of two extensions of `Bₓ` over `Aₓ` between which morphisms exist
in both directions: the stalk of the coefficient inclusion `A ⟶ A[B]` one way, and evaluation
of a polynomial at a set-theoretic section of `Aₓ → Bₓ` the other way.  So the comparison is a
homotopy equivalence on stalks.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_trivialNaiveCotangentComplexComparison :
    QuasiIso (trivialNaiveCotangentComplexComparison A B a)
declarations.comment: NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A} for the trivial presentation α = a : A ⟶ B of B over A

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_naiveCotangentComplexInverseImageMap
declarations.doc:
**The comparison chain map `f⁻¹ NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{f⁻¹B/f⁻¹A}` is an isomorphism.** Both
complexes vanish outside the degrees `-1` and `0`, where the comparison is the isomorphism of
conormal sheaves and the isomorphism of the scalar extensions of the differentials.
declarations.statement:
instance isIso_naiveCotangentComplexInverseImageMap :
    IsIso (naiveCotangentComplexInverseImageMap f A B a)
declarations.comment: invertibility of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the naive cotangent complex is the naive cotangent complex of the
inverse image**: `f⁻¹ NL_{B/A} ≅ NL_{f⁻¹B/f⁻¹A}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplexInverseImageIso :
    ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (inverseImageRingHom f B)).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, u, u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a) ≅
      naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, u, u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).obj A)
        ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).obj B)
        ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).map a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
The naive cotangent complex `NL_f = NL_{X/Y}` of a morphism of ringed spaces
`f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)`: the naive cotangent complex of the homomorphism of sheaves of rings
`f^{-1}𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` on `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplex :
    CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) X.sheaf)) ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialsSheafificationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TP.** Relative differentials commute with passing from presheaves
of commutative rings to their associated sheaves: the sheaf of differentials of `O₂^#` over
`O₁^#` is canonically the sheaf associated to the presheaf `X ↦ Ω[O₂(X)⁄O₁(X)]`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialsSheafificationIso (O₁ O₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (f : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :
    (derivationsFunctor.{v} (associatedCommRingSheaf J O₁) (associatedCommRingSheaf J O₂)
        (associatedCommRingSheafMap J f)).coreprX ≅
      sheafifiedObjectwiseDifferentials.{v, v₁} J f
declarations.comment: isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialsSheafificationIso_inv_unit_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TP**, the canonicality of the comparison: the inverse of
`differentialsSheafificationIso` carries the image of the objectwise universal differential
`d b` to the sheaf-level universal derivation evaluated on the image of `b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma differentialsSheafificationIso_inv_unit_d (O₁ O₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (f : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (X : Cᵒᵖ) (b : O₂.obj X) :
    ((differentialsSheafificationIso.{v, v₁} J O₁ O₂ f).inv.val.app X)
        (objectwiseDifferentialInSheafification.{v, v₁} J f X b) =
      (derivationsFunctor.{v} (associatedCommRingSheaf J O₁) (associatedCommRingSheaf J O₂)
        (associatedCommRingSheafMap J f)).coreprx.d
          ((toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂).app X b)
declarations.comment: canonicality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isIso_objectwiseDifferentialsSheafificationHom
declarations.doc:
The sheafification of the objectwise Kähler differentials is the sheaf of relative
differentials: `objectwiseDifferentialsSheafificationHom` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_objectwiseDifferentialsSheafificationHom :
    IsIso (objectwiseDifferentialsSheafificationHom.{v} O₁ O₂ φ)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of rings, as an isomorphism out of the sheafification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isLocallyInjective_objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TP**, injectivity half: the comparison from the objectwise Kähler differentials
to the sheaf of relative differentials is locally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyInjective_objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf :
    PresheafOfModules.IsLocallyInjective J (objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf.{v} O₁ O₂ φ)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of rings, local injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isLocallySurjective_objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TP**, surjectivity half: the comparison from the objectwise Kähler differentials
to the sheaf of relative differentials is locally surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySurjective_objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf :
    PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective J (objectwiseDifferentialsToSheaf.{v} O₁ O₂ φ)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of rings, local surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.pullbackDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TQ.** For a morphism of topoi presented by a continuous functor of
the underlying sites, the inverse image of the sheaf of relative differentials is canonically
the sheaf of relative differentials of the inverse-image morphism of sheaves of rings.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackDifferentialsIso :
    inverseImageModule J K F O₂ (moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ φ) ≅
      moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageRing J K F O₁) (inverseImageRing J K F O₂)
        ((F.sheafPullback CommRingCat.{u} J K).map φ)
declarations.comment:
the canonical identification, with the morphism of topoi presented by a
continuous functor of the underlying sites, both sites small in the single universe of the
sections of the sheaves of rings and of the modules, and the inverse image of sheaves of
commutative rings assumed to exist

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.pullbackDifferentialsIso_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TQ.** The canonical identification carries the inverse image of the
universal derivation to the universal derivation.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDifferentialsIso_compatible :
    (inverseImageDerivation J K F φ (moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ φ)
          (universalDerivation O₁ O₂ φ)).postcomp
        (pullbackDifferentialsIso J K F φ).hom.val =
      universalDerivation (inverseImageRing J K F O₁) (inverseImageRing J K F O₂)
        ((F.sheafPullback CommRingCat.{u} J K).map φ)
declarations.comment: compatibility with universal derivations

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.pullbackDifferentialsIso_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TQ.** Compatibility with universal derivations characterises the
canonical identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDifferentialsIso_unique
    (e : inverseImageModule J K F O₂ (moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ φ) ≅
      moduleOfDifferentials (inverseImageRing J K F O₁) (inverseImageRing J K F O₂)
        ((F.sheafPullback CommRingCat.{u} J K).map φ))
    (he : (inverseImageDerivation J K F φ (moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ φ)
        (universalDerivation O₁ O₂ φ)).postcomp e.hom.val =
      universalDerivation (inverseImageRing J K F O₁) (inverseImageRing J K F O₂)
        ((F.sheafPullback CommRingCat.{u} J K).map φ)) :
    e = pullbackDifferentialsIso J K F φ
declarations.comment: canonicity

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.inverseImageDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TQ.** The inverse image of the sheaf of relative differentials of a homomorphism
of sheaves of commutative rings along a morphism of topoi is the sheaf of relative differentials
of the inverse image: `f⁻¹Ω_{P/A} ≅ Ω_{f⁻¹P/f⁻¹A}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageDifferentialsIso :
    inverseImageDifferentials f a ≅
      moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w}
        (f.inverseImageRing.obj A) (f.inverseImageRing.obj P) (f.inverseImageRing.map a)
declarations.comment:
for an arbitrary morphism of topoi, with the object, arrow and section universes
of the two sites independent

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.homEquiv_inverseImageDifferentialsIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TQ.** The identification is the one carrying the inverse image of the universal
derivation of `Ω_{P/A}` to the universal derivation of `Ω_{f⁻¹P/f⁻¹A}`: transposing it along
`f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` and the universal property of `Ω_{P/A}` returns the universal derivation.
declarations.statement:
lemma homEquiv_inverseImageDifferentialsIso_hom :
    (inverseImageDifferentialsCorepresentableBy f a).homEquiv
        (inverseImageDifferentialsIso f a).hom =
      universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w}
        (f.inverseImageRing.obj A) (f.inverseImageRing.obj P) (f.inverseImageRing.map a)
declarations.comment: compatibility with the universal derivations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.functorialDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TR.** The canonical morphism on sheaves of relative differentials associated to a
commutative square, together with its characterisation on local differentials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def functorialDifferentials {O₁ O₂ O₁' O₂' : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    (a : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (a' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (f₁ : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (f₂ : O₂ ⟶ O₂')
    (sq : a ≫ f₂ = f₁ ≫ a') :
    DifferentialsMapData.{v, u, w, m} a a' f₁ f₂ sq
declarations.comment: the canonical map and uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.mapDifferentials_id_apply
declarations.doc:
The canonical map on differentials associated to the identity square is the identity on
every local section.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapDifferentials_id_apply {O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} (a : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ a).val.obj X) :
    (mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, m} a a (𝟙 O₁) (𝟙 O₂) (by simp)).val.app X x = x
declarations.comment: identity law

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.mapDifferentials_comp_apply
declarations.doc:
Canonical maps on differentials respect composition of commutative squares, on every local
section.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapDifferentials_comp_apply {O₁ O₂ O₁' O₂' O₁'' O₂'' : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    (a : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (a' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (a'' : O₁'' ⟶ O₂'')
    (f₁ : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (f₂ : O₂ ⟶ O₂') (g₁ : O₁' ⟶ O₁'') (g₂ : O₂' ⟶ O₂'')
    (sqf : a ≫ f₂ = f₁ ≫ a') (sqg : a' ≫ g₂ = g₁ ≫ a'')
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ a).val.obj X) :
    (mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, m} a a'' (f₁ ≫ g₁) (f₂ ≫ g₂)
      (by
        calc
          a ≫ (f₂ ≫ g₂) = (a ≫ f₂) ≫ g₂ := (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm
          _ = (f₁ ≫ a') ≫ g₂ := by rw [sqf]
          _ = f₁ ≫ (a' ≫ g₂) := Category.assoc _ _ _
          _ = f₁ ≫ (g₁ ≫ a'') := by rw [sqg]
          _ = (f₁ ≫ g₁) ≫ a'' := (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm)).val.app X x =
      (mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, m} a' a'' g₁ g₂ sqg).val.app X
        ((mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, m} a a' f₁ f₂ sqf).val.app X x)
declarations.comment: composition law

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence
declarations.doc:
The conormal sequence `I/I² ⟶ B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} ⟶ Ω_{B/R} ⟶ 0`, with its middle and right
terms expressed by the sheaves of relative differentials that corepresent derivations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialSequence :
    ShortComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max w u v z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))
declarations.comment: the canonical exact sequence of `O'₂`-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_exact
declarations.doc: The transported sequence is exact at the extension of scalars of `Ω_{A/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_exact :
    (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_epi
declarations.doc: The transported sequence surjects onto `Ω_{B/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_epi :
    Epi (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g
declarations.comment: exactness on the right

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_f_class
declarations.doc:
The left-hand map carries the conormal class of a local section of the kernel to the
source's `d x ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_f_class (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : kernelIdeal φ.hom X) :
    ((differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).f.val.app X)
      (conormalClass.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ X x) =
      ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
          (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
        ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x.1)
declarations.comment: the rule `f ↦ d f ⊗ 1` for the leftmost map

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_g_differential
declarations.doc: The right-hand map carries `d x ⊗ 1` to the universal differential of the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_g_differential (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : A.obj.obj X) :
    ((differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g.val.app X)
      (((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
          (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
        ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x)) =
      (universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R B (a ≫ φ)).d (φ.hom.app X x)
declarations.comment: the right-hand map on local differentials

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_g_eq_mapDifferentials
declarations.doc:
Under extension/restriction of scalars, the right-hand map is exactly the canonical map
on relative differentials attached to the square `R → A → B` by Stacks 08TR.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_g_eq_mapDifferentials :
    (_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
      (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).homEquiv
      (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)
        (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R B (a ≫ φ))
        (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).g =
      mapDifferentials.{v, u, w, z} a (a ≫ φ) (𝟙 R) φ (by simp)
declarations.comment: the map on the right is the one of Stacks 08TR

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_f_unique
declarations.doc: The formula on local conormal classes determines the left-hand map.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_f_unique
    (g : (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).X₁ ⟶
      (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).X₂)
    (hg : ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : kernelIdeal φ.hom X),
      g.val.app X (conormalClass.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ X x) =
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
          (underlyingRingHomForPullback J A B φ)).unit.app
            (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a)).val.app X
          ((universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, z} R A a).d x.1)) :
    g = (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).f
declarations.comment: the rule `f ↦ d f ⊗ 1` characterises the leftmost map

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Conormal.differentialSequence_X₁_desc_unique
declarations.doc:
**The leftmost term of the sequence is `I/I²`.** A morphism of sheaves of `O'₂`-modules out
of it is the same thing as an `O₂`-linear natural family of maps `I(U) ⟶ N(U)` out of the
kernel ideal: every such family descends to the term, uniquely, by the rule that the conormal
class of a local section `f` of `I` goes to the value of the family at `f`. The family
annihilates `I²` automatically, a local section of `I` acting as zero on a sheaf of
`O'₂`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialSequence_X₁_desc_unique
    (N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max w u v z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))
    (ρ : IdealRestriction.{v, u, w, z} φ N) :
    ∃! g : (differentialSequence.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ).X₁ ⟶ N,
      ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : kernelIdeal φ.hom X),
        g.val.app X (conormalClass.{v, u, w, z} J R A B a φ X x) = ρ.app X x
declarations.comment: the leftmost term is `I/I²`, by its universal property

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation
declarations.doc: **Stacks 08TU.** The canonical morphism `A[B] → B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalPresentation (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    freeAlgebraSheaf J A (underlyingPresheaf J B) ⟶ B
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation_spec
declarations.doc: The canonical presentation is induced by coefficient evaluation and `[b] ↦ b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalPresentation_spec (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    (toSheafification J CommRingCat.{w}).app
        (polynomialPresheaf J A (underlyingPresheaf J B)) ≫
      (sheafToPresheaf J CommRingCat.{w}).map (canonicalPresentation J A B a) =
        canonicalEvaluation J A B a
declarations.comment: evaluation on coefficients and variables

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation_comp_coefficientMap
declarations.doc: The canonical presentation `A[B] → B` respects the structural maps from `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalPresentation_comp_coefficientMap
    (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    freeAlgebraSheafCoefficientMap J A (underlyingPresheaf J B) ≫
      canonicalPresentation J A B a = a
declarations.comment: compatibility with the A-algebra structures

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc: The canonical presentation `A[B] → B` is surjective as a morphism of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalPresentation_isLocallySurjective
    (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J
      (Functor.whiskerRight
        ((sheafToPresheaf J CommRingCat.{w}).map (canonicalPresentation J A B a))
        (forget CommRingCat.{w}))
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
The conormal sequence for the canonical polynomial presentation of `B` over `A`.
Its first two terms are `I/I²` and `B ⊗[A[B]] Ω[A[B]/A]`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev canonicalConormalSequence
    (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    ShortComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max w u v z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))
declarations.comment: the canonical map is the left-hand map of this sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TW.** The naive cotangent complex of `B` over `A`, with `I/I²` in degree `-1`
and `B ⊗[A[B]] Ω[A[B]/A]` in degree `0`. This two-term complex is the one displayed in
Stacks 08TI, and 08TJ names it for a morphism of sheaves of rings.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplex
    (A B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (a : A ⟶ B) :
    CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max w u v z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B)) ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.freeAlgebraMapOfSquare_comp_canonicalPresentation
declarations.doc:
The morphism `A[B] ⟶ A'[B']` attached to a commutative square is compatible with the two
canonical presentations.
declarations.statement:
theorem freeAlgebraMapOfSquare_comp_canonicalPresentation :
    canonicalFreeAlgebraMapOfSquare J A A' B B' f β ≫
        Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation J A' B' a' =
      Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation J A B a ≫ β
declarations.comment: the canonical map A[B] ⟶ A'[B'] attached to the square

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TX.** The canonical `B`-linear chain map `NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'}` attached to a
commutative square of sheaves of rings: it is the map of conormal sheaves in degree `-1` and the
map of the scalar extensions of the differentials in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare :
    naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, w, z} J A B a ⟶
      ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max w u v z}
          (underlyingRingHomOfSite β)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, w, z} J A' B' a')
declarations.comment: the canonical B-linear map of complexes NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'}

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TX.** The canonical chain map attached to a commutative square of sheaves of
rings is compatible with compositions: given a commutative diagram
```
B ──β──▸ B' ──β'──▸ B''
▲         ▲          ▲
a         a'         a''
│         │          │
A ──f──▸ A' ──f'──▸ A''
```
the composition `NL_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B'/A'} ⟶ NL_{B''/A''}` is the map attached to the outer
rectangle.  The target of the composite is the iterated restriction of scalars along `β` and
`β'`, which is the restriction of scalars along `β ≫ β'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare_comp :
    naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, z} J A B a A' B' a' f β hsq ≫
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max w u v z}
            (underlyingRingHomOfSite β)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
          (naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, z} J A' B' a' A'' B'' a'' f' β' hsq') =
      naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, z} J A B a A'' B'' a'' (f ≫ f') (β ≫ β')
        (square_comp hsq hsq')
declarations.comment: compatibility of the canonical map of complexes with compositions

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexComparison_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TY**, normalisation at the canonical presentation. The canonical presentation is
the one whose family of generators is the identity of `B`, and there the comparison map
`NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A}` is the identity; so the identification of `NL(α)` with `NL_{B/A}` is the
identity for `α = id_B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplexComparison_id :
    naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{v, u, w, z} J A B a
      (Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.underlyingPresheaf J B) (𝟙 _) = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment:
normalisation: the canonical comparison map is the identity at the canonical
presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexComparison_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TY**, compatibility with functorialities. The comparison maps `NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A}`
of two polynomial presentations of `B` over `A` are compatible with every morphism of
presentations between them, so the identification of `NL(α)` with `NL_{B/A}` is canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplexComparison_naturality :
    presentationNaiveCotangentComplexMap.{v, u, w, z} J A E₁ E₂ h B a α₁ α₂ hα ≫
        naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E₂ α₂ =
      naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E₁ α₁
declarations.comment:
canonicality: the comparison maps are compatible with every morphism of
presentations

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationNaiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TY** in degree `0`. For every polynomial presentation `α : E ⟶ B` of `B` over
`A` the degree `0` cohomology sheaf of `NL(α)` is the sheaf of relative differentials
`Ω_{B/A}`, one and the same sheaf of `B`-modules for all `α`; in particular it agrees with the
degree `0` cohomology sheaf of `NL_{B/A}`, which is the case `α = id_B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presentationNaiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIso :
    (presentationNaiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E α).homology 0 ≅
      moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, z} A B a
declarations.comment:
degree 0 of the canonical isomorphism: H⁰(NL(α)) is Ω_{B/A} for every
presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_cokernel_map_presentationConormalSequence_f
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TY** in degree `0`, for the comparison map. A morphism of polynomial
presentations induces an isomorphism on the degree `0` cohomology sheaves of the two naive
cotangent complexes, these being the cokernels of the two conormal maps: both are `Ω_{B/A}`
and the induced map is the identity there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cokernel_map_presentationConormalSequence_f :
    IsIso (cokernel.map
      (presentationConormalSequence.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E₁ α₁).f
      (presentationConormalSequence.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E₂ α₂).f
      (presentationConormalMap.{v, u, w, z} J A E₁ E₂ h B a α₁ α₂ hα)
      (presentationTensorMap.{v, u, w, z} J A E₁ E₂ h B a α₁ α₂ hα)
      (Stacks.Sites.Conormal.conormalSequence_f_naturality.{v, u, w, z} J A B
        (Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.freeAlgebraSheaf J A E₁)
        (Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.freeAlgebraSheaf J A E₂)
        (Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.freeAlgebraSheafCoefficientMap J A E₁)
        (Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.freeAlgebraSheafCoefficientMap J A E₂)
        (presentation J A B a E₁ α₁) (presentation J A B a E₂ α₂)
        (freeAlgebraMap J A E₁ E₂ h)
        (freeAlgebraMap_comp_presentation J A E₁ E₂ h B a α₁ α₂ hα)
        (freeAlgebraSheafCoefficientMap_comp_freeAlgebraMap J A E₁ E₂ h)))
declarations.comment: degree 0: a morphism of presentations induces an isomorphism on H⁰

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplexComparison_site
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08TY.**  For every polynomial presentation `α : E ⟶ B` of `B` over `A` the
canonical comparison map `NL(α) ⟶ NL_{B/A}` is a quasi-isomorphism, so `NL(α)` and `NL_{B/A}`
are canonically isomorphic in the derived category of `B`-modules: the naive cotangent complex
does not depend on the presentation.

The comparison map is the chain map of the morphism of presentations `α : (E, α) ⟶ (B, id)`, so
this is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_presentationNaiveCotangentComplexMap` at the canonical
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplexComparison_site :
    QuasiIso (naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{v, u, w, z} J A B a E α)
declarations.comment:
the canonical isomorphism NL(α) ≅ NL_{B/A} in D(B): the comparison map of a
polynomial presentation is a quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.inverseImageConormalIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the conormal sheaf is the conormal sheaf of the inverse image**:
`f⁻¹(ℐ/ℐ²) ≅ ℐ'/(ℐ')²`, where `ℐ = Ker φ` and `ℐ' = Ker(f⁻¹φ)`. This is the degree `-1` term
of the identification `f⁻¹ NL_{ℬ/𝒜} = NL_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}` of Stacks 08TZ.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageConormalIso :
    (inverseImageCommModules.{w, w', v, u, v', u'} f B).obj
        (conormalModule.{w', v', u'} K φ) ≅
      conormalModule.{w, v, u} J (f.inverseImageRing.map φ)
declarations.comment: the degree -1 term, for an arbitrary locally surjective homomorphism of sheaves of rings, of which the conormal term of the tag is the instance at the canonical polynomial presentation. The instantiation is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentNegOneIso` and the isomorphism of complexes is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.inverseImageFreeAlgebraHom_comp_canonicalPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TZ.** The inverse image of the canonical polynomial presentation
`A[B] ⟶ B` is the canonical polynomial presentation `(f⁻¹A)[f⁻¹B] ⟶ f⁻¹B` of the inverse-image
homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageFreeAlgebraHom_comp_canonicalPresentation (a : A ⟶ B) :
    inverseImageFreeAlgebraHom f A B ≫
        canonicalPresentation J (f.inverseImageRing.obj A) (f.inverseImageRing.obj B)
          (f.inverseImageRing.map a) =
      f.inverseImageRing.map (canonicalPresentation K A B a)
declarations.comment: the inverse image of the canonical polynomial presentation is the canonical polynomial presentation of the inverse image, from which both terms of the complex are built

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08TZ.** The inverse image of the degree-`0` term of the naive
cotangent complex of `a` and the degree-`0` term of the naive cotangent complex of `f⁻¹a` have
the same morphisms into every sheaf of `f⁻¹B`-modules: both represent the `f⁻¹A`-derivations of
the canonical polynomial presentation of `f⁻¹B` over `f⁻¹A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroHomEquiv
    (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (f.inverseImageRing.obj B))) :
    ((inverseImageModules f
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u', v', max u' v' w'} (J := K)) B)).obj
        (canonicalConormalSequence.{v', u', max u' v' w', max u' v' w'} K A B a).X₂ ⟶ M) ≃
      ((canonicalConormalSequence.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w} J (f.inverseImageRing.obj A)
        (f.inverseImageRing.obj B) (f.inverseImageRing.map a)).X₂ ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: the degree 0 term: its inverse image and the degree 0 term of the inverse image represent the same functor of derivations. Naturality of this bijection is `inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroHomEquiv_naturality` and the resulting isomorphism of degree 0 terms is `inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroIso`; the isomorphism of complexes assembled from it is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the naive cotangent complex is the naive cotangent complex of the
inverse image**: `f⁻¹ NL_{B/A} ≅ NL_{f⁻¹B/f⁻¹A}`, as an isomorphism of two-term complexes of
sheaves of `f⁻¹B`-modules, with the identification of the degree `-1` terms in degree `-1` and
the identification of the degree `0` terms in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso :
    ((inverseImageTargetModules.{u, v, w, u', v', w'} J K f
            (B := B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex.{v', u', max u' v' w', max u' v' w'} K A B a) ≅
      naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w} J (f.inverseImageRing.obj A)
        (f.inverseImageRing.obj B) (f.inverseImageRing.map a)
declarations.comment: the inverse image of the naive cotangent complex is the naive cotangent complex of the inverse image, as an isomorphism of complexes: the identification the tag states, assembled from the degree -1 and the degree 0 comparison and their commutation with the conormal differentials

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the degree-`0` term of the naive cotangent complex is the degree-`0`
term of the naive cotangent complex of the inverse image**:
`f⁻¹(B ⊗_{A[B]} Ω_{A[B]/A}) ≅ f⁻¹B ⊗_{(f⁻¹A)[f⁻¹B]} Ω_{(f⁻¹A)[f⁻¹B]/f⁻¹A}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageNaiveCotangentZeroIso :
    (inverseImageModules f (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u', v', max u' v' w'} B)).obj
        (canonicalConormalSequence.{v', u', max u' v' w', max u' v' w'} K A B a).X₂ ≅
      (canonicalConormalSequence.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w} J (f.inverseImageRing.obj A)
        (f.inverseImageRing.obj B) (f.inverseImageRing.map a)).X₂
declarations.comment: the degree 0 term as an isomorphism, obtained from naturality of the corepresentability bijection by Yoneda. The degree -1 term is `inverseImageConormalIso` and the isomorphism of complexes assembled from the two is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
The naive cotangent complex `NL_f = NL_{𝒪_C/f⁻¹𝒪_D}` of a morphism of ringed topoi
`(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), 𝒪_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)`: the two-term complex `I/I² ⟶ 𝒪_C ⊗_{P₀} Ω_{P₀/f⁻¹𝒪_D}` in
cohomological degrees `-1` and `0`, formed from the inverse-image form `f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C` of its
structure map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplex :
    CochainComplex (Sheaf.targetModules.{u, v, w} X.J X.O) ℤ

the complex `NL_f`, with the free algebra sheaf of the source's presentation
spelled by the degree-zero term `P₀` of the standard resolution of `f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C`; the

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded
declarations.doc:
**`RΓ(𝒞, -)` over a base ring commutes with `R lim`**: `A`-linear derived global sections
carry a derived inverse limit in `D(𝒪)` to a derived inverse limit in `D(A)`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 08U1] for `derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded`, through
`Stacks.Injectives.isDerivedLimit_map_rightDerivedFunctor`: the functor is the right derived
functor of `moduleGlobalSectionsOver` by
`derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded_isRightDerivedFunctor`, that functor preserves countable
products, `Mod(𝒪)` is Grothendieck abelian and the countable products of `ModuleCat A` are
exact. This is the site-and-base-ring form of [Stacks, Tag 0D6K], whose `Γ(𝒞, -)`-valued form
is `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalSections.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedGlobalSections`, and the
ringed-site counterpart of [Stacks, Tag 0D60] for a ringed space,
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsOverBase.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsOver`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hL : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded X A ρ).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded X A ρ) h
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOverUnbounded X A ρ).obj L)
declarations.comment: for A-linear derived global sections on a ringed site

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isDerivedLimit_map_rightDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08U1.** The right derived functor of an additive functor from a Grothendieck
abelian category to an abelian category with exact countable products carries every
derived-limit triangle to a derived-limit triangle, if the functor preserves countable
products. Its structural map is the image of the supplied `p`, followed by the canonical
product comparison; hence its projections are `RF.map (p ≫ Pi.π _ n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_rightDerivedFunctor (X : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory A)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩] (K : DerivedCategory A)
    (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hK : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          X.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory A)) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ RF.obj (X.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      letI := h
      ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ RF.obj (X.obj ⟨n⟩)) ⟶ (RF.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk (RF.map p ≫ piComparison RF (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.obj ⟨n⟩))
          (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ RF.obj (X.obj ⟨n⟩)) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ RF.obj (X.obj ⟨n⟩)) (n + 1) ≫
              RF.map (X.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.exists_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_vanishing_on_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08U2**, in the form the source states it: the canonical map
`E ⟶ R lim τ_{≥ -n} E` *is* an isomorphism. The derived limit and the canonical map are

theorem exists_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_vanishing_on_cover {X : TopCat.{u}}

    (hvanishing : ∀ U ∈ 𝔅, ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ), pb m < (p : ℤ) →

        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),

      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_vanishing_on_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08U2.** Let `E` be an object of the derived category of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules on a ringed space, let `p(-)` be a function and let `𝔅` be a set of opens of `X`
such that every open of `X` is a union of members of `𝔅` and `Hᵖ(U, H^{m-p}(E))` vanishes for
`U ∈ 𝔅` and `p > p(m)`. Then the tower of truncations `τ_{≥ -n} E` from below has a derived
limit `R lim τ_{≥ -n} E` with a canonical map of Remark 0H72 from `E`, and every such canonical
map to every derived limit of the tower is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_vanishing_on_cover
    {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (pb : ℤ → ℤ) (𝔅 : Set (Opens X))
    (hcov : ∀ V : Opens X, ∃ 𝒰 : Set (Opens X), 𝒰 ⊆ 𝔅 ∧ (V : Set X) = ⋃ U ∈ 𝒰, (U : Set X))
    (hvanishing : ∀ U ∈ 𝔅, ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ), pb m < (p : ℤ) →

      (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
      (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦

      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E)) ∧
    ∀ (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
      (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound
declarations.doc:
Degree-dependent bounds for cohomology on a locally covering class imply that the canonical
map to the derived limit of the lower-truncation tower is an isomorphism.

This is a variant of [Stacks, Tag 08U3]: the enough-injectives and product hypotheses below are
not hypotheses of the source, and they are avoidable.  The full statement is
`Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeBound.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound`, which
discharges them by taking the module universe large enough to contain the site and the structure
rings.  This single-universe form is kept for the consumers that are already stated at it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound
    (S : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    [HasSheafify S.J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [S.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [EnoughInjectives (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)))
    (degreeBound : ℤ → ℤ) (B : Set S.C)
    (basisCover : ∀ U : S.C, ∃ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} U,
      𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ S.J U ∧ ∀ i, B (𝒰.X i))
    (vanishing : ∀ (V : S.C), B V → ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ),
      degreeBound m < (p : ℤ) →
        IsZero (moduleCohomology (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O) V p
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))
            (m - (p : ℤ))).obj E)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (q : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ :
      (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶
          L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk q (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
              (n + 1) ≫
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).map
              (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang
          (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))))
    (c : E ⟶ L)
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ q ≫ Pi.π
      (fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c
declarations.comment:
variant: the single-universe form, for a ringed site whose module category has
enough injectives and the countable product of the truncation tower; the tag, with neither of
these, is Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeBound.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeBound.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08U3.** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on a site `C` and let `E` be an
object of the derived category of sheaves of `O`-modules.  Suppose there are a function
`p(-) : ℤ → ℤ` and a set `B` of objects of `C` such that every object of `C` has a covering whose
members are elements of `B`, and such that `H^p(V, H^{m - p}(E)) = 0` for all `p > p(m)` and all
`V ∈ B`.  Then the canonical map `E ⟶ R lim τ_{≥ -n} E` is an isomorphism.

Nothing else is assumed: sheafification, enough injectives and the countable products presenting
the derived limit are all theorems at this module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_degreeBound
    (O : Sheaf J RingCat.{r})
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O))
    (degreeBound : ℤ → ℤ) (B : Set C)
    (basisCover : ∀ U : C, ∃ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{max u v} U,
      𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i, B (𝒰.X i))
    (vanishing : ∀ (V : C), B V → ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ), degreeBound m < (p : ℤ) →
      IsZero (@moduleCohomology C instC J O hasSheafifyMax.{u, v, r, w}
        wEqualsLocallyBijectiveMax.{u, v, r, w}
        (SiteModules.moduleSheavesEnoughInjectives.{u, v, r, w} O) V p
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O)
          (m - (p : ℤ))).obj E)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O))
    (c : E ⟶ L)
    (q : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶
          L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk q (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
              (n + 1) ≫
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).map
              (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O)))
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ q ≫
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c

declarations.name: Rlim.lim_hasRightDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08U4.** The inverse-limit functor on inverse systems of abelian groups has a
right derived functor from `D(Ab(N))` to `D(Ab)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem lim_hasRightDerivedFunctor :
    let F : Rlim.InvSystemAb ⥤ Ab.{0} := lim
    ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory Rlim.InvSystemAb ⥤ DerivedCategory Ab.{0})
      (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF),
      RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso Rlim.InvSystemAb (ComplexShape.up ℤ))

declarations.name: Rlim.derivedLimit_iso_rightDerivedLimit_and_homology_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08U5.** Let `E` be an inverse system in `D(Ab)` and let `K` be a derived
limit of `E`.  The system has a lift to `D(Ab(N))`, and the value on every lift of a
right-derived inverse-limit functor is isomorphic to `K`.  In particular this value is
independent, up to isomorphism, of the chosen lift.

For every `p`, the defining product triangle of `K` induces the canonical short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ R¹ lim H^(p-1)(Eₙ) ⟶ H^p(K) ⟶ lim H^p(Eₙ) ⟶ 0`.  The two maps are
specified by the connecting morphism and the map from `K` to the product, respectively.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedLimit_iso_rightDerivedLimit_and_homology_shortExact
(E : Functor ℕᵒᵖ (DerivedCategory Ab.{0})) :
    let F : Functor Rlim.InvSystemAb Ab.{0} := lim
    ∃ (RF : Functor (DerivedCategory Rlim.InvSystemAb) (DerivedCategory Ab.{0}))
      (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF),
      RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso Rlim.InvSystemAb (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
        (∃ K : DerivedCategory Ab.{0}, Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit E K) ∧
        (∃ (M : DerivedCategory Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.AbN)
          (ψ : ∀ n, (Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.evD n).obj M ≅ E.obj n),
          ∀ ⦃a b : ℕᵒᵖ⦄ (f : a ⟶ b),
            (Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.evTrans f).app M ≫ (ψ b).hom = (ψ a).hom ≫
              E.map f) ∧
        ∀ (K : DerivedCategory Ab.{0}), Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit E K →
        (∀ (M : DerivedCategory Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.AbN)
            (ψ : ∀ n, (Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.evD n).obj M ≅ E.obj n),
            (∀ ⦃a b : ℕᵒᵖ⦄ (f : a ⟶ b),
              (Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.evTrans f).app M ≫ (ψ b).hom = (ψ a).hom
                ≫ E.map f) →
            Nonempty (K ≅ RF.obj M)) ∧
        let P := ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => E.obj (Opposite.op n)
        let d : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => E.obj (Opposite.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
              E.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
        ∃ (a : K ⟶ P) (b : P ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk a d b ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory Ab.{0}) ∧
          ∀ p : ℤ,
            let H : ℤ → Rlim.InvSystemAb := fun q =>
              E ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} q
            let HP : ℤ → Ab.{0} := fun q =>
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} q).obj P
            let PH : ℤ → Ab.{0} := fun q =>
              ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (H q).obj (Opposite.op n)
            let δH : (q : ℤ) → (PH q ⟶ PH q) := fun q => Rlim.delta (H q)
            let R1lim := Rlim.firstDerivedLimit (H (p - 1))
            let HpK := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} p).obj K
            let limHp := lim.obj (H p)
            let T := Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk a d b
            let connecting : HP (p - 1) ⟶ HpK :=
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} 0).homologySequenceδ
                T (p - 1) p (by omega)
            ∃ (ePrev : HP (p - 1) ≅ PH (p - 1)) (eCurr : HP p ≅ PH p),
              (∀ n : ℕ, ePrev.hom ≫ Pi.π
                  (fun n : ℕ => (H (p - 1)).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} (p - 1)).map
                  (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n)) ∧
              (∀ n : ℕ, eCurr.hom ≫ Pi.π
                  (fun n : ℕ => (H p).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} p).map
                  (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n)) ∧
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} (p - 1)).map d ≫ ePrev.hom =
                ePrev.hom ≫ δH (p - 1) ∧
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} p).map d ≫ eCurr.hom =
                eCurr.hom ≫ δH p ∧
              ∃ (eLim : limHp ≅ kernel (δH p))
                (hConnecting : δH (p - 1) ≫ ePrev.inv ≫ connecting = 0)
                (hKernel : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} p).map a ≫
                  eCurr.hom ≫ δH p = 0),
                (∀ n : ℕ, eLim.hom ≫ kernel.ι (δH p) ≫
                    Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (H p).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                  limit.π (H p) (Opposite.op n)) ∧
                let i : R1lim ⟶ HpK :=
                  cokernel.desc (δH (p - 1)) (ePrev.inv ≫ connecting) hConnecting
                let q : HpK ⟶ limHp :=
                  kernel.lift (δH p)
                    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{0} p).map a ≫ eCurr.hom)
                    hKernel ≫ eLim.inv
                ∃ w : i ≫ q = 0, (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationSolution
declarations.doc:
A solution of the first order deformation problem for a fixed
first order thickening `t : S ⟶ S'`, morphism `f : X ⟶ S`, `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` and prescribed map
`c : f^* t^* 𝒥 ⟶ 𝒢`: a first order thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` and a morphism `f' : X' ⟶ S'` over
`t`, together with an identification of the ideal of `i` with `𝒢` under which the vertical map
on ideals induced by `f'` is exactly `c`.
declarations.statement:
structure DeformationSolution {X S S' : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (t : S ⟶ S')
    (ht : IsFirstOrderThickening t) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (c : (modulePullback f).obj
      ((modulePullback t).obj (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.idealSheaf t)) ⟶ G)
declarations.comment: the deformation problem to solve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationIdealDiagram.lifting_obstruction_and_torsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08U8.** In the situation of **Stacks 08U9** — a commutative cube of
ringed spaces whose horizontal arrows are first order thickenings, with `𝒢_j = Ker(i_j^♯)`, a
`g`-map `ν : 𝒢₁ ⟶ 𝒢₂`, and front and back solutions of **Stacks 08U7** making the diagram of
ideal rows of **Stacks 08UA** commute (`D : DeformationIdealDiagram`):

1. the canonical element `D.obstructionClass` of `Ext¹_{𝒪_{X₂}}(Lg^*NL_{X₁/S₁}, 𝒢₂)` vanishes
   if and only if there is a morphism of ringed spaces `X'₂ ⟶ X'₁` fitting into (08U9)
   compatibly with `ν`;
2. if there is such a morphism, the set of all of them is a principal homogeneous space under
   `Hom_{𝒪_{X₁}}(Ω_{X₁/S₁}, g_*𝒢₂)`: the action `liftAct` (given by the source's formula,
   `liftAct_spec`) is trivial at `0`, additive, and simply transitive, and is the action of an
   `AddTorsor` structure on the set.

The other two spellings of the acting group in the source's display are identified with this
one by `actingGroupPullbackAddEquiv` (`Hom_{𝒪_{X₂}}(g^*Ω_{X₁/S₁}, 𝒢₂)`) and
`extZeroDerivedPullbackNaiveCotangentAddEquiv` (`Ext⁰_{𝒪_{X₂}}(Lg^*NL_{X₁/S₁}, 𝒢₂)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem lifting_obstruction_and_torsor :
    (D.obstructionClass = 0 ↔ Nonempty D.Lifts) ∧
      (∀ φ : D.Lifts, D.liftAct 0 φ = φ) ∧
      (∀ (φ : D.Lifts) (θ θ' : D.ActingGroup),
        D.liftAct θ' (D.liftAct θ φ) = D.liftAct (θ + θ') φ) ∧
      (∀ φ ψ : D.Lifts, ∃! θ : D.ActingGroup, D.liftAct θ φ = ψ) ∧
      (∀ _φ₀ : D.Lifts, ∃ T : AddTorsor D.ActingGroup D.Lifts,
        ∀ (θ : D.ActingGroup) (φ ψ : D.Lifts), T.vadd θ φ = ψ ↔ D.liftAct θ φ = ψ)
declarations.comment: both clauses, for the source's diagram of ringed spaces: the canonical class in Ext^1(Lg^*NL_{X_1/S_1}, G_2) vanishes iff a morphism X'_2 -> X'_1 fitting into the diagram compatibly with nu exists, and the set of such morphisms is a principal homogeneous space under Hom(Omega_{X_1/S_1}, g_*G_2), which actingGroupPullbackAddEquiv and extZeroDerivedPullbackNaiveCotangentAddEquiv identify with Hom(g^*Omega_{X_1/S_1}, G_2) and Ext^0(Lg^*NL_{X_1/S_1}, G_2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationCube
declarations.doc:
The commutative diagram of morphisms of ringed spaces
comparing two deformation situations: a square `i₂ : X₂ ⟶ X₂'` over `t₂ : S₂ ⟶ S₂'` at the
back, a square `i₁ : X₁ ⟶ X₁'` over `t₁ : S₁ ⟶ S₁'` at the front, and comparison morphisms
`g : X₂ ⟶ X₁`, `h : S₂ ⟶ S₁`, `h' : S₂' ⟶ S₁'` making the four closed faces commute. There
is no comparison `X₂' ⟶ X₁'`.
declarations.statement: structure DeformationCube
declarations.comment: the displayed commutative diagram of ringed spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationIdealDiagram
declarations.doc:
The commutative diagram of the four short exact ideal rows attached to a deformation cube
whose horizontal arrows are first order thickenings: modules `𝒢₁`, `𝒢₂` identifying the ideals
of `i₁` and `i₂`, prescribed maps `c₁`, `c₂` making front and back solutions of the deformation
problem, and a `g`-map `ν : 𝒢₁ ⟶ 𝒢₂` compatible with the
comparison `DeformationCube.baseIdealMap` of the ideals of `t₁` and `t₂`.
declarations.statement: structure DeformationIdealDiagram
declarations.comment: the displayed commutative diagram of the four ideal rows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.exists_conormalRepresentative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UB.** Every class of `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(𝖭𝖫_{X/S}, 𝒢)` is the class of a
homomorphism `δ : 𝒥/𝒥² ⟶ 𝒢` out of the conormal sheaf of a suitable family of generators
`α : ℰ ⟶ 𝒪_X` of `𝒪_X` over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`, transported to `𝖭𝖫_{X/S}` through the quasi-isomorphism
of **Stacks 08TL**.

The family of generators comes with the class and is not a refinement of a prescribed one; that
is all the source gives, and it is all that is needed where the acting group of the torsor of
**Stacks 08UC** is the presentation-free `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(𝖭𝖫_{X/S}, 𝒢)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_conormalRepresentative (ξ : relativeObj f ⟶ shiftedSingleObj G) :
    ∃ (E : Functor (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ (Type u))
      (α : E ⟶ underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) X.sheaf)
      (hsurj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
        (generatorsPresentation f E α).hom),
      letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
        (generatorsPresentation f E α).hom := hsurj
      ∃ δ : (twoTerm f E α).conormal ⟶ G,
        (naiveCotangentIso f E α).inv ≫ (twoTerm f E α).conormalExtClass G δ = ξ
declarations.comment: over a ringed space, in the two-term idiom of NaiveCotangentTwoTerm: the class of a conormal homomorphism of a family of generators produced with it, transported to 𝖭𝖫_{X/S}

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ConormalRepresentative.exists_enlargement_conormalExtClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UB.** Let `𝒜 ⟶ ℬ` be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative
rings on a topological space, let `𝒢` be a `ℬ`-module and let `ξ` be a first Ext class of
`NL_{ℬ/𝒜}` with values in `𝒢`. There is a family of generators `α : ℰ ⟶ ℬ` presenting `ℬ` over
`𝒜` for which `ξ`, restricted along the canonical comparison map `NL(α) ⟶ NL_{ℬ/𝒜}`, is the
class of a homomorphism `ℐ/ℐ² ⟶ 𝒢` out of the conormal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_enlargement_conormalExtClass
    [HasWeakSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{max w u}]
    [(Opens.grothendieckTopology X).HasSheafCompose
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max w u} RingCat.{max w u})]
    (A B : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{max w u}) (a : A ⟶ B)
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}]
    [(Opens.grothendieckTopology X).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max w u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))]
    (G : SheafOfModules.{max w u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf B))
    (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, max w u, w}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a))
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj G) 1) :
    ∃ (E : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Type (max w u)))
      (α : E.obj ⟶ underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B)
      (hsurj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentation (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a E.obj α).hom),
      letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentation (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a E.obj α).hom :=
        hsurj
      ∃ f : (Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationConormalSequence.{u, u, max w u, w}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a E.obj α).X₁ ⟶ G,
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{u, u, max w u, w}
              (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a E.obj α) ≫ ξ =
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.presentationConormalExtClass.{u, u, w, w}
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a E.obj α G f
declarations.comment: on the site of open sets of a topological space, the setting of the statement; the family of generators and the homomorphism are produced by the proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.exists_addTorsor_solutionClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UC.** If there exists a solution to the deformation problem
(91.7.0.1) of **Stacks 08U7**, then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal
homogeneous under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/S}, 𝒢)`.

The statement holds at every model `H` of the derived category `D(𝒪_X)`, with the canonical group
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentExt` of the homomorphism `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X` in degree one. The
set of isomorphism classes is `SolutionClasses t ht f G c`, the quotient of the solutions by
`Isomorphic` (some morphism of solutions — a morphism of the deformed spaces under `X`, over
`S'`, and the identity on `𝒢` — is an isomorphism). "Principal homogeneous" is Mathlib's
`AddTorsor`: an action of the group which is free and transitive, the unique element carrying
one class to another being `-ᵥ`. The structure is not an arbitrary one: the element separating
the classes of `X'₁` and `X'₂` is the difference class `o(X'₁, X'₂)` of the two solutions (the
class of the square-zero extension of `f⁻¹𝒪_S`-algebras which is their difference, read in the
model `H`), and `ξ` acts on the class of `X'` by the class of the solution `X'_ξ` of the
source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addTorsor_solutionClasses (h : Nonempty (DeformationSolution t ht f G c)) :
    ∃ T : AddTorsor (modelExtOneNaiveCotangent H f G) (SolutionClasses t ht f G c),
      letI := T
      (∀ Q₁ Q₂ : DeformationSolution t ht f G c,
        ((⟦Q₁⟧ : SolutionClasses t ht f G c) -ᵥ ⟦Q₂⟧) =
          extOneNaiveCotangentModelAddEquiv f G (differenceClass Q₁ Q₂)) ∧
      ∀ (ξ : modelExtOneNaiveCotangent H f G) (Q : DeformationSolution t ht f G c),
        ξ +ᵥ (⟦Q⟧ : SolutionClasses t ht f G c) =
          ⟦solutionTwist Q ((extOneNaiveCotangentModelAddEquiv f G).symm ξ)⟧
declarations.comment: at any model of D(𝒪_X), with the canonical Ext¹(NL_{X/S}, 𝒢); the separating element of two classes is their difference class and ξ acts on [X'] by [X'_ξ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.isomorphic_iff_nonempty_solutionHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UC**, the half asserting that the obstruction separates isomorphism
classes. Two solutions of the deformation problem of Tag 08U7 are isomorphic exactly when there
is a morphism of solutions between them: by `SolutionHom.isIso_hom` every morphism of solutions
is already invertible. This is the source's "clearly, this element is the obstruction to the
existence of an isomorphism, hence separates the isomorphism classes" — the obstruction class of
Tag 08U8, which obstructs a *morphism* of solutions, thereby obstructs an isomorphism.

The other half of the tag — that the isomorphism classes form a principal homogeneous space
under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/S}, 𝒢)` — is not claimed here; the full statement of the tag is
`exists_addTorsor_solutionClasses` in
`StacksFrontier/Deformation/RingedSpaceThickening/SolutionClassesPrincipalHomogeneous.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isomorphic_iff_nonempty_solutionHom (Q₁ Q₂ : DeformationSolution t ht f G c) :
    Isomorphic Q₁ Q₂ ↔ Nonempty (SolutionHom Q₁ Q₂)
declarations.comment: the step of the proof that the obstruction to a morphism of solutions is the obstruction to an isomorphism; the full statement is exists_addTorsor_solutionClasses

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.ArbitrarySiteExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08UF on arbitrary equivalent sites.** A solution of the extension problem on a given
thickened source ringed topos `X'`. The displayed diagram of sheaves is pulled back along the
equivalence underlying `i`, and the invertible 2-morphism records the morphism of thickenings.
declarations.statement:
public structure CompatibleFirstOrderThickening
    (S : ArbitrarySiteExtensionProblem X B B')
    (X' : RingedTopos.{v''', u''', w'''})
    [X'.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w'''})]
    [X'.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w'''} RingCat.{w'''})]
declarations.comment: arbitrary equivalent sites

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram.translate_existsUnique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UG**, clause (2). The morphisms
`(Sh(C'₂), O'₂) ⟶ (Sh(C'₁), O'₁)` fitting into the source's diagram compatibly with `ν` form a
principal homogeneous space: any one of them is carried to any other by exactly one derivation
of the diagram. Together with `translate_zero` and `translate_add` this is the free and
transitive action of the source's clause (2), with the acting group written as the group of
section-wise derivations out of `O'₁` rather than as
`Hom_{O₁}(Ω_{O₁/O_{B₁}}, g_*G₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem translate_existsUnique (p q : Lift D) :
    ∃! δ : Derivation D.toSituation, translate p δ = q
declarations.comment: clause (2): the lifts are a principal homogeneous space under Derivation

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.FirstOrderLiftDiagram.derivationEquivDifferentialsHom
declarations.doc:
The derivations of the diagram, under which the lifts form a principal homogeneous space by
`Deformation.ToposThickening.FirstOrderLiftDiagram.existsUnique_translateHom`, are the
homomorphisms `Hom_{𝒪₁}(Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, g_*𝒢₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivationEquivDifferentialsHom :
    Derivation D.toSituation ≃+ (frontDifferentials D ⟶ pushedIdeal D)
declarations.comment: clause (2): the identification of the acting group of `FirstOrderLiftDiagram.existsUnique_translateHom` with the first group of the source's display, Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2). Nothing assumed

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.FirstOrderLiftDiagram.translateHom_zero
declarations.doc: The zero homomorphism acts trivially on the lifts of the diagram.
declarations.statement: public theorem translateHom_zero (p : D.Lift) : translateHom D p 0 = p
declarations.comment: clause (2): triviality of the action of 0 in the principal homogeneous space structure under Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.FirstOrderLiftDiagram.translateHom_add
declarations.doc: Translation of the lifts of the diagram is additive in the translating homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem translateHom_add (p : D.Lift) (a b : frontDifferentials D ⟶ pushedIdeal D) :
    translateHom D (translateHom D p a) b = translateHom D p (a + b)
declarations.comment: clause (2): additivity of the action in the principal homogeneous space structure under Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.FirstOrderLiftDiagram.existsUnique_translateHom
declarations.doc:
The morphisms `(Sh(𝒞'₂), 𝒪'₂) ⟶ (Sh(𝒞'₁), 𝒪'₁)` fitting into the diagram compatibly with `ν`
form a principal homogeneous space under `Hom_{𝒪₁}(Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, g_*𝒢₂)`: any one of them is
carried to any other by exactly one homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_translateHom (p q : D.Lift) :
    ∃! a : frontDifferentials D ⟶ pushedIdeal D, translateHom D p a = q
declarations.comment: clause (2) in full, with nothing assumed: the morphisms fitting into the source's diagram compatibly with nu are a principal homogeneous space under the source's own acting group Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2), the underlying topoi identified as in the source's own reduction

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.obstructionClass_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UG, clause (1).** For the diagram (08UH) of ringed topoi, whose
horizontal arrows are first order thickenings, and a `g⁻¹𝒪₁`-linear map `ν : g⁻¹𝒢₁ ⟶ 𝒢₂` making
(08UI) commute with front and back rows solutions of (08UF), the canonical element
`obstructionClass D` of `Ext¹_{𝒪₂}(Lg^*NL_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, 𝒢₂)` vanishes if and only if there is a
