morphism of ringed topoi `(Sh(𝒞'₂), 𝒪'₂) ⟶ (Sh(𝒞'₁), 𝒪'₁)` fitting into (08UH) compatibly
with `ν`.
declarations.statement:
theorem obstructionClass_eq_zero_iff :
    obstructionClass D = 0 ↔ Nonempty (CompatibleLift D)
declarations.comment: clause (1) for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi between four arbitrary ringed topoi: the canonical class in Ext^1_{O_2}(Lg^*NL_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, G_2), Lg^* the derived pullback of 06YY, is zero exactly when a morphism (Sh(C'_2), O'_2) -> (Sh(C'_1), O'_1) fitting into (08UH) compatibly with nu exists

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.pullbackDifferentialsHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The first equality of the display of Stacks 08UG, clause (2)**:
`Hom_{𝒪₁}(Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, g_*𝒢₂) = Hom_{𝒪₂}(g^*Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, 𝒢₂)`, the adjunction `g^* ⊣ g_*` of
sheaves of modules of Stacks 03D7.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackDifferentialsHomEquiv :
    (D.g.toRingedToposModulesHom.pullbackModules.obj (differentials₁ D) ⟶
      (show SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X₂.O) from D.S₂.G)) ≃+
      (differentials₁ D ⟶ pushedIdeal₁ D)
declarations.comment: clause (2), the first equality of the display: Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2) = Hom_{O_2}(g^* Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, G_2), as an additive equivalence, for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.extZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The second equality of the display of Stacks 08UG, clause (2)**:
`Hom_{𝒪₁}(Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, g_*𝒢₂) = Ext⁰_{𝒪₂}(Lg^*NL_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, 𝒢₂)`, as an additive
equivalence: Stacks 0GQ8 in degree `0`, `Ext⁰(NL, 𝒢) = Hom(Ω, 𝒢)` on `𝒞₂`, and the identification
`actingGroupEquiv`. `Lg^*` is the derived pullback of Tag 06YY, at the model
`HasDerivedCategory.standard` at which it is constructed.
declarations.statement:
def extZeroEquiv :
    @DerivedCategory.Ext _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback D.g).obj
        ((@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)).obj
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex.{u, u, u, u} X₁.J
            ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor D.S₁.f.toToposHom).obj B₁.O) X₁.O
            D.S₁.f.fSharpInverseImage)))
      ((@DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) 0).obj D.S₂.G) 0 ≃+
      (differentials₁ D ⟶ pushedIdeal₁ D)
declarations.comment: clause (2), the second equality of the display: Ext^0_{O_2}(Lg^* NL_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, G_2) = Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2), as an additive equivalence, for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.translate_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 08UG**, clause (2): the zero homomorphism acts trivially.
declarations.statement: theorem translate_zero (p : CompatibleLift D) : translate D p 0 = p
declarations.comment: clause (2), for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi: triviality of the action of 0 in the principal homogeneous space structure under Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.translate_add
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 08UG**, clause (2): the action is additive.
declarations.statement:
theorem translate_add (p : CompatibleLift D) (a b : differentials₁ D ⟶ pushedIdeal₁ D) :
    translate D (translate D p a) b = translate D p (a + b)
declarations.comment: clause (2), for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi: additivity of the action in the principal homogeneous space structure under Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram.existsUnique_translate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UG**, clause (2). If there is a morphism of ringed topoi
`(Sh(𝒞'₂), 𝒪'₂) ⟶ (Sh(𝒞'₁), 𝒪'₁)` fitting into (08UH) compatibly with `ν`, the set of all such
morphisms is a principal homogeneous space under `Hom_{𝒪₁}(Ω_{𝒪₁/𝒪_{ℬ₁}}, g_*𝒢₂)`: any one of
them is carried to any other by exactly one homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_translate (p q : CompatibleLift D) :
    ∃! a : differentials₁ D ⟶ pushedIdeal₁ D, translate D p a = q
declarations.comment: clause (2) for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi between four arbitrary ringed topoi: the morphisms fitting into (08UH) compatibly with nu are a principal homogeneous space under Hom_{O_1}(Omega_{O_1/O_{B_1}}, g_* G_2), with the action translate_zero, translate_add

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram
declarations.doc:
**The diagram of first order thickenings of ringed topoi and the diagram (08UI) of their
ideals**, for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi.

* `S₁`, `Q₁` are the front layer: the morphism `f₁ : (Sh(𝒞₁), 𝒪₁) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ₁), 𝒪_{ℬ₁})`, the first
  order thickening `t₁` of the base, with `f₁⁻¹𝒥₁`, the ideal `𝒢₁` of `i₁`, and the front row of
  (08UI), which is a solution of (08UF) — the thickening `𝒪'₁ ⟶ 𝒪₁` with its ideal `𝒢₁` and the
  structure map `f₁⁻¹𝒪_{ℬ'₁} ⟶ 𝒪'₁` of `f'₁`.
* `S₂`, `Q₂` are the back layer, the same data with index `2`.
* `g : (Sh(𝒞₂), 𝒪₂) ⟶ (Sh(𝒞₁), 𝒪₁)` and `h : (Sh(ℬ₂), 𝒪_{ℬ₂}) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ₁), 𝒪_{ℬ₁})` are the two
  oblique arrows of the reduced part, with `f₁ ∘ g = h ∘ f₂`.
* `hB'` is the oblique arrow `h' : (Sh(ℬ'₂), 𝒪_{ℬ'₂}) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ'₁), 𝒪_{ℬ'₁})` of the thickened
  bases; the underlying topoi being identified it induces `h` on the topoi, and it is recorded by
  its comorphism `h⁻¹𝒪_{ℬ'₁} ⟶ 𝒪_{ℬ'₂}`. `hB'_reduction` is `t₁ ∘ h = h' ∘ t₂`.
* `nu` is `ν : g⁻¹𝒢₁ ⟶ 𝒢₂`, linear over `g⁻¹𝒪₁`, and `nu_base` the commutativity of the left
  square of (08UI); see the module docstring.

The faces `f'ⱼ ∘ iⱼ = tⱼ ∘ fⱼ` of (08UH) are part of the solutions `Qⱼ`. The special case
where everything lives on one site, with identity underlying topoi, is
`Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram`.
declarations.statement: structure RingedToposLiftDiagram
declarations.comment: the commutative diagram of morphisms of ringed topoi, for genuine morphisms f₁, f₂, g, h between four arbitrary ringed topoi, each thickening presented on the site of its reduction as in the source's convention

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposLiftDiagram
declarations.doc:
**The diagram of first order thickenings of ringed topoi and the diagram (08UI) of their
ideals**, for genuine morphisms of ringed topoi.

* `S₁`, `Q₁` are the front layer: the morphism `f₁ : (Sh(𝒞₁), 𝒪₁) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ₁), 𝒪_{ℬ₁})`, the first
  order thickening `t₁` of the base, with `f₁⁻¹𝒥₁`, the ideal `𝒢₁` of `i₁`, and the front row of
  (08UI), which is a solution of (08UF) — the thickening `𝒪'₁ ⟶ 𝒪₁` with its ideal `𝒢₁` and the
  structure map `f₁⁻¹𝒪_{ℬ'₁} ⟶ 𝒪'₁` of `f'₁`.
* `S₂`, `Q₂` are the back layer, the same data with index `2`.
* `g : (Sh(𝒞₂), 𝒪₂) ⟶ (Sh(𝒞₁), 𝒪₁)` and `h : (Sh(ℬ₂), 𝒪_{ℬ₂}) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ₁), 𝒪_{ℬ₁})` are the two
  oblique arrows of the reduced part, with `f₁ ∘ g = h ∘ f₂`.
* `hB'` is the oblique arrow `h' : (Sh(ℬ'₂), 𝒪_{ℬ'₂}) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ'₁), 𝒪_{ℬ'₁})` of the thickened
  bases; the underlying topoi being identified it induces `h` on the topoi, and it is recorded by
  its comorphism `h⁻¹𝒪_{ℬ'₁} ⟶ 𝒪_{ℬ'₂}`. `hB'_reduction` is `t₁ ∘ h = h' ∘ t₂`.
* `nu` is `ν : g⁻¹𝒢₁ ⟶ 𝒢₂`, linear over `g⁻¹𝒪₁`, and `nu_base` the commutativity of the left
  square of (08UI); see the module docstring.

The faces `f'ⱼ ∘ iⱼ = tⱼ ∘ fⱼ` of (08UH) are part of the solutions `Qⱼ`. The special case
where everything lives on one site, with identity underlying topoi, is
`Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram`.
declarations.statement: structure RingedToposLiftDiagram
declarations.comment: the commutative diagram of exact ideal rows: the front and back rows are the solutions `Q₁`, `Q₂` of (08UF) (the exact sequences `0 → 𝒢ⱼ → 𝒪'ⱼ → 𝒪ⱼ → 0` over `0 → fⱼ⁻¹𝒥ⱼ → fⱼ⁻¹𝒪_{ℬ'ⱼ} → fⱼ⁻¹𝒪_{ℬⱼ} → 0` with the maps `cⱼ`), the north-north-west arrows are `nu` (a map of `g⁻¹𝒪₁`-modules `g⁻¹𝒢₁ → 𝒢₂`), `g^♯` and the base comparisons through `h` and `hB'`, and the only condition on `nu` is the source's: the left square `ν ∘ g⁻¹c₁ = c₂ ∘ (g⁻¹f₁⁻¹𝒥₁ → f₂⁻¹𝒥₂)` commutes (`nu_base`, stated after the injection `𝒢₂ ⊂ 𝒪'₂` on sections of the base ideal); the remaining squares commute by `comm`, `hB'_reduction` and the solutions' faces

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_presentation_conormalExtClass
declarations.doc:
Let `A ⟶ B` be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on a site, let `G` be a `B`-module and let
`ξ` be a first Ext class of the naive cotangent complex `NL_{B/A}` with values in `G`. Then there
is a map of sheaves of sets `α : E ⟶ B` presenting `B` over `A` for which `ξ`, viewed in
`Ext¹_B(NL(α), G)` along the canonical comparison map, is the class of a homomorphism `I/I² ⟶ G`
out of the conormal sheaf of the presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_presentation_conormalExtClass
    (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, max w u v, w} J A B a))
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj G) 1) :
    ∃ (E : Sheaf J (Type (max w u v))) (α : E.obj ⟶ underlyingPresheaf J B)
      (hsurj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (presentation J A B a E.obj α).hom),
      letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (presentation J A B a E.obj α).hom := hsurj
      ∃ f : (presentationConormalSequence.{v, u, max w u v, w} J A B a E.obj α).X₁ ⟶ G,
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (naiveCotangentComplexComparison.{v, u, max w u v, w} J A B a E.obj α) ≫ ξ =
          presentationConormalExtClass.{v, u, w, t} J A B a E.obj α G f

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.exists_addTorsor_isomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UK.** For the square-zero extension problem of [Stacks 08UF] — a
first order thickening of `(Sh(ℬ), 𝒪_ℬ)` with ideal `𝒥`, a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(ℬ), 𝒪_ℬ)`, an `𝒪`-module `𝒢` and `c : f⁻¹𝒥 ⟶ 𝒢` — if a solution exists,
then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
`Ext¹_𝒪(NL_{𝒪/𝒪_ℬ}, 𝒢)`.

The structure is the source's: `ξ` carries the class of a solution `𝒪'` to the class of the
pushout solution `𝒪'_ξ` of the proof, and it carries the class of `𝒪'₁` to the class of `𝒪'₂`
exactly when the obstruction class `o(𝒪'₁, 𝒪'₂)` of [Stacks 08UG] is `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addTorsor_isomorphismClasses (S : RingedToposExtensionProblem X B)
    (hne : Nonempty S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening) :
    ∃ T : AddTorsor
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentExt.{u, u, u, u, t} X.J
          ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor S.f.toToposHom).obj B.O) X.O S.f.fSharpInverseImage S.G 1)
        (IsomorphismClasses S),
      (∀ (ξ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentExt.{u, u, u, u, t} X.J
          ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor S.f.toToposHom).obj B.O) X.O S.f.fSharpInverseImage S.G 1)
          (P Q : S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening),
        T.vadd ξ (Quotient.mk (isomorphicSetoid S) P) = Quotient.mk (isomorphicSetoid S) Q ↔
          pairObstruction P Q = ξ) ∧
      ∀ (ξ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentExt.{u, u, u, u, t} X.J
          ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor S.f.toToposHom).obj B.O) X.O S.f.fSharpInverseImage S.G 1)
          (P : S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening),
        T.vadd ξ (Quotient.mk (isomorphicSetoid S) P) =
          Quotient.mk (isomorphicSetoid S) (P.twist ξ)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.isomorphic_iff_nonempty_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UK**, the half asserting that the obstruction class separates the
isomorphism classes of solutions. Two solutions of the square-zero extension problem of
[Stacks Project, Tag 08UF] are isomorphic exactly when there is a *morphism* of solutions
between them: by `CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.Hom.isIso` every morphism of solutions is
already invertible.

This is the source's "clearly, this element is the obstruction to the existence of an
isomorphism, hence separates the isomorphism classes" — the obstruction class of
[Stacks Project, Tag 08UG], which obstructs a morphism `O'₁ ⟶ O'₂` fitting into the diagram
(`Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram.liftingObstruction_eq_zero_iff`), thereby obstructs an
isomorphism of solutions.

The other half of the tag — that the isomorphism classes form a principal homogeneous space
under `Ext¹_O(NL_{O/O_B}, G)` — is **not** claimed here; see the implementation notes of this
file.
declarations.comment: the half asserting that the obstruction class of Stacks 08UG separates the isomorphism classes of solutions, namely that a morphism of solutions of the extension problem of Stacks 08UF is automatically an isomorphism; not the torsor half, which needs the pair-dependent presentation of the source's last paragraph and its omitted calculation

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.isomorphismClasses_mk_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UK**, the half asserting that the obstruction class separates the
isomorphism classes, stated for the set of isomorphism classes itself. Two solutions of the
square-zero extension problem of [Stacks Project, Tag 08UF] have the same class in
`CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.IsomorphismClasses S` exactly when there is a morphism of
solutions between them, so the obstruction class of [Stacks Project, Tag 08UG] — which
obstructs such a morphism — is a complete invariant of the isomorphism class.

That these classes are moreover *principal homogeneous* under
`Ext¹_O(NL_{O/O_B}, G)` is **not** claimed; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isomorphismClasses_mk_eq_iff (P Q : S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening) :
    (Quotient.mk (CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.isomorphicSetoid S) P :
        CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.IsomorphismClasses S) =
      Quotient.mk (CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.isomorphicSetoid S) Q ↔
      Nonempty (CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.Hom P Q)
declarations.comment: the half asserting that the obstruction class of Stacks 08UG separates the isomorphism classes, stated for the quotient `IsomorphismClasses` itself: two solutions have the same isomorphism class exactly when a morphism of solutions joins them; not the torsor half

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram.liftingObstruction_eq_zero_iff_exists_isIso_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UK**, the half asserting that the obstruction class separates the
isomorphism classes, in the vocabulary of the diagram of [Stacks Project, Tag 08UG]. When the
two comparison maps of the diagram are bijective on sections — as they are for two solutions of
one square-zero extension problem, where both are identities — the class of Step 1 of the proof
of Tag 08UG vanishes if and only if there is an *isomorphism* `O'₁ ≅ O'₂` fitting into the
diagram, and not merely a morphism.

This is the source's "clearly, this element is the obstruction to the existence of an
isomorphism, hence separates the isomorphism classes", combined with the vanishing criterion
`Deformation.ToposThickening.LiftDiagram.liftingObstruction_eq_zero_iff` of Tag 08UG, whose
hypotheses `P` and `ξ` are inherited verbatim. That criterion is stated for the factorizations
of `ξ` through the degree `0` term and assumes nothing; the bijection `e` of Steps 1 to 3 of the
source's proof, which identifies those factorizations with the lifts of the diagram, is carried
here.
declarations.statement:
public theorem liftingObstruction_eq_zero_iff_exists_isIso_lift (D : LiftDiagram J)
    {single : M ⥤ T} [single.Full] [single.Faithful] [single.Additive]
    (hg : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Bijective (D.g.hom.app U))
    (hgs : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J D.g.hom)
    (hnu : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Bijective (D.nuSection (U := U)))
    (P : NaiveCotangentTwoTerm single) (G : M) (ξ : P.conormal ⟶ G)
    (e : D.Lift ≃ {θ : P.base ⟶ G // P.d ≫ θ = ξ}) :
    liftingObstruction P G ξ = 0 ↔ ∃ p : D.Lift, IsIso p.hom
declarations.comment: the half asserting that the obstruction class of Stacks 08UG separates the isomorphism classes, stated in the vocabulary of the diagram of that tag: when the two comparison maps of the diagram are bijective on sections the class vanishes exactly when an isomorphism fits into the diagram; the hypotheses carried are those of Stacks 08UG itself, and the torsor half of 08UK is not claimed

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.naiveIsomorphismClassesAddTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08UK**, the torsor half: if the square-zero extension problem has a solution, the
isomorphism classes of solutions are a principal homogeneous space under `Ext¹_O(NL_f, G)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveIsomorphismClassesAddTorsor [Nonempty S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening] :
    AddTorsor (S.f.naiveCotangentExt (targetG S) 1) (IsomorphismClasses S)
declarations.comment: the half asserting that, if a solution exists, the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext¹(NL_f, G); the element separating two classes is their obstruction class

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the identification over the henselized source.** Let `A → A^h` be a
henselization of the local ring `A` and let `C` be an `A^h`-algebra. Then
`L_{C/A} = L_{C/A^h}` in `D(C)`.

This is the first equality of the lemma, at `C = B^h`: the fundamental triangle of the tower
`A → A^h → C` has first vertex `L_{A^h/A} ⊗^𝐋_{A^h} C`, which vanishes because `L_{A^h/A} = 0`,
so its second arrow `L_{C/A} ⟶ L_{C/A^h}` is an isomorphism. Both the henselization `A^h` and a
strict henselization `A^{sh}` are instances of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization`, so the statement
covers the lemma's `resp.` variant as well.
declarations.comment: the FIRST of the lemma's two equalities, `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A}`, and its `resp.` strict variant `L_{B^{sh}/A^{sh}} = L_{B^{sh}/A}` — one statement for both, because the henselization and a strict henselization are the two instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). It is proved for an ARBITRARY `A^h`-algebra `C` in place of `B^h`, which is a generalization of the lemma and not a weakening of it. TWO carried hypotheses: `hT`, the distinguished triangle of Proposition 08QX for the tower `A → A^h → C`, which is not formalized in this library (see the `No @[stacks 08QX]` section of `StacksFrontier.Cotangent.Triangle.Distinguished`), and `hQX`, the family of instances of Proposition 08QX that items (7) and (8) of Stacks 08R2 consume. The source's input `L_{A^h/A} = 0` is NOT carried: it is proved here, as `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived`, which is what makes the henselization hypothesis on `A^h` load-bearing. The lemma's SECOND equality, `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the derived scalar-extension identification.** Let `A → B` be a ring
map, let `B → B^h` be a henselization of the local ring `B`, and let `A → B → B^h` be a tower.
Then `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h` in `D(B^h)`.

This is the second equality of the lemma: the fundamental triangle of the tower `A → B → B^h`
has third vertex `L_{B^h/B}`, which vanishes because `B → B^h` is a henselization, so its first
arrow is an isomorphism. As above, one statement covers the lemma's `resp.` variant.
declarations.comment: the SECOND of the lemma's two equalities, `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, and its `resp.` strict variant `L_{B^{sh}/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^{sh}` — one statement for both, the henselization and a strict henselization being the two instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). TWO carried hypotheses: `hT`, the distinguished triangle of Proposition 08QX for the tower `A → B → B^h`, not formalized in this library, and `hQX`, the family of instances of Proposition 08QX that items (7) and (8) of Stacks 08R2 consume. The source's input `L_{B^h/B} = 0` is NOT carried: it is proved here, as `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived`, so the henselization hypothesis on `B^h` is load-bearing. The lemma's FIRST equality, `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A}`, is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization`. NOTE that the local ring homomorphism `A → B` of the source is not assumed: the conclusion holds for any ring map `A → B` whose target is local, which is a generalization

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the full chain.** Let `A → B` be a ring map of local rings, let
`A → A^h` and `B → B^h` be henselizations, and let `A^h → B^h` be compatible with them. Then
`L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h` in `D(B^h)`, read as an isomorphism
`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h ≅ L_{B^h/A^h}`.

This composes the two identifications above. The `resp.` strict variant is the same statement
at `L_A = κ_A^sep` and `L_B = κ_B^sep`.
declarations.comment: the lemma's full chain `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, read as the isomorphism `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h ≅ L_{B^h/A^h}` in `D(B^h)` obtained by composing the two equalities, together with its `resp.` strict variant — one statement for both, the henselization and a strict henselization being the instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). The induced map `A^h → B^h` is taken as given data (an `A^h`-algebra structure on `B^h` with `IsScalarTower A A^h B^h`) rather than constructed. FOUR carried hypotheses: the two distinguished triangles `hT₁` and `hT₂` of Proposition 08QX, for the towers `A → B → B^h` and `A → A^h → B^h`, Proposition 08QX not being formalized in this library; and `hQXA`, `hQXB`, the families of instances of Proposition 08QX that items (7) and (8) of Stacks 08R2 consume over `A` and over `B`. The source's inputs `L_{A^h/A} = 0` and `L_{B^h/B} = 0` are NOT carried: both are proved, by `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived`, so both henselization hypotheses are load-bearing

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the identification over the henselized source.** Let `A → A^h` be a
henselization of the local ring `A` and let `C` be an `A^h`-algebra. Then
`L_{C/A} = L_{C/A^h}` in `D(C)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization` at the
triangle of the tower `A → A^h → C` that Proposition 08QX provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization_unconditional
    [IsLocalRing A] (L : Type v) [Field L] [Algebra (ResidueField A) L]
    (Ah : Type u) [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah] [IsHenselization A L Ah]
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra Ah C] [IsScalarTower A Ah C] :
    Nonempty (fundamentalVertex₂.{u, u} A C ≅ fundamentalVertex₃.{u, u} Ah C)
declarations.comment: the FIRST of the lemma's two equalities, `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A}`, and its `resp.` strict variant `L_{B^{sh}/A^{sh}} = L_{B^{sh}/A}` — one statement for both, because the henselization and a strict henselization are the two instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). It is proved for an ARBITRARY `A^h`-algebra `C` in place of `B^h`, which is a generalization of the lemma and not a weakening of it. NOTHING is carried: the distinguished triangle of the tower `A → A^h → C` is Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`. The source's input `L_{A^h/A} = 0` is not carried either: it is proved, as `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived_unconditional`, which is what makes the henselization hypothesis on `A^h` load-bearing. The lemma's SECOND equality, `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization_unconditional`

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the derived scalar-extension identification.** Let `A → B` be a ring
map, let `B → B^h` be a henselization of the local ring `B`, and let `A → B → B^h` be a tower.
Then `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h` in `D(B^h)`.

This is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization` at the
triangle of the tower `A → B → B^h` that Proposition 08QX provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₂_henselization_unconditional
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B] (L : Type v) [Field L]
    [Algebra (ResidueField B) L]
    (Bh : Type u) [CommRing Bh] [IsLocalRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh] [IsHenselization B L Bh]
    [Algebra A Bh] [IsScalarTower A B Bh] :
    Nonempty (fundamentalVertex₁.{u, u} A B Bh ≅ fundamentalVertex₂.{u, u} A Bh)
declarations.comment: the SECOND of the lemma's two equalities, `L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, and its `resp.` strict variant `L_{B^{sh}/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^{sh}` — one statement for both, the henselization and a strict henselization being the two instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). NOTHING is carried: the distinguished triangle of the tower `A → B → B^h` is Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`. The source's input `L_{B^h/B} = 0` is not carried either: it is proved, as `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived_unconditional`, so the henselization hypothesis on `B^h` is load-bearing. The lemma's FIRST equality, `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A}`, is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₂_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization_unconditional`. NOTE that the local ring homomorphism `A → B` of the source is not assumed: the conclusion holds for any ring map `A → B` whose target is local, which is a generalization

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 08UN], the full chain.** Let `A → B` be a ring map of local rings, let
`A → A^h` and `B → B^h` be henselizations, and let `A^h → B^h` be compatible with them. Then
`L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h` in `D(B^h)`, read as an isomorphism
`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h ≅ L_{B^h/A^h}`.

This is `CommAlgCat.nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization` at the
triangles of the towers `A → B → B^h` and `A → A^h → B^h` that Proposition 08QX provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fundamentalVertex₁_iso_fundamentalVertex₃_henselization_unconditional
    [IsLocalRing A] (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (LA : Type v) [Field LA] [Algebra (ResidueField A) LA]
    (LB : Type w) [Field LB] [Algebra (ResidueField B) LB]
    (Ah : Type u) [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah] [IsHenselization A LA Ah]
    (Bh : Type u) [CommRing Bh] [IsLocalRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh] [IsHenselization B LB Bh]
    [Algebra A Bh] [IsScalarTower A B Bh] [Algebra Ah Bh] [IsScalarTower A Ah Bh] :
    Nonempty (fundamentalVertex₁.{u, u} A B Bh ≅ fundamentalVertex₃.{u, u} Ah Bh)
declarations.comment: the lemma's full chain `L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h`, read as the isomorphism `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B B^h ≅ L_{B^h/A^h}` in `D(B^h)` obtained by composing the two equalities, together with its `resp.` strict variant — one statement for both, the henselization and a strict henselization being the instances `L = κ` and `L = κ^sep` of `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization` (Stacks 04GQ). The induced map `A^h → B^h` is taken as given data (an `A^h`-algebra structure on `B^h` with `IsScalarTower A A^h B^h`) rather than constructed. NOTHING is carried: the distinguished triangles of the towers `A → B → B^h` and `A → A^h → B^h` are both Proposition 08QX, `CommAlgCat.productFundamentalTriangle_distinguished`. The source's inputs `L_{A^h/A} = 0` and `L_{B^h/B} = 0` are not carried either: both are proved, by `IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived_unconditional`, so both henselization hypotheses are load-bearing

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.explicitNaiveComparison_comp_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** The explicit chain map `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}` of the remark
induces, in `D(B)`, a map inverse to the comparison map `c` of Lemma 08RB: composed with `c` it is
the truncation map `L_{B/A} ⟶ τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}`.  This is the verification the source omits ("We
omit the verification that this is the same as the map of Lemma 92.11.3"), with `c` the tagged map
`Stacks.Cotangent.comparison` of Tag 08R9 at the object `A[B] → B` of `C_{B/A}`.

The proof reduces the equation, by the naturality of `truncGEπ` and the definition of
`Stacks.Cotangent.truncGEConeIso`, to the vanishing of the difference `f ≫ e - ι` in `D(B)` after
`τ_{≥ -1}`; see the module docstring for the route.
declarations.statement:
theorem explicitNaiveComparison_comp_comparison :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map (explicitNaiveComparison A B) ≫
        comparison A B (standardResolutionExtension A B 0)
          (isPolynomialAlgebra_standardResolutionExtension_ring A B 0) =
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-1)).app
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex A B))
declarations.comment: the chain map of the remark induces the comparison map of Lemma 08RB: composed with the map of Tag 08R9 at the object A[B] → B it is the truncation map L_{B/A} → τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A} in D(B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.explicitNaiveComparison_comp_comparisonAtNaive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** The same equation with `Stacks.Cotangent.comparisonAtNaive`,
the comparison map of Lemma 08RB at the spelling `Stacks.Cotangent.conormalExtension A B (op ⦋0⦌)`
of the presentation `A[B] → B`: the two spellings of `NL_{B/A}` differ only by the section of the
augmentation they carry, and `Stacks.Cotangent.naiveSpellingIso` is the isomorphism between them
induced by the identity of `A[B]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem explicitNaiveComparison_comp_comparisonAtNaive :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map (explicitNaiveComparison A B ≫ (naiveSpellingIso A B 0).hom) ≫
        comparisonAtNaive A B =
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-1)).app
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex A B))
declarations.comment: the chain map of the remark induces the comparison map of Lemma 08RB: composed with comparisonAtNaive it is the truncation map L_{B/A} → τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A} in D(B), after the isomorphism naiveSpellingIso identifying the two spellings of NL_{B/A}

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.comparisonComponent_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** Outside cohomological degrees `0` and `-1` the comparison is
zero: the bottom row of the diagram vanishes there, so every downward arrow from
`Ω[Pₙ⁄A] ⊗[Pₙ] B` with `n ≥ 2` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem comparisonComponent_eq_zero (i : ℤ) (h : i ≠ 0) (h' : i ≠ -1) :
    comparisonComponent A B i = 0
declarations.comment:
the comparison vanishes outside degrees 0 and -1, the bottom row being zero
there

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.explicitNaiveComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** The map of complexes `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}` displayed by the
remark: the identity in degree zero, the explicit arrow `d f ⊗ b ↦ (d₀ f - d₁ f) b` in degree
`-1`, and zero above. This is the source's "Hence a map of complexes": the two commuting squares
are `CommAlgCat.core_lower` and `CommAlgCat.core_upper`, and in every other pair of adjacent
degrees the bottom row vanishes.

The agreement of this map with the comparison map `c` of Tag 08RB — the verification the source
omits — is not claimed by this definition; it is
`Stacks.Cotangent.explicitNaiveComparison_comp_comparison` of
`StacksFrontier/Cotangent/NaiveComparisonAgreement.lean`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def explicitNaiveComparison :
    cotangentComplex A B ⟶
      Algebra.Extension.naiveComplex (standardResolutionExtension A B 0)
declarations.comment:
the map of complexes L_{B/A} → NL_{B/A} itself, assembled from the two squares
(the source's `Hence a map of complexes`): the identity in degree 0, the explicit arrow
d f ⊗ b ↦ (d₀ f - d₁ f) b in degree -1, and zero in every other degree

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isIso_comparisonDegreeZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** In degree zero the comparison is an isomorphism: the two rows
of the diagram have the same term `Ω[P₀⁄A] ⊗[P₀] B` there and the downward arrow is the identity
between the two presentations of it.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_comparisonDegreeZero : IsIso (comparisonDegreeZero A B)
declarations.comment:
degree zero: the downward arrow is the identity, hence an isomorphism, the two
rows having the same term there

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.naiveCotangentComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UP.** The downward arrow of the comparison diagram in degree one:
the difference of the two faces `P₁ → P₀`, which lands in the kernel `I` of the augmentation,
read as a map `Ω[P₁⁄A] ⊗[P₁] B → I/I²`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComparison :
    (standardResolutionExtension A B 1).CotangentSpace →ₗ[B]
      (standardResolutionExtension A B 0).Cotangent
declarations.comment:
the explicit downward arrow of the diagram, `d f ⊗ b ↦ (d₀ f - d₁ f) b`, with no
hypothesis beyond the remark's own standard resolution of B over A; well defined by
construction, as the remark's two omitted verifications are discussed in this module's
implementation notes

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.naiveCotangentComparison_tmul
declarations.doc: The arrow sends `d f ⊗ b` to `b` times the class of `d₀ f - d₁ f` in `I/I²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComparison_tmul (b : B)
    (f : (standardResolutionExtension A B 1).Ring) :
    naiveCotangentComparison A B
        (b ⊗ₜ KaehlerDifferential.D A (standardResolutionExtension A B 1).Ring f) =
      b • Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.mk
        ((standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 0).subToKer
          (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 1) f)
declarations.comment: the value of the arrow on a pure differential

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.naiveCotangentComparison_subToKer_coe
declarations.doc: The element of `I` whose class the arrow takes: the difference of the two faces.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComparison_subToKer_coe
    (f : (standardResolutionExtension A B 1).Ring) :
    ((standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 0).subToKer
        (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 1) f).val =
      (standardResolution A B).left.δ (0 : Fin 2) f -
        (standardResolution A B).left.δ (1 : Fin 2) f
declarations.comment: the difference of the two faces, which is the element of `I` the arrow uses

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.naiveCotangentComparison_cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
The lower commuting square of the diagram: following the arrow by the differential
`I/I² → Ω[P₀⁄A] ⊗[P₀] B` of the naive cotangent complex is the differential
`Ω[P₁⁄A] ⊗[P₁] B → Ω[P₀⁄A] ⊗[P₀] B`, the difference of the two faces.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComparison_cotangentComplex :
    (standardResolutionExtension A B 0).cotangentComplex ∘ₗ naiveCotangentComparison A B =
      Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 0) -
        Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 0 1)
declarations.comment: the lower square: compatibility with the differential out of degree one

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.naiveCotangentComparison_faceSum
declarations.doc:
The upper commuting square of the diagram: the arrow annihilates the alternating sum of the
three faces `P₂ → P₁`, which is the differential of the cotangent complex out of degree two.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComparison_faceSum :
    naiveCotangentComparison A B ∘ₗ
        (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 1 0) -
          Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 1 1) +
          Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map (standardResolutionExtensionFace A B 1 2)) = 0
declarations.comment: the upper square: the arrow annihilates the differential into degree one

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
The zeroth homology of the cotangent complex of a morphism of sheaves of
commutative rings on a site is its sheaf of relative differentials, the sheaf of modules
corepresenting the relative derivations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso :
    (cotangentComplex J f).homology 0 ≅
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.derivationsFunctor.{max u v w} A B f).coreprX

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonNegOne_conormalClass
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparisonNegOne_conormalClass (U : Cᵒᵖ)
    (x : (resolutionTerm J f (op ⦋1⦌)).obj.obj U) :
    (naiveComparisonNegOne J f).val.app U
        (((cotangentSimplicialModule J f).universalDerivation (op ⦋1⦌)).d x) =
      conormalClassSection J f U (faceDifference J f U x)
declarations.comment:
the degree `-1` component of the canonical map `L_{B/A} → NL_{B/A}`, with its
value `[d₀ x - d₁ x]` on a pure differential. Hypotheses beyond the source: the naive cotangent
complex is realized as the conormal sequence of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ B` by the degree-zero
term of the standard resolution, and the identification of that presentation with
`Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation` is not carried. The identification of the naive
complex with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}` is NOT proved: the source proves it by comparison
with the chaotic topology, and that comparison is not carried. Tag 08TZ, which it uses, IS
formalized, as `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonNegOne_comp_conormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08US, the lower commuting square.** Following the degree `-1` component by the
differential `I/I² ⟶ B ⊗_{P₀} Ω_{P₀/A}` of the naive cotangent complex is the difference of the
two faces `Ω_{P₁/A} ⊗ B ⇉ Ω_{P₀/A} ⊗ B` followed by the degree-zero component.  The difference
of the two faces is the differential of the cotangent complex out of degree `-1`, so this is the
lower square of the comparison diagram: the differential of the naive complex sends
`[d₀ x - d₁ x]` to `1 ⊗ d(d₀ x - d₁ x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparisonNegOne_comp_conormal :
    naiveComparisonNegOne J f ≫ (naiveSequence J f).f =
      (cotangentSimplicialModule J f).object.δ 0 ≫ naiveComparisonZero J f -
        (cotangentSimplicialModule J f).object.δ 1 ≫ naiveComparisonZero J f
declarations.comment:
the lower commuting square: the degree `-1` component composed with the
differential of the naive cotangent complex is the difference of the two faces composed with the
degree-zero component. Hypotheses beyond the source: the naive cotangent complex is realized as
the conormal sequence of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ B` by the degree-zero term of the standard
resolution, and the differential of `L_{B/A}` appears as the difference of the two face maps of
the base-changed simplicial module rather than transported through
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_degreeIso`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonNegOne_faceSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08US, the upper commuting square.** The degree `-1` component annihilates the
alternating sum of the three faces `Ω_{P₂/A} ⊗ B ⟶ Ω_{P₁/A} ⊗ B`, which is the differential of
the cotangent complex into degree `-1`.  The naive cotangent complex is zero in degree `-2`, so
this is exactly the commutation of the comparison with that differential.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparisonNegOne_faceSum :
    ((cotangentSimplicialModule J f).object.δ (0 : Fin 3) -
        (cotangentSimplicialModule J f).object.δ (1 : Fin 3) +
        (cotangentSimplicialModule J f).object.δ (2 : Fin 3)) ≫
      naiveComparisonNegOne J f = 0
declarations.comment:
the upper commuting square: the degree `-1` component annihilates the alternating
sum of the three faces, which is the differential of `L_{B/A}` into degree `-1`, the naive
cotangent complex being zero in degree `-2`. Hypotheses beyond the source: the naive cotangent
complex is realized as the conormal sequence of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ B` by the degree-zero term
of the standard resolution, and the differential of `L_{B/A}` appears as the alternating sum of
the face maps of the base-changed simplicial module rather than transported through
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_degreeIso`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveCotangentComplexIsoCanonical
declarations.doc:
The naive cotangent complex of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ B` is the naive cotangent complex
`NL_{B/A}` of Tag 08TW, through the isomorphism `P₀ ≅ A[B]` of `A`-algebras over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplexIsoCanonical :
    naiveCotangentComplex.{u, v, w} J f ≅
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, max u v w, u} J A B f
declarations.comment: the naive cotangent complex of the presentation P₀ = A[B] is the naive cotangent complex NL_{B/A} of Tag 08TW

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.canonicalNaiveComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08US, the canonical map.** The canonical map `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}` from the cotangent
complex to the naive cotangent complex of Tag 08TW: `d x ⊗ b ↦ b · [d₀ x - d₁ x]` in degree `-1`
and `d p ⊗ b ↦ b ⊗ d p` in degree `0` (`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparison`), read in
`NL_{B/A}` through the isomorphism `P₀ ≅ A[B]` of `A`-algebras over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalNaiveComparison :
    cotangentComplex.{u, v, w} J f ⟶
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, max u v w, u} J A B f
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_{B/A} → NL_{B/A}`, into the naive cotangent complex
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex` of Tag 08TW

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08US.** The canonical map `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}` into the naive cotangent complex of
Tag 08TW is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every degree `≥ -1`.  Since `NL_{B/A}` has
no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0` (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex_isZero_X`),
this says that the canonical map identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
`τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap (i : ℤ) (hi : -1 ≤ i) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (canonicalNaiveComparison J f) i)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map identifies the naive cotangent complex `NL_{B/A}` of Tag 08TW
with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}`: it is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every
degree `≥ -1`, the naive complex having no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical map of complexes `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}`: it is `d x ⊗ b ↦ b · [d₀ x - d₁ x]` in
degree `-1`, it is `d p ⊗ b ↦ b ⊗ d p` in degree `0`, and it is zero in every other degree, the
naive cotangent complex having no other terms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveComparison :
    cotangentComplex.{u, v, w} J f ⟶ naiveCotangentComplex.{u, v, w} J f
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_{B/A} → NL_{B/A}` as a map of complexes, assembled from the
degreewise comparison and its two squares. Hypotheses beyond the source: the naive cotangent
complex is realized as the conormal sequence of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ B` by the degree-zero term
of the standard resolution, and the identification of that presentation with
`Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation` is not carried

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
If the canonical map `L_{B/A} ⟶ NL_{B/A}` is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaves of
degrees `0` and `-1` (the hypotheses `homologyZeroIsIso` and `homologyNegOneIsIso`), then it is an
isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every degree `≥ -1`. Since the naive cotangent complex has
no cohomology below degree `-1`, this says that the canonical map identifies `NL_{B/A}` with the
truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
    (homologyZeroIsIso :
      IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (naiveComparison.{u, v, w} J f) 0))
    (homologyNegOneIsIso :
      IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (naiveComparison.{u, v, w} J f) (-1)))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : -1 ≤ i) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (naiveComparison.{u, v, w} J f) i)
declarations.comment:
the identification of the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
`τ_{≥ -1} L_{B/A}`, stated as: the canonical map is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of
every degree `≥ -1`, the naive complex having no cohomology below degree `-1` by
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveCotangentComplex_isZero_homology`. Hypotheses carried:
`homologyZeroIsIso` and `homologyNegOneIsIso`, the isomorphisms on `H⁰` and on `H^{-1}`, which
are the final step of the source's proof — the comparison with the chaotic topology, reducing
them to the ring-level map of Tag 08UP and transporting along the inverse-image isomorphism of
Tag 08TZ. That tag IS carried as an isomorphism of complexes,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`; what is not carried is the
comparison with the chaotic topology

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
The cotangent complex `L_{X/S}` of a morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ S`: the cotangent
complex of the morphism of sheaves of commutative rings `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X` on the site of open
subsets of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cotangentComplex (f : X ⟶ S) :
    CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ
declarations.comment: the complex L_f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.cotangentComplexDerived
declarations.doc: `L_{X/S}` regarded as an object of the derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev cotangentComplexDerived (f : X ⟶ S)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))] :
    DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
declarations.comment: the object L_f of the derived category of O_X-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08UV.** The zeroth cohomology of the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed
spaces `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (S, 𝒪_S)` is its sheaf of relative differentials:
`H⁰(L_{X/S}) ≅ Ω_{X/S}`. Both sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules corepresent the relative derivations of
`𝒪_X` over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`, so they are canonically isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso (f : X ⟶ S) :
    (cotangentComplex f).homology 0 ≅ moduleOfDifferentials f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.canonicalNaiveComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_{X/S} ⟶ NL_{X/S}` from the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed
spaces to its naive cotangent complex `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex`: the
canonical map `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.canonicalNaiveComparison` for the morphism of sheaves of
rings `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalNaiveComparison (f : X ⟶ S) :
    cotangentComplex f ⟶ RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex f
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_{X/Y} → NL_{X/Y}`, into the naive cotangent complex
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex` of Tag 08TN; the special case of the map of
Tag 08US

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_{X/S} ⟶ NL_{X/S}` is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every
degree `≥ -1`. Since `NL_{X/S}` has no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex_isZero_X`), the canonical map identifies
the naive cotangent complex with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap (f : X ⟶ S) (i : ℤ) (hi : -1 ≤ i) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (canonicalNaiveComparison f) i)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map identifies the naive cotangent complex `NL_{X/Y}` with the
truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_{X/Y}`: it is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every degree
`≥ -1`, the naive complex having no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0`; the special case of
Tag 08US

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical chain map `L_{X/S} ⟶ NL_{X/S}` of a morphism of ringed spaces:
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparison` at the morphism of sheaves of rings `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveComparison (f : X ⟶ S) :
    cotangentComplex f ⟶ naivePresentationComplex f
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_{X/Y} → NL_{X/Y}` as a morphism of cochain complexes of
sheaves of `O_X`-modules, with both of its components pinned by the lemmas below. Hypotheses
beyond the source: `NL_{X/Y}` is realized as the two-term complex of the conormal sequence of
the presentation `P₀ ⟶ O_X` by the degree-zero term of the standard resolution, whose free
algebra is spelled by `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeAlgebraSheaf`; the identification of that model
with the one of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.naiveCotangentComplex` is not carried. The second
half of the tag, that this map identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
`tau_{>=-1} L_{X/Y}`, is NOT proved and is nowhere assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison_f_negOne
declarations.doc:
The degree `-1` component of the canonical map is the comparison arrow
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonNegOne` for the morphism of sheaves of rings
`f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparison_f_negOne (f : X ⟶ S) :
    (naiveComparison f).f (-1) ≫ (naivePresentationComplexXNegOneIso f).hom =
      (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_degreeIso (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f) 1).hom ≫
        CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonNegOne (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f)
declarations.comment:
the degree `-1` component of the canonical map is the comparison arrow
`Omega_{P_1} ⊗ O_X → I/I²`, so the map is the canonical one. Same hypotheses as
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison_f_zero
declarations.doc:
The degree `0` component of the canonical map is the comparison arrow
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonZero` for the morphism of sheaves of rings `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparison_f_zero (f : X ⟶ S) :
    (naiveComparison f).f 0 ≫ (naivePresentationComplexXZeroIso f).hom =
      (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_degreeIso (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f) 0).hom ≫
        CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparisonZero (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f)
declarations.comment:
the degree `0` component of the canonical map is the comparison arrow
`Omega_{P_0} ⊗ O_X → O_X ⊗ Omega_{P_0}`, so the map is the canonical one. Same hypotheses as
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison_f_negOne_apply
declarations.doc:
On local sections over an open `U` the degree `-1` component of the canonical map sends the
pure differential `d x` of a section `x` of `P₁` to the class of `d₀ x - d₁ x` in `I/I²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparison_f_negOne_apply (f : X ⟶ S) (U : (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ)
    (x : (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.resolutionTerm (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
      (inverseImageStructureMap f) (op ⦋1⦌)).obj.obj U) :
    ((CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentComplex_degreeIso (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f) 1).inv ≫ (naiveComparison f).f (-1) ≫
        (naivePresentationComplexXNegOneIso f).hom).val.app U
        (((CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cotangentSimplicialModule
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f)).universalDerivation (op ⦋1⦌)).d x) =
      CategoryTheory.Sheaf.conormalClassSection (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
        (inverseImageStructureMap f) U
        (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.faceDifference (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
          (inverseImageStructureMap f) U x)
declarations.comment:
the value of the canonical map on local sections in degree `-1`: the pure
differential `d x` goes to the class of `d_0 x - d_1 x` in `I/I²`. Same hypotheses as
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.isIso_homologyMap_naiveComparison_zero
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_{X/S} ⟶ NL_{X/S}` is an isomorphism on the degree-zero cohomology
sheaf, both sides being the sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyMap_naiveComparison_zero (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (naiveComparison f) 0)
declarations.comment:
the degree-zero clause of the second assertion: the canonical map
`L_{X/Y} → NL_{X/Y}` is an isomorphism on the degree-zero cohomology sheaf, both sides being
`Omega_{X/Y}`. `NL_{X/Y}` is realized as the two-term complex of the conormal sequence of the
presentation `P₀ ⟶ O_X` by the degree-zero term of the standard resolution, as for
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceCotangent.naiveComparison`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationSolution
declarations.doc:
A solution of the first order deformation problem for a fixed
first order thickening `t : S ⟶ S'`, morphism `f : X ⟶ S`, `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` and prescribed map
`c : f^* t^* 𝒥 ⟶ 𝒢`: a first order thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` and a morphism `f' : X' ⟶ S'` over
`t`, together with an identification of the ideal of `i` with `𝒢` under which the vertical map
on ideals induced by `f'` is exactly `c`.
declarations.statement:
structure DeformationSolution {X S S' : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (t : S ⟶ S')
    (ht : IsFirstOrderThickening t) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (c : (modulePullback f).obj
      ((modulePullback t).obj (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.idealSheaf t)) ⟶ G)
declarations.comment: the same displayed deformation problem for ringed spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.solutionClassesCotangentAddTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UZ, clause (2).** If there exists a solution of the deformation
problem of **Stacks 08UY**, then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal
homogeneous under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)`, as Mathlib's `AddTorsor`.

The set of isomorphism classes is `SolutionClasses t ht f G c`, the `Quotient` of the solutions
by `Isomorphic`. The structure is the one of **Stacks 08UC** (`solutionClassesAddTorsor`) under
`Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(𝖭𝖫_{X/S}, 𝒢)`, read through the identification
`Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(𝖭𝖫_{X/S}, 𝒢) = Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)` of **Stacks 08UW**
(`naiveExtCotangentAddEquiv`). `hne` is the source's "if there exists a solution".
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def solutionClassesCotangentAddTorsor
    (hne : Nonempty (DeformationSolution t ht f G c)) :
    AddTorsor (cotangentExt f G 1) (SolutionClasses t ht f G c)
declarations.comment: clause (2): if a solution of 08UY exists, the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext¹(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.cotangentObstruction_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UZ, clause (1).** Let `t : S ⟶ S'` be a first order thickening of
ringed spaces with ideal `𝒥`, `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism of ringed spaces, `𝒢` an `𝒪_X`-module and
`c : f^* t^* 𝒥 ⟶ 𝒢` the prescribed map on ideals (the setup of **Stacks 08UY**). The canonical
class `ξ = cotangentObstruction f G ht c ∈ Ext²_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)` vanishes if and only if the
deformation problem (08UY) has a solution.

The proof is the source's: by **Stacks 0GQ3** (realized here through square-zero extensions of
`(f ∘ t)⁻¹𝒪_{S'}`-algebras with bijective ideal, `exists_ideal_bijective_extClass_eq`, and the
correspondence `DeformationSolution.toAlgebraExtension` / `toDeformationSolution` with solutions)
a solution exists exactly when `ξ' = c ∘ κ ∈ Ext¹(L_{A/A'} ⊗_A 𝒪_X, 𝒢)` comes from
`Ext¹(L_{X/S'}, 𝒢) = Ext¹(𝖭𝖫_{X/S'}, 𝒢)` (**Stacks 08UW**), and the long exact sequence of the
distinguished triangle of **Stacks 08T4** identifies those classes with the ones whose image
in `Ext²(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangentObstruction_eq_zero_iff :
    cotangentObstruction f G ht c = 0 ↔ Nonempty (DeformationSolution t ht f G c)
declarations.comment: clause (1): there is a canonical element ξ ∈ Ext²(L_{X/S}, 𝒢) whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence of a solution to (08UY)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.DeformationSolution.solutionAutMulEquivCotangentExt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08UZ, clause (3).** Given a solution `X'` of the deformation problem
of (08UY), the group of automorphisms of `X'` fitting into that diagram is canonically
isomorphic to `Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)`.

The automorphisms in question are the `SolutionHom Q Q`: morphisms of the deformed space under
`X`, over `S'`, and the identity on the prescribed ideal `𝒢`. Every one is invertible by
`SolutionHom.isIso_hom`, so these are the automorphisms of `X'` in the diagram; they form a
group under composition (`SolutionHom.instGroup`, with `SolutionHom.mul_hom`,
`SolutionHom.one_hom`, `SolutionHom.inv_hom`). The isomorphism is a group isomorphism onto the
additive group `Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)`, written multiplicatively. Its underlying bijection is
`solutionHomEquivCotangentExt`: an automorphism is `x ↦ x + δ(x)` for a unique relative
derivation `δ` of `𝒪_X` over `f⁻¹𝒪_S` with values in `𝒢`, and these derivations are
`Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/S}, 𝒢) = Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(L_{X/S}, 𝒢)`. Composition goes to addition because
`(id + δ₁) ∘ (id + δ₂) = id + δ₁ + δ₂`, the ideal having square zero (`toDerivation_mul`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def solutionAutMulEquivCotangentExt :
    SolutionHom Q Q ≃* Multiplicative (cotangentExt f G 0)
declarations.comment: clause (3): the group of automorphisms of a solution X' fitting into (08UY), under composition, is isomorphic to the additive group Ext^0(L_{X/S}, G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V0.** The zeroth homology of the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi
is its sheaf of relative differentials: `H⁰(L_f) = Ω_f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cotangentComplex_homologyZeroIso :
    (f.cotangentComplex).homology 0 ≅ f.differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.exists_distTriang_transitivity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V1.** Let `f : (Sh(C₁), 𝒪₁) ⟶ (Sh(C₂), 𝒪₂)` and `g : (Sh(C₂), 𝒪₂) ⟶ (Sh(C₃), 𝒪₃)`
be morphisms of ringed topoi. The canonical triangle

`Lf^* L_g ⟶ L_{g ∘ f} ⟶ L_f ⟶ Lf^* L_g[1]`

is distinguished in `D(𝒪₁)`. Its first two arrows are `transitivityUnit` and
`transitivityCounit`, those of the fundamental triangle of the tower
`(g ∘ f)⁻¹𝒪₃ = f⁻¹g⁻¹𝒪₃ ⟶ f⁻¹𝒪₂ ⟶ 𝒪₁` of Tag 08SZ; its first vertex is the derived pullback of
`L_g`, which `L_g` being a bounded above complex of flat modules computes degreewise as
`L_{f⁻¹𝒪₂/f⁻¹g⁻¹𝒪₃} ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪₂} 𝒪₁` (Tags 06YY and 08SV).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distTriang_transitivity :
    ∃ δ : G.cotangentComplexDerived ⟶ ((derivedPullback G).obj F.cotangentComplexDerived)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk (transitivityUnit F G) (transitivityCounit F G) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (Sheaf.targetModules.{u, v, w} X.J X.O))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.canonicalNaiveComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V2, the canonical map.** The canonical map `L_f ⟶ NL_f` of a morphism of ringed
topoi `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), 𝒪_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)`, into `NL_f = NL_{𝒪_C/f⁻¹𝒪_D}` of Tag 08TW: the
special case at `f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C` of the map of Tag 08US.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalNaiveComparison :
    f.cotangentComplex ⟶
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex.{v, u, max u v w, u} X.J _ X.O
        f.fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_f → NL_f` of a morphism of ringed topoi, into the naive
cotangent complex `NL_{𝒪_C/f⁻¹𝒪_D}` of Tag 08TW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V2.** The canonical map `L_f ⟶ NL_f` is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of
every degree `≥ -1`; since `NL_f` has no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0`, it identifies the
naive cotangent complex with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalNaiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap (i : ℤ) (hi : -1 ≤ i) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f.canonicalNaiveComparison i)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map identifies the naive cotangent complex `NL_f` with the truncation
`τ_{≥ -1} L_f`: it is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every degree `≥ -1`, the naive
complex having no terms outside degrees `-1` and `0`; the special case of Tag 08US

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_f ⟶ NL_f` from the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi to its
naive cotangent complex: `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.naiveComparison` at the inverse-image form
`f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C` of the structure map. It is `d x ⊗ b ↦ b · [d₀ x - d₁ x]` in degree `-1`, it is
`d p ⊗ b ↦ b ⊗ d p` in degree `0`, and it is zero in every other degree.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def naiveComparison : f.cotangentComplex ⟶ f.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `L_f → NL_f` of a morphism of ringed topoi, as a map of complexes
of sheaves of `𝒪_C`-modules. Hypotheses beyond the source: `NL_f` is realized as the conormal
sequence of the presentation `P₀ ⟶ 𝒪_C` by the degree-zero term of the standard resolution of
`f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C`, and the identification of that presentation with
`Stacks.Sites.FreeAlgebra.canonicalPresentation` is not carried, so the map is not transported to
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplex`. The second assertion of the tag, that this map
identifies `NL_f` with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_f`, is the separate carrier
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
If the canonical map `L_f ⟶ NL_f` is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaves of degrees `0`
and `-1` (the hypotheses `homologyZeroIsIso` and `homologyNegOneIsIso`), then it is an isomorphism
on the cohomology sheaf of every degree `≥ -1`. Since `NL_f` has no cohomology below degree `-1`,
by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveCotangentComplex_isZero_homology`, this says that the
canonical map identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveComparison_isIso_homologyMap
    (homologyZeroIsIso : IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f.naiveComparison 0))
    (homologyNegOneIsIso : IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f.naiveComparison (-1)))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : -1 ≤ i) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f.naiveComparison i)
declarations.comment:
the second assertion of the tag: the canonical map identifies `NL_f` with the
truncation `τ_{≥ -1} L_f`, stated as: it is an isomorphism on the cohomology sheaf of every
degree `≥ -1`, the naive complex having no cohomology below degree `-1` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.naiveCotangentComplex_isZero_homology`. Hypotheses carried:
`homologyZeroIsIso` and `homologyNegOneIsIso`, the isomorphisms on `H⁰` and on `H^{-1}`, which
are the final step of the proof of Tag 08US that this tag is the special case of — the comparison
with the chaotic topology, reducing them to the ring-level map of Tag 08UP and transporting along
the inverse-image isomorphism of Tag 08TZ. That tag IS carried as an isomorphism of complexes,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`; what is not carried is the
comparison with the chaotic topology

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.ArbitrarySiteExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08UF on arbitrary equivalent sites.** A solution of the extension problem on a given
thickened source ringed topos `X'`. The displayed diagram of sheaves is pulled back along the
equivalence underlying `i`, and the invertible 2-morphism records the morphism of thickenings.
declarations.statement:
public structure CompatibleFirstOrderThickening
    (S : ArbitrarySiteExtensionProblem X B B')
    (X' : RingedTopos.{v''', u''', w'''})
    [X'.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w'''})]
    [X'.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w'''} RingCat.{w'''})]
declarations.comment: the same square-zero extension problem, as stated in the Cotangent chapter

registrations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening
registrations.comment: the displayed diagram, same-site presentation

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.nonempty_iff_obstructionClass_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V5 (1)**: a solution of the square-zero extension problem exists if and only if
the obstruction class in `Ext²_O(L_f, G)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iff_obstructionClass_eq_zero :
    Nonempty S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening ↔ S.obstructionClass = 0
declarations.comment: (1): the element `obstructionClass` of `Ext²_O(L_f, G)`, the image of the class of `c` under the connecting morphism of the fundamental triangle of `f⁻¹O_{B'} → f⁻¹O_B → O`, vanishes exactly when a solution exists

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.autEquivDerivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08V5, clause (3).** The automorphisms of a solution of the square-zero
extension problem of [Stacks Project, Tag 08V4] fitting into that diagram are canonically
bijective to the derivations of that solution — section-wise maps from its thickened structure
sheaf to the prescribed module `G` satisfying the Leibniz rule and vanishing on `G` and on the
image of `f⁻¹O_{B'}`. With `autEquivDerivation_mul` this is an isomorphism of groups.

The source writes the group as `Ext⁰_O(L_f, G)`; that identification is **not** proved here, and
the three steps separating the two readings are recorded in the implementation notes of this
file.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def autEquivDerivation (P : S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening) :
    P.AutomorphismGroup ≃ Derivation P
declarations.comment: clause (3), the automorphism group of a solution, computed for the concrete group of section-wise derivations of the solution rather than Ext⁰_O(L_f, G); that identification is not proved, as in the library's Stacks 08UG and Stacks 08UK

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.autEquivDerivation_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08V5, clause (3).** The canonical bijection between the automorphisms
of a solution and the derivations of that solution is an isomorphism of groups: composition of
automorphisms is addition of derivations.
declarations.comment: clause (3), that the canonical bijection of `autEquivDerivation` between the automorphisms of a solution and its section-wise derivations is a group isomorphism; the group is not identified with Ext⁰_O(L_f, G), as in the library's Stacks 08UG and Stacks 08UK

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.autMulEquivExtZero
declarations.doc:
Given a solution `P` of a square-zero extension problem of ringed topoi, the group of
automorphisms of `P` fitting into the diagram of the problem is canonically isomorphic to
`Ext⁰_O(L_f, G)`: an automorphism `a` goes to the class whose degree-zero homology
`Ω_f = H⁰(L_f) ⟶ G` sends `d(x mod G)` to the section of `G` by which `a(x)` differs from `x`;
composition of automorphisms goes to addition of classes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def autMulEquivExtZero :
    P.AutomorphismGroup ≃* Multiplicative (S.f.cotangentExt (targetG S) 0)
declarations.comment: clause (3): given a solution, its automorphisms fitting into the diagram of 08V4 form a group canonically isomorphic to Ext⁰_O(L_f, G)

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.RingedToposExtensionProblem.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.isomorphismClassesAddTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08V5**, clause (2): if the square-zero extension problem has a solution, the
isomorphism classes of solutions are a principal homogeneous space under `Ext¹_O(L_f, G)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isomorphismClassesAddTorsor [Nonempty S.CompatibleFirstOrderThickening] :
    AddTorsor (S.f.cotangentExt (targetG S) 1) (IsomorphismClasses S)
declarations.comment: clause (2): if a solution exists, the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext¹(L_f, G); the element separating two classes is the image of their obstruction class under Ext¹(NL_f, G) = Ext¹(L_f, G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeOverRing.constantComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison `L_{𝒪_X/Λ̲} ⟶ L_{X/Spec Λ}`: the change-of-base-ring map of the tower
`Λ̲ ⟶ p⁻¹𝒪_{Spec Λ} ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement: def constantComparison : cotangentComplexConstant Λ p ⟶ cotangentComplexRelative Λ p
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison L_{O_X/const Lambda} ⟶ L_{X/Spec Lambda} of the tag, constructed unconditionally as the change-of-base arrow of Tag 08SZ for the tower const Lambda ⟶ p^-1 O_{Spec Lambda} ⟶ O_X, with the constant sheaf being Mathlib's constantSheaf and the target the cotangent complex of p of Tag 08UU (cotangentComplexRelative_eq). That it is an ISOMORPHISM is NOT claimed by this declaration; see isIso_constantComparison_iff and the module documentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeOverRing.isIso_constantComparison_iff
declarations.doc:
Granted the short exact sequence Tag 08SZ carries for the tower `Λ̲ ⟶ p⁻¹𝒪_{Spec Λ} ⟶ 𝒪_X`, the
canonical comparison `L_{𝒪_X/Λ̲} ⟶ L_{X/Spec Λ}` is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_X)` exactly when the
first vertex `L_{p⁻¹𝒪_{Spec Λ}/Λ̲} ⊗_{p⁻¹𝒪_{Spec Λ}} 𝒪_X` of the fundamental triangle vanishes
there.

The hypothesis carried is the one Tag 08SZ carries, in the same shape: a short complex `S` of
complexes of sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules that is short exact (`hS`), whose three terms are the three
vertices (`e₁`, `e₂`, `e₃`) and whose two maps are the two canonical arrows (`hf`, `hg`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_constantComparison_iff
    [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.targetModules.{u, u, u}
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (structureSheafOfSite X))]
    (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex
      (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.targetModules.{u, u, u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X)
        (structureSheafOfSite X)) ℤ))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (e₁ : S.X₁ ≅ pullbackCotangentComplex Λ p)
    (e₂ : S.X₂ ≅ cotangentComplexConstant Λ p)
    (e₃ : S.X₃ ≅ cotangentComplexRelative Λ p)
    (hf : S.f = e₁.hom ≫ CategoryTheory.Sheaf.towerCotangentBaseChange.{u, u, u}
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (constantToPullback Λ p)
      (pullbackStructureMap Λ p) ≫ e₂.inv)
    (hg : S.g = e₂.hom ≫ constantComparison Λ p ≫ e₃.inv) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := CategoryTheory.Sheaf.targetModules.{u, u, u}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (structureSheafOfSite X))).map
        (constantComparison Λ p)) ↔
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := CategoryTheory.Sheaf.targetModules.{u, u, u}
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (structureSheafOfSite X))).obj
          (pullbackCotangentComplex Λ p))
declarations.comment: the REDUCTION of the tag, not the tag: an IFF between the comparison being an isomorphism in D(O_X) and the vanishing of the first vertex of the fundamental triangle, the pullback of the source's L_q. The vanishing -- the source's Tag 08T0 plus Tag 08R2 step -- is NOT proved here and is not assumed either; it is the right-hand side. ONE carried hypothesis, exactly the one Tag 08SZ carries: the short exact sequence `S`/`hS` realizing the two canonical arrows (`hf`, `hg`) on the three vertices (`e1`, `e2`, `e3`), the sheaf-level analogue of Tag 08SD, absent from this library. See the module documentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeOverRing.isIso_constantComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08V6.** Let `Λ` be a ring and let `X` be a scheme over `Λ`. Then
`L_{X/Spec Λ} = L_{𝒪_X/Λ̲}` in `D(𝒪_X)`, where `Λ̲` is the constant sheaf with value `Λ` on `X`:
the canonical comparison `L_{𝒪_X/Λ̲} ⟶ L_{X/Spec Λ}`, the change-of-base map of the tower
`Λ̲ ⟶ p⁻¹𝒪_{Spec Λ} ⟶ 𝒪_X`, is an isomorphism in the derived category.
declarations.comment: L_{X/Spec Lambda} = L_{O_X/const Lambda} in D(O_X) for a scheme X over a ring Lambda, const Lambda the constant sheaf with value Lambda on X: the canonical comparison L_{O_X/const Lambda} ⟶ L_{X/Spec Lambda} (constantComparison) is an isomorphism in D(O_X)

structure PolynomialChart (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] (X : Scheme.{u})
