declarations.name: Module.isInjectiveHull_fractionRing
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion of a domain into its fraction field is an injective hull.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInjectiveHull_fractionRing
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] :
    let M : Submodule R K := (Algebra.linearMap R K).range
    let i : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ ModuleCat.of R K :=
      ModuleCat.ofHom M.subtype
    letI : Mono i :=
      (ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective i).2 M.injective_subtype
    IsInjectiveHull i

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Indecomposable
registrations.comment: for any category with zero morphisms and binary biproducts, e.g. an additive category

declarations.name: Module.Subobject.isInjectiveHull_arrow_of_indecomposable
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of any nonzero submodule of an indecomposable injective module exhibits the
ambient module as its injective hull.
declarations.statement:
lemma Subobject.isInjectiveHull_arrow_of_indecomposable
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] (E : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective E]
    (hE : Indecomposable E) (M : Subobject E) (hM : M ≠ ⊥) :
    IsInjectiveHull M.arrow
declarations.comment: injective_hull

declarations.name: Module.Subobject.inf_ne_bot_of_indecomposable_injective
declarations.doc: Two nonzero submodules of an indecomposable injective module have nonzero intersection.
declarations.statement:
lemma Subobject.inf_ne_bot_of_indecomposable_injective (R : Type u) [Ring R]
    (E : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective E] (hE : Indecomposable E)
    (A B : Subobject E) (hA : A ≠ ⊥) (hB : B ≠ ⊥) : A ⊓ B ≠ ⊥
declarations.comment: nonzero_intersection

declarations.name: Module.endomorphismRing_isLocalRing
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism ring of an indecomposable injective module is a (possibly
noncommutative) local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem endomorphismRing_isLocalRing
    {R : Type u} {E : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    [Module.Injective R E]
    (hE : Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R E)) :
    IsLocalRing (Module.End R E)
declarations.comment: endomorphism_ring_local

declarations.name: Module.exists_maximalIdeal_endomorphismRing
declarations.doc:
The maximal two-sided ideal of the endomorphism ring consists exactly of the
endomorphisms with nonzero kernel, and every endomorphism outside it is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_maximalIdeal_endomorphismRing
    {R : Type u} {E : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    [Module.Injective R E]
    (hE : Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R E)) :
    ∃ I : Ideal (Module.End R E), I.IsTwoSided ∧ I.IsMaximal ∧
      (∀ φ : Module.End R E, φ ∈ I ↔ LinearMap.ker φ ≠ ⊥) ∧
      (∀ φ : Module.End R E, φ ∉ I → IsUnit φ)
declarations.comment: endomorphism_ring_local

declarations.name: Module.exists_prime_eq_zeroDivisorsOn
declarations.doc:
The set of zerodivisors on an indecomposable injective module is the underlying set of a prime
ideal.
declarations.comment: zero_divisors_prime

declarations.name: Module.exists_injective_localizationAtPrime_module
declarations.doc:
An indecomposable injective module is an injective module over the localization at its prime
ideal of zerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_localizationAtPrime_module
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (E : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective E]
    (hE : Indecomposable E) (p : Ideal R) (hp : p.IsPrime)
    (hpE : (p : Set R) = {r : R | ∃ m : E, m ≠ 0 ∧ r • m = 0}) :
    ∃ moduleStructure : Module (Localization.AtPrime p) E,
      letI := moduleStructure
      (∀ (r : R) (x : E), algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p) r • x = r • x) ∧
        CategoryTheory.Injective (ModuleCat.of (Localization.AtPrime p) E)
declarations.comment: injective_over_localization

declarations.name: Module.exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_localization
declarations.doc:
The injective hull of `R ⧸ p` is naturally an injective hull of the residue field at `p` over
`Rₚ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_localization
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} R) (i : ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ p) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : IsInjectiveHull i) :
    ∃ moduleStructure : Module (Localization.AtPrime p) E,
      letI := moduleStructure
      ∃ tower : IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime p) E,
        letI := tower
        ∃ j : ModuleCat.of (Localization.AtPrime p) p.ResidueField ⟶
            ModuleCat.of (Localization.AtPrime p) E,
          ∃ monoJ : Mono j,
            letI := monoJ
            ModuleCat.ofHom
                ((LinearMap.restrictScalars R j.hom).comp
                  (LinearMap.restrictScalars R
                    (Algebra.linearMap (R ⧸ p) p.ResidueField))) = i ∧
              IsInjectiveHull j
declarations.comment: localized_hull

declarations.name: Module.exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_of_quotient
declarations.doc:
An injective hull of the quotient by a prime ideal is also an injective hull of the prime's
residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_of_quotient
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (E : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (R ⧸ p)) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : IsInjectiveHull i) :
    ∃ (j : ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} p.ResidueField) ⟶ E) (_ : Mono j),
      IsInjectiveHull j
declarations.comment: hull_of_residue_field

declarations.name: Module.indecomposable_of_isInjectiveHull_quotient
declarations.doc: The injective hull of the quotient by a prime ideal is indecomposable.
declarations.statement:
theorem indecomposable_of_isInjectiveHull_quotient
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    {E : ModuleCat.{max v u} R}
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (R ⧸ p)) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : IsInjectiveHull i) : Indecomposable E
declarations.comment: indecomposable

declarations.name: Module.exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_of_indecomposable
declarations.doc:
An indecomposable injective module over a Noetherian ring is an injective hull of the residue
field at some prime ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInjectiveHull_residueField_of_indecomposable
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (E : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective E] (hE : Indecomposable E) :
    ∃ (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (K : ModuleCat.{v} R),
      Nonempty (K ≃ₗ[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∧
        ∃ (i : K ⟶ E) (_ : Mono i), IsInjectiveHull i

declarations.name: Module.exists_iso_directSum_of_injective
declarations.doc:
An injective module over a Noetherian ring is isomorphic to a direct sum of indecomposable
injective modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_directSum_of_injective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective I] :
    ∃ (ι : Type v) (E : ι → ModuleCat.{v} R)
      (_ : I ≅ ModuleCat.of R (⨁ i, E i)),
      (∀ i, CategoryTheory.Injective (E i)) ∧ (∀ i, Indecomposable (E i))
declarations.comment: direct sum decomposition

declarations.name: Module.exists_residueField_injectiveHull
declarations.doc:
An indecomposable injective module over a Noetherian ring is an injective hull of the residue
field at a prime ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_residueField_injectiveHull
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (E : ModuleCat.{v} R) [CategoryTheory.Injective E] (hE : Indecomposable E) :
    ∃ (p : Ideal R) (hp : p.IsPrime),
      letI := hp
      ∃ (K : ModuleCat.{v} R) (_ : K ≃ₗ[R] p.ResidueField)
        (i : K ⟶ E) (hi : Mono i),
        letI := hi
        IsInjectiveHull i
declarations.comment: indecomposable injective modules

declarations.name: tensorHomAdjEquiv

**Stacks 08YQ**: `Hom_R(M ⊗_S N, P) = Hom_S(M, Hom_R(N, P))` for `S`-modules `M`, `N` and an
`R`-module `P`.

Stated `S`-linearly rather than as a bare bijection: both sides carry the source `S`-action —
the left through `M ⊗_S N`, the right through `Hom_R(N, P)` — so `S` is the finer structure and
`R`-linearity is its restriction. This matches how Mathlib states the sibling tag 05DQ, where
`LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv` is linear over the *bigger* ring.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedChangeOfRings.derivedTensorModuleStructuresDiffer
declarations.doc:
In the example `R = k[x,y]`, `A = R/(xy)`, and `N = R/(x)`, the objects
`N_R ⊗_R^ᴸ A` and `N ⊗_R^ᴸ A_R` of `D(A)` are not isomorphic. The returned data
includes the two displayed K-flat resolutions and augmentations, their quasi-isomorphism
certificates, and the canonical identifications with `A → A` and `N[1] ⊕ N`.
declarations.statement:

    (k : Type u) [CommRing k] [Nontrivial k] :
    DerivedTensorComparison k

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.IteratedChangeOfRings.derivedTensorProduct_doubleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Canonical associativity of derived change of rings, with its signed interchange. The
ordinary maps send `(x ⊗ n) ⊗ k` to `x ⊗ (n ⊗ k)` and to `(-1)^(deg n * deg k) (x ⊗ k) ⊗ n`,
respectively. These equations and the specified counits of `DerivedTensorChangeOfRings` fix the
derived comparisons, including for nonflat `N` and `K`.

`rightFactor` identifies the complex used by `together` with `N ⊗ᴸ_B K`;
`baseFactor` identifies the second signed factor with `N ⊗ᴸ_B C`. The final isomorphism
to extension of scalars followed by tensoring is exactly the change-of-rings projection.
All comparisons are natural in the object of `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorProduct_doubleBaseChange
    {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {C : Type uC} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C)
    (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} B) ℤ)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} C) ℤ) :
    let Q_A := DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} A)
    let Q_B := DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} B)
    let Q_C := DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} C)
    let W_A := HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
      (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let PN := CochainComplex.KFlat.chosenResolution.{uB, max v uA uC} N
    let LK := CochainComplex.KFlat.chosenResolution.{uC, max v uA uB} K
    let AN := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uA, uB, max v uA uB uC} f N
    let AP := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uA, uB, max v uA uB uC} f PN.complex
    let BK := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uB, uC, max v uA uB uC} g K
    let BL := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uB, uC, max v uA uB uC} g LK.complex
    let AC := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uA, uC, max v uA uB uC}
      (g.comp f) (BL.directTensor.obj PN.complex)
    let AL := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uA, uC, max v uA uB uC}
      (g.comp f) LK.complex
    let AK := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uA, uC, max v uA uB uC} (g.comp f) K
    let CP := canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{uC, uC, max v uA uB uC}
      (RingHom.id C)
      ((extendScalarsLarge.{max v uA uB uC, uB, uC} g).obj PN.complex)
    let iterated := AN.F ⋙ BK.F
    let together := AC.F
    let signed := AK.F ⋙ CP.F
    ∃ (replaceN : AP.F ≅ AN.F) (replaceK : BL.F ≅ BK.F) (replaceAK : AL.F ≅ AK.F),
      replaceN.hom = AP.map AN PN.π ∧
      replaceK.hom = BL.map BK LK.π ∧
      replaceAK.hom = AL.map AK LK.π ∧
      ∃ (rightFactor : BK.F.obj (Q_B.obj N) ≅ Q_C.obj (BL.directTensor.obj PN.complex))
        (baseFactor : BK.B.obj (Q_B.obj N) ≅
          Q_C.obj ((extendScalarsLarge.{max v uA uB uC, uB, uC} g).obj PN.complex)),
        BL.F.map (Q_B.map PN.π) ≫ replaceK.hom.app (Q_B.obj N) ≫ rightFactor.hom =
          BL.alphaF.app PN.complex ∧
        BK.B.map (Q_B.map PN.π) ≫ baseFactor.hom = BK.alphaB.app PN.complex ∧
        ∃ (ordinaryAssociator : AP.directTensor ⋙ BL.directTensor ≅ AC.directTensor)
          (ordinaryInterchange : AP.directTensor ⋙ BL.directTensor ≅
            AL.directTensor ⋙ CP.directTensor),
          (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} A) ℤ)
              (i j k : ℤ) (x : M.X i) (n : PN.complex.X j) (l : LK.complex.X k),
            (ordinaryAssociator.hom.app M).f ((i + j) + k)
                (BL.tensorElement (AP.directTensor.obj M) (i + j) k ((i + j) + k) rfl
                  (AP.tensorElement M i j (i + j) rfl x n) l) =
              AC.tensorElement M i (j + k) ((i + j) + k) (by omega) x
                (BL.tensorElement PN.complex j k (j + k) rfl n l)) ∧
          (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB uC} A) ℤ)
              (i j k : ℤ) (x : M.X i) (n : PN.complex.X j) (l : LK.complex.X k),
            (ordinaryInterchange.hom.app M).f ((i + j) + k)
                (BL.tensorElement (AP.directTensor.obj M) (i + j) k ((i + j) + k) rfl
                  (AP.tensorElement M i j (i + j) rfl x n) l) =
              (-1 : C) ^ (j * k).natAbs •
                CP.tensorElement (AL.directTensor.obj M) (i + k) j ((i + j) + k)
                  (by omega) (AL.tensorElement M i k (i + k) rfl x l)
                  ((1 : C) ⊗ₜ[B,g] n)) ∧
          let replaceIterated := Functor.isoWhiskerRight replaceN BL.F ≪≫
            Functor.isoWhiskerLeft AN.F replaceK
          let replaceSigned := Functor.isoWhiskerRight replaceAK CP.F
          let direct := (AP.directTensor ⋙ BL.directTensor) ⋙ Q_C
          let iteratedComparison : Q_A ⋙ iterated ⟶ direct :=
            Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A replaceIterated.inv ≫ compositeCounit.{uA, uB, uC, v} AP BL
          let togetherComparison : Q_A ⋙ together ⟶ direct :=
            AC.alphaF ≫ Functor.whiskerRight ordinaryAssociator.inv Q_C
          let signedCounit := Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A replaceSigned.inv ≫
            compositeCounit.{uA, uC, uC, max v uB} AL CP
          iterated.IsLeftDerivedFunctor iteratedComparison W_A ∧
          together.IsLeftDerivedFunctor togetherComparison W_A ∧
          ∃ (doubleBaseChange : iterated ≅ together)
            (signedComparison : iterated ≅ signed)
            (baseChangeComparison : iterated ≅ AC.B ⋙ AC.G),
            Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A doubleBaseChange.hom ≫ togetherComparison =
              iteratedComparison ∧
            (∀ e : iterated ≅ together,
              Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A e.hom ≫ togetherComparison = iteratedComparison →
                e = doubleBaseChange) ∧
            Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A signedComparison.hom ≫ signedCounit =
              iteratedComparison ≫ Functor.whiskerRight ordinaryInterchange.hom Q_C ∧
            (∀ e : iterated ≅ signed,
              Functor.whiskerLeft Q_A e.hom ≫ signedCounit =
                iteratedComparison ≫ Functor.whiskerRight ordinaryInterchange.hom Q_C →
                  e = signedComparison) ∧
            baseChangeComparison = doubleBaseChange ≪≫ AC.changeOfRings

declarations.name: Module.Injective.of_isEpi
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be an epimorphism of rings and let `E` be an `S`-module. If `E` is injective as
an `R`-module, then `E` is an injective `S`-module.

An `S`-linear map into `E` out of an `S`-module is in particular `R`-linear, so it extends
`R`-linearly along an injective `S`-linear map, and that extension is `S`-linear because
`R → S` is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Injective.of_isEpi (R : Type*) {S E : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsEpi R S] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] [Module S E]
    [IsScalarTower R S E] (h : Module.Injective R E) : Module.Injective S E

declarations.name: Dualizing.injectiveHullDual_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08YZ.** The `E`-valued duality preserves finite limits, hence takes
finite colimits of finite modules to finite limits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injectiveHullDual_preservesFiniteLimits :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (injectiveHullDual R E i hi)

declarations.name: Dualizing.injectiveHullDual_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08YZ.** The `E`-valued duality preserves finite colimits, hence takes
finite limits of finite modules to finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injectiveHullDual_preservesFiniteColimits :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (injectiveHullDual R E i hi)
declarations.comment: exactness: colimits

declarations.name: Dualizing.injectiveHullDualEvaluation_isIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical evaluation maps give a natural isomorphism from the
identity functor to the square of the `E`-valued duality.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injectiveHullDualEvaluation_isIso :
    IsIso (injectiveHullDualEvaluation R E i hi)
declarations.comment: canonical double-dual identification

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualTorsionEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z0.** Restricting a functional to the elements of `M` killed by `I`
induces the canonical identification of the quotient of the dual of `M` by `I` with the dual of
that submodule.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualTorsionEquiv
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (E : Type v) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] [Module.Injective R (ULift.{u} E)]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) :
    { e : ((M →ₗ[R] E) ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R (M →ₗ[R] E)))) ≃ₗ[R]
        (Submodule.torsionBySet R M (I : Set R) →ₗ[R] E) //
      ∀ f : M →ₗ[R] E,
        e (Submodule.Quotient.mk f) =
          f.comp (Submodule.subtype (Submodule.torsionBySet R M (I : Set R))) }
declarations.comment: the dual of ideal torsion

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualQuotientEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z0.** Precomposing with the quotient map identifies the dual of
`M / I M` with the submodule of functionals on `M` killed by `I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualQuotientEquiv
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (E : Type v) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) :
    { e : ((M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) →ₗ[R] E) ≃ₗ[R]
        Submodule.torsionBySet R (M →ₗ[R] E) (I : Set R) //
      ∀ (f : (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) →ₗ[R] E) (m : M),
        (e f : M →ₗ[R] E) m = f (Submodule.Quotient.mk m) }
declarations.comment: the dual of the quotient by an ideal

declarations.name: Dualizing.isInjectiveHull_kernelTorsion_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z2.** For a surjective ring homomorphism, the
submodule of an injective hull annihilated by the kernel is an injective hull
over the quotient ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInjectiveHull_kernelTorsion_of_surjective
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    {K : ModuleCat.{w} S} {E : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (i : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{w} f).obj K ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    Module.IsInjectiveHull (kernelTorsionInclusion f hf i)

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_injective_to_pi_injectiveHull
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z3.** A module which is power-torsion for the maximal ideal embeds
in the direct sum of as many copies of an injective hull of the residue field as the dimension
of its socle.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_injective_to_pi_injectiveHull
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type v) (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ⟶ ModuleCat.of R E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i)
    (hM : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ^ e : Ideal R),
      r • x = 0)
    (n : ℕ)
    [Module.Finite (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (Submodule.torsionBySet R M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))]
    (hn : Module.finrank (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (Submodule.torsionBySet R M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) = n) :
    ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] (Fin n → E), Function.Injective f

declarations.name: Dualizing.maximalIdealPowTorsion_isInjectiveHull
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z4.** The submodule of an injective hull of the residue field
annihilated by a positive power of the maximal ideal is an injective hull over the corresponding
quotient ring. This is the canonical realization of the source's equality
`E_n = E[𝔪^(n + 1)]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem maximalIdealPowTorsion_isInjectiveHull
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (K E : ModuleCat.{v} R) (e : IsLocalRing.ResidueField R ≃ₗ[R] K)
    (i : K ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hE : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) (n : ℕ) :
    let hK := residueFieldModelIsTorsionByMaximalIdealPow R K e n
    letI := hK.module
    let j := residueFieldToMaximalIdealPowTorsion R e i n
    letI : Mono (ModuleCat.ofHom j) :=
      (ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).2
        (residueFieldToMaximalIdealPowTorsion_injective R e i
          ((ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective i).1 (by infer_instance)) n)
    Module.IsInjectiveHull (ModuleCat.ofHom j)
declarations.comment: the submodules E_n

declarations.name: Dualizing.iSup_maximalIdealPowTorsion_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z4.** The submodules annihilated by positive powers of the maximal
ideal exhaust an injective hull of the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iSup_maximalIdealPowTorsion_eq_top
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (K E : ModuleCat.{v} R) (e : IsLocalRing.ResidueField R ≃ₗ[R] K)
    (i : K ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hE : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    (⨆ n : ℕ, maximalIdealPowTorsion R E n) = ⊤
declarations.comment: the union

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_iso_injectiveHull_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z5.** Injective hulls of the residue fields of a
flat local homomorphism with trivial closed fibre agree after restriction of
scalars.  The comparison isomorphism extends the induced identification of
residue fields.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_injectiveHull_residueField
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    (hflat : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap R S))
    (hclosed : Function.Bijective (closedFiberMap R S))
    {E_R : ModuleCat.{u} R} {E_S : ModuleCat.{u} S}
    (i_R : ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R) ⟶ E_R)
    (i_S : ModuleCat.of S (ResidueField S) ⟶ E_S)
    [Mono i_R] [Mono i_S]
    (hR : Module.IsInjectiveHull i_R)
    (hS : Module.IsInjectiveHull i_S) :
    ∃ e : E_R ≅ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj E_S,
      i_R ≫ e.hom = residueFieldMap R S ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).map i_S

declarations.name: Dualizing.endAlgEquivAdicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z6.** The endomorphism ring of an injective hull of
the residue field of a Noetherian local ring is canonically isomorphic to its
completion.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def endAlgEquivAdicCompletion
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ⟶ ModuleCat.of R E)
    [Mono i] (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    Module.End R E ≃ₐ[R] AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R

declarations.name: Dualizing.isArtinian_of_isInjectiveHull_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z7.** An injective hull of the residue field of a
Noetherian local ring is an Artinian module.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isArtinian_of_isInjectiveHull_residueField
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) ⟶ ModuleCat.of R E)
    [Mono i] (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    IsArtinian R E

declarations.name: Dualizing.isNoetherian_iff_module_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z8, part (1).** Over a Noetherian ring, the ascending chain condition
on submodules is equivalent to finite generation.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isNoetherian_iff_module_finite (R : Type u) [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsNoetherian R M ↔ Module.Finite R M
declarations.comment: part (1): ascending chain condition and finite generation

declarations.name: Dualizing.module_finite_iff_exists_finite_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z8, part (1).** A finite module over a Noetherian ring admits a
presentation by two finite free modules.
declarations.statement:
public lemma module_finite_iff_exists_finite_presentation
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Finite R M ↔
      ∃ (n m : ℕ) (f : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (g : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ Function.Exact g f
declarations.comment: part (1): finite presentation

declarations.name: Dualizing.isArtinian_iff_powerTorsion_and_finiteSocle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z8, part (2).** A module has the descending chain condition exactly
when it is maximal-ideal-power torsion and has finite-dimensional socle.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isArtinian_iff_powerTorsion_and_finiteSocle
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsArtinian R M ↔
      (IsIPowerTorsion R M (maximalIdeal R) ∧ HasFiniteSocle R M)
declarations.comment: part (2): descending chain condition and torsion

declarations.name: Dualizing.powerTorsion_and_finiteSocle_iff_exists_finite_copresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08Z8, part (2).** The torsion and finite-socle condition is equivalent to
the existence of a copresentation by finite sums of an injective hull of the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public lemma powerTorsion_and_finiteSocle_iff_exists_finite_copresentation
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (i : ResidueField R →ₗ[R] E) [Mono (ModuleCat.ofHom i)]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull (ModuleCat.ofHom i)) :
    (IsIPowerTorsion R M (maximalIdeal R) ∧ HasFiniteSocle R M) ↔
      ∃ (n m : ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] (Fin n → E))
        (g : (Fin n → E) →ₗ[R] (Fin m → E)),
        Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Exact f g
declarations.comment: part (2): finite copresentation

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_matlisEvaluation_of_isArtinian
declarations.doc:
The canonical map to the double Matlis dual is an isomorphism for every module satisfying
the descending chain condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_matlisEvaluation_of_isArtinian
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    (E M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (i : residueFieldModule.{u, v} R ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) [IsArtinian R M] :
    IsIso ((matlisEvaluation R E).app M)
declarations.comment: biduality for modules with the descending chain condition

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_matlisEvaluation_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
The canonical map to the double Matlis dual is an isomorphism for every module satisfying
the ascending chain condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_matlisEvaluation_of_isNoetherian
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    (E M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (i : residueFieldModule.{u, v} R ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) [IsNoetherian R M] :
    IsIso ((matlisEvaluation R E).app M)
declarations.comment: biduality for modules with the ascending chain condition

declarations.name: Dualizing.matlisDuality
declarations.doc:
**Matlis duality (Stacks Project, Tag 08Z9).** The canonical anti-equivalence between
Artinian and Noetherian modules over a complete local Noetherian ring.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def matlisDuality
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    (E : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (i : residueFieldModule.{u, v} R ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    (ArtinianModules.{u, v} R)ᵒᵖ ≌ NoetherianModules.{u, v} R
declarations.comment: anti-equivalence

declarations.name: Dualizing.matlisDualityFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
The functor underlying `matlisDuality`, after inclusion in all modules, is naturally
isomorphic to `Hom_R(-, E)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def matlisDualityFunctorIso
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    (E : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (i : residueFieldModule.{u, v} R ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    (matlisDuality R E i hi).functor ⋙
        ObjectProperty.ι (fun M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R ↦ IsNoetherian R M) ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι (fun M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R ↦ IsArtinian R M)).op ⋙
        (linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj E
declarations.comment: the anti-equivalence is induced by the Matlis dual functor

declarations.name: fibreProduct_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08ZH.** Let `f : X → Z` and `g : Y → Z` be continuous maps of topological spaces.
If `Z` is Hausdorff, then the fibre product `X ×_Z Y` is a closed subset of `X × Y`, being the
equaliser of `f ∘ Prod.fst` and `g ∘ Prod.snd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreProduct_isClosed
    {X Y Z : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace Z]
    [T2Space Z] {f : X → Z} {g : Y → Z} (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
    IsClosed (fibreProduct f g)

declarations.name: TopCat.compactSpace_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08ZV.** Let `F : J ⥤ TopCat` be a diagram such that every `F.obj j` is quasi-compact
(`CompactSpace`) and Hausdorff (`T2Space`). Then the point of any limit cone over `F` is
quasi-compact.

The index category `J : Type v` with `Category.{w} J` is arbitrary and need not be small.
The instance `TopCat.compactSpace_limit` is the case of the chosen limit `limit F`. In the Stacks
project the index category of a limit has a set of objects (Stacks 002G), which is the case
`J : Type u` with `SmallCategory J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_of_isLimit
    {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] (F : J ⥤ TopCat.{u})
    [∀ j, CompactSpace (F.obj j)] [∀ j, T2Space (F.obj j)]
    (c : Cone F) (hc : IsLimit c) : CompactSpace c.pt

declarations.name: IsProfiniteStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08ZX** (definition of profinite). A topological space `X` is profinite if it is
homeomorphic to (the underlying space of) the limit of some diagram of finite discrete topological
spaces.
declarations.statement: def IsProfiniteStacks (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop

declarations.name: isProfiniteStacks_iff_t2_compact_totallyDisconnected_and_isProfinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 08ZY.** For a topological space `X` the following are equivalent: (1) `X` is a
profinite space, i.e. homeomorphic to the limit of a diagram of finite discrete spaces (Stacks
08ZX, `IsProfiniteStacks`); (2) `X` is Hausdorff, quasi-compact and totally disconnected. If this
is true, then `X` is a cofiltered limit of finite discrete spaces (`IsProfinite`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isProfiniteStacks_iff_t2_compact_totallyDisconnected_and_isProfinite
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    (IsProfiniteStacks X ↔ T2Space X ∧ CompactSpace X ∧ TotallyDisconnectedSpace X) ∧
      (IsProfiniteStacks X → IsProfinite X)
declarations.comment: Both directions and the final sentence. Profinite is `IsProfiniteStacks` (Stacks 08ZX): homeomorphic to the limit of an arbitrary diagram of finite discrete spaces indexed by a small category in the universe of `X`; the cofiltered conclusion is `IsProfinite`.
